translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke Demetrio aloo e huɛmɛ gali ɔmɛ kɛ nɔ ko ngɛ sane ko ɔ, kojomi ligbihi ngɛ, nɛ amlaalofo ɔmɛ hu ngɛ; nyɛ ha a kɛ sane ɔ nɛ ya a hɛ mi.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: Se ke munyu kpa komɛ a nya nyɛ ngɛ hlae ɔ, ma gua a nɛ ye ngɛ mlaa nya.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Ejakaa piɛ nguɛ nya nɛ wa ko na sane, ke mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ nɔ hoo peemi nɛ ɔ he nɛ a ya po wa nya kaa atua wa ngɛ tsɔe ɔ, mɛni nya jemi wa ngɛ?”

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e de enɛ ɔ se ɔ, e wo asafo ɔ blɔ.

english_verse: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
translation_verse: Se benɛ gidigidi peemi ɔ se po ɔ, Paulo tsɔ ya tsɛ kaseli ɔmɛ kɛ ba kpe, nɛ e tu munyu tsɔɔ mɛ nɛ e sɛ mɛ, nɛ e pue nɔ kɛ yaa Makedonia.

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e ya gu lejɛ ɔ ni ɔmɛ a mi nɛ e wo mɛ ga kɛ munyuhi fuu ɔ, e ba Hela,

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: nɛ e ye hlami etɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Akɛnɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ wo lɛ ka benɛ e ngɛ hlae nɛ e hia kɛ ya Syria a he je ɔ, e to e yi mi kaa e maa kpale e se kɛ ya gu Makedonia ekohu.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sopatre, Beroia no ɔ nɛ ji Pirho bi ɔ, kɛ Aristarko kɛ Sekundo, Tesalonikabi ɔmɛ, kɛ Gaio, Derbe no ɔ, kɛ Timoteo, kɛ Tihiko kɛ Tromfimo, Asiabi ɔmɛ, kɛ lɛ ya Asia.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Ni nɛ ɔmɛ sɛ hlami nɛ a ya mlɛ wɔ ngɛ Troia.

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: Se wɔɔ lɛɛ wa hia kɛ je Filipi ngɛ akpiti ligbi ɔmɛ a se, nɛ ligbi nɛ ji ligbi enuɔ ɔ, wa ya su a ngɔ ngɛ Troia, nɛ wa hi lejɛ ɔ ligbi kpaago. Paulo kɛ Troia asafo ɔ ye sɛ

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Otsi ɔ mi kekleekle ligbi ɔ nɔ ɔ, benɛ kaseli ɔmɛ kpane a he nya konɛ a kuɔ abolo ɔ, Paulo tu munyu tsɔɔ mɛ, nɛ e ngɛ nɔ kɛ ya su nyɔ mi kpɛti, ejakaa e nɔ je na mɔtu ɔ e maa je.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: A su kane fuu ngɛ hiɔwe tsu ɔ mi he nɛ a kpane a he nya ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Se niheyo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Eutiko ɔ hii si ngɛ saflɛ ɔ nya, nɛ mahɛ gbe lɛ, ejakaa Paulo munyu ɔ se kɛ. Mahɛ ɔ sɔuu ha e tsɔ kɛ je siaudo etɛ ɔ nɔ kɛ ba nɔ si, nɛ a ya wo lɛ nɛ e gbo.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Se Paulo kple si nɛ e ya bu e nɔ, nɛ e fua lɛ nɛ e ke: “Nyɛ ko pee hoo, ejakaa wami ngɛ e mi.”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e kuɔ kɛ ba ekohu ɔ, e ba ku abolo ɔ, nɛ e ye eko, nɛ e tsa e munyu ɔ nɔ hluu kɛ ba su je nami, kɛkɛ nɛ e pue nɔ.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Nɛ a kɛ niheyo ɔ ho hɛ kalɔ nɛ a bua jɔ a he nitse. Paulo si Troia kɛ ya Mileeto

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Se wɔɔ lɛɛ wa sɛ hlami kɛ ya sɛ lɛ mi, nɛ wa hia kɛ ya Aso nɛ wa ya ngɔ Paulo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ejakaa e de wɔ ngɔ to momo ke e maa gu zugba.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e ba na wɔ ngɛ Aso ɔ, wa ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba lɛ ɔ mi, nɛ wa ba Mitilene.

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: Wa hia kɛ je lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e nɔ je na a, wa ba su Kio hanɔ. Nɛ e nɔ je na nɔ ekohu ɔ wa ba su Samo, nɛ wa hi Trogilo, nɛ e nɔ je na a wa ba Mileeto.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Paulo pee e juɛmi kaa e maa tsɔ Efeso he, benɛ pee nɛ e ko kɛ ngɛ Asia; ejakaa e ngɛ esɔ mie, nɛ ke e ma nyɛ ɔ nɛ e ya ye Pentekoste ligbi ɔ ngɛ Yerusalem. Paulo kɛ Efeso nikɔtɔma amɛ ye sɛ

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Paulo tsɔ kɛ je Mileeto nɛ a ya tsɛ Efeso nikɔtɔma amɛ ba ha lɛ.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ a ba e ngɔ ɔ, e de mɛ ke: “Nyɛ le bɔ nɛ i kɛ nyɛ hi si be mluku ɔ tsuo, kɛ je kekleekle ligbi nɛ i ba Asia a.

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: I sɔmɔ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kɛ he si bami juɛmi tsuo kɛ vo nyu fuu kɛ kahi nɛ ba ye nɔ ngɛ Yudafohi a ka womi ɔmɛ a mi,

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: bɔ nɛ i laa we nyɛ nihi nɛ he ngɛ se nami ha nyɛ ɔ eko nɔ, nɛ i jaje tsɔɔ nyɛ faii ngɛ ma nɔ kɛ we tsuaa we mi hulɔ;

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: nɛ i ye tsui tsakemi kɛ Mawu hami kɛ wa Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo nɔ hemi kɛ yemi ɔ he odase ngɔ tsɔɔ Yudafohi kɛ Helabihi kulaa.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: Nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ, oʼɛ e fi mi ngɛ mumi mi he je ɔ i yaa Yerusalem, nɛ i li nihi nɛ maa ba ye nɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ,

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: kaa ja nɔ́ nɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ yeɔ odase faii ngɛ ma tsuaa ma mi kaa kpa kɛ amanehluhi lɛ ngɛ mi mlɛe ɔ?

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Se kɛ̃ ɔ, i bui enɛ ɔmɛ a mi kake ngmelu, nɛ ye wami hu i bui kaa e he jua wa ngɛ ye hɛ mi, benɛ pee nɛ i kɛ bua jɔmi nɛ gbe ye blɔ nyɛɛmi ɔ kɛ sɔmɔmi nɛ i na kɛ je Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu dɛ mi, kaa ma ye Mawu dloomi sane kpakpa a he odase faii, ɔ nya.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: “Nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ, oʼɛ, i le kaa, nyɛ nihi tsuo nɛ i nyɛɛ nyɛ kpɛti kɛ fiɛ Mawu matsɛ yemi ɔ he sane ɔ, nyɛ be ye hɛ mi nae hu.

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: Ejakaa i jaje Mawu yi mi tomi mluku ɔ tsuo ngɔ tsɔɔ nyɛ nɛ i laa we eko nɔ.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ nyɛɛ le nyɛ he nɔ hyemi kɛ tohi a kuu ɔ kulaa nɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu wo nyɛ a nɔ hyɛli ɔ, konɛ nyɛɛ lɛ Mawu asafo ɔ nɛ e kɛ lɛ nitsɛ e muɔ he ɔ.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: Ejakaa i le kaa ke i je ɔ, ogbetee ni hali maa sɛ nyɛ kpɛti, nɛ a be tohi a kuu ɔ yi baae.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Nɛ nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ kpɛti hu ɔ, nyumuhi nɛ tuɔ nihi nɛ dɛ maa te si, nɛ a ma kpaka kaseli ɔmɛ ngɔ pue a se.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he je ɔ nyɛɛ huɔ nɛ nyɛ kai kaa jeha etɛ sɔuu i kɛ vo nyu jɔɔ we nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ kɔkɔ bɔmi nyɔ kɛ pia.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: “Nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ, mamimɛ, i ngɛ nyɛ tue kɛ ngɛ Mawu kɛ e dloomi munyu ɔ dɛ mi woe, lɛ lɛ e ngɛ he wami nɛ e kɛ ma ha nyɛ nane nɛ pi si nɛ e ngɔ wɔfase ni ɔmɛ ngɔ ha nyɛ ngɛ nihi tsuo nɛ a tsukɔ a he ɔmɛ a kpɛti.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: Ye hɛ kɔɛ nyɛ ti nɔ ko sika hiɔ loo sika tsu loo tade nɔ.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ le kaa, nihi nɛ hiaa mi kɛ nihi nɛ kɛ mi ngɛ ɔ, kikɛmɛ a nine nɛ ɔmɛ nɔuu i kɛ tsu he ni.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: I kɛ kulaa tsɔɔ nyɛ kaa jã e sa kaa a tsu ni nɛ a kɛ ye bua nihi nɛ be he wami, nɛ a kai Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu munyu ɔmɛ kaa lɛ nitsɛ e ke: ‘Nɔ hami mi ngɛ gbaami pe hemi.’ ”

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e de kikɛ ɔ, e kplã si nɛ mɛ tsuo a sɔle.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Nɛ nɔ́ nɛ dɔ mɛ titli ji munyu nɛ e de ke a be e hɛ mi nae hu ɔ. Nɛ a ya je lɛ blɔ ngɛ lɛ ɔ mi.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Jeha nɛ ɔ e ba mi kaa benɛ waa kɛ mɛ ye sɛ nɛ wa gba mi ɔ, wa hia tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ba Koo, nɛ e nɔ je na a waba Rodo, nɛ wa je lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ wa ya na lɛ ko nɛ yaa Foinike ɔ, wa sɛ mi nɛ wa pue nɔ.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Se benɛ wa ngɛ Kipro hyɛe ngɛ wa hɛ mi ɔ, wa fia lɛ fɔ muɔ nɔ nɛ wa ba Siria, nɛ wa ba kple ngɛ Tiro, ejakaa lejɛ ɔ a ma je lɛ ɔ mi ni ngɛ.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Nɛ e ba mi kaa benɛ wa ye ligbi ɔmɛ tã a, wa pue nɔ, nɛ a kɛ a yihi kɛ a bimɛ kulaa ba je wɔ blɔ kɛ je ma a mi, nɛ wa kpla si ngɛ wo ɔ nya nɛ wa sɔle.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ waa kɛ wa he ye sɛ ɔ, wa sɛ lɛ mi, nɛ mɛ hu a kpale a se kɛ ho a wehi a mi ya.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Se wɔɔ lɛɛ wa je Tiro kɛ ba Ptolemai nɛ waa kɛ gbe wo hɛ mi nyɛɛmi ɔ nya. Wa ya nga nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ waa kɛ mɛ hi si ligbi kake.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: E nɔ je na a wa pue nɔ kɛ ho Kaisarea ya, nɛ wa ya sɛ sane kpakpa fiɛlɔ Filipo nɛ ji ni kpaago ɔ a kpɛti nɔ kake ɔ we mi, nɛ waa kɛ lɛ hi si.

english_verse: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
translation_verse: E ngɛ bimɛ yihewi eywiɛ nɛ gbaa.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Benɛ wa hi lejɛ ɔ be saii ɔ, gbalɔ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Agabo ɔ je Yudea ba.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Benɛ e ba wa ngɔ ɔ, e ngɔ Paulo mlɛ mi fimi nɔ́ ɔ nɛ e kɛ fi lɛ nitse e ninehi kɛ e nanehi nɛ e ke: Bɔ nɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: Nyumu nɔ nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ji mlɛ mi fimi nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ɔ, kikɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ maa fi lɛ ngɛ Yerusalem, nɛ a maa ngɔ lɛ ngɔ wo majemajeli a bimɛ ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Se benɛ wa nu enɛ ɔ ɔ, waa kɛ lejɛ ɔ bi ɔmɛ tsuo kpa lɛ pɛɛ ke e ko ya Yerusalem ɔ.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Paulo he nɔ nɛ e ke: “Mɛni nyɛ ngɛ pee nɛ ɔ, nyɛ ngɛ ya foe kɛ ma tsɔ ye tsui? Se imi lɛɛ, pi fimi kɛkɛ nɛ i dla ye he ngɔ to, se mohu gbenɔ nitse ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu biɛ ɔ he ngɛ Yerusalem.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ e kplɛɛ we he je ɔ, wa pee kɔ nɛ wa ke: “A pee nɔ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ suɔ.”

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ wa bo tlomi nɛ wa pue nɔ kɛ ho Yerusalem ya.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Kaseli nɛ je Kaisarea a a ti ni komɛ kɛ wɔ ho, nɛ a ha wa yato Mnason, Kipro no ko nɛ ji kaselɔ kɛ je kɛ ɔ ngɔ. Paulo ya slaa Yakobo

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Benɛ wa su Yerusalem ɔ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ he wɔ hɛmuɔ.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Nɛ e nɔ je na a Paulo kɛ wɔ ya Yakobo ngɔ; nɛ nikɔtɔma amɛ tsuo hu ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e nga mɛ ɔ, e bɔ mɛ nihi nɛ Mawu gu e sɔmɔmi ɔ nɔ tsu ngɛ majemajeli ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ kakaaka.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Benɛ a nu ɔ, a wo Mawu hɛ mi nyami, nɛ a de lɛ ke: “Mami, hyɛ Yudafohi akpehi abɔ nɛ a he ye nɛ ɔ; mɛ tsuo ɔ, Mlaa a he hɛdɔli ji mɛ.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Se a ba sɛɛ o he sane ha mɛ kaa o tsɔɔ Yudafohi nɛ ngɛ majemajeli ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ ke a kua Mose, nɛ o deɔ ke a ko po a bimɛ, nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu a ko nyɛɛ a kusumi nɛ ɔmɛ a se.

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ pee nɔ́ nɛ wa ngɛ mo de nɛ ɔ: Wa ngɛ nyumuhi eywiɛ nɛ wo si.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ngɔɔ mɛ nɛ o kɛ mɛ tsuo ya tsukɔ nyɛ he, nɛ o wo nɔ́ nɛ a haa a ngɔ ha mɛ, konɛ a sɛ a yi nɛ ni ɔmɛ kulaa nɛ na kaa, nihi nɛ a ba sɛɛ ngɛ o he ɔ be mi, se mohu mo nitsɛ po o baa o je mi ngɛ Mlaa a nya, nɛ o yeɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Se majemajeli a bimɛ nɛ he ye ɔ a he ɔ, wɔ nitsɛmɛ wa ngma nɛ wa kpɛ mi kaa a ko ye kikɛmɛ a ni nɛ ɔmɛ eko nɔ, se mohu a nyɛ bɔ nɛ a sa ha wɔhi kɛ muɔ kɛ lohwehi nɛ a kita a kuɛ kɛ ajuama bɔmi kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e nɔ je na a Paulo kpaka nyumu ɔmɛ kɛ ho, nɛ benɛ e kɛ mɛ kulaa tsukɔ a he ɔ, e kɛ mɛ sɛ sɔlemi we ɔ, nɛ e ya fiɛ he tsukɔmi ligbi ɔmɛ a nyagbe ɔ ngɔ tsɔɔ faii kɛ ya su be nɛ a sa bɔ ɔ ha a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ. A nu Paulo ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Benɛ e piɛ bɔɔ nɛ a maa gbe ligbi kpaago ɔ nya a, Yudafohi nɛ je Asia a na lɛ ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ, nɛ a su asafo ɔ ngɔ wo e he.

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Nɛ a kpa ngmlaa ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ Israelbi, nyɛ ba piɛ wa he! oʼɛ nyumu ɔ nɛ tuɔ ma nɛ ɔ kɛ Mlaa a kɛ hiɛ ɔ he munyu yaya ngɔ tsɔɔ nihi tsuo ngɛ he tsuaa he ɔ; nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ e kɛ Helabi ba sɔlemi we ɔ ba ble he klɔuklɔu nɛ ɔ hulɔ.”

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Ejakaa a na lɛ kɛ Trofimo nɛ je Efeso ɔ ngɛ ma a mi mo he je ɔ, a susu kaa lɛ nɛ Paulo kɛ ba sɔlemi we ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Nɛ ma mluku ɔ kulaa bu, nɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ sa fo kɛ ba kpane a he nya; nɛ a nu Paulo nɛ a sa lɛ kɛ je sɔlemi we ɔ kɛ je kpo, nɛ amlɔ ɔ nɔuu ɔ, a nga sinya amɛ.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Se benɛ a ngɛ hlae nɛ a gbe lɛ ɔ, a ya ju si sɛɛ ha asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a ke Yerusalem kulaa pee gidigidi.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Nɛ amlɔ ɔ, e ngɔ aslaafohi kɛ asafoatsɛmɛ nɛ e kɛ mɛ kple si kɛ fo kɛ ba na mɛ. Se benɛ a na asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a kɛ aslaafo ɔmɛ ɔ, a jɔɔ Paulo ni fiami.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a hɛ lɛ su e he nɛ e pɛtɛ e he, nɛ e fa ke a wo lɛ kɔsɔkɔsɔhi enyɔ, nɛ e bi nɔ nɛ ji lɛ kɛ nɔ́ nɛ e pee.

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Se asafo ɔ mi ni komɛ ngɛ ngmlaa kpae kikɛ, nɛ ni komɛ hu ngɛ ekpa dee. Nɛ akɛnɛ e nɛ́ mi anɔkuale ngɛ hoo peemi ɔ he ɔ, e fa ke a kɛ lɛ nɛ ya mɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e su atlaakpe ɔ nya a, e ba mi kaa asafo ɔ gidigidi peemi he je ɔ aslaafo ɔmɛ wo lɛ,

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: ejakaa ma bi asafo jiji ɔ nyɛɛ se ngɛ ngmlaa kpae ke: “Agbe lɛ!” Paulo je e nya

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Benɛ a kɛ Paulo ba sɛ mɔ ɔ mi ɔ, e bi asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a ke: “I ngɛ he blɔ kaa i kɛ mo tuɔ munyu ko lo?” Asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtama a ke: “O tuɔ Hela gbi lo?

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Paulo ke: “Imi lɛɛ Yuda no ji mi, nɛ i je Tarso, Kilikia ma ko nɛ ngɛ biɛ ɔ mi. Se i kpa mo pɛɛ, ha mi blɔ nɛ ma tu munyu ngɔ tsɔɔ ma a.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ a ha lɛ blɔ ɔ, Paulo da atlaakpe ɔ nɔ, nɛ e fɔ ma a nine, nɛ benɛ lejɛ ɔ jɔ klanaa a, e tu munyu ngɛ Hebri gbi mi de ke:

english_verse: “My friends and leaders of our nation, listen as I explain what happened!”
translation_verse: “Mamimɛ kɛ tsaatsɛmɛ, nyɛɛ bu ye nya jemi nɛ ɔ tue.”

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ a nu kaa Hebri gbi e kɛ mɛ ngɛ tue ɔ, a pee kɔ dii pe kekle ɔ. Nɛ e ke:

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: “I mi lɛɛ Yuda no ji mi, nɛ a fɔ mi ngɛ Tarso ngɛ Kilikia mohu, se ma nɛ ɔ mi a lɛ mi ngɛ, nɛ Gamaliel nane nya a tsɔse mi ngɛ, ngɛ wa tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a Mlaa a nya fitsofitso, nɛ ye hɛ dɔɔ ngɛ Mawu sane he, kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ tsuo nyɛ ngɛ pee mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: I waa nihi nɛ hɛɛ kikɛmɛ a tsɔɔmi nɛ ɔ yi mi kɛ ya suu gbenɔ mi, nɛ i fiɔ nyumuhi kɛ yihi tsuo ngɔ haa nɛ a woɔ mɛ tsu mi,

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: bɔ nɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma a tete kɛ nikɔtɔma amɛ kulaa yeɔ mi odase ɔ. Ni nɛ ɔmɛ nɔuu hu lɛ a ha mi womi nɛ jinɛ ma kɛ ya ha nyɛmimɛ nɛ ngɛ Damasko ɔ, nɛ ma fi nihi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ hu kɛ ba Yerusalem, konɛ a gbla a tue.” Paulo sɛɛ e tsakemi

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: “Se e ba mi kaa benɛ i nyɛɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ nɛ i su Damasko ta maa pee pudami be mi ɔ, tlukaa a la ko nɛ kpemi nya wa je hiɔwe ba bɔle mi;

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: nɛ i tsɔ fia si, nɛ i nu gbi ko de mi ke: ‘Saulo, Saulo, mɛ he je o ngɛ mi yi mi wae?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Nɛ i he nɔ ke: ‘Mo mɛnɔ, Nyɔmtsɛ?’ Nɛ e de mi ke: ‘Imi Yesu, Nazareno ɔ, nɛ o ngɛ lɛ yi mi wae ɔ ʼi.’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ kɛ mi nyɛɛ ɔ na la a, nɛ a ye gbeye, se a nui nɔ nɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ɔ gbi.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Nɛ i ke: ‘Mɛni ma pee, Nyɔmtsɛ?’ Nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ de mi ke: ‘Tee si nɛ o ya Damasko, nɛ lejɛ ɔ a maa tsɔɔ mo nihi kulaa nɛ a to kaa o pee ɔ.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ i hyɛ we nɔ́ hu ngɛ jamɛ a la a kpemi ɔ nya a, nihi nɛ kɛ mi nyɛɛ ɔ pɛtɛ ye nine mi nɛ a ya sɛ mi Damasko.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: “Nyumu ko ngɛ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Anania nɛ yee Mawu gbeye ngɛ Mlaa a nya, nɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ kulaa nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ tuɔ e he munyu kpakpa.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Lɛ nɛ e ba ye ngɔ nɛ e ba da ye kasa nyɛ nɛ e de mi ke: ‘Maminyumu Saulo, hyɛ nɔ!’ Nɛ jamɛ a ngmlɛfia a nɔ nɔuu ɔ i na lɛ.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Nɛ e ke: ‘Wa tsɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ hla mo ngɔ to nɛ o le e suɔmi nya ni nɛ o na Dalɔ ɔ nɛ o nu e nya mi gbi ko;

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: “Benɛ i kpale ye se kɛ ba Yerusalem ekohu nɛ i ngɛ sɔlee ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ, e pee kaa nɔ́ nɛ nɔ́ nɔ ye nɔ,

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: nɛ i na lɛ nɛ e ngɛ mi dee ke: ‘Pee esɔ nɛ o je Yerusalem, ejakaa a be ye he odase nɛ o ngɛ yee ɔ tue bue.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: Nɛ i ke: ‘Nyɔmtsɛ, mɛ nitsɛmɛ a le kaa imi nɔuu ji nɔ nɛ sa a i woɔ nihi nɛ heɔ o nɔ yeɔ ɔ tsu mi, nɛ i fiaa mɛ ni ngɛ kpe he tsuaa kpe he,

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: nɛ benɛ a pue Stefano, o he odaseyelɔ ɔ, muɔ si ɔ, imi hu i daa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ ye bua jɔ e gbenɔ he, nɛ i bu nihi nɛ gbe lɛ ɔmɛ a bo ɔmɛ a he.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Nɛ e de mi ke: ‘Yaa, ejakaa ma tsɔ mo majemajeli nɛ ngɛ lokoo ɔmɛ a ngɔ.’ ”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Se benɛ a ngɛ ngmlaa kpae nɛ a ngɛ a tadehi kpɔe nɛ a ngɛ bunyuku gbee kɛ ngɛ kɔɔyɔ mi woe ɔ,

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a fa ke a kɛ lɛ nɛ ya mɔ ɔ mi, nɛ e de ke a ngɔ kplibi kɛ hla e yi mi, konɛ e le nɔ́ sane he je nɛ a ngɛ ngmlaa kpae kɛ ngɛ lɛ woe kikɛ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Se benɛ a fi lɛ nɛ a maa fia lɛ kpa a, Paulo bi asafoatsɛ nɛ daa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ke: “Nyɛ ngɛ he blɔ kaa nyɛ fiaa Roma no ko nɛ a bui lɛ fɔ ɔ kplibi lo?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Se benɛ asafoatsɛ ɔ nu enɛ ɔ ɔ, e ya asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a ngɔ nɛ e ya de lɛ ke: “Mɛni o maa pee nɛ ɔ? Ejakaa kikɛmɛ a nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ Roma no ʼi.”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a ba nɛ e ba bi lɛ ke: “De mi, anɛ Roma no ji mo lo?” Nɛ Paulo ke: “Ee.”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Nɛ asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a he nɔ ke: “Sika fuu i kɛ he kikɛmɛ a ma mi no plɛmi nɛ ɔ.” Nɛ Paulo ke: “Se imi lɛɛ pe a kɛ fɔ mi.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ amlɔ ɔ nɔuu nɛ nihi nɛ yaa hla e yi mi ɔ je e kasa nya. Asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a hu, akɛnɛ e fi lɛ he je ɔ, benɛ e na le kaa Roma no ji lɛ ɔ, e tsui po. Paulo ngɛ gua ngua a hɛ mi

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a ngɛ hlae nɛ e le nɔ́ tutuutu he je nɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ po e nya a, e nɔ je na nɔ ɔ, e pɛne lɛ, nɛ e fa ke osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ kɛ gua ngua a kulaa nɛ ba. Nɛ e kɛ Paulo kple si, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ya da a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Paulo tɛ̃tɛ̃ e hɛ mi nɛ e hyɛ gua ngua a kɛ kpe nɛ e ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ kɛ mamimɛ, imi lɛɛ he nile kpakpa sɔuu i kɛ ba ye je mi ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi kɛ ba su mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma Anania fa nihi nɛ daa si ngɛ e kasa nya a ke a gba e nya ma.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Paulo de lɛ ke: “Ma kɛ̃ Mawu ma gba mo, mo gli nɛ a sa he kalo! O hii si ngɛ mi kojoe ngɛ Mlaa a nya, nɛ o pa jee Mlaa a se faa ke a gba mi ma?”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Se nihi nɛ daa si ngɛ e kasa nya a de lɛ ke: “Ee! Mawu osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma a o ngɛ jɛe nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Paulo ke: “Mamimɛ, i li kaa osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma ʼi; ejakaa a ngma ke: ‘Koo tu o ma mi nɔkɔtɔma he munyu yaya.’ ”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Se benɛ Paulo kpa si kaa fã kake ɔ Sadukifohi ji mɛ, nɛ fã kpa a Farisifohi ʼi ɔ, e nga ngɛ gua ngua a kpɛti ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ kɛ mamimɛ, imi lɛɛ Farisifo no ji mi kɛ Farisifo no bi hulɔ. Hɛ nɔ kami kɛ ni gbogboehi a si temi ɔ he a ngɛ mi kojoe nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: Benɛ e de kikɛ ɔ, kɛkɛ nɛ pɛ sɛ Farisifo ɔmɛ kɛ Sadukifo ɔmɛ a kpɛti, nɛ aafo ɔ mi gba enyɔ.

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: Ejakaa Sadukifo ɔmɛ deɔ ke ni gbogboehi a si temi ko be nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu hiɔwe bɔfo loo mumi ko hu be. Se Farisifo ɔmɛ deɔ ke enyɔ ɔ tsuo ngɛ.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Nɛ huhui babauu ba te si, nɛ mlaatsɔɔli ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Farisifo ɔmɛ a se ɔ te si nɛ a pɛ de ke: “Wa nɛ nɔ ko yaya ko ngɛ kikɛmɛ a nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ he. Se ke alinɔ mumi ko loo hiɔwe bɔfo ko nɛ e kɛ lɛ tu munyu ɔ nɛɛ?”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Se benɛ pɛ ɔ mi ba wa a, asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a ye gbeye kaa eko ɔ a ma tsɔtslɔɔ Paulo mi he je ɔ, e fa aslaafo ɔmɛ ke a kple si nɛ a ya kpɔ lɛ ngɛ a dɛ, nɛ a kɛ lɛ nɛ ba mɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Se e nɔ nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ba da e kasa nyɛ nɛ e ke: “Paulo, ha o tsui nɛ nɔ o mi, ejakaa bɔ nɛ o ye hye odase ngɛ Yerusalem nɛ ɔ ɔ, ja o ya ye odase jã nɔuu ngɛ Roma hulɔ.” A so Paulo yi nɔ

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Nɛ a ya osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ kɛ ma nikɔtɔma amɛ a ngɔ ya de ke: “Waa kɛ kita kami so kaa, wa be wa nya mi nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko woe ja wa gbe Paulo lolo.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ jeha nɛ ɔ nyɛɛ kɛ gua ngua a tsuo ya de asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a, konɛ e kɛ Paulo nɛ kple si kɛ ba nyɛ ngɔ, kaa nɔ́ nɛ e sane ɔ mi nyɛ ma hyemi fitsofitso. Se wɔɔ lɛɛ loko e maa su nyɛ ngɔ ɔ, wa dla wa he nɛ wa maa gbe lɛ.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Se Paulo nyɛmiyo bi ko nu a ka womi ɔ he, nɛ e pue nɔ kɛ ya mɔ ɔ mi, nɛ e ya wo Paulo tue nɔ.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Paulo tsɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti nɔ kake kɛ ba e ngɔ, nɛ e ke: “Ngɔɔ kikɛmɛ a niheyo nɛ ɔ nɛ o kɛ lɛ nɛ ya asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a ngɔ, ejakaa e ngɛ munyu ko nɛ e maa sɛɛ ha lɛ.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e ngɔ lɛ nɛ e kɛ lɛ ya asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a ngɔ nɛ e ya de ke: “Pamino Paulo ɔ tsɛ mi kɛ ya e ngɔ, nɛ e kpa mi pɛɛ ke i kɛ kikɛmɛ a niheyo nɛ ɔ nɛ ba o ngɔ, ejakaa e ngɛ munyu ko nɛ e maa sɛɛ ha mo.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Nɛ asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a nu e nine si, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ya se, nɛ e bi lɛ ke: “Mɛni sane o ngɛ nɛ o ma de mi?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Nɛ e ke: “Yudafo ɔmɛ pee kake ke a ma ba bi mo nɛ hwɔɔ ɔ nɛ o kɛ Paulo nɛ kple si kɛ ba gua ngua a hɛ mi, kaa nɔ́ nɛ e sane ɔ mi a ma hlami fitsofitso.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a wo niheyo ɔ blɔ, nɛ e wo lɛ hiɔngɔ ke: “Ko de nɔ ko nɔ ko ke o wo sane nɛ ɔ nɔ tã de mi.” A kɛ Paulo ya ha amlaalo Felike

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Nɛ e de ke, a dla okpɔngɔhi hulɔ ngɔ to nɛ a ha Paulo nɛ hi nɔ, nɛ a kɛ lɛ ya ha amlaalo Felike sɔkee.

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Nɛ e ngma womi nɛ e de ngɛ mi ke:

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: “Klaudio Lisia biɔ amlaalo kpakpa Felike saminya!

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Kikɛmɛ a nyumu nɛ ɔ ɔ, Yudafo ɔmɛ nu lɛ nɛ jinɛ a maa gbe lɛ. Se benɛ i na le kaa Roma no ji lɛ ɔ, ikɛ aslaafohi ya ya kpɔ lɛ.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: Nɛ akɛnɛ i ngɛ hlae nɛ ma le nɔ́ sane he je nɛ a ngɛ e nya poe ɔ, i kɛ lɛ ya a gua ngua a hɛ mi,

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: nɛ i na kaa a Mlaa a he nguane jemi sane komɛ a he nɛ a ngɛ e nya poe ɔ nɛ, se sane ko nɛ sa gbenɔ aloo tsu mi womi ko be e he.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Se benɛ a ba ju si de mi ke Yudafo ɔmɛ wo nyumu ɔ ka a, amlɔ ɔ, i tsɔ ke a kɛ lɛ nɛ ba o ngɔ, nɛ i fa le nya poli ɔmɛ hu ke a ba o hɛ mi nɛ a ba jaje sanehi nɛ a kɛ lɛ ngɛ ɔ. He manye!”

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ aslaafo ɔmɛ ngɔ Paulo kaa bɔ nɛ a fa mɛ ɔ, nɛ a nyɛɛ nyɔ ɔ mi nɛ a kɛ lɛ ba Antipatri.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: E nɔ je na a, a ha okpɔngɔtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ kɛ lɛ ho, se mɛɛ lɛɛ a kpale a se kɛ ba mɔ ɔ mi ekohu.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Benɛ a su Kaisarea nɛ a kɛwomi ɔ ya ha amlaalo ɔ, a kɛ Paulo hu ba da e hɛ mi.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ amlaalo ɔ kane womi ɔ, e bi ke jije zugba nɔ e je, nɛ benɛ e na le kaa Kilikia e je ɔ,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: e ke: “Ke o nya poli ɔmɛ hu ba a, kɔlɔ ɔ loko ma bu mo tue saminya.” Nɛ e fa ke a kɛ lɛ ya to Herode mɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Ligbi enyɔ se ɔ, osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma Anania kɛ ma nikɔtɔma amɛ ekomɛ kɛ otsiame ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Tertulo ɔ ba lejɛ ɔ, nɛ a ba jaje Paulo he sane ngɔ tsɔɔ amlaalo ɔ.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ a ya tsɛ Paulo kɛ ba a, Tertulo bɔni e nya pomi, nɛ e ke: “Wa nɔmo Felike, akɛnɛ o yinɔ nɛ ɔ wa tue mi jɔ wɔ babauu, nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu o nɔ hyɛmi ɔ nya a o ha nihi fuu ba hɛngmɛ nɔ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ he ɔ,

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: wa naa mo si babauu daa nɛ ɔ ngɛ he tsuaa he ngɛ enɛ ɔmɛ kulaa he.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Se benɛ pee nɛ ye munyu se nɛ ko kɛ fuu tsɔ he je ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o bu wɔ tue bɔɔ ngɛ o mi mi himi nya.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: E ji anɔkuale kaa wa na nyumu nɛ ɔ kaa e ji nihi a tue puɛlɔ, e woɔ Yudafohi tsuo nɛ ngɛ zugba mluku ɔ kulaa nɔ ɔ yi mi nɛ a tsɔ atua, nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu e ji Nazaretsɛmɛ a kuu ɔ nya kpa.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: nɛ e fa e nya poli ɔmɛ ke a ba o ngɔ], nɛ ke mo nitsɛ o bi e nya mi munyu ɔ, o maa na sanehi nɛ wa ngɛ e nya poe ngɛ he ɔ kulaa.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Nɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ hu ka nɔ, nɛ a ma nɔ mi ke munyu nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ mi ja. Paulo je e nya ngɛ Felike hɛ mi

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Se benɛ amlaalo ɔ fɔ Paulo nine ke e tu munyu ɔ, e wo e nya nɔ nɛ e ke: “Akɛnɛ i le kaa tsa pi mwɔnɛ nɛ o je bɔni zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ amlaalo yemi he je ɔ, i na bua jɔmi nɛ ma kɛ je ye nya.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Ke o bu ɔ, o maa na kaa ligbi nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ pɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ i ba be kɛ ho Yerusalem ya ke ma ya ja Mawu.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu a nɛ mi hyɛ kaa i kɛ nihi ngɛ nya sae, aloo i ngɛ nihi bue ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ, aloo kpe he ɔmɛ, aloo ma a mi.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu sanehi nɛ a kɛ ngɛ ye nɔ fɔe nɛ ɔ, a be nya nyɛe maa tsɔɔ.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ mi gbae pãa ngɛ dee ji enɛ ɔ kaa, tsɔɔmi nɛ a ngɛ tsɛe ke nyangɔ tsɔɔmi ɔ, kɔlɔ ɔ nɔuu nya i jaa wa tsɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ ngɛ; i heɔ nihi kulaa nɛ a ngma ngɛ Mlaa a kɛ gbali ɔmɛ a mi ɔ yeɔ.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: I ngɛ Mawu nɔ hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi kaa ni gbogboehi a si temi maa ba, nɛ dali kɛ nihi nɛ dɛ́ kulaa maa te si, kɔlɔ ɔ nɔuu blɔ ni nɛ ɔmɛ hu ngɛ hyɛe.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he nɛ i kɛ ye he fɔɛ si ɔ nɛ, benɛ pee nɛ ma na he nile nɛ yobu be he ngɛ Mawu kɛ nimli a hɛ mi ngɛ nihi kulaa mi.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Nɛ jehahi fuu a se ɔ, i ba nɛ i kɛ nike ni ba ha ye ma a nɛ ma sã bɔ hulɔ.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ mi nɛ a na mi kaa i ngɛ ye he tsukɔe ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ, se a nɛ́ mi kɛ asafo ko ɔ, a n nɛ́ mi kɛ hoopeemi ko hulɔ.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Se Yudafohi komɛ nɛ je Asia a ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, jinɛ mɛ nɛ sa kaa a ba o hɛ mi, nɛ ke a ngɛ ye he sane ko ɔ nɛ a ba jaje.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Aloo ni nɛ ɔmɛ nitsɛmɛ po, ke a na nɔ́ ko nɛ dɛ ngɛ ye he benɛ i daa si ngɛ gua ngua a hɛ mi ɔ, a de;

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: kaa ja kikɛmɛ a munyu kake nɛ benɛ i da a kpɛti nɛ i wo ye gbi nɔ de ke: Ni gbogboehi a sitemi he je nyɛ ngɛ mi kojoe mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ’ ɔ he kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ Felike le kikɛmɛ a tsɔɔmi nɛ ɔ he sane pɛpɛɛpe he je ɔ, e tsɛ̃ mɛ ngɔ to, nɛ e ke: “Ke asafoatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma Lisia ba a, ma hyɛ nyɛ sane ɔ ma ye.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Nɛ e fa asafoatsɛ ɔ ke e ngɔ Paulo ngɔ to, nɛ e ha e na hejɔmi, nɛ ke e he nimli ma lɛ sɔmɔmi loo slaami ɔ e ko tsi mɛ blɔ. Paulo ngɛ Felike kɛ Drusila hɛ mi

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Se be saii se ɔ, Felike kɛ e yo Drusila nɛ ji Yudayo ɔ ba, nɛ e ha a ya tsɛ Paulo kɛ ba, konɛ e bu Kristo nɔ hemi kɛ yemi he sane ɔ tue.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Se benɛ e ngɛ dami kɛ he nɔ yemi kɛ kojomi nɛ maa ba a he munyu tue ɔ, Felike ye gbeye wawɛɛ, nɛ e de lɛ ke: “Yaa lolo; se ke i na ye he deka hu ɔ, ma tsɛ mo ekohu.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Se jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, e hɛ ngɛ nɔ kaa Paulo ma ha lɛ sika konɛ e ngmɛɛ e he, kɔlɔ ɔ he nɛ e tsɛɛ lɛ kpitikpiti nɛ e kɛ lɛ ba sɛɛ ni ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Se jeha enyɔ se ɔ, Porkio Festo ba ye Felike nane mi; nɛ akɛnɛ Felike suɔ kaa e pee nɔ́ nɛ sa Yudafo ɔmɛ a hɛ mi he je ɔ, e si Paulo ngɛ tsu ɔ mi.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Festo ba ye amlaalo, ligbi etɛ se pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ e je Kaisarea kɛ ho Yerusalem ya.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ kɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ a nikɔtɔma amɛ ba po Paulo nya ha lɛ, nɛ a kpa lɛ pɛɛ,

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: nɛ a bi ke e hyɛ a hɛ mi nɛ e tsɔ nɛ a ya ngɔ Paulo kɛ ba Yerusalem; ejakaa a wo e he ka konɛ a gbe lɛ ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Se Festo he nɔ ke, Paulo nɛ hi tsu ɔ mi ngɛ Kaisarea, se lɛ nitsɛ hu e be kɛe nɛ e maa ya lejɛ ɔ,

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: he je ɔ e ke: “Nyɛ ha nyɛ nya dali ɔmɛ nɛ a kɛ mi nɛ ya lejɛ ɔ, nɛ ke sane yaya ko ngɛ nyumu ɔ he ɔ nɛ a de.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e ye maa pee ligbi kpaanyɔ loo nyɔngma ngɛ a ngɔ ɔ, e pue nɔ kɛ ho Kaisarea ya, nɛ e nɔ je na a e ya hi kojomi sɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ e fa ke a kɛ Paulo nɛ ba.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Se benɛ e ba lejɛ ɔ, Yudafohi nɛ je Yerusalem ba a ba bɔle lɛ kɛ kpe nɛ a kɛ nya pomi sanehi fuu nɛ nya wa ba pue Paulo nɔ, se a nyɛ we nya nɛ a tsɔɔ.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Paulo je e nya de ke: “I tɔ́ we Yudafohi a mlaa ko ɔ, jeha nɛ ɔ hu, i tɔ́ we sɔlemi we ɔ loo Kaisare nɔ.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ Festo suɔ kaa e pee nɔ́ nɛ sa Yudafo ɔmɛ a hɛ mi he je ɔ, e bi Paulo ke: “O suɔ kaa o ya Yerusalem nɛ ma ya kojo mo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a sane nɛ ɔmɛ a he lo?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Se Paulo ke: “Kaisare kojomi sɛ ɔ hɛ mi i daa si ngɛ nɛ ɔ nɛ, he nɛ sa kaa a kojoɔ mi ngɛ ɔ. Yudafo ɔmɛ ɔ, i tɔ́ we a ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ o le saminya a.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ ke i ye sane yaya ko nɛ i pee nɔ́ ko nɛ sa gbenɔ ɔ, i kua we gbenɔ. Se ke sanehi nɛ ni nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ ye nya poe ngɛ he nɛ ɔ eko eko be mi ɔ, nɔ ko be nyɛe maa ngɔ mi ngɔ wo a dɛ mi. I ngɔ ye sane ɔ ngɔ ha Kaisare yemi.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Festo kɛ e ga woli ɔmɛ hla mi, nɛ e ke: “Nɛ o kɛ o sane ɔ ha Kaisare yemi nɛ ɔ ɔ, Kaisare ngɔ nɔuu o maa ya.” Paulo ngɛ Agripa kɛ Bernike hɛ mi

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Be ko se ɔ, matsɛ Agripa kɛ Bernike ba Kaisarea nɛ a ba nga Festo.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ a ye be saii ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, Festo jaje Paulo sane ɔ ngɔ tsɔɔ matsɛ ɔ nɛ e ke: “Nyumu ko ngɛ hiɛ ɔ nɛ Felike si lɛ ngɛ tsu mi;

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: benɛ i ya Yerusalem ɔ osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ kɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ a nikɔtɔma amɛ ba ye ngɔ kɛ e nya pomi, nɛ a kpa mi pɛɛ ke ma bu lɛ fɔ.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: I ha mɛ heto ke, e be Romabi a mlaa mi kaa a gbaa nɔ ko nɔ ngɔ haa gbenɔ, ja nɔ nɛ a po e nya a kɛ e nya poli ɔmɛ kpe hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi nɛ nɔ ɔ na he blɔ je e nya ngɛ sane nɛ a ngɔ fɔ e nɔ ɔ he lolo.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, benɛ a nya ba bua ngɛ hiɛ ɔ ɔ, i tui tslee, se je na nɔ ɔ, i ya hi kojomi sɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ i fa ke a ngɔ nyumu ɔ kɛ ba.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Se benɛ e nya poli ɔmɛ ba da si ɔ, a kɛ sanehi nɛ i susu ɔmɛ a kpɛti ngu kake bɛ́ ba pui e nya,

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: se mohu mɛ nitsɛmɛ a Mawu jami he nguane jemi sanehi komɛ kɛ Yesu ko nɛ e gbo nɛ Paulo ma nɔ mi ke e hɛ ngɛ ɔ he sanehi a hɛɛ kɛ ba.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ i li bɔ nɛ ma pee kɛ hla kikɛmɛ a sane nɛ ɔmɛ a mi he je ɔ, i bi lɛ ke e maa suɔ kaa e ya Yerusalem nɛ a ya ye kikɛmɛ a sane nɛ ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ lo?

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ Paulo dai e sane ɔ ngɔ ha Kaisare nitsɛ yemi he je ɔ, i fa ke a ngɔ lɛ ngɔ to kɛ ya su be nɛ ma ha a ngɔ lɛ kɛ ya Kaisare ngɔ.”

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Agripa de Festo ke: “Jinɛ imi hu ma suɔ kaa ma bu nɔmlɔ ɔ tue.” Nɛ e ke: “Hwɔɔ ɔ o maa bu lɛ tue.”

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e nɔ je na a, benɛ Agripa kɛ Bernike mia gbegbelii kɛ ba nɛ a kɛ asafoatsɛmɛ nikɔtɔmahi kɛ ma a mi nimli ngua amɛ ba sɛ sane tue bumi he ɔ, Festo fa, nɛ a kɛ Paulo ba.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Nɛ Festo ke: “Matsɛ Agripa, kɛ nyɛ nihi tsuo nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ wɔ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, nyɛ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a nyumu nɛ ɔ nɛ Yudafohi asafo mluku ɔ kulaa ba kpa mi pɛɛ ngɛ Yerusalem kɛ hiɛ ɔ tsuo nɛ a kpa ngmlaa wo mi ke e sɛ́ kaa e hii je mi hu ɔ hyɛe.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Se imi lɛɛ i na kaa e pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ sa gbenɔ, nɛ akɛnɛ lɛ nitsɛ e tu e sane ɔ ngɔ wo Kaisare dɛ mi he je ɔ, i ma nya si kaa a kɛ lɛ ya ha lɛ.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Se i be sane tutuutu ko nɛ jinɛ ma ngma ya ha nyɔmtsɛ ɔ, lɔ ɔ he hulɔ nɛ i kɛ lɛ ba nyɛ hɛ mi, benɛ pee nɛ ke a hla sane ɔ mi ɔ, nɛ ma na nɔ́ ko ma ngma.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Se e peɔ mi kaa e dɛ́ kaa a ngɔɔ pamino ko ngɔ maneɔ nɛ a tsɔɔ we nɔ́ nɛ a ke e pee.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Paul, “You may now speak for yourself.” Paul stretched out his hand and said:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Agripa de Paulo ke: “A ngmɛ mo blɔ kaa o ja o gbi.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Paulo fɔ e nine nɛ e je e nya ke:

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: “Matsɛ Agripa, e ngɔ ye nya kaa ma je ye nya mwɔnɛ ngɛ o hɛ mi, ngɛ nihi tsuo nɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ kɛ ngɛ ye nya poe ɔ he.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: O le Yudafo ɔmɛ a blɔ nya ni ɔmɛ kɛ nguane jemi sane ɔmɛ kulaa mi pɛpɛɛpɛ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o to tsui nɛ o bu mi tue.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Ke a suɔ kaa a maa ye he odase ɔ, a le mi sa kɛ je sisije ɔ, kaa i ba ye je mi ngɛ wa jami ɔ mi kuu nɛ ngɛ veveeve pe kulaa nya, kaa Farisifono.

english_verse: Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
translation_verse: Nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ, si nɛ Mawu wo wa tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi ɔ he nɛ i daa si ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, nɛ a ngɛ mi kojoe nɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Kɔlɔ ɔ nɔ wa wetso nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ ɔ hɛ ngɛ he je nɛ a hɛɛ nyɔ kɛ pia jami nɛ nya wa a mi, benɛ pee nɛ a nine nɛ su nɔ. Matsɛ Agripa, kikɛmɛ a hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi nɛ ɔ he je nɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ ngɛ ye nya poe nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ nyɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ nyɛ buu kaa e be mi kaa Mawu tleɔ ni gbogboehi a si ɔ?

english_verse: I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth.
translation_verse: “Imi nitsɛ hu e pee mi kaa e sa kaa ma pee nihi fuu nɛ ma kɛ te si ngɔ si Yesu, Nazareno ɔ biɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: I na pee ja hulɔ ngɛ Yerusalem, nɛ akɛnɛ i na he blɔ kɛ je osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ a ngɔ he je ɔ, i wo ni klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ a kpɛti nihi fuu tsu mi, nɛ ke a maa gbe mɛ ɔ, ye nya ngɛ mi eko.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: Nɛ i pɔɔ mɛ yi mi wami ngɛ kpe he ɔmɛ kulaa, nɛ i waa mɛ yi mi kaa a tu musu bɔmi munyuhi, nɛ i nuu a he godo wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ i waa mɛ yi mi kɛ yaa ma se mahi a mi tete. Paul sɛɛ e tsakemi ɔ

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: “Enɛ ɔ nɔ nɔuu i nyɛɛ nɛ i hia blɔ kɛ yaa Damasko ngɛ osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ a he wami blɔ ngmɛmi nya.

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: Nɛ piani katakata, benɛ i nyɛɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ ɔ, matsɛ, i na la ko nɛ ngɛ kpɛe pe pu je hiɔwe ba bɔle mi kɛ nihi nɛ kɛ mi nyɛɛ ɔ.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ wɔ tsuo wa ya nɔ si ɔ, i nu gbi ko nɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ngɛ Hebri gbi mi ke: ‘Saul, Saul, Mɛni he je o ngɛ mi yi mi wae? E wa ha mo kaa o maa hia nazi ngɔ si lohwehi a kpakami tso nya dade ɔ.’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: Nɛ i ke: ‘Mo mɛnɔ ʼi, Nyɔmtsɛ?’ Nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ke: ‘Imi Yesu nɛ o ngɛ lɛ yi mi wae ɔ ʼi.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Tee si nɛ o da o nane nɔ; enɛ ɔ he nɛ i je ye he kpo tsɔɔ mo nɛ ɔ nɛ, konɛ ma pee mo sɔmɔlɔ kɛ odase yelɔ ngɛ nihi nɛ o na kɛ nihi nɛ ma je ye he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ mo ngɛ he ɔmɛ a he.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: Ma je mo kɛ maa je ma a kɛ majemajeli nɛ i ngɛ mo a ngɔ tsɔe ɔ a dɛ mi,

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: nɛ o ya bli a hɛngmɛ komɛ a kpale kɛ je diblii mi kɛ ba la he, kɛ je abosiami he wami mi kɛ ba Mawu ngɔ, nɛ a na a he yayami pami kɛ gbo si ni ngɛ nihi nɛ a kɛ ye nɔ hemi kɛ yemi pee mɛ klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ a kpɛti.’ ” Paulo sɛɛ e nitsumi he ni

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: se mohu i jaje ngɔ tsɔɔni hi nɛ ngɛ Damasko ɔ kekle, kɛ nihi nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem kɛ Yudea zugba a nɔ kulaa, kɛ majeli ɔmɛ hulɔ, ke a tsake a tsui nɛ a kpale kɛ ba Mawu ngɔ nɛ a tsu nihi nɛ sa tsui tsakemi.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔmɛ a he je nɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ nu mi ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ, nɛ a ka mi gbemi ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Se Mawu yemi kɛ buami nya i kɛ daa si kɛ ba su mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ i ngɛ odase yee kɛ ngɛ nimli tsɔwi kɛ nimli nguahi tsɔɔe nɛ ɔ nɛ. I tu we munyu ko kaa ja nihi nɛ gbali ɔmɛ kɛ Mose hu de ke a maa ba a,

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: kaa Kristo ɔ maa na amanehlu, nɛ e ba plɛ kekleekle nɔ ngɛ ni gbogboehi a sitemi ɔ mi, nɛ e ba jaje la a he sane ngɔ tsɔɔ ma a kɛ majeli ɔmɛ.”

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Paulo je e nya kikɛ ɔ, Festo de kɛ gbi wawɛɛ ke: “Paulo, godo o ngɛ nue nɛ ɔ! Womi kasemi sɔuu lɛ ha o ngɛ godo nue nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Se Paulo ke: “I nui godo, wa nɔmo Festo, se anɔkuale kɛ hɛ si kami munyu i ngɛ tue nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ nɛ i ngɛ munyu tue kɛ kã kɛ ngɛ lɛ tsɔɔe nɛ ɔ le sane nɛ ɔmɛ a mi. I kpa we si kaa ni nɛ ɔmɛ eko ngɛ nɛ a kɛ laa lɛ; ejakaa tsa pi laami mi nɛ a pee enɛ ɔ ngɛ.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Tse o heɔ gbali ɔmɛ yeɔ, Matsɛ Agripa? I le kaa o heɔ yeɔ.”

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Agripa de Paulo ke: “Piɛ bɔɔ nɛ o ko ha ye yi mi plɛ nɛ i pee Kristofono.”

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Se Paulo ke: “I na nɛ jinɛ Mawu ha ba mi kaa, e piɛ bɔɔ jio, e piɛ fuu jio, pi mo o nɔ kake kɛkɛ, se mohu nihi kulaa nɛ ngɛ mi tue bue mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ hu ko plɛ kaa i mi, se pã nɛ ɔmɛ eko kɛkɛ nɛ a ko ka mɛ.”

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e de kikɛ ɔ, matsɛ ɔ kɛ amlaalo ɔ kɛ Bernike kɛ nihi nɛ kɛ mɛ hii si ɔ te si,

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: nɛ a ya se, nɛ a ya da, nɛ a ke: “Nyumu nɔ pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ sa gbenɔ loo tsu mi womi.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Agripa de Festo ke: “Kaa nyumu nɛ ɔ ngɔɛ e sane ɔ ngɔ ha we Kaisare yemi jinɛ, a ma nyɛ e he maa ngmɛɛ.”

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Bɛnɛ a ma nya si kaa wa maa ya Italia a, a ngɔ Paulo kɛ pamitsɛmɛ kpa komɛ hu ngɔ wo asafoatsɛ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Yulio nɛ je Agusto ta asafo ɔ mi ɔ dɛ mi.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Benɛ wa sɛ Adramitio lɛ ko nɛ maa hia kɛ ya gu Asia wo nya ma amɛ a nɔ ɔ mi ɔ, wa hia, nɛ Aristarko, Makedonia no ko nɛ je Tesalonika a piɛ wa he.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Nɛ e nɔ je na a, wa ya da Zidon, nɛ akɛnɛ Yulio hɛɛ Paulo dɔdɔɔdɔ he je ɔ, e ngmɛ lɛ blɔ ke e ya jɔɔ e he.

english_verse: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
translation_verse: Nɛ wa hia ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, wa tsɔ Kipro zugba nɛ wo bɔle lɛ ɔ he, ejakaa wa ngɛ kɔɔhiɔ kpee.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ wa po Kilikia kɛ Pamfilia wo ɔ, wa ba da Mira ngɛ Likia.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛ ɔ na Aleksandria lɛ ko ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ yaa Italia, nɛ e je wɔ ngɔ wo mi.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Wa nyɛɛ blɛoo be saii, nɛ beble loko wa su Knido hanɔ, nɛ akɛnɛ kɔɔhiɔ ɔ ngmɛ́ wɔ blɔ he je ɔ, wa tsɔ Kreta he kɛ ba Salmone.

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: Nɛ beble loko wa po mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba he ko nɛ a tsɛɛ Lɛsimuɔmi he kpakpa nɛ kɛ Lasea ma a he kɛ we ɔ.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Se jeha nɛ ɔ, benɛ wa puɛ be fuu nɛ wo hɛ mi nyɛɛmi ɔ hu pee dengme, ejakaa hwɔhami be ɔ be mo he je ɔ, Paulo wo mɛ ga.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: E ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ, i na kaa dengme gbomi kɛ nihi a hɛ mi kpatami babauu maa ba blɔ hiami nɛ ɔ mi, pi lɛ mi ni ɔmɛ kɛ lɛ ɔ kɛkɛ, se mohu wa wami nitsɛ hulɔ.”

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Se asafoatsɛ ɔ heɔ kudɔɔtsɛ ɔ kɛ lɛtsɛ ɔ yeɔ pe munyu nɛ Paulo ngɛ tue ɔ.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ lɛ si muɔmi he ɔ hi saminya bɔ nɛ a ma nyɛ maa ye fiɛ be ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a ti nihi fuu wo ga ke a hia kɛ je lejɛ ɔ nɛ a hyɛ kaa a ma nyɛ su Foinike nɛ ji Kreta lɛ si muɔmi he nɛ ngɛ leneyi-bonyoku kɛ omleyi-bonyoku kpɛti ɔ lo, konɛ a ya ye fiɛ be ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Wo nɔ kɔɔhiɔ ngua

english_verse: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ leneyi kɔɔhiɔ bɔni fiami blɛoo ɔ, e pee mɛ kaa nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ hlae ɔ ba mi, nɛ a hia kɛ be ngɛ Kreta he tataata.

english_verse: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
translation_verse: Se e kɛ we kɛkɛ nɛ wo nɔ kɔɔhiɔ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ omleyi-beleku kɔɔhiɔ ɔ hia kɛ ba kpee mɛ.

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: Se benɛ kɔɔhiɔ ɔ sɛ lɛ ɔ mi nɛ e nyɛ we nya dami hu ɔ, wa ngmɛɛ he nɛ e fɔ nɔ.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ wa sa fo kɛ tsɔ zugba kpɔ nyafii ko nɛ wo bɔle lɛ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Klaudia, kɔɔhiɔ ya he ɔ he ɔ, dengme kɛ pɔtɔ loko wa nyɛ boto ɔ nu.

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ a wo boto ɔ nɔ ɔ, a kɛ kpahi fi lɛ, nɛ akɛnɛ a ngɛ gbeye yee kaa alinɔ a ma ya nɔ zia mɔsɔ ɔ mi he je ɔ, a gbe abalaa a, nɛ a fɔ́ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Nɛ akɛnɛ wo nɔ kɔɔhiɔ ɔ ngɛ wɔ fiae basabasa wawɛɛ he je ɔ, je na nɔ ɔ, a je lɛ ɔ mi ni ɔmɛ eko ngɔ pue he.

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: Nɛ ligbi nɛ ji ligbi etɛ ɔ waa kɛ wɔ nitsɛmɛ wa ninehi je lɛ ɔ he ni ɔmɛ ngɔ pue he.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Akɛnɛ wa nɛ́ pu loo dodoehi ligbihi fuu, nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu kɔɔhiɔ ɔ nɛ ngɛ fiae ngɛ wɔ kpee ɔ nya wa wawɛɛ he je ɔ, jeha nɛ ɔ wa hɛ̃ bé nɔ kaa wa maa yɛ.

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Se benɛ a yi ni be saii ɔ, Paulo te si da a kpɛti nɛ e ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ, jinɛ e sa kaa nyɛ buɔ mi tue nɛ a ko hia ngɛ Kreta nɛ a ba na kikɛmɛ a dengme kɛ nihi a hɛ mi kpatami nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
translation_verse: Jeha nɛ ɔ hu i ngɛ nyɛ ga woe ke nyɛ na tsui; ejakaa nyɛ ti nɔ ko yi be tae, ja lɛ ɔ kɛkɛ.

english_verse: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
translation_verse: Ejakaa nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, Mawu nɔ nɔ́ nɛ i ji kɛ nɔ hu nɛ i sɔmɔɔ ɔ bɔfo ba da ye kasa nya,

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: nɛ e ke: ‘Koo ye gbeye, Paulo! Ja a kɛ mo ya da Kaisare hɛ mi kɛ̃. Nɛ oʼɛ, Mawu ngɔ nihi kulaa nɛ kɛ mo nyɛɛ lɛ ɔ mi ɔ ngɔ ke mo.’

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ a po osɛkɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ wo wo ɔ mi, nɛ a pɛne kudɔɔ ɔ he kpa amɛ hulɔ, nɛ a wo kpɛti a balaa a kɛ kpee kɔɔhiɔ nɛ ngɛ fiae ɔ, nɛ a plɛ lɛ ɔ yi ngɔ ha wo nya blɔ.

english_verse: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
translation_verse: Se benɛ lɛ mi nitsuli ɔmɛ ngɛ hlae nɛ a tu fo kɛ je lɛ ɔ mi ɔ, a bua nɛ a si boto ɔ ngɔ ma wo ɔ hɛ kaa nɔ́ nɛ pe a yaa fɔ́ osɛkɛhi ngɛ lɛ ɔ yi je.

english_verse: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a ye gbeye kaa alinɔ wa ma ya nɔ tɛ sahi a nɔ, nɛ a fɔ osɛkɛhi eywiɛ ngɛ lɛ ɔ se je, a kɛ ngɛ je nami mlɛe.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Paulo de asafoatsɛ ɔ kɛ aslaafo ɔmɛ ke: “Ke ni nɛ ɔmɛ je lɛ ɔ mi ɔ, lɔ ɔ lɛɛ nyɛ yi be wami nae.”

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ aslaafo ɔmɛ po boto ɔ he kpa amɛ, na a ha e ya nɔ si.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ i kpa nyɛ pɛɛ nɛ nyɛɛ ye ni; ejakaa lɔ ɔ lɛ ma ha nyɛ yi ma na wa, ejakaa nyɛ ti nɔ ko nɔ ko yi bwɔmi kake be e yi mi jee ngɔ nɔ si.”

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ e de jã a e kɛ̃ loo e wo abolo nɛ e na Mawu si ngɛ mɛ kulaa a hɛ mi, nɛ e ku mi nɛ e bɔni yemi.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ mɛ kulaa a na tsui, nɛ mɛ hu a ye ni.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Se benɛ a ye ni nɛ a tɔ ɔ, a sake blɛfo nɛ a wo ɔ ngɔ pue wo ɔ mi, nɛ a ha lɛ ɔ pee huyɛhuyɛ. Lɛ ɔ butumi

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ je na a, a li zugba a, se a na wo nya kɔkɔɔmi he ko kɛ e nya zia, nɛ a to a yi mi kaa, ke a ma nyɛ ɔ, a ma ha lɛ ɔ ya sa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ a ya nɔ wo enyɔ kpe he he je ɔ, a kɛ lɛ ɔ ya sa si; e yi je ɔ ya hɛ si kpɛii, se e supa a, oslɔke ɔmɛ a nyawami ɔ ywia lɛ.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Aslaafo ɔmɛ a yi mi tomi ji kaa a maa gbe pamitsɛmɛ ɔmɛ konɛ a ti nɔ ko nɛ ko sle kɛ ho nɛ e ba tu fo.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ asafoatsɛ ɔ ngɛ hlae nɛ e he Paulo yi wami he je ɔ, e tsi a yi mi tomi ɔ nya, nɛ e fa ke ninɛmɛ nɛ le slemi ɔ kekle a tu ngɔ pue wo ɔ mi, nɛ a ya nu kpo;

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: se ninɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ a ti ni komɛ a bu gbegbelihi a nɔ. Bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Tnɛ kulaa a nu kpo sɔkee ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ wa je mi sɔkee ɔ loko wa ba le kaa zugba kpɔ nɛ wo bɔle lɛ ɔ biɛ ji Melita.

english_verse: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
translation_verse: Lejɛ ɔ tsɛmɛ pee wɔ kpakpa babauu; ejakaa a slɛ la nɛ a he wɔ tsuo kulaa kɛ hɛmuɔ ngɛ hiɔmi nɛmi babauu kɛ fiɛ ɔ he.

english_verse: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
translation_verse: Se benɛ Paulo bua lɛ tsɔwi nya nɛ e kɛ yaa wo la a mi ɔ, sinɔ ko je la gligli ɔ mi mla e nine he.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Se benɛ lejɛ ɔ tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ na lohwe ɔ nɛ mla Paulo nine he ɔ, a de a he ke: “Bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, kikɛmɛ a nyumu nɛ ɔ awiyelɔ ji lɛ, nɛ a he e yi wami kɛ je wo ɔ mi lɛɛ, se lueyemi ngmɛ́ lɛ blɔ nɛ e yi nɛ na wa.”

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Se Paulo huanya lohwe ɔ ngɔ wo la a mi, nɛ e yi lɛ awi ko.

english_verse: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
translation_verse: Se a hɛ ngɛ nɔ kaa e maa fuu loo e maa fia si gbo tlukaa. Se benɛ a hyɛ blɔ hluu nɛ a na kaa nɔ́ ko slɔɔto ko pee we lɛ ɔ, a tsake a juɛmi nɛ a ke mawu ko ji lɛ.

english_verse: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
translation_verse: Jeha nɛ ɔ zugba kpɔ nɛ wo bɔle lɛ ɔ nɔ nɔkɔtɔma nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Publio ɔ ngɛ a bɔɔ ko ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ni ɔmɛ a mi. Lɛ lɛ e he wɔ kɛ hɛmuɔ nɛ e kɛ tsui mi jɔmi pee wɔ nibwɔ ligbi etɛ sɔuu.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Se e ba mi kaa asla kɛ muklii mi pa nu Publio tsɛ kɛ fɔɔ si. Paulo ya e ngɔ, nɛ e sɔle nɛ e ngɔ e ninehi ngɔ pue e nɔ nɛ e tsa lɛ.

english_verse: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
translation_verse: Jeha nɛ ɔ benɛ a pee enɛ ɔ ɔ, ni kpa komɛ hu nɛ ngɛ gboe ngɛ zugba kpɔ nɛ wo bɔle lɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ ba, nɛ a tsa mɛ.

english_verse: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
translation_verse: Nɛ mɛ hu a wo wa hɛ mi nyami babauu, nɛ benɛ wa hia kɛ je lejɛ ɔ, a ha wɔ nihi nɛ hia wɔ. Paulo je Melita kɛ ya Roma

english_verse: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
translation_verse: Hlami etɛ se ɔ wa ya sɛ Aleksandria lɛ ko nɛ e he so ji Dioskurioi nɛ ba ye fiɛ be ɔ ngɛ zugba kpɔ nɛ wo bɔle lɛ ɔnɔ ɔ mi, nɛ wa hia kɛ ho.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ wa ya da si ngɛ Sirakusa a, wa hi lejɛ ɔ ligbi etɛ.

english_verse: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
translation_verse: Nɛ wa je lejɛ ɔ, wa lɔgɔ si kɛ ba Regio; nɛ je na nɔ ɔ, benɛ leneyi kɔɔhiɔ ɔ ba fia a, wa pue nɔ, nɛ ligbi nɛ ji enyɔ ɔ wa su Putueli.

english_verse: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
translation_verse: Wa ba na nyɛmimɛ komɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. A kpa wɔ pɛɛ ke waa kɛ mɛ nɛ hi si ligbi kpaago. Kɛkɛ nɛ wa ba su Roma.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Nɛ benɛ nyɛmimɛ nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nu wa he ɔ, a ba kpee wɔ ngɛ Apiiforo kɛ Tretaberna. Benɛ Paulo na mɛ ɔ e na Mawu si nɛ e na tsui. Paulo ngɛ Roma

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
