translation_verse: Benɛ Isak gbaa Yakob ta, nɛ Yakob je e tsɛ ɔ ngɔ pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ e nyɛmi Esau hu je de dami kɛ ba.

english_verse: He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Lɛ hu e ba pee niye ní nɛ ngɔɔ, nɛ e kɛ ba ha e tsɛ ɔ. E de lɛ ke, “Tsaatsɛ, i kpa mo pɛɛ, tee si nɛ o hi si, nɛ o ye de lo nɛ i kɛ ba a eko, konɛ o gbaa mi.”

english_verse: “Who are you?” Isaac asked. “I am Esau, your first-born son.”
translation_verse: Isak bi lɛ ke, “Mo mɛnɔ?” Esau he nɔ ke, “Imi o bi ɔ; o bitɛte Esau!”

english_verse: Isaac started trembling and said, “Then who brought me some wild meat right before you came in? I ate it and gave him a blessing that cannot be taken back.”
translation_verse: Isak he do blibliibli wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ e bi ke, “Lɛɛ mɛnɔ ji nɔ nɛ ya gbe de lo ɔ nɛ e ngɔ ba ha mi ɔ?” E ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Loko o ba a, i ye ní ɔ tsuo nɛ i gbaa lɛ momo. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, amlɔ nɛ ɔ, gbaami ɔ pee e nɔ́!”

english_verse: Isaac answered, “Your brother tricked me and stole your blessing.”
translation_verse: Se Isak he nɔ ke, “O nyɛmi ɔ ba sisi mi, nɛ e ba he o gbaami ɔ kɛ je.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
translation_verse: Esau de ke, “E biɛ Yakob ɔ di e he, ejakaa enɛ ɔ ji si enyɔ sɔuu nɛ e sisi mi. E he ye bitɛte blɔ nya a momo, nɛ amlɔ nɛ ɔ hu e ba he ye gbaami ɔ! Anɛ o si we gbaami ɔ eko ha we mi lo?”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
translation_verse: Isak he nɔ ke, “I pee lɛ o nyɔmtsɛ momo, nɛ i pee nyɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ tsuo e nyɔguɛhi. I ha lɛ ngma kɛ wai. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ye bi, nɔ́ ko pa be nɛ ma pee ha mo!”

english_verse: “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
translation_verse: Esau bi e tsɛ ɔ ke, “Tsaatsɛ, gbaami kake nɛ ɔ pɛ o ngɛ lo? Tsaatsɛ, moo gbaa imi hulɔ!” Kɛkɛ nɛ Esau wo ya.

english_verse: So his father said: “Your home will be far from that fertile land, where dew comes down from the heavens.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Isak de lɛ ke, “O maa hi zugba nɛ bɛ ní nɔ, Hiɔwe bɔ́ hu be nɛe ha mo.

english_verse: You will live by the power of your sword and be your brother's slave. But when you decide to be free, you will break loose.”
translation_verse: O klaate nɛ o kɛ ma he o yi wami. O ma sɔmɔ o nyɛminyumu ɔ. Se ke o na blɔ ɔ, O ma tsɔ e hɛ mi atuã, Nɛ o maa ye o he.”

english_verse: Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
translation_verse: Esau nyɛ Yakob ngɛ gbaami ɔ nɛ e tsɛ gbaa Yakob ɔ he. E de ngɛ e yi mi ke, “Tsaatsɛ gbenɔ be su ta. Ke tsaatsɛ gbo nɛ a pee ya se ɔ, ma gbe ye nyɛmi Yakob.”

english_verse: When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you.
translation_verse: Benɛ Rebeka nu kaa Esau to e yi mi kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ, e tsɔ ya tsɛ Yakob kɛ ba, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “O nyɛmi Esau to kaa e maa gbe mo nɛ e kɛ ye e he lue.

english_verse: Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ye bi, bu tue! Tuu fo esɔ kɛ ya ye nyɛminyumu Laban ngɔ ngɛ Haran.

english_verse: and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry
translation_verse: Yaa hi e ngɔ bɔɔ kɛ yaa si o nyɛmi ɔ mi mi fumi ɔ nya maa ba si,

english_verse: and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
translation_verse: nɛ e hɛ maa je nɔ́ nɛ o pee lɛ ɔ nɔ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ma tsɔ nɛ a ba ngɔ mo kɛ ba. Mɛni he je ye bimɛ enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo a yi maa ta ligbi kake too?” Isak wo Yakob blɔ kɛ ya ha Laban

english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Rebeka de Isak ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ ma se yiwi nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ Esau ya ngɔ ɔ, a sane ba gbe ye nya. Ke e maa ba mi kaa Yakob hu ma ya ngɔ Hit yihewi nɛ ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko ɔ, lɛɛ afani nɛ ma gbo mohu.”

english_verse: Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said: Don't marry any of those Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Isak tsɛ Yakob, nɛ e gbaa lɛ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Koo ngɔ Kanaan yo.

english_verse: Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translation_verse: Yaa Mesopotamia, esɔ. Yaa o nɛ̃ Betuel we ɔ mi, nɛ o ya ngɔ o tsɛko Laban biyi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake.

english_verse: I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation.
translation_verse: Mawu Ope ɔ nɛ gbaa mo, nɛ e ha mo bimɛ babauu, konɛ o ba pee je mahi babauu a tsɛ.

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: Mawu Ope ɔ nɛ gbaa mo, kɛ o nina kaa bɔ nɛ e gbaa Abraham ɔ, konɛ zugba nɛ ɔ nɛ o ba to nubwɔ ngɛ nɔ ɔ, e ba pee o nɔ́, ejakaa Mawu kɛ zugba a ha Abraham.”

english_verse: Isaac then sent Jacob to stay with Rebekah's brother Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean. Esau Marries the Daughter of Ishmael
translation_verse: Isak wo Yakob blɔ kɛ ho Mesopotamia ya, kɛ ya ha Aram no ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Betuel ɔ binyumu Laban. Laban nyɛmiyo ji Rebeka, Esau kɛ Yakob a nyɛ ɔ. Esau ngɔ yo he

english_verse: Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria
translation_verse: Esau na kaa Isak gbaa Yakob nɛ e wo lɛ blɔ kɛ ho Mesopotamia ya, konɛ e ya ngɔ yo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. E na hu kaa benɛ Isak gbaa Yakob ɔ, e ka lɛ kita ke e ko ngɔ Kanaan yo.

english_verse: and that he had obeyed his father and mother.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, e na kaa Yakob bu e nyɛ kɛ e tsɛ tue, nɛ e ho Mesopotamia ya.

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Esau ba yɔse kaa e tsɛ Isak ɔ sume Kanaan yihi.

english_verse: So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham. Jacob's Dream at Bethel
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e pue nɔ kɛ ho Abraham binyumu Ishmael ngɔ ya, nɛ e ya ngɔ Ishmael biyo Mahalat, Nebayot nyɛmiyo ɔ kɛ piɛ e yi ɔmɛ a he. Yakob nla ngɛ Betel

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Yakob je Beersheba, nɛ e pue blɔ kɛ yaa Haran.

english_verse: At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock.
translation_verse: Benɛ pu nɔ si ɔ, e ya su he ko, nɛ e to si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. E ngɔ tɛ nɛ e tslɔ, nɛ e hwɔ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
translation_verse: E nla nɛ gba he tso ko maa si ngɛ zugba nɛ e yi mi ya pi hiɔwe, nɛ Mawu bɔfohi ngɛ gba he tso ɔ kuɔe nɛ a ngɛ kplee.

english_verse: The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said: I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ ba da si ngɛ e kasa nya, nɛ e de ke, “Imi ji Yawɛ, o nɛ̃ Abraham kɛ o tsɛ Isak a Mawu ɔ. Zugba a nɛ o hwɔɔ si ngɛ nɔ nɛ ɔ, ma ngɔ kɛ ha mo kɛ o nina.

english_verse: Your descendants will spread over the earth in all directions and will become as numerous as the specks of dust. Your family will be a blessing to all people.
translation_verse: O nina maa hiɛ babauu kaa tabo zu. A maa ha zugba a nɔ tsuo kɛ je beleku je kɛ yaa si bonyoku je, jehanɛ kɛ je omleyi je kɛ yaa si leneyi je. Mo, kɛ o nina a nɔ a maa gu kɛ gbaa je ma amɛ tsuo.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I will watch over you, then later I will bring you back to this land. I won't leave you—I will do all I have promised.
translation_verse: I kɛ mo maa hi si. He tsuaa he nɛ o yaa a, ma bu o he, nɛ ma kpale mo kɛ ba zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ ekohu. I be o he jee; ma pee níhi nɛ i wo mo a he si ɔ ha mo kokooko.”

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yakob hɛ tsɛ̃, nɛ e de ke, “Akuanyɛ! Mamoo Yawɛ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, nɛ i li!”

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: E tsui po, nɛ e de ke, “Hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ ngɛ gbeye! Mawu we ji hiɛ ɔ nɛ, tsa pi he kpa ko; hiɔwe agbo ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Yakob te si mɔtu kpla, nɛ e ngɔ tɛ ɔ nɛ e tslɔ ɔ ngɔ ma si kaa kaimi titima. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e plɛ nu ngɔ pue nɔ, nɛ e kɛ pee tɛ ɔ klɔuklɔu ha Mawu.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
translation_verse: E wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Betel, se sa a, a tsɛɛ ma nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ke Luz.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Yakob ka Yawɛ kita ke, “Ke o kɛ mi maa hi si, nɛ o maa bu ye he ngɛ blɔ nɛ i ngɛ hiae nɛ ɔ nɔ, ke o ma ha mi ngma nɛ ma ye, kɛ tade nɛ ma wo;

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: ke o maa kpale mi kɛ ba tsaatsɛ we ɔ mi fiafiaafia ekohu ɔ, lɛɛ mo Yawɛ, o maa pee ye Mawu.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Tlukaa a, e ya pã vu ko nɔ ngɛ nga a nɔ, nɛ to kuu etɛ hwɔɔ si kɛ bɔle vu ɔ. Jamɛ a vu ɔ mi nɛ a yɛɛ nyu ngɛ kɛ haa tohi nɛ a nuɔ, nɛ tɛ agbo ko ngɛ vu ɔ nya.

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: Ke to ɔmɛ tsuo ba bua a he nya ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, to hyɛli ɔmɛ ma kpɛne tɛ ɔ kɛ je vu ɔ nya nɛ a ma ha to ɔmɛ nyu. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a ma kpɛne tɛ ɔ kɛ ya to e blɔ he ekohu.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Yakob bi to hyɛli ɔmɛ ke, “Ye nyɛmimɛ, jije nyɛ je?” A he nɔ ke, “Wa je Haran.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: E bi mɛ ekohu ke, “Anɛ nyɛ le Nahor binyumu Laban lo?” A he nɔ ke, “Ee, wa le lɛ.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: E pa bi mɛ ke, “E ngɛ saminya lo?” A he nɔ ke, “Ee, e ngɛ saminya. Hyɛ, e biyo Rahel nɛ kpaka e to ɔmɛ kɛ ma a nɛ!”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Yakob de mɛ ke, “Je jɔɛ lolo; e sui be nɛ a maa wo lohwe ɔmɛ tsu mi. Nyɛ ha to ɔmɛ nyu nɛ a nu, nɛ nyɛɛ kpale mɛ kɛ ho nɛ a ya ye ní.”

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: To hyɛli ɔmɛ he nɔ ke, “Dɛbi, wa be nyɛe maa pee ja, ja to ɔmɛ tsuo ba bua a he nya ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, nɛ a kpɛne tɛ ɔ kɛ je vu ɔ nya, loko wa ma ha mɛ nyu.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob kɛ mɛ ngɛ munyu tue kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ, Rahel ba su lejɛ ɔ kɛ e tsɛ to ɔmɛ; ejakaa lɛ ji nɔ nɛ hyɛɛ to ɔmɛ.

english_verse: When Jacob saw her and his uncle's sheep, he rolled the rock away and watered the sheep.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob na Rahel kɛ e tsɛko Laban to ɔmɛ ɔ, e ya kpɛne tɛ ɔ kɛ je vu ɔ nya nɛ e ha to ɔmɛ nyu.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e fua Rahel atuu, nɛ e kɛ bua jɔmi fo ya pue e nɔ.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: E de Rahel ke, “Ye nyɛmi ji mo; o tsɛ nyɛmiyo Rebeka a, e bi ji mi.” Rahel tu fo kɛ ho nɛ e ya bɔ e tsɛ amaniɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Benɛ Laban nu e wɔfase Yakob he ɔ, e tu fo ya kpee lɛ, nɛ e pee lɛ atuu; e fiɔ e nya he, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ba we mi. Benɛ Yakob bɔ Laban nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ba a,

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: Laban de ke, “Niinɛ, imi nitsɛ ye nyɛmi tutuutu ji mo!” Yakob hi Laban ngɔ hlami kake. Yakob sɔmɔ Laban

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Laban de Yakob ke, “E ngɛ mi kaa o weku no ji mi lɛɛ, se e sɛ kaa o tsuɔ ní kɛ haa mi yaka. Tsɔɔ mi hiɔwo nɛ o ngɛ hlae.”

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Lea hɛngmɛ ngɛ fɛu saminyayoo, se Rahel lɛɛ e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ kɛ e nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ hi kɛ pi si; e he ngɛ fɛu saminya.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Akɛnɛ Yakob suɔ Rahel he je ɔ, e de Laban ke, “Ma tsu ní ha mo jeha kpaago konɛ o kɛ Rahel, o bi wayo ɔ ha mi nɛ ma ngɔ.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Laban he nɔ ke, “Saminya! I suɔ kaa i kɛ lɛ ma ha mo pe kaa i kɛ lɛ ma ha nɔ kpa ko. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, moo hi ye ngɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Yakob tsu ní jeha kpaago konɛ e kɛ na he blɔ nɛ e ngɔ Rahel. Se suɔmi nɛ e ngɛ kɛ ha Rahel he je ɔ, jeha kpaago ɔ be nɛ e pee lɛ kaa ligbi bɔɔ kɛkɛ.

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Laban ngmɛ okplɔɔ agbo, nɛ e kpee nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba ní yemi ɔ.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Se jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Laban kɛ e bi Lea mohu ba ha Yakob, nɛ e kɛ lɛ hwɔ.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Yakob li kaa mamoo Lea mohu e kɛ hwɔ si ɔ, kɛ ya si mɔtu. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e bi Laban ke, “Mɛni o pee mi nɛ ɔ? Anɛ i tsu we ní ha we mo konɛ ma ngɔ Rahel lo? Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ o sisi mi?”

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Laban he nɔ ke, “Wa hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ kusumi ngmɛ́ blɔ ja; a ha we jokuɛyo gba be mi nɛ nɔkɔtɔma gba we lolo.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Mlɛ kɛ yaa si ayɛflo he nyami otsi ɔ maa be. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ke o maa wo si kaa o ma tsu ní ha mi jeha kpaago kpa kɛ piɛ he ɔ, i kɛ Rahel hu ma ha mo.”

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Yakob kɛ Rahel hu na bɔmi, nɛ e suɔ lɛ kulaa pe Lea. Yakob tsu ní ha Laban jeha kpaago kɛ piɛ he. Yakob bimɛ

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yawɛ na kaa Yakob sume Lea kaa bɔ nɛ e suɔ Rahel ɔ, e ha Lea fɔ bimɛ; se Rahel pee yosa.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Lea ba na mi nɛ e fɔ binyumu. E wo lɛ biɛ ke Ruben, nɛ e de ke, “Yawɛ na ye we amanehlu ɔ; jehanɛ lɛɛ ye huno ɔ maa suɔ mi.”

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Lea ba na mi ekohu, nɛ e fɔ binyumu. E wo lɛ biɛ ke Simeon, nɛ e de ke, “Yawɛ nu kaa a sume mi, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e ha mi binyumu nɛ ɔ hulɔ.”

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Lea ba na mi ekohu, nɛ e fɔ binyumu. E wo lɛ biɛ ke Levi, nɛ e de ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ ye huno ɔ kɛ e he maa mɛtɛ ye he kpɛii, ejakaa i fɔ binyumuhi etɛ ha lɛ.”

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Benɛ Rahel na kaa e fɔ we ha Yakob ɔ, e hɛ kɔ̃ e nyɛmiyo ɔ nɔ, nɛ e de Yakob ke, “Ha mi bimɛ, ke pi ja a, ma gbo.”

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Yakob mi mi fu lɛ wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ e bi lɛ ke, “Anɛ Mawu ji mi lo? Lɛ ji nɔ nɛ tsi o fɔmi nya a nɛ.”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Rahel he nɔ ke, “Hyɛ, ye mawayo Bilha ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; o kɛ lɛ nɛ hwɔ, nɛ e fɔ ha mi, konɛ imi hu ma na bimɛ kɛ gu e nɔ.”

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Bilha ba na mi nɛ e fɔ binyumu ha Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Rahel wo lɛ biɛ ke Dan, nɛ e de ke, “Mawu wo mi nguɔ. E nu ye kue fami ɔ, nɛ e ha mi binyumu.”

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Bilha ba na mi ekohu, nɛ e fɔ binyumu enyɔne ha Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Rahel wo lɛ biɛ ke Naftali, nɛ e de ke, “I kɛ wa wenyɛ ɔ hwu ta nɛ nya wa, nɛ i ye e nɔ.”

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Benɛ Lea na kaa e fɔmi se po ɔ, e kɛ e mawayo Zilpa ha Yakob kaa e yo,

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: nɛ Yakob kɛ lɛ fɔ binyumu.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Lea wo lɛ biɛ ke Gad, nɛ e de ke, “Ye he ba ní pɛ!”

english_verse: When they had another son,
translation_verse: Zilpa fɔ binyumu enyɔne ha Yakob.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Lea wo lɛ biɛ ke Asher, nɛ e de ke, “Hyɛ bɔ nɛ ye bua jɔ ha! Yi kpa amɛ ma de ke a gbaa mi saminya.”

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Ligbi ko, benɛ a ngɛ ngma kpae ɔ, Ruben ya na suɔmi tso yiblii komɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ, nɛ e ngɔ kɛ ba ha e nyɛ Lea. Rahel de Lea ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, ha mi suɔmi tso yiblii nɛ o bi ɔ kɛ ba a eko.”

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Lea he nɔ ke, “Nɛ o kpɔ ye huno ɔ ngɛ ye dɛ ɔ, lɔ ɔ pi ha mo lolo? Ye bi ɔ suɔmi tso yiblii nɛ ɔ hu o ma kpɔ lo?” Rahel de lɛ ke, “Ha mi o bi ɔ suɔmi tso yiblii ɔ, konɛ Yakob kɛ mo nɛ hwɔ nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Gbɔkuɛ nya si benɛ Yakob je ngmɔ mi kɛ ma a, Lea je kpo ya kpee lɛ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ma hwɔ o ngɔ mwɔnɛ ɔ, ejakaa i kɛ suɔmi tso yiblii ɔ nɛ ye bi ɔ kɛ ba a wo he hiɔ.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yakob kɛ lɛ na bɔmi jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Mawu bu Lea kue fami ɔ tue, nɛ e ba na mi, nɛ e kɛ Yakob fɔ binyumu enuɔne.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Lea wo lɛ biɛ ke Isakar, nɛ e de ke, “I kɛ ye mawayo ɔ ha ye huno, nɛ Mawu wo mi hiɔ.”

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: E wo lɛ biɛ ke Zebulun, nɛ e de ke, “Mawu ke mi nɔ́ kpakpa ko. Jehanɛ lɛɛ ye huno kɛ mi maa hi si saminya, ejakaa i kɛ lɛ fɔ binyumuhi ekpa.”

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, e fɔ biyo nɛ e wo lɛ biɛ ke Dina.

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Benɛ a fɔ Yosef se ɔ, Yakob de Laban ke, “Wo mi blɔ konɛ ma kpale kɛ ho ye je he, kɛ ye zugba nɔ ya.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Ye yi ɔmɛ kɛ ye bimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ i tsu ní ha mo nɛ i kɛ na mɛ ɔ, ngɔɔ mɛ ngɔ ha mi nɛ ma ho. Mo nitsɛ o le kaa i sɔmɔ mo saminya.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Yakob he nɔ ke, “Mo nitsɛ o le bɔ nɛ i sɔmɔ mo, kɛ bɔ nɛ i hyɛ o lohwe ɔmɛ.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Benɛ i ba a, lohwe bɔɔ pɛ o ngɛ. Se amlɔ nɛ ɔ lohwe ɔmɛ bɔ, nɛ a he hiɛ babauu; Yawɛ gu ye nɔ nɛ e kɛ gbaa mo babauu. Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, e su be nɛ ma to blɔ nya kɛ ha imi nitsɛ ye we ɔ.”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Laban bi lɛ ke, “Nyɛmɛ ma ha mo?” Yakob he nɔ ke, “I hla we hiɔwo ko. Ke o maa pee nɔ́ nɛ ma bi mo nɛ ɔ ha mi ɔ, lɛɛ ma tsa nɔ ma hyɛ o to ɔmɛ ha mo.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Ngmɛɛ mi blɔ nɛ ma ya kpa o to ɔmɛ tsuo a mi mwɔnɛ ɔ, nɛ ma ngɔ jijɔ yumu tsuaa jijɔ yumu, kɛ apletsi bi tsuaa apletsi bi nɛ e he ngɛ huatahuata, loo a tsɔɔtsɔɔ e he. Hiɔwo pɛ nɛ i ngɛ hlae ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Pee se, ke o ma ye hiɔwo ɔ bumi ɔ, o maa na kaa i ye mo anɔkuale, loo i sisi mo. Ke o ba na akpakpo ko nɛ e he be huatahuata nɛ a tsɔɔtsɔɔ we e he hulɔ, aloo jijɔ ko nɛ yu we ɔ, lɛɛ o le kaa imi nɛ i ju lɛ.”

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Laban he nɔ ke, “Saminya! Wa maa pee kaa bɔ nɛ o de ɔ.”

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: nɛ e kɛ mɛ kɛ lohwe ɔmɛ je Yakob he, nɛ e nyɛɛ ligbi etɛ. Yakob hyɛ Laban lohwe kpa amɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Yakob ya po tso kɔnihi kɛ je tso slɔɔto etɛ a he. E ngmla tso toto ɔ ngɛ he komɛ, nɛ futaa je si ngɛ tso kɔni ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: E ngɔ tso kɔnihi nɛ e ngmla a he ɔ ba pue to nyu numi ní ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ to ɔmɛ a hɛ mi. E ngɔ mɛ ba pue lejɛ ɔ, ejakaa ke to ɔmɛ ba nyu numi ɔ, a kuɔɔ a he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Yakob je jijɔ ɔmɛ kɛ je apletsi ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e ha nɛ a plɛ a hɛ mi ngɔ kpee Laban to huatahuata amɛ, kɛ yumuyumu ɔmɛ. Bɔ nɛ Yakob pee nɛ e kɛ na lɛ nitsɛ e to tsu ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; e kɛ e to ɔmɛ futuu we Laban ní ɔmɛ.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Ke lohwe ɔmɛ be he wami kpakpa ko ɔ, lɛɛ Yakob kɛ tso kɔni ɔmɛ be a hɛ mi fɔe. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, lohwe wudɔwudɔ ɔmɛ ba pee Laban níhi, nɛ ní nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ he wami saminya a ba pee Yakob níhi.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Blɔ nɔ nɛ Yakob gu nɛ e kɛ na ní kpɔtɔɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. E na tohi, nyɔguɛhi, afukpɔngɔhi, kɛ tejihi babauu.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Yakob nu kaa Laban bimɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ dee ke, “Yakob kpɔ wa tsɛ weto ní tsuo ngɛ e dɛ, nɛ e kɛ na e he.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Yakob yɔse kaa Laban tsɔ we e hɛ mi ha we lɛ hu kaa sa a.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de Yakob ke, “Kpale o se kɛ ho o weku li a ngɔ ya, ngɛ o tsɛmɛ a zugba a nɔ. I kɛ mo maa hi si.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Yakob tsɔ ya de Rahel kɛ Lea ke a kɛ lɛ ba kpe ngɛ nga a nɔ, he nɛ e to ɔmɛ ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: E de mɛ ke, “I na kaa nyɛ tsɛ tsɔ we e hɛ mi ha we mi hu kaa sa a; se tsaatsɛ e Mawu ɔ kɛ mi ngɛ.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Nyɛ tsuo nyɛ le kaa i tsu ní ha nyɛ tsɛ kɛ ye he wami tsuo.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: Nyɛ tsɛ sisi mi, nɛ e tsake ye hiɔwo ɔ si nyɔngma. Se Mawu ngmɛ́ lɛ blɔ nɛ e pee mi yayami ko.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: Be tsuaa be nɛ Laban ma de ke, ‘A kɛ lohwehi kɛ a he huatahuata maa wo mo hiɔ’ ɔ, kɛkɛ jijɔ ɔmɛ tsuo fɔ bimɛ kɛ a he huatahuata.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Mawu pee nɛ e kɛ kpɔ nyɛ tsɛ lohwe ɔmɛ kɛ ha mi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Imi ji Mawu ɔ nɛ je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ mo ngɛ Betel ɔ nɛ. Lejɛ ɔ o pɔ tɛ ko nu ngɛ; lejɛ ɔ nɔuu lɛ o ka mi kita ngɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, dla nɛ o kpale o se esɔ kɛ ya zugba a nɔ he nɛ a fɔ mo ngɛ ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: E buu wɔ kaa ma se yihi. E jua wɔ, nɛ wa yi ní ɔ hu e ye ta!

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Níhi tsuo nɛ Mawu kpɔ ngɛ wa tsɛ dɛ ɔ ma ba pee waa kɛ wa bimɛ wa nɔ́. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Mawu de mo ke o pee ɔ, pee.”

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, Laban ho e to ɔmɛ a he bwɔmi sami ya; nɛ benɛ e be we ɔ mi ɔ, Rahel ju e tsɛ wɔ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: long years to earn your two daughters and another
translation_verse: Yakob sisi Laban, Aram no ɔ; e ha we nɛ Laban nɛ le kaa e yaa.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: Yakob ngɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ e dɛ ɔ kɛ tu fo. E po Yufrate pa a, nɛ e pue nɔ kɛ yaa Gilead yo ɔ he. Laban nyɛɛ Yakob se

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Ligbi etɛne ɔ nɔ ɔ, nɔ ko ya de Laban ke Yakob tu fo.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Laban ngɔ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ piɛ e he, nɛ a nyɛɛ Yakob se ligbi kpaago kɛ ya si a ya na lɛ ngɛ Gilead yo ɔ he.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Mawu je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ Laban, Aram no ɔ ngɛ nlami je, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Hyɛ nɛ hi nɛ o kɛ Yakob ko tu munyu ko; yaya jio, kpakpa jio.”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Benɛ Laban ya na Yakob ɔ, Yakob ma e bo tsu ɔ ngɛ yo ɔ he, nɛ lɛ, Laban ɔ lɛɛ e kɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ma a bo tsu ɔ ngɛ Gilead yo ɔ he.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Laban de Yakob ke, “Mɛni ji nɔ́ nɛ o pee mi nɛ ɔ? O ngɔ ye biyi ɔmɛ kɛ tu fo kɛ yaa kaa nyɔguɛhi nɛ a nuu mɛ ngɛ ta mi.

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Mɛni he je o sisi mi, nɛ o ku kɛ je nigii nɛ o de we mi ɔ? Kaa o de mi jinɛ tse i kɛ bua jɔmi, kɛ la, kɛ miɛ, kɛ saku ba je mo blɔ!

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: O ha we po nɛ i kɛ ye bibi ɔmɛ, kɛ ye biyi ɔmɛ nɛ ye sɛ. O ye kuasiahi a sane.

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: Jinɛ i ngɛ he wami nɛ ma nyɛ pee mo yayami, se hiɛ nyɔ mi ɔ, o tsɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ bɔ mi kɔkɔ ke i kɛ mo ko tu munyu yaya ko.

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: I le kaa o hɛ ngɛ jae ngɛ we he, nɛ lɔ ɔ he o je ɔ nɛ. Se mɛni he je o ju ye wɔ ɔmɛ kɛ je?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Yakob he nɔ ke, “I ya ye gbeye; i susu kaa o ma kpɔ o biyi ɔmɛ ngɛ ye dɛ pani nya.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: O wɔ ɔmɛ lɛɛ ke o na mɛ ngɛ wa ti nɔ ko dɛ ngɛ hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ, ja a gbe lɛ. Ngɛ wa nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi ɔ, tsɔɔ mi o nɔ́ ko nɛ ba je ye dɛ, konɛ o ngɔ.” Se Yakob li tete kaa Rahel ju Laban wɔ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Laban ya hla e wɔ ɔmɛ ngɛ Yakob, kɛ Lea, kɛ mawayi enyɔ ɔmɛ a bo tsu ɔmɛ a mi, se e nɛ. Kɛkɛ nɛ e ya sɛ Rahel bo tsu ɔ mi.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Rahel ji nɔ nɛ ju wɔ ɔmɛ; e kɛ wɔ ɔmɛ wo e we afukpɔngɔ ɔ se kotoku ɔ mi, nɛ e hi nɔ. Laban hla wɔ ɔmɛ kɛ kpa bo tsu ɔ mi tsuo, se e nɛ.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Rahel de e tsɛ ɔ ke, “Tsaatsɛ, o mi mi ko fu mi kaa i ti si ha we mo; i je mi.” Laban hla wɔ ɔmɛ kɛ kpa bo tsu ɔ mi, se e nɛ.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Jehanɛ lɛɛ Yakob tsui ba, nɛ e kɛ abofu de Laban ke, “Mɛni yayami i pee? Mɛni mlaa i tɔ, loko o hɛ dɔ kɛ nyɛɛ ye se kikɛ nɛ ɔ?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: O kpa ye níhi tsuo a mi. Mɛni ji nɔ́ nɛ o na nɛ ji o nɔ́ ngɛ ní ɔmɛ a kpɛti? Je lɛ kpo kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ, ngɛ ye nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ mo hu o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ a kojo i kɛ mo.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Ke lohwe awi yeli ba tsɔtslɔɔ jijɔ ko mi ɔ, hiɔ ɔ peeɔ ye nɔ́ nɛ i woɔ; i kɛ lohwe gbogboe ko ba tsɔɔ we mo hyɛ. Ke a ju nɔ́ ko, piani jio, nyɔ mi jio, o haa nɛ i woɔ mo hiɔ sisiisi.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Latsa tsaa mi piani, nɛ fĩɛ yee mi nyɔ mi; nɛ be komɛ ɔ, mahe jee ye hɛ mi.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Ke pi nɛnɛ Abraham, kɛ tsaatsɛ Isak a Mawu ɔ nɛ e kɛ mi ngɛ ɔ, jinɛ o wo mi blɔ dɛ gu kɛ je momo. Se Mawu na ye nɔ́ nami ɔ, kɛ ní tsumi kpakpataa nɛ i tsu ɔ; enɛ ɔ he je nɛ e ka o hɛ mi hiɛ nyɔ mi ɔ nɛ.” Yakob kɛ Laban so

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Laban he nɔ nɛ e de Yakob ke, “Yihewi nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, ye bimɛ ji mɛ; a bimɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, ye bimɛ ji mɛ, nɛ to nɛ ɔmɛ hu ye níhi ji mɛ. Anɔkuale mi ɔ, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ hyɛe ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, ye níhi ji mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ. Se akɛnɛ i be nyɛe ma tsi ye biyi ɔmɛ, kɛ a bimɛ ɔmɛ a nya he je ɔ,

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: ha nɛ i kɛ mo waa so. Ha nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ nɛ pee odase ngɛ i kɛ mo wa kpɛti.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yakob ya wo tɛ ba ma si kaa kaimi nɔ́.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: E fa e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke a bua tɛhi a nya nɛ a to glekuglekuu. Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, a ye ní ngɛ tɛhi nɛ a to glekuglekuu ɔ a kasa nya ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Yegar Sahaduta; se Yakob lɛɛ e wo lɛ ke Galeed.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban de Yakob ke, “Kikɛmɛ a tɛ kuu nɛ ɔ maa pee odase nɔ́ ha wɔ ni enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo.” Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ a wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Galeed ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Laban hu de Yakob ke, “Be mi nɛ i kɛ mo wa mi gba a, Yawɛ nɛ bu wa he.” Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ kpa ke Mizpa.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Laban ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Ke o ya wa ye biyi ɔmɛ yi mi, aloo o ya ngɔ yi kpa komɛ ngɔ piɛ a he nɛ i li po ɔ, kai kaa Mawu ji imi kɛ mo wa we odase.

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Tɛ kuu nɛ ɔ, kɛ kaimi tɛ nɛ ɔ ji odasehi. I be tɛ kuu nɛ ɔ he bee gblegbleegble kɛ ba tua mo. Ja nɔuu, mo hu o ko be tɛ kuu nɛ ɔ, loo kaimi tɛ nɛ ɔ he kɔkɔɔkɔ kɛ ba tua mi.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Abraham kɛ Nahor a Mawu ɔ nɛ ji a tsɛ ɔ Mawu ɔ maa kojo imi kɛ mo wa kpɛti.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Yakob ngɔ Mawu nɛ e tsɛ Isak jaa lɛ ɔ biɛ kɛ ka kita kaa e maa ye si womi nɛ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Yakob gbe lohwe nɛ e kɛ sã bɔ ngɛ yoku ɔ nɔ. E tsɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ní yemi; benɛ a ye ní ɔ gbe nya a, a hi yoku ɔ nɔ nyɔ ɔ mi tsuo.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Makɛ mla a, Laban fiɔ e bibimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ e biyi ɔmɛ a nya he, nɛ e gbaa mɛ, nɛ e kpale e se kɛ ho e ma mi ya.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ yaa a, e kɛ Mawu bɔfo komɛ kpe.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob na mɛ ɔ, e de ke, “Mawu hi he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ;” lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Mahanaim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Yakob tsɔ nihi kɛ sɛ e hlami kɛ ho e nyɛmi Esau ngɔ ya ngɛ Edom zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: I ngɛ na, teji, to, kɛ nyɔguɛhi nyumuhi kɛ yihi. Ye nyɔmtsɛ, i tsɔ tsɔli nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a ba ha nɛ o le kaa i ma we; i heɔ yeɔ kaa o ma he mi atuu.”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Benɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ kpale a se kɛ ba Yakob ngɔ ɔ, a de lɛ ke, “Wa ya na o nyɛmi Esau ɔ, nɛ lɛ hu e kɛ nihi lafa eywiɛ ma nɛ a ba kpee mo.”

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: E de ngɛ e yi mi ke, “Ke Esau ba tua kuu kake ɔ, kuu enyɔne ɔ maa tu fo kɛ je.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yakob fa kue ha Mawu ke, “Mawu lee! Nɛnɛ Abraham Mawu, kɛ tsaatsɛ Isak Mawu! Yawɛ, mo lɛ o de mi ke ma kpale ye se kɛ ba ye zugba nɔ, ngɛ ye weku li a ngɔ, nɛ o maa pee mi saminya.

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o je mi kɛ je ye nyɛmi Esau dɛ mi. I ngɛ gbeye yee kaa e ma ba tua wɔ nɛ e ma kpata waa kɛ wa yi ɔmɛ, kɛ wa bimɛ ɔmɛ tsuo wa hɛ mi.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Kai kaa mo lɛ o wo mi si ke o maa pee mi saminya. Kai kaa mo lɛ o de ke o ma ha mi nina babauu kaa wo nya zia, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be nyɛe maa kane.”

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: Nyɛ hɛ nɛ hi nɔ nɛ nyɛ de lɛ ke, ‘O tsɔlɔ Yakob ngɛ wa se kɛ ma’ ” Yakob de ngɛ e yi mi ke, “I kɛ nike ní nɛ sɛ hlami ɔ ma kpata lɛ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ke i kɛ lɛ kpe hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi ɔ, eko ɔ, e kɛ ye tɔmi maa ke mi.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Yakob wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Peniel, nɛ e de ke, “I wo kikɛmɛ a biɛ nɛ ɔ, ejakaa i na Mawu hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi, se i gbo we.”

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: E de tsɔlɔ ɔ nɛ sɛ hlami ɔ ke, “Ke o kɛ ye nyɛmi Esau kpe, nɛ e bi mo ke, ‘Mɛnɔ ji o nyɔmtsɛ? Jije o yaa? Lohwe nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ nyɛɛ o hɛ mi ɔ, mɛnɔ lohwehi?’ ɔ,

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”
translation_verse: de lɛ ke, ‘Lohwehi nɛ o tsɔlɔ Yakob tsɔ nɛ a kɛ ba ke mo, e nyɔmtsɛ Esau ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. Yakob nitsɛ ngɛ se kɛ ma.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: Yakob de tsɔlɔ enyɔne ɔ, etɛne ɔ, kɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ ngɛ lohwe ɔmɛ a nya a hu ke, “Ke nyɛɛ kɛ Esau kpe ɔ, bɔ nɛ nyɛ ma de lɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Yakob kɛ nike ní ɔ mane, se lɛ nitsɛ lɛɛ e hwɔ sito he ɔ jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi. Yakob kɛ nɔ ko fia atlibo ngɛ Peniel

english_verse: Jacob got up in the middle of the night and took his wives, his eleven children, and everything he owned across to the other side of the Jabbok River for safety.
translation_verse: Benɛ e kɛ mɛ po pa a ta a, e ngɔ e níhi tsuo hu kɛ po pa a,

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: nɛ e ba piɛ lɛ Yakob ɔ nɔ kake ngmelu ngɛ se. Kɛkɛ nɛ nyumu ko kɛ lɛ ba fia atlibo kɛ ya si makɛ.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Benɛ nyumu ɔ na kaa e nyɛ we Yakob ɔ, e fia Yakob mlɛ mi nɔ́, nɛ Yakob gbongu huã.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ de Yakob ke, “Ngmɛɛ ye he nɛ ma ho; je ngɛ mi nae!” Yakob he nɔ ke, “I be hae nɛ o ya, ja o gbaa mi lolo!”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Kɛ a tsɛɛ mo kɛɛ?” Yakob he nɔ ke, “Ye biɛ ji Yakob.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ de lɛ ke, “A be o biɛ tsɛe ke Yakob hu. O kɛ Mawu kɛ nimlihi nɔ kunɔ, nɛ o ye kunimi; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, jehanɛ a ma tsɛ mo ke Israel.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Yakob de nyumu ɔ ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ moo tsɔɔ mi o biɛ.” Se nyumu ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he je o ngɛ hlae nɛ o le ye biɛ ɔ? Kɛkɛ nɛ e gbaa Yakob.”

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob je Peniel ɔ, pu gba; nɛ e gbongu ɔ nɛ huã he je ɔ, e nyɛ we nɛ e nyɛɛ tutuutu.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.

translation_verse: Yakob de tsɔlɔ enyɔne ɔ, etɛne ɔ, kɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ ngɛ lohwe ɔmɛ a nya a hu ke, “Ke nyɛɛ kɛ Esau kpe ɔ, bɔ nɛ nyɛ ma de lɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Yakob kɛ nike ní ɔ mane, se lɛ nitsɛ lɛɛ e hwɔ sito he ɔ jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi. Yakob kɛ nɔ ko fia atlibo ngɛ Peniel

english_verse: Jacob got up in the middle of the night and took his wives, his eleven children, and everything he owned across to the other side of the Jabbok River for safety.
translation_verse: Benɛ e kɛ mɛ po pa a ta a, e ngɔ e níhi tsuo hu kɛ po pa a,

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: nɛ e ba piɛ lɛ Yakob ɔ nɔ kake ngmelu ngɛ se. Kɛkɛ nɛ nyumu ko kɛ lɛ ba fia atlibo kɛ ya si makɛ.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Benɛ nyumu ɔ na kaa e nyɛ we Yakob ɔ, e fia Yakob mlɛ mi nɔ́, nɛ Yakob gbongu huã.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ de Yakob ke, “Ngmɛɛ ye he nɛ ma ho; je ngɛ mi nae!” Yakob he nɔ ke, “I be hae nɛ o ya, ja o gbaa mi lolo!”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Kɛ a tsɛɛ mo kɛɛ?” Yakob he nɔ ke, “Ye biɛ ji Yakob.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ de lɛ ke, “A be o biɛ tsɛe ke Yakob hu. O kɛ Mawu kɛ nimlihi nɔ kunɔ, nɛ o ye kunimi; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, jehanɛ a ma tsɛ mo ke Israel.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Yakob de nyumu ɔ ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ moo tsɔɔ mi o biɛ.” Se nyumu ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he je o ngɛ hlae nɛ o le ye biɛ ɔ? Kɛkɛ nɛ e gbaa Yakob.”

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob je Peniel ɔ, pu gba; nɛ e gbongu ɔ nɛ huã he je ɔ, e nyɛ we nɛ e nyɛɛ tutuutu.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ, Israel bi yi lo nɛ ngɛ mlɛ mi tsami he ɔ, ejakaa Yakob mlɛ mi tsami he ɔ ji he nɛ nyumu ɔ fia nɔ́ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph.
translation_verse: E ngɔ mawayi ɔmɛ kɛ a bimɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ to hɛ mi. Lea kɛ e bimɛ ɔmɛ nyɛɛ se, nɛ nyagbe ɔ, Rahel kɛ Yosef ba.

english_verse: Jacob himself walked in front of them all, bowing to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
translation_verse: Yakob nitsɛ lɛɛ e sɛ hlami, nɛ benɛ e kɛ e nyɛmi ɔ maa ho buami ya a, e kpla si nɛ e kɛ e hɛ mi bu si si kpaago.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Se Esau tu fo ba kpee Yakob nɛ e fua lɛ atuu. E kɛ e nine fɔ e kuɛ mi, nɛ e fiɔ e nya he, nɛ a fo ya.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Esau na yi ɔmɛ kɛ jokuɛwi ɔmɛ ɔ, e bi ke, “Mɛnɔmɛ o kɛ nyɛɛ ɔ?” Yakob he nɔ ke, “Bimɛ nɛ Mawu kɛ dloo imi, o tsɔlɔ ɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ mawayi ɔmɛ kɛ a bimɛ ɔmɛ hɛ mɛ kɛ ba, nɛ a ba kpla si.

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
translation_verse: Lea kɛ e bimɛ ɔmɛ hu ba, nɛ a ba kpla si. Nyagbe ɔ, Yosef kɛ Rahel hu ba, nɛ a ba kpla si ja nɔuu.

english_verse: Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?” “Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Esau bi ke, “Lohwe kuukuu nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ i kɛ kpe ɔ, kɛ ji e sisi kɛɛ?” Yakob he nɔ ke, “Nike ní nɛ i kɛ ma mo, ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kpatami ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Se Esau de lɛ ke, “Ye nyɛmi, nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ ɔ hiɛ; ha nɛ enɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a hi si ha mo.”

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Yakob he nɔ ke, “Dɛbi! I kpa mo pɛɛ, ke o kɛ ye tɔmi pa mi ɔ, lɛɛ mo he ye nike ní nɛ ɔmɛ. Anɔkuale mi ɔ, nɛ i na o hɛ mi ɔ, e ngɛ kaa nɔ́ nɛ i na Mawu nitsɛ hɛ mi; ejakaa o ná ye he tsui, nɛ o he mi atuu.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o he nike ní nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ i ngɔ ba ha mo ɔ; Mawu nɛ na mi mɔbɔ, nɛ e ha mi nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ hia mi.” Kikɛ nɛ ɔ Yakob hao Esau hluu kɛ ya si Esau kplɛɛ nɛ e he nike ní ɔmɛ.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Esau de Yakob ke, “Ha waa ho; ma sɛ o hlami.”

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Yakob he nɔ ke, “Ye nyɔmtsɛ, mo nitsɛ o na kaa jokuɛwi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi fa we lolo. Jehanɛ hu, tohi kɛ nahi nɛ a bimɛ ji nyɔ nya lolo ɔ hu a he ní tsumi fɔɔ si ngɛ ye kuɛ nɔ. Ke a ha nɛ a nyɛɛ tsɔ pe nine ligbi kake po ɔ, lohwe ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ ma gbo.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, ye nyɔmtsɛ, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o sɛ hlami; i kɛ lohwe ɔmɛ kɛ jokuɛwi ɔmɛ maa hi nyɛɛe blɛuublɛuu kɛ yaa si wa ma ba na mo ngɛ Edom.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Esau de lɛ ke, “Saminya! Lɛɛ ma si ye we bi ɔmɛ ekomɛ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ nɛ a tsɔɔ nyɛ blɔ.” Se Yakob he nɔ ke, “Oo! E he hia we! Ke ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ na ye he tsui kɛkɛ ɔ, lɔ ɔ hiɛ.”

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Se Yakob lɛɛ e pue nɔ kɛ ho Sukot ya. E ya po we ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e ma tsu ha e lohwe ɔmɛ hulɔ. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Sukot.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Yakob kpale e se kɛ je Mesopotamia kɛ ba Shekem ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ fiafiaafia, nɛ e ba ma e bo tsu ɔmɛ ngɛ zugba ko nɔ, ngɛ ma a nya.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: E he jamɛ a zugba a ngɛ Shekem tsɛ Hamor dɛ kɛ sika hiɔ yi lafa. Hamor ji nɔ nɛ to Shekem ma a sisi.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Yakob ma bɔ sami la tɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e kɛ Israel Mawu ɔ biɛ wo lɛ.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Lea biyo ɔ nɛ e kɛ Yakob fɔ, nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Dina a je kpo konɛ e ya slaa Kanaan yi ɔmɛ ekomɛ.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Benɛ Hamor binyumu Shekem na Dina a, e nu lɛ pani nya nɛ e kɛ lɛ hwɔ. Hamor nɛ ɔ, Hiv no ji lɛ, nɛ lɛ ji jamɛ a zugba a nɔ yelɔ.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: Shekem na Dina he bua jɔmi; e suɔ lɛ saminya, nɛ e kɛ lɛ sɛɛ ni.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Shekem de e tsɛ Hamor ke, “Yaa bi yiheyo nɛ ɔ si ha mi nɛ ma ngɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Yakob nu kaa nɔ ko ya pee e biyo Dina basabasa; se akɛnɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ kɛ e lohwe ɔmɛ ho nga nɔ ya he je ɔ, e de we nɔ́ ko kɛ ya si a kpale kɛ ba.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, Yakob binyumu ɔmɛ hu je nga nɔ kɛ ba. Benɛ a nu sane nɛ ba a, a mi mi fu wawɛɛ nitsɛ kaa Shekem tsu zo ní kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ ngɛ Israel; kaa e nu Yakob biyo pani nya, nɛ e kɛ lɛ hwɔ. Nɔ́ nɛ Shekem pee nɛ ɔ, a hiɔ̃.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Hamor de Yakob ke, “Ye binyumu Shekem suɔ kaa e kɛ o biyo ɔ maa hi si. I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o kɛ o biyo ɔ nɛ ha lɛ nɛ e ngɔ.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Nyɛ ha nɛ wa ha wa he gba; nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ biyi ɔmɛ ha wɔ, konɛ nyɛ hu nyɛɛ ngɔ wa biyi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ kplɛɛ ja a, waa kɛ nyɛ maa hi si. Wa zugba a fɔɔ si ha nyɛ; nyɛɛ kɛ wɔ maa hi si faa, nyɛ maa ye jua, nɛ nyɛ ma na nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ weto ní.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ Shekem ble Dina, Yakob binyumu ɔmɛ a nyɛmiyo ɔ he je ɔ, mɛ hu a sisi Shekem kɛ e tsɛ Hamor ɔ.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: A de mɛ ke, “Wa be nyɛe maa pee ja kaa waa kɛ wa nyɛmiyo ma ha mɔmlɔtɔtsɛ; ke wa pee ja kɛkɛ wa pue wa hɛ mi si.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ maa pee kaa bɔ nɛ wa ngɛ ɔ, nɛ nyɛ maa po nyɛ nyumu ɔmɛ tsuo ɔ, lɛɛ wa maa kplɛɛ nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ de ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ pee ja lɛɛ waa kɛ wa biyi ɔmɛ ma ha nyɛ, nɛ wɔ hu wa maa ngɔ nyɛ biyi ɔmɛ. Waa kɛ nyɛ maa hi si, nɛ wa maa pee ma kake.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Se ke nyɛ kplɛɛ we kaa a po nyɛ ɔ, lɛɛ wa maa ngɔ wa nyɛmiyo ɔ kɛ ho.”

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: E yi be ko nɛ Shekem ya pee nɔ́ nɛ a de lɛ ke e sa kaa e pee ɔ; ejakaa e suɔ Yakob biyo ɔ saminya. Jehanɛ se hu, a buu lɛ wawɛɛ nitsɛ ngɛ e tsɛ weku li ɔmɛ a kpɛti.

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: “Kikɛmɛ a nimli nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ wɔ ngɛ saminya; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛ ha nɛ a hi zugba a nɔ nɛ a ye jua, ejakaa zugba a kle ha mɛ bɔ nɛ sa. Nyɛ ha nɛ waa ngɔ a biyi ɔmɛ, nɛ mɛ hu a ngɔ wa biyi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Ni ɔmɛ kplɛɛ kaa a kɛ wɔ maa hi si nɛ a kɛ wɔ maa pee ma kake, ke ji kaa wa maa po wa kpɛti nyumu ɔmɛ tsuo, kaa bɔ nɛ a po mɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Ke wa pee ja a, a lohwe ɔmɛ, kɛ a nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ma ba pee wa nɔ. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, nyɛ ha nɛ waa kplɛɛ ha mɛ kɛkɛ, konɛ a kɛ wɔ nɛ hi si.”

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Ligbi etɛne ɔ nɔ, benɛ pa a ngɛ ni ɔmɛ yee wawɛɛ ɔ, Yakob binyumuhi enyɔ, Simeon kɛ Levi ngɔ a klaate ɔmɛ nɛ a ya tua ma a tlukaa, nɛ a gbe nyumu ɔmɛ tsuo. Simeon kɛ Levi nɛ ɔ, Dina nyɛbimɛ ji mɛ.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: A gbe Hamor kɛ e bi Shekem hulɔ, nɛ a ya ngɔ Dina ngɛ Shekem we ɔ mi kɛ je.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Yakob binyumu ɔmɛ tsuo ya sɛ ma a mi, nɛ a ha ní ngɛ a nyɛmiyo ɔ nɛ a pue e hɛ mi si ɔ he.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: A nuu to, kɛ na, kɛ teji, nɛ a muɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ ma a mi, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ nga nɔ kɛ je.

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: A ngɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ he jua wa. A nuu yihi kɛ jokuɛwi tsuo, nɛ a ha ní ngɛ wehi a mi.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Yakob de Simeon kɛ Levi ke, “Nyɛɛ kɛ mi wo amanehlu mi pɛ; jehanɛ lɛɛ Kanaan, kɛ Periz bi ɔmɛ, kɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ maa nyɛ mi. I be we bi babauu; ke nimli nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo bla ngɔ wo ye he, nɛ a ba tua mi ɔ, a ma kpata wɔ tsuo wa hɛ mi.”

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Se a he nɔ ke, “Anɛ e sa kaa waa ngmɛ blɔ nɛ a pee wa nyɛmiyo ɔ kaa a peeɔ yo yaholɔ lo?”

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Wa ngɛ hiɛ ɔ jee kɛ yaa Betel. Ma ma bɔ sami la tɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ha Mawu ɔ nɛ piɛ ye he ngɛ ye amanehlu be ɔ mi, nɛ e kɛ mi ngɛ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: A ngɔ a ma se mawu ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ ngɛ a dɛ ɔ, kɛ a tue nya ní ɔmɛ ba ha Yakob; nɛ Yakob pu ngɛ tso ngua a sisi ngɛ Shekem kasa nya.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob kɛ e yi ɔmɛ, e bimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ hia kɛ yaa a, sawale nu ni ɔmɛ ngɛ ma amɛ nɛ bɔle mɛ ɔ a mi; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a nyɛɛ we a se.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Yakob ma bɔ sami la tɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e kɛ Betel Mawu ɔ biɛ wo lɛ; ejakaa lejɛ ɔ ji he nɛ Mawu je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ lɛ ngɛ, benɛ e tu e nyɛmi Esau nya fo ɔ.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Bimɛanyɛ ɔ nɛ hyɛ Rebeka ngɛ e jokuɛ mi, nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Debora a ba gbo, nɛ a pu lɛ ngɛ tso ngua a sisi, ngɛ Betel leneyi je. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke, “Tso ngua he nɛ a woɔ ya ngɛ.”

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Zugba a nɛ i ngɔ kɛ ha Abraham kɛ Isak ɔ, i kɛ ma ha mo kɛ o nina.”

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Yakob kɛ kaimi tɛ ko ma si ngɛ he nɛ Mawu kɛ lɛ ba tu munyu ngɛ ɔ. E plɛ wai kɛ oliv nu ngɔ pue nɔ, nɛ e kɛ pee tɛ ɔ klɔuklɔu kɛ ha Mawu.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: E wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Betel; e sisi ji Mawu we. Rahel gbenɔ

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Yakob kɛ e yi ɔmɛ, kɛ e bimɛ ɔmɛ hia kɛ je Betel, nɛ a pue blɔ. Benɛ e piɛ bɔɔ nɛ a maa su Efrat ɔ, Rahel fɔmi be su, nɛ e nu kɔɔmi nɛ nya wa.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Benɛ e fɔmi ɔ he ba wa a, fɔlɔyo ɔ nɛ ngɛ lɛ hyɛe ɔ de lɛ ke, “Rahel, koo ye gbeye; o fɔ binyumu ekohu!”

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Se Rahel miɔ nɛ e ma gbo. Loko e ma e nya a, e wo bi ɔ nɛ e fɔ ɔ ke Benoni; se e tsɛ lɛɛ biɛ nɛ e wo lɛ ji Benyamin.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Benɛ Rahel gbo ɔ, a pu lɛ ngɛ blɔ nɛ yaa Efrat ɔ he. Amlɔ nɛ ɔ lɛɛ a tsɛɛ Efrat ma a ke Betlehem.

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Yakob kɛ kaimi tɛ ma Rahel yɔkɔ ɔ nɔ, nɛ tɛ ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Yakob, nɛ e biɛ tsake pee Israel ɔ, tsa e nyɛɛmi ɔ nɔ, nɛ e ya ma e bo tsu ɔ ngɛ Eder mɔ ɔ se. Yakob binyumu ɔmɛ (Kronika I,

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob ngɛ jamɛ a zugba a nɔ ɔ, Ruben kɛ Bilha, e tsɛ pla amɛ a ti nɔ kake ɔ ya na bɔmi; nɛ Yakob nu he. Yakob ngɛ binyumuhi nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Yakob ba e tsɛ Isak ngɔ ngɛ Mamre, he nɛ Abraham kɛ Isak ba to nubwɔ ngɛ ɔ. Mamre biɛ kpa ji Kiriat Arba, aloo Hebron.

english_verse: Isaac died at the ripe old age of

translation_verse: Esau ngɔ Kanaan yihi. Mɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: Hit no ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Elon ɔ biyo Ada, kɛ Hiv no ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Zibeon ɔ bi Ana biyo Oholibama,

translation_verse: kɛ Ishmael biyo Basemat, Nebayot nyɛmiyo ɔ.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: nɛ Oholibama fɔ Yeush, Yalam, kɛ Kora. Binyumuhi nɛ Esau fɔ ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Esau ngɔ e yi ɔmɛ, e binyumu ɔmɛ, e biyi ɔmɛ, kɛ nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ e we ɔ mi ɔ, e lohwe ɔmɛ, kɛ níhi tsuo nɛ e bua nya ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ ɔ, nɛ e je e nyɛmi Yakob he kɛ ho zugba kpa nɔ ya.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Esau hia kɛ ya hi Edom yo ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Wɛtsohi nɛ je Esau mi ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: Esau bitɛte Elifaz ji wɛtso nɛ ɔmɛ a nɛ̃: Teman, Omar, Zefo, Kenaz,

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: Kora, Gatam kɛ Amalek. Esau yo Ada nina ji ni nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
translation_verse: Esau binyumu Reuel ji wɛtso nɛ ɔmɛ a nɛ̃: Nahat, Zera, Shama, kɛ Miza. Esau yo Basemat nina ji ni nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Wɛtso nɛ ɔmɛ je Esau yo Oholibama, Ana biyo ɔ mi: Yeush, Yalam, kɛ Kora.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Esau nina ji wɛtso nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo. Seir nina (Kronika I,

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lotan binyumuhi ji Hori kɛ Heman. Lotan ngɛ nyɛmiyo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Timna.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Shobal binyumuhi ji Alvan, Manahat, Ebal, Shefo, kɛ Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Zibeon binyumuhi ji Aya kɛ Ana. Ana nɛ ɔ ji nɔ nɛ ya na nyu la vuhi ngɛ nga a nɔ, benɛ e ngɛ e tsɛ Zibeon teji ɔmɛ hyɛe ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Ezer binyumuhi ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: Bilhan, Zaavan, kɛ Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Dishan binyumuhi ji Uz kɛ Aran.

english_verse: Before there were kings in Israel, the following kings ruled Edom one after another: Bela son of Beor from Dinhabah; Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah; Husham from the land of Teman; Hadad son of Bedad from Avith ; Samlah from Masrekah; Shaul from the city of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River; Baalhanan son of Achbor; Hadar from the city of Pau .
translation_verse: Loko a wo matsɛ ngɛ Israel ɔ, nyumuhi nɛ ye matsɛ ngɛ Edom zugba a nɔ kɛ nyɛɛ a sibi a se ji nɛ ɔmɛ: Beor bi Bela nɛ je Dinhaba Zera bi Yobab nɛ je Bozra Husham nɛ je Teman zugba a nɔ Bedad bi Hadad nɛ je Avit Samla nɛ je Masreka Shaul nɛ je Rehobot, ngɛ pa a he Akbor bi Baal Hanan Hadad nɛ je Pau

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: Esau ji Edom wɛtso nɛ ɔmɛ a nɛ̃: Timna, Alva, Yetet, Oholibama, Ela, Pinon, Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, Magdiel, kɛ Iram. A kɛ wɛtso nɛ ɔmɛ a biɛhi wo hehi nɛ a hi ɔ.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Yakob hi Kanaan zugba a nɛ e tsɛ ba to nubwɔ ngɛ nɔ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ de lɛ ke, “A je hiɛ ɔ; i nu nɛ a ngɛ dee ke a yaa Dotan.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Yosef fie e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a se, nɛ e ya na mɛ ngɛ Dotan.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Yakob suɔ Yosef sane pe e bimɛ ɔmɛ tsuo; ejakaa benɛ a fɔ Yosef ɔ, lɛ Yakob ɔ bwɔ momo. Yakob kpɛ tade klɔii saminyayoo ko ngɔ wo Yosef.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ na kaa a tsɛ suɔ Yosef pe mɛ tsuo ɔ, a nyɛ lɛ, nɛ a ha we lɛ hɛ mi.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Yosef nla nlami ko; nɛ benɛ e bɔ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nlami ɔ, a nyɛ lɛ pe sa a.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: E de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ bu nlami nɛ i nla nɛ ɔ tue.

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Wɔ tsuo wa ngɛ ngmɔ mi nɛ wa ngɛ ngma fie. Kɛkɛ nɛ ye ngma a nɛ i fi ɔ te da si; nɛ nyɛ ngma amɛ ba bɔle ye ngma a, nɛ a kpla si ha lɛ.”

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: E nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ bi lɛ ke, “Lɛɛ tse o ma ba ye wa nɔ matsɛ, pi ja lo?” Nlami ɔ nɛ Yosef sɛɛ ha e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ha nɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nyɛ lɛ pe kekle ɔ.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Yosef nla nlami kpa, nɛ e bɔ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke, “I pa nla nlami kpa. I nla nɛ pu kɛ hlami kɛ dodoe nyɔngma kɛ kake ba kpla si ngɛ ye hɛ mi.”

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: E ya bɔ e tsɛ hu nlami nɛ ɔ, nɛ e tsɛ ka e hɛ mi ke, “Mɛni nlami ji nɛ ɔ? Lɛɛ tse i kɛ o nyɛ kɛ o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ma ba kpla si ha mo lo?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a mi mi wo la wawɛɛ nitsɛ, se e tsɛ ɔ lɛɛ daa nɛ ɔ, e ngɛ sane ɔmɛ a he susue. A jua Yosef kɛ ho Egipt ya

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Ligbi ko, benɛ Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ tsɔ̃ a tsɛ to ɔmɛ kɛ ho Shekem ya nɛ a ya hyɛ mɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ,

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Yakob de Yosef ke, “O nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kɛ to ɔmɛ ho Shekem ya nɛ a ya hyɛ mɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Ma suɔ nɛ ma tsɔ mo a ngɔ.” Yosef he nɔ ke, “Ma ya.”

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: E tsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya slaa o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ o hyɛ kaa to ɔmɛ hu nɔ́ ko be a he lo, nɛ o ba de mi.” Kɛkɛ nɛ e tsɛ ɔ wo lɛ blɔ kɛ je Hebron kɔ̃ ɔ mi. Benɛ e ba su Shekem ɔ,

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: E he nɔ ke, “I ngɛ ye nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ hlae. I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o tsɔɔ mi he nɛ a ngɛ a to ɔmɛ hyɛe ngɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: A na lɛ nɛ e ma jee; nɛ benɛ e na we nɛ e su a ngɔ lolo ɔ, a so e yi nɔ kaa a maa gbe lɛ.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: A de a sibi ke, “Nlalɔ ɔ lɛ ma a nɛ.

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Benɛ Ruben nu he ɔ, e hla kaa e ma kpɔ Yosef ngɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a dɛ. E de e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke, “Wa ko gbe lɛ.

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Nyɛ sake lɛ kɛ wo muɔ nɛ ɔ mi ngɛ nga a nɔ kɛkɛ; se nyɛ ko gbe lɛ.” Ruben de ja, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ e kpɔ Yosef ngɛ a dɛ, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ya ha e tsɛ.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Benɛ Yosef ba su e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a ngɔ ɔ, a je tade klɔii saminyayoo ɔ ngɛ e he.

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Benɛ a hii si nɛ a ngɛ ní yee ɔ, a na Ishmael bi blɔ hiali komɛ ngɛ afukpɔngɔhi a nɔ nɛ a ma. A je Gilead, nɛ a hɛɛ tsopahi kɛ a he via kɛ yaa Egipt.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Yuda de e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke, “Ke wa gbe wa nyɛmi nɛ ɔ nɛ wa laa nɔ ɔ, mɛni se wa ma na?

english_verse: Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ha nɛ waa jua lɛ ha Ishmael bi ɔmɛ. Nyɛ ko ha wa nine nɛ kpa ngɛ e nɔ; ejakaa wɔ nitsɛmɛ wa nyɛmi tutuutu ji lɛ.” E nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kplɛɛ,

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Benɛ Ruben kpale e se kɛ ba muɔ ɔ he, nɛ e na kaa Yosef be muɔ ɔ mi ɔ, e kɛ aywilɛho hía e he tade ɔmɛ kɛ tsɔɔ kaa e hao lɛ.

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: E kpale kɛ ho e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a ngɔ ya, nɛ e ya de mɛ ke, “Jokuɛ niheyo ɔ be lejɛ ɔ. Bubuubui! Kɛ ma pee kɛɛ?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a gbe apletsi ko, nɛ a ngɔ Yosef tade klɔii saminyayoo ɔ kɛ tsɔ muɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: A kɛ tade ɔ ya ha a tsɛ ɔ, nɛ a de lɛ ke, “Wa na tade nɛ ɔ ngɛ nga a nɔ; hyɛ kaa o bi Yosef tade ɔ ji nɛ ɔ lo.”

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Yakob le tade ɔ mi tso, nɛ e de ke, “Ye bi ɔ tade ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Lohwe awi yelɔ ko ye lɛ; lohwe ko tsɔtslɔɔ ye bi Yosef mi.”

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yakob kɛ aywilɛho hía e he tade ɔmɛ, nɛ e bu kpekpe ya bo; nɛ e nyɛ ya ha e bi ɔ ligbi babauu.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Yakob binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ e biyi ɔmɛ tsuo ba ba wo lɛ bua, se e kplɛɛ we. E de ke, “Ma ye kɔmɔ hluu kɛ yaa si gbeje.” Nɛ e tsa nɔ nɛ e ye kɔmɔ ha e bi Yosef ɔ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, jua yeli ɔmɛ ya jua Yosef ngɛ Egipt ngɔ ha Egipt matsɛ ɔ tsɔlɔ kake nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Potifar. Potifar ji matsɛ we buli ɔmɛ a nyatsɛ.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, Yuda je e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e ya hi nyumu ko nɛ je Adulam, nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Hira ngɔ.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Yuda ya na Kanaan yiheyo ko ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ e tsɛ biɛ ke Shua. E ngɔ lɛ,

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: nɛ e kɛ lɛ fɔ binyumu, nɛ Yuda wo lɛ biɛ ke Er.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: E kpale fɔ binyumu ekohu, nɛ e wo lɛ Shela. Benɛ a fɔ binyumuyo nɛ ɔ, Yuda ngɛ Akzib.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Yuda ya ngɔ yo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Tamar ba ha Er, e bitɛte ɔ.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Yuda bitɛte Er pee e he nɔmlɔ yayami. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ngɔɛ Yawɛ nya; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yawɛ gbe lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Se nɔ́ nɛ e pee nɛ ɔ sɛ́ Yawɛ hɛ mi; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yawɛ gbe lɛ hulɔ.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yuda de e nganyɛ Tamar ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya hi si ngɛ o tsɛ we ɔ mi kaa yalɔyo kɛ yaa si ye bi Shela maa wa.” E de enɛ ɔ, ejakaa e ye gbeye kaa lɛ hu e ma ba gbo kaa bɔ nɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ gbo ɔ. Lɔ he ɔ, Tamar je kɛ ho e tsɛ we mi ya.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Yuda yo ɔ nɛ ji Shua biyo ɔ ba gbo. Benɛ Yuda nyɛ ya ha lɛ ta a, e kɛ e huɛ Hira nɛ je Adulam ɔ ho Timna ya, ngɛ he nɛ e to ɔmɛ a he bwɔmi sali ɔmɛ ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
