translation_verse: Nɔ ko ya naa Tamar nane nɔ kaa e ngatsɛ ɔ yaa Timna nɛ e ya sã e to ɔmɛ a he bwɔmi.

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e je yalɔyo bo ɔ nɛ e bu ɔ ngɔ fɔ si. E tsake e he; e kɛ hɛ mi hami nɔ́ ha e hɛ mi, nɛ e ho ya hi si ngɛ Enaim ma a nya, ngɛ Timna blɔ ɔ nɔ. E pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, ejakaa e na kaa Shela wa, se a kɛ lɛ Tamar a ha we lɛ.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Benɛ Yuda na lɛ ɔ, e bu lɛ kaa yo yaholɔ ko; ejakaa e kɛ nɔ́ ha e hɛ mi.

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Yuda bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni ma si ha mo kɛ to mo awaba a?” Tamar he nɔ ke, “O womi nya sɔumi nɔ́ kɛ e he kpa, kɛ o dɛma tso ɔ.” Yuda ngɔ ní ɔmɛ ngɔ ha lɛ. Kɛkɛ nɛ e kɛ lɛ na bɔmi, nɛ Tamar ngɔ hɔ.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Tamar je kɛ ho we mi ya, nɛ e ya je e hɛ mi hami nɔ́ ɔ ngɔ fɔ si, nɛ e bu e yalɔyo bo ɔ.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Yuda tsɔ e huɛ Hira ke e ngɔ apletsi ɔ ya ha yo ɔ, konɛ e he ní ɔmɛ nɛ e kɛ to lɛ awaba a ngɛ e dɛ kɛ ba. Se Hira nɛ yo ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: E bi nyumu komɛ ngɛ Enaim ma a mi ke, “Yo yaholɔ ɔ nɛ hii si ngɛ hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ, jije e ngɛ?” Se a he nɔ ke, “Yo yaholɔ ko kaa ja be hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Hira kpale e se kɛ ba Yuda ngɔ ekohu, nɛ e ba de lɛ ke, “I nɛ yo ɔ. Nyumu ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ hu ke yo yaholɔ ko kaa ja be lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Yuda de ke, “Ha ní ɔmɛ nɛ a hi e dɛ. Wa be suɔe nɛ nihi nɛ a ba muɔ wɔ; i bɔ mɔde kaa ma wo lɛ hiɔ, se mo nɛ o nɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Maa pee hlami etɛ se ɔ, nɔ ko ba de Yuda ke, “O nganyɛ Tamar ya nyɛɛ basabasa, nɛ hɔ ba e he nɛ a li hɔtsɛ.” Yuda fa ke, “A je lɛ kpo, nɛ a ya sã lɛ.”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Benɛ a kɛ lɛ je kpo kɛ ba a, e tsɔ nɛ a ya de e ngatsɛ ɔ ke, “Nɔ nɛ níhi ji nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, lɛ nɛ wo mi hɔ ɔ nɛ. Hyɛ kaa o maa le ní nɛ ɔmɛ a tsɛ lo; womi nya sɔumi nɔ́ kɛ e he kpa nɛ ɔ, kɛ tso nɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Yuda le ní ɔmɛ a mi tso, nɛ e de ke, “E nɔ́ da; ye nɔ́ be mi. Jinɛ e sa kaa i ko ngɔ lɛ ngɔ ha ye bi Shela nɛ e gba lɛ.” Nɛ́ pee ja a, Yuda kɛ Tamar na we bɔmi hu.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, benɛ e nu kɔɔmi ɔ, hayo ɔ kake je e nine kpo. Fɔlɔyo ɔ nu e nine ɔ, nɛ e kɛ kpa tsu fi nine ɔ he, nɛ e de ke, “Nɔ nɛ ɔ ba kekle.”

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Se hayo ɔ gbla e nine ɔ se, nɛ e nyɛmi ɔ kple kɛ sɛ e hlami. Kɛkɛ nɛ fɔlɔyo ɔ de ke, “Bɔ nɛ o gba o blɔ kɛ ba ha ji nɛ ɔ!” Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a wo lɛ biɛ ke Perez.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e nyɛmi ɔ hu kple kɛ e nine kpa tsu ɔ, nɛ a wo lɛ Zera.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Ishmael bi ɔmɛ kɛ Yosef ba Egipt nɛ a ba jua lɛ ngɔ ha Egipt matsɛ ɔ tsɔlɔ kake nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Potifar; lɛ ji matsɛ we buli ɔmɛ a nyatsɛ.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yosef nyɔmtsɛ ɔ na kaa Yawɛ gbaa Yosef, nɛ e haa e yeɔ manye ngɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ mi ɔ,

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: e na e he bua jɔmi. Potifar wo lɛ nɔkɔtɔma ngɛ e we ɔ mi, nɛ e to e nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ngɔ wo e dɛ.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Potifar to e nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ kɛ wo Yosef dɛ, nɛ e gba we e he nya ngɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko he kaa ja nɔ́ nɛ e maa ye kɛkɛ. Yosef ɔ, nyumu nɛ he ngɛ fɛu saminya ji lɛ.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Saii mi ɔ, e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ yo ɔ bɔni e se nyɛɛmi nɛ e kɛ lɛ nɛ na bɔmi.

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Yosef kplɛɛ we; nɛ e de e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ yo ɔ ke, “Hyɛ, ye nyɔmtsɛ gba we e he nya ngɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko he ngɛ we nɛ ɔ mi, ejakaa i ngɛ hiɛ ɔ. E to e nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ngɔ wo ye dɛ.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: I ngɛ he wami ngɛ we nɛ ɔ mi kaa bɔ nɛ lɛ hu e ngɛ ɔ. Nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be nɛ ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ je we he gbi ha mi, kaa ja mo pɛ; ejakaa moo lɛɛ e yo ji mo. Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ ma tsu yi wu tso ní kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ, nɛ ma pee yayami kɛ si Mawu?”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Yo nɛ ɔ hao Yosef daa ligbi kɛ kikɛmɛ a munyu nɛ ɔ; se Yosef kplɛɛ we kaa e kɛ lɛ ma na bɔmi, loo e maa hɛ lɛ kɛ su e he po.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Se ligbi ko benɛ Yosef ba we ɔ mi nɛ e ba tsu ní ɔ, tsɔli ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko be we ɔ mi.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ yo ɔ nu Yosef tade ɔ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ba nɛ o kɛ mi ba hwɔ si.” Se Yosef tu fo kɛ je kpo, nɛ e je e tade ɔ he ngɛ yo ɔ dɛ mi.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: e tsɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ nɛ tsuɔ ní ngɛ we ɔ mi ɔ, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ hyɛ! Ye huno ya ngɔ kikɛmɛ a Hebri no nɛ ɔ kɛ ba futu wɔ, konɛ e ba ye wa he fɛu. Nyumu nɛ ɔ ba ye ngɔ konɛ e ba tua mi, se i kpa bubuubui.

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: Benɛ e nu nɛ i ngɛ bubuubui ɔ kpae ɔ, e tu fo kɛ je kpo, nɛ e je e tade ɔ he.”

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Yo ɔ ngɔ Yosef tade ɔ ngɔ to kɛ ya si Yosef nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ba we ɔ mi.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Se benɛ i kpa bubuubui ɔ, e tu fo kɛ je kpo, nɛ e je e tade ɔ he.”

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: nɛ e ha a nu Yosef kɛ wo tsu ngɛ he nɛ a woɔ matsɛ pamitsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsu ngɛ ɔ; nɛ e hi lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ kɛ Yosef ngɛ; nɛ e na lɛ mɔbɔ, nɛ e ha nɛ pamitsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ hyɛlɔ ɔ na e he bua jɔmi.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Pamitsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ hyɛlɔ ɔ to pamitsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ wo Yosef dɛ mi. Lɛ ji nɔ nɛ hyɛɛ a nɔ kɛ peeɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: nɛ e wo mɛ tsu ngɛ matsɛ we buli a nyatsɛ ɔ we ɔ mi. Lejɛ ɔ nɛ a wo Yosef hu tsu ngɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: A se kɛ saminya ngɛ tsu ɔ mi, nɛ matsɛ we buli a nyatsɛ ɔ tu mɛ ngɔ wo Yosef dɛ mi nɛ e sɔmɔ mɛ.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Mɔtu, benɛ Yosef ba a ngɔ ɔ, e na kaa a hɛ mi pee mɔbɔmɔbɔ.

english_verse: and he asked, “Why are you so worried today?”
translation_verse: E bi mɛ ke, “Mwɔnɛ ɔ lɛɛ mɛni he je nyɛ hɛ mi pee mɔbɔmɔbɔ kikɛ nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: A he nɔ ke, “Wa ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ nla nlami ko, nɛ nɔ ko be nɛ maa tsɔɔ wɔ sisi.” Yosef de mɛ ke, “Mawu lɛ tsɔɔ nlamihi a sisi; i kpa nyɛ pɛɛ nɛ nyɛɛ sɛɛ nlami ɔmɛ ha mi.”

english_verse: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ dã nɔ hyɛlɔ nɔkɔtɔma a de Yosef e nlami ɔ ke, “I nla nɛ wai tso ko maa si ngɛ ye hɛ mi,

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: nɛ tso ɔ gba kɔni etɛ. Benɛ ba amɛ je kpo pɛ nɛ mɔmɔ ɔmɛ gba, nɛ wai yiblii nɛ tsu je kpo.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Yosef de lɛ ke, “Nlami ɔ sisi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: tso kɔni etɛ ɔmɛ daa si ha ligbi etɛ.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Se, i kpa mo pɛɛ, ke níhi a mi ya hi ha mo ɔ, mo kai mi nɛ o na mi mɔbɔ; moo tu ye he munyu kpakpa ha Farao ɔ, nɛ e ba je mi kɛ je tsu nɛ ɔ mi.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Pani nya nɛ a nu mi kɛ je Hebri bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ; nɛ Egipt hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ hu i pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ sa kaa a wo mi tsu.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Benɛ abolo salɔ nɔkɔtɔma a na kaa Yosef tsɔɔ nlami ɔ sisi saminya a, e de lɛ ke, “Imi hu i nla nɛ i tloo abolo kusii etɛ.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Niye ní slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi nɛ a sã ha Farao ɔ ngɛ kusii nɛ ngɛ hiɔwe pe kulaa a mi; nɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ ba ngɛ yee.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Yosef de lɛ ke, “Nlami ɔ sisi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: kusii etɛ ɔmɛ daa si ha ligbi etɛ.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ ligbi etɛ ɔ, Farao ɔ ma je mo kɛ je tsu mi, nɛ e ma ha a sɛu mo ngɛ tso nɔ, nɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ ma ba ye o he lo ɔ.”

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Ligbi etɛ se ɔ, Farao ɔ ye e fɔmi ligbi. E tsɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo ní yemi, nɛ e ha a ya je e dã nɔ hyɛlɔ nɔkɔtɔma a, kɛ abolo salɔ nɔkɔtɔma a ngɛ tsu ɔ mi kɛ ba.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: Se abolo salɔ nɔkɔtɔma a lɛɛ Farao ɔ ha a sɛu lɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Yosef tsɔɔ a nlami ɔmɛ a sisi ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Se dã nɔ hyɛlɔ nɔkɔtɔma a kai we Yosef hu; e hɛ je e nɔ pɛsɛpɛsɛ.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Jeha enyɔ se ɔ, Farao ɔ nla nlami ko. E nla nɛ e daa si ngɛ Nilo pa a nya.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ na yo kpaago nɛ a he ngɛ fɛu, nɛ a plɔke, hia kpo kɛ je pa a mi, nɛ a ba bɔni ní yemi ngɛ nga a mi.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: E sɛ mahe mi ekohu, nɛ e kpale nla nlami kpa ko. E nla nɛ blɛfo kpaago, nɛ a wo ní saminya gbɔ ngɛ tso kake nɔ.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Blɛfo kpaago kpa hu ba tso ɔ nɔ; mɛɛ a wui ní, nɛ jehanɛ se hu, ahlabata kɔɔhiɔ ngla mɛ.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Blɛfo kpaago nɛ wui ní ɔ, mii blɛfo kpaago kpa amɛ nɛ wo ní ɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ hɛ tsɛ, nɛ e na kaa e ngɛ nlae.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Benɛ je na a, e hao; nɛ e tsɔ ya tsɛ Egipt kunya yeli ɔmɛ, kɛ ní leli ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ba. E de mɛ e nlami ɔmɛ, se nɔ ko nɔ ko nyɛ we nɛ e tsɔɔ sisi.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ dã nɔ hyɛlɔ nɔkɔtɔma a de lɛ ke, “I ngɛ jajee mwɔnɛ ɔ kaa i tɔ̃.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: O mi mi fu imi, kɛ abolo salɔ nɔkɔtɔma a, nɛ o wo wɔ tsu ngɛ matsɛ we buli a nyatsɛ ɔ we ɔ mi.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Hebri niheyo ko, nɛ ji matsɛ we buli a nyatsɛ ɔ nyɔguɛ ko hu ngɛ tsu ɔ mi kɛ wɔ. Wa sɛɛ wa nlami ɔmɛ ha lɛ, nɛ e tsɔɔ wɔ a sisi pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ e tsɔɔ wɔ nlami ɔmɛ a sisi ɔ, ja pɛpɛɛpɛ a ba mi; o ngɔ mi ngɔ to ye blɔ he ɔ ekohu, se abolo salɔ ɔ lɛɛ o sɛu lɛ.”

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ tsɔ nɛ a ya je Yosef kɛ je tsu ɔ mi amlɔ nɔuu. E sɛ e kpɛni, nɛ e tsake e tade, nɛ e ba Farao ɔ ngɔ.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Farao ɔ de Yosef ke, “I nla nlami ko, se nɔ ko nyɛ we nɛ e tsɔɔ mi sisi. I nu kaa a ke moo lɛɛ o nyɛɔ tsɔɔ nlamihi a sisi.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Yosef he nɔ ke, “Nɛnɛ, pi imi. Mawu ji nɔ nɛ maa tsɔɔ mo nlami ɔ sisi bɔ nɛ maa sa o hɛ mi.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ de Yosef ke, “I nla nɛ i daa si ngɛ Nilo pa a nya.

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ na yo kpaago nɛ a he ngɛ fɛu, nɛ a plɔke, hia kpo kɛ je pa a mi, nɛ a ba bɔni nga kpemi.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na yo kpaago kpa hu hia kpo kɛ nyɛɛ a se kɛ ba; mɛɛ lɛɛ a flãã nɛ a ngɛ kanyakanya. I nɛ nahi kɛ a he tai nɛ ɔmɛ a henɔ hyɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a tsuo nɔ.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Se benɛ a mii mɛ ta a, nɔ ko nɛ kulaa kaa a ye nɔ́ ko; ejakaa bɔ nɛ a ngɛ kanyakanya sa a, ja ko nɛ a ngɛ.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, i nla ekohu nɛ blɛfo tso kpaago, nɛ a wo ní saminya gbɔ ngɛ tso kake nɔ.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ blɛfo tso kpaago kpa hu ba tso ɔ nɔ; mɛɛ a wui ní, nɛ jehanɛ se hu, ahlabata kɔɔhiɔ ngla mɛ.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Blɛfo tso kpaago nɛ wui ní ɔ mii blɛfo tso kpaago kpa amɛ nɛ wo ní ɔ. I de kunya yeli ɔmɛ nlami nɛ ɔmɛ, se a ti nɔ ko nɔ ko nyɛ we nɛ e tsɔɔ mi sisi.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Yosef de matsɛ ɔ ke, “O nlami ɔmɛ tsuo, nlami kake; Mawu je nɔ́ ko nɛ e yaa pee ɔ kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ mo.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Na kpaago ɔmɛ nɛ plɔke ɔ, daa si ha jeha kpaago. Blɛfo tso kpaago ɔmɛ nɛ wo ní ɔ, hu daa si ha jeha kpaago; a ngɛ sisi tsɔɔmi kake too.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Na kpaago ɔmɛ nɛ flãã, nɛ a pee kanyakanya, nɛ nyɛɛ se kɛ ba a, daa si ha hwɔ be jeha kpaago. Jã kɛ̃ ji blɛfo tso kpaago ɔmɛ nɛ wui ní, nɛ ahlabata kɔɔhiɔ ngla mɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Kaa bɔ nɛ i de mo ɔ, Mawu je nɔ́ ko nɛ e yaa pee ɔ kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ mo.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Niye ní babauu maa ba Egipt zugba a tsuo nɔ jeha kpaago.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Hwɔ ɔ nya maa wa wawɛɛ nitsɛ bɔ nɛ nihi a hɛ maa je kplɔkɔtɔ be ɔ nɛ sɛ hlami ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ a tĩ o nlami ɔ mi si enyɔ ɔ tsɔɔ kaa Mawu to e yi mi kaa e maa pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ niinɛ; nɛ e be kɛe kulaa.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mo hla nɔ ko nɛ le ní, nɛ e hɛ mi ka si nɛ o ngɔ to Egipt ma a nya.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, moo to nɔ hyɛli kpahi ngɛ ma a nya, nɛ o ngɔ niye ní nɛ maa ba kplɔkɔtɔ be jeha kpaago ɔ mi dlami enuɔ mi kake ngɔ to.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Niye ní tsuo nɛ maa ba ngɛ jeha kpakpa amɛ a mi ɔ, ha nɛ a bua nya. Moo wo mlaa nɛ a to blɛfo ngɛ ma tsuaa ma mi, nɛ a bu he.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: A kɛ niye ní nɛ ɔ maa to kɛ yaa si hwɔ maa ba Egipt zugba a nɔ jeha kpaago nɛ nyɛɛ se ɔ. Bɔ nɛ o maa pee nɛ hwɔ be zugba a hɛ mi kpatae ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.” A wo Yosef ganɔ ngɛ Egipt

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: E bi e tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “Anɛ wa maa na nɔ kpa ko kaa Yosef, nɛ Mawu mumi ngɛ e mi kikɛ nɛ ɔ lo?”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ de Yosef ke, “Akɛnɛ Mawu lɛ je ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɔ tsɔɔ mo ɔ, e tsɔɔ kaa nɔ kpa ko be nɛ le ní, nɛ e hɛ mi ka si kaa ja mo pɛ.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ mo ngɔ to ye ma a nya, nɛ ma a tsuo maa bu mo tue; ye se ɔ, lɛɛ mo.”

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ je e nguɛ ga kɛ e nɔ womi nya sɔumi nɔ́ ɔ, nɛ e kɛ wo Yosef nguɛ. E wo lɛ kploba tade klɔii saminyayoo ko, nɛ e kɛ sika tsu kɔsɔkɔsɔ wo e kuɛ.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: E kɛ lɛ wo matsɛ ta zugba lɛ enyɔne ɔ mi, nɛ matsɛ tsɔli nyɛɛ e hɛ mi kɛ ngmlaa ke, “Nyɛ kpla si oo! E ma oo!” Bɔ nɛ a pee kɛ wo Yosef ganɔ ngɛ Egipt zugba a tsuo nɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Kplɔkɔtɔ jeha kpaago ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, zugba a ba ní babauu nitsɛ,

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: nɛ Yosef bua ní ɔ tsuo nya nɛ e to ngɛ ma amɛ a mi.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Blɛfo nɛ Yosef bua nya a hiɛ babauu kaa wo nya zia. E kane blɛfo kɛ kotoku hluu kɛ ya si e kpa kanemi; ejakaa blɛfo ɔ hiɛ tsɔ.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Loko hwɔ ba jeha kpaago ɔ, Yosef kɛ osɔfo Potifera nɛ je Heliopolis ɔ biyo ɔ fɔ binyumuhi enyɔ.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: E wo e bitɛte ɔ Manase, nɛ e de ke, “Mawu ha nɛ ye hɛ je ye haomi ɔ tsuo, kɛ ye weku li tsuo a nɔ.”

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: E wo enyɔne ɔ Efraim, nɛ e de ke, “Mawu ha nɛ i wo ngmɛdu ngɛ zugba nɛ i na amanehlu ngɛ nɔ ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Jeha kpaago ɔmɛ nɛ niye ní ba babauu ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ se ba po,

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: nɛ jeha kpaago kɛ e mi hwɔ nɛ nya wa hu je sisi kaa bɔ nɛ Yosef de ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Hwɔ nɛ nya wa ye ngɛ zugba amɛ tsuo a nɔ; se Egipt zugba a nɔ tsuo lɛɛ niye ní ngɛ.

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Benɛ hwɔ ɔ nya ba wa ngɛ zugba a tsuo nɔ ɔ, Yosef bli nito he ɔmɛ tsuo a nya, nɛ e jua blɛfo ha Egipt bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Nihi je je ma amɛ tsuo a mi kɛ ba Egipt nɛ a ba he blɛfo ngɛ Yosef dɛ; ejakaa hwɔ ɔ nya wa wawɛɛ nitsɛ ngɛ he tsuaa he.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob nu kaa blɛfo ngɛ Egipt ɔ, e bi e binyumu ɔmɛ ke, “Mɛni nyɛ ngɛ nyɛ sibi hyɛe ngɛ pee?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: I nu kaa blɛfo ngɛ Egipt. Nyɛɛ ya lejɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛ ya he eko kɛ ba nɛ waa ye, nɛ hwɔ ko ba gbe wɔ.”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yosef tsɛbimɛ nyɔngma amɛ pue nɔ kɛ ho Egipt ya, konɛ a ya he blɛfo.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Se Yosef nyɛbi Benyamin lɛɛ Yakob ha we nɛ e kɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a ya; ejakaa Yakob ye gbeye kaa, alini, nɔ́ ko ma ya pee lɛ ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Yakob bimɛ ɔmɛ piɛ nihi nɛ ba blɛfo hemi ɔ a he; ejakaa hwɔ ba Kanaan zugba a hu nɔ.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Yosef, ganɔ nɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ, ji nɔ nɛ ngɛ blɛfo ɔ juae ha nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ba blɛfo hemi ɔ nɛ. Kɛkɛ nɛ Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ba kpla si ngɛ e hɛ mi, nɛ a kɛ a hɛ mi bu si.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: E kai nlami ɔmɛ nɛ e nla ngɛ a he ɔ, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Slaali ji nyɛ! Nyɛ ba nɛ nyɛ ba slaa wa zugba a, konɛ nyɛɛ hyɛ he nɛ wa huza amɛ a he wɛ ngɛ.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: A he nɔ ke, “Dɛbi! Wa nyɔmtsɛ, wa kpa mo pɛɛ, niye ní wa ma hemi.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Nyumu kake bimɛ ji wɔ tsuo. Anɔkualetsɛmɛ ji wɔ; pi slaali ji wɔ.”

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Yosef de mɛ ke, “Dɛbi! Nyɛ ba nɛ nyɛ ba hyɛ he nɛ wa huza amɛ a he wɛ ngɛ.”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: A de Yosef ke, “Nyumu kake bimɛ ji wɔ; wa tsɛ je Kanaan zugba a nɔ. Jinɛ nyɛmimɛ nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ ji wɔ; se wa ti nɔ kake be je mi, nɛ jokuɛyo ɔ hu ngɛ wa tsɛ ngɔ.”

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ i kɛ ma kpa nyɛ si ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. I na Farao ɔ kaa nyɛ be hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ jee; ja nyɛ nyɛmi jokuɛyo ɔ ba hiɛ ɔ loko nyɛ maa ho.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Nyɛ ti nɔ kake nɛ ya ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba. Nyɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ lɛɛ a maa wo nyɛ tsu kɛ yaa si nyɛ nyɛmi ɔ maa ba. Blɔ nɔ nɛ wa maa gu kɛ hyɛ kaa anɔkuale munyu nɛ nyɛ tu ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Se ke e ba mi kaa lakpa munyu nyɛ ba tu mi ɔ, lɛɛ i na Farao ɔ kaa slaali ji nyɛ.”

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e wo mɛ tsu ligbi etɛ.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji etɛ ɔ, Yosef de mɛ ke, “Imi lɛɛ i yeɔ Mawu gbeye; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ maa pee kɛ he nyɛ yi wami ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Ke anɔkualetsɛmɛ ji nyɛ niinɛ ɔ, nyɛ ha a wo nyɛ ti nɔ kake tsu ngɛ he nɛ a je nyɛ kɛ je ɔ. Nyɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ nyɛ piɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ ngɔ blɛfo nɛ nyɛ he ɔ kɛ ya we ya ha nyɛ weku li nɛ hwɔ ngɛ mɛ yee ɔ,

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: konɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ nyɛ nyɛmi jokuɛyo ɔ kɛ ba. Enɛ ɔ maa tsɔɔ kaa sane ɔ nɛ nyɛ ba gba mi ɔ, anɔkuale, nɛ i be nyɛ gbee.” A kplɛɛ,

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: nɛ a de a sibi ke, “Niinɛ, nɔ́ nɛ wa pee wa nyɛmi ɔ be ko nɛ be ɔ, lɔ ɔ he nɔ́ wa ngɛ nae nɛ ɔ nɛ. Wa na bɔ nɛ e hao, nɛ e kpa wɔ pɛɛ ke waa na lɛ mɔbɔ; se wa pui mi. Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ kikɛmɛ a haomi nɛ ɔ ba wa nɔ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Ruben de mɛ ke, “Tse i de nyɛ ke nyɛ ko pee jokuɛ ɔ yayami ko nɛ nyɛ bui mi tue; e gbenɔ ɔ he tue gblami nɛ wa ngɛ nae nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: A li tete kaa Yosef nu nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ dee ɔ sisi; ejakaa benɛ a kɛ lɛ ngɛ munyu ɔ tue ɔ, nɔ ko je gbi nya ha mɛ.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Yosef je a he, nɛ e ya fo ya. Benɛ e kpale e se kɛ ba, nɛ e kɛ mɛ ba tu munyu ekohu ɔ, e je Simeon ngɛ a kpɛti, nɛ e ha a fi lɛ ngɛ a hɛ mi. Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kpale kɛ ho Kanaan ya

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Yosef fa e tsɔli ɔmɛ ke a wo e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a blɛfo kotoku ɔmɛ a mi blɛfo nɛ a hyi tɔtɔɔtɔ. Jehanɛ se hu, e fa ke a kpale nɔ tsuaa nɔ sika nɛ e hɛɛ kɛ ba a kɛ wo e kotoku ɔ mi, nɛ a ha mɛ niye ní nɛ a ya ye ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ. Tsɔli ɔmɛ pee ja.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Benɛ a ya su nibwɔhi a to he ɔ, nɛ a ti nɔ kake pɛne e kotoku ɔ nya konɛ e ha e teji ɔ ní ɔ, e na e sika a ngɛ kotoku ɔ nya.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e de e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke, “A kpale ye sika a kɛ wo ye kotoku ɔ mi!” A tsui po, nɛ a kɛ he domi bi a sibi ke, “Mɛni po Mawu pee wɔ nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Benɛ a ba su a tsɛ Yakob ngɔ ngɛ Kanaan ɔ, a bɔ lɛ níhi tsuo nɛ a pee mɛ ɔ. A de lɛ ke,

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Wa de lɛ ke, ‘Tsa pi slaali ji wɔ; anɔkualetsɛmɛ ji wɔ.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Nyumu kake bimɛ ji wɔ. Jinɛ nyɛmimɛ nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ ji wɔ; se wa ti nɔ kake be je mi, nɛ jokuɛyo ɔ hu ngɛ wa tsɛ ngɔ ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ.’

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: konɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ nyɛ nyɛmi jokuɛyo ɔ kɛ ba. Enɛ ɔ ma kɛ le kaa anɔkualetsɛmɛ ji nyɛ, se pi slaali ji nyɛ. Ma kpale nyɛ nyɛmi ɔ kɛ ha nyɛ, nɛ nyɛ ma nyɛ hi hiɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛɛ ye jua faa.’ ”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Benɛ a ngɛ kotoku ɔmɛ a nya pɛnee ɔ, a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ na e sika kɛ kpɛɛ ɔ ngɛ e kotoku ɔ mi; benɛ a na sika a, a kɛ a tsɛ Yakob ɔ tsuo a tsui po.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a tsɛ Yakob de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ ma ha ye bimɛ ɔmɛ ma gbo ta ye he lo? Yosef be; Simeon be; nɛ jehanɛ, nyɛ ngɛ hlae nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ Benyamin hu kɛ ho. Nɔ yeyee maa hi mi pee kikɛ nɛ ɔ!”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Ruben de e tsɛ ɔ ke, “Ke i kpale we Benyamin ba ha we mo ɔ, lɛɛ gbee ye binyumuwi enyɔ ɔmɛ. Moo to Benyamin ngɔ wo ye dɛ mi, nɛ ma kpale lɛ kɛ ba ha mo.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Se Yakob de ke, “Ye bi ɔ kɛ nyɛ be yae; e nyɛmi ɔ gbo, nɛ lɛ nɔ kake too e piɛ. Ke i kɛ lɛ ha nyɛ ɔ, nɔ́ ko ma ya pee lɛ ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ. I bwɔ, nɛ nyɛ ma ha nɛ i kɛ aywilɛho maa ya gbeje.”

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Hwɔ ɔ nya ba wa ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob kɛ e we mi bi ɔmɛ ye blɛfo ɔ nɛ a kɛ je Egipt kɛ ba a tsuo ta a, Yakob de e bimɛ ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ kpale kɛ ya, nɛ nyɛ ya he niye ní bɔɔ kɛ ba.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Se ke o kplɛɛ we nɛ e kɛ wɔ nɛ ya a, wɔ hu wa be yae; ejakaa nyumu ɔ de wɔ ke ke waa kɛ wa nyɛmi ɔ bɛ ɔ, wa be e hɛngmɛ mi nae.”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Yakob bi mɛ ke, “Mɛni he je nyɛɛ kɛ haomi nɛ ɔ ba ye nɔ ɔ? Mɛni he je nɛ nyɛ de nyumu ɔ ke nyɛ ngɛ nyɛmi kpa ko hulɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: A he nɔ ke, “Nyumu nɛ ɔ ta wa nya mi saminya kɛ bi wɔ níhi nɛ kɔɔ wɔ nitsɛmɛ, kɛ wa weku li a he. E bi wɔ ke, ‘Nyɛ tsɛ ngɛ je mi kɛ mwɔɔ lo? Nyɛ ngɛ nyɛmi kpa ko hu lo?’ Wɔɔ lɛɛ e munyu ɔmɛ a heto kɛkɛ wa ha lɛ. Kɛ wa maa pee kɛ le kaa e ma de wɔ ke waa ngɔ wa nyɛmi ɔ kɛ ba kɛɛ?”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Yuda de e tsɛ Yakob ke, “Ngɔɔ jokuɛ ɔ ngɔ ha mi, nɛ́ wa pue blɔ nɔuu, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ hwɔ ko ba gbe wɔ, kɛ mo, kɛ wa bimɛ tsɔwitsɔwi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ ye wami kɛ da si ha lɛ; bi e si ngɛ ye dɛ. Ke i kpale we lɛ ba ha we mo fiafiaafia a, lɛɛ i yeɔ fɔ ye wami be ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Kaa tsa pi tsle nɛ wa to ɔ, jinɛ be nɛ ɔ mi wa ya ba si enyɔ momo.”

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: A tsɛ Yakob de mɛ ke, “Ke ja ji sane ɔ, lɛɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ ní kpakpa amɛ ekomɛ kɛ wo nyɛ kotoku ɔmɛ a mi, nɛ nyɛ kɛ ya ke ganɔ ɔ. Nyɛɛ ngɔ tsopa nu bɔɔ, bila, hwo bɔɔ, kɛ tsopahi kɛ a he via bɔɔ, gigɛ bɔɔ, kɛ ngmɛ́ bɔɔ.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, nyɛɛ hɛɛ sika nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ ma he ní ɔ, nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ nɔ́ nɛ a kpale ngɔ wo kotoku ɔmɛ a mi ha nyɛ ɔ kɛ ho; eko piɔ, e be a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ngɔ nyɛ nyɛmi ɔ, nɛ nyɛɛ ho esɔesɔ.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Mawu Ope ɔ nɛ ha nɛ nyumu ɔ nɛ na nyɛ mɔbɔ, konɛ e ngmɛɛ Benyamin, kɛ nyɛ nyɛmi kaketsɛ ɔ he ha nyɛ. Imi lɛɛ ke ji ye bimɛ ma gbo kɛ wo mi aywilɛho po, e ba mi ja.”

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ nike ní ɔmɛ, kɛ sika nɛ a kɛ yaa he ní ɔ, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ a kpale kɛ yaa a, nɛ a kɛ Benyamin tsuo pue nɔ kɛ ho Egipt ya. Benɛ a ya su ɔ, a kɛ a he ya tsɔɔ Yosef.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Yosef na Benyamin ngɛ a kpɛti ɔ, e de nyumu ɔ nɛ hyɛɛ e we ɔ nɔ ɔ ke, “O kɛ nyumu nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ya ye we ɔ mi. A kɛ mi maa ye ní piani nɛ ɔ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, yaa gbe lohwe nɛ o pee niye ní ngɔ to.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Tsɔlɔ ɔ pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yosef fa lɛ ɔ, nɛ e kɛ nyumu ɔmɛ ho Yosef we ɔ mi ya.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Benɛ a kɛ mɛ yaa Yosef we ɔ mi ɔ, a tsui po, nɛ a de a sibi ke, “Sika a nɛ a kpale ngɔ wo wa kotoku ɔmɛ a mi benɛ wa ba hiɛ ɔ kekleekle ɔ, lɔ ɔ he je nɛ a ngɔ wɔ kɛ ba hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ nɛ. A ma ba tua wɔ tlukaa; a ma kpɔ wa teji ɔmɛ ngɛ wa dɛ, nɛ a maa pee wɔ nyɔguɛhi.”

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a ya na tsɔlɔ ɔ nɛ hyɛɛ Yosef we ɔ nɔ ɔ ngɛ agbo ɔ nya, nɛ a de lɛ ke,

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: “Wa kpa mo pɛɛ, wa nyɔmtsɛ, wa ba hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ eko momo ba he niye ní.

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: Benɛ wa kpale wa se kɛ yaa, nɛ wa ya to si ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ ɔ, wa pɛne wa kotoku ɔmɛ a nya. Kɛkɛ ɔ, wa ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ na sika nɛ e kɛ ba he ní ɔ susui ngɛ e kotoku nya. Wa kpale sika a kɛ ba.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, wa hɛɛ sika kpa kɛ ba nɛ waa kɛ ma he niye ní. Wa li nɔ nɛ kpale wa sika a kɛ wo wa kotoku ɔmɛ a mi.”

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Tsɔlɔ ɔ de ke, “Nyɛ ko ye kɔmɔ. Nyɛ tsui nɛ ko po. Nyɛ Mawu ɔ, nyɛ tsɛ e Mawu ɔ, lɛ nɛ e kɛ sika a wo nyɛ kotoku ɔmɛ a mi ha nyɛ. Ye nine su nyɛ sika a nɔ.” Kɛkɛ nɛ e je Simeon kɛ ba ha mɛ.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Tsɔlɔ ɔ kɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ba Yosef we ɔ mi. E ha mɛ nyu nɛ a kɛ fɔ a nanehi a he, nɛ e ha a teji ɔmɛ ní.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: A dla nike ní ɔmɛ nɛ a kɛ ma ha Yosef ɔ ngɔ to, konɛ ke e ba we ɔ mi piani nɛ a kɛ ha lɛ; ejakaa a nu kaa a maa ye ní ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: A he nɔ ke, “Wa tsɛ ngɛ je mi kɛ mwɔɔ; e ngɛ saminya.” Kɛkɛ nɛ a kpla si, nɛ a kɛ a hɛ mi bu si.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Yosef na e nyɛmi Benyamin, e nyɛbi ɔ, e de ke, “Nyɛ nyɛmi jokuɛyo ɔ nɛ nyɛ wo e biɛ ta a ji nɛ ɔ lo? Ye bi, Mawu nɛ gbaa mo!”

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, e fɔ e hɛ mi, nɛ e je kpo kɛ ba. E bɔ mɔde mia e hɛ mi, nɛ e fa ke a kɛ niye ní ɔ nɛ ba ma si.

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: A to okplɔɔ munomuno etɛ: Yosef nɔ́ kake, e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ́ kake, kɛ Egipt bi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, mɛ hu a nɔ kake. A pee ja, ejakaa Egipt bi kɛ Hebri bi ka we nine kɛ yi ní; a hiee Hebri bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: A ha Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ sɛ ngɛ a wami nya, kɛ je nɔkɔtɔma a nɔ kɛ ya si jokuɛyo ɔ nɔ, nɛ a plɛ a hɛ mi ngɔ kpee Yosef. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ pee mɛ nyakpɛ nɛ a hyɛ a sibi a hɛ mi kɛ kpe.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: A gba ní kɛ je Yosef okplɔɔ ɔ he ya ha e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ Benyamin nɔ́ ɔ hiɛ pe a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɔ́ si enuɔ. A kɛ Yosef ye ní, nɛ a nu ní kɛ ya si mɛ tsuo a de dã.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Ngɔɔ ye sika hiɔ kplu ɔ kɛ wo jokuɛyo ɔ kotoku ɔ mi kɛ piɛ sika nɛ e kɛ ba he blɛfo ɔ he.” Tsɔlɔ ɔ pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yosef fa lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena mɔtu kpla a, a wo nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ blɔ kɛ ho kɛ a teji ɔmɛ.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Benɛ a je ma a mi, nɛ a sui he ko tsitsaa lolo ɔ, Yosef de tsɔlɔ ɔ nɛ hyɛɛ e we ɔ nɔ ɔ ke, “Tee si esɔ, nɛ o nyɛɛ nyumu ɔmɛ a se. Ke o ya na mɛ ɔ, bi mɛ ke, ‘Mɛni he je nyɛɛ kɛ yayami to kpakpa nɛ a pee nyɛ ɔ nane mi ɔ?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Mɛni he je nyɛ ju ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ sika hiɔ kplu ɔ? Kplu pɛ nɛ e kɛ nuu nyu ji lɔ ɔ nɛ, nɛ lɔ ɔ kɛ̃ e kɛ klaa. Nyɛ pee yayami agbo!’ ”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Benɛ tsɔlɔ ɔ ya na mɛ ɔ, e bi mɛ munyu nɛ ɔmɛ nɔuu.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: A he nɔ ke, “Wa nyɔmtsɛ, mɛni he je o kɛ wɔ ngɛ munyu tue kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Wa be nyɛe maa pee nɔ́ ko kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Sika a nɛ wa ya na ngɛ wa kotoku ɔmɛ a mi ɔ pohu wa kpale kɛ je Kanaan zugba a nɔ tɔɔ kɛ ba ha mo. Kɛ maa pee kɛɛ mɔ nɛ wa maa ju sika hiɔ, loo sika tsu ngɛ o nyɔmtsɛ ɔ we ɔ mi?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Ke a na nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ngɛ wa ti nɔ ko dɛ mi ɔ, a gbe lɛ, nɛ wɔ ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ, wa maa pee o nyɔguɛhi.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: E de mɛ ke, “Saminya! A pee kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ de ɔ. Se mohu, nɔ nɛ dɛ mi nɛ a maa na kplu ɔ ngɛ ɔ, lɛ pɛ ji nɔ nɛ maa pee ye nyɔguɛ ɔ nɛ; nyɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ lɛɛ nyɛ maa ye nyɛ he.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a he sɔ kɛ je kotoku ɔmɛ ngɛ a teji ɔmɛ a nɔ kɛ ma si, nɛ a pɛne nya.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Yosef tsɔlɔ ɔ hyɛ kotoku ɔmɛ a mi fitsofitso, kɛ je nɔkɔtɔma a nɔ́ ɔ mi kɛ ya gbe nya ngɛ jokuɛyo ɔ nɔ́ ɔ mi. Nɛ a ya na kplu ɔ ngɛ Benyamin kotoku ɔ mi.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kɛ aywilɛho hia a he tade ɔmɛ. A ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ wo e teji nɔ ní ekohu, nɛ a kpale a se kɛ ho ma a mi ya.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Benɛ Yuda kɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ba Yosef we ɔ mi ɔ, Yosef ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ mwɔɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ a kpla si, nɛ a kɛ a hɛ mi bu si ngɛ e hɛ mi.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: Yosef bi mɛ ke, “Mɛni nyɛ pee nɛ ɔ? Anɛ nyɛ li kaa nɔmlɔ kaa imi ɔ, i klaa lo?”

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Yuda he nɔ ke, “Wa nyɔmtsɛ, mɛni ngɛ wa nya nɛ wa ma de mo? Kɛ wa maa pee kɛ je wa nya kɛɛ? Mawu nitsɛ je wɔ kpo kaa wa tɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, piɔ lɛɛ o nyɔguɛhi ji wɔ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ, se pi nɔ nɛ a na kplu ɔ ngɛ e dɛ mi ɔ kɛkɛ.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Yosef he nɔ ke, “Dɛbi! I be ja pee kɔkɔɔkɔ! Nɔ nɛ a na kplu ɔ ngɛ e dɛ ɔ, lɛ pɛ ji nɔ nɛ maa pee ye nyɔguɛ ɔ nɛ. Nyɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ kpale kɛ ho nyɛ tsɛ ngɔ ya fiafiaafia.” Yuda kpa pɛɛ ha Benyamin

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yuda hɛ lɛ kɛ su Yosef he, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Nyɔmtsɛ, i kpa mo pɛɛ, ha nɛ ma kɛ hiami sane kake nɛ ɔ pɛ fɔ o hɛ mi. O ngɛ kaa Farao ɔ kɛ̃. O mi mi ko fu mi.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: I kpa mo pɛɛ, o bi wɔ ke, ‘Nyɛ tsɛ ngɛ je mi lo? Nyɛ ngɛ nyɛminyumu kpa ko hu lo?’

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Wa de mo ke, ‘Wa tsɛ ngɛ je mi se e bwɔ. Wa senɔ nɛ ji wa tsɛ nakutsomibi nɛ e fɔ ngɛ e bwɔmi si hu ngɛ. Lɛ nɔ ɔ e nyɛminyumu ɔ gbo, nɛ lɛ pɛ ji e nyɛbi nɛ piɛ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, wa tsɛ suɔ lɛ saminya.’

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: O fa wɔ ke waa ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba nɛ o na lɛ kɛ o hɛngmɛ.

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Se o kplɛɛ we. O de wɔ ke, ‘Ke nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ nyɛmi wayo ɔ bɛ nɛ ma na lɛ ɔ, lɛɛ nyɛ be ye hɛ mi nae.’

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: “Benɛ wa kpale kɛ ho wa tsɛ ɔ ngɔ ya a, wa ya bɔ lɛ nɔ́ nɛ o de wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, e de wɔ ke waa kpale kɛ ba hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ, nɛ wa ba he niye ní kɛ ba.

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Wa de lɛ ke, ‘Ja wa nyɛmi wayo ɔ piɛ wa he loko wa maa ya. Ke wa nyɛmi wayo ɔ kɛ wɔ yɛ ɔ, a be wɔ blɔ ngmɛe nɛ waa na nyumu ɔ hɛ mi.’

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Wa tsɛ de wɔ ke, ‘Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ le kaa ye yo Rahel ɔ, binyumuhi enyɔ i kɛ lɛ fɔ.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, a ti nɔ kake je kpo, nɛ i nɛ lɛ hu kɛ ba si piɔ; daa nɛ ɔ, i susuɔ kaa pu mi lohwehi nɛ a tsɔtslɔɔ e mi.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ ngɔ nɔ nɛ ɔ hu kɛ je ye he, nɛ nɔ́ ko ya pee lɛ ɔ, nyɛ ma ha i kɛ aywilɛho maa ya gbeje; i bwɔ.’ ”

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ se hu, i ngɔ ye wami kɛ da si ha niheyo wayo ɔ. I ka tsaatsɛ kita, nɛ i de lɛ ke ke i kpale we Benyamin kɛ ba ha we lɛ fiafiaafia a, lɛɛ i yeɔ fɔ ye wami be ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, ye nyɔmtsɛ, ma hi hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ kaa o nyɔguɛ ngɛ niheyo wayo ɔ nane mi; ha nɛ e kɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a kpale kɛ ho.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Kɛ ma pee kɛ kpale kɛ ya tsaatsɛ ngɔ kɛɛ, nɛ niheyo wayo ɔ piɛ we ye he kɛ yɛ? Aywilɛho nɛ maa pee tsaatsɛ ɔ, i be nyɛe ma hyɛ.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ lɛɛ Yosef nyɛ we nɛ e mia e hɛ mi hu ngɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ nɛ daa si ɔ a hɛ mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e fa mɛ ke mɛ tsuo a je tsu ɔ mi. Benɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo je lejɛ ɔ, Yosef je e he si ngɔ tsɔɔ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: E fo ya boboobo. Egipt bi ɔmɛ nu he, nɛ munyu ɔ ya pɛ ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ mi hulɔ.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yosef de e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ekohu ke, “Nyɛɛ hɛ nyɛ kɛ ba ye ngɔ.” A pee ja, nɛ e ya nɔ de ke, “Imi ji nyɛ nyɛmi Yosef ɔ nɛ nyɛ jua kɛ ba Egipt ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: E ko hao nyɛ, nɛ nyɛ ko pia nyɛ he hulɔ kaa nyɛ jua mi kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ. Mawu nitsɛ lɛ tsɔ mi kɛ nyɛɛ nyɛ hɛ mi, konɛ ma ba he nihi a yi wami.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Jeha enyɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ hwɔ ba zugba a nɔ tsuo. Se e pa piɛ jeha enuɔ ngɛ wa hɛ mi nɛ a be ní gbae ɔ, a be ní kpae hulɔ.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Mawu tsɔ mi kɛ nyɛɛ nyɛ hɛ mi, konɛ ma ba he nyɛ yi wami ngɛ nyakpɛ blɔ nɛ ɔ nɔ; nɛ ma hyɛ nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ nina nɛ wo ngmɛdu ngɛ zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Tsa pi nyɛ nɛ nyɛ ha i ba hiɛ ɔ; Mawu mohu lɛ ha nɛ i ba hiɛ ɔ nɛ. E ngɔ mi ngɔ pee Farao ɔ ga wolɔ; imi lɛ i hyɛɛ e we ɔ nɔ, nɛ imi lɛ i yeɔ Egipt zugba a tsuo nɔ.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ kpale kɛ ho tsaatsɛ ngɔ ya esɔesɔ, nɛ nyɛ ya de lɛ ke bɔ nɛ e bi Yosef ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Mawu ngɔ mi ngɔ pee Egipt zugba a tsuo nɔ yelɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ba nɔuu; koo to tsle.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: O ma ba hi Goshen zugba a nɔ, ngɛ ye kasa nya. O kɛ o bimɛ ɔmɛ, o bibimɛ ɔmɛ, o to ɔmɛ, o na amɛ, kɛ o weto ní tsuo nɛ ba.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ke o ba je Goshen ɔ, ma hyɛ o nɔ. E piɛ jeha enuɔ sɔuu ngɛ wa hɛ mi loko hwɔ ɔ se maa po; nɛ i be suɔe nɛ mo, loo o we mi bi ɔmɛ, loo o lohwe ɔmɛ nɛ ba ha hwɔ.’ ”

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Yosef ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Jehanɛ, nyɛɛ kɛ ye nyɛmi Benyamin tsuo nyɛ na kaa imi Yosef tutuutu lɛ i kɛ nyɛ ngɛ munyu tue ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ya bɔ tsaatsɛ blɔ nya ngua nɛ i hɛɛ ngɛ Egipt, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ ba na kɛ nyɛ hɛngmɛ; nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ lɛ nɛ ba hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ nɔuu.”

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, benɛ Yosef ngɛ ya foe kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ, e fua e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kakaaka, nɛ e fiɔ a nya he. Kɛkɛ nɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kɛ lɛ bɔni ní sɛɛmi.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Benɛ munyu ɔ ya pɛ ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ mi kaa Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ba a, Farao ɔ kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ a bua jɔ.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ de Yosef ke, “De o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke a wo a lohwe ɔmɛ a nɔ ní, nɛ a kpale kɛ ho Kanaan zugba a nɔ ya.

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: Ha nɛ a ya ngɔ a tsɛ, kɛ a we mi bi ɔmɛ, nɛ a kpale kɛ ba hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ. Ma ha mɛ Egipt zugba a he nɛ hi pe kulaa, nɛ a ma na ní kpakpa babauu maa ye.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, de mɛ ke a ngɔ ta zugba lɛ kɛ je Egipt kɛ ho, nɛ a kɛ ya ngɔ a yi ɔmɛ, kɛ a bimɛ tsɔwitsɔwi ɔmɛ, kɛ a tsɛ ɔ kɛ ba.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: E ko hao mɛ kaa a maa je a weto níhi a he; ejakaa Egipt zugba a nɔ ní kpakpahi tsuo maa pee a nɔ́.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Yakob bimɛ ɔmɛ pee kaa bɔ nɛ a de mɛ ɔ. Yosef ha mɛ ta zugba lɛhi kaa bɔ nɛ Farao ɔ fa ke a pee ɔ; nɛ e ha mɛ niye ní nɛ a maa ye ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ hulɔ.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Jehanɛ e ha a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ he dlami tade kakaaka; se Benyamin lɛɛ, e ha lɛ sika hiɔ yi lafa etɛ kɛ he dlami tade enuɔ.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Níhi nɛ e mane e tsɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: teji nyɔngma kɛ a se mi Egipt ní kpakpahi, kɛ teji yo nyɔngma kɛ a se mi blɛfo kɛ abolo, kɛ niye ní nɛ e tsɛ ɔ maa ye ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ ba.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, e wo e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ blɔ, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nɛ nyɛ yaa nɛ ɔ, nyɛ ko ya pɛ ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ je Egipt, nɛ a kpale kɛ ba a tsɛ Yakob ngɔ ngɛ Kanaan.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: A ba bɔ lɛ amaniɛ ke, “Yosef ngɛ je mi kɛ mwɔɔ, nɛ lɛ ji nɔ nɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a tsuo nɔ yee!” Yakob he mi po, ejakaa e he we mɛ yi.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Se benɛ a bɔ lɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Yosef de mɛ, nɛ e na zugba lɛ ɔmɛ nɛ Yosef ngɔ mane nɛ a kɛ ba ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba a, e nɔ gbagba te.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Yakob de ke, “Ye bi Yosef ngɛ je mi kɛ mwɔɔ! Enɛ ɔ kɛkɛ hiɛ ha mi! Ma ya nɛ ma ya na e hɛ mi loko ma gbo.”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Yakob hia, kɛ e nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́. Benɛ e su Beersheba a, e sã bɔ kɛ ha e tsɛ Isak Mawu ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Nyɔ mi ɔ, Mawu kɛ lɛ tu munyu ngɛ nina mi. Mawu tsɛ lɛ ke, “Yakob, Yakob!” Yakob he nɔ ke, “I ngɛ hiɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Mawu de lɛ ke, “Imi ji Mawu, o tsɛ Isak Mawu ɔ. Koo ye gbeye kaa o maa ya Egipt; ejakaa ma ha nɛ o nina maa pee ma agbo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: I kɛ mo maa ya Egipt, nɛ o ma ya gbo ngɔ fɔ Yosef gugue mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ; se o nina lɛɛ, ma kpale mɛ kɛ ba hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ ekohu.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Binyumuhi nɛ Yakob kɛ Lea, fɔ ngɛ Mesopotamia ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. A fɔ biyo kake hulɔ, nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Dina. Nina tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ, nyumuhi kɛ yihi nɛ Yakob na kɛ gu Lea nɔ ɔ, a hiɛmi ji nyingmi etɛ kɛ etɛ.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Ke Farao ɔ tsɔ ba tsɛ nyɛ, nɛ e bi nyɛ ke mɛni ní tsumi nyɛ tsuɔ ɔ,

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Nimli nyɔngma kɛ ekpa nɛ ɔmɛ ji nina nɛ Yakob na kɛ gu Zilpa nɔ. Zilpa ji nyɔguɛ yo ɔ nɛ Laban ha e biyo Lea a nɛ.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Nimli kpaago nɛ ɔmɛ ji nina nɛ Yakob na kɛ gu Bilha nɔ. Bilha ji nyɔguɛ yo ɔ nɛ Laban ha e biyo Rahel ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Yakob nina tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ nɛ ya Egipt ɔ, ke a je e binyumu ɔmɛ a yi ɔmɛ kɛ je mi ɔ, a hiɛmi ji nyingmi ekpa kɛ ekpa.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Yakob tsɔ Yuda kɛ sɛ hlami, konɛ e ya de Yosef nɛ e kɛ lɛ ba kpe ngɛ Goshen. E kɛ we nɛ a ya su Goshen.

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Yosef hi e zugba ta lɛ ɔ mi, nɛ e ho konɛ e ya kpee e tsɛ ngɛ Goshen. Benɛ a kpe hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi ɔ, Yosef kɛ e nine kpla e tsɛ kuɛ mi, nɛ e fo ya ngɔ pue e nɔ hluu.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Yakob de Yosef ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ nɛ i na o hɛ mi, nɛ i na kaa o ngɛ je mi kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ, ke i gbo hu, e pi nɔ́ ko.”

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yosef de e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ e tsɛ weku li ɔmɛ ke, “I yaa nɛ ma ya de Farao ɔ ke, ‘Ye nyɛmimɛ, kɛ tsaatsɛ weku ɔ tsuo je Kanaan kɛ ba ye ngɔ.’

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Ma de lɛ ke to hyɛli kɛ na tsɔ̃li ji nyɛ; nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ to ɔmɛ, nyɛ na amɛ, kɛ nyɛ weto ní tsuo ba.

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: nyɛ de lɛ ke, ‘Kɛ je wa nihe mi kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ, lohwe wa lɛɛ; wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ hu kikɛmɛ a ní tsumi nɛ ɔ nɔuu a tsu.’ Ke nyɛ de lɛ ja a, e ma ha nɛ nyɛɛ hi Goshen zugba a nɔ; ejakaa Egipt bimɛ hiee lohwe lɛli.”

english_verse: Joseph took five of his brothers to the king and told him, “My father and my brothers have come from Canaan. They have brought their sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else they own to the region of Goshen.” Then he introduced his brothers to the king,
translation_verse: Yosef hla e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a ti nihi enuɔ, nɛ e kɛ mɛ ya tsɔɔ Farao ɔ. Yosef de Farao ɔ ke, “Tsaatsɛ kɛ ye nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ je Kanaan zugba a nɔ kɛ ba. A kɛ a tohi, kɛ a nahi, kɛ a weto ní tsuo ba. Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, a pueɔ si ngɛ Goshen zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ bi Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke, “Mɛni ní tsumi nyɛ tsuɔ?” A he nɔ ke, “Lohwe lɛli ji wɔ; wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ hu kikɛmɛ a ní tsumi nɛ ɔ nɔuu a tsu.

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Wa ba nɛ wa ba hi hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ bɔɔ. Wa nɛ niye ní ha wa lohwe ɔmɛ ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ, ejakaa hwɔ ɔ nya wa ngɛ lejɛ ɔ wawɛɛ nitsɛ. Wa kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o ha nɛ waa hi Goshen zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ de Yosef ke, “O tsɛ kɛ o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ba mo tomi.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Egipt zugba a lɛ ngɛ o hɛ mi tilaa nɛ ɔ nɛ. Ha nɛ o tsɛ kɛ o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a hi Goshen zugba a nɔ; lejɛ ɔ ji he nɛ hi pe zugba a tsuo. Ke o na kaa a ti ni komɛ le lohwe lɛmi ní tsumi nɛ ɔ saminya a, ha nɛ a ya hyɛ imi nitsɛ ye lohwe ɔmɛ a nɔ.”

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Yosef ngɔ e tsɛ Yakob hu kɛ ba tsɔɔ Farao ɔ. Yakob gbaa Farao ɔ,

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: nɛ Farao ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Jeha nyɛmɛ o ye?”

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yakob gbaa Farao ɔ ekohu, nɛ e je e ngɔ.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Yosef ha e tsɛ kɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ sihi he ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ. Kaa bɔ nɛ Farao ɔ fa lɛ Yosef ɔ, e ha mɛ weto ní ngɛ Rameses kasa nya, nɛ ji zugba nɛ hi pe zugba a tsuo.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Sika nɛ a kɛ je Egipt kɛ Kanaan zugba amɛ a nɔ kɛ ba he blɛfo ɔ, Yosef bua lɛ tsuo nya, nɛ e ngɔ kɛ ho matsɛ we ɔ mi ya.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Benɛ sika nɛ ngɛ Egipt kɛ Kanaan tsuo ba ta a, Egipt bi ɔmɛ ba de Yosef ke, “Ha wɔ ní nɛ waa ye! Anɛ o maa hi wɔ hyɛe nɛ wa gbo lo? Wa sika tsuo ta.”

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Yosef he nɔ ke, “Ke nyɛ sika ta a, nyɛɛ ngɔ nyɛ lohwe ɔmɛ kɛ ba, nɛ ma ha nyɛ niye ní kɛ to nya.”

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Jeha nɛ nyɛɛ se ɔ, Egipt bi ɔmɛ ba Yosef ngɔ ekohu, nɛ a ba de lɛ ke, “Wa nyɔmtsɛ, wa be mo nɔ́ ko nɔ laae. Anɔkuale mi ɔ, wa sika tsuo ta; nɛ wa lohwe ɔmɛ hu ba pee o níhi. Nɔ́ kpa ko pa be wa dɛ pe wɔ nitsɛmɛ, kɛ wa zugba a.

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Yosef he Egipt zugba a tsuo kɛ ha Farao ɔ. Egipt no tsuaa Egipt no jua e zugba, ejakaa hwɔ ɔ nya ba wa tsɔ. Nɛ zugba a tsuo ba pee Farao ɔ nɔ́.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Zugba pɛ nɛ Yosef he we ji osɔfo ɔmɛ a zugba a. Osɔfo ɔmɛ lɛɛ e hia we kaa a jua a zugba a, ejakaa mɛɛ lɛɛ a haa mɛ niye ní kɛ jeɔ Farao ɔ nitsɛ ngɔ.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Yosef de ma a ke, “I he nyɛ kɛ nyɛ zugba a mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ kɛ ha Farao ɔ. Blɛfo ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; nyɛ ba ngɔ nɛ nyɛ ya du.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ kpa ní ɔ, nyɛɛ ngɔ mi dlami enuɔ mi kake ba ha Farao ɔ, konɛ nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ɔ nɛ pee nyɛ nitsɛmɛ, kɛ nyɛ bimɛ, kɛ nyɛ we mi bimɛ nyɛ nɔ́; nyɛɛ ye eko, nɛ nyɛ du eko.”

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Ma a he nɔ ke, “O he wa yi wami! Wa nyɔmtsɛ, ke e sa o hɛ mi ɔ, wa maa pee Farao ɔ nyɔguɛhi.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yosef wo mlaa nɛ ngɛ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, kaa Egipt zugba a niba ní ɔ mi dlami enuɔ mi kake maa pee Farao ɔ nɔ́. Osɔfo ɔmɛ a zugba a pɛ ji nɔ́ nɛ be Farao ɔ nɔ́ pee. Yakob nyagbe hiami nɔ́

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ hi Goshen zugba a nɔ ngɛ Egipt. A na ní, nɛ a fɔ bimɛ, nɛ a he hiɛ babauu.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob gbenɔ be su ɔ, e tsɛ e bi Yosef, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ke o suɔ nɛ o sa ye hɛ mi ɔ, ngɔɔ o nine kɛ wo ye fiɔ enyɔ ɔmɛ a kpɛ, nɛ o ka mi kita kaa o maa ye mi anɔkuale, nɛ o be mi pue ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Yakob de Yosef ke, “Ka mi kita kaa o maa pee ja.” Yosef ka lɛ kita kaa e maa pee ja. Kɛkɛ nɛ Yakob kpla si ngɛ e sa a yiti je, nɛ e na si.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, a ba de Yosef ke e tsɛ be he wami. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e ngɔ e binyumu enyɔ ɔmɛ, Manase kɛ Efraim kɛ ho, konɛ e ya slaa e tsɛ ɔ.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Benɛ a de Yakob ke e bi Yosef ma lɛ slaami ɔ, Yakob wlua lɛ, nɛ e te si, nɛ e hi si ngɛ sa a nɔ.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Yakob de Yosef ke, “Mawu Ope ɔ je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ mi ngɛ Luz, ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ, nɛ e gbaa mi.

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: E de mi ke, ‘Ma ha mo bimɛ babauu, nɛ o nina ma ba pee mahi babauu. Ma ngɔ zugba nɛ ɔ ngɔ ha o nina, nɛ e maa pee a weto ní kɛ maa ya neneene.’ ”

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: Yakob ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Binyumuwi enyɔ nɛ o fɔ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ loko i ba hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ maa pee ye bimɛ, kaa bɔ nɛ Ruben kɛ Simeon ngɛ ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Bimɛ nɛ o ma fɔ ngɛ a se ɔ maa pee moo o níhi; se mɛɛ lɛɛ a ma na a weto ní kaa Efraim kɛ Manase a nina.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: I ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ pee ngɛ o nyɛ Rahel he. Benɛ i je Mesopotamia kɛ ma a, Rahel gbo fɔ ye nɔ ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ, ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ, benɛ e piɛ bɔɔ nɛ ma su Efrat ɔ. I pu lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ngɛ Efrat blɔ ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob was very old and almost blind. He did not recognize the two boys, and so he asked Joseph, “Who are these boys?” Joseph answered, “They are my sons. God has given them to me here in Egypt.” “Bring them to me,” Jacob said. “I want to give them my blessing.” Joseph brought the boys to him, and he hugged and kissed them.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, Yakob hɛngmɛ hyɛ we nɔ́ saminya; ejakaa e bwɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yosef ngɔ jokuɛwi ɔmɛ kɛ ba su Yakob he haa. Yakob fua mɛ atuu, nɛ e fiɔ a nya he.

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Yakob de Yosef ke, “Jinɛ i susuu we kaa ma na o hɛ mi ekohu; se hyɛ, o bimɛ pohu Mawu ha nɛ i ba na mɛ.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yosef je jokuɛwi ɔmɛ kɛ je e tsɛ ɔ tɛ nɔ; nɛ e kpla si ngɛ e hɛ mi, nɛ e ngɔ e hɛ mi ngɔ bu si.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Yosef ngɔ Efraim ba da Yakob muɔ nine nɔ, nɛ e ngɔ Manase ba da e tsɛ ɔ hiɔ nine nɔ.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Se Yakob je blɔ tsake e nine ɔmɛ; e kɛ e hi ɔ nine fɔ Efraim, jokuɛyo ɔ yi mi, nɛ e kɛ e muɔ nine fɔ Manase, nɔkɔtɔma a mohu yi mi.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e gbaa Yosef, nɛ e de ke, “Mawu ɔ nɛ ye nɛ̃ Abraham kɛ tsaatsɛ Isak sɔmɔ lɛ ɔ, e gbaa nyumuwi nɛ ɔmɛ! Mawu ɔ nɛ hyɛ mi kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, e gbaa nyumuwi nɛ ɔmɛ!

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: Mawu bɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ ye nɔ, nɛ je mi kɛ je haomihi tsuo a mi ɔ, e gbaa nyumuwi nɛ ɔmɛ! Nyumuwi nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a wo imi, kɛ nɛnɛ Abraham, kɛ tsaatsɛ Isak wa biɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi nyami daa! A fɔ, nɛ a he nɛ hiɛ babauu ngɛ zugba a nɔ!”

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yosef na kaa e tsɛ ɔ ngɔ e hiɔ nine ngɔ fɔ Efraim yi mi ɔ, e ngɔɛ e nya. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, e nu e tsɛ ɔ nine si, nɛ e je e nine ɔ kɛ je Efraim yi mi kɛ ya fɔ Manase yi mi.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: E de e tsɛ ɔ ke, “Tsaatsɛ, dɛbi, pi ja! Nɔ nɛ ɔ mohu ji bitɛte; ngɔɔ o hiɔ nine ngɔ fɔ e yi mi.”

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Se e tsɛ ɔ kplɛɛ we. E tsɛ ɔ de ke, “I le, ye bi, i le. Manase ɔ, lɛ hu e nina ma ba pee ma agbo hwɔɔ se. Se mohu ɔ, e senɔ ɔ ma ba pee nɔmlɔ agbo pe lɛ, nɛ e senɔ ɔ nina ma ba pee je ma nguanguahi.”

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yakob gbaa nyumuwi ɔmɛ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, nɛ e de ke, “Israel bi ɔmɛ maa ngɔ nyɛ biɛ kɛ gbaa nihi. A ma de ke, ‘Mawu nɛ ha nɛ nyɛɛ pee kaa Efraim kɛ Manase.’ ” Kikɛ nɛ ɔ Yakob pee kɛ ngɔ Manase nɔkɔtɔma blɔ nya a kɛ ha Efraim.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yakob de Yosef ke, “Kaa bɔ nɛ o ngɛ hyɛe ɔ, i miɔ nɛ ma gbo. Mawu kɛ nyɛ maa hi si, nɛ e maa kpale nyɛ kɛ ya nyɛ nɛmɛ a zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Yakob tsɔ ya de e bimɛ ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ ba bua nyɛ he nya nɛ ma de nyɛ nɔ́ nɛ maa ba nyɛ nɔ hwɔɔ se.

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: “Ruben, mo ji ye bitɛte; mo ji ye he wami, kɛ ye nihe mi kekleekle bi. Mo ji nɔ nɛ bu ngɛ o he, nɛ o ngɛ he wami pe ye bimɛ ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: O ngɛ kaa pa nɛ hia kɛ bee. Se jehanɛ lɛɛ, o kekleekle blɔ he ɔ ma bɔ mo. Ejakaa o kɛ ye plã ya hwɔ si Nɛ o ble o tsɛ sa a.

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: “Simeon kɛ Levi ɔ, nyɛmimɛ ji mɛ. A kɛ a dɛ mi dade po tsuɔ yi wu tso ní tsumi.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: I kɛ mɛ be soe kɔkɔɔkɔ, I kɛ mɛ be bɔe hulɔ, Ejakaa ke a mi mi fu ɔ, a gbeɔ nɔmlɔ, Nɛ a plaa nahi kɛ jeɔ a hɛja.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: A gbiɛ a mi mi fumi ɔ, Ejakaa e nya wa, nɛ a kɛ peeɔ yi wu tso níhi. Ma gbɛ mɛ ngɔ fĩa Israel zugba a nɔ ngɛ a ma mi bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: “Yuda, o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ma je o yi. O ma kpata o he nyɛli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi. O nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ma kpla si ngɛ o hɛ mi.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Yuda ngɛ kaa jata nɛ ya ye de lo nɛ e kpale ba ba buu si, ngɛ e he jɔɔe; mɛnɔ ma nyɛ maa tsɛ̃ɛ̃ lɛ?

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: E fiɔ e teji ngɔ woɔ wai tso he E fiɔ e teji bimɛ kɛ woɔ wai tso kpakpahi a he. E fɔɔ e tadehi a he ngɛ wai nɛ tsuɔ kaa muɔ mi.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: E hɛngmɛ tsuɔ kɔlukɔlu pe wai. Jã kɛ̃ e lungu hiɛ futafuta pe na nyɔ nyu.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
