translation_verse: “Zebulun maa hi wo nya. E hi he ɔ maa pee lɛsimuɔ he, nɛ e kɛ Sidon maa wo huzu.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: “Isakar ngɛ kaa teji nɛ e wuhi a mi tsa; E buu si ngɛ lohwehi a tsuhi a mi.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: “Dan maa ye e ma mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ kaa Israel wɛtso kpa amɛ.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: “Yawɛ, i ngɛ mo blɔ hyɛe nɛ o ba kpɔ mi.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: “Asher zugba a maa ba ní saminya; E ma ha niye ní nɛ sa matsɛmɛ.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: “Naftali ngɛ kaa tso ko nɛ bɔ. Nɛ e gba tso kɔni saminyawiiwi.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: “Yosef ngɛ kaa nga mi teji ngɛ pa he. E ngɛ kaa nga mi okpɔngɔ bi ngɛ yoku he.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Se Yosef lɛɛ e kɛ̃ɛ̃ ɔ ji e dɛ gblegbleegble. E he wami ɔ je Yakob Mawu Ope ɔ dɛ mi, To hyɛlɔ ɔ, nɛ ji Israel he bulɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: O tsɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ nɛ gbaa mo, Mawu Ope ɔ nɛ gbaa mo. E ha nɛ hiɔmi nɛ nɛ ha mo kɛ je hiɔwe; E ha nɛ nyu nɛ ba ha mo kɛ je zugba a mi. E ha mo lohwehi kɛ bimɛ babauu.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: E ha mo ngma kɛ mɔmɔhi. E ha mo ní kpakpahi kɛ je blema yoku ɔmɛ a nɔ. Mo Yosef, nɛ a hla mo ngɔ to kɛ je o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ, Mawu nɛ gbaa mo ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: Jacob told his sons: Soon I will die, and I want you to bury me in Machpelah Cave. Abraham bought this cave as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite, and it is near the town of Mamre in Canaan. Abraham and Sarah are buried there, and so are Isaac and Rebekah. I buried Leah there too.
translation_verse: Lejɛ ɔ a pu Abraham kɛ e yo Sara ngɛ; lejɛ ɔ a pu Isak kɛ e yo Rebeka ngɛ; nɛ lejɛ ɔ ji he nɛ imi hu i pu Lea ngɛ.

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Zugba a kɛ tɛ puɔ ɔ nɛ ngɛ nɔ ɔ, Hit bi ɔmɛ a dɛ a he ngɛ. Nyɛ ya pu mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob ka e bimɛ ɔmɛ kita a gbe nya a, e ya hwɔ si ekohu, nɛ e gbo.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Yosef wo ya ngɔ pue e tsɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ e fiɔ e nya he.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Benɛ a pee ya gbe nya a, Yosef de matsɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “I kpa nyɛ pɛɛ nɛ nyɛ ya na Farao ɔ ha mi.

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ he nɔ ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya pu o tsɛ ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ o ka lɛ kita ke o maa pee ɔ.”

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Benɛ a su ngma mi sami he ɔ ngɛ Atad, ngɛ Yordan pa a beleku je ɔ, a wo yana wawɛɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ be saii; nɛ Yosef pee kusumi kɛ nyɛ ya ligbi kpaago.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Yakob bimɛ ɔmɛ pee kaa bɔ nɛ e fa mɛ ɔ.

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob gbo se ɔ, Yosef nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ de ke, “Eko piɔ, wa he dɔmi ngɛ Yosef mi kɛ mwɔɔ, nɛ e maa to wɔ yayami tsuo nɛ wa pee lɛ ɔ nane mi.”

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a ngɔ sɛ gbi ngɔ mane Yosef ke, “Loko tsaatsɛ gbo ɔ,

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: e ke wa de mo ke, ‘I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o kɛ o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a yayami nɛ a pee mo ɔ ngɔ pa mɛ.’ Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, wa kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o ngɔ wa yayami ɔ ngɔ pa wɔ; ejakaa wɔ hu o tsɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ lɛ wa jaa.” Benɛ a ya bɔ Yosef amaniɛ nɛ ɔ, e wo ya.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nitsɛmɛ ba, nɛ a ba kpla si ngɛ e hɛ mi, nɛ a de lɛ ke, “Wɔ o nyɔguɛ ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Se Yosef de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ ko ye gbeye. Nyɛ susu kaa Mawu ji mi lo?

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ lɛɛ nyɛ so kaa nyɛ maa pee mi yayami, se Mawu tsake nyɛ yi mi tomi ɔ kɛ pee nɔ́ kpakpa; bɔ nɛ pee nɛ e kɛ he nihi babauu a yi wami, kaa bɔ nɛ e ba mi mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛ ko ye gbeye. Ma lɛ nyɛ, kɛ nyɛ bimɛ ɔmɛ.” Bɔ nɛ Yosef pee nɛ e kɛ munyu ngɔngɔɛhi wo e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ bua ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Yosef gbo

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Yosef kɛ e tsɛ we mi bi ɔmɛ hi Egipt. E ye jeha lafa kɛ nyɔngma benɛ e gbo ɔ.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: E he bibimɛ kɛ gu Efraim nɔ. Jehanɛ, Manase binyumu Makir hu fɔ bimɛ kɛ wo weku ɔ mi.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Yosef de e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke, “E be kɛe nɛ ma gbo. Se Mawu maa hyɛ nyɛ nɔ kɛ̃, nɛ e ma kpaka nyɛ kɛ je zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ kɛ ya zugba a nɛ e wo Abraham, kɛ Isak, kɛ Yakob he si ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Be ko se ɔ, Yosef kɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ jamɛ a yi nɔ bi ɔmɛ tsuo ba gbo.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Se a nina nɛ ji Israel bi ɔmɛ ɔ, bi ngɛ a he; a fɔ babauu nɛ a he hiɛ, nɛ a hyi zugba a nɔ tɔ. A he hu wa saminya.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Jehanɛ ɔ, matsɛ he ko ba bɔni tsɛ yemi ngɛ Egipt, nɛ lɛɛ e li Yosef.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: E de e ma mi bi ɔmɛ ke, “Tse nyɛ na kaa Israel bi ɔmɛ hiɛ tsɔ, nɛ a he hu wa saminya.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ha waa to a he ga, ke pi ja a, a ma ba hiɛ tsɔ pe nine, nɛ ke ta ko ba a, a ma ya piɛ wa he nyɛli ɔmɛ a he, nɛ a kɛ wɔ maa hwu, nɛ a maa tu fo kɛ je.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Egipt bi ɔmɛ ngɔ nyɔguɛhi a nɔ yeli ngɔ to Israel bi ɔmɛ a nya, konɛ a wa mɛ yi mi kɛ ní tsumihi nɛ he wa. Israel bi ɔmɛ ma Pitom kɛ Rameses, nɛ ji mahi nɛ a toɔ ní ngɛ a mi kɛ ha Farao ɔ.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Se si abɔ nɛ a ngɛ mɛ yi mi wae ɔ, si abɔ nɛ a ngɛ hiɛe nɛ a ngɛ gbɛe kɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ hae. Egipt bi ɔmɛ ye Israel bi ɔmɛ gbeye.

english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: A ha nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ tsu ní kaa nyɔguɛhi.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: A hɛɛ zu, a peeɔ bliikisi, nɛ a tsuɔ ngmɔ ní tsumi slɔɔtohi; nɛ ní tsumi ɔ eko tsuaa eko mi ɔ, a waa mɛ yi mi wawɛɛ.

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Se fɔliyi ɔmɛ yee Mawu gbeye; a gbi binyumuwi ɔmɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Egipt matsɛ ɔ fa mɛ ɔ; mohu ɔ, a baa a yi.

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Fɔliyi ɔmɛ de Farao ɔ ke, “Hebri yi ɔmɛ be kaa Egipt yi ɔmɛ; mɛɛ lɛɛ a he wa saminya, nɛ a fɔmi ɔ sɔɔ. Loko fɔlɔyo ko ke e suu a ngɔ ɔ, a fɔ momo.”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Akɛnɛ fɔliyi ɔmɛ yee Mawu gbeye he je ɔ, Mawu gbaa mɛ, nɛ e ha mɛ nitsɛmɛ bimɛ. Israel bi ɔmɛ hu fɔ babauu, nɛ a he wa.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ wo e ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo mlaa ke, “Binyumu tsuaa binyumu nɛ Hebri no ko ma fɔ ɔ, nyɛ ya sake lɛ ngɔ fɔ Nilo pa a mi; se biyo tsuaa biyo lɛɛ nyɛ ha nɛ e yi nɛ na wami.”

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Yo ɔ ba na mi, nɛ e fɔ binyumu. Benɛ e na kaa jokuɛ ɔ he ngɛ fɛu ɔ, e ngɔ lɛ ngɔ laa nyɔhiɔ etɛ.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Se benɛ e nyɛ we nɛ e kɛ lɛ nɛ laa hu ɔ, e ngɔ kusii ko nɛ a kɛ ngɔwu lo, nɛ e kpa he amã. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ngɔ bimwɔyo ɔ kɛ wo kusii ɔ mi, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ya ma ngɔwu ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ pa a tue.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Bimwɔyo ɔ nyɛmiyo daa si ngɛ se banee ngɛ hyɛe kaa mɛni lɛ maa pee bimwɔyo ɔ lo.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: E ba mi kaa Farao ɔ biyo ɔ ba nɛ e ba du ngɛ pa a mi, nɛ e mawa amɛ ngɛ si poe ngɛ pa a nya. E na kusii ɔ ngɛ ngɔwu a mi, nɛ e tsɔ e mawa kake ke e ya wo kɛ ba.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Benɛ e bli nya a, e na bimwɔyo ɔ; kɛkɛ nɛ bimwɔyo ɔ hia ya. E ní pee lɛ mɔbɔ, nɛ e de ke, “Hebri bi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko bi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ bimwɔyo ɔ nyɛmiyo ɔ de Farao ɔ biyo ɔ ke, “Ma ya nɛ ma ya tsɛ bimɛanyɛ ko ngɛ Hebri yi ɔmɛ a kpɛti kɛ ba nɛ e ba hyɛ jokuɛyo ɔ nɔ ha mo lo?”

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ biyo ɔ de lɛ ke, “Ngɔɔ jokuɛ nɛ ɔ kɛ ho nɛ o ya hyɛ e nɔ ha mi nɛ ma wo mo hiɔ.” Yo ɔ ngɔ bimwɔyo ɔ nɛ e ya hyɛ e nɔ.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Benɛ jokuɛ ɔ ba wa a, yo ɔ ngɔ lɛ ya ha Farao ɔ biyo ɔ, nɛ e ba pee e bi. E wo lɛ biɛ ke Mose, nɛ e de ke, “I wo lɛ kikɛmɛ a biɛ nɛ ɔ, ejakaa nyu mi i je lɛ kɛ je.” Mose ku kɛ ho Midian ya

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Benɛ Mose ba wa a, e je kpo ligbi ko kɛ ho e nyɛmimɛ Hebri bi ɔmɛ a ngɔ ya, nɛ e ya hyɛ pɔtɔ, kɛ dengme ní tsumi kpakpataa nɛ a ngɛ tsue ɔ. E na Egipt no ko nɛ ngɛ e nyɛmimɛ Hebri bi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake gbee.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Mose plɛ hyɛ hiɛ kɛ hiɛ, nɛ e nɛ nɔ ko. Kɛkɛ nɛ e fia Egipt no ɔ nɔ́ nɛ e gbe, nɛ e kɛ zia tsi e nɔ.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, benɛ Mose je kpo ekohu ɔ, e ya na Hebri bi enyɔ nɛ a ngɛ kunɔ nɔe. E bi nɔ nɛ nɔ́ dɛ ɔ ke, “Mɛni he je nɛ o ngɛ o nyɛmi ɔ nɔ fiae?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ he nɔ ke, “Mɛnɔ wo mo wa nyatsɛ kɛ kojolɔ? Pe o ngɛ hlae nɛ o gbe mi kaa bɔ nɛ o gbe Egipt no ɔ lo?” Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose tsui po, nɛ e de ke, “Akuanyɛ! Sane ɔ je kpo.”

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Se to hyɛli kpa komɛ ba nɛ a ba fie Yetro biyi ɔmɛ. Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose te nɛ e fie to hyɛli kpa amɛ, nɛ e ha yihewi ɔmɛ a to ɔmɛ nyu.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Benɛ a kpale kɛ ba a tsɛ ɔ ngɔ ɔ, e bi mɛ ke, “Mwɔnɛ ɔ lɛɛ kɛ pee kɛɛ nɛ nyɛ ba mla kikɛ nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: A de lɛ ke, “Egipt no ko lɛ je wɔ ngɛ to hyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e sa nyu ha wɔ nɛ wa to ɔmɛ nu.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Yetro bi e biyi ɔmɛ ke, “Nɛ jije e ngɛ? Mɛni he je nyɛ je nyumu ɔ he? Nyɛ ya tsɛ lɛ kɛ ba nɛ e ba wo e nya mi nɔ́ ko.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Mose kplɛɛ kaa e kɛ osɔfo ɔ maa hi si. Pee se ɔ, osɔfo ɔ ngɔ e biyo Zipora ngɔ ha Mose.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Zipora fɔ binyumu, nɛ Mose wo lɛ biɛ ke Gershon, nɛ e de ke, “I wo lɛ kikɛmɛ a biɛ nɛ ɔ, ejakaa i ba to nubwɔ ngɛ ma se zugba nɔ.”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Jeha komɛ a se ɔ, Egipt matsɛ ɔ ba gbo. Se Israel bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ kɛmɛmi kɛkɛ a ngɛ kɛmɛe ngɛ a nyɔguɛ yemi ɔ mi. A fa kue ha Mawu, nɛ Mawu hu nu a gbi.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Benɛ Mawu nu a kɛmɛmi ɔ, e kai somi nɛ e kɛ a nɛmɛ Abraham, Isak, kɛ Yakob so ɔ.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mawu mi mi sã lɛ ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a si himi ɔ he; ejakaa e na kaa be su nɛ sa kaa e pee he nɔ́ ko.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Mose ngɛ e ngatsɛ Yetro, Midian osɔfo ɔ tohi hyɛe ngɛ nga a nɔ. Ligbi ko ɔ, e tsɔ̃ to ɔmɛ kɛ ya gu nga a nɔ, kɛ ya pã si ngɛ Mawu yo, Horeb ɔ he.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Benɛ e ba lejɛ ɔ, Yawɛ bɔfo ko ba je e he kpo tsɔɔ lɛ kaa la lilɛ nɛ ngɛ tsoe ngɛ mio tso ko mi. Benɛ e ke e hyɛɛ ɔ, e na kaa mio tso ɔ ngɛ tsoe, se e sɛ̃.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose de ke, “Enɛ ɔ lɛɛ ma gba nɛ ma ya hyɛ nyakpɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, nɔ he je nɛ mio tso ɔ sɛ̃ ɔ.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Yawɛ na kaa e gba kɛ ma hyɛmi ɔ, e tsɛ lɛ kɛ je mio tso ɔ mi ke, “Mose! Mose!” Nɛ Mose he nɔ ke, “Tsaatsɛ! Imi ji nɛ!”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Mawu de lɛ ke, “Koo hɛ mo kɛ su hiɛ ɔ! Je o tokota a, ejakaa zugba klɔuklɔu nɔ o daa si ngɛ ɔ nɛ!”

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: E ya nɔ nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Imi ji o nɛmɛ Abraham, Isak, kɛ Yakob a Mawu ɔ nɛ!” Mose ngɔ nɔ́ kɛ ha e hɛ mi, ejakaa e ngɛ gbeye yee kaa e maa na Mawu.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de ke, “Amanehlu nɛ ye ma a ngɛ nae ngɛ Egipt ɔ, i na; nɛ ya nɛ a ngɛ foe kɛ ngɛ balɔ tsɛe ɔ hu i nu. Niinɛ, i le a nɔ́ nami ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kple si kɛ ba, konɛ ma ba kpɔ mɛ kɛ je Egipt bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi, nɛ ma je mɛ kɛ je zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ kɛ ya zugba kpakpa nɛ kle, nɛ baa ní nɔ. Kanaan bi, Hit bi, Amor bi, Periz bi, Hiv bi, kɛ Yebus bi a hi he ɔ i ngɛ tsɔɔe ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Niinɛ, i nu Israel bi ɔmɛ a ya fomi ɔ, nɛ i na bɔ nɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ ngɛ mɛ yi mi wae ha.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ha nɛ ma tsɔ mo Farao ɔ ngɔ nɛ o ya je ye ma, nɛ ji Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Egipt.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Se Mose bi Mawu ke, “Mɛnɔ ji mi, nɛ ma ya Farao ɔ ngɔ, nɛ ma ya je Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Egipt ɔ?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Mawu ha lɛ heto ke, “Ma piɛ o he. Ke o ya jé ma a kɛ je Egipt kɛ ba a, nyɛ ma ba ja mi ngɛ yo nɛ ɔ nɔ. Jamɛ a be ɔ loko o maa le niinɛ kaa imi nɛ i tsɔ mo.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Mose bi Mawu ke, “Ke i ya Israel bi ɔmɛ a ngɔ, nɛ i ya de mɛ ke, ‘Mawu ɔ nɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ja lɛ ɔ tsɔ mi nyɛ ngɔ,’ nɛ a bi mi ke, ‘Kɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ kɛɛ?’ ɔ, kɛ ma de mɛ kɛɛ?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Mawu de Mose ekohu ke, “Mo de Israel bi ɔmɛ ke, Yawɛ, nyɛ nɛmɛ Abraham, Isak, kɛ Yakob a Mawu ɔ, lɛ nɛ e tsɔ mi nyɛ ngɔ. Biɛ nɛ ɔ ji ye biɛ kɛ yaa neneene, nɛ yi nɔhi nɛ maa ba a, mɛ hu a ma tsɛ mi jã.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Yaa nɛ o ya bua Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ a nya, nɛ o de mɛ ke, Yawɛ, Mawu ɔ nɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ Abraham, Isak, kɛ Yakob ja lɛ ɔ je e he kpo tsɔɔ mi, nɛ e de mi ke, ‘I na nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ nyɛ pee ngɛ Egipt ɔ,

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: nɛ i ngɛ si woe kaa ma je nyɛ kɛ je Egipt nɔ́ nami ɔ mi, kɛ ya zugba nɛ kle, nɛ baa ní nɔ. Kanaan bi, Hit bi, Amor bi, Periz bi, Hiv bi, kɛ Yebus bi a hi he ɔ i ngɛ tsɔɔe ɔ nɛ.’

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: “A maa bu o gbi tue; nɛ o kɛ Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ maa ya Egipt matsɛ ɔ ngɔ, nɛ nyɛ ma ya de lɛ ke, ‘Yawɛ, Hebri bi ɔmɛ a Mawu ɔ kɛ wɔ ba kpe; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, wa kpa mo pɛɛ, ha wɔ blɔ nɛ waa nyɛɛ ligbi etɛ blɔ kɛ ya nga a nɔ nɛ wa ya sã bɔ ha Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: I le kaa ke nyɛ doo Egipt matsɛ ɔ nya wawɛɛ tete po, e be nyɛ he ngmɛɛe.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma ngɔ ye nyakpɛ níhi tsuo nɛ ma pee ngɛ a kpɛti ɔ kɛ fia mɛ ní kɛ tsɔɔ mɛ ye nine si wami. Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, e maa ngmɛɛ nyɛ he.

english_verse: After I punish the Egyptians, they will be so afraid of you that they will give you anything you want. You are my people, and I will let you take many things with you when you leave the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: “Ma ha nɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ maa na ye ma nɛ ɔ mɔbɔ; nɛ ke e su be nɛ nyɛ maa je ɔ, nyɛ be jee kɛ nyɛ dɛ gu.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Se mohu Hebri yo tsuaa Hebri yo ma ya ba june ní, sika tsu, sika hiɔ, kɛ bo ngɛ e nɔle nɔ nɛ ji Egipt no, loo e we mi yo nɛ ji Egipt no ngɔ, nɛ nyɛ maa ngɔ kɛ dla nyɛ binyumuhi, kɛ nyɛ biyihi a he ha mɛ. Blɔ nɔ nɛ nyɛ maa gu kɛ kpakpaa Egipt bi ɔmɛ a he níhi kɛ je ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Mose de Mawu ke, “Se o na, a be mi hee maa ye, nɛ a be ye gbi hu tue bue; nɔ́ nɛ a ma de ji, ‘Yawɛ je we e he si ha mo.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni lɛ ngɛ o dɛ mi ɔ?” Mose he nɔ ke, “Tso.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Sake ngɔ fɔ zugba!” Mose sake tso ɔ ngɔ fɔ zugba, nɛ tso ɔ plɛ pee sinɔ, nɛ Mose tu fo kɛ je he.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Hɛɛ mo kɛ ya nɛ o nu e hlemi. Se benɛ Mose hɛ lɛ kɛ ya, nɛ e nu sinɔ ɔ, e plɛ pee tso ngɛ e dɛ mi.”

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de ke, “Enɛ ɔ maa tsɔɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ kaa Mawu ɔ nɛ a nɛmɛ Abraham, Isak, kɛ Yakob ja lɛ ɔ je e he kpo tsɔɔ mo.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de lɛ ekohu ke, “Ngɔɔ o nine kɛ hɔ o tade ɔ mi ngɛ o tsui nya.” Nɛ e pee jã. Se benɛ e je e nine ɔ, tsaoo, e nine ɔ he pee patapata kɛ hiɔ tsu, nɛ e hiɛ kaa snoo.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Ngɔɔ o nine ɔ kɛ hɔ o tade ɔ mi ngɛ o tsui nya ekohu.” Nɛ e pee jã. Se benɛ e je e nine ɔ, e tsake pee kaa bɔ nɛ e ngɛ sa a.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ke a he we okadi enyɔ ɔmɛ yi, nɛ jehanɛ hu a bui mo tue ɔ, lɛɛ o ma ya yɛ nyu ngɛ Nilo pa a mi, nɛ o ma plɛ pue zugba gbigbli nɔ, nɛ Nilo pa a mi nyu ɔ ma plɛ pee muɔ ngɛ zugba a.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Se Mose de Yawɛ ke, “Ye Nyɔmtsɛ, ye nya mi tsɔ we kɛ je sá, nɛ kɛ je be nɛ o kɛ imi, o tsɔlɔ ɔ bɔni munyu tumi nɛ ɔ hu tsakemi ko bɛ; ye munyu tumi ngɛ blɛuu, nɛ ye lilɛ hu jiɔ.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Mɛnɔ nɛ haa nɔmlɔ tuɔ munyu, loo e tui munyu? Mɛnɔ nɛ haa nɔmlɔ hyɛɛ nɔ́, loo e hyɛ we nɔ́? Mɛnɔ nɛ haa nɔmlɔ nuɔ nɔ, loo e nui nɔ́? Anɛ pi imi, Yawɛ lo?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, moo ya. Ma ha o nya mi ma tsɔ, nɛ ma tsɔɔ mo nɔ́ nɛ o de.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Se Mose ke, “Ye Nyɔmtsɛ, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o tsɔ nɔ kpa.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ lɛɛ Yawɛ mi mi fu Mose, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Anɛ o susu kaa i li kaa o nyɛmi Aaron, Levi no ɔ nya mi tsɔ lo? Hyɛ, e ngɛ blɔ nɔ kɛ ma nɛ e kɛ mo ba kpe, nɛ ke e na mo ɔ, e bua maa jɔ e he saminya.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: Moo o maa pee kaa Mawu, nɛ o maa tsɔɔ lɛ nɔ́ nɛ e de, nɛ lɛɛ e maa pee o we otsiamɛ, nɛ e ma je o munyu ɔ nya ha ni ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Moo hɛɛ o tso ɔ, nɛ lɔ ɔ ji nɔ́ nɛ o kɛ maa pee nyakpɛ ní ɔmɛ ɔ nɛ.” Mose kpale e se kɛ ho Egipt ya

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Mose kpale kɛ ho e ngatsɛ Yetro ngɔ ya nɛ e ya de lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, ha mi blɔ nɛ ma kpale kɛ ya Egipt, nɛ ma ya hyɛ kaa ye nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ je mi kɛ mwɔɔ lo.” Yetro de Mose ke, “Blɔ ngɛ faa; blɔ ɔ nɔ nɛ jɔ ha mo.”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ kɛ Mose tu munyu ngɛ Midian, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Moo kpale o se kɛ ho Egipt ya, ejakaa nihi nɛ ngɛ hlae nɛ a tane o yi ɔ, mɛ tsuo a gbo.”

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Ke o kpale kɛ ya Egipt ɔ, nyakpɛ níhi tsuo kulaa nɛ i ngɔ kɛ wo o dɛ ɔ, hyɛ nɛ o pee lɛ tsuo ngɛ Farao ɔ hɛ mi; se imi lɛɛ ma kplii Farao ɔ tsui, nɛ e be hae nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ je.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ o ma de Farao ɔ ji, Yawɛ ke, ‘Israel ɔ, ye binyumu ji lɛ; ee ye bitɛte ji lɛ!

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: I de mo ke o ha nɛ ye bi ɔ nɛ ya nɛ e ya ja mi, se o kplɛɛ we. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma gbe o binyumu ɔ, o bitɛte ɔ!’ ”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Benɛ Mose yaa a, Yawɛ ya je e he si ha lɛ ngɛ nibwɔhi a to he ko, nɛ e piɛ nguɛ nya nɛ e tane e yi.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Aaron ke, “Mose ma ngɛ nga a nɔ; yaa nɛ o ya kpee lɛ.” Kɛkɛ nɛ e ho nɛ e kɛ lɛ ya kpe ngɛ Mawu yo ɔ he; nɛ e fua lɛ atuu.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Mose bɔ Aaron munyu ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ Yawɛ kɛ tsɔ lɛ ɔ, kɛ okadihi nɛ e fa lɛ ke e pee ɔ.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Nɛ Aaron bɔ mɛ níhi tsuo nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ɔ, nɛ Mose pee okadi ɔmɛ kɛ tsɔɔ ma nimeli ɔmɛ.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Ma a he ye. Benɛ a nu kaa Yawɛ ba na Israel bi ɔmɛ a nɔ́ nami ɔ, nɛ e ma nɛ e ba pee he nɔ́ ko ha mɛ ɔ, a kpla si nɛ a ja Mawu.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Mose kɛ Aaron ho Farao ɔ ngɔ ya, nɛ a ya de lɛ ke, “Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Ha ye ma a nɛ ho, nɛ a ya ye nyami ligbi nɛ a kɛ ja mi ngɛ nga a nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Se Farao ɔ bi mɛ ke, “Mɛnɔ ji jamɛ a Yawɛ ɔ? Mɛni he je nɛ e sa kaa ma bu e gbi tue nɛ ma ha Israel nɛ ho ɔ? I li Yawɛ nɛ ɔ, nɛ pohu i be hae nɛ a ya.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: A ha lɛ heto ke, “Hebri bi ɔmɛ a Mawu ɔ ba je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ wɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, wa kpa mo pɛɛ, mo ha nɛ waa nyɛɛ ligbi etɛ blɔ kɛ ya nga a nɔ nɛ wa ya sã bɔ ha Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ. Ke wa pee we ja a, e kɛ gbenɔ hiɔ maa gbe wɔ, loo e ma ha nɛ a gbe wɔ ngɛ ta mi.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Farao ɔ ya nɔ nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ hyɛ, nyɛ bi ɔmɛ a he hiɛ babauu ngɛ zugba a nɔ pe zugbatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ nyɛ ma ha a kpa ní tsumi!”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ nɔuu ɔ, Farao ɔ fa nyɔguɛhi a nɔ yeli ɔmɛ, kɛ Israel bi nɛ hyɛɛ ní tsumi ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ ke,

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Nyɛ ko ha ni ɔmɛ nga nɛ a kɛ pee bliikisi ɔ hu kaa sa a; nyɛ ha nɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a ya nɛ a ya fa nga a.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Se nyɛ ha nɛ a po bliikisi ɔ nɛ hiɛ kaa sa a nɔuu; nyɛ ko je nɔ, ejakaa a ngɛ hejɔ pee. A ngɛ huhui kpae ke, ‘Nyɛ ha waa ho nɛ wa ya sã bɔ ha wa Mawu ɔ,’ ejakaa hejɔtsɛmɛ ji mɛ.

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko ha mɛ deka; nyɛ pue ní tsumi ɔ nɔ ha mɛ nɛ a tsu, konɛ a ko ya hi lakpa munyuhi tue bue hu.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɔguɛhi a nɔ yeli ɔmɛ, kɛ ní tsuli ɔmɛ a nɔ hyɛli ɔmɛ ho nɛ a ya de ma a ke, “Farao ɔ ke e be nyɛ nga hae.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya fa nga ngɛ he saisaa nɛ nyɛ ma na nga ngɛ; se nyɛ ní tsumi ɔ lɛɛ e nɔ ko gbɔ.”

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Nyɔguɛhi a nɔ yeli ɔmɛ nyɛ a nɔ ke a gbe a daa ligbi ní tsumi ɔmɛ a nya kaa bɔ nɛ a peeɔ be nɛ a haa mɛ nga a.

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Ke pee ɔ, Farao ɔ nyɔguɛhi a nɔ yeli ɔmɛ fiaa Israel ní tsuli ɔmɛ a nɔ hyɛli ɔmɛ nɛ a to ɔ ní, nɛ a biɔ mɛ ke, “Kɛ pee kɛɛ nɛ nyɛ gbi bliikisi peemi ní tsumi ɔ nya kaa bɔ nɛ a to ha nyɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Israel ní tsuli a mɔ hyɛli ɔmɛ ba Farao ɔ ngɔ nɛ a ba fa kue ha lɛ, nɛ a bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he je o kɛ wɔ o tsɔli ɔmɛ ngɛ sane yee kikɛ nɛ ɔ?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: A ha we wɔ nga, se a ke waa po bliikisi bami kaa bɔ nɛ wa poo daa ligbi ɔ. Jehanɛ hu a dɔ kpa to wa nɔ be mi nɛ tɔmi ɔ ji wɔ; se e je o ma mi bi ɔmɛ mohu.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Se matsɛ ɔ de mɛ ke, “Hejɔtsɛmɛ ji nyɛ! Hejɔtsɛmɛ! Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ nyɛ ke ma ha nɛ nyɛɛ ho nɛ nyɛ ya sã bɔ ha Yawɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Esɔ nɛ nyɛɛ ho nɛ nyɛ ya tsu ní! A be nyɛ nga hae, se nyɛ maa po bliikisi abɔ nɛ nyɛ poo daa ligbi ɔ kɛ̃!”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Israel ní tsuli ɔmɛ a nɔ hyɛli ɔmɛ yɔse kaa sane yobu ye mɛ benɛ a de mɛ ke daa ligbi ɔ, a po bliikisi ɔ nɛ e hiɛ kaa kekle ɔ, nɛ a ko ha e nɔ nɛ gbɔ ɔ.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Benɛ a si Farao ɔ, a ba na Mose kɛ Aaron nɛ a ngɛ mɛ mlɛe.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Nɛ a de mɛ ke, “Yawɛ maa wo nyɛ hiɔ; ejakaa nyɛ ha wa he je fu wo Farao ɔ kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ, nɛ nyɛ ngɔ klaate ngɔ wo a dɛ mi nɛ a kɛ gbe wɔ.” Mose ya ye kɔmɔ ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose kpale e se kɛ ho Yawɛ ngɔ ya ekohu, nɛ e ya bi lɛ ke, “Yawɛ, mɛni he je o pee o ma a yayami kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Mɛni he je o tsɔ mi kulaa?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Kɛ je be nɛ i ba Farao ɔ ngɔ nɛ i kɛ lɛ ba tu munyu ngɛ o biɛ mi ɔ kɛ ba si amlɔ nɛ ɔ, yi mi sɔuu nɛ e ngɛ ma a wae. Nɛ mo hu o pee we nɔ́ ko kulaa kaa o ma kpɔ o ma a.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Kpaako loko o maa na nɔ́ nɛ ma pee Farao ɔ, ejakaa lɛ nitsɛ e kɛ e he wami maa fie Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ maa je e zugba a nɔ.” Mawu tsɛ Mose

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: I je ye he kpo tsɔɔ Abraham, Isak, kɛ Yakob kaa Mawu Ope; se ye biɛ Yawɛ ɔ lɛɛ i ha we nɛ a le.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ se hu, i kɛ mɛ so kaa Kanaan zugba a nɛ a ya to nubwɔ ngɛ nɔ ɔ, ma ngɔ kɛ ha mɛ.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ hu, bɔ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɛ awe nyae ɔ, i nu, nɛ i kai ye somi ɔ.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ nyɛ kɛ pee imi nitsɛ ye ma, nɛ ma pee nyɛ Mawu; nɛ nyɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ Mawu, nɔ nɛ je Egipt bi ɔmɛ a tlomi ɔmɛ kɛ je nyɛ nɔ ɔ.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ nyɛ kɛ ya zugba nɛ i wo si kaa i kɛ ma ha Abraham, Isak, kɛ Yakob ɔ nɔ; ma ngɔ kɛ ha nyɛ, nɛ e maa pee nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ nɔ. Imi Yawɛ nɛ i de.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Se Mose de Yawɛ ke, “O nɛ, Israel bi ɔmɛ po bui mi tue; kɛ maa pee kɛɛ nɛ Farao ɔ lɛɛ e maa bu mi tue; imi nɛ ye nya mi tsɔ we nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose kɛ Aaron ke, “Nyɛ ya de Israel ma a, kɛ Egipt matsɛ ɔ ke i fa nyɛ ke nyɛ ba kpaka Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ.” Mose kɛ Aaron a weku he sane

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron a weku he sane ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: Ruben, Israel bitɛte ɔ bimɛ ji Hanok, Palu, Hezron, kɛ Karmi. Ruben weku ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simeon bimɛ ji Yemuel, Yamin, Ohad, Yakin, Zohar, kɛ Shaul, Kanaan yo ɔ bi ɔ. Simeon weku ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gershon binyumu ɔmɛ ji Libni kɛ Shimei, nɛ a nina hiɛ babauu.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Merari binyumu ɔmɛ ji Mahli kɛ Mushi. Levi weku ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Izhar binyumu ɔmɛ ji Kora, Nefeg, kɛ Zikri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Uziel binyumu ɔmɛ ji Mishael, Elzafan, kɛ Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aaron ngɔ Aminadab biyo Elisheba, Nahshon nyɛmiyo ɔ; nɛ e kɛ lɛ fɔ Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, kɛ Itamar.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Aaron bi Eleazar ngɔ Putiel biyi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake, nɛ e kɛ lɛ fɔ Finehas. Levi weku ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Aaron kɛ Mose nɛ ɔ ji nihi nɛ Yawɛ de mɛ ke a ya nɛ a ya kpaka Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ kɛ ba a nɛ.

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Mɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ a kɛ Egipt matsɛ ɔ ya tu Israel bi ɔmɛ a jemi kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ he munyu ɔ nɛ. Jamɛ a Mose kɛ Aaron ɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. Yawɛ fa Mose kɛ Aaron

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Ligbi ɔ nɛ Yawɛ kɛ Mose tu munyu ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Imi ji Yawɛ. Yaa nɛ o ya bɔ Egipt matsɛ ɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ i de mo ɔ.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Se Mose de Yawɛ ke, “Tse o le kaa ye nya mi tsɔ we. Kɛ ma pee kɛɛ nɛ Farao ɔ maa bu mi tue?”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “O nɛ, i pee mo kaa Mawu ha Farao ɔ, nɛ o nyɛmi Aaron maa pee o gbalɔ.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: O maa bɔ Aaron nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ma de mo ɔ, nɛ o nyɛminyumu Aaron ma de Farao ɔ ke e ha nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ a je e zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, ma nu Egipt kã nya, nɛ ma kpaka ye ma kpekpemi ɔ nɛ ji Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ; nɛ ma ye dami sane ha nyɛ.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke i pee ní nɛ ɔmɛ loko Egipt bi ɔmɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Ke Farao ɔ de nyɛ ke nyɛɛ pee nyakpɛ nɔ́ ko nɛ nyɛ kɛ ye nyɛ he odase ɔ, mo de Aaron nɛ e sake e tso ɔ kɛ fɔ zugba ngɛ matsɛ ɔ hɛ mi; nɛ tso ɔ ma plɛ pee sinɔ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose kɛ Aaron je kɛ ho Farao ɔ ngɔ ya, nɛ a ya pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa mɛ ɔ. Aaron sake e tso ɔ ngɔ fɔ zugba ngɛ Farao ɔ kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi; nɛ e plɛ pee sinɔ.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ hu tsɛ e ní leli ɔmɛ, kɛ kunya yeli ɔmɛ nɛ ji Egipt wɔnɔ ɔmɛ kɛ ba, nɛ mɛ hu a gu a ga blɔ ɔmɛ a nɔ kɛ pee ja nɔuu.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: A ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ sake e tso ngɔ fɔ zugba, nɛ tso ɔmɛ plɛ pee sinɔhi. Se Aaron tso ɔ mii a tso ɔmɛ.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Se Farao ɔ kplii e tsui; nɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ɔ, e bui Mose kɛ Aaron tue. Haomihi ba Egipt Nyu plɛ pee muɔ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Farao ɔ kplii e tsui; e kplɛɛ we nɛ e ha ni ɔmɛ nɛ a ho.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: nɛ o de lɛ ke, ‘Yawɛ, Hebri bi ɔmɛ a Mawu ɔ tsɔ mi o ngɔ ke ma ba de mo ke o ha ye ma a nɛ ho nɛ a ya ja mi ngɛ nga a nɔ, nɛ kɛ ba si amlɔ nɛ ɔ, o bui tue.’

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Enɛ ɔ a kɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ. Ma wo tso nɛ ngɛ ye dɛ mi ɔ kɛ fia Nilo pa a, nɛ nyu ɔ ma plɛ muɔ.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Lohi nɛ ngɛ pa a mi ɔ kulaa ma gbo. Nilo pa a mi nyu ɔ maa sa; e maa je fu, nɛ e maa nyɛɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ a he mi ha mɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Yawɛ kpale de Mose ke, “De Aaron ke, ‘Ngɔɔ o tso ɔ, nɛ o kpã o nine mi ngɛ Egipt pa amɛ, nyu dɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ taku ɔmɛ tsuo a nɔ, nɛ a mi nyu ɔ kulaa ma plɛ pee muɔ. A maa na muɔ ngɛ he tsuaa he ngɛ Egipt, ngɛ tso buɛhi, kɛ tɛ buɛhi a mi.’ ”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Nɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa Mose kɛ Aaron ke a pee ɔ, Aaron wo tso ɔ nɔ nɛ e kɛ fia Nilo pa a hɛ mi ngɛ Farao ɔ kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi. Nyu ɔ tsuo plɛ pee muɔ.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Lohi nɛ ngɛ pa a mi ɔ kulaa gbo, nɛ Nilo pa a he fu tsɔ bɔ nɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ nyɛ we nɛ a nu pa a mi nyu ɔ. Nɛ nyu nɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ tsuo plɛ pee muɔ.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Egipt kunya yeli ɔmɛ gu a ga blɔ ɔmɛ a nɔ nɛ a pee ja nɔuu. Se Farao ɔ lɛɛ e kplii e tsui kaa sa a. Nɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ngɔ to ɔ, e bui mɛ tue fɛɛ.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ plɛ e he nɛ e ho we mi ya; enɛ ɔ kulaa pue we e tsui nɔ.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Egipt bi ɔmɛ tsua vuhi ngɛ Nilo pa a tue nɛ́ a na nyu nɛ a nu; ejakaa Nilo pa a nitsɛ mi nyu ɔ lɛɛ e hi numi saasaa.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Benɛ Yawɛ fia pa a nɔ́ nɛ e plɛ pee muɔ se ɔ, ligbi kpaago ba po mi.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Yaa Farao ɔ ngɔ nɛ o ya de lɛ ke Yawɛ ke, ‘Ha ye ma a nɛ ho nɛ a ya ja mi.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Nilo pa a maa wo ovɔnɔhi fuu, nɛ ovɔnɔ ɔmɛ maa sɛ he tsuaa he. A maa sɛ o we mi; a maa sɛ o se tsu mi, nɛ o sa nitsɛ po a maa kuɔ. Jehanɛ a maa sɛ o tsɔli ɔmɛ kɛ o ma mi bi ɔmɛ a wehi a mi; a maa sɛ o flɔɔnɔɔhi kɛ o ní hoomi níhi a mi.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ovɔnɔ ɔmɛ maa tuu kɛ mla mo nitsɛ, o we mi bi ɔmɛ, kɛ o tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Mo de Aaron ke e wo e tso ɔ nɔ ngɛ pa amɛ, kɛ nyu dɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ taku ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ́ e ha ovɔnɔhi nɛ ba Egipt zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ, tsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ kpa Yawɛ pɛɛ nɛ e je ovɔnɔ ɔmɛ kɛ je i kɛ ye ma mi bi ɔmɛ wa nɔ, konɛ ma ha nyɛ we bi ɔmɛ nɛ a ho nɛ a ya sã bɔ ha Yawɛ.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Mose de Farao ɔ ke, “Moo lɛɛ e je o nya nɛ o de kɛkɛ kaa be nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, ma kpa pɛɛ ha mo, kɛ o ma mi bi ɔmɛ, kɛkɛ a maa gbe ovɔnɔ ɔmɛ nɛ a be eko nae ngɛ he ko, ja Nilo pa a mi pɛ.”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Farao ɔ de lɛ ke, “Hwɔɔ nɛ o sɔle ha mi.” Mose de lɛ ke, “Ma pee kaa bɔ nɛ o bi ɔ, konɛ o na nɛ o le kaa nɔ ko nɔ ko be nɛ ngɛ kaa Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Ovɔnɔ ɔmɛ maa ta zugba a nɔ he tsuaa he pɛsɛpɛsɛ, ja Nilo pa a mi pɛ.”

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mose kɛ Aaron je Farao ɔ ngɔ. Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Mose wo e gbi nɔ nɛ e fa kue ha Yawɛ ngɛ ovɔnɔ ɔmɛ a he kaa bɔ nɛ e kɛ Farao ɔ tu ɔ.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Nɛ a bua a nya glekugleku ngɔ pue si, nɛ zugba a nɔ je fu.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Se benɛ Farao ɔ na mumi wo he bɔɔ ɔ, e kplii e tsui ekohu, nɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ɔ, e bui mɛ tue. Pwɔmihi ba

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “De Aaron nɛ e ngɔ e tso ɔ kɛ fia tabo zu ɔ nɔ, nɛ tabo zu ɔ ma plɛ pee pwɔmi ngɛ Egipt zugba a tsuo nɔ.”

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Aaron ngɔ e tso ɔ kɛ fia tabo zu ɔ nɔ, kɛkɛ nɛ tabo zu ɔ tsuo plɛ pee pwɔmi nɛ bɔni nimli, kɛ lohwehi tsuo bublemi ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ tsuo.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Pwɔmi ɔmɛ ha nɔ tsuaa nɔ. Wɔnɔ ɔmɛ ka kaa mɛ hu a maa gu a ga blɔ ɔmɛ a nɔ kɛ ha pwɔmihi nɛ ba lo; se a nyɛ we.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ wɔnɔ ɔmɛ de Farao ɔ ke, “Mawu nɔ́ peepee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.” Se kɛ̃ Farao ɔ kplii e tsui; nɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ɔ, e bui mɛ tue. Pwɔlwɛhi ba

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Moo bu tue! Hwɔɔ mɔtu ɔ, Farao ɔ maa ya Nilo pa a nya. Yaa nɛ o kɛ lɛ ya kpe ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ o de lɛ ke bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Ha ye ma a nɛ ho nɛ a ya ja mi.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Se ke o ha we nɛ ye ma a nɛ ya a, ma ha nɛ pwɔlwɛhi maa bungɔ mo, kɛ o tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ o ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo. Nɛ mo nitsɛ o we ɔ mi, Egipt bi ɔmɛ a we ɔmɛ a mi, kɛ nyɛ zugba a nɔ tsuo ma hyi kɛ pwɔlwɛhi.

english_verse: “The Lord's people in Goshen won't be bothered by flies, but your people in the rest of the country will be tormented by them. That's how you will know that the Lord is here in Egypt. This miracle will happen tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ma gba ye we bi ɔmɛ, kɛ o we bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti. Ma to okadi nɛ ɔ hwɔɔmɛ a je hwɔɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Yawɛ pee ja, nɛ pwɔlwɛhi wo fuu ngɛ Farao ɔ we ɔ, kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ a we ɔmɛ a mi. Nɛ pwɔlwɛ ɔmɛ kpata Egipt zugba a tsuo hɛ mi.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ tsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya sã bɔ ha nyɛ Mawu ɔ ngɛ zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Wa maa nyɛɛ ligbi etɛ blɔ kɛ ya nga a nɔ nɛ wa ya sã bɔ ha Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ e maa tsɔɔ ke waa pee ɔ.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ de mɛ ke, “Yoo, ma ha nyɛ blɔ nɛ nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya sã bɔ ha Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ ngɛ nga a nɔ; se nyɛ ko ya tsitsaa. Jehanɛ hu, nyɛ kpa pɛɛ ha mi.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mose de lɛ ke, “Ke i je o ngɔ pɛ i yaa nɛ ma ya kpa Yawɛ pɛɛ, konɛ hwɔɔmɛ a je hwɔɔ ɔ, pwɔlwɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a jɔɔ mo, o tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ o ma mi bi ɔmɛ bungɔmi. Sisimi kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ ko sisi wɔ hu kaa e maa tsi ma a nya nɛ a ko ya nɛ a ya sã bɔ ha Yawɛ.”

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Yawɛ hu pee kaa bɔ nɛ Mose bi lɛ ɔ, nɛ e hwu pwɔlwɛ ɔmɛ kɛ je Farao ɔ, kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ e ma mi bi ɔmɛ a he; pwɔlwɛ kake ngmelu po píɛ.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Se Farao ɔ kplii e tsui ekohu, nɛ e ngmɛɛ we Israel bi ɔmɛ a he nɛ a ho.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Yaa Farao ɔ ngɔ nɛ o ya de lɛ ke bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, Hebri bi ɔmɛ a Mawu ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Ha ye ma a nɛ ho nɛ a ya ja mi.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Ma gba Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ a lohwe ɔmɛ a mi, nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a ní ɔmɛ lɛɛ ekoeko be gboe.

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, Yawɛ pee kaa bɔ nɛ e de ɔ. Egipt bi ɔmɛ a lohwe ɔmɛ tsuo gbo; se Israel bi ɔmɛ a ní ɔmɛ lɛɛ kake ngmelu po gbo we.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose kɛ Aaron ke, “Nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya je la zu dɛ mamɛ kakaaka ngɛ flɔɔnɔɔ mi, nɛ Mose nɛ fɔ kɛ ya hiɔwe ngɛ Farao ɔ hɛ mi;

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: nɛ e maa pee kaa ahlabata bunyuku ngɛ Egipt kɔɔhiɔ mi tsuo. Nɛ enɛ ɔ ma plɛ tslɔɔ nɛ sa, nɛ e ngɛ pãe ngɛ nimli, kɛ we mi lohwehi tsuo a he.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a ya je flɔɔnɔɔ mi la zu nɛ a kɛ ba Farao ɔ ngɔ. Mose fia la zu ɔ kɛ mane hiɔwe, nɛ e plɛ pee tslɔɔ nɛ pã ngɛ nimli, kɛ we mi lohwehi a he.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Tslɔɔ ɔ he je ɔ, wɔnɔ ɔmɛ nyɛ we Mose hɛ mi nɛ a da; ejakaa tslɔɔ ɔ fuu wɔnɔ ɔmɛ kɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ tsuo kulaa.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ ha nɛ Farao ɔ kplii e tsui, nɛ kaa bɔ nɛ e de Mose ɔ, Farao ɔ bui mɛ tue fɛɛ. Gbiɛ ngo ngu

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Hwɔɔ mɔtu mla a, yaa Farao ɔ ngɔ nɛ o ya de lɛ ke bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, Hebri bi ɔmɛ a Mawu ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Ha ye ma a nɛ ho konɛ a ya ja mi.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ ɔ lɛɛ i be o tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ o ma a kɛkɛ tue gblae; se mohu ma ha nɛ nɔ́ nami ɔ maa sa mo nitsɛ hu o he, konɛ o le kaa nɔ ko nɔ ko be nɛ e kɛ mi sɔ ngɛ je ɔ mi tsuo.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Jinɛ be nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, i kɛ gbenɔ hiɔ sa o kɛ o ma a he momo; nɛ jinɛ a je mo kɛ je je ɔ mi momo.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Se i ha nɛ o ngɛ je mi, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ ma je ye he wami kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ mo, konɛ a wo ye biɛ ta ngɛ je ɔ mi tsuo.

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ tsɔli ɔmɛ a ti ni nɛmɛ nɛ ya ye Yawɛ munyu ɔ gbeye ɔ ha nɛ a nyɔguɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ a lohwe ɔmɛ tu fo kɛ ba we mi.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Se ni nɛmɛ nɛ bui Yawɛ munyu ɔ, mɛɛ lɛɛ a si a nyɔguɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ a lohwe ɔmɛ ngɛ nga nɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Mo wo o nine kɛ tsɔɔ hiɔwe, nɛ gbiɛ ngo ngu nɛ́ nɛ kɛ pue zugba a tsuo nɔ, kɛ pue nimli, lohwehi, kɛ nga nɔ tsohi a nɔ.”

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Benɛ gbiɛ ngo ngu ɔ ngɛ nɛe ɔ, oslabai hu ngɛ la pãe plamplam. Gbiɛ ngo ngu nɛ́ nɛ ɔ, a nɛ e nya wami ɔ eko hyɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ tsuo kɛ je be nɛ a to ma a sisi.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Se Goshen zugba a nɔ he nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɛ ɔ lɛɛ gbiɛ ngo ngu kake po nɔɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ tsɔ nɛ a ya tsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron kɛ ba, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ i pee yayami; Yawɛ nɔ́ da, se i kɛ ye ma a, wa tɔ̃.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Nyɛ kpa Yawɛ pɛɛ! Hiɔwe simi kɛ gbiɛ ngo ngu nɛmi nɛ ɔ ba hiɛ. Ma ngmɛɛ nyɛ he nɛ nyɛɛ ho; i be nyɛ nya tsie hu.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mose de lɛ ke, “Ke i je ma a mi pɛ ma wo ye nine nɔ ngɔ tsɔɔ Yawɛ. Hiɔwe simi ɔ se maa po, nɛ gbiɛ ngo ngu ɔ be nɛe hu, konɛ o na nɛ o le kaa Yawɛ nɔ́ ji je ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Se i le kaa o kɛ o tsɔli ɔmɛ ɔ, nyɛ na we nɛ nyɛɛ ye Yawɛ Mawu ɔ gbeye lolo.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Nɛ́ pee ja a, doti, kɛ ngma nɛ a du kɛ sɛ hlami ɔ kulaa hɛ mi kpata; ejakaa jamɛ a ngma a je deke, nɛ doti ɔ hu gba mɔmɔ.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Se ngma kpa a lɛɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko pee we lɛ; ejakaa a kpɛ se kɛ du lɔ ɔ.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ ɔ, Mose si Farao ɔ, nɛ e je ma a mi, nɛ e wo e nine nɔ, nɛ e fa kue ha Yawɛ. Kɛkɛ nɛ hiɔwe simi ɔ, kɛ gbiɛ ngo ngu nɛmi ɔ se po, nɛ hiɔmi ɔ hu kpa.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Se benɛ Farao ɔ na kaa hiɔmi ɔ, gbiɛ ngo ngu ɔ, kɛ hiɔwe simi ɔ se po ɔ, e ya nɔ nɛ e pee yayami; nɛ e kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ kplii a tsui.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ kplii e tsui, nɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ gu Mose nɔ de to ɔ, e ha we nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ a ya.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya na Farao ɔ. I kplii e kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ a tsui, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ ma pee ye we okadi nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ a kpɛti,

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: konɛ okadihi nɛ i pee ngɛ Egipt, kɛ bɔ nɛ i ha nɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ pee a he kuasia ha a, nyɛɛ sɛɛ nɛ nyɛ bimɛ, kɛ nyɛ bibimɛ nɛ a nu, konɛ nyɛ na nɛ nyɛɛ le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron ho Farao ɔ ngɔ ya, nɛ a ya de lɛ ke, “Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, Hebri bi ɔmɛ a Mawu ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Mɛni be o ma kua o he si bami ha mi kɛ yaa si? Ha ye ma a nɛ ya nɛ a ya ja mi.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Ke o kplɛɛ we nɛ ye ma a nɛ ya a, lɛɛ hwɔɔmɛ a je hwɔɔ ɔ, ma ha baalɛhi maa ba o zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: A maa ha zugba a tsuo nɔ, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be zugba zu ɔ nae. A maa ye nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ha nyɛ ngɛ gbiɛ ngo ngu ɔ se; tso tsuaa tso nɛ puɛ po a maa ye.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: O we ɔmɛ a mi, o tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ, kɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ a we ɔmɛ a mi ma hyi tɔ kɛ baalɛhi bɔ nɛ nyɛ tsɛmɛ kɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ nɛ eko gblee kɛ je be nɛ a bɔ ade kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ.’ ” Kɛkɛ nɛ e plɛ e he nɛ e je.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Farao ɔ tsɔli ɔmɛ de lɛ ke, “Mɛni be po nyumu nɛ ɔ maa jɔɔ wɔ haomi? Ha nɛ e ni ɔmɛ nɛ a ho nɛ a ya ja Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ. Anɛ o nɛ kɛ mwɔɔ kaa Egipt hɛ mi ngɛ kpatae lo?”

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a ya tsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron kɛ ba Farao ɔ ngɔ ekohu, nɛ Farao ɔ de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ho nɛ nyɛ ya ja Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ. Se mɛnɔmɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ maa ya a?”

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mose ha lɛ heto ke, “Wɔ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ nɛ wa maa ya a nɛ; jokuɛwi kɛ nikɔtɔmahi. Waa kɛ wa binyumuhi, wa biyihi, kɛ wa lohwehi kulaa maa ya; ejakaa wa yaa nɛ wa ya ye nyami ligbi kɛ wo Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami.”

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Nɛ Farao ɔ de mɛ ke, “Yawɛ nɛ gbaa nyɛ, ke i ngmɛ nyɛ blɔ nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ bimɛ ɔmɛ ho fii! Ɛhɛɛ, juɛmi yaya ko ngɛ nyɛ yi mi.

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Dɛbi! Nyɛ nyumu ɔmɛ, nyɛ kɛkɛ nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya ja Yawɛ, ejakaa lɔ ɔ ji nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ hlae.” Kɛkɛ nɛ a fie mɛ kɛ je Farao ɔ hɛ mi.

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose wo e tso ɔ nɔ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ, nɛ Yawɛ ha kɔɔhiɔ bɔni fiami kɛ je beleku jamɛ a ligbi ɔ kulaa nyɔ kɛ pia; nɛ benɛ je na a, beleku kɔɔhiɔ ɔ muɔ baalɛhi kɛ ba.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Baalɛ ɔmɛ pue Egipt zugba a nɔ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔ nɛ eko bɛ hyɛ, loo e maa ba.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: A ha zugba a nɔ tsuo, nɛ lɔ ɔ ha zugba a nɔ yu tuu. A ye tsohi tsuo ngɛ zugba a nɔ, kɛ tso yibliihi nɛ gbiɛ ngo ngu ɔ si ɔ; nɛ nɔ mumu ko kulaa píɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a tsuo nɔ.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ tsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron nɔuu nɛ e de mɛ ke, “I pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ; nɛ nyɛ hu i tɔ̃ nyɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Yawɛ tsake beleku kɔɔhiɔ ɔ kɛ pee bonyoku kɔɔhiɔ nɛ nya wa, nɛ kɔɔhiɔ ɔ muɔ baalɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ya pue Wo Tsu ɔ mi; e píɛ kake ngmelu ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ kplii Farao ɔ tsui ekohu nɛ e ha we nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ a ya. Diblii wo

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Wo o nine nɔ kɛ tsɔɔ hiɔwe, konɛ diblii kpii nɛ wo ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Mose pee ja, nɛ diblii kpii wo ngɛ Egipt ligbi etɛ.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Nɔ ko nɔ ko nɛ e nyɛmi, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ti si kɛ ji he nɛ e ngɛ ɔ ligbi etɛ. Se Israel bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ je mi tsɔ ha mɛ ngɛ a hi he ɔmɛ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Farao ɔ tsɛ Mose nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ho nɛ nyɛ ya ja Yawɛ ɔ; nyɛ bimɛ ɔmɛ ma nyɛ nɛ a kɛ nyɛ nɛ ya, se nyɛ to ɔmɛ, kɛ nyɛ na amɛ lɛɛ nyɛ si mɛ.”

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Se Mose bi lɛ ke, “Lɛɛ mo nitsɛ o ma ha wɔ lohwehi nɛ wa kɛ ya sã bɔ ha Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ lo?

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ kplii Farao ɔ tsui ekohu, nɛ e ha we nɛ a ya.

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Mose de lɛ ke, “Saminya! Kaa bɔ nɛ o de ɔ, o be imi hu ye hɛ mi nae hu gblegbleegble!”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “E piɛ haomi kake nɛ i kɛ maa ba Farao ɔ kɛ Egipt nɔ, nɛ lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ma ha nɛ nyɛɛ je. Ke be ɔ su nɛ e ma ha nɛ nyɛɛ ho ɔ, pe e maa fie nyɛ, nɛ e maa bɛɛ nyɛ kaa a bɛɛɔ dwɔmi.

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Yawɛ dloomi nya a, Egipt bi ɔmɛ na Israel bi ɔmɛ a he bua jɔmi. Niinɛ, Farao ɔ tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ ma a tsuo buu Mose kaa nɔmlɔ ngua nitsɛnitsɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Mose de Farao ɔ ke, “Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Maa pee nyɔ mi kpɛti ɔ, ma je kpo nɛ ma ya kpa Egipt zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: Bitɛte tsuaa bitɛte ngɛ Egipt ɔ ma gbo, kɛ je Farao ɔ bitɛte nɛ ma ba ye e tsɛ se hwɔɔ se ɔ nɔ, kɛ yaa si nyɔguɛ yo nɛ ngɛ mamu wɛɛe ngɛ wɛ se ɔ bitɛte nɔ, kɛ lohwehi hu a kekleekle bihi tsuo.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Ya nɛ pɛ́ hyɛ, nɛ eko hu be pɛe ligbi ko maa pɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ tsuo.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Se Israel bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ gbe po be huãe kɛ wo nɔmlɔ ko, loo lohwe ko. Nɛ enɛ ɔmɛ nyɛ ma kɛ le kaa imi Yawɛ, i kɛ mi gbami ba Egipt bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti.’

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: O tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo ma ba kpla si ha mi, nɛ a ma kpa mi pɛɛ ma de ke, ‘Nyɛɛ ho, nyɛɛ kɛ nihi nɛ nyɛɛ nyɛ se ɔ tsuo.’ Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ma je.” Nɛ Mose kɛ mi mi la nɛ nya wa je Farao ɔ hɛ mi.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Farao ɔ be mo tue bue bɔ nɛ pee nɛ ye nyakpɛ ní ɔmɛ nɛ hiɛ babauu ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Aaron pee nyakpɛ ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ Farao ɔ hɛ mi; se Yawɛ kplii Farao ɔ tsui, nɛ e ha we nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ a je zugba a nɔ kɛ ho.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose kɛ Aaron ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ ke,

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: “Nyɔhiɔ nɛ ɔ maa pee kekleekle nyɔhiɔ ngɛ jeha a mi ha nyɛ.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Nyɛ de Israel ma a tsuo ke nyɔhiɔ nɛ ɔ ligbi nɛ ji nyɔngma a, nyumu tsuaa nyumu nɛ hla to bi kake, jijɔ, loo apletsi kɛ ha e we.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ to lohwe ɔmɛ kɛ ya si nyɔhiɔ ɔ ligbi nɛ ji nyɔngma kɛ eywiɛ ɔ. Jamɛ a gbɔkuɛ ɔ ji be nɛ Israel ma a tsuo maa gbe to bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a ngɔ muɔ ɔ eko kɛ diki we mi he nɛ a maa ye lo ɔ ngɛ ɔ sinya tso enyɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ a yiti nɔ́ ɔ a he.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: A sã lo ɔ, nɛ a ye lɛ kɛ agba pui, kɛ abolo kplolo jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi nɔuu.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: A ko ye lo ɔ mumu, nɛ a ko hoo lɛ ngɛ nyu mi hulɔ. Se a sã lohwe ɔ mluku; e yi ɔ, e nane ɔmɛ, kɛ e mi ní ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: A ko si eko nɛ je nɛ na yi. Ke eko piɛ kɛ ya si mɔtu ɔ, a sã.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ye ní ɔ kaa blɔ hiali. Nyɛɛ fi nyɛ kpɛti; nyɛ tokota nɛ hi nyɛ nane; nyɛ dɛma tso nɛ hi nyɛ dɛ mi, nɛ nyɛɛ ye ní ɔ esɔesɔ; ejakaa Hetsɔmi nyami ligbi kɛ ha imi, Yawɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: “Jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, ma gu Egipt zugba a nɔ kɛ be, nɛ ma gbe bitɛtehi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ, kɛ a lohwe ɔmɛ hu a kekleekle bi kuhi. Egipt mawu ɔmɛ lɛɛ ma kpata mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a hɛ mi. Imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Muɔ ɔ maa to nyɛ we ɔmɛ a he so, nɛ ke i na muɔ ɔ pɛ ma tsɔ nyɛ he kɛ be, nɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ a tue gblami ɔ, nyɛɛ lɛɛ eko be nyɛ nɔ bae.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: “Kɛ je kekleekle ligbi ɔ kɛ yaa si ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, nyɛɛ ye abolo kplolo. Nyɛ kpa masa peemi ngɛ we ɔmɛ a mi kɛ je kekleekle ligbi ɔ. Mo nɔ nɛ o maa ye masa nɔ́ ko ɔ, a ma je mo we kɛ je Israel.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Kekleekle ligbi ɔ, kɛ ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, nyɛɛ bɔ gua nɛ nyɛ ja Yawɛ. A ko tsu nɔ́ ko jamɛ a ligbi enyɔ ɔmɛ; ní nɛ nɔ maa ye pɛ nɛ nyɛ maa hoo.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Nyɛ bɔni abolo kplolo yemi kɛ je kekleekle nyɔhiɔ ɔ ligbi nyɔngma kɛ eywiɛ ɔ gbɔkuɛ kɛ yaa si nyɔhiɔ ɔ ligbi nɛ ji nyingmi enyɔ kɛ kake ɔ gbɔkuɛ nya si.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɔ ko nɛ ko to masa ngɛ e we mi ligbi kpaago. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ye masa nɔ́ ko ɔ, nubwɔ ji lɛ jio, we no ji lɛ jio, a je lɛ we.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko ye masa nɔ́ ko; he tsuaa he nɛ ji nyɛ we nɔ ɔ, nyɛɛ ye abolo kplolo pɛ.” Kekleekle Hetsɔmi ɔ

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Mose tsɛ Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ tsuo kpe, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ ya hla jijɔhi nyɛɛ to we puɔ nya we puɔ nya, nɛ nyɛɛ gbe kɛ ha Hetsɔmi ɔ yemi.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ngɔ muɔ ɔ kɛ wo kã mi. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, nyɛɛ fi nga kɛ bla kaa bɛ, nɛ nyɛ kɛ sɔ muɔ ɔ kɛ kpa sinya tso enyɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ yiti nɔ́ ɔ a he. Nyɛ ti nɔ ko nɛ ko gu sinya a nya kɛ je kpo kɛ yaa si mɔtu,
