english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: ejakaa Yawɛ ma ba gu ma a mi kɛ be nɛ e ya gbe Egipt bi ɔmɛ. Se ke e na muɔ ɔ ngɛ sinya tso ɔmɛ a he ɔ, e maa tsɔ sinya a he kɛ be, nɛ e be hae nɛ gbenɔ bɔfo ɔ nɛ ji nɔ hɛ mi kpatalɔ ɔ maa sɛ nyɛ we ɔmɛ a mi nɛ e ba gbe nyɛ.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ ya su zugba a nɛ Yawɛ wo si kaa e kɛ ma ha nyɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ, nyɛɛ pee kusumi nɛ ɔ daa.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Nɛ ke nyɛ bimɛ bi nyɛ ke, ‘Kusumi nɛ ɔ sisi nɛɛ?’ ɔ,

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: nyɛ de mɛ ke, ‘Yawɛ Hetsɔmi ɔ bɔ sami ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; ejakaa e tsɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ a he ngɛ Egipt. E gbe Egipt bi ɔmɛ, se wɔɔ lɛɛ e ha wa yi na wami.’ ” Kɛkɛ nɛ ni ɔmɛ ma a yi si nɛ a ja Mawu.

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ ho nɛ a ya pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de Mose kɛ Aaron ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bitɛte ɔmɛ a gbenɔ

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Nyɔ mi kɔ̃kɔ̃ɔ̃kɔ̃ ɔ, Yawɛ gbe Egipt zugba a nɔ kekleekle binyumuhi tsuo, kɛ je Farao ɔ bitɛte ɔ nɛ maa ye tsɛ ngɛ sɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ ya si pã mi no bitɛte nɔ. We mi lohwehi hu Yawɛ gbe a kekleekle bihi tsuo.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Farao ɔ te si; e kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ tsuo, nɛ a wo yana nguaa ngɛ Egipt, ejakaa we ko we ko be nɛ a gbo we ngɛ mi.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Nɛ nyɔ ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, Farao ɔ tsɔ nɛ a ya tsɛ Mose kɛ Aaron kɛ ba, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ te si nɛ nyɛɛ je ye ma mi bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti, nyɛɛ kɛ Israel ma a tsuo, nɛ nyɛ ya ja Yawɛ kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ de ɔ.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ho kɛ nyɛ to ɔmɛ, kɛ nyɛ na amɛ kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ de ɔ. Nyɛɛ sɔle ha mi, konɛ Yawɛ nɛ gbaa imi hulɔ.”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ tsitsɛɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a yi se ke a pee esɔ nɛ a je a zugba a nɔ; ejakaa a kɛ hɛdɔ de ke, “Wa yi ta oo!”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɔ a ma nɛ sa we lolo ɔ, kɛ ma sowe ɔmɛ, nɛ a fi kpla a konɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ pee kaa bɔ nɛ Mose de mɛ ɔ; a ya ba june ní, sika hiɔ, sika tsu, kɛ bohi ngɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ a dɛ.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ha Egipt bi ɔmɛ ná Israel bi ɔmɛ a he bua jɔmi, nɛ a ha mɛ níhi nɛ a ya ba ngɛ a dɛ ɔ. Blɔ nɔ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ gu kɛ kpakpaa Egipt bi ɔmɛ a he níhi kɛ je ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Israel bi ɔmɛ je Egipt

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ nyɛɛ nane kɛ je Rameses kɛ ho Sukot ya. Nyumu ɔmɛ kɛkɛ a hiɛmi maa pee akpe lafa ekpa; slo yihi kɛ jokuɛwi.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Futufutu nimli komɛ hu piɛ a he, kɛ tohi, kɛ nahi babauu.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Nɛ a ngɔ ma a nɛ a kɛ je Egipt ɔ kɛ sã abolo kplolo. A na we be nɛ a kɛ gbe ma a; niye ní hu a hoo we, ejakaa pe a fie mɛ kpatakpata kɛ je Egipt.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ ji nyɔ nɛ Yawɛ huɔ nɛ e kɛ je Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ nɛ. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ pee nyɔ nɛ daa jeha a, Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ a nina tsuo huɔɔ nyɔ kɛ haa Yawɛ. Hetsɔmi nyami be ɔ he mlaahi

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose kɛ Aaron ke, “Hetsɔmi nyami be ɔ he mlaahi ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: ma je no ko ma je no ko kó ye Hetsɔmi niye ní ɔ.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Se nyɔguɛ nɛ a he ma nyɛ nɛ e ye eko ke a po lɛ se.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Nubwɔ, loo apaatsɛ nɛ ko ye eko.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ye ní ɔ ngɛ we mi he nɛ a gbe to ɔ ngɛ ɔ; a kɛ lo ɔ eko ko je kpo kɛ je we ɔ mi, nɛ a ko ywia lohwe ɔ wu ko hulɔ.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Israel ma a tsuo nɛ ye nyami be nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Se ke nubwɔ ko nɛ ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti suɔ nɛ e ye Yawɛ Hetsɔmi ɔ, moo po nyumuhi tsuo nɛ ngɛ e we ɔ mi ɔ; kɛkɛ e pee kaa we no. Se mɔmlɔtɔtsɛ be he blɔ kaa e yeɔ.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Mlaa kake too nɛ ɔ maa fɔ si ha we no kɛ nubwɔ tsuo.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ tsuo bu tue, nɛ a pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ wo Mose kɛ Aaron mlaa a.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nɛ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ nɔuu ɔ, Yawɛ je Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ wɛtso nya wɛtso nya.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Moo ngɔ kekleekle binyumu ɔmɛ tsuo ngɔ to ha mi. Binyumu tsuaa binyumu nɛ bliɔ fɔmi nya ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ, nɔmlɔ bi jio, lohwe bi jio, ye nɔ ji lɛ.” Abolokplolo nyami be

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Ke Yawɛ kɛ nyɛ ya su zugba kpakpa, zugba nɛ kle nɛ baa ní ɔ nɔ ɔ, nyɛɛ ye nyami be nɛ ɔ ngɛ nyɔhiɔ nɛ ɔ mi daa jeha. Kanaan bi, Hit bi, Amor bi, Hiv bi, kɛ Yebus bi a zugba a nɛ Yawɛ ka nyɛ nɛmɛ kita ke e ma ha nyɛ ɔ nɛ i ngɛ tsɔɔe ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ye abolo kplolo ligbi kpaago, se ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ lɛɛ nyɛ nya kɛ wo Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Á ye abolo kplolo ligbi kpaago ɔmɛ tsuo. A ko na masa abolo ko ngɛ nyɛ dɛ mi, nɛ a ko na masa ko ngɛ nyɛ huza a nɔ he ko he ko.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, nyɛ ma de nyɛ bimɛ ɔmɛ ke nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ pee ha wɔ be nɛ wa hia kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ he je nɛ wa ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ pee ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nɛ enɛ ɔ maa pee kaa okadi ngɛ nyɛ nine he, kɛ nyɛ hɛ nya, konɛ Yawɛ mlaa a nɛ hi nyɛ nya daa; ejakaa he wami kpetekpleenyɛ nɛ Yawɛ kɛ je nyɛ kɛ je Egipt.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ pee kusumi nɛ ɔ daa jeha be nɛ a to ɔ. Bitɛte

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: “Ke Yawɛ kɛ nyɛ ba Kanaan zugba a nɔ kaa bɔ nɛ e ka nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ kita ke e maa pee ɔ,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: nyɛɛ gbaa bitɛte tsuaa bitɛte nɛ bliɔ fɔmi nya a nɔ kɛ ha Yawɛ.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Nyɛ teji kekleekle bi ku lɛɛ nyɛ maa ngɔ jijɔ kɛ dani lɛ. Nɛ ke nyɛ be suɔe nɛ nyɛ dani lɛ ɔ, lɛɛ nyɛ maa ku e kuɛ. Bitɛte tsuaa bitɛte ngɛ nyɛ binyumu ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ, nyɛ dani lɛ.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Hwɔɔ se ke nɔ ko binyumu bi lɛ ke mɛni ji kusumi nɛ ɔ sisi ɔ, e de lɛ ke, ‘Yawɛ kɛ he wami kpetekpleenyɛ je wɔ kɛ je nyɔguɛ yemi sisi ngɛ Egipt.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Farao ɔ kplii e tsui nɛ e kplɛɛ we kaa waa ho ɔ, Yawɛ gbe Egipt kekleekle bimɛ tsuo; nimli a bitɛtehi, kɛ lohwehi a kekleekle bihi. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, lohwe ku tsuaa lohwe ku nɛ bliɔ fɔmi nya a, i kɛ sãã bɔ ngɔ haa Yawɛ; se ye bitɛte ɔmɛ lɛɛ i danii mɛ.

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Kusumi nɛ ɔ maa pee okadi ngɛ o nine he, kɛ o hɛ nya, ejakaa he wami kpetekpleenyɛ nɛ Yawɛ kɛ je wɔ kɛ je Egipt.’ ” Yawɛ nyɛɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Farao ɔ ha nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ je ɔ, Mawu kpakaa we mɛ kɛ gu blɔ kpiti ɔ nɛ gu Filisti bi ɔmɛ a zugba a mi ɔ. Mawu de ke, “Ke ta ba na ma nɛ ɔ pɛ, ke o li peemi ɔ, a yi mi ma plɛ, nɛ a maa kpale kɛ ho Egipt ya.”

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Mose ngɔ Yosef wuhi kɛ ho; ejakaa Yosef ka Israel bi ɔmɛ kita, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, Mawu ma ba je nyɛ. Ke jamɛ a be ɔ su ɔ, nyɛɛ ngɔ ye wuhi kɛ je hiɛ ɔ kɛ to dɛ kɛ ho.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Nɛ a hia kɛ je Sukot, nɛ a ya to si ngɛ Etam ngɛ nga a nya.

english_verse: During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
translation_verse: Piani ɔ, bɔku titima a ngɛ ma a hɛ mi, nɛ nyɔ mi ɔ, la titima a ngɛ ma a hɛ mi.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “De Israel bi ɔmɛ ke a kpale a se nɛ a ya to si ngɛ Pi Hahirot hɛ mi, ngɛ Migdol kɛ wo ɔ a kpɛti. A sito he ɔ nɛ kpee Baal Zefon hɛ mi ngɛ wo ɔ nya.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ ma susu kaa Israel bi ɔmɛ ya tla blɔ, nɛ a ngɛ lalaalo woe ngɛ nga a nɔ, nɛ nga a sá a yi.

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Ma kplii Farao ɔ tsui, nɛ e maa fie a se. Nɛ manye nɛ ma ye ngɛ Farao ɔ, kɛ e ta a tsuo a nɔ ɔ ma ha ye hɛ mi maa ba nyami. Jamɛ a be ɔ, Egipt bi ɔmɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.” Nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ pee ja.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Benɛ a ya bɔ Egipt matsɛ ɔ ke ni ɔmɛ tu fo kɛ je ɔ, Farao ɔ kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsake a juɛmi ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a he, nɛ a de ke, “Mɛni wa pee nɛ ɔ, kaa wa ngmɛɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a he nɛ a ho nɛ a be wɔ sɔmɔe hu nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ dla e ta zugba lɛ ɔ, kɛ e tabo ɔ,

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Yawɛ kplii Egipt matsɛ ɔ tsui, nɛ be nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ yaa kɛ gɛjɛmi ɔ, e fie a se.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Farao ɔ we okpɔngɔ ɔmɛ, e tabo ɔ, kɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ tsuo hia kɛ nyɛɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a se, nɛ a ya na mɛ be nɛ a pueɔ si ngɛ Wo Tsu ɔ nya, ngɛ Pi Hahirot kasa nya, ngɛ Baal Zefon hɛ mi ɔ.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Benɛ Farao ɔ ná mɛ ta, nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ wo a hɛ nɔ nɛ a na kaa Egipt bi ɔmɛ nyɛɛ a se kɛ ma a, sawale nu mɛ, nɛ a kpa bubuubui kɛ tsɛ Yawɛ.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: A bi Mose ke, “Anɛ yɔkɔhi nɛ be Egipt he je nɛ o kpaka wɔ kɛ ba nɛ wa ba gbo tlɔ nga pa lo? Mɛni he je o kɛ wɔ ye kikɛmɛ a sane, nɛ o ngɔ wɔ kɛ je Egipt ɔ?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he nɛ wa de mo ngɛ Egipt ke o ngmɛɛ wa he nɛ wa sɔmɔ Egipt bi ɔmɛ ɔ nɛ; ejakaa afani nɛ wa ma sɔmɔ Egipt bi ɔmɛ pe kaa wa ma gbo tlɔ nga pa.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Se Mose de ma a ke, “Nyɛ ko je fɔ̃, nyɛɛ da si kaa nyumuhi, nɛ nyɛ maa na bɔ nɛ Yawɛ maa pee kɛ he nyɛ yi wami mwɔnɛ ɔ. Egipt bi ɔmɛ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ mɛ hyɛe mwɔnɛ ɔ, nyɛ be mɛ nae hu gblegbleegble.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ maa hwu ha nyɛ; nyɛɛ lɛɛ nyɛɛ buɛ dii!”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Yawɛ bi Mose ke, “Mɛni he je o ngɛ ngmlaa kpae kɛ ngɛ mi tsɛe ɔ? De Israel bi ɔmɛ ke a ya a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Wo o tso ɔ nɔ nɛ o kpã o nine mi ngɛ wo ɔ nɔ, nɛ o dla e mi enyɔ, konɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ a nyɛɛ zugba gbigbli nɔ kɛ po wo ɔ.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Ma kplii Egipt bi ɔmɛ a tsui, nɛ a maa nyɛɛ a se; kɛkɛ ɔ, ye hɛ mi maa ba nyami, ejakaa ma ye Farao ɔ kɛ e tabo ɔ, e ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ e we okpɔngɔ ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo a nɔ kunimi.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mawu bɔfo ɔ nɛ nyɛɛ Israel tabo ɔ hɛ mi ɔ plɛ ya je a se. Bɔku titima a je a hɛ mi, nɛ e ho ya je a se blɔ,

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: ngɛ Egipt tabo ɔ, kɛ Israel tabo ɔ a kpɛti. Bɔku ɔ ha diblii wo Egipt bi ɔmɛ, se Israel bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ a hyɛ nɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, tabo enyɔ ɔmɛ nyɛ we nɛ a su a sibi a he nɛ je kɛ na.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose wo e nine nɔ ngɛ wo ɔ nɔ, nɛ Yawɛ ha kɔɔhiɔ nguaa ko fia kɛ je beleku jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi tsuo kɛ tsɛ̃ wo ɔ kɛ ya se. Nɛ wo ɔ mi gba enyɔ hiɛ kɛ hiɛ, nɛ e kpɛti ɔ plɛ pee zugba gbigbli.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ nyɛɛ zugba gbigbli nɔ kɛ gu wo ɔ kpɛti, nɛ nyu ɔ pee kaa gbogbo ngɛ a hiɔ nɔ kɛ a muɔ nɔ.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Mɔtu kpla a, Yawɛ hyɛ Egipt tabo ɔ kɛ gu la titima a, kɛ bɔku titima a a mi, nɛ e ha nɛ sawale nu mɛ.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ ha nɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ a ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ a nanehi pu zu, nɛ a nyɛɛmi pee dengme. Egipt bi ɔmɛ a nya hé gbi nɛ a de ke, “Nyɛ ha waa tu fo ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a nya; ejakaa Yawɛ piɛ a he nɛ e kɛ wɔ Egipt bi ɔmɛ ngɛ fiae.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Mo wo o nine nɔ ngɛ wo ɔ nɔ, konɛ nyu ɔ nɛ kpale ku pue Egipt bi ɔmɛ, kɛ a ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ a we okpɔngɔ ta buli ɔmɛ a nɔ.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Mose wo e nine nɔ ngɛ wo ɔ nɔ, nɛ benɛ je maa na a, wo ɔ kpale tsa ekohu. Egipt bi ɔmɛ tu fo nɛ a kɛ wo ɔ ba kpe, nɛ Yawɛ tsitsɛɛ mɛ kɛ pue wo ɔ mi.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Nyu ɔ kpale ba tsa, nɛ Farao ɔ ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ, e we okpɔngɔ ta buli ɔmɛ, kɛ e tabo ɔ tsuo nɛ nyɛɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a se kɛ ya sɛ wo ɔ mi ɔ tlɔ mi nɛ a ti nɔ kake po píɛ.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Se Israel bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ a nyɛɛ zugba gbigbli nɔ kɛ po wo ɔ, nɛ nyu ɔ wlua kaa gbogbo ngɛ a hiɔ nɔ kɛ a muɔ nɔ.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ pee kɛ kpɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Egipt bi ɔmɛ a dɛ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Israel bi ɔmɛ na Egipt bi ɔmɛ nɛ a gbo kɛ pueɔ si ngɛ wo ɔ nya.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ na he wami nguaa nɛ Yawɛ kɛ ye Egipt bi ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ, a ye lɛ gbeye, nɛ a he lɛ, kɛ e tsɔlɔ Mose ɔ ye.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ la la nɛ ɔ kɛ je Yawɛ yi: “Ma la kɛ je Yawɛ yi, ejakaa e ye kunimi nguaa. E tsɛ̃ okpɔngɔ kɛ e nɔ hilɔ ɔ kɛ wo wo ɔ mi.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ji ye he falɔ kpanaa; lɛ ji nɔ nɛ he ye yi wami. Ma je e yi, ejakaa lɛ ji ye Mawu; ma wo e hɛ mi nyami, ejakaa Tsaatsɛ e Mawu ji lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Yawɛ ɔ, tatsɛ ji lɛ; e biɛ ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: “E tsɛ̃ Farao ɔ ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ e tabo ɔ tsuo ngɔ wo wo ɔ mi bum! Nɛ e tatsɛ ngua amɛ hu gbo tlɔ Wo Tsu ɔ mi.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: “Yawɛ, o hiɔ nine he wami ɔ ngɛ gbeye; o hiɔ nine ɔ tsɔtslɔɔ he nyɛli ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: O kɛ o we agboje tsɛ̃ o he nyɛli ɔmɛ kɛ pue si. Nɛ o mi mi la a tso gegeege nɛ e sã mɛ kaa dwɔmi.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: O fli o gugwɔ mi ngɛ wo ɔ nɔ, nɛ nyu ɔ bua e he nya da si kaa gbogbo; ohue mi nyu ɔ fi, nɛ e wlua gɛgɛnii.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: He nyɛlɔ ɔ ke, ‘Ma nyɛɛ a se nɛ ma ya na mɛ; ma dla ta ní ɔmɛ ngɛ ye suɔmi nya. Ma hia ye ha a, nɛ ma kpata a hɛ mi.’

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Se o ha kɔɔhiɔ fia, nɛ wo ɔ ha a nɔ; Egipt bi ɔmɛ mu kaa sumue ngɛ nyu nɛ he ngɛ gbeye ɔ mi.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: “Yawɛ lee, mɛnɔ ngɛ kaa mo? Mɛnɔ ngɛ kaa mo ngɛ mawu ɔmɛ a kpɛti? O je agbo; o he ngɛ gbeye; mo, mo nyakpɛ ní peelɔ.

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: O je o he wami ɔ kpo, nɛ zugba a mii wa he nyɛli ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Je ma amɛ nu he, nɛ a tsui po; sawale nu Filisti bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Edom matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a he mi jɔ̃; sawale nu Moab nimeli ɔmɛ; Kanaan bi ɔmɛ tsuo a kã a laa.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Gbeye kɛ fɔ̃ nu mɛ; Yawɛ, o he wami ɔ ha a nya jɔ kɛ ya si be nɛ mo Yawɛ, o ma a nɛ mo nitsɛ o he ɔ ba be kɛ ho.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: Yawɛ maa ye matsɛ kɛ maa ya neneene.” Miriam la

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Aaron nyɛmiyo Miriam, gbalɔyo ɔ ngɔ fao, nɛ yi ɔmɛ tsuo nyɛɛ e se kɛ fao fiami kɛ domi.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Nɛ Miriam la ha mɛ ke, “Nyɛ la kɛ je Yawɛ yi, ejakaa e ye kunimi nguaa. E tsɛ̃ okpɔngɔ kɛ e nɔ hilɔ ɔ kɛ wo wo ɔ mi bum!” Nyu doodooe ɔ

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Mose kpaka Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Wo Tsu ɔ he kɛ ho Shur nga a nɔ ya. A nyɛɛ nga a nɔ ligbi etɛ nɛ a nɛ́ nyu.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ ma a tu munyu huitihuiti kɛ si Mose ke, “Mɛni wa maa nu?”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ hɛdɔ tsɛ Yawɛ, nɛ Yawɛ tsɔɔ lɛ tso ko. Mose sake tso ɔ ngɔ fɔ nyu ɔ mi, kɛkɛ nɛ nyu ɔ jɔ. Lejɛ ɔ nɛ Yawɛ wo mɛ mlaa ngɛ, nɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ e ka mɛ ngɛ.

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: E de mɛ ke, “Ke nyɛ maa bu Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ tue, nɛ nyɛ maa pee nɔ́ nɛ da ngɛ e hɛ mi, nɛ nyɛ maa ye e kita amɛ, kɛ e mlaa amɛ tsuo a nɔ ɔ, lɛɛ hiɔ ɔmɛ nɛ i kɛ gbla Egipt bi ɔmɛ a tue ɔ, ekoeko be nyɛ nɔ bae. Imi ji Yawɛ; imi ji nyɛ tsalɔ.”

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Israel ma a tsuo hia kɛ je Elim, nɛ a ba su Sin nga a nɔ, ngɛ Elim kɛ Sinai a kpɛti. Nɛ́ a je Egipt ɔ se nyɔhiɔ enyɔne ɔ ligbi nɛ ji nyɔngma kɛ enuɔ ɔ nɛ a hia a nɛ.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo tu munyu huitihuiti kɛ si Mose kɛ Aaron ngɛ nga a nɔ,

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: nɛ a de ke, “Wa ná nɛ Yawɛ gbe wɔ mohu ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ, he nɛ wa hii si ngɛ pɔ buɛhi a he, nɛ wa yeɔ ní wa tɔɔ ɔ. Hyɛ kaa nyɛ ngɔ wɔ kɛ ba nga nɛ ɔ nɔ, konɛ nyɛ ba gbe asafo nɛ ɔ tsuo kɛ mi mi hwɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Hyɛ, ma ha abolo maa nɛ kɛ je hiɔwe pue si ha nyɛ. Daa ligbi ɔ, ma a maa ya nɛ a ya bua nɔ́ nɛ maa su mɛ ligbi kake yemi nya, nɛ ma kɛ ka mɛ ma hyɛ kaa a maa ye ye mlaa amɛ a nɔ lo.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji ekpa a lɛɛ a bua ligbi enyɔ yeye nya, nɛ a dla kɛ to.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose kɛ Aaron de Israel bi ɔmɛ tsuo ke, “Gbɔkuɛ nɛ ɔ, nyɛ ma na maa le kaa Yawɛ ji nɔ nɛ jé nyɛ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Mɔtu ɔ, nyɛ maa na Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ; ejakaa e nu nyɛ munyu huitihuiti nɛ nyɛ tu kɛ si lɛ ɔ. Wɔɔ lɛɛ wa pi ni komɛ nɛ ke nyɛ hɔɔ nya si wo wa he nɛ e peeɔ nɔ́ ko.”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Mose de mɛ ke, “Yawɛ ma ha nyɛ lo nɛ nyɛɛ ye gbɔkuɛ, kɛ abolo nɛ maa tɔ nyɛ mɔtu; ejakaa e nu nya si nɛ nyɛ hɔɔ kɛ wo e he ɔ. Nyɛ munyu huitihuiti ɔmɛ ɔ, pi wɔ nɛ nyɛ tu kɛ si, se Yawɛ mohu.”

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Mose de Aaron ke, “De Israel ma a kulaa ke a hɛ mɛ kɛ su Yawɛ he, ejakaa e nu a munyu huitihuiti ɔmɛ.”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Benɛ Aaron kɛ Israel ma a ngɛ munyu ɔ tue nɛ a plɛ nɛ a maa hyɛ nga a nɔ blɔ ɔ, né Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami nɛ je kpo ngɛ bɔku ɔ mi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “I nu Israel bi ɔmɛ a nya si hɔɔmi ɔ. De mɛ ke gbɔkuɛ nya si nɛ ɔ, nyɛ ma na lo maa ye, nɛ mɔtu ɔ, nyɛ ma na abolo maa ye nɛ nyɛ maa tɔ, kɛkɛ nyɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Gbɔkuɛ ɔ, hɔnehi fuu ba ba ha a sito he ɔ; nɛ mɔtu ɔ, bɔ́ nɛ kɛ bɔle ma a.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Benɛ bɔ́ ɔ gbli ɔ, ní komɛ pue si ngɛ nga a nɔ pɛtɛpɛtɛ futafuta kaa ngo kpɔhi ngɛ zugba.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ na a, a li nɔ́ nɛ ji. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a de ngɛ a je gbi mi ke, “Mana.” E sisi ji, “Mɛni ji nɛ ɔ?” Mose de mɛ ke, “Abolo nɛ Yawɛ ha nyɛ nɛ nyɛɛ ye ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ pee ja; ni komɛ muɔ fuu, nɛ ni komɛ hu muɔ bɔɔ pɛ.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Mose de mɛ ke, “Nɔ ko nɔ ko kó to eko nɛ je nɛ na yi.”

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Se a ti ni komɛ bui nɔ́ nɛ Mose de ɔ tue, nɛ a to. Benɛ je na a, e sa nɛ e wo gɔgɔ kɛ e he fu gbii. Nɛ eko kɛ ya si je na Mose mi mi fu mɛ.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Daa mɔtu ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ yaa nɛ e ya buaa bɔ nɛ maa su lɛ yemi nya; se ke pu nya wa pɛ e sile.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji ekpa a lɛɛ a bua ligbi enyɔ yemi hiɛmi nya, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ ná lita eywiɛɛywiɛ. Nɛ benɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ tsuo ba bɔ Mose amaniɛ ɔ,

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Mose de mɛ ke, “Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Hwɔɔ ji he jɔɔmi ligbi, Yawɛ Hejɔɔmi ligbi klɔuklɔu. Nyɛɛ sã nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ sami, nɛ nyɛɛ hoo nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ hoomi, nɛ nɔ́ nɛ maa piɛ ngɛ se ɔ, nyɛ ngɔ to si kɛ yaa si mɔtu.’ ”

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Mose de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ye enɛ ɔ mwɔnɛ ɔ, ejakaa mwɔnɛ ɔ ji Yawɛ Hejɔɔmi ligbi; mwɔnɛ ɔ, nyɛ be eko nae ngɛ nga a nɔ.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Nyɛ ma bua nya ligbi ekpa; se ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, nɛ ji Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ, nyɛ be eko nae.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, a ti ni komɛ je kpo nɛ a ya bua niye ní nya, se a nɛ eko.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Kɛ yaa si mɛni be nɛ nyɛ maa ya nɔ ma gbo mi tue nɛ nyɛ ma kua ye mlaa amɛ a nɔ yemi?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ hyɛ, imi Yawɛ, i ha nyɛ Hejɔɔmi ligbi; nɛ lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ligbi nɛ ji ekpa a nɔ ɔ, i haa nyɛ ligbi enyɔ nya ní. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ hi si ngɛ he nɛ e ngɛ; nɔ ko nɔ ko kó je kpo kɛ ya he ko ngɛ ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ tsɛ niye ní ɔ ke mana. E ngɛ kaa tso yiblii mi wu nyafii; e hiɛ futafuta, nɛ e ngɔɔmi ngɛ kaa akpɔɔnɔɔ nɛ hwo ngɛ mi.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Mose de ke, “Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘A susu mana lita enyɔ hiɛmi nya ngɔ to si ha nyɛ nina, konɛ a ba na niye ní nɛ i kɛ lɛ nyɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ benɛ i je nyɛ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Mose de Aaron ke, “Hla buɛ ko, nɛ o kɛ mana lita enyɔ hiɛmi nya nɛ wo mi, nɛ o kɛ ma Yawɛ hɛ mi, nɛ a kɛ to si ha nyɛ nina.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Nɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa Mose ɔ, Aaron ngɔ kɛ ma somi daka a hɛ mi.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Israel ma mluku ɔ tsuo hia kɛ je Sin nga a nɔ bɔɔ bɔɔ bɔɔ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa mɛ ɔ, nɛ a ya to si ngɛ Refidim; se nyu be lejɛ ɔ nɛ ma a maa nu.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma a pia Mose, nɛ a de lɛ ke, “Ha wɔ nyu nɛ waa nu!” Mose de mɛ ke, “Mɛni he je nyɛ ngɛ mi piae? Mɛni he je nɛ nyɛ ngɛ Yawɛ kae ɔ?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Se kuma ngɛ ma a yee, nɛ a tu munyu huitihuiti kɛ si Mose, nɛ a de ke, “Mɛni he je o je wɔ kɛ je Egipt nɛ o ma ha nɛ kuma ba gbe wɔ, wa bimɛ, kɛ wa lohwehi tsuo nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Mose kɛ hɛdɔ fa kue ha Yawɛ ke, “Kɛ ma pee ma nɛ ɔ kɛɛ? A miɔ nɛ a maa fia mi tɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Moo nyɛɛ ma a hlami kɛ ho. O kɛ Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ ekomɛ nɛ ya, nɛ o hɛɛ tso ɔ nɛ o kɛ fia Nilo pa a ngɛ o dɛ mi.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: O nɛ, ma da o hɛ mi ngɛ tɛ sa a nɔ ngɛ Sinai yo ɔ nɔ. Ngɔɔ tso ɔ kɛ fia tɛ sa a, nɛ nyu maa je mi kɛ ba ha ma a nɛ a nu.” Nɛ Mose pee ja ngɛ Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Mose wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Masa kɛ Meriba, nɛ e de ke, “I wo kikɛmɛ a biɛ nɛ ɔ, ejakaa lejɛ ɔ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ pia Yawɛ ngɛ, nɛ lejɛ ɔ nɔuu a ka lɛ ngɛ benɛ a bi ke, ‘Anɛ Yawɛ ngɛ wa kpɛti, aloo e be?’ ɔ.” Israel kɛ Amalek hwu ta

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɛ Refidim ɔ, Amalek bi ɔmɛ hia ta ba tua mɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Mose de Yoshua ke, “Moo hla nyumu ɔmɛ ekomɛ, nɛ hwɔɔ a kɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ ya hwu. Imi lɛɛ ma ya da yoku ɔ yi mi kɛ Mawu tso ɔ ngɛ ye dɛ mi.”

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Yoshua pee kaa bɔ nɛ Mose de lɛ ɔ, nɛ e ho nɛ e kɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ ya hwu. Nɛ Mose, Aaron, kɛ Hur kuɔ yoku ɔ kɛ ho e yi mi ya.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Nɛ e ba mi kaa ke Mose wo e nine nɔ pɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a nine gu Amalek bi ɔmɛ a nɔ. Ke e nine ba si pɛ kɛkɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ a nine bɔni Israel bi ɔmɛ a he ngɔmi.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Se Mose kɔni ba gbo, nɛ Aaron kɛ Hur ya hla tɛ ba wo sisi. Nɔ kake da e kasa nya hiɛ, nɛ nɔ kake hu da e kasa nya hiɛ, nɛ a hɛɛ e kɔni ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ hiɔwe kɛ ya si pu nɔ si.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Nɛ Yoshua ye Amalek bi ɔmɛ a nɔ butuu.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Ngmaa nɔ nɛ ɔ kɛ wo womi mi nɛ e pee kaimi nɔ́. Ha nɛ e su Yoshua kaa ma kpata Amalek bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ a be mɛ kaie hu ngɛ zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Mose ma bɔ sami la tɛ ko nɛ e wo lɛ ke, “Yawɛ ji ye we aflangaa.”

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: E de ngɔ piɛ he ke, “Yawɛ hɛɛ e we aflangaa a ngɛ e dɛ mi. Yawɛ kɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ maa hwu kɛ maa ya neneene!”

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Nɛ e tsɔ ya de lɛ ke, “Imi, o ngatsɛ Yetro, kɛ o yo ɔ, kɛ o binyumuwi enyɔ ɔmɛ wa ma o ngɔ.”

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Mose je kpo nɛ e kɛ e ngatsɛ ɔ ya kpe; e ba e he si nɛ e fua lɛ atuu. Nɛ benɛ a nga a he ta a, a sɛ bo tsu ɔ mi.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Mose bɔ e ngatsɛ ɔ a blɔ hiami ɔ mi sanehi tsuo: níhi nɛ Yawɛ pee Farao ɔ kɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ nɛ e kɛ kpɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ, a blɔ hiami ɔ mi pɔtɔ kɛ dengme, kɛ bɔ nɛ Yawɛ je mɛ kɛ je kulaa mi.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: Kpaako loko i ná le paa kaa Yawɛ kle pe mawu ɔmɛ kulaa; ejakaa e he ma a yi wami kɛ je Egipt bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi, benɛ a ngɛ mɛ nisɛ ní pee ɔ.”

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Pɔ maa tɔ o kɛ ma a tsuo; ejakaa ma a tlomi ɔ jiɔ tsɔ, nɛ mo nɔ kake o be nyɛe tloomi.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, Mose he sɛ, nɛ a kɛ ma sanehi ba e hɛ mi nɛ e kojo. E kojo kɛ je mɔtu kɛ ya si du bubui nɛ ni ɔmɛ daa si.

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: Benɛ Mose ngatsɛ ɔ na níhi tsuo nɛ Mose ngɛ tsue ngɛ ma a mi ɔ, e bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni o ngɛ pee nɛ ɔ? Mɛni he je o ngɔ ní tsumi nɛ ɔ ngɔ fɔ mo nɔ kake too o nɔ, nɛ ma a tsuo daa si ngɛ o kuɛ nɔ mɔtumɔtu kɛ ya si du bubui kikɛ nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Mose he nɔ ke, “Ye ní tsumi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ, ejakaa ma a baa ye ngɔ ba biɔ Mawu ga womi.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Ke nɔ ko kɛ e nyɛmi na sane ɔ, a kɛ baa ye ngɔ nɛ i hyɛɛ mi, nɛ i tsɔɔ mɛ Mawu kita amɛ, kɛ Mawu blɔ nya tomi ɔmɛ.”

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose ngatsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “O blɔ nya tomi ɔ piɛ bɔɔ.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, moo bu mi tue nɛ ma wo mo ga; Mawu nɛ piɛ o he. Moo lɛɛ moo da ma a nane mi ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi, nɛ o ngɔ a sane ɔmɛ kɛ ba fɔ Mawu hɛ mi.

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: Moo lɛɛ moo tsɔɔ mɛ Mawu mlaa amɛ, kɛ e suɔmi nya ní ɔmɛ. Moo tsɔɔ mɛ bɔ nɛ sa nɛ a ba a je mi, kɛ níhi nɛ sa nɛ a peeɔ.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Ke o pee enɛ ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ Mawu fa mo ɔ, lɛɛ pɔ be mo tɔe, nɛ ni ɔmɛ tsuo maa kpale kɛ ho a wehi a mi ya kɛ tue mi jɔmi.”

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Mɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ kojoɔ ma a sanehi daa be tsuaa be. Mɛ nitsɛmɛ nɛ a buá sane tsɔwitsɔwihi a he; se sanehi nɛ a he wa lɛɛ a kɛ baa Mose ngɔ.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Mose wo e ngatsɛ ɔ blɔ, nɛ Yetro kpale kɛ ho e ma mi ya.

english_verse: The Israelites left Rephidim and arrived at the desert. Then two months after leaving Egypt, they arrived at the desert near Mount Sinai, where they set up camp at the foot of the mountain. This was two months after they had left Egypt.
translation_verse: Nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ je Egipt ɔ se nyɔhiɔ etɛne ɔ kekleekle ligbi ɔ, a je Refidim kɛ ho Sinai nga a nɔ ya, nɛ a ya to si ngɛ Sinai yo ɔ sisi.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Mose kuɔ yo ɔ kɛ ho Mawu ngɔ ya. Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ tsɛ Mose ngɛ yo ɔ mi, nɛ e de lɛ ke e ya nɛ e ya de Israel bi ɔmɛ, nɛ ji Yakob nina a ke,

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: “Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ na nɔ́ nɛ i pee Egipt bi ɔmɛ, kɛ bɔ nɛ i kɛ he wami je nyɛ kɛ je Egipt kaa nɔ́ nɛ kɔle pɛli nɔ nɛ nyɛ hii si ngɛ, nɛ i ngɔ nyɛ kɛ ba imi nitsɛ ye ngɔ.

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Se nyɛɛ lɛɛ nyɛ maa pee ye ma klɔuklɔu, nɛ nyɛ ma sɔmɔ mi kaa osɔfohi. Sɛ gbi nɛ ɔ, mo de Israel bi ɔmɛ.”

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Mose kple si kɛ ba nɛ e ba tsɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ, nɛ e ngɔ Yawɛ sɛ gbi ɔ ngɔ ha mɛ.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Nɛ ma a tsuo he nɔ nɛ a de ke, “Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ de ɔ, wa maa pee.” Mose kpale ya bɔ Yawɛ bɔ nɛ ma a de ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Hyɛ, i ma o ngɔ ngɛ bɔku kpii mi, konɛ ke ma a nu nɛ i kɛ mo ngɛ munyu tue ɔ, a he mo nɛ a ye kɛ ya neneene.” Mose ho nɛ e ya bɔ Yawɛ heto nɛ ma a ha lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya tsukɔ ma a he mwɔnɛ ɔ kɛ hwɔɔ. Ha nɛ a fɔ a tadehi a he,

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: nɛ benɛ e maa su ligbi nɛ ji etɛ ɔ, a dla a he; ejakaa hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ ligbi nɛ ji etɛ ɔ, imi Yawɛ, ma kple si kɛ ba Sinai yo ɔ nɔ, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ maa na mi.

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Nɔ ko nɔ ko nine nɛ ko sa nɔ ɔ he, se mohu a fia lɛ tɛ, loo a tsɛ̃ lɛ kɛ̃ɛ̃; lohwe ji lɛ jio, nɔmlɔ ji lɛ jio, e ko hi je mi. Ke titimati ɔ pɛ wawɛɛ nɛ e se kɛ ɔ, loko ma a nɛ kuɔ yo ɔ kɛ ba.”

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Mose kple si kɛ je yo ɔ nɔ kɛ ba ma a ngɔ, nɛ e ha ni ɔmɛ tsukɔ a he, nɛ a fɔ a tade ɔmɛ a he.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: E de ma a ke, “Nyɛ dla nyɛ he ha hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ ligbi nɛ ji etɛ ɔ; nɔ ko nɔ ko kó ta yo he.”

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji etɛ ɔ mɔtu ɔ, a nu hiɔmi simi, oslabai gbami, kɛ titimati pɛmi wawɛɛ ngɛ yo ɔ nɔ; bɔku kpii hu wo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Sawale nu ma a tsuo ngɛ a sito he ɔ, nɛ a he kpokpo.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose nyɛɛ ma a hɛ mi kɛ je sito he ɔ kɛ je kpo konɛ a kɛ Mawu nɛ ya kpe; nɛ a ho ya da si ngɛ yo ɔ sisi.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Sinai yo ɔ tsuo hyi kɛ la su ku; ejakaa Yawɛ kple si kɛ ba yo ɔ nɔ ngɛ la mi. La su ku ɔ ngɛ si tee kɛ ngɛ hiɔwe yae kaa buɛsa he la su ku, nɛ yo ɔ tsuo mimiɛ wawɛɛ nitsɛ.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Benɛ bɛ pɛmi ɔ nya wa a, Mose tu munyu, nɛ Mawu ha lɛ heto kɛ hiɔwe simi.

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Yawɛ kple si kɛ ba Sinai yo ɔ nɔ nɛ e tsɛ Mose, nɛ Mose kuɔ kɛ ho yo ɔ yi mi ya.

english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Kple si nɛ o ya tu munyu ngɔ tsɔɔ ma a, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko kó de ke e ngɛ piɛ ɔ gbae kɛ ma mi hyɛmi, nɛ́ nihi babauu a hɛ mi ko ba kpata.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Jã kɛ̃, osɔfo ɔmɛ nɛ mɛɛ a nyɛɔ suu ye he ɔ, mɛ hu hyɛ nɛ a tsukɔ a he, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Yawɛ ko ba kpata a hɛ mi.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
translation_verse: Mose de Yawɛ ke, “Ma a be nyɛe maa kuɔ Sinai yo ɔ; ejakaa mo nitsɛ nɛ o wo mlaa ke waa po piɛ kɛ wo he kɛ tsɔɔ kaa yo ɔ ngɛ klɔuklɔu.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Kple si nɛ o ya ngɔ Aaron kɛ ba. Se osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ ma a lɛɛ ko ha nɛ a gba piɛ ɔ nɛ a kuɔ kɛ ba ye ngɔ, nɛ ma ko ba gbla a tue.”

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose kple si nɛ e ya bɔ ma a nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: God said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Mawu tu munyu, nɛ e de ke,

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Se ma a daa si ngɛ se lokoo, nɛ Mose pɛ nɛ e hɛ lɛ kɛ su diblii kpii ɔ he ngɛ he nɛ Mawu ngɛ ɔ. Bɔ sami la tɛhi a he mlaahi

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
translation_verse: “Imi ji Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ nɛ je mo kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ kɛ je nyɔguɛ yemi mi ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Do not worship any god except me.
translation_verse: “Ko ja mawu ko kɛ piɛ ye he.

english_verse: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
translation_verse: “Koo puɛ amaga, loo nɔ́ ko nɛ ngɛ kaa nɔ́ ko nɛ ngɛ hiɔwe, loo nɔ́ ko nɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ, loo nɔ́ ko nɛ ngɛ nyu mi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english_verse: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
translation_verse: Se nihi akpe abɔ nɛ suɔ mi, nɛ a yeɔ ye mlaa amɛ a nɔ ɔ, mɛɛ i naa mɛ mɔbɔ.

english_verse: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
translation_verse: “Ko tsɛ Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ biɛ yaka gu; ejakaa nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ peeɔ ja a, Yawɛ kɛ e he be lɛ kee.

english_verse: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
translation_verse: “Mo kai Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ, nɛ o ye lɛ ngɛ mumi mi he tsɔmi mi.

english_verse: You have six days when you can do your work,
translation_verse: Ngɔɔ ligbi ekpa kɛ tsu nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ tsumi.

english_verse: but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns.
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ ji Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ Hejɔɔmi ligbi. Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, ko tsu nɔ́ ko kulaa; mo nitsɛ jio, o binyumu jio, o biyo jio, o tsɔlɔ nyumu jio, o mawayo jio, o lohwe jio, nubwɔ nɛ ngɛ o ma a mi jio;

english_verse: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
translation_verse: ejakaa ligbi ekpa Yawɛ ngɔ kɛ pee hiɔwe, zugba, kɛ wo kɛ a mi nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́, nɛ ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, e jɔɔ e he. Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ e gbaa Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ, nɛ e pee lɛ klɔuklɔu ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
translation_verse: “Moo bu o tsɛ kɛ o nyɛ, konɛ o se nɛ kɛ ngɛ zugba nɛ Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ ngɔ ha mo ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Do not murder.
translation_verse: “Koo gbe nɔmlɔ.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: “Ko puɛ gba.

english_verse: Do not tell lies about others.
translation_verse: “Koo ye lakpa odase kɛ si o nyɛmi.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: “O hɛ ko kɔ o nyɛmi we nɔ; o hɛ ko kɔ o nyɛmi e yo, aloo e tsɔlɔ nyumu, aloo e mawayo, aloo e na, aloo e teji, aloo e nɔ́ kpa ko nɔ.” Ma a ye gbeye (Mose V,

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko ngɔ sika hiɔ, loo sika tsu kɛ pee mawuhi ha nyɛ he nɛ nyɛ ja kɛ piɛ ye he.

english_verse: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
translation_verse: Benɛ ma a tsuo nu hiɔwe simi ɔ, kɛ titimati pɛmi ɔ, nɛ a na oslabai la a, kɛ la su ku nɛ je ngɛ yo ɔ mi ɔ, a ye gbeye, nɛ a je ya da si ngɛ se banee.

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: Nɛ a de Mose ke, “Mo nitsɛ o kɛ wɔ nɛ tu munyu nɛ waa nu; ko ha nɛ Mawu kɛ wɔ nɛ tu munyu nɛ wa ba gbo.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Mose de ma a ke, “Nyɛ ko ye gbeye; kami kɛkɛ Mawu ma nyɛ kami konɛ nyɛɛ ye lɛ gbeye nɛ nyɛ ko pee yayami.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Yawɛ fa Mose ke e ya de Israel bi ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ na kaa hiɔwe nɛ i kɛ nyɛ tu munyu kɛ je ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ngɔ zu kɛ puɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ha mi, nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ jijɔ, kɛ na kɛ pee sami bɔ, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔ ngɛ nɔ. He tsuaa he nɛ i fa nyɛ ke nyɛ ja mi ngɛ ɔ, ma ba lejɛ ɔ nɛ ma ba gbaa nyɛ.

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ maa puɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ha mi kɛ tɛ ɔ, nyɛ ko ngɔ tɛ nɛ a gba kɛ pee; ejakaa ke nyɛ ngɔ ní tsumi dade kɛ ta tɛ ɔ he pɛ nyɛ ble tɛ ɔ.

english_verse: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko pee kpoku kɛ kuɔ kɛ ya ye bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he, konɛ a ko na nyɛ he nɛ fɔɔ si.”

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa fia e tsɛ, aloo e nyɛ nɔ́ ɔ, a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
translation_verse: “Ke ni enyɔ pɛ, nɛ nɔ kake fia e nyɛmi tɛ, loo kɔ, nɛ nɔ ɔ tlɔ sa mi, se e gbo we ɔ,

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ, mlaahi nɛ o maa wo Israel bi ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.

english_verse: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
translation_verse: Ke mo nɔ ko o he Hebri no nyɔguɛ ɔ, e ma sɔmɔ mo jeha ekpa. Jeha nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, e ye e he nɛ o ko he nɔ́ ko ngɛ e dɛ.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Ke lɛ nɔ kake nɛ ba a, lɛ nɔ kake ɔ nɔuu nɛ kpale kɛ ho. Se ke e kɛ e yo ba a, lɛɛ e kɛ e yo ɔ nɛ ho.

english_verse: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
translation_verse: Ke e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ha lɛ yo, nɛ e fɔ binyumuhi, loo biyihi ha lɛ ɔ, yo ɔ kɛ e bimɛ ɔmɛ maa pee e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ níhi; nɛ lɛ nɔ kake too e maa ho.

english_verse: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
translation_verse: lɛɛ e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ maa ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba Mawu hɛ mi. E kɛ lɛ ma ba da sinya a nya, loo sinya tso ɔ he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e maa ngɔ tue gbumi nɔ́ kɛ gbu e tue ha lɛ. Kɛkɛ e ma tsa nɔ ma sɔmɔ kɛ yaa si lɛ, nyɔguɛ ɔ ma gbo.

english_verse: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
translation_verse: “Ke nyumu ko jua e biyo kaa nyɔguɛ, nɛ he yemi be ɔ su ɔ, a ko ngmɛɛ e he kaa bɔ nɛ a peeɔ nyumu nyɔguɛhi.

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Ke e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nɛ to kaa e maa ngɔ lɛ ɔ sume lɛ ɔ, lɛɛ e ha nɛ yo ɔ tsɛ nɛ fɔ lɛ ɔ ba kpɔ lɛ. E be he blɔ nɛ e juaa yo ɔ kɛ haa ma se no, ejakaa e sisi lɛ.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Ke nyɔguɛtsɛ ɔ ngɔ lɛ ngɔ ha e binyumu ɔ, lɛɛ e hɛɛ lɛ kaa lɛ nitsɛ e biyo.

english_verse: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
translation_verse: Ke e binyumu nɛ ɔ ya ngɔ yo kpa kɛ piɛ nɔ kaketsɛ ɔ he ɔ, e ha kekle yo ɔ e tsu nya yo blɔ nya nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ pɛpɛɛpɛ; eko nɛ ko je nɔ. E he bo, e nya mi ngma, kɛ e yogbayo blɔ nya nɛ ko bɔ lɛ.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ke e pee we ní etɛ nɛ ɔmɛ ha lɛ ɔ, lɛɛ yo ɔ ngɛ he blɔ nɛ e jee faa nɛ hiɔ wowoe ko be mi. Mlaahi nɛ kɔɔ awi yemi he

english_verse: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
translation_verse: Ke e nine ya kpa ngɛ nɔ ɔ nɔ tlukaa, se pi kaa e je blɔ pee ɔ, lɛɛ ma tsɔɔ mo he nɛ e tu fo kɛ ya.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Se ke nɔ ko mi mi fu nɛ e dɔ ya tua e nyɛmi nɛ e gbe lɛ ɔ, lɛɛ ke e tu fo ya sa we ngɛ ye bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he po, a nu lɛ nɛ a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
translation_verse: “Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ju nɔmlɔ nɛ e maa jua, loo a maa na lɛ ngɛ e dɛ ɔ, a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa gbiɛ e tsɛ, loo e nyɛ ɔ, a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
translation_verse: nɔ nɛ fia tɛ ɔ maa ye e he. Ke nɔ ɔ na he wami nɛ e je kpo, nɛ e hɛɛ tso kɛ ngɛ nyɛɛe ɔ, nɔ nɛ fia lɛ tɛ ɔ nɛ wo nɔ ɔ be nɛ e puɛ ha lɛ ɔ kɛkɛ he hiɔ, nɛ e hyɛ nɛ e tsa lɛ kɛ pi si.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko ngɔ tso kɛ fia e nyɔguɛ nyumu, loo yo, nɛ e gbo ngɛ e dɛ mi ɔ, a gbla e tue.

english_verse: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
translation_verse: Se ke e gbo we amlɔ, nɛ ligbi kake, loo ligbi enyɔ be loko e gbo ɔ, a ko gbla nyɔmtsɛ ɔ tue; ejakaa nyɔguɛ ɔ gbenɔ ɔ ngɛ kaa nyɔguɛtsɛ ɔ sika nɛ laa.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: “Ke nyumuhi ngɛ kunɔ nɔe nɛ a ya fia yohɔyo ko nɔ́ nɛ e muklii ɔ sane, se nɔ́ yobu kpa ko nyɛɛ we se ɔ, a bɔ nɔ nɛ plaa lɛ ɔ hiɔ. Yo ɔ huno ɔ nɛ tsɔɔ hiɔ ɔ, konɛ kojoli ɔmɛ nɛ a buá he.

english_verse: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
translation_verse: Se ke yo ɔ plaa a, tue gblami ɔ ji a plaa nɔ nɛ plaa lɛ ɔ kɛ to nane mi. Ke e gbo,

english_verse: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
translation_verse: loo e hɛngmɛ pɛ, loo e lungu hia, loo e nine, loo e nane plaa,

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: “Ke nyumu ko fia e nyɔguɛ nyumu, loo nyɔguɛ yo hɛngmɛ nɔ́ nɛ hɛngmɛ ɔ pɛ ɔ, hɛngmɛ ɔ he je ɔ, e ngmɛɛ nyɔguɛ ɔ he nɛ e ho.

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: “Ke na si nɔ ko koli, nyumu jio, yo jio, nɛ nɔ ɔ gbo ɔ, a fia na a tɛ nɛ e gbo, se a ko ye lo ɔ; natsɛ ɔ nitsɛ lɛɛ e yi fɔ.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Se ke na a pɔɔ nihi koli simi, nɛ a tu munyu tsɔɔ natsɛ ɔ, se kɛ̃ e hyɛ we nɛ a wo na a tsu mi, nɛ e ba mi kaa e ya si nɔ ko koli nɛ e gbe nɔ ɔ, nyumu jio, yo jio, a fia na a tɛ nɛ e gbo, nɛ natsɛ ɔ hu a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Ke na a ya gbe nɔ ko binyumu, loo biyo ɔ, a kɛ lɛ nɛ ye ngɛ kikɛmɛ a mlaa nɛ ɔ nɔuu nya.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko si muɔ ngɔ fɔ si nɛ e hɛ́ nya, aloo e ya tsua muɔ nɛ e bu we nya, nɛ na, loo teji ya nɔ mi ɔ,

english_verse: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
translation_verse: nɔ nɛ tsua muɔ ɔ nɛ wo lohwetsɛ ɔ hiɔ, konɛ e ngɔ lohwe gbogboe ɔ.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: Ke nɔ ko na ku ya gbe e nyɛmi na a, natsɛmɛ enyɔ ɔmɛ nɛ a jua na hɛngmengmletsɛ ɔ, nɛ a gba sika a fiee; lohwe gbogboe ɔ hu a dla lɛ fiee.

english_verse: But if you cannot afford to replace the animals, you must be sold as a slave to pay for what you have stolen. If you steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and are caught with it still alive, you must pay the owner double. If you happen to kill a burglar who breaks into your home after dark, you are not guilty. But if you kill someone who breaks in during the day, you are guilty of murder.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko ya ju na nɛ e gbe, loo e jua a, a ma he lɛ na enuɔ kɛ to na kake ɔ nya; ke to ɔ, lɛɛ a ma he lɛ to eywiɛ kɛ to to kake ɔ nya. Ke a na lohwe ɔ nɛ e ju ɔ ngɛ e dɛ hɛ ngmengmle ɔ, na jio, teji jio, to jio, lohwe kake he ɔ, e wo lohwe enyɔ nya hiɔ. Ke nɔ́ ko be e dɛ ɔ, a jua lɛ kaa nyɔguɛ nɛ a kɛ wo nɔ́ nɛ e ju ɔ he hiɔ. “Nyɔ mi ke a nu julɔ nɛ ngɛ we ko mi sɛe, nɛ a fia lɛ nɔ́ nɛ a gbe ɔ, nɔ nɛ gbe lɛ ɔ yi fɔ kaa e gbe nɔmlɔ. Se ke piani nɛ e ba mi ja a, lɛɛ nɔ nɛ gbe julɔ ɔ yeɔ fɔ kaa e gbe nɔmlɔ.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko ngmɛɛ e lohwe he nɛ e ya ye ní ngɛ nɔ kpa e ngmɔ nɔ, aloo e wai abɔɔ mi ɔ, lohwetsɛ ɔ maa ngɔ e ngmɔ, loo abɔɔ mi ní nɛ hi pe kulaa kɛ to nane mi.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko ha e nyɛmi sika, loo ní titli komɛ si tomi nɛ a ba ju ɔ, ke a nu julɔ ɔ, hiɔ nɛ ba a, a ku kɛ bɔ he si enyɔ nɛ e wo.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: “Ke na, loo teji, loo to, loo heha ní, loo nɔ́ kpa ko laa, nɛ nihi enyɔ ngɛ he plee ɔ, a ngɔ mɛ kɛ ba Mawu hɛ mi. A ti nɔ nɛ Mawu maa bu fɔ ɔ maa wo nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ he plee ɔ he hiɔ ngwɔhe enyɔ kɛ ha nɔtsɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko ngɔ e teji, loo na, loo to, loo lohwe kpa ko ngɔ ha e nyɛmi si tomi, nɛ lohwe ɔ gbo, aloo a plaa lɛ, aloo nihi ba po lohwe ɔ kɛ je nɛ nɔ ko nɛ ɔ,

english_verse: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
translation_verse: nɔ nɛ a ha lɛ nɔ́ si tomi ɔ nɛ ya ka Yawɛ kita ha e nyɛmi ɔ kaa e nine tɛ lohwe ɔ he. Ke e pee ja a, kɛkɛ lɛɛ e sa nɛ lohwetsɛ ɔ nɛ kplɛɛ nɔ kaa e nyɛmi ɔ be nane mi ko nɛ e toɔ.

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Se ke jumi a ju ngɛ e dɛ ɔ, lɛɛ é to nɔtsɛ ɔ nane mi.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ hu, ke nga mi lohwehi nɛ tsɔtslɔɔ e mi ɔ, e ngɔ nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ɔ kɛ ba ye odase. Ke e ba ja a, kɛkɛ lɛɛ nane mi tomi ko be nɛ e maa to ha nɔtsɛ ɔ hu.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko ya ba lohwe ngɛ e nyɛmi dɛ nɛ lohwe ɔ plaa, aloo e gbo, be mi nɛ nɔtsɛ ɔ be lejɛ ɔ, é to nɔtsɛ ɔ nane mi sisiisi.

english_verse: But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it. Laws for Everyday Life The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ke nɔtsɛ ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ jamɛ a be ɔ, lɛɛ e ko to lɛ nane mi. Ke apaa yemi lohwe ɔ, apaa hiɔwo ɔ woɔ lohwe ɔ he hiɔ. Ní komɛ nɛ a hiɔ ɔ a he mlaahi

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko mlɔɔ yomiyo ko nɛ e kɛ lɛ hwɔ ɔ, e ya pee e he ní nɛ e ngɔ lɛ.

english_verse: But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
translation_verse: Se ke yomiyo ɔ tsɛ kua ke e kɛ lɛ be nyumu ɔ hae ɔ, lɛɛ bitsɛ ɔ nɛ he yo he ní peemi nya sika ngɛ nyumu ɔ nɛ puɛ e biyo ɔ dɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
translation_verse: “Yo tsuaa yo nɛ tsuɔ kunya a, a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ nɛ e kɛ lohwe ma na yo kɛ nyumu bɔmi ɔ, a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
translation_verse: “Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa sã bɔ kɛ ha mawu kpa ko, se pi imi Yawɛ ɔ, a kpata e hɛ mi.

english_verse: Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
translation_verse: “Koo pee nubwɔ yayami, nɛ koo wa lɛ yi mi; ejakaa nyɛ hu nyɛ ya to nubwɔ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: Do not mistreat widows or orphans.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko wa yalɔyo, aloo awusa yi mi.

english_verse: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ wa mɛ yi mi, nɛ a fo ya kɛ tsɛ mi ɔ, niinɛ, ma bu a ya fomi ɔ tue,

english_verse: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
translation_verse: nɛ ye mi mi ma fu wawɛɛ, nɛ ma gbe nyɛ ngɛ ta mi. Nyɛ yi ɔmɛ maa pee yalɔyihi, nɛ nyɛ bimɛ ɔmɛ maa pee awusahi.

english_verse: Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need.
translation_verse: “Ke o pa sika ha ye ma mi bi ɔmɛ a ti ohiatsɛ ko nɛ kɛ mo ngɛ ɔ, mo ko he lɛ hekpa kaa sika palɔ peeɔ.

english_verse: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
translation_verse: Ke nɔ ko ngɔ e bo kɛ ba to mo awaba a, kpale ya ha lɛ loko pu nɛ nɔ si,

english_verse: because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
translation_verse: ejakaa lɔ ɔ pɛ ji e heha nɔ́ nɛ e kɛ maa tsi fĩɛ; mɛni hu ngɛ e dɛ nɛ e maa ha kɛ hwɔ si? Ke nyɛ pee we ja, nɛ e fo ya kɛ tsɛ mi ɔ, ma bu lɛ tue; ejakaa mɔbɔ nalɔ ji mi.

english_verse: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
translation_verse: “Ko jɛ Mawu; nɛ koo gbiɛ o matsɛ.

english_verse: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
translation_verse: “Ngɔɔ ngma, wai, kɛ oliv nu nɛ je o ngmɔ ɔmɛ a mi ɔ kɛ ba sã bɔ ha mi ngɛ be nɛ sa mi. “Ngɔɔ o bitɛte ɔmɛ kɛ ba ha mi.

english_verse: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
translation_verse: Ngɔɔ o na amɛ, kɛ o to ɔmɛ a kekleekle bi ku ɔmɛ hu ba ha mi. Ke a fɔ mɛ se ɔ, ha nɛ a hi a nyɛmɛ a kasa nya ligbi kpaago; ligbi nɛ ji kpaanyɔ ɔ, ngɔɔ mɛ kɛ ba sã bɔ ha mi.

english_verse: You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
translation_verse: “Ye ni klɔuklɔuhi ji nyɛ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, lohwe ko nɛ nga mi lohwehi tsɔtslɔɔ mi ɔ, nyɛ ko ye; nyɛ sake ngɔ fɔ he ha gbehi.

english_verse: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
translation_verse: Koo nyɛɛ nihi fuu a se kɛ pee nɔ́ yaya; nɛ koo piɛ a he kɛ ye lakpa odase kɛ plɛ dami sane hɛ mi kɛ bu si.

english_verse: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
translation_verse: Ko dla ohiatsɛ sane he ha lɛ ngɛ kojomi he.

english_verse: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
translation_verse: “Ke o na o he nyɛlɔ e na, loo e teji nɛ laa blɔ ɔ, mo kpaka lohwe ɔ kɛ ya ha lɛ.

english_verse: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
translation_verse: Ke o na o futsɛ teji nɛ tlɔ zugba kɛ e se mi tlomi nɛ jiɔ pe lɛ ɔ, koo be e he nɛ o je; mohu wa o futsɛ ɔ, konɛ lohwe ɔ nɛ te nɛ e da e nane nɔ ekohu.

english_verse: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
translation_verse: “Ko plɛ ohiatsɛ sane hɛ mi ngɔ bu si ngɛ kojomi he.

english_verse: Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
translation_verse: Koo po sane ngɔ fɔ nɔ nɔ, nɛ nɔ nɛ pee we nɔ́ yaya ko ɔ, koo gbe lɛ; ejakaa nɔ nɛ peeɔ yayami kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ, i kɛ e he be lɛ kee.

english_verse: Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like. Laws for the Sabbath The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Koo wa nubwɔ yi mi; nyɛ le bɔ nɛ nubwɔ si himi ngɛ ha, ejakaa nyɛ ya hi si kaa nibwɔhi ngɛ Egipt. Jeha kpaagone ɔ kɛ ligbi kpaagone ɔ

english_verse: Plant and harvest your crops for six years,
translation_verse: “Du ní ngɛ o ngmɔ ɔ mi nɛ o kpa jeha ekpa.

english_verse: but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
translation_verse: Se jeha nɛ ji kpaago ɔ lɛɛ ngmɛɛ ngmɔ ɔ he nɛ e fɔ si gu nɛ e jɔɔ e he, nɛ o ko ya kpa e nɔ ní, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ o ma a mi ohiatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a ye e nɔ ní, konɛ nɔ́ nɛ maa piɛ ɔ, pu mi lohwehi hu nɛ a ye. O wai ngmɔ ɔmɛ kɛ oliv abɔɔ ɔmɛ hu, mo tsu a mi ní jã kɛ̃.

english_verse: Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
translation_verse: “Ligbi ekpa o kɛ tsu ní ngɛ otsi mi, se ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ lɛɛ mo ko tsu nɔ́ ko, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ o na amɛ, o teji ɔmɛ, o nyɔguɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ o nibwɔ ɔmɛ nɛ tsuɔ ní ha mo ɔ nɛ a jɔɔ a he.

english_verse: Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names. Three Annual Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: “Nyɛɛ bu níhi tsuo nɛ imi Yawɛ, i de nyɛ ɔ tue saminya nɛ nyɛɛ ye nɔ. Nyɛ ko fa kue ha mawu kpa komɛ, nɛ a ko nu a biɛhi tete po ngɛ nyɛ nya. Nyami ligbi ngua etɛ (Mose II,

english_verse: Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
translation_verse: “Koo ngɔ masa nɔ́ ko kɛ piɛ bɔ sami muɔ ko he kɛ ba ye hɛ mi; lohwe zɔ nɛ a kɛ sã bɔ ha mi nyami be ɔ, ko ha je nɛ na yi.

english_verse: Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
translation_verse: Yo ko mi be sanee, nɛ yo ko hu be yosa pee ngɛ zugba a nɔ. Ma ha o wami se maa kɛ.

english_verse: Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
translation_verse: Daa jeha a, o ma a mi nyumu ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ a ba bua si etɛ ngɛ imi Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ, ye hɛ mi.

english_verse: Celebrate three festivals each year in my honor.
translation_verse: “Moo ye nyami be slɔɔto etɛ ha mi ngɛ jeha mi.

english_verse: Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
translation_verse: Kekleekle nɔ́ ji Abolokplolo nyami be. Kaa bɔ nɛ i fa mo ɔ, o maa ye nyami be nɛ ɔ daa jeha ngɛ kekleekle nyɔhiɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Abib ɔ mi; ejakaa jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɛ o je Egipt ɔ nɛ. O maa ye abolo kplolo ligbi kpaago, nɛ nɔ ko kó ba ye hɛ mi kɛ e dɛ gu.

english_verse: Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. A Promise and a Warning The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Daa jeha a, ngɔɔ o zugba a nɔ kekleekle yiblii kɛ ba imi Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ, ye we ɔ. “Koo hoo apletsi bi ngɛ e nyɛ nyɔ nyu mi. Siwohi kɛ slɔmihi

english_verse: I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you.
translation_verse: “Hyɛ, i ngɛ bɔfo ko tsɔe kɛ nyɛɛ o hɛ mi, nɛ e bu o he ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ hluu kɛ yaa si he nɛ i dla ngɔ to mo ɔ.

english_verse: Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion.
translation_verse: Moo bu lɛ, nɛ o nu e gbi, nɛ o ko tsɔ e hɛ mi atuã; ejakaa imi nɛ i tsɔ lɛ, nɛ e kɛ nyɛ tɔmi ɔmɛ be nyɛ pae.

english_verse: My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
translation_verse: Ye bɔfo ɔ maa nyɛɛ o hɛ mi kɛ yaa su Amor bi, Hit bi, Periz bi, Kanaan bi, Hiv bi, kɛ Yebus bi ɔmɛ tsuo a zugba a nɔ; nɛ ma kpata a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong.
translation_verse: O ma ja imi Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ, nɛ ma gbaa mo kɛ nya mi ngma, kɛ nyu, nɛ o be hiɔ nue.

english_verse: But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere.
translation_verse: I be mɛ fiee kɛ je zugba a nɔ ngɛ jeha kake mi, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ zugba a nɛ ko fɔ si gu, nɛ nga mi lohwehi ko ba hiɛ tsɔ ha mo.

english_verse: Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
translation_verse: I ma hi mɛ fie bɔɔ bɔɔ bɔɔ kɛ je o blɔ nɔ kɛ yaa si be nɛ nyɛ he maa hiɛ, nɛ nyɛ nine maa su zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land.
translation_verse: Ma bli o huzu ɔmɛ a mi kɛ je Wo Tsu ɔ nya kɛ ya su Mediterenia wo ɔ nya; jehanɛ hu, kɛ je nga a nɔ kɛ ya pi Yufrate pa a. Ma ngɔ zugba a nɔ bi ɔmɛ kɛ wo o dɛ mi, nɛ o maa fie mɛ kɛ je o blɔ nɔ.

english_verse: But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods.
translation_verse: O kɛ mɛ, loo a mawu ɔmɛ ko so somi ko.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke, “O kɛ Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, kɛ Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ a kpɛti ni nyingmi kpaago nɛ kuɔ kɛ ba ye ngɔ. Be nɛ nyɛ ngɛ tsitsaa lokoo kɛ ma a, nyɛ kpla si nɛ nyɛ ja mi.

english_verse: Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said. The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel.
