english_verse: If all of you disobey one of my laws without knowing it, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice, a wine offering, and a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Ke e ba mi kaa ma mluku nɛ ɔ li a he be nɛ a ya tɔ ɔ, lɛɛ ma a tsuo maa ngɔ na niheyo kake kɛ ba sã sami bɔ nɛ jee via ha Yawɛ. A ngɔ niye ní bɔ, kɛ dã nɛ a kɛ maa sã bɔ ɔ ngɔ piɛ he kaa bɔ nɛ kusumi ɔ ngɛ ɔ. Jehanɛ, a kɛ akpakpo kake hu ba sã yayami pami bɔ.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong without knowing it, you must sacrifice a year-old female goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ kake ko li be nɛ e ya tɔ ɔ, e ngɔ apletsi yo kake nɛ ye jeha kake kɛ ba sã yayami pami bɔ.

english_verse: The priest will then ask me to forgive you, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Osɔfo ɔ maa pee kusumi kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha lɛ; nɛ a kɛ e he yayami ɔ maa pa lɛ.

english_verse: The law will be the same for anyone who does wrong without meaning to, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
translation_verse: Mlaa kake ɔ nɔuu ngɛ kɛ ha nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ li e he be nɛ e ya pee yayami ko, Israel fɔmi bi jio, nɔ kpa ko nɛ ba to nyɛ nubwɔ jio.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong on purpose, whether Israelite or foreigner, you have sinned against me by disobeying my laws. You will no longer belong to my people. A Man Put to Death for Gathering Firewood on the Sabbath
translation_verse: Akɛnɛ e bui Yawɛ munyu ɔ tue, nɛ e ya tɔ e mlaa a nɔ he je ɔ, a je lɛ we pɛsɛpɛsɛ; e musu nɛ tloo lɛ.” Nyumu ɔ nɛ ble Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ

english_verse: Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ, e ba mi kaa a ya na nyumu ko nɛ ngɛ lɛ́ lɛe Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: But no one knew what to do with him, so he was not allowed to leave.
translation_verse: A tsi e nya ngɛ tsu mi, ejakaa a na we nɛ a tsɔɔ nɔ́ pɔtɛɛ nɛ sa kaa a pee lɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the people to take that man outside the camp and stone him to death!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “A gbe nyumu ɔ; ma a tsuo nɛ ya fia lɛ tɛ ngɛ ma sito he ɔ se!”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel, “Sew tassels onto the bottom edge of your clothes and tie a blue string to each tassel.
translation_verse: “De Israel bi ɔmɛ ke a kpɛ deke ngɔ wo a tade ɔmɛ a nya ngɛ yi nɔhi tsuo; nɛ a ngɔ kpa bluu kɛ fi deke ɔmɛ kɛ wo tade ɔmɛ a nya.

english_verse: These will remind you that you must obey my laws and teachings. And when you do, you will be dedicated to me and won't follow your own sinful desires.
translation_verse: Deke ɔmɛ ma ha nyɛ ma kai ye mlaa amɛ tsuo, nɛ nyɛ maa ye a nɔ, konɛ nyɛɛ pee nyɛ he klɔuklɔu kɛ ha nyɛ Mawu ɔ.

english_verse: and Aaron and said, “Why do you think you're so much better than everyone else? We're part of the Lord's holy people, and he's with all of us. What makes you think you're the only ones in charge?”
translation_verse: A kpe kɛ wo Mose kɛ Aaron a he, nɛ a de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ ngɛ nɔ́ ko pee tsɔ. Ma kpekpemi nɛ ɔ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ nimli klɔuklɔuhi ji mɛ; nɛ Yawɛ ngɛ a kpɛti. Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ nyɛ he nɔ woe ngɛ Yawɛ ma kpekpemi ɔ nɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: When Moses heard this, he knelt down to pray.
translation_verse: Benɛ Mose nu nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, e kɛ e hɛ mi bu si,

english_verse: Then he said to Korah and his followers: Tomorrow morning the Lord will show us the person he has chosen to be his priest, and that man will faithfully serve him.
translation_verse: nɛ e de Kora kɛ e se nyɛɛli ɔmɛ ke, “Hwɔɔ mɔtu ɔ, Yawɛ nitsɛ maa tsɔɔ wɔ nɔmlɔ nɛ ji e nɔ, kɛ nɔ nɛ ji nɔ klɔuklɔu. Nɔmlɔ nɛ ji e nɔ nɛ e maa hla a, Yawɛ ma ha nɛ e hɛ lɛ kɛ ba e ngɔ.

english_verse: Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
translation_verse: Hwɔɔ mɔtu ɔ, nyɛɛ je la kɛ wo ngɛyu ɔmɛ a mi. Nyɛɛ ngɔ tsopa kɛ e he via kɛ pue la a nɔ, nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ kɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi. Nɔmlɔ nɛ Yawɛ nitsɛ maa hla a, lɛ ji nɔ klɔuklɔu ɔ nɛ. Nyɛ Levi bi, nyɛ ngɛ nyɛ he nɔ woe tsɔ!”

english_verse: You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want?
translation_verse: anɛ e pi ha nyɛ kaa Israel Mawu ɔ hla nyɛ kɛ je Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ mi konɛ nyɛɛ ba e ngɔ, nɛ nyɛ ba tsu ní ngɛ Yawɛ kpe he ɔ, nɛ nyɛɛ da ma kpekpemi ɔ nya kaa a sɔmɔli lo?

english_verse: The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest.
translation_verse: Mawu ha mo, kɛ o nyɛmimɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ tsuo kikɛmɛ a blɔ nya nɛ ɔ. Nɛ jehanɛ lɛɛ nyɛ pa ngɛ osɔfo yemi ɔ hu hlae lo.

english_verse: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come!
translation_verse: Mose tsɔ ke a ya tsɛ Datan, kɛ Abiram, Eliab bimɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ba. Se a de ke, “Wa be bae!

english_verse: It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around!
translation_verse: O kpaka wɔ kɛ je zugba nɛ hi, nɛ baa ní nɔ, nɛ́ o ba gbe wɔ ngɛ nga nɛ ɔ nɔ. Anɛ enɛ ɔ pi ha mo, nɛ o pa ngɛ hlae nɛ o ye ganɔ ngɛ wa nɔ?

english_verse: Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
translation_verse: Mose mi mi fu wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ e de Yawɛ ke, “Ko he bɔ ɔmɛ nɛ a ba sã a! I he we teji kake po ngɛ a dɛ, nɛ i yi a ti nɔ ko nɔ ko sane yayami ko hulɔ.”

english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose de Kora ke, “Hwɔɔ ɔ, o kɛ o se nyɛɛli ɔmɛ tsuo kulaa nyɛɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi; Aaron hu maa ba lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
translation_verse: O se nyɛɛli lafa enyɔ kɛ nyingmi enuɔ ɔmɛ ɔ, a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ngɔ lɛ nitsɛ e ngɛyu, nɛ e kɛ tsopa kɛ e he via wo mi, nɛ e kɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi.”

english_verse: The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ ho ya ngɔ ngɛyu, nɛ e je la kɛ wo mi, nɛ e ngɔ tsopa kɛ e he via kɛ pue nɔ, nɛ e ba da si ngɛ kpe he bo tsu sinya a nya ngɛ Mose kɛ Aaron a kasa nya.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Kora ya kpee ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo kɛ ba kpe he bo tsu sinya a nya, nɛ a plɛ a hɛ mi ngɔ kpee Mose kɛ Aaron. Tlukaa a, Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ ba je e he kpo kɛ tsɔɔ ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose kɛ Aaron ke,

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: “Nyɛɛ hɛ nyɛ kɛ je ma nɛ ɔ he kɛ ya se, nɛ ma kpata a hɛ mi hɛngmɛfia.”

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Se Mose kɛ Aaron ngɔ a hɛ mi ngɔ bu si, nɛ a de ke, “Mawu lee, mo nɛ o ji adesahi tsuo a mumi. Anɛ ke nɔ kake pee yayami ɔ, o mi mi ma fu ma a tsuo lo?”

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: “De ma a ke a hɛ mɛ kɛ je Kora, kɛ Datan, kɛ Abiram a bo tsu ɔmɛ a he.”

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose te si, nɛ e kɛ Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ pue nɔ kɛ ho Datan, kɛ Abiram a ngɔ ya.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: E de ma a ke, “Nyɛɛ hɛ nyɛ kɛ je nimli yiwutsotsɛmɛ nɛ ɔmɛ a bo tsu ɔmɛ a he. Ke pi ja a, a ma kpata nyɛɛ kɛ mɛ tsuo nyɛ hɛ mi ngɛ a he yayami ɔmɛ a he.”

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Mose de ke, “Nɔ́ nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ maa le kaa Yawɛ nitsɛ lɛ tsɔ mi ke ma ba tsu ní nɛ ɔmɛ, se pi imi nitsɛ ye yi mi tomi nya ji

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Se ke Yawɛ pee nɔ́ ko nɛ bɛ hyɛ, nɛ zugba bli e nya mi nɛ e mii mɛ kɛ ho yɔkɔ mi ya hɛ ngmengmle, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ ɔ, lɛɛ nyɛ maa le kaa nimli nɛ ɔmɛ kua Yawɛ niinɛ.”

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Mose nya nɛ e ke e nɔɔ si kikɛ nɛ ɔ kɛkɛ nɛ zugba a mi gba enyɔ ngɛ a sisi,

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a ho gbeje ya hɛ ngmengmle, kɛ a nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́. Zugba a sa a yi, nɛ a hɛ mi kpata.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Israel bi tsuo nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ tu fo benɛ a nu ni ɔmɛ a ngmlaa kpami ɔ. A de ke, “Nyɛ ha waa tu fo, ke pi ja a wɔ hu zugba a maa mii wɔ!”

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: “Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred,
translation_verse: “De osɔfo Aaron bi Eleazar nɛ e ya je ngɛyu ɔmɛ kɛ je la a mi, nɛ e gbɛ la a kɛ ya se lokoo; ejakaa ngɛyu ɔmɛ a he tsɔ.

english_verse: because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
translation_verse: Benɛ a ngɔ ngɛyu ɔmɛ kɛ ya Yawɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ a pee ní klɔuklɔuhi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nimli nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a gbe mɛ ngɛ a he yayami he ɔ, mo de Eleazar nɛ e ya je a ngɛyu ɔmɛ nɛ a fiaa nɔ tɛtlɛɛ, nɛ a kɛ ha bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ maa pee kɔkɔ bɔmi nɔ́ kɛ ha Israel ma a.”

english_verse: Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ osɔfo Eleazar ya kukuɔ akɔblee ngɛyu ɔmɛ, nɛ e ha a fia a nɔ tɛtlɛɛ, nɛ a kɛ pee bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he hami nɔ́,

english_verse: The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, Israel ma a tsuo hɔɔ nya si kɛ wo Mose kɛ Aaron, nɛ a de ke, “Nyɛ lɛ nyɛ gbe Yawɛ ni ɔmɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent.
translation_verse: Se benɛ ma a tsuo nya bua ngɔ wo Mose kɛ Aaron he ɔ, a plɛ kɛ kpee kpe he bo tsu ɔ, nɛ a na kaa bɔku ɔ ba ma lejɛ ɔ, nɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ je e he kpo.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose kɛ Aaron ho ya da si ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ hɛ mi,

english_verse: where the Lord said to them,
translation_verse: nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: “Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.” They immediately bowed down and prayed.
translation_verse: “Nyɛɛ hɛ nyɛ kɛ je ma nɛ ɔ he kɛ ya se nɛ ma kpata a hɛ mi ngɛ hɛngmɛfia mi!” Se Mose kɛ Aaron kpla si nɛ a ngɔ a hɛ mi kɛ bu si,

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
translation_verse: nɛ Mose de Aaron ke, “Ngɔɔ ngɛyu ɔ, nɛ o je la ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ kɛ wo mi. Ngɔɔ tsopa kɛ e he via kɛ pue nɔ, nɛ o hɛɛ kɛ ya ma a ngɔ esɔesɔ, nɛ o ya kpata Yawɛ ha mɛ. Yawɛ mi mi fu, nɛ gbenɔ hiɔ ɔ je sisi.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Muɔ tso ɔmɛ ya pue somi daka a hɛ mi ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ mi he nɛ i kɛ mo kpee ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Nɔ nɛ ma hla a, e tso ɔ ma tsɛ̃ mɔmɔ; nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ma ha nɛ munyu huitihuiti nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ tuɔ kɛ siɔ nyɛ ngɛ ye he ɔ se maa po.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Mose kɛ Israel ma a ya tu, nɛ wɛtsoyi ɔmɛ tsuo ngɔ dɛma tso kakaaka kɛ ba; lɛ tsuo peeɔ nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ, nɛ Aaron tso ɔ hu piɛ he.

english_verse: Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose muɔ tso ɔmɛ tsuo ya pue Yawɛ somi daka a hɛ mi ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ mi.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Mose muɔ tso ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi kɛ je kpo ya tsɔɔ Israel ma a tsuo. Benɛ a na nɔ́ nɛ ba a, wɛtsoyi ɔmɛ tsuo ho ya ngɔ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a tso ɔmɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Kpale Aaron dɛma tso ɔ ya fɔ daka a nɛ somi womi ɔ ngɛ mi ɔ hɛ mi ekohu, nɛ e hi lejɛ ɔ kaa kɔkɔ bɔmi nɔ́ kɛ ha atuã tsɔli ɔmɛ bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a munyu huitihuiti ɔmɛ nɛ a tuɔ kɛ siɔ mi ɔ se nɛ po. Ke pi ja a, a ma gbo.”

english_verse: Moses did what he was told.
translation_verse: Mose pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa lɛ ke e pee ɔ.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: A ma sɔmɔ mo, nɛ a ma tsu bo tsu ɔ he ní tsumihi tsuo. Se mohu, á hyɛ nɛ a ko ta bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ, loo ní ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ a he, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a kɛ nyɛ tsuo nyɛ ko gbo.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: A maa piɛ nyɛ he kɛ tsu ní tsumi tsuaa ní tsumi ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ mi; nɔ kpa ko nɛ ko ba nyɛ kasa nya.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Imi nitsɛ lɛ i hla nyɛ nyɛmimɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti, nɛ i ngɔ mɛ kɛ ha nyɛ kaa nike ní. A hla mɛ ngɔ to ha mi, konɛ a nyɛ nɛ a tsu ní ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ mi.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Se o kɛ o bimɛ ɔmɛ pɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ he blɔ kaa nyɛ tsuɔ osɔfo ní tsumihi nɛ kɔɔ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ, kɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a a he. Enɛ ɔmɛ ji nyɛ ní tsumi; ejakaa imi lɛ i kɛ osɔfo yemi ní tsumi ɔ ke nyɛ. Nɔ kpa ko nɛ maa hɛ lɛ kɛ su ní klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ a he ɔ, a gbe lɛ.” Osɔfo ɔmɛ a blɔ fa mi nɔ

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: A lo ɔ maa pee o nɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ bɔ nɛ a fɔɔ kɛ yaa kɛ baa a gugue ɔ, kɛ e hiɔ fiɔ ɔ peeɔ o nɔ ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Ní klɔuklɔu pe kulaa nɛ a sɛ̃ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ, a kpɛti enɛ ɔmɛ maa pee o níhi: niye ní bɔ, yayami pami bɔ, kɛ fɔ yemi bɔ. Nike ní klɔuklɔu tsuaa nike ní klɔuklɔu nɛ a kɛ ba ha mi ɔ maa pee o kɛ o bimɛ nyɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ye ngɛ he ko nɛ ngɛ klɔuklɔu; nyumuhi pɛ lɛ a ye. E ji niye ní klɔuklɔu ha nyɛ.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ, nike ní klɛdɛɛ kpa komɛ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ baa a, lɔ ɔmɛ hu maa pee o nɔ. I ngɔ mɛ kɛ ha mo, kɛ o binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ o biyi ɔmɛ, kaa nyɛ blɔ fa mi nɔ́ kɛ yaa neneene. O we mi bimɛ tsuo nɛ a he tsɔ ɔ, a ye eko.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ, nu, wai he, kɛ blɛfo kpokploku, nɛ ji kekleekle yiblii nɛ a kɛ ba haa imi Yawɛ ɔ, lɔ ɔmɛ hu i ngɔ kɛ ha mo.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Jã kɛ̃, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ puɛɔ ngɛ a zugba a nɔ ɔ, a kekleekle yiblii nɛ a kɛ ba haa mi ɔ maa pee o nɔ. O we mi bimɛ tsuo nɛ a he tsɔ ɔ, a ye eko.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: “Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ngɛ Israel nɛ a hla ngɔ to ha mi ɔ maa pee o nɔ.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: “Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ bliɔ muklii nya, nɛ a kɛ ba ha Yawɛ ɔ maa pee o nɔ, nɔmlɔ jio, we mi lohwe jio. Se nɔmlɔ adesa e kekleekle bi, kɛ lohwe nɛ he tsɔ we e kekleekle bi lɛɛ o ha nɛ a kpɔ mɛ.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Níhi nɛ a ma kpɔ ɔ, ke a ye nyɔhiɔ kake pɛ a kpɔ mɛ. Jua nɛ a po fɔ si kɛ ha a kpɔmi ji sika hiɔ yi enuɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ jua nɛ a po ɔ ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Na, loo jijɔ, loo apletsi kekleekle bi lɛɛ a ko kpɔ; ejakaa mɛɛ a he tsɔ. Ngɔɔ a muɔ ɔ kɛ fĩa bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ o sã a zɔ ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ jeɔ via ha Yawɛ.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: “Nike ní klɔuklɔu nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ ba haa Yawɛ ɔ, i ngɔ mɛ tsuo kɛ ha mo, kɛ o binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ o biyi ɔmɛ kaa nyɛ blɔ fa mi nɔ nɛ fɔɔ si daa. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ji somi ko nɛ i kɛ mo, kɛ o nina so, nɛ a be mi poe gblegbleegble.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Yawɛ de Aaron ke, “O be weto ní ko nae ngɛ Israel zugba a nɔ, nɛ blɔ fa mi nɔ ko hu o be nae. Imi ji o blɔ fa mi nɔ, kɛ o weto ní ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti.” Levi bi ɔmɛ a blɔ fa mi nɔ

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de ke, “Levi bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ i ngɔ Israel níhi tsuo a mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka kɛ ngɛ mɛ hae kaa a weto ní, ngɛ ní nɛ a tsuɔ ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ mi ɔ he.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Levi bi ɔmɛ pɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ ma tsu ní ngɛ kpe he ɔ; ke sane ko ba a, mɛ lɛ a ma bi. Enɛ ɔ ji mlaa nɛ fɔɔ si daa kɛ ha nyɛ bimɛ; se weto ní ko lɛɛ a be nae ngɛ Israel,

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Yawɛ fa Mose ke

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: e de Levi bi ɔmɛ ke, “Ke nyɛ nine su Israel bi ɔmɛ a níhi a mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka a nɛ Yawɛ kɛ ha nyɛ kaa nyɛ weto ní ɔ nɔ ɔ, nyɛ hu nyɛɛ ngɔ mi dlami nyɔngma mi kake nɛ ɔ hu mi dlami nyɔngma mi kake kɛ ba ha mi kaa nike ní klɛdɛɛ.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Yawɛ maa ngɔ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ kaa ngma nɛ je nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ ngma mi sami he, loo wai he nɛ je nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ wai muɔ mi.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛɛ kɛ nɔ́ nɛ hi pe kulaa a ba ha Yawɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ ngɔ nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ɔ kɛ to, kaa bɔ nɛ ke ngmɔ hulɔ ya sã bɔ nɛ e ngɔɔ nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ɔ kɛ toɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ we mi bimɛ nɛ ye nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ɔ ngɛ he tsuaa he; ejakaa ní tsumi nɛ nyɛ tsuɔ ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ mi ɔ, e he hiɔwo ji lɔ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ ngɔ nɔ́ nɛ hi pe lɛ tsuo ɔ kɛ ba ha Yawɛ ɔ, tue gblami ko be nyɛ nɔ bae. Se nyɛɛ hyɛ nɛ nyɛ ko ble Israel bi ɔmɛ a nike ní klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ, nɛ a ko gbe nyɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: “Mlaa nɛ Yawɛ wo ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: nyɛ de Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ a ngɔ na yo tsu nɛ nye, loo kpa ko be e he, nɛ a kɛ kuɛpã hu wui lɛ hyɛ kɛ ba

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: osɔfo Eleazar ngɔ. A kpaka na a kɛ ya sito he ɔ se, nɛ a ya gbe lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ngɛ osɔfo ɔ hɛ mi.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Osɔfo Eleazar nɛ ngɔ e nine nguɛ kɛ sɔ muɔ ɔ mi, nɛ e fĩa muɔ ɔ eko kɛ ya kpe he bo tsu ɔ hɛ mi si kpaago.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: A sã na yo ɔ, e he womi ɔ, e lo ɔ, e muɔ ɔ, kɛ e mi ní ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ osɔfo Eleazar hɛ mi.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ hla seda tso, kɛ nga nɛ a fi kaa bɛ, kɛ kpa tsu, nɛ e sake mɛ ngɔ pue la a nɛ a ngɛ na yo ɔ sãe ngɛ nɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Osɔfo ɔ nɛ fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e du e he loko e kpale kɛ ba sito he ɔ; se kɛ̃ ɔ, e he tsɔ we kɛ yaa si gbɔkuɛ.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Nɔ nɛ sã na yo ɔ, lɛ hu e fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e du e he ja nɔuu; lɛ hu e he tsɔ we kɛ yaa si gbɔkuɛ.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Nyagbe ɔ, nɔ ko nɛ he tsɔ nɛ ya muɔ na yo ɔ la zu ɔ kɛ ya pue he ko nɛ tsɔ ngɛ sito he ɔ se. A ngɔ la zu nɛ ɔ ngɔ to lejɛ ɔ, konɛ a kɛ futu nyu mi, nɛ a ngɔ nyu nɛ ɔ kɛ du Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ a he, nɛ a kɛ je a he yayami ɔmɛ.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nɔ nɛ muɔ na yo ɔ la zu ɔ, lɛ hu e fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he; se kɛ̃ ɔ, e he tsɔ we kɛ yaa si gbɔkuɛ. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ maa pee mlaa nɛ fɔɔ si daa kɛ ha Israel bi, kɛ nibwɔhi nɛ ba to mɛ ɔ. Nɔ gbogboe he kɔhi

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: “Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta nɔ gbogboe he ɔ, e ble e he; nɛ e he tsɔ we kɛ yaa si ligbi kpaago.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Loko e he ma tsɔ ɔ, e ngɔ nyu nɛ a kɛ fɔɔ nɔ he yayami ɔ kɛ julaa e he ngɛ ligbi etɛne ɔ, kɛ ligbi kpaagone ɔ a nɔ. Ke e kɛ nyu ɔ fɔ we e he ngɛ ligbi nɛ ji etɛ ɔ kɛ ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ a nɔ ɔ, e he be tsɔe.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta nɔ gbogboe he, nɛ e kɛ nyu nɛ a kɛ fɔɔ nɔ he yayami nɛ ɔ be e he julaae ɔ, e he tsɔ we; mu ngɛ e he. Ke e ba mi ja a, nɔ ɔ ble Yawɛ kpe he ɔ. A ma je lɛ we, nɛ a be lɛ bue ngɔ si Mawu ma mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ hu.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko gbo ngɛ bo tsu mi ɔ, mlaa nɛ ngɛ he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ bo tsu ɔ mi jamɛ a be ɔ mi, aloo nihi tsuo nɛ ma ba sɛ mi ɔ, a he tsɔ we kɛ yaa si ligbi kpaago.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Kekleekle ɔ, nɔ ko nɛ he tsɔ nɛ ngɔ nga nɛ a fi kaa bɛ kɛ sɔ nyu ɔ mi, nɛ e kɛ fĩa bo tsu ɔ, kɛ e mi ní ɔmɛ tsuo, kɛ nimli tsuo nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ a nɔ. Jehanɛ, nɔ nɛ ya ta nɔ gbogboe wu, loo yɔkɔ, loo nɔ ko nɛ a gbe lɛ, loo nɔ ko nɛ gbo lɛ nitsɛ e gbenɔ he ɔ, nɔ nɛ he tsɔ ɔ nɛ ngɔ nyu ɔ kɛ fĩa e nɔ.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ nɛ ble e he, se e julaa we e he ɔ, mu ngɛ e he, nɛ e he tsɔ we; ejakaa a kɛ nyu nɛ a kɛ fɔɔ nɔ he yayami ɔ pue we e nɔ. Ke e ba mi ja a, nɔ ɔ ble Yawɛ kpe he ɔ. A ma je lɛ we, nɛ a be lɛ bue ngɔ si Mawu ma mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ hu.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Mlaa nɛ fɔɔ si daa kɛ ha mɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Nɔ nɛ fĩaa nyu nɛ a kɛ fɔɔ nɔ he yayami ɔ ngɔ pueɔ nihi a nɔ ɔ, lɛ hu e fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he; nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ nyu nɛ ɔ eko ma pue e nɔ ɔ, lɛ hu e he tsɔ we kɛ yaa si gbɔkuɛ.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ nɔ ko nɛ he tsɔ we maa ta he ɔ, e ble nɔ́ ɔ; ke nɔ ko ta jamɛ a nɔ́ ɔ he ɔ, lɛ hu e he tsɔ we kɛ yaa si gbɔkuɛ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo ba Zin nga a nɔ kekleekle nyɔhiɔ ɔ, nɛ a ba to si ngɛ Kadesh. Benɛ a ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, Miriam ba gbo, nɛ a pu lɛ. Nyu hwɔ

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: nɛ a kɛ Mose pɛ, nɛ a de ke, “Wa ná nɛ wa piɛ wa nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a he kɛ gbo ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi.

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Mɛni he je nɛ o ngɔ wɔ, Yawɛ ma kpekpemi ɔ, kɛ wa lohwehi tsuo kɛ ba nga nɛ ɔ nɔ nɛ wa ba gbo ngɛ hiɛ ɔ?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Mɛni he je nɛ o kpaka wɔ kɛ je Egipt kɛ ba zugba yaya nɛ bɛ ní nɛ ɔ nɔ? Blɛfo be ɔ, ngmɔkɔ be; wai be ɔ, akutu hu be. Nyu nunui kpamakpa hu be hiɛ ɔ!”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose kɛ Aaron hɛ mɛ kɛ je gua a he kɛ ya da kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya, nɛ a ngɔ a hɛ mi ngɔ bu si; nɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ je e he kpo kɛ tsɔɔ mɛ.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Yaa ngɔ tso ɔ nɛ ngɛ somi daka a hɛ mi ɔ, nɛ o kɛ o nyɛmi Aaron ya bua ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo nya. Mo fa tɛ sa a ngɛ mɛ tsuo a hɛ mi, kɛkɛ nyu maa je mi kɛ ha ma kpekpemi ɔ, kɛ lohwe ɔmɛ nɛ a nu.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose ya ngɔ tso ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Mose kɛ Aaron ho nɛ a ya bua ma mluku ɔ nya ngɛ tɛ sa a hɛ mi; nɛ Mose de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ atuã tsɔli, nyɛɛ bu mi tue! Anɛ e he hia kaa wa je nyu ngɛ tɛ sa nɛ ɔ mi kɛ ha nyɛ lo?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Kikɛ nɛ ɔ nɛ Mose de pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ e wo e nine nɔ, nɛ e kɛ e tso ɔ fia tɛ sa a si enyɔ, nɛ nyu babauu je mi babaaba ha ma kpekpemi ɔ, kɛ a lohwe ɔmɛ nɛ a nu.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ de Mose kɛ Aaron ke, “Akɛnɛ hemi kɛ yemi nɛ nyɛ ngɛ kɛ ha mi ɔ pi, bɔ nɛ nyɛ ma nyɛ maa ye ye he wami klɔuklɔu ɔ he odase kɛ tsɔɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ he je ɔ, nyɛ be ma kpekpemi nɛ ɔ hɛ mi nyɛɛe kɛ ya su zugba nɛ i ngɔ ha mɛ ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Sane nɛ ɔ ba ngɛ Meriba. Lejɛ ɔ ji he nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ Yawɛ pɛ ngɛ; nɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ e je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ mɛ ngɛ kaa Mawu klɔuklɔu. Israel kɛ Edom

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Mose tsɔ nihi kɛ je Kadesh ke a ngɔ sɛ gbi ya ha Edom matsɛ, nɛ a de lɛ ke, “Bɔ nɛ o nyɛmimɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: mo nitsɛ o le amanehluhi nɛ wa na;

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: bɔ nɛ wa kpa ngmlaa kɛ tsɛ Yawɛ, nɛ e nu wa gbi, nɛ e tsɔ bɔfo kɛ ba kpaka wɔ kɛ je Egipt. Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, wa ba su Kadesh, nɛ ji ma nɛ kɛ o zugba a wo huzu ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Wa kpa mo pɛɛ, ha nɛ waa gu o zugba a nɔ kɛ be. Wa be ngmɔ, loo wai abɔɔ ko mi gue; wa be vu ko vu ko mi nyu nue. Matsɛ gbɛjegbɛ ɔ nɔ kɛkɛ wa maa nyɛɛ tɛɛ kɛ yaa si wa maa po mi ngɛ o zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Se Edom bi ɔmɛ he nɔ ke, “Dɛbi, nyɛ be wa zugba a nɔ gue! Ke nyɛ li peemi nɛ nyɛ ba wa zugba a nɔ ɔ, wa maa hia ta kɛ ba tua nyɛ.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ de ke, “Gbɛjegbɛ ɔ nɔ kɛkɛ wa maa nyɛɛ; nɛ ke e ba mi kaa wɔ, loo wa lohwe ɔmɛ nu nyɛ nyu ɔ eko ɔ, wa maa wo he hiɔ. Moo lɛɛ moo ngmɛ wɔ blɔ nɛ waa gu o zugba a nɔ kɛ be kɛkɛ; enɛ ɔ pɛ wa ngɛ bie.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Se Edom bi ɔmɛ he nɔ ke “Dɛbi! Nyɛ be wa zugba a nɔ gue.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Edom ta buli babauu je kpo kɛ ba, konɛ a ba tua Israel bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, akɛnɛ Edom bi ɔmɛ ngmɛ́ blɔ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ gu a zugba a nɔ ɔ, mɛ hu a kpale a se ya gu he kpa. Aaron gbenɔ

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo hia kɛ je Kadesh kɛ ba Hor yo ɔ he,

english_verse: on the Edomite border, the Lord said,
translation_verse: ngɛ Edom huzu ɔ nya. Lejɛ ɔ Yawɛ de Mose kɛ Aaron ke,

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Aaron ma gbo, nɛ e nane enyɔ be zugba a nɛ i ngɔ ha Israel ma a nɔ mae; ejakaa nyɛ ni enyɔ ɔmɛ nyɛ tsɔ atuã wo mi ngɛ Meriba nyu ɔ he.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Ngɔɔ Aaron kɛ e bi Eleazar kɛ ba Hor yo ɔ nɔ,

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: nɛ o je Aaron tade ɔmɛ ngɛ e he kɛ wo e bi Eleazar. Aaron ma gbo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Mose pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa lɛ ɔ. A kuɔ Hor yo ɔ ngɛ ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo a hɛ mi,

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: nɛ Mose je Aaron he tade ɔmɛ kɛ wo e bi Eleazar. Nɛ Aaron gbo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ngɛ yo ɔ yi mi, nɛ Mose kɛ Eleazar kple si kɛ ba.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo ná le kaa Aaron gbo ɔ, a nyɛ ya ha lɛ ligbi nyingmi etɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ si Hor yo ɔ, a ya gu Wo Tsu ɔ nya blɔ, konɛ a kɛ tsɔ Edom zugba a he. Se a tsui si tomi ya ta ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ,

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: nɛ a tu munyu kɛ si Mawu kɛ Mose ke, “Mɛni he je nɛ nyɛ kpaka wɔ kɛ je Egipt nɛ wa ba gbo ngɛ nga nɛ ɔ nɔ, he nɛ niye ní, loo nyu ko be ɔ? Kikɛmɛ a niye ní gbogboe nɛ ɔ lɛɛ wa sume oo, wa sume!”

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ ma a ba Mose ngɔ, nɛ a ba de ke, “Wa pee yayami kaa wa tu munyu kɛ si Yawɛ, kɛ mo hulɔ. Mo kpa Yawɛ pɛɛ nɛ e ba je sinɔ ɔmɛ kɛ je wa kpɛti.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose kpa pɛɛ ha ma a,

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Moo pee akɔblee sinɔ nɛ o ngɔ kɛ kpla tso he. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ sinɔ maa kɔ lɛ, nɛ e maa hyɛ akɔblee sinɔ nɛ ɔ, e yi ma na wami.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Mose pee akɔblee sinɔ, nɛ e kɛ kpla tso he; nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ sinɔ kɔ lɛ, nɛ e hyɛ akɔblee sinɔ ɔ, e yi na wami niinɛ. A ba Moab kɔ̃ ɔ mi

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ tsa a blɔ hiami ɔ nɔ, nɛ a ya to si ngɛ Obot.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Nɛ́ a je lejɛ ɔ, a ya to si ngɛ Arnon pa a omleyi je ngɛ nga a nɔ kɛ yaa Amor bi ɔmɛ a huzu ɔ nya. .

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a deɔ ngɛ Yawɛ Tahi Womi ɔ mi ke, “Wa ya be ngɛ Waheb ngɛ Sufa, kɛ Arnon nyu dɔ ɔmɛ a he,

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: kɛ nyu dɔ ɔmɛ a si kplemi he ɔ nɛ maa e yi si kɛ yaa he nɛ Ar fɔɔ si ngɛ ɔ, ngɛ Moab huza amɛ a nɔ.”

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Nɛ́ a je lejɛ ɔ, a pue nɔ kɛ ho Beer ya. Beer ji vu nɛ Yawɛ de Mose ngɛ he ke, “Bua ma a nya nɛ a ha mɛ nyu nɛ a nu” ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ la la nɛ ɔ: “Vu, ha o nyu ɔ nɛ ba, konɛ wa la kɛ kpee lɛ.

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Vu nɛ ganɔhi tsua, nɛ ma nimeli ngɔ matsɛ tso, kɛ dɛma tso kɛ je mi.” Benɛ a hia kɛ je nga a nɔ ɔ, a pue nɔ kɛ ho Matana ya.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Nɛ́ a je Bamot ɔ, a ya gu kɔ̃ ɔ mi ngɛ Moab bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ, kɛ ho Pisga yo ɔ nɛ hyɛɛ nga kplanaa a nɔ ɔ yi mi ya. A ye Matsɛ Sihon kɛ Matsɛ Og a nɔ (Mose V,

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Heshbon ji Amor matsɛ, Sihon matsɛ ma. Sihon nɛ ɔ ji nɔ nɛ e kɛ kekle Moab matsɛ ɔ hwu ta nɛ e ngɔ e zugba a tsuo ngɛ e dɛ kɛ ba si Arnon pa a nya a nɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Israel ma a tsɔ nihi ke a ya de Amor matsɛ, Sihon ke,

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Wa kpa mo pɛɛ, ha nɛ waa gu o zugba a nɔ kɛ be. Wa be ngmɔ, loo wai abɔɔ ko mi gue; wa be vu ko vu ko mi nyu nue. Matsɛ gbɛjegbɛ ɔ nɔ kɛkɛ wa maa nyɛɛ tɛɛ kɛ yaa si wa maa po mi ngɛ o zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Se Sihon ha we nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ gu e zugba a nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e bua e ta a tsuo nya kɛ ho Yahaz ya, nɛ e kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ya hwu ta ngɛ nga a nɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Se Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ klaate tane a yi, nɛ a ngɔ a zugba a kɛ je Arnon pa a nya kɛ ya pue Yabok pa a nɛ ji Amon bi ɔmɛ a huzu ɔ nya, ejakaa Amon bi ɔmɛ a huzu ɔ, a fia gbogbo ngɛ nɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɔ Amor bi ɔmɛ a ma ngua amɛ tsuo, kaa Heshbon kikɛ nɛ ɔ; nɛ a hi Amor bi ɔmɛ a ma ngua amɛ, kɛ kɔpe ɔmɛ tsuo a mi.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ asilɛte ɔmɛ laa nɛ a deɔ ke, “Nyɛɛ ba Matsɛ Sihon ma Heshbon! Nyɛ ha nɛ a fia ma a, nɛ a dla lɛ ekohu.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Heshbon ma nɛ ɔ mi Sihon tabo ɔ je, nɛ a ya kpata Ar nɛ ngɛ Moab, kɛ Arnon yo ɔmɛ a nɔ nyɔmtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi kaa la nɛ ngɛ tsoe kpataa nɔ hɛ mi ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Moab bi, due ha nyɛ! Nyɛ Kemosh jali, nyɛ hɛ mi kpata! Nyɛ mawu ɔ ha nyɛ binyumu ɔmɛ pee ko bɔli; nɛ nyɛ biyi ɔmɛ hu pee Amor matsɛ, Sihon nyɔguɛhi.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Se piɔ lɛɛ a kpata a nina hɛ mi kɛ je Heshbon kɛ ya si Dibon tɔɔ, kɛ je Nashim kɛ ya si Nofa, ngɛ Medeba kasa nya.”

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Mose tsɔ nihi ya slaa Yazer ma a. Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɔ ma a, kɛ kɔpehi nɛ bɔle lɛ ɔ tsuo; nɛ a fie Amor bi ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ kpale a se ya gu Bashan blɔ ɔ nɔ. Bashan matsɛ, Og kɛ e tabo ɔ tsuo hia ta, nɛ a kɛ mɛ ba bua ngɛ Edrei, nɛ a hwu ta.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ de Mose ke, “Koo ye lɛ gbeye; ejakaa i ngɔ lɛ kɛ e ma a, kɛ e zugba a tsuo ngɔ wo o dɛ mi. Bɔ nɛ o pee Amor bi ɔmɛ a Matsɛ Sihon nɛ ye tsɛ ngɛ Heshbon ɔ, ja nɔuu o pee lɛ.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ gbe Og, kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ e ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo; nɔ kake ngmelu po píɛ. Nɛ a ngɔ zugba a.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ pue nɔ, nɛ a ya to si ngɛ Moab nga kpataa a nɔ ngɛ Yordan pa a se, ngɛ Yeriko hanɔ.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Moab bi ɔmɛ ya de Midian ma nimeli ɔmɛ ke, “E be kɛe nɛ ta nɛ ɔ ma kpata nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ bɔle wɔ ɔ hɛ mi kaa bɔ nɛ na ku kpeɔ nga ngɛ nga nɔ ɔ.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Matsɛ Balak

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: tsɔ nihi kɛ ho Petor ya, ngɛ Yufrate pa a kasa nya, ngɛ Amaw bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ, nɛ́ a ya kpee Beor binyumu Balaam kɛ ba. E sɛ gbi ji, “I ngɛ hae nɛ o le kaa ma ko je Egipt kɛ ba, nɛ a ha zugba a tsuo nɔ. Amlɔ nɛ ɔ po a su ye ngɔ ta.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ, ba nɛ o ba gbiɛ ma nɛ ɔ ha wɔ kaa, alini wa maa ye a nɔ, nɛ wa maa fie mɛ kɛ je zugba a nɔ lo; ejakaa a hiɛ pe wɔ. I le kaa ke o gbaa nɔ ko ɔ, kɛkɛ a gbaa lɛ; nɛ ke o gbiɛ nɔ ko ɔ, kɛkɛ a gbiɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Moab ma nimeli ɔmɛ, kɛ Midian ma nimeli ɔmɛ pue nɔ kɛ ho Balaam ngɔ ya. A hɛɛ sika nɛ a kɛ maa wo nɔ gbiɛmi ɔ he hiɔ ngɛ a dɛ, nɛ benɛ a ya su ɔ, a ngɔ Balak sɛ gbi ɔ ngɔ ha Balaam.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Balaam de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ hwɔ hiɛ ɔ nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi, konɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ ma de mi ɔ, ma ha nɛ nyɛɛ le.” Nɛ Moab ma nimeli ɔmɛ hwɔ Balaam ngɔ.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Mawu ba Balaam ngɔ, nɛ e ba bi lɛ ke, “Nyumu ɔmɛ nɛ ba to mo ɔ, mɛnɔmɛ ji mɛ?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Balaam ha heto ke, “Moab matsɛ, Balak, Zipor binyumu ɔ, lɛ nɛ e tsɔ mɛ ke a ba de mi ke

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: ma a nɛ je Egipt kɛ ba a, ha zugba a tsuo nɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e ngɛ hlae nɛ ma ba gbiɛ mɛ ha lɛ, konɛ e nyɛ nɛ e kɛ mɛ nɛ hwu ta, nɛ e fie mɛ kɛ je zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Mawu de Balaam ke, “O kɛ mɛ ko ya, nɛ koo gbiɛ Israel ma a hulɔ; ejakaa a gbaa mɛ.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Balaam te si mɔtu nɛ e ya de Balak nimeli ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ kpale kɛ ho nyɛ ma mi ya; ejakaa Yawɛ kplɛɛ we kaa i kɛ nyɛ nɛ ya.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Balak kpale tsɔ ma nimeli kpahi kɛ ho; ni nɛ ɔmɛ hiɛ pe kekle ni ɔmɛ, nɛ a hɛ mi hu ngɛ nyami pe mɛ.

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: Ma wo o hɛ mi nyami babauu, nɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o ma de mi ɔ, ma pee. I kpa mo pɛɛ, ba nɛ o ba gbiɛ kikɛmɛ a ma nɛ ɔ ha mi.”

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Se kɛ̃, nyɛ hu nyɛɛ hwɔ hiɛ ɔ nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi, konɛ ma hyɛ kaa Yawɛ ngɛ nɔ́ kpa ko nɛ e ma de mi lo.”

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Balaam te si mɔtu, nɛ e wo e teji yo ɔ nɔ ní; nɛ e kɛ Moab ma nimeli ɔmɛ pue nɔ kɛ ho. Balaam kɛ e teji yo ɔ

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Se Mawu mi mi fu kaa Balaam ho. Benɛ Balaam hi e teji yo ɔ nɔ nɛ e kɛ e tsɔli enyɔ ɔmɛ yaa a, Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ ya po lɛ ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Benɛ teji yo ɔ na bɔfo ɔ nɛ e hia klaate kɛ daa si ngɛ blɔ ɔ mi ɔ, e gba kɛ je blɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ ho nga a mi ya. Balaam fia teji yo ɔ nɔ́, konɛ e kɛ dɔ e yi kɛ ba blɔ ɔ nɔ ekohu.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ ya da si ngɛ nane blɔ ko mi ngɛ wai ngmɔ enyɔ komɛ a kpɛti; nɛ gbogbo ngɛ hiɛ kɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Benɛ teji yo ɔ na Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ, e ngɔ e he ya kpasa gbogbo ɔ, nɛ e mia Balaam nane kɛ wo gbogbo ɔ he. Balaam fia lɛ nɔ́ ekohu.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ ya e hɛ mi ekohu, nɛ e ya da si ngɛ he ko tokofii, he nɛ blɔ ko blɔ ko be nɛ a kɛ plɛɔ he kɛ yaa nɔ hiɔ nɔ, loo nɔ muɔ nɔ.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Benɛ teji yo ɔ na Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ ekohu ɔ, e kpla si ngɛ Balaam sisi. Balaam mi mi fu, nɛ e ngɔ e dɛma tso ɔ kɛ fia teji yo ɔ.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ bli teji yo ɔ nya, nɛ e bi Balaam ke, “Mɛni i pee mo loko o fia mi nɔ́ si etɛ sɔuu kikɛ nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Balaam he nɔ nɛ e de teji yo ɔ ke, “Ejakaa o pee mi kuasia. I hɛɛ klaate jinɛ i gbe mo momo.”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ ɔ, Yawɛ bli Balaam hɛngmɛ, nɛ e na Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ nɛ hɛɛ klaate kɛ daa si ngɛ blɔ ɔ mi. Kɛkɛ nɛ Balaam ma e yi si, nɛ e kɛ e hɛ mi bu si.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ bi Balaam ke, “Mɛni he je nɛ o fia o teji yo ɔ nɔ́ si etɛ sɔuu kikɛ nɛ ɔ? O nɛ, pe i ba nɛ ma ba tsi mo blɔ; ejakaa blɔ nɛ o hia nɛ ɔ ngɔɛ ye nya.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Teji yo ɔ na mi nɛ e yu e he kɛ je ye hɛ mi si etɛ sɔuu. Niinɛ, kaa e pee we ja jinɛ i gbe mo, nɛ i he teji yo ɔ yi wami.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Balaam de Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ ke, “I pee yayami; i li kaa mo lɛ o ba po mi ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke blɔ nɛ i hia nɛ ɔ dɛ ha mo ɔ, lɛɛ ma kpale ye se mɔ.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ de Balaam ke, “O kɛ nyumu ɔmɛ nɛ ya kɛkɛ; se mohu, munyu nɛ ma ngɔ kɛ wo o nya ke o tu ɔ, lɔ ɔ pɛ o de.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Balaam kɛ Balak tsɔli ɔmɛ pue nɔ kɛ ho. Balak ba kpee Balaam

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Benɛ Balak nu kaa Balaam ma a, e ho nɛ e ya kpee lɛ ngɛ Ar tɔɔ. Ma nɛ ɔ ji ma ko nɛ ngɛ Arnon pa a nya, ngɛ Moab huzu ɔ nyagbe.

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Balak kɛ Balaam pue nɔ kɛ ho Kiriat Huzot ya.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Balak ngɔ nahi, kɛ tohi kɛ sã bɔ, nɛ e kɛ lo ɔ eko ha Balaam, kɛ ma nimeli nɛ piɛ e he ɔ. Balaam kekleekle gbami

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, Balak ngɔ Balaam kɛ ho Bamot Baal ya, nɛ Balaam na Israel ma a fa ko kɛ je lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Balaam de Balak ke, “Moo puɛ bɔ sami la tɛ kpaago ha mi ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, nɛ o ya hla na ku kpaago, kɛ agbosu kpaago kɛ ba.”

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak pee bɔ nɛ Balaam de lɛ ɔ, nɛ e kɛ Balaam sã na ku kake, kɛ agbosu kake ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ tsuaa bɔ sami la tɛ nɔ.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.

translation_verse: Hyɛ, gbaami a fa mi ke ma ba gbaa. Lɛɛ e gbaa momo; imi lɛɛ i be nyɛe ma kpale se.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Benɛ Balaam na kaa Yawɛ suɔ kaa e gbaa Israel ma a, e yɛ nɛ e ya bi Yawɛ ní kaa bɔ nɛ e pee sa a. Mohu, e plɛ e hɛ mi kɛ kpee nga a nɔ blɔ,

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.

translation_verse: E bua e he nya, nɛ e buu si kaa jata ku; Ee e buu si kaa jata yo. Mɛnɔ ma nyɛ maa tsɛɛ lɛ? Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ gbaa mo ɔ, a maa gbaa lɛ; Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ gbiɛɛ mo ɔ, a maa gbiɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Balak mi mi fu Balaam wawɛɛ, nɛ e gba e dɛ mi ma, nɛ e de Balaam ke, “I kpee mo kɛ ba nɛ o ba gbiɛ ye he nyɛli ha mi; se si etɛ sɔuu ji nɛ ɔ nɛ o ngɛ mɛ gbaae mohu.

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, moo je hiɛ ɔ nɛ o ho esɔesɔ! I wo mo si kaa ma wo o hɛ mi nyami, se Yawɛ tsi o hɛ mi nyami womi ɔ nya.”

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, piɔ lɛɛ i kpale kɛ yaa imi nitsɛ ye ma mi. Se loko ma je ɔ, ma suɔ nɛ ma wo o tue nɔ ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ kikɛmɛ a ma nɛ ɔ maa pee mo nitsɛ o ma mi bi ɔmɛ hwɔɔ se ɔ he.”

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ gba gbi nɛ ɔ ba e nya, nɛ e de ke, “Beor binyumu Balaam sɛ gbi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Nyumu ɔ nɛ hyɛɛ nɔ́ saminya a sɛ gbi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Lɛ nɛ e nuɔ Mawu gbi; Lɛ nɛ Mawu Ope ɔ jeɔ ninahi kɛ tsɔɔ; Lɛ nɛ ke e hɛli po e hɛngmɛhi fɔɔ si paa.

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.

english_verse: From Zedad, the border will continue east to Ziphron and end at Hazar-Enan.

english_verse: to say to them: When you receive your tribal lands, you must give towns and pastures to the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: “De Israel bi ɔmɛ ke, weto ní ɔ nɛ a nine su nɔ ɔ, a ha Levi bi ɔmɛ ma amɛ ekomɛ, kɛ a he lohwe lɛmi hehi nɛ mɛ hu a hi lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Six of the towns you give them will be Safe Towns where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection. But you will also give the Levites
translation_verse: Nyɛ ma ha Levi bi ɔmɛ ma ekpa nɛ a ngɔ to kaa wesa hehi nɛ nɔ ko ma nyɛ tu fo kɛ ya laa e he ngɛ, ke e li e he be nɛ e nine ya kpa ngɛ nɔ ko nɔ tlukaa a. Jehanɛ, nyɛ ma ha mɛ ma kpa nyingmi eywiɛ kɛ enyɔ.

english_verse: by one of the victim's relatives. He will take revengefor his relative's death as soon as he finds you.
translation_verse: Nɔ nɛ a gbe ɔ nyɛmi tutuutu ji muɔ he lue yelɔ ɔ nɛ. Be tsuaa be nɛ e maa na nɔ nɛ gbe e nyɛmi ɔ, e gbe lɛ.

english_verse: There are to be six of these Safe Towns,
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ hla ma ekpa kɛ pee wesa he nɛ ɔmɛ,

english_verse: The Lord then told Moses
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Mose ke,

english_verse: to tell the people of Israel: After you have crossed the Jordan River and are settled in Canaan,
translation_verse: “De Israel bi ɔmɛ ke, ke nyɛ po Yordan pa a kɛ ya Kanaan zugba a nɔ ɔ,

english_verse: If the victim's relatives think it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of these Safe Towns for protection and not be killed before a trial is held.
translation_verse: Ma nɛ ɔmɛ maa pee wesa hehi ha nyɛ kɛ maa je muɔ he lue yelɔ ɔ dɛ mi. Ke nɔ ko nine ya kpa ngɛ nɔ ko nɔ tlukaa a, a ko gbe lɛ kɛ yaa si a kɛ lɛ ma ba da ma kpekpemi ɔ hɛ mi, nɛ a maa kojo lɛ lolo.

english_verse: three on each side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: ma etɛ ngɛ Yordan se, kɛ etɛ hu ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: Suppose you hit someone with a piece of iron or a large stone or a dangerous wooden tool. If that person dies, then you are a murderer and must be put to death
translation_verse: “Se ke nɔ ko ngɔ awi yemi nɔ́ ko kaa dade, loo tɛ, loo tso kɛ fia nɔ, nɛ nɔ ɔ gbo ɔ, e gbe nɔmlɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, lɛ hu ja a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Or suppose you get angry and kill someone by pushing or hitting or by throwing something. You are a murderer and must be put to death by one of the victim's relatives.
translation_verse: aloo ke e ngɔ abofu kɛ gba lɛ ma, nɛ e nɔ si, nɛ e gbo ɔ, nɔmlɔ gbelɔ ji lɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, lɛ hu ja a gbe lɛ. Be tsuaa be nɛ muɔ he lue yelɔ ɔ, kɛ nɔmlɔ gbelɔ nɛ ɔ maa kpe ɔ, e gbe lɛ.

english_verse: But if you are not angry and accidentally kill someone in any of these ways, the townspeople must hold a trial and decide if you are guilty.
translation_verse: lɛɛ ma kpekpemi ɔ nɛ kojo nɔ nɛ fia nɔ nɔ́ ɔ, kɛ muɔ he lue yelɔ ɔ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ a nya.

english_verse: Death is the penalty for murder. But no one accused of murder can be put to death unless there are at least two witnesses to the crime.
translation_verse: “Ke nɔ ko gbe nɔ ko ɔ, a da odase yeli enyɔ, loo nɔ́ a nya mi munyu nɔ nɛ a kɛ kojo lɛ loko a gbe lɛ; a ko da odase yelɔ kake pɛ nya mi munyu nɔ kɛ gbe nɔ ko.

english_verse: You cannot give someone money to escape the death penalty; you must pay with your own life!
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, nyɛ ko he wami kpɔmi nɔ́ ko ngɛ nɔ ko nɛ je blɔ gbe nɔ ɔ dɛ; ja a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: And if you have been proven innocent of murder and are living in a Safe Town, you cannot pay to go back home; you must stay there until the high priest dies.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ se hu, ke nɔ ko tu fo kɛ ya sa we ngɛ ma ko mi ɔ, nyɛ ko he wami kpɔmi nɔ́ ko ngɛ e dɛ; konɛ e ko kpale kɛ ba hi lɛ nitsɛ e zugba nɔ, be mi nɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa a na we nɛ e gbo lolo ɔ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, live among you people of Israel, so your land must be kept pure. But when a murder takes place, blood pollutes the land, and it becomes unclean. If that happens, the murderer must be put to death, so the land will be clean again. Keep murder out of Israel!
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko ble zugba nɛ nyɛ ngɛ nɔ ɔ, he nɛ imi hu i hii ɔ; ejakaa imi ji Yawɛ, nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti lɛ i hii.”

english_verse: One day the family leaders from the Gilead clan of the Manasseh tribe went to Moses and the other family leaders of Israel
translation_verse: Nikɔtɔmahi nɛ ngɛ Makir binyumu Gilead, nɛ ji Yosef binyumu Manase bibi ɔ weku ɔ mi ɔ ba Mose, kɛ Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ a ngɔ;

english_verse: and said, “Sir, the Lord has said that he will show what land each tribe will receive as their own. And the Lord has commanded you to give the daughters of our relative Zelophehad the land that he would have received.
translation_verse: nɛ a ba de mɛ ke, “Yawɛ fa mo, wa nyɔmtsɛ ɔ, ke o fɔ sɔ kɛ dla zugba a ha Israel bi ɔmɛ. Jehanɛ se hu, Yawɛ fa mo ke o ngɔ wa nyɛminyumu Zelofehad gbosi ní ɔ ngɔ ha e biyi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Even when land is returned to its original owner in the Year of Celebration, we will not get back Zelophehad's land—it will belong to the tribe into which his daughters married.”
translation_verse: Ke Heyemi jeha a su, nɛ a kpale gbosi níhi tsuo ngɔ ha nɔtsɛmɛ ɔ, a maa ngɔ Zelofehad biyi ɔmɛ a gbosi ní ɔ ngɔ piɛ wɛtso nɛ a ya dumɔ ɔ a nɔ ɔ he. Kɛkɛ ɔ, wɔɔ lɛɛ wa nɛmɛ a weto ní ɔ nɔ ma gbɔ.”

english_verse: So Moses told the people that the Lord had said: These men from the Manasseh tribe are right.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose wo Israel bi ɔmɛ mlaa nɛ ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa lɛ ɔ ke, “Sane nɛ Yosef binyumu Manase wɛtso ɔ kɛ ba a, sane ɔ da.

english_verse: I will allow Zelophehad's daughters to marry anyone, as long as those men belong to one of the clans of the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yawɛ ke, Zelofehad biyi ɔmɛ ngɛ he blɔ nɛ a gbaa nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ a suɔ; se mohu a gba ngɛ a tsɛmɛ a wɛtso ɔ mi pɛ,

translation_verse: bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a gbosi ní nɛ ko je wɛtso kake mi kɛ ya wɛtso kpa mi; se mohu, Israel no tsuaa Israel no nɛ ye gbosi ní ngɛ e tsɛ wɛtso mi.

english_verse: In the future, any daughter who inherits land must marry someone from her own tribe. Israel's tribal land is never to be passed from one tribe to another.
translation_verse: nɛ gbosi ní kó je wɛtso kake mi kɛ ya wɛtso kpa mi, se mohu Israel wɛtso tsuaa wɛtso nɛ pɛtɛ lɛ nitsɛ e weto ní he.”

english_verse: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah the daughters of Zelophehad obeyed the Lord and married their uncles' sons
translation_verse: Zelofehad biyi ɔmɛ, Mahla, Tirza, Hogla, Milka, kɛ Noa pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa Mose ɔ, nɛ a gba a tsɛ nyɛminyumuhi a binyumuhi

english_verse: and remained part of the Manasseh tribe. So their land stayed in their father's clan.
translation_verse: ngɛ Yosef binyumu Manase weku ɔ mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a gbosi ní ɔmɛ tlɔ a tsɛ wɛtso ɔ mi.

translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, i wo nyɛ níhi tsuo nɛ sa kaa nyɛɛ pee ɔ a he mlaa. A tsɔ slaali kɛ je Kadesh Barnea (Mose IV,

english_verse: Right after the Lord commanded us to leave Mount Sinai, I told you: Israel, being your leader is too big a job for one person.
translation_verse: Mose de Israel ma a ke, “Jamɛ a be ɔ mi, benɛ wa ngɛ Sinai yo ɔ he ɔ, i de nyɛ ke, ‘Imi nɔ kake, i be nyɛ nɔ nyɛe ma hyɛ hu;

english_verse: God has even promised to bless us a thousand times more, and I pray that he will.
translation_verse: Yawɛ, nyɛ nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ ma ha nyɛ maa hiɛ pe bɔ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ nɛ ɔ si akpe abɔ; nɛ e maa gbaa nyɛ kaa bɔ nɛ e wo si ɔ.

english_verse: and others became judges. I gave these judges the following instructions: When you settle legal cases, your decisions must be fair. It doesn't matter if the case is between two Israelites, or between an Israelite and a foreigner living in your community.
translation_verse: “Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, i wo ma nya dali ɔmɛ mlaa ke, ‘Sanehi nɛ nyɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kɛ maa ba nyɛ hɛ mi ɔ, nyɛɛ hyɛ a mi. Nyɛɛ kojo ngɛ blɔ nɛ da nɔ, nyɛ nyɛmimɛ Israel bi sɔuu a kpɛti sane jio, a ti nɔ ko kɛ nibwɔhi nɛ ngɛ nyɛ ngɔ a kpɛti sane jio.

english_verse: And it doesn't matter if one is helpless and the other is powerful. Don't be afraid of anyone! No matter who shows up in your court, God will help you make a fair decision. If any case is too hard for you, bring the people to me, and I will make the decision.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko hyɛ nɔ hɛ mi ngɛ sane yemi mi; nyɛɛ bu nɔ tsuaa nɔ tue pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nyɛ ko ye nɔmlɔ adesa hɛ mi gbeye; ejakaa Mawu ji nɔ nɛ buáá sane he. Se ke sane ko pa nyɛ ɔ, lɛɛ nyɛ kɛ ba ye hɛ mi, konɛ imi nitsɛ ma hyɛ mi.’

english_verse: even though he had always been with us in the desert. During the daytime, the Lord was in the cloud, leading us in the right direction and showing us where to camp. And at night, he was there in the fire.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded us to leave Mount Sinai and go to the hill country that belonged to the Amorites, so we started out into the huge desert. You remember how frightening it was, but soon we were at Kadesh-Barnea,
translation_verse: “Kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ fa wɔ ɔ, wa hia kɛ je Sinai yo ɔ he, kɛ gu nga kplanaa nɛ nɔ ngɛ gbeye ɔ nɔ, kɛ ya be ngɛ Amor bi ɔmɛ a yo zugba amɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: and I told you, “We have reached the hill country. It belongs to the Amorites now, but the Lord our God is giving it to us. He is the same God our ancestors worshiped, and he has told us to go in and take this land, so don't hesitate and be afraid.”
translation_verse: Benɛ wa ba su Kadesh Barnea a, i de nyɛ ke, ‘Jehanɛ lɛɛ nyɛ su Amor bi ɔmɛ a yo zugba nɛ Yawɛ, wa nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ kɛ ngɛ wɔ hae ɔ nɔ. Nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya ngɔ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa wɔ ɔ. Nyɛ ko to tsle, nɛ nyɛ ko ye gbeye.’

english_verse: Then all of you came to me and said, “Before we go into the land, let's send some men to explore it. When they come back, they can tell us about the towns we will find and what roads we should take to get there.”
translation_verse: “Se nyɛ tsuo nyɛ ba ye ngɔ, nɛ nyɛ ba de mi ke, ‘Waa tsɔ nyumuhi kɛ sɛ hlami kɛ ya slaa zugba a, nɛ́ a ba tsɔɔ wɔ blɔ nɛ wa maa gu nɔ ɔ, nɛ́ a de wɔ mahi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ a he nɔ́ ko.’

english_verse: It seemed like a good idea, so I chose twelve men, one from each tribe.
translation_verse: “Ga nɛ nyɛ wo ɔ, i na kaa e hi, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i hla nyɛ kpɛti nihi nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ, nɔ kakaaka ngɛ nyɛ wɛtso ɔmɛ a nya.

english_verse: and even brought back some of the fruit. They said, “The Lord our God is giving us good land.” Israel Refused To Obey the Lord (Numbers
translation_verse: A ngɔ zugba a nɔ tso yiblii ɔ eko kɛ kple si kɛ ba bɔ wɔ amaniɛ ke, ‘Zugba nɛ Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ ngɛ wɔ hae nɛ ɔ, e ji zugba kpakpa.’

english_verse: Then you came back to the place of worship at Kadesh-Barnea and wept, but the Lord would not listen to your prayers. Israel Spent Years in the Desert Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Nyɛ kpale kɛ ba nɛ nyɛ ba wo yana ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi; se Yawɛ bui nyɛ tue, nɛ e he we nyɛ nɔ hulɔ. Jehahi nɛ a ye ngɛ nga kplanaa a nɔ

english_verse: You did not want to go into the land, and you refused to obey the Lord your God.
translation_verse: “Se nyɛ tsɔ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ hɛ mi atuã; nyɛ bui e fami ɔ fɛɛ; nyɛ kua yo ɔ kuɔmi;

english_verse: We are afraid, because the men who explored the land told us that the cities are large, with walls that reach to the sky. The people who live there are taller and stronger than we are, and some of them are Anakim. We have nowhere to go.”
translation_verse: Jije wa maa ya? Wa nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ha wa tsui po. A ke nihi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ je oblai; a he wa, nɛ a ka pe wɔ. A ke mahi nɛ a ngɛ mi ɔ, ma nguanguahi nɛ a fia gbogbohi nɛ ya hiɔwe ploplooplo ngɔ wo a he. Jehanɛ hu, mɛ nitsɛmɛ a na oblai nɛ ɔmɛ paa kɛ a hɛngmɛ!’

english_verse: The Lord our God will lead the way. He will fight on our side, just as he did when we saw him do all those things to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ nyɛɛ nyɛ hɛ mi ɔ, lɛ nitsɛ e maa hwu ha nyɛ kaa bɔ nɛ e pee ha nyɛ ngɛ Egipt,

english_verse: And you know that the Lord has taken care of us the whole time we've been in the desert, just as you might carry one of your children.”
translation_verse: kɛ nga kplanaa a nɔ nɛ nyɛ na kɛ nyɛ hɛngmɛ ɔ. Nyɛ na bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ hɛɛ nyɛ fiafiaafia hluu kɛ ba hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ tsɛ hɛɛɔ e bi ɔ.’

english_verse: You had made the Lord angry, and he said:
translation_verse: “Benɛ Yawɛ nu nyɛ munyu ɔmɛ ɔ, e mi mi wo la, nɛ e ka kita ke,

translation_verse: ‘Ke kikɛmɛ a yi nɔ yaya bi nɛ ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko na zugba kpakpa nɛ i ka he kita ke ma ngɔ ha nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ɔ fii!

english_verse: Caleb son of Jephunneh is the only one of your generation that I will allow to go in. He obeyed me completely, so I will give him and his descendants the land he explored.
translation_verse: Yefune bi Kaleb pɛ lɛ maa na zugba a. Lɛɛ e ye mi anɔkuale, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma ngɔ zugba nɛ e ya slaa a ngɔ ha lɛ kɛ e nina.’

english_verse: The Lord was even angry with me because of you people, and he said, “Moses, I won't let you go into the land either.
translation_verse: Nyɛ he ɔ, Yawɛ mi mi fu imi hulɔ, nɛ e de ke, ‘Mo Mose po, o be lejɛ ɔ sue.

english_verse: Then the Lord spoke to you again: People of Israel, you said that your innocent young children would be taken prisoner in the battle for the land. But someday I will let them go into the land, and with my help they will conquer it and live there.
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ Yawɛ de wɔ tsuo ke, ‘Nyɛ bimɛ tsɔwi ɔmɛ nɛ na we nɛ a le slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ kpakpa kɛ yayami a kpɛti lolo, nɛ́ nyɛ de ngɛ a he ke he nyɛli ma ba nuu mɛ ɔ, mɛ ma ngɔ zugba a kɛ ha nɛ a hi nɔ.

english_verse: Then you told me, “We disobeyed the Lord our God, but now we want to obey him. We will go into the hill country and fight, just as he told us to do.” So you picked up your weapons, thinking it would be easy to take over the hill country.
translation_verse: “Nyɛ he nɔ ke, ‘Wa tɔ̃ Yawɛ nɔ. Jehanɛ lɛɛ wa maa ya nɛ wa ya hwu ta a kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ fa wɔ ɔ.’ Kɛkɛ nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ wo e ta hwumi ní; nyɛ ngɔ lɛ kaa plasee nɔ́ ko kaa nyɛ ma ya tua yo nɔ ma a.

english_verse: But the Lord said, “Moses, warn them not to go into the hill country. I won't help them fight, and their enemies will defeat them.”
translation_verse: “Se Yawɛ de mi ke, ‘De mɛ ke a ko hia ta, nɛ a ko hwu ta; ejakaa i be a he piɛe. Ke a hia ta a, a he nyɛli ɔmɛ maa ye a nɔ.’

english_verse: I told you what the Lord had said, but you paid no attention. You disobeyed him and went into the hill country anyway. You thought you were so great!
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ i de nyɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; se nyɛ bui tue. Nyɛ tsɔ Yawɛ hɛ mi atuã; nyɛ si nyɛ gugue, nɛ nyɛ kuɔ kɛ ho yo ɔ nɔ ya.

english_verse: But when the Amorites in the hill country attacked from their towns, you ran from them as you would run from a swarm of bees. The Amorites chased your troops into Seir as far as Hormah, killing them as they went.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Amor bi ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Edom yo ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ je kpo kɛ ba kaa hwo bihi, nɛ a kɛ nyɛ ba kpe. A fie nyɛ hluu kɛ ya su Horma, nɛ a ye nyɛ nɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ngɛ Edom yo zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: until the Lord said: Moses,
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Yawɛ de mi ke,

english_verse: Israel has wandered in these hills long enough. Turn and go north.
translation_verse: ‘Bɔ nɛ nyɛ wo lalaalo ngɛ yo zugba a nɔ ɔ, e hiɛ; nyɛ plɛ kɛ ya omleyi je.

english_verse: And give the people these orders: “Be very careful, because you will soon go through the land that belongs to your relatives, the descendants of Esau. They are afraid of you,
translation_verse: De ma a tsuo ke nyɛ yaa be ngɛ nyɛ nyɛmimɛ Esau bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ kɛ ho. Mɛɛ lɛɛ Edom yo ɔ he a hii. A maa ye nyɛ gbeye.

english_verse: but don't start a war with them. I have given them the hill country of Seir, so I won't give any of it to you, not even enough to set a foot on.
translation_verse: Se nyɛɛ hyɛ saminya nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ mɛ ko hwu ta. I be nyɛ a zugba a ekoeko hae; nane mami he kake po be nyɛ nɔ́ pee; ejakaa i ngɔ Edom yo ɔ ngɔ ha Esau nina kaa a weto ní.

english_verse: And as you go through their land, you will have to buy food and water from them.”
translation_verse: Nyɛ ma he niye ní nɛ nyɛ maa wo he hiɔ kɛ nyu ngɛ a dɛ.’

english_verse: We went past the territory that belonged to our relatives, the descendants of Esau. We followed Arabah Road that starts in the south at Elath and Ezion-Geber, then we turned onto the desert road that leads to Moab.
translation_verse: “Kɛkɛ nɛ wa pue nɔ; wa si blɔ nɛ yaa Elat kɛ Eziongeber ma amɛ a mi ɔ, nɛ wa gu Ngo wo ɔ nya blɔ. Jehanɛ, wa plɛ kɛ gu omleyi je, kɛ beleku je a kpɛti blɔ kɛ yaa Moab nga a nɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told me, “Don't try to start a war with Moab. Leave them alone, because I gave the land of Ar to them, and I will not let you have any of it.” Tribes That Lived near Canaan
translation_verse: Yawɛ de mi ke, ‘Koo hao Moab bi ɔmɛ nɛ ji Lot nina a. I ngɔ Ar ma a ngɔ ha mɛ. I be mo a zugba a eko hae.’ ”

english_verse: Before the Lord gave the Moabites their land, a large and powerful tribe lived there. They were the Emim, and they were as tall as the Anakim.
translation_verse: Oblai komɛ nɛ a tsɛɛ mɛ Emim bi hu hi Ar sa a; nɛ e mi nihi hiɛ. Oblai nɛ ɔmɛ ka kaa Anak bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: The Moabites called them Emim, though others sometimes used the name Rephaim for both the Anakim and the Emim.
translation_verse: A tsɛɛ mɛ ke Refaim hulɔ; se Moab bi ɔmɛ tsɛɛ mɛ Emim bi.

english_verse: The Horites used to live in Seir, but the Edomites took over that region. They killed many of the Horites and forced the rest of them to leave, just as Israel did to the people in the land that the Lord gave them. Israel Crossed the Zered Gorge Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Hor bi ɔmɛ hu hi Edom sa a; se Esau nina a ba fie mɛ, nɛ a kpata a hɛ mi, nɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a hi lejɛ ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ hu ba fie a he nyɛli ɔmɛ kɛ je zugba nɛ ji weto ní nɛ Yawɛ ngɔ ha mɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ.

english_verse: When we came to the Zered Gorge along the southern border of Moab, the Lord told us to cross the gorge into Moab, and we did.
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ, wa ya po Zered pa a kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord kept getting rid of them until finally none of them were left.
translation_verse: “Benɛ ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi kpata se ɔ,

english_verse: Then the Lord told me,
translation_verse: Yawɛ de wɔ ke,

english_verse: “Moses, now go past the town of Ar and cross Moab's northern border
translation_verse: ‘Mwɔnɛ ɔ, nyɛ yaa gu Moab huzu nya ngɛ Ar kasa nya.

english_verse: into Ammon. But don't start a war with the Ammonites. I gave them their land, and I won't give any of it to Israel.” More Nations That Lived near Canaan
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ ya su Amon bi ɔmɛ nɛ ji Lot nina a a zugba a huzu nya a, nyɛ ko hao mɛ, nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ mɛ ko hwu ta hulɔ; ejakaa i be nyɛ a zugba a ekoeko hae.’ ”

english_verse: Before the Ammonites conquered the land that the Lord had given them, some of the Rephaim used to live there, although the Ammonites called them Zamzummim.
translation_verse: (A buu zugba nɛ ɔ hu kaa oblaihi nɛ a tsɛɛ mɛ Refaim ɔ a zugba; mɛ lɛ a hi lejɛ ɔ sa a; se Amon bi ɔmɛ tsɛɛ mɛ Zamzum bi.

english_verse: The Lord helped them as he had helped the Edomites, who killed many of the Horites in Seir and forced the rest to leave before settling there themselves.
translation_verse: Yawɛ pee Edom bi ɔmɛ nɛ ji Esau nina a jã nɔuu. E kpata Hor bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ Edom bi ɔmɛ ya ngɔ a zugba a, nɛ a hi lejɛ ɔ. A ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ mwɔɔ.

english_verse: A group called the Avvim used to live in villages as far south as Gaza, but the Philistines killed them and settled on their land. Israel Crossed the Arnon Gorge Moses said:
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ je pa kpɔ Kreta nɔ ɔ, hi Mediterenia wo nya zugba a nɔ be ko. Mɛ lɛ a gbe Avim bi ɔmɛ nɛ hi lejɛ ɔ sa a, nɛ a ngɔ a zugba a tsuo nɛ ngɛ leneyi je ɔ kɛ ya su Gaza tɔɔ.)

english_verse: After we went through Ammon, the Lord told us: Israel, pack up your possessions, take down your tents, and cross the Arnon River gorge. The territory of the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon lies on the other side of the river, but I now give you his land. So attack and take it!
translation_verse: “Benɛ wa nyɛɛ Moab zugba a nɔ kɛ be se ɔ, Yawɛ de mi ke, ‘Nyɛ pue blɔ nɛ nyɛ ya po Arnon pa a. I ngɔ Amor matsɛ, Sihon nɛ je Heshbon kɛ e zugba a ngɔ wo nyɛ dɛ. Nyɛ ya tua lɛ, nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ e zugba a.

english_verse: Today I will start making all other nations afraid of you. They will tremble with fear when anyone mentions you, and they will be terrified when you show up. The Defeat of King Sihon of Heshbon (Numbers
translation_verse: Kɛ je mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ kɛ yaa a, ma ha nihi nɛ ngɛ je ɔ mi tsuo maa ye nyɛ gbeye. Ke a wo nyɛ ta a, sawale maa nu nɔ tsuaa nɔ.’ Israel ye Matsɛ Sihon nɔ (Mose IV,

english_verse: After we had crossed the Arnon and had set up camp in the Kedemoth Desert, I sent messengers to King Sihon of Heshbon, telling him that his nation and ours could be at peace. I said:
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ, i tsɔ nihi kɛ je Kedemot nga kplanaa a nɔ kɛ ho Heshbon matsɛ, Sihon ngɔ ya kɛ he jɔmi munyu ke,

english_verse: Please let Israel go across your country. We will walk straight through, without turning off the road.
translation_verse: ‘Mo ha nɛ waa gu o huzu ɔ nya kɛ be; wa maa nyɛɛ blɔ tɛɛ kɛ ho. Wa be blɔ ɔ nɔ jee.

english_verse: You can even sell us food and water, and we will pay with silver. We need to reach the Jordan River and cross it, because the Lord our God is giving us the land on the west side. The Edomites and Moabites have already let us cross their land. Please let us cross your land as well.
