translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ngɛ Yordan pa a bonyoku je ɔ, mahi nɛ a hla kaa wesa hehi ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: Kedesh ngɛ Galilea, ngɛ Naftali yo ɔ nɔ; Shekem ngɛ Efraim yo ɔ nɔ, kɛ Kiriat Arba ngɛ Yuda yo ɔ nɔ. Kiriat Arba biɛ kpa ji Hebron.

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Yordan pa a beleku je, ngɛ yo zugba kpataa a nɔ, ngɛ Yeriko beleku je ɔ, a hla ma nɛ ɔmɛ: Bezer, ngɛ Ruben zugba a mi, Ramot Gilead ngɛ Gad zugba a mi, kɛ Golan ngɛ Bashan, ngɛ Manase zugba a mi.

english_verse: While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
translation_verse: ngɛ Shilo, ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ. A kɛ hiami nɛ ɔ ba fɔ a hɛ mi ke, “Yawɛ fa kɛ gu Mose nɔ ke a ha wɔ mahi nɛ waa hi mi, kɛ a he lohwe lɛmi hehi kɛ ha wa we mi lohwehi.”

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa a, Israel bi ɔmɛ ha Levi bi ɔmɛ ma komɛ, kɛ lohwe lɛmi hehi ngɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba amɛ a mi.

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Jinɛ a ngɔ ma nɛ ɔmɛ nyɔngma kɛ etɛ kɛ ha Yuda, Simeon, kɛ Benyamin wɛtso ɔmɛ momo. Se a fɔ sɔ, nɛ a he ngɛ a dɛ kɛ ha osɔfo ɔmɛ ekomɛ nɛ je Kohat we puɔ nya ngɛ Levi wɛtso ɔ mi. Osɔfo Aaron nina ji nimli nɛ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ fɔ sɔ kɛ dla ma nɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ a he lohwe lɛmi zugba amɛ ngɔ ha Levi bi ɔmɛ, kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa kɛ gu Mose nɔ ke a pee ɔ.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Mahi, kɛ a he lohwe lɛmi zugbahi tsuo nɛ a ha osɔfo Aaron nina a peeɔ nyɔngma kɛ etɛ.

english_verse: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
translation_verse: Mahi kɛ lohwe lɛmi zugbahi nɛ Gershon bi ɔmɛ na we puɔ nya we puɔ nya ji nyɔngma kɛ etɛ.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ngɔ zugba a tsuo ngɔ ha Israel bi ɔmɛ kaa bɔ nɛ e ka a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ kita ke e ma ha mɛ ɔ. Benɛ a nine su zugba a nɔ ɔ, a hi lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ha mɛ tue mi jɔmi ngɛ zugba a nɔ tsuo kaa bɔ nɛ e ka a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ kita ke e maa pee ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. A he nyɛli ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko nɔ ko nyɛ we mɛ; ejakaa Yawɛ ha Israel bi ɔmɛ ye mɛ tsuo a nɔ.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Ní kpakpahi tsuo nɛ Yawɛ wo Israel ma a si ke e ma ha mɛ ɔ, ekoeko tlɔɛ si; a ná lɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Yoshua tsɛ Ruben wɛtso ɔ, Gad wɛtso ɔ, kɛ Manase wɛtso fa a,

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ, nyɛ si we nyɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, se mohu nyɛ ye mlaa amɛ tsuo nɛ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ wo nyɛ ɔ a nɔ sisiisi.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ ha nyɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ tue mi jɔmi kaa bɔ nɛ e wo si ɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, jehanɛ, nyɛɛ kpale kɛ ho zugba a nɛ nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ ná kaa nyɛ weto ní ɔ nɔ ya. Zugba nɛ ɔ ji nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ tsɔlɔ Mose ngɔ ha nyɛ ngɛ Yordan pa a beleku je ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ hyɛ saminya, nɛ nyɛɛ ye mlaa amɛ nɛ Yawɛ tsɔlɔ Mose wo nyɛ ɔ a nɔ. Nyɛɛ suɔ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ; nyɛɛ pee e suɔmi nya ní; nyɛɛ ye e mlaa amɛ a nɔ, nyɛɛ ye lɛ anɔkuale, nɛ nyɛ sɔmɔ lɛ kɛ nyɛ tsui tsuo, kɛ nyɛ klaa tsuo.”

english_verse: You've become rich from what you've taken from your enemies. You have big herds of cattle, lots of silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and plenty of clothes. Take everything home with you and share with the people of your tribe. I pray that God will be kind to you. You are now free to go home. The tribes of Reuben and Gad started back to Gilead, their own land. Moses had given the land of Bashan to the East Manasseh tribe, so they started back along with Reuben and Gad. God had told Moses that these two and a half tribes should conquer Gilead and Bashan, and they had done so. Joshua had given land west of the Jordan River to the other half of the Manasseh tribe, so they stayed at Shiloh in the land of Canaan with the rest of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Ruben wɛtso ɔ, Gad wɛtso ɔ, kɛ Manase wɛtso fa a kpale kɛ ho a zugba amɛ a nɔ ya. A je Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ a he ngɛ Shilo, ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ, nɛ a pue nɔ kɛ ho mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba a nɔ ya, ngɛ Gilead, he nɛ a ngɔ ha mɛ momo ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ gu Mose nɔ fa mɛ ke a pee ɔ. Bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɛ ngɛ Yordan pa a nya a

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Israel bi kpa amɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ nu kaa Ruben wɛtso ɔ, Gad wɛtso ɔ, kɛ Manase wɛtso fa a ya ma bɔ sami la tɛ ngɛ Yordan pa a he ngɛ Gelilot, ngɛ a zugba a mi.

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ tsɔ osɔfo Eleazar binyumu Finehas kɛ ho Ruben wɛtso ɔ, Gad wɛtso ɔ, kɛ Manase wɛtso fa a a ngɔ ya ngɛ Gilead zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: Ma nimeli nyɔngma, kɛ Finehas ho. Israel wɛtso nyɔngma amɛ nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ, a wɛtsoyihi ji ma nimeli nɛ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: A ba Gilead nɛ a ba na Ruben wɛtso ɔ, Gad wɛtso ɔ, kɛ Manase wɛtso fa a.

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: A bi mɛ ngɛ Yawɛ ma a tsuo nane mi ke, “Mɛni he je nɛ nyɛ pee yayami kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ kɛ si Israel Mawu ɔ? Bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛ ma nɛ ɔ tsɔɔ kaa nyɛ kua Yawɛ, nɛ nyɛ tsɔ e hɛ mi atuã!

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Anɛ nyɛ kaii we yayami nɛ wa pee ngɛ Peor, benɛ Yawɛ kɛ gbenɔ hiɔ gbla lɛ nitsɛ e ma a tue ɔ lo? Wa ngɛ nɔ́ nae kɛ mwɔɔ ngɛ jamɛ a yayami ɔ he. Anɛ jamɛ a yayami ɔ pi ha wɔ lo?

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ, nyɛ ma kua Yawɛ, nɛ nyɛ be lɛ sɔmɔe hu lo? Ke nyɛ kua Yawɛ mwɔnɛ ɔ, Yawɛ ma na Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo he abofu hwɔɔ!

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke nyɛ zugba a nɔ hí nɛ́ a ja Mawu ngɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ kpale kɛ ba Yawɛ zugba a nɔ, he nɛ e bo tsu ɔ ngɛ ɔ. Nyɛ ha nɛ a ha nyɛ zugba ko ngɛ wa ngɔ. Nyɛ ko tsɔ atuã kɛ si Yawɛ, nɛ nyɛ ko pee wɔ hu atuã tsɔli kaa nyɛ maa ma bɔ sami la tɛ kpa ko kɛ piɛ Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he.

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Anɛ nyɛ kaii we Zera binyumu Akan lo? Benɛ Akan tɔ mlaa nɛ kɔɔ níhi nɛ sa kaa a kpata a hɛ mi ɔ he ɔ, a gbla Israel ma a tsuo tue; pi Akan nɔ kake pɛ nɛ gbo ngɛ yayami nɛ ɔ he.”

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: “Yawɛ, Mawu Ope! Yawɛ Mawu Ope! Lɛ pɛ nɛ e le nɔ́ he je nɛ wa pee enɛ ɔ, nɛ wa suɔ kaa nyɛ hu nyɛɛ le! Ke wa tsɔ atuã, nɛ wa yi Yawɛ anɔkuale ɔ, lɛɛ nyɛɛ gbe wɔ!

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Ke wa bui Yawɛ tue, nɛ wa ma wɔ nitsɛmɛ wa bɔ sami la tɛ, nɛ́ waa sã sami bɔhi, loo ngma bɔhi, loo tue mi jɔmi bɔhi ngɛ nɔ ɔ, lɛɛ Yawɛ nitsɛ nɛ gbla wa tue!

english_verse: We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.” Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Lɛ nitsɛ nɛ e ngɔ Yordan pa a ngɔ wo huzu ngɛ waa kɛ nyɛ, Ruben bi, kɛ Gad bi wa kpɛti. Nyɛɛ kɛ Yawɛ be nɔ́ ko peemi.’ Ke e ba mi ja a, nyɛ nina ma ha wa nina maa jɔɔ Yawɛ jami.

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ wa ma bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɛ; pi kaa a sã sami bɔ, loo bɔ kpa komɛ ngɛ nɔ;

english_verse: To build another altar for offering sacrifices would be the same as turning our backs on the Lord and rebelling against him. We could never do that! No, we built the altar to remind us and you and the generations to come that we will worship the Lord. And so we will keep bringing our sacrifices to the Lord's altar, there in front of his sacred tent. Now your descendants will never be able to say to our descendants, “You can't worship the Lord.” But if they do say this, our descendants can answer back, “Look at this altar our ancestors built! It's like the Lord's altar, but it isn't for offering sacrifices. It's here to remind us and you that we belong to the Lord, just as much as you do.”
translation_verse: Wa be Yawɛ hɛ mi atuã tsɔe kɔkɔɔkɔ, nɛ wa be e se jee gblegbleegble kɛ ya ma bɔ sami la tɛ kpa ko nɛ waa sã sami bɔ, loo niye ní bɔ, loo bɔ kpa ko ngɛ nɔ. Wa be bɔ sami la tɛ kpa ko mae kɛ piɛ Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɛ ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ hɛ mi ɔ he.”

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Osɔfo Eleazar bi Finehas de mɛ ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ wa na kaa Yawɛ kɛ wɔ ngɛ. Nyɛ tsɔ we e hɛ mi atuã; mohu ɔ, nyɛ je Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ je tue gblami nɛ Yawɛ kɛ maa ba a nɔ ɔ mi.”

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Finehas kɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ je Ruben bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Gad bi ɔmɛ a he ngɛ Gilead; nɛ a kpale kɛ ba Israel bi ɔmɛ a ngɔ, ba bɔ mɛ amaniɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ngɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ a nya, nɛ a je Mawu yi. A de we hu ke a maa hwu ta nɛ a kpata zugba a nɛ Ruben bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Gad bi ɔmɛ ngɛ nɔ ɔ hɛ mi.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Ruben bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Gad bi ɔmɛ de ke, “Bɔ sami la tɛ nɛ ɔ ji odase ha wɔ, kɛ nyɛ tsuo, kaa Yawɛ ji Mawu.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a wo bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ biɛ ke “Odase”.

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Be saii se ɔ, Yawɛ ha Israel tue mi jɔmi, nɛ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ nɛ bɔle mɛ ɔ doo we a nya hu. Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, Yoshua bwɔ kotokoto.

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e tsɛ Israel ma a tsuo kɛ ba e ngɔ: ma nimeli, asafoatsɛmɛ, kojoli, kɛ tsɔli. E de mɛ ke, “Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, i bwɔ.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Nyɛ na bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ pee je ma nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ nyɛ he. Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ ji nɔ nɛ hwu ta ha nyɛ.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ ma ha nyɛ he nyɛli ɔmɛ maa gbee senyasenya; nɛ e maa fie mɛ kɛ je nyɛ blɔ mi. Nyɛ maa ngɔ a zugba a kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ wo nyɛ si ɔ.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ a ngma ngɛ Mose mlaa womi ɔ mi ɔ, nyɛɛ ye nɔ sisiisi. Nyɛ ko si eko,

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: bɔ nɛ pee nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ je ma nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti ɔ ko bɔ. Nyɛ ko wo a mawu ɔmɛ a ta, nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ a biɛhi kó ka kita; nyɛ ko ja mɛ, nɛ nyɛ ko kpla si ha mɛ.

english_verse: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
translation_verse: Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ ye Yawɛ anɔkuale, kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ ye lɛ anɔkuale kɛ ba su mwɔnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: Yawɛ fie je ma nguahi nɛ a he wa kɛ je nyɛ blɔ mi, nɛ a ti nɔ ko nɔ ko nyɛ we nyɛ.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ti nɔ kake ma nyɛ wo nihi akpe fo, ejakaa Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ ngɛ ta hwue ha nyɛ kaa bɔ nɛ e wo si ɔ.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ hyɛ saminya, nɛ nyɛɛ suɔ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: nyɛ na nɛ nyɛɛ le kaa, ke nyɛ hia kɛ yaa a, Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ be je ma nɛ ɔmɛ fiee kɛ je nyɛ blɔ mi hu. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ he nyɛli ɔmɛ maa pee kaa klama ko nɛ a tsɔ nyɛ, loo muɔ nɛ a tsua ngɛ nyɛ sisi. A maa pee kaa kpa nɛ a kɛ ngɛ nyɛ se mi fiae, nɛ maa sãã nyɛ, loo mio nɛ ngɛ nyɛ hɛngmɛ mi gbɔɔe. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ma tsa nɔ kɛ yaa si be nɛ nyɛ ti nɔ ko nɔ ko be piɛe ngɛ zugba kpakpa nɛ ɔ nɛ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ ngɔ ha nyɛ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ, ye gbenɔ be su. Nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ le ngɛ e tsui mi, kɛ e klaa mi kaa Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ ha nyɛ ní kpakpa amɛ tsuo nɛ e wo si ke e ma ha nyɛ ɔ. E ye e si womi ɔmɛ tsuo kulaa nɔ; e si we eko.

english_verse: Yes, when the Lord makes a promise, he does what he has promised. But when he makes a threat, he will also do what he has threatened. The Lord is our God. He gave us this wonderful land and made an agreement with us that we would worship only him. But if you worship other gods, it will make the Lord furious. He will start getting rid of you, and soon not one of you will be left in this good land that he has given you.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ yi somi nɛ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ kɛ nyɛ so ɔ nɔ, nɛ nyɛ ya sɔmɔ mawu kpahi, nɛ nyɛ ja mɛ ɔ, lɔ ɔ lɛɛ e kɛ abofu maa gbla nyɛ tue, nɛ e be kɛe kulaa nɛ nyɛ ti nɔ ko nɔ ko be piɛe ngɛ zugba kpakpa nɛ ɔ nɛ e ngɔ ha nyɛ ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Yoshua bua Israel wɛtso ɔmɛ a nya kɛ ba kpe ngɛ Shekem. E tsɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ, asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kojoli ɔmɛ, kɛ Israel tsɔli ɔmɛ kɛ ba Mawu hɛ mi.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Yoshua de ma a tsuo ke, “Nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ ngɛ nyɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Blema lokoo ɔ, nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ hi Yufrate pa a se, nɛ a ja mawu kpahi. Nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Tera a ji Abraham kɛ Nahor a tsɛ.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: I ngɔ nyɛ nɛ̃, Abraham kɛ je zugba a nɛ ngɛ Yufrate pa a se ɔ nɔ, nɛ i kpaka lɛ kɛ gu Kanaan zugba a tsuo nɔ, nɛ i ha lɛ nina babauu. I ha lɛ Isak.

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: I ha Isak fɔ Yakob kɛ Esau. I ngɔ Edom yo nɔ zugba a ngɔ ha Esau kaa e weto ní; se nyɛ nɛ̃, Yakob kɛ e bimɛ ɔmɛ lɛɛ a ya hi Egipt.

english_verse: Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea.
translation_verse: i je nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ kɛ je Egipt, nɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ nyɛɛ a se kɛ ta zugba lɛhi, kɛ ta okpɔngɔ nɔ hili. Benɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ya su Wo Tsu ɔ he ɔ,

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: a fa kue ha mi, nɛ i ha diblii wo ngɛ a kɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti. Nyagbe ɔ, i ha wo ɔ ba ha Egipt bi ɔmɛ a nɔ. Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ na nɔ́ nɛ i pee Egipt ɔ. “ ‘Nyɛ hi nga kplanaa a nɔ be babauu.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, i ngɔ nyɛ kɛ ba Amor bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ, ngɛ Yordan pa a beleku je. A kɛ nyɛ hwu ta; se i ha nyɛ ye a nɔ, nɛ nyɛ ngɔ a zugba a. I kpata a hɛ mi, nɛ i ha nyɛ blɔ mi tɛ̃ ha nyɛ.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Zipor bi Balak, Moab matsɛ ɔ kɛ nyɛ ba hwu ta. E tsɔ ya de Beor binyumu Balaam ke e gbiɛ nyɛ.

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: Se i bui Balaam tue; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e gbaa nyɛ mohu. Blɔ nɔ nɛ i gu kɛ je nyɛ kɛ je Balak dɛ mi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: Nyɛ po Yordan pa a, nɛ nyɛ ba Yeriko. Yeriko bi ɔmɛ kɛ nyɛ hwu ta kaa bɔ nɛ Amor, Periz, Kanaan, Hit, Girgash, Hiv, kɛ Yebus bi ɔmɛ tsuo hu kɛ nyɛ hwu ta a. Se i ha nyɛ ye mɛ tsuo a nɔ.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Benɛ nyɛ ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ ma a, i ha sawale nu mɛ. I pee enɛ ɔ kɛ fie Amor matsɛmɛ enyɔ ɔmɛ kɛ je nyɛ blɔ mi. Pi nyɛ klaate, nɛ pi nyɛ kɛ̃ɛ̃ nɛ ye kunimi nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: I ha nyɛ zugba nɛ́ nyɛ gbo we he dengme ko, kɛ mahi nɛ pi nyɛ nɛ nyɛ po. Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, nyɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ nyɛ ngɛ wai ngmɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ oliv ngmɔ ɔmɛ nɛ pi nyɛ nɛ nyɛ tsu a he ní ɔ a mi ní yee.’ ”

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: Yoshua ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ ye Yawɛ gbeye, nɛ nyɛ sɔmɔ lɛ saminya ngɛ anɔkuale mi. Nyɛ je mawu ɔmɛ nɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ja ngɛ Mesopotamia kɛ Egipt ɔ ngɔ pue he, nɛ nyɛ sɔmɔ Yawɛ pɛ.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ sume kaa nyɛ ma sɔmɔ lɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ tsɔɔ mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ nɔ nɛ nyɛ ma sɔmɔ; ke mawu ɔmɛ nɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ja ngɛ Mesopotamia a jio, loo Amor bi ɔmɛ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ a zugba a nɔ ɔ a mawu ɔmɛ jio. Se imi kɛ ye we ɔ lɛɛ, wa ma sɔmɔ Yawɛ.”

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Ma a he nɔ ke, “Wa be Yawɛ sie nɛ wa ya sɔmɔ mawu kpahi!

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ lɛ je wɔ, kɛ wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ kɛ je nyɔguɛ yemi mi ngɛ Egipt, nɛ wa na nyakpɛ níhi nɛ e pee ɔ. E baa wa yi, nɛ e je wɔ kɛ je wa he nyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi ngɛ he tsuaa he nɛ wa gu ɔ.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Yawɛ fie je ma amɛ, kɛ Amor bi ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ kɛ je wa blɔ mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, wɔ hu Yawɛ lɛ wa ma sɔmɔ; lɛ ji wa Mawu.”

english_verse: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
translation_verse: Yoshua ya nɔ, nɛ e de ma a ke, “E ngɛ mi ja; se eko ɔ, nyɛ be Yawɛ nyɛe ma sɔmɔ. Mawu klɔuklɔu ji lɛ, nɛ e kɛ nyɛ tɔmi ɔmɛ, kɛ yayami ɔmɛ be nyɛ pae. A kɛ lɛ plee we nɔ́ he,

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: nɛ ke nyɛ si lɛ nɛ nyɛ ya sɔmɔ ma se mawuhi ɔ, e mi mi maa wo la, nɛ e maa gbla nyɛ tue. E ngɛ mi kaa e pee nyɛ kpakpa hyɛ lɛɛ, se e ma kpata nyɛ hɛ mi.”

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ma a de Yoshua ke, “Dɛbi! Wa ma sɔmɔ Yawɛ.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Yoshua de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ ji odase yeli kaa nyɛ de ke nyɛ ma sɔmɔ Yawɛ.” Ma a he nɔ ke, “Ee, wɔ lɛ wa de ja; odase yeli ji wɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Yoshua kɛ fɔ a hɛ mi ke, “Ke jã a, lɛɛ nyɛ je ma se mawu ɔmɛ ngɔ hɛ pue he, nɛ nyɛɛ wo si kaa nyɛ maa ye Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ anɔkuale.”

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Ma a de Yoshua ke, “Wa ma sɔmɔ Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ. Wa maa ye e mlaa amɛ a nɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yoshua kɛ ma a so somi jamɛ a ligbi ɔ ngɛ Shekem, nɛ e wo mɛ mlaahi, nɛ e tsɔɔ mɛ blɔ nya tomihi nɛ́ a ye nɔ.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Yoshua ngma mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ wo Mawu mlaa womi ɔ mi. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ngɔ tɛ agbo ko ngɔ ma tso ngua a sisi ngɛ Yawɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ.

english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: E de ma a tsuo ke, “Tɛ nɛ ɔ maa pee odase ha wɔ. E nu munyu ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ Yawɛ kɛ wɔ tu ɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke e ba mi kaa nyɛ tsɔ nyɛ Mawu ɔ hɛ mi atuã a, e maa ye odase kɛ si nyɛ.”

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Yoshua wo ma a blɔ, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ kpale kɛ ho lɛ nitsɛ e tita nɔ ya. Yoshua kɛ Eleazar gbo

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Yawɛ tsɔlɔ Yoshua, Nun bi ɔ ba gbo. E ye jeha lafa kɛ nyɔngma.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: A pu lɛ ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e zugba nɔ, ngɛ Timnat Sera, ngɛ Efraim yo ɔ nɔ, ngɛ Gaash yo ɔ omleyi je.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Yoshua wami ligbi ɔmɛ tsuo ɔ, ma a sɔmɔ Yawɛ. Yoshua gbenɔ se, be mi nɛ ma nimeli nɛ na ní nguanguahi tsuo nɛ Yawɛ tsu ha Israel ɔ na we nɛ a gbo lolo ɔ, a ya nɔ nɛ a sɔmɔ Yawɛ ja nɔuu.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: A pu Yosef wuhi nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɔ kɛ je Egipt kɛ ba a ngɛ Shekem, ngɛ zugba ko nɛ Yakob he ɔ mi. E he zugba nɛ ɔ kɛ sika hiɔ kpɔ lafa ngɛ Shekem tsɛ, Hamor bimɛ ɔmɛ a dɛ. Zugba nɛ ɔ ba pee Yosef nina a weto ní.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Aaron bi Eleazar hu ba gbo, nɛ a pu lɛ ngɛ Gibea ngɛ Efraim yo ɔ nɔ, he nɛ a ngɔ kɛ ha e binyumu Finehas ɔ.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Yoshua gbenɔ se ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ bi Yawɛ ke, “Wa kpɛti mɛnɔmɛ ma ya tua Kanaan bi ɔmɛ kekleekle?”

english_verse: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de mɛ ke, “Yuda wɛtso ɔ maa sɛ hlami; i ngɔ zugba a ngɔ wo a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ de a nyɛmimɛ Simeon bi ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ ha waa ho zugba a nɛ a ngɔ ha wɔ ɔ nɔ ya, nɛ waa kɛ Kanaan bi ɔmɛ ya hwu. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, waa kɛ nyɛ maa ya nyɛ hu nyɛ zugba a nɔ.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Simeon bi ɔmɛ kɛ mɛ ho.

english_verse: Together they attacked an army of
translation_verse: A ya na Adonibezek ngɛ Bezek, nɛ a kɛ lɛ hwu ta.

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Yuda bi ɔmɛ ya tua Kanaan bi nɛ ngɛ Hebron nɛ sa a, e biɛ ji Kiriat Arba a, nɛ a gbe Sheshai, Ahiman, kɛ Talmai bi ɔmɛ. Otniel ye Debir ma a nɔ kunimi

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: Adonibezek tu fo, se a nyɛɛ e se, nɛ a ya nu lɛ, nɛ a po e nine gɔleku, kɛ e nane gɔleku.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ ya tua Yerusalem, nɛ a ngɔ ma a. A kɛ klaate gbe ma mi bi ɔmɛ, nɛ a mɛ ma a he la.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a ya tua Kanaan bi nɛ ngɛ yoku ɔmɛ a nɔ ngɛ leneyi je ɔ, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ nga nɔ zugba a nɔ ɔ.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Nɛ́ a je lejɛ ɔ, a ya tua Debir nɛ sa a, a tsɛɛ lɛ Kiriat Sefer ɔ.

english_verse: Caleb told his troops, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
translation_verse: Kaleb de ke, “Nɔ nɛ ma tua Kiriat Sefer nɛ e maa ngɔ ma a, ma ha lɛ ye biyo Aksa nɛ e ngɔ.”

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Otniel, Kaleb senɔ nyumu Kenaz binyumu ɔ ya ngɔ ma a; nɛ Kaleb kɛ e biyo Aksa a ha lɛ.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Benɛ a kpee Aksa a, e wo e huno ɔ yi mi ke e bi e ngatsɛ ɔ ngmɔ zugba ko. Aksa kple si kɛ je e teji ɔ nɔ, nɛ Kaleb bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni o suɔ nɛ ma pee ha mo?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: Aksa he nɔ ke, “Moo ke mi nɔ́ ko. O ha mi zugba ngɛ leneyi je he nɛ nyu be momo, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o ha mi he ko nɛ nyu ngɛ kɛ piɛ he!” Nɛ Kaleb ha lɛ hehi nɛ nyu ngɛ, ngɛ yo nɔ kɛ kɔ̃ mi. Yuda kɛ Benyamin ye kunimi

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Mose ngatsɛ, Ken no ɔ nina nɛ ji Ken bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ je Yeriko, tã ma a mi kɛ ba Yuda nga a nɔ, ngɛ Arad leneyi je, nɛ a kɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ ba hi si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ, kɛ a nyɛmimɛ Simeon bi ɔmɛ ho ya tua Kanaan bi nɛ ngɛ Zefat ɔ. A gbe mɛ basabasa, nɛ a kpata ma a hɛ mi pɛsɛpɛsɛ; nɛ a wo ma a biɛ ke Horma.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: Yawɛ piɛ Yuda he nɛ a kɛ ngɔ yoku nɔ zugba amɛ. Se ni nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi ɔ lɛɛ a nyɛ we nɛ a fie mɛ; ejakaa dade ta zugba lɛhi ngɛ a dɛ.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: A kɛ Hebron ha Kaleb kaa bɔ nɛ Mose fa mɛ ɔ; nɛ e fie Anak binyumu etɛ ɔmɛ kɛ je lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Se Yebus bi nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ lɛɛ Benyamin bi ɔmɛ fie we mɛ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a kɛ Benyamin bi ɔmɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ. Efraim kɛ Manase ye Betel nɔ

english_verse: The Ephraim and Manasseh tribes were getting ready to attack Bethel, which at that time was called Luz. And the Lord helped them when they sent spies to find out as much as they could about Bethel.
translation_verse: Yosef bi ɔmɛ, nɛ ji Efraim kɛ Manase wɛtso ɔmɛ hu ya tua Betel nɛ sa a, e biɛ ji Luz ɔ; nɛ Yawɛ piɛ a he. Kekleekle ɔ, a tsɔ nihi ya slaa ma a lolo.

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Slaali ɔmɛ na nyumu ko nɛ je ma a mi kɛ ma, nɛ a de lɛ ke, “Wa kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o tsɔɔ wɔ blɔ nɛ a kɛ yaa ma a mi. Ke o tsɔɔ wɔ blɔ ɔ, wa maa na mo mɔbɔ.”

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ tsɔɔ mɛ blɔ nɛ a kɛ yaa ma a mi ɔ, nɛ benɛ a sɛ ma a mi ɔ, a kɛ klaate gbe ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo pɛsɛpɛsɛ. Se nyumu ɔ kɛ e weku li lɛɛ a tɛ a he.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, nyumu ɔ je kɛ ho Hit bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ ya, nɛ e ya po ma ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. E wo ma a biɛ ke Luz; nɛ jã ji e biɛ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ. Nihi nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ fie we mɛ

english_verse: Canaanites lived in the towns of Beth-Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and all the villages nearby. The Canaanites were determined to stay, and the Manasseh tribe never did get rid of them. But later on, when the Israelites grew more powerful, they made slaves of the Canaanites.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a he ba wa a, a fie we Kanaan bi ɔmɛ kɛ ji zugba a nɔ pɛsɛpɛsɛ; se mohu a nyɛ a nɔ, nɛ a tsu ní ha mɛ.

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Efraim bi ɔmɛ hu fie we Kanaan bi ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Gezer ɔ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Kanaan bi ɔmɛ kɛ mɛ hi lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Zebulun bi ɔmɛ fie we Kitron, kɛ Nahala bi ɔmɛ. Kanaan bi nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ mɛ hi si; se mohu Israel bi ɔmɛ nyɛ a nɔ nɛ a tsu ní ha mɛ.

english_verse: The Asher tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob, and the Asher tribe lived with Canaanites all around them.
translation_verse: Asher bi nɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ Kanaan bi nɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ hi si; ejakaa a fie we mɛ.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Naftali bi ɔmɛ fie we Bet Shemesh, kɛ Bet Anat bi ɔmɛ. Naftali bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Kanaan bi nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ hi si; se mohu a nyɛ Bet Shemesh, kɛ Bet Anat bi ɔmɛ a nɔ nɛ a tsu ní ha mɛ.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amor bi ɔmɛ sá Dan bi ɔmɛ a yi ngɔ wo yoku ɔmɛ a nɔ; nɛ a ngmɛ́ mɛ blɔ nɛ a kple si kɛ ba nga a nɔ.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Amor bi ɔmɛ hi Heres yo ɔ nɔ, Aiyalon, kɛ Shaalbim; se Yosef nina nɛ ji Efraim kɛ Manase ɔ, a nine si wa ngɛ Amor bi ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ a nyɛ a nɔ nɛ a tsu ní ha mɛ.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Amor bi ɔmɛ a huzu ɔ ngɛ kɛ je Akrabim yo kpɛ blɔ ɔ he kɛ ya gu Sela, kɛ po mi kɛ ho yiti je ya.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ je Gilgal kɛ ba Bokim, nɛ e ba de Israel ma a ke, “I je nyɛ kɛ je Egipt, nɛ i kɛ nyɛ ba zugba nɛ i wo nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ si ke ma ha mɛ ɔ nɔ. I de ke, ‘Somi nɛ i kɛ nyɛ so ɔ, i be se jee gblegbleegble.

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: Nyɛ hu nyɛɛ kɛ zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ bi ɔmɛ nɛ ko so somi ko; se mohu nyɛɛ ku a bɔ sami la tɛ ɔmɛ.’ Se nyɛ bui mi tue. Nyɛɛ hyɛ nɔ nɛ nyɛ ya pee!

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, imi hu i ngɛ nyɛ dee ke i be ni ɔmɛ fiee kɛ je nyɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ. A ma plɛ pee nyɛ he nyɛli, nɛ a mawu ɔmɛ hu ma plɛ pee klama nɛ a tsɔ nyɛ.”

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Bokim; e sisi ji ya foli. Nɛ a sã bɔhi ha Yawɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Yoshua gbenɔ

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: A pu lɛ ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e zugba nɔ ngɛ Timnat Heres, ngɛ Efraim yo ɔmɛ a nɔ, ngɛ Gaas yo ɔ we omleyi je.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a yi nɔ bi ɔmɛ tsuo kulaa hu ba gbo. Nɛ yi nɔ kpa bimɛ nɛ ba ngɛ a se ɔ, mɛɛ lɛɛ a li Yawɛ, kɛ ní tsumi nɛ e tsu ha Israel ɔ. Israel kpa Yawɛ sɔmɔmi

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: He tsuaa he nɛ a gba ta kɛ gu kɛkɛ Yawɛ ha matahu ba po mɛ kaa bɔ nɛ e ka kita ke e maa pee mɛ ɔ. Nɛ a yi fi wawɛɛ nitsɛ.

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ je manyadali komɛ ha Israel, nɛ a ba kpɔ ma a kɛ je ní hali ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Se manyadali ɔmɛ po a bui mɛ; nɛ Yawɛ hu a yi lɛ anɔkuale. Mohu ɔ, a ya nyɛɛ mawu kpahi a se, nɛ a ja mɛ; nɛ a je blɔ nɛ a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ nyɛɛ nɔ ɔ nɔ. A nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ye Yawɛ mlaa amɛ a nɔ; se mɛɛ lɛɛ a pee we ja.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Be tsuaa be nɛ Yawɛ ma ha Israel manyadalɔ ko ɔ, e piɛɔ e he kɛ kpɔɔ ma a kɛ jeɔ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi e wami ligbi ɔmɛ tsuo. Ejakaa kɛmɛmi nɛ a hii kɛmɛe ngɛ a yi mi wali, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ haoɔ mɛ ɔ a dɛ mi ɔ peeɔ Yawɛ mɔbɔ.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Se ke manyadalɔ ɔ gbo pɛ, ma a kpaleɔ a se kɛ ya nyɛɛɔ a blɔ momo ɔmɛ a nɔ ekohu; nɛ a peeɔ yayami nɛ nya wa pe a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ po. A ya nyɛɛɔ mawu kpahi a se; a sɔmɔɔ mɛ, nɛ a jaa mɛ. Nɛ a ngmɛɛ we a yayami ɔmɛ, kɛ a kuɛ mi timi ɔ he.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ɔ, Yawɛ mi mi ma fu Israel, nɛ e ma de ke, “Akɛnɛ ma nɛ ɔ yi somi ɔ nɛ i wo a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ mlaa ngɛ he ɔ nɔ, nɛ imi nitsɛ hu a bui mi he je ɔ,

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: kɛ je mwɔnɛ ɔ kɛ yaa a, je ma amɛ nɛ piɛ benɛ Yoshua gbo ɔ, i be mɛ fiee kɛ je zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ mɛ kɛ ka Israel nɛ ma hyɛ kaa a maa nyɛɛ ye blɔ ɔmɛ a nɔ kaa bɔ nɛ a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ pee ɔ, loo a be ja pee.”

english_verse: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
translation_verse: Yawɛ pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Israel yi nɔ bimɛ nɛ maa ba ngɛ se ɔ, a tsɔɔ mɛ ta hwumi; titli ɔ, a ti ni nɛmɛ nɛ yɛ ta hyɛ ɔ.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Je ma amɛ ji Filisti bi a matsɛmɛ enuɔ ɔmɛ, Sidon bi, kɛ Hiv bi nɛ ngɛ Lebanon yo ɔmɛ a nɔ kɛ je Baal Hermon yo ɔ he kɛ ya si Hamat yo kpɛ blɔ ɔ nya.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: A si mɛ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a ngɔ mɛ kɛ ka Israel, nɛ a hyɛ kaa a maa ye Yawɛ mlaa amɛ nɛ e wo a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ kɛ gu Mose nɔ ɔ a nɔ lo.

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: A ngɔ ma je li ɔmɛ a biyihi, nɛ mɛ hu a kɛ a biyihi ha ma je li ɔmɛ a binyumuhi; nɛ a sɔmɔ a mawu ɔmɛ. Otniel

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ a hɛ je Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ nɔ; a pee yayami kɛ si lɛ, nɛ a ya sɔmɔ Baalhi kɛ Ashera.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yawɛ mi mi fu Israel, nɛ e ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo Mesopotamia matsɛ, Kushan Rishataim dɛ mi; nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ sɔmɔ Kushan Rishataim jeha kpaanyɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Se Israel bi ɔmɛ fa kue ha Yawɛ, nɛ Yawɛ je nyumu ko ha mɛ, nɛ e ba kpɔ mɛ. Lɛ ji Otniel, Kaleb senɔ nyumu Kenaz binyumu ɔ.

english_verse: and Israel was at peace until Othniel died about
translation_verse: Zugba a nɔ jɔ jeha nyingmi eywiɛ. Nɛ Kenaz binyumu Otniel ba gbo. Ehud

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ ekohu. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Yawɛ ya piɛ Moab matsɛ, Eglon he, nɛ e kɛ Israel to ní.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Eglon, kɛ Amon bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ pee kake kɛ ya tua Israel bi ɔmɛ. A ye a nɔ, nɛ a ngɔ ma a nɛ tãhi ngɛ mi ɔ.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Benɛ Ehud ngɔ nike ní ɔmɛ kɛ ya ha lɛ se ɔ, e wo nihi nɛ tloo nike ní ɔmɛ kɛ ya a blɔ.

english_verse: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, benɛ lɛ matsɛ ɔ nɔ kake too e hii si ngɛ e hiɔwe tsu nɛ e mi jɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Ehud ba e ngɔ nɛ e ba de lɛ ke, “I hɛɛ sɛ ko kɛ je Mawu ngɔ kɛ ma mo hami.” Matsɛ ɔ te si pam!

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Ehud ngɔ e muɔ nine kɛ hia klaate ɔ ngɛ e hiɔ nɔ fiɔ he, nɛ e kɛ klaate ɔ gbɔ matsɛ ɔ muklii mi.

english_verse: that even the handle was buried in his fat. Ehud left the dagger there. Then after closing and locking the doors to the room, he climbed through a window onto the porch
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Ehud gu asa a nɔ kɛ je kpo. E nga hiɔwe tsu ɔ sinya amɛ, nɛ e ngmɛ a mi ngɛ se.

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Benɛ matsɛ ɔ tsɔli ɔmɛ ngɛ mlɛe ɔ, Ehud je momo; e ya be ngɛ he nɛ amaga amɛ ngɛ ɔ, nɛ e tsa nɔ kɛ ho Seira ya.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: E de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ nyɛɛ ye se! Yawɛ ngɔ nyɛ he nyɛli, Moab bi ɔmɛ kɛ wo nyɛ dɛ mi.” Nɛ a nyɛɛ e se kɛ ya ngɔ he nɛ a poo Yordan pa a ngɛ kɛ yaa Moab ɔ; a ha we nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko nɛ po pa a.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Israel ye Moab nɔ kunimi jamɛ a ligbi ɔ. Nɛ zugba a nɔ jɔ jeha nyingmi kpaanyɔ. Shamgar

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Ehud se ɔ, Anat binyumu Shamgar ba. Lɛ hu e kɛ na tsɔmi tso gbe Filisti bi lafa ekpa, nɛ e kɛ he Israel yi wami.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ehud gbenɔ se ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ ekohu.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yawɛ ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo Kanaan matsɛ, Yabin nɛ ye matsɛ ngɛ Hazor ma a mi ɔ dɛ mi. E tatsɛ ji Sisera, nɛ lɛɛ e hi Haroshet ngɛ ma je li ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Sisera de lɛ ke, “Yaa da si ngɛ bo tsu sinya a nya. Ke nɔ ko ba bi mo ke nɔ ko ngɛ hiɛ ɔ lo ɔ, de lɛ ke, ‘Dɛbi.’ ”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, gbalɔyo ko ji nɔ nɛ ngɛ Israel ma a nya. Lɛ ji Lapidot yo Debora.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: E pɔɔ si himi ngɛ tã ko sisi ngɛ Rama kɛ Betel a kpɛti, ngɛ Efraim yo ɔmɛ a nɔ. Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ a sane yaa e ngɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e hyɛɛ mi ha mɛ.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, e tsɔ ya tsɛ Abinoam binyumu Barak ngɛ Kedesh nɛ ngɛ Naftali ɔ kɛ ba, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ ngɛ mo fae ke, ‘Yaa nɛ o ya hla nyumuhi akpe nyɔngma kɛ je Naftali kɛ Zebulun wɛtso ɔmɛ a mi, nɛ o kɛ mɛ nɛ ba Tabor yo ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Ma ha Yabin tatsɛ Sisera kɛ e ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ e ta buli ɔmɛ kɛ mo ma ba kpe ngɛ Kishon pa a nya; nɛ ma ngɔ lɛ ngɔ wo o dɛ mi.’ ”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Debora he nɔ ke, “I kɛ mo maa ya tsɔ. Se mohu blɔ nɛ o ngɛ hiae nɛ ɔ, hɛ mi nyami nɛ maa ba a be o nɔ́ pee; ejakaa Yawɛ maa ngɔ Sisera kɛ wo yo dɛ mi.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Debora te si nɛ e kɛ Barak je kɛ ho Kedesh ya.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, Ken no ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Heber ɔ tsɔ e he kɛ je Ken bi, nɛ ji Mose ngatsɛ Hobab nina a a he; nɛ e ya ma e bo tsu ɔ ngɛ tso ngua a nɛ ngɛ Zaananim ɔ he, ngɛ Kedesh kasa nya tɔɔ.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Benɛ a ya bɔ Sisera amaniɛ kaa Abinoam binyumu Barak hia ta kɛ ho Tabor yo ɔ nɔ ya a,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Debora de Barak ke, “Tee si! Mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, Yawɛ ngɔ Sisera kɛ wo o dɛ mi. Anɛ pi Yawɛ nitsɛ nɛ hia kɛ nyɛɛ o hɛ mi kɛ yaa a lo?” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Barak kple Tabor yo ɔ, kɛ e we bi akpe nyɔngma amɛ ngɛ e se.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Benɛ Barak gba ta a, Yawɛ ha nɛ Sisera kɛ e ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ e tabo ɔmɛ tsuo jija, nɛ a kɛ klaate gbe mɛ pɛsɛpɛsɛ. Sisera nitsɛ lɛɛ e kple si kɛ je e ta zugba lɛ ɔ mi, nɛ e kɛ e nane to he.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Sisera tu fo kɛ ya sɛ Ken no, Heber e yo Yael bo tsu mi; ejakaa tue mi jɔmi ngɛ Hazor matsɛ, Yabin we ɔ, kɛ Ken no, Heber we ɔ a kpɛti.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Yael je kpo nɛ e kɛ Sisera ya kpe; nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ye nyɔmtsɛ, moo ba! Moo sɛ ye bo tsu ɔ mi! Koo ye gbeye!” Kɛkɛ nɛ e sɛ bo tsu ɔ mi, nɛ Yael ngɔ sa nɔ bo kɛ ha e nɔ.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Sisera de lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, ha mi nyu bɔɔ nɛ ma nu; kuma ngɛ mi yee.” Yael bli lohwehi a he womi kotoku ko nɛ nyɔ nyu ngɛ mi nya, nɛ e ha lɛ eko nɛ e nu; nɛ e ngɔ sa nɔ bo kɛ ha e nɔ ekohu.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Sisera kɛ pɔ tɔtɔɛ hwɔ mahe vii. Kɛkɛ nɛ Heber e yo Yael ngɔ bo tsu plɛɛko kɛ hamle, nɛ e nyɛɛ blɛuu kɛ ho e ngɔ ya, nɛ e ya ka plɛɛko ɔ kɛ wo e tue si kɛ sɛ zu mi. Nɛ Sisera gbo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Benɛ Barak nyɛɛ Sisera se kɛ ba lejɛ ɔ, Yael je kpo kɛ lɛ ba kpe; nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ba nɛ ma tsɔɔ mo nyumu ɔ nɛ o ngɛ hlae ɔ.” Barak kɛ lɛ sɛ bo tsu ɔ mi, nɛ e na Sisera nɛ e gbo kɛ hwɔɔ si kɛ bo tsu tso plɛɛko ɔ nɛ a ka kɛ wo e tue si ɔ.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Mawu ha Israel bi ɔmɛ ye Kanaan matsɛ, Yabin nɔ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ kɔni si wami nyɛɛ Kanaan matsɛ, Yabin se kɛ ya si a kpata e hɛ mi pɛsɛpɛsɛ.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, Debora kɛ Abinoam binyumu Barak la la nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: Nyɛ je Yawɛ yi! Israel nikɔtɔma amɛ nyɛɛ ma a hɛ mi, nɛ ma a ngɔ a he ha kɛ bua jɔmi.

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Nyɛ matsɛmɛ, nyɛɛ bu tue! Ganɔhi nyɛ ta tue! Ma la; i kɛ gbi ngɔngɔɛ ma je Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ yi.

english_verse: Our Lord, God of Israel, when you came from Seir, where the Edomites live,
translation_verse: Yawɛ, benɛ o je Seir, nɛ o hia kɛ je Edom kɛ ma a, zugba mimiɛ, nɛ hiɔmi nɛ. Niinɛ, nyu je bɔku ɔmɛ a mi pue si.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Anat binyumu Shamgar, kɛ Yael a be ɔ mi ɔ, gbɛjegbɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ fɔɔ si gu, nɛ blɔ nyɛɛli guu nane blɔ.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Israel kɔpe ɔmɛ pee ma dokuhi; nɔ ko be a mi loko mo, Debora, o ba kaa Israel ma a a nyɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ya hla mawu hehi ɔ, ta te si ngɛ zugba a nɔ. Se Israel nyumuhi akpe nyingmi eywiɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, a nɛ tsɛ̃i, loo akplɔ ngɛ nɔ kake po dɛ mi.

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: Israel tatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɔ a he ngɔ ke ɔ, i ná a he bua jɔmi. Nyɛ je Yawɛ yi!

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ bu tue! Nimli asafo ɔ nɛ pueɔ si ngɛ nyɛ nyu yɛmi he ɔmɛ ɔ, a ngɛ lae, nɛ a ngɛ gbae bɔ nɛ Yawɛ ye manye ha Israel. Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ ma a kɛ gɛjɛmi nyɛɛ kɛ ba agbo ɔmɛ a nya.

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ odehehi nɛ piɛ ɔ kple si kɛ ba. Yawɛ ma a kple si kɛ ba na he nyɛli ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: A je Efraim kɛ ba kɔ̃ ɔ mi. A nyɛɛ mo Benyamin, kɛ o ma mi bi ɔmɛ a se. Tatsɛmɛ je Makir kɛ ba, nɛ tatsɛ tso hɛɛli hu je Zebulun kɛ ba.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Isakar ganɔ ɔmɛ ya piɛ Debora he; Isakar mɛtɛ Barak he kpɛii. A nyɛɛ e se kɛ fo kɛ ho kɔ̃ ɔ mi ya. Se Ruben wɛtso ɔ lɛɛ mi gbami ngɛ a kpɛti, nɛ a nya be kake.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Mɛni he je o hii si ngɛ to ɔmɛ a kpɛti nɛ o ngɛ to ɔmɛ a tsɛmi bɛ ɔmɛ tue bue ɔ? Niinɛ, Ruben wɛtso ɔ lɛɛ mi gbami ngɛ a kpɛti, nɛ a nya be kake.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gilead tlɔ Yordan pa a se; Dan hu, mɛni he je e tlɔ lɛ ɔmɛ a he ɔ? Asher hii si kpoo ngɛ wo ɔ nya he nɛ lɛ ɔmɛ ba saa si ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Se Zebulun, kɛ Naftali lɛɛ a ngɔ a wami ngɔ ke gbenɔ ngɛ ta nga nɔ.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: Matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ba Taanak ba hwu ta ngɛ Megido pa a nya; Kanaan matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ba hwu ta, se a nɛ sika hiɔ nɔ́ ko nɛ a ha.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Dodoehi po hwu ta ngɛ hiɔwe; a je a blɔ hehi nɛ a kɛ Sisera ba hwu ta.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kishon pa a muɔ mɛ kɛ ho; niinɛ, Kishon nyu dɔ ɔ muɔ mɛ kɛ ho. Imi lɛɛ ma nyɛɛ kɛ he wami!

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ okpɔngɔ ɔmɛ tuu kɛ ba; a si a nane kokloto si.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ de ke, “Nyɛɛ gbiɛ Meroz; nyɛɛ gbiɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ wawɛɛ! Ejakaa a bɛ nɛ a ba piɛ Yawɛ he benɛ e kɛ he nyɛli ɔmɛ ngɛ hwue ɔ.”

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Ken no Heber e yo Yael ɔ, a maa gbaa lɛ pe yihi tsuo nɛ hii bo tsu mi.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Sisera bi lɛ nyu, se Yael ha lɛ nyɔ nyu. E kɛ nyami wo tsimi saminyayoo ko mi kɛ ba.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: E hɛɛ bo tsu plɛɛko ngɛ e muɔ nine mi. Ní tsuli a hamle ngɛ e hiɔ nine mi. E ka tso plɛɛko ɔ kɛ wo Sisera tue si; e kɛ gbɔ lɛ, nɛ e ywia e yi.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: Sisera nyɛ ya hyɛ saflɛ mi; e kpa huhui kɛ je saflɛ puɔ ɔmɛ a se nɛ e bi ke, “Mɛni he je e ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ bɛ lolo ɔ? Mɛni he je wa nui okpɔngɔ ɔmɛ a nane kokloto he lolo ɔ?”

english_verse: She and her wisest women gave the same answer:
translation_verse: Yihi ní leli ɔmɛ ha lɛ heto. Lɛ nitsɛ hu e de e he si abɔ ke,

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: Yawɛ, ha o he nyɛli ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi nɛ kpata kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ. Se o huɛmɛ ɔmɛ lɛɛ ha nɛ a pee kaa pu nɛ ngɛ si tee kɛ he wami! Nɛ zugba a nɔ jɔ jeha nyingmi eywiɛ.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ ekohu. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yawɛ hu ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo Midian bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi jeha kpaago.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Be tsuaa be nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ma du ní ɔ, Midian, kɛ Amalek bi, kɛ ma amɛ nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ ma ba tua mɛ.

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Ke a ma a, a hɛɛɔ a lohwehi, kɛ a bo tsuhi kɛ baa, nɛ a he hiɛɛ babauu kaa baalɛhi. A kɛ a we afukpɔngɔ ɔmɛ ɔ, nɔ ko nɔ ko nyɛ we mɛ kanemi; nɛ ke a ba a, a kpataa nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ hɛ mi ngɛ zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ fa kue ha Yawɛ kɛ bi yemi kɛ buami ɔ,

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a prophet to them with this message: I am the Lord God of Israel, so listen to what I say. You were slaves in Egypt, but I set you free and led you out of Egypt into this land. And when nations here made life miserable for you, I rescued you and helped you get rid of them and take their land.
translation_verse: Imi lɛ i je nyɛ kɛ je Egipt bi ɔmɛ, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ wa nyɛ yi mi ɔ tsuo a dɛ mi. Imi lɛ i fie mɛ kɛ je a zugba a nɔ, nɛ i ngɔ zugba a kɛ ha nyɛ,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: nɛ i de nyɛ ke, ‘Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛ ko ja Amor bi ɔmɛ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ a zugba a nɔ ɔ a mawu ɔmɛ.’ Se nyɛ bui mi tue.” Gideon tsɛmi

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ ba Ofra, nɛ e ba hi si ngɛ Yoash, Abiezer no ɔ tso ngua a sisi. Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, e binyumu Gideon ya laa e he, nɛ e ngɛ ngma gbee ngɛ wai muɔ mi, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Midian bi ɔmɛ ko na lɛ.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ je e he si tsɔɔ lɛ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Mo nyumu katsɛ, Yawɛ kɛ mo ngɛ!”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Gideon de lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, ke Yawɛ kɛ wɔ ngɛ niinɛ ɔ, mɛni he je lɛ ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ba wa nɔ mɔ? Nyakpɛ níhi tsuo nɛ wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ gba wɔ ke Yawɛ pee ha mɛ ɔ, jije a ngɛ? Pi lɛ nɛ e kpaka mɛ kɛ je Egipt kɛ ba a? Amlɔ nɛ ɔ lɛɛ Yawɛ sake wɔ ngɔ fɔ he; e ngɔ wɔ kɛ wo Midian bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ hyɛ lɛ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Yaa, nɛ o kɛ o he wami nɛ ɔ ya kpɔ Israel kɛ je Midian dɛ mi. Imi nitsɛ lɛ i tsɔ mo!”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Gideon de lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ Yawɛ, kɛ ma pee kɛ kpɔ Israel kɛɛ? Weku nɛ i je mi ɔ ji weku nyafii pe kulaa ngɛ Manase wɛtso ɔ mi. Tsaatsɛ we ɔ mi hu imi ji jokuɛyo pe kulaa.”

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Ma piɛ o he; o maa fia Midian bi ɔmɛ nɔ nɛ o maa gbe mɛ kaa a gbeɔ nɔ kake.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Gideon de lɛ ke, “Ke o ngɛ ye he suɔmi ɔ, lɛɛ moo to mi okadi ko nɛ ma kɛ na kaa mo, Yawɛ nitsɛ lɛ o kɛ mi ngɛ munyu tue ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Gideon ho nɛ e ya gbe apletsi bɔbɔyoo ko, nɛ e kɛ mamu kilo nyɔngma pee abolo kplolo. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e kɛ lo ɔ wo kusii mi, nɛ e plɛ e he nyu ɔ kɛ wo kutu mi; nɛ e ngɔ kɛ ba ha Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ ngɛ tso ngua a sisi.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Se Mawu bɔfo ɔ de lɛ ke, “Ngɔɔ lo ɔ, kɛ abolo kplolo ɔ kɛ pue tɛ sa nɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ o plɛ lo ɔ he nyu ɔ kɛ pue nɔ.” Gideon pee ja.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ kpã e nine mi, nɛ e kɛ tso ɔ nɛ e hɛɛ ɔ nya sa lo ɔ kɛ abolo kplolo ɔ he. La je tɛ sa a mi sã lo ɔ, kɛ abolo kplolo ɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ bɔfo ɔ laa.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Gideon na kaa Yawɛ bɔfo nɛ e na a, e de ke, “Akuanyɛ! Yawɛ Mawu! Yawɛ bɔfo pam lɛ i na hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi paa kikɛ nɛ ɔ!”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “He jɔmi ha mo. Koo ye gbeye; o be gboe!”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Gideon pee bɔ sami la tɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ha Yawɛ, nɛ e wo lɛ biɛ ke, “Yawɛ ji he jɔmi.” Bɔ sami la tɛ nɛ ɔ maa si ngɛ Abiezer bi ɔmɛ a ma a mi ngɛ Ofra kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, Yawɛ de Gideon ke, “Yaa nu o tsɛ na ku ɔ, kɛ na ku kpa nɛ ye jeha kpaago; nɛ o ya ku bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɛ o tsɛ pee kɛ ha Baal ɔ, kɛ yo wɔ Ashera nɛ ngɛ e kasa nya a,

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: nɛ o ma bɔ sami la tɛ ha Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ ngɛ tɛ sa nɛ ɔ nɔ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ngɔɔ Ashera he tso ɔmɛ nɛ o ku pue si ɔ kɛ pee lɛ́, nɛ o ngɔ na ku enyɔne ɔ kɛ sã sami bɔ.”

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Gideon hla e tsɔli ɔmɛ a kpɛti ni nyɔngma, nɛ e pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ɔ. Akɛnɛ e ngɛ e we mi bi ɔmɛ, kɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ gbeye yee he je ɔ, e nyɛ we nɛ e tsu ní tsumi nɛ ɔ piani, se nyɔ mi.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Mɔtu kpla benɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ te si ɔ, a na kaa a ywia Baal bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ, kɛ yo wɔ Ashera nɔ́ ɔ nɛ ngɛ e kasa nya a. A na hu kaa a sã na ku enyɔne ɔ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ nɛ a ma a nɔ;

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: nɛ a bi a sibi ke, “Mɛnɔ po pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ?” Se benɛ a hla mi, nɛ a bi si, nɛ a ná le kaa Gideon, Yoash binyumu ɔ ji nɔ nɛ ye jamɛ a sane ɔ,

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: ma mi bi ɔmɛ de Yoash ke, “Ngɔɔ o bi ɔ kɛ ba nɛ a gbe lɛ; ejakaa e ywia Baal bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ, kɛ yo wɔ Ashera hu nɔ́ ɔ.”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Se Yoash de ni ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ ba bɔle lɛ ɔ ke, “Baal he nɛ nyɛ ngɛ pɛe nɛ ɔ? Baal he nɛ nyɛ ngɛ fae nɛ ɔ? Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ngɛ Baal he pɛe ɔ, a maa gbe lɛ loko je maa na. Baal ɔ, ke mawu ji lɛ ɔ, nyɛ ha e fa lɛ nitsɛ e he; e bɔ sami la tɛ lɛ a ywia a nɛ!”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, kɛ je jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, biɛ nɛ a tsɛɔ Gideon ji Yerubaal. E sisi ji, “Ha nɛ Baal kɛ lɛ ya to ní,” ejakaa e ywia Baal bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ.

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: E kɛ we kulaa nɛ Midian bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ, kɛ ma amɛ nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ ba bua a he nya. A po Yordan pa a, nɛ a ya bua a he nya ekohu ngɛ Yezreel kɔ̃ ɔ mi.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ mumi ɔ ba Gideon nɔ, nɛ e kpa titimati kɛ tsɛ Abiezer bi ɔmɛ ke a ba piɛ e he.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: E tsɔ ya kpee Manase bi ɔmɛ; nɛ mɛ hu a ba piɛ e he. Jehanɛ, e tsɔ ya kpee Asher, Zebulun, kɛ Naftali wɛtso ɔmɛ; nɛ mɛ hu a ba piɛ e he.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: lɛɛ o nɛ, i kɛ jijɔ he womi maa fɔ si ngɛ ngma mi sami he ɔ. Ke bɔ́ nɛ, nɛ to he womi ɔ pɛ pɔ, se zugba a tsuo lɛɛ e gbli ɔ, lɔ ɔ i kɛ maa le kaa o maa gu ye nɔ kɛ he Israel yi wami niinɛ kaa bɔ nɛ o de ɔ.”

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Nɛ e ba mi ja niinɛ. E nɔ jena mɔtu kpla be nɛ Gideon te si nɛ e nga to he womi ɔ mi ɔ, nyu nɛ je mi ɔ hyi tsimi kake.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Gideon de Mawu ke, “O mi mi nɛ ko fu mi; ha ma tu munyu si kake nɛ ɔ pɛ! I kpa mo pɛɛ, ha ma ngɔ to he womi nɛ ɔ kɛ kpa nɔ́ si si kake nɛ ɔ pɛ! Jehanɛ lɛɛ i kpa mo pɛɛ, ha nɛ bɔ́ nɛ nɛ ngɛ zugba a tsuo nɔ, konɛ to he womi ɔ pɛ lɛɛ e gbli.”

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mawu ha e ba mi ja; jamɛ a nyɔ mi ɔ, bɔ́ nɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ tsuo, se to he womi ɔ pɛ nɛ lɛɛ e gbli.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Yerubaal nɛ ji Gideon, kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo te si mɔtu kpla, nɛ a ya bua a he nya ngɛ Harod nyu vu ɔ nya. Midian ta a ngɛ omleyi je ha mɛ ngɛ More yo ɔ kasa nya, ngɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Gideon ke, “Ta nɛ nyɛɛ o se ɔ, a he hiɛ tsɔ. Ke i ngɔ Midian ngɔ wo a dɛ mi ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ ma wo a he nɔ, nɛ a ma de ke mɛ nitsɛmɛ a kɔni si wami lɛ a kɛ he a yi wami.

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ha nɛ ma a tsuo nɛ nu kaa, ‘Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ngɛ gbeye yee nɛ e he ngɛ doe ɔ, e kpale kɛ ho we mi ya.’ ” Benɛ Gideon ka mɛ ɔ, nimli akpe nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enyɔ kpale a se; nɛ e piɛ nimli akpe nyɔngma.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Ke o ngɛ gbeye yee kaa mo nɔ kake too o maa ya a, lɛɛ o kɛ o tsɔlɔ Pura nɛ ya,

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Gideon ke, “Ma nɛ piɛ ɔ, mɛ hu a he hiɛ tsɔ. Ngɔɔ mɛ kɛ kple si kɛ ya pa a nya, nɛ imi nitsɛ ma ka mɛ ha mo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Ke i de mo ke, ‘O kɛ nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ nɛ ya’ a, o kɛ lɛ nɛ ya; se ke i de mo ke, ‘O kɛ nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ ko ya’ a, o kɛ lɛ ko ya.”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Gideon kɛ ma a kple si kɛ ho pa a nya ya; nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Nihi tsuo nɛ a kɛ a lilɛ maa nu nyu ɔ kaa gbe nuɔ nyu ɔ, ngɔɔ mɛ kɛ da he kake, konɛ o ngɔ ni nɛmɛ nɛ mɛɛ a kpla si ngɛ a nakutso nya kɛ nu nyu ɔ hu ngɔ da he kake.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Gideon ke, “Ma ngɔ nyumuhi lafa etɛ ɔmɛ nɛ nu nyu ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ gbe nuɔ nyu ɔ kɛ he nyɛ yi wami, nɛ ma ngɔ Midian bi ɔmɛ kɛ wo a dɛ mi. Ma a nɛ piɛ ɔ, ha nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ho e we mi ya.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, Yawɛ de Gideon ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya tua he nyɛli ɔmɛ a ta a esɔesɔ; ejakaa i ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo o dɛ mi!

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: nɛ o ya bu a ní sɛɛmi ɔ tue. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, o ma na kã ko kɛ kple si kɛ ya tua ta a.” Gideon kɛ e tsɔlɔ Pura kple si kɛ ho he nyɛli ɔmɛ a ta a nya ya haa.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Midian bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ, kɛ ma amɛ nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ pueɔ si ngɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi babauu kaa baalɛhi. A we afukpɔngɔ ɔmɛ ɔ, nɔ ko li a nya; a he hiɛ babauu kaa wo nya zia.
