english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Dan bi ɔmɛ hla nyumuhi katsɛmɛ enuɔ kɛ je a wɛtso ɔ mi, nɛ a tsɔ mɛ kɛ je Zora kɛ Eshtaol nɛ a ya slaa zugba a. Benɛ a su Efraim yo ɔ nɔ ɔ, a ya to Mika we ɔ mi.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Benɛ a ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, a yɔse Levi no niheyo ɔ munyu tutui, nɛ a ya bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni o ngɛ pee ngɛ hiɛ ɔ? Mɛnɔ ngɔ mo kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: E de mɛ ke, “I kɛ Mika so somi ko; e bɔ mi apaa, nɛ i ngɛ osɔfo yee ha lɛ.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: A de lɛ ke, “Wa kpa mo pɛɛ, mo bi Mawu ha wɔ kaa blɔ nɛ wa hia nɛ ɔ maa pee jɔjɔɛ ha wɔ lo.”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Osɔfo ɔ de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ya kɛ manye! Yawɛ maa bu nyɛ he ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ nyumu ni enuɔ ɔmɛ je lejɛ ɔ, nɛ a pue nɔ kɛ ho Laish ya. A na kaa lejɛ ɔ ma a mi bi ɔmɛ a he mi jɔ mɛ kaa Sidon bi ɔmɛ. A ngɛ kpoo nɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko pue we a tsui nɔ; a ngɛ níhi babauu, nɛ je nɛ ɔ mi nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko hia we mɛ. Jehanɛ se hu, a kɛ Sidon bi ɔmɛ a he kɛ, nɛ a kɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko bɔɛ.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Benɛ a kpale kɛ ba a nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a ngɔ ngɛ Zora kɛ Eshtaol ɔ, a nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ bi mɛ ke, “Kɛ nyɛ ya na lejɛ ɔ kɛɛ?”

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ ya a, nyɛ maa na zugba agbo ko kɛ e mi nimli nɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko pee we mɛ kɔmɔ. Niinɛ, zugba, he nɛ je nɛ ɔ mi nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko hia we ngɛ ɔ, jamɛ a zugba a ji zugba nɛ Mawu ngɔ kɛ wo nyɛ dɛ mi nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ nyumuhi lafa ekpa nɛ je Dan bi ɔmɛ a wɛtso ɔ mi ɔ kpla gbaja, nɛ a dla a he kɛ ta hwumi níhi. A hia kɛ je Zora kɛ Eshtaol,

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: nɛ a ya bua a he nya ngɛ Kiriat Yearim, ngɛ Yuda. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ, biɛ nɛ a kɛ tsɛɛ lejɛ ɔ ji Mahane Dan. E ngɛ Kiriat Yearim bonyoku je.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Nɛ́ a je lejɛ ɔ, a nyɛɛ kɛ ya si a ya pã si ngɛ Mika we ɔ mi, ngɛ Efraim yo ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ nyumu ni enuɔ ɔmɛ nɛ ya slaa Laish zugba a de a nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke, “Anɛ nyɛ le kaa efɔd, kɛ amaga nɛ a kpɛ́, kɛ amaga nɛ a hlɔ nɛ a kɛ sika hiɔ ha he ngɛ we ɔ kake mi lo? Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ hyɛ bɔ nɛ nyɛ maa pee ha!”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: A de lɛ ke, “Ma o nya, nɛ o pee dii! Ba nɛ waa ho, nɛ o ya pee wa tsɛ kɛ wa osɔfo. Anɛ o suɔ kaa o maa ye osɔfo ngɛ nɔmlɔ kake we mi, pe kaa o maa ye osɔfo ha wɛtso mluku ngɛ Israel lo?”

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a tsa a blɔ hiami ɔ nɔ; a ngɔ a bimɛ tsɔwitsɔwi ɔmɛ, a we mi lohwe ɔmɛ, kɛ a tlomi ɔmɛ kɛ sɛ hlami.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Benɛ Dan bi ɔmɛ je, nɛ a kɛ Mika we ɔ he kɛ saii ɔ, Mika ya bua e huza nɔ bi ɔmɛ a nya, nɛ e kɛ mɛ nyɛɛ Dan bi ɔmɛ a se.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Benɛ a ya na mɛ ɔ, a kpa ngmlaa kɛ tsɛ Dan bi ɔmɛ a yi se. Nɛ mɛ hu a plɛ, nɛ a bi Mika ke, “Mɛni ngɛ mo pee? Jije o kɛ nimli kpekpemi nɛ ɔmɛ yaa?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: E he nɔ ke, “Nyɛ ba ngɔ ye osɔfo ɔ, kɛ amagahi nɛ i pee ɔ, nɛ nyɛ je kɛ yaa! Mɛni piɛ ha mi? Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ngɔ nyɛ nya nɛ nyɛ kpale ngɛ mi bie ke, ‘Mɛni ngɛ mo pee?’ ”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Dan bi ɔmɛ de lɛ ke, “Ke o hla we nɛ nimli nɛ ɔmɛ a muklii mi nɛ fu, nɛ a kpata o kɛ o we bi ɔmɛ tsuo nyɛ hɛ mi ɔ, lɛɛ moo pee kɔ̃.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Dan bi ɔmɛ tsa a nyɛɛmi ɔ nɔ. Benɛ Mika na kaa a he wa pe lɛ ɔ, e kpale e se kɛ ho we mi ya.

english_verse: The tribe of Dan took Micah's priest and the things Micah had made, and headed for Laish, which was located in a valley controlled by the town of Beth-Rehob. Laish was defenseless, because it had no walls and was too far from Sidon for the Sidonians to help defend it. The leaders of Laish had not even asked nearby towns to help them in case of an attack. The warriors from Dan made a surprise attack on Laish, killing everyone and burning it down. Then they rebuilt the town and settled there themselves.
translation_verse: Benɛ Dan bi ɔmɛ a nine su ní ɔmɛ nɛ Mika pee ɔ, kɛ e osɔfo ɔ a nɔ ɔ, a ho nɛ a ya tua Laish ma kɛ e mi bi kpoo nɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko pue we a tsui nɔ ɔ ngɛ Bet Rehob bi ɔmɛ a kɔ̃ ɔ mi. A kɛ klaate gbe ma a mi bi ɔmɛ, nɛ a mɛ ma a he la. Nɔ ko nɔ ko ji ngmlaa ha mɛ, ejakaa Laish kɛ Sidon he kɛ, nɛ jehanɛ hu, a kɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be bɔmi. Dan bi ɔmɛ dla po ma a, nɛ a hi lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: A kɛ a tsɛ Dan, Yakob binyumu ɔ biɛ wo ma a; jinɛ sa a, a tsɛɛ ma a ke Laish.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɛ Israel na we matsɛ lolo ɔ, Levi no ko ya to nubwɔ ngɛ Efraim yo ɔmɛ a nɔ tsitsaa lokoo; nɛ e ya su yo ko ngɛ Betlehem Yuda.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: E ba mi kaa e plã yo ɔ mi mi fu lɛ, nɛ e tu fo kɛ ho e tsɛ we ya ngɛ Betlehem Yuda, nɛ e ya hi lejɛ ɔ nyɔhiɔ eywiɛ.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, e huno ɔ bu e nɔ konɛ e kɛ lɛ ya tu ngɛ he jɔmi mi, nɛ e kpale kɛ ba. E kɛ e tsɔlɔ ɔ, kɛ teji enyɔ ho. Benɛ e ba su yo ɔ tsɛ we ɔ mi ɔ, yo ɔ tsɛ ɔ na lɛ, nɛ e kɛ bua jɔmi ba kpee lɛ.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: E ngatsɛ ɔ tsi e nya, nɛ e ye ligbi etɛ ngɛ e ngɔ. A ye ní, nɛ a nu dã, nɛ a hwɔ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji eywiɛ ɔ, a te si mɔtu kpla nɛ a dla konɛ a pue blɔ, se yo ɔ tsɛ ɔ de e ngatsɛ ɔ ke, “Moo mlɛ nɛ o wo o nya mi nɔ́ ko loko o ho.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ nyumu ni enyɔ ɔmɛ hi si nɛ a ye ní, nɛ a nu dã; nɛ yo ɔ tsɛ ɔ de nyumu ɔ ke, “Moo hwɔ hiɛ ɔ gbɔkuɛ nɛ ɔ hulɔ, nɛ o na bua jɔmi.”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Benɛ Levi no ɔ te si nɛ e maa je ɔ, e ngatsɛ ɔ hɛɛ mi hluu nɛ e tsi e nya nɛ e hwɔ lejɛ ɔ ekohu.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji enuɔ ɔ, e te si mɔtu kpla konɛ e hia blɔ ɔ. Se yo ɔ tsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Moo wo o nya mi nɔ́ ko, nɛ o mlɛ kɛ yaa si gbɔkuɛ.” Nɛ mɛ ni enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo a ye ní.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Benɛ nyumu ɔ, kɛ e plã a, kɛ e tsɔlɔ ɔ dla nɛ a maa ho ɔ, e ngatsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Hyɛ, du bu ta; nyɛɛ hwɔ hiɛ ɔ! O nɛ, je jɔ; nyɛɛ hwɔ hiɛ ɔ kɛ yaa si je maa na, nɛ o bua nɛ jɔ o he; konɛ nyɛɛ te si hwɔɔ mɔtu mla, nɛ nyɛ pue nɔ kɛ ho o ma a mi ya.”

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Se nyumu ɔ kplɛɛ we kaa e maa hwɔ lejɛ ɔ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ. E kɛ e plã a, e tsɔlɔ ɔ, kɛ teji enyɔ ɔmɛ nɛ a wo a nɔ ní ɔ pue nɔ kɛ ya si a ya su Yebus hanɔ.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Benɛ a su Yebus ta a, du bu, nɛ tsɔlɔ ɔ de e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ke, “Ha wa gba Yebus bi ɔmɛ a ma a mi, nɛ wa ya hwɔ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Se e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Wa be ni komɛ nɛ pi Israel bi ji mɛ a ma mi gbae, se mohu wa maa po mi kɛ ya Gibea.

english_verse: or maybe we can even reach Ramah before dark.”
translation_verse: Ha waa nyɛɛ kɛ ya wa hɛ mi bɔɔ, nɛ wa ya hwɔ Gibea, loo Rama.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a tsa nɔ kɛ ho. Benɛ e piɛ bɔɔ nɛ a maa su Gibea ngɛ Benyamin zugba a nɔ ɔ, pu nɔ si.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a gba konɛ a ya hwɔ Gibea. A ya to si ngɛ magbɛ nɔ; ejakaa nɔ ko nɔ ko ba ngɔɛ mɛ kɛ yɛ e we mi nɛ a ya to lɛ.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Gbɔkuɛ ɔ, nɔmoyo ko ji nɛ ɔ nɛ je ngmɔ nɔ kɛ ma. Nyumu nɛ ɔ, Efraim yo ɔmɛ a nɔ nɛ e je kɛ ba to nubwɔ ngɛ Gibea, ngɛ Benyamin bi a kpɛti.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Benɛ nɔmoyo ɔ na blɔ hialɔ ɔ ngɛ magbɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ, e bi lɛ ke, “Jije o je? Nɛ jije o yaa?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Levi no ɔ de lɛ ke, “Wa ba be kɛ ho Betlehem Yuda ya, nɛ wa kpale kɛ yaa we ngɛ Efraim yo ɔmɛ a nɔ tsitsaa lokoo, se nɔ ko nɔ ko ngɔɛ wɔ kɛ yɛ e we mi.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Wa ngɛ nga, kɛ niye ní ha wa teji ɔmɛ. Jehanɛ hu, wa hɛɛ niye ní, kɛ wai kɛ ha imi nitsɛ kɛ o mawayo ɔ, kɛ niheyo ɔ nɛ kɛ o tsɔli ɔmɛ nyɛɛ ɔ; nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko hia we wɔ.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Nɔmoyo ɔ de ke, “Nyɛ hee! Mawu nɛ gbaa nyɛ! Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ maa hia nyɛ ɔ, ma pee ha nyɛ; se magbɛ ɔ nɔ kɛkɛ nɛ nyɛ ko hwɔ.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: E ngɔ mɛ kɛ ho e we mi ya, nɛ e ya ha teji ɔmɛ ní. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a fɔ a nanehi a he, nɛ a ye ní, nɛ a nu dã.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Benɛ a bua jɔ a he ɔ, yakayaka nyumu komɛ nɛ ngɛ ma a mi ɔ ba bɔle we ɔ kɛ kpe. A si sinya a kɛ he wami, nɛ a de nɔmoyo ɔ nɛ ji wetsɛ ɔ ke, “Nyumu ɔ nɛ ba o we ɔ mi ɔ, je lɛ ha wɔ nɛ waa kɛ lɛ nɛ hwɔ.”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Se wetsɛ ɔ je kpo kɛ ya na mɛ, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Dɛbi! Ye nyɛmimɛ, nyɛ ko pee yayami ko nɛ ngɛ kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ! Nyumu nɛ ɔ, ye nubwɔ ji lɛ; nyɛ ko tsu kikɛmɛ a zo ní nɛ ɔ!

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Ye bi zangmayo nɛ li nyumu, kɛ nyumu ɔ hu plã ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. Ma je mɛ kpo ha nyɛ nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ mɛ kɛ ho, nɛ nyɛ ya pee mɛ bɔ nɛ nyɛ suɔ. Se nyumu nɛ ɔ lɛɛ, nyɛ ko pee lɛ zo nɔ́ ko kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Se nyumu ɔmɛ bui lɛ tue. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Levi no ɔ ya nu e plã a nɛ e tsitsɛɛ e yi se mane mɛ. A kɛ lɛ hwɔ, nɛ a pee lɛ basabasa nyɔ ɔ mi tsuo kɛ ya si mɔtu. Benɛ je mi maa ho tsɔmi ya a, a ngmɛɛ e he.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Makɛ futɛfutɛ mi ɔ, yo ɔ ba nɛ e ba tsɔ fia si ngɛ nɔmoyo ɔ sinya a nya, ngɛ we mi he nɛ e huno ɔ ngɛ ɔ; nɛ e tlɔ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ya si je mi tsɔ.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Benɛ e huno ɔ te si mɔtu nɛ e bli sinya a konɛ e je kpo nɛ e pue blɔ ɔ, e plã a ji nɛ ɔ nɛ hwɔɔ si ngɛ sinya a nya, nɛ e ninehi pueɔ si ngɛ kpoku ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: E de lɛ ke, “Tee si nɛ waa ho!” Se yo ɔ he we nɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e ngɔ lɛ ngɔ fɔ e teji ɔ nɔ, nɛ e pue nɔ kɛ ho e ma mi ya.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Benɛ e ya su e we ɔ mi ɔ, e ngɔ ha nɛ e poo e plã a mi kpɔ nya kpɔ nya nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ, nɛ e tsɔ nɛ a kɛ ya ha Israel wɛtso nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo kakaaka.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ na nɔ́ nɛ ɔ de ke, “Kɛ je ligbi ɔ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ hluu kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ ɔ eko bɛ hyɛ; nɛ a nɛ eko hu hyɛ. Nyɛ susu he; nyɛɛ wo he ga, nɛ nyɛ de nɔ́ ko!”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Levi no ɔ, nɛ ji yo nɛ a gbe ɔ e huno ɔ he nɔ nɛ e de ke, “I kɛ ye plã a ya Gibea ngɛ Benyamin zugba a nɔ nɛ wa ya hwɔ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Benɛ ye plã a gbo ɔ, i poo e mi kpɔ nya kpɔ nya, nɛ i tsɔ kɛ ya ha Israel wɛtso nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo kakaaka; ejakaa nimli nɛ ɔmɛ bɔ musu, nɛ a tsu zo ní ngɛ Israel.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ye nyɛmimɛ Israel bi, kɛ nyɛ susu kɛɛ? Mɛni wa ngɛ pee ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ he?”

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Israel wɛtso ɔmɛ tsɔ nihi kɛ ho Benyamin wɛtso ɔ tsuo ngɔ ya, nɛ a ya de mɛ kɛ, “Mɛni musu nyɛ bɔ nɛ ɔ?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Nyɛ je Gibea nyumuhi yakayaka nimli ɔmɛ ha wɔ nɛ waa gbe mɛ kɛ kpa musu ngɛ Israel.” Se Benyamin bi ɔmɛ bui a nyɛmimɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ tue.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Mohu ɔ, Benyamin bi ɔmɛ je a ma amɛ a mi kɛ ba bua a he nya ngɛ Gibea konɛ a kɛ Israel bi kpa amɛ nɛ hwu.

english_verse: The other Israelite tribes organized their army and found they had
translation_verse: Israel wɛtso kpa amɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ hu bua ta buli akpe lafa eywiɛ nya. Israel gba ta kɛ wo Benyamin

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ te si mɔtu, nɛ a ya bua a he nya ngɛ Gibea kasa nya.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: A wo za, nɛ a gba ta kɛ wo Benyamin bi ɔmɛ a he ngɛ Gibea.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Benyamin bi ɔmɛ je Gibea ma a mi ba na mɛ, nɛ a gbe Israel ta buli akpe nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enyɔ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: nɛ Finehas, Aaron binyumu Eleazar bi ɔ ji osɔfo nɛ hyɛɛ nɔ. Israel bi ɔmɛ ya bi Yawɛ ga womi ke, “Anɛ waa ya nɛ waa kɛ wa nyɛmimɛ Benyamin bi ɔmɛ ya hwu ekohu, aloo wa ko ya?” Yawɛ he nɔ ke, “Nyɛɛ ya, ejakaa hwɔɔ ɔ, ma ngɔ mɛ ngɔ wo nyɛ dɛ mi.”

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɔ ni komɛ kɛ wo ka kɛ bɔle Gibea kɛ kpe.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a gbee senyasenya ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ a tu fo kɛ gu nga a nɔ blɔ. Se ta a nyɛɛ a se, nɛ ka woli ɔmɛ nɛ je ma a mi hu kɛ mɛ ba bua; nɛ a kpata a hɛ mi.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: A sa Benyamin bi ɔmɛ a yi kɛ kpe; nɛ a nyɛɛ a se hlididiidi kɛ mɛ gbemi nɛ he jɔmi be mi, kɛ je Noha kɛ ya si Gibea hanɔ, ngɛ beleku je.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Benyamin bi nɛ a gbe jamɛ a ligbi ɔ ji akpe nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enuɔ; ta buli katsɛmɛ ji mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ya bua a he nya ngɛ Mizpa a, a ka kita ke, “Wa ti nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛ e biyo be gba hae ngɛ Benyamin.”

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ ma a ba Betel nɛ a ba hi si ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ya si gbɔkuɛ. A wo yana boboobo, nɛ a bi ke,

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: “Yawɛ, Israel Mawu, mɛni he je nɛ e ba mi kaa mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ, wɛtso kake ngɛ laae ngɛ Israel ɔ?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, ma a te si makɛ mla nɛ a ma bɔ sami la tɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ a sã sami bɔhi, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔhi.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ bi ke, “Anɛ Israel wɛtso ɔmɛ ekomɛ ngɛ nɛ mɛɛ a bɛ gua a mi ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi lo?” A ka kita agbo ke, nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ bɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi ngɛ Mizpa a, a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Benyamin bi ɔmɛ a ní pee a nyɛmimɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ mɔbɔ, nɛ a de ke, “Mwɔnɛ ɔ, a po Israel wɛtso kake ngɔ fɔ he.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Wa ka Yawɛ kita kaa waa kɛ wa biyihi be gba hae ngɛ Benyamin. Lɛɛ kɛ wa maa pee kɛ na yihi ha ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ nɛ a ngɔ?”

english_verse: Again the Israelites asked, “Did any of the tribes stay away from the meeting at Mizpah?” After asking around, they discovered that no one had come from Jabesh in Gilead.
translation_verse: ejakaa benɛ a kane ma a, a na kaa Yabesh Gilead bi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko nɔ ko be lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Ma kpekpemi ɔ tsɔ nihi kɛ ho Benyamin bi ɔmɛ a ngɔ ya ngɛ Rimon tɛ sa a nɔ, nɛ a kɛ mɛ ya kpata.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Benyamin bi ɔmɛ kpale a se kɛ ba, nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɔ yihi nɛ a he a yi wami ngɛ Yabesh Gilead yi ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ ngɔ ha mɛ; se yi ɔmɛ sui nyumu ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Benyamin bi ɔmɛ a ní pee ma a mɔbɔ, ejakaa Yawɛ kɛ mi gbami ba Israel wɛtso ɔmɛ a kpɛti.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nimeli nɛ ngɛ gua a mi ɔ de ke, “Nɛ a kpata Benyamin yi ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a hɛ mi nɛ ɔ nɛɛ, kɛ wa maa pee kɛɛ nɛ wa ma na yihi ha nyumu ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ nɛ a ngɔ?”

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Se wɔɔ lɛɛ wa be nyɛe nɛ waa kɛ wa biyihi ma ha mɛ gba; ejakaa Israel ma a ka kita nɛ a de ke, ‘Nɔ nɛ maa ngɔ yo ko kɛ ha gba ngɛ Benyamin ɔ, a maa gbiɛ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a kai kaa daa jeha a, a yeɔ Yawɛ nyami ligbi ko ngɛ Shilo nɛ ngɛ Lebona kɛ Betel a kpɛti ɔ, ngɛ gbɛjegbɛ ɔ nɛ je Betel kɛ yaa Shekem ɔ beleku je ɔ.

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Nɛ a de Benyamin bi ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya wo ka ngɛ wai ngmɔ ɔmɛ a mi, nɛ nyɛɛ huɔ.

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: Ke nyami ligbi ɔ su, nɛ Shilo zangmawi ɔmɛ ba nɛ a ba ngɛ doe ɔ, nyɛɛ je wai ngmɔ ɔmɛ a mi kɛ ba. Ke nyɛ ba a, nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ nu Shilo zangmayo kake pani nya, nɛ e ngɔ lɛ kɛ ya Benyamin zugba a nɔ, nɛ e ya pee e yo.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Ke a tsɛmɛ, loo a nyɛminyumuhi ba nɛ a ba bi wɔ sane ko ɔ, wa ma de mɛ ke, ‘Nyɛɛ na wɔ mɔbɔ, nɛ nyɛɛ ngmɛɛ a he ha wɔ kɛkɛ; ejakaa wa na we yihi kɛ ha a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ benɛ wa kpata Yabesh Gilead hɛ mi ngɛ ta a mi ɔ. Jehanɛ se hu, akɛnɛ pi nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nɛ nyɛ ngɔ zangmawi ɔmɛ ngɔ ha mɛ he je ɔ, nyɛ yi fɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Benyamin bi ɔmɛ pee ja. A nuu yiwi ɔmɛ nɛ ba ngɛ doe ɔ kakaaka, nɛ a ngɔ mɛ kɛ ho. Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, a kpale kɛ ho mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɔ ya; nɛ a ya dla po ma amɛ, nɛ a hi a mi.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, matsɛ ko matsɛ ko be Israel, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ e suɔ.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Manyadali ɔmɛ a yi nɔ, benɛ matsɛmɛ na we nɛ a bɔni Israel ma a nɔ yemi lolo ɔ, hwɔ ba zugba a nɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyumu ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Elimelek, nɛ je Efrat weku ɔ mi, kɛ e yo Naomi, kɛ a bimɛ nihewi enyɔ, Malon kɛ Kilion, hia kɛ je Betlehem ngɛ Yuda zugba a nɔ kɛ ya to nubwɔ ngɛ Moab zugba a nɔ. Benɛ a ngɛ lejɛ ɔ,

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Elimelek ba gbo, nɛ e piɛ e yo Naomi kɛ e binyumu enyɔ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Elimelek binyumu ɔmɛ ngɔ Moab yihi: nɔ kake biɛ ji Orpa, nɛ nɔ kake hu biɛ ji Rut. Benɛ a hi lejɛ ɔ maa pee jeha nyɔngma se ɔ,

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Naomi de e nganyɛmɛ enyɔ ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ kpale nyɛ se nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ho e nyɛ ngɔ ya. I kpa Yawɛ pɛɛ nɛ e na nyɛ mɔbɔ ngɛ si himi kpakpa nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ mi, kɛ nihi nɛ si wɔ ɔ hi ɔ he.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Yawɛ nɛ ha nɛ nyɛɛ gba ekohu, konɛ nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ na he ko nɛ e hi.” Benɛ e fua mɛ nɛ e kɛ mɛ ye sɛ ɔ, a wo yana,

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: nɛ a de ke, “Dɛbi! Waa kɛ mo maa ya o weku li ɔmɛ a ngɔ.”

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Se Naomi de mɛ ke, “Ye bimɛ, nyɛɛ kpale nyɛ se! Mɛni he je nyɛɛ kɛ mi maa yaa? Nyɛ susu kaa ma nyɛ ma fɔ binyumuhi ekohu ha nyɛ nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ mɛ nɛ hi si lo?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ kpale nyɛ se, ejakaa i be gba si himi nya. Nɛ ke kaa i kɛ nyumu ko bua nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi nɛ i fɔ binyumuwi po,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: anɛ enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, nyɛ maa tsi nyɛ he nya nɛ nyɛ be gbae; nɛ nyɛ maa mlɛ kɛ yaa si be nɛ a maa wa lo? Dɛbi, ye bimɛ, nyɛ le kaa nɔ́ nɛ ɔ be mi bae; ejakaa sane nɛ Yawɛ kɛ mi ye ɔ nya wa; se nyɛɛ lɛɛ nyɛ ní peeɔ mi mɔbɔ.”

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Naomi de lɛ ke, “O nɛ, o hunongua yo ɔ kpale e se kɛ ho e weku li kɛ e mawu ɔmɛ a ngɔ ya. Mo hu, kpale o se nɛ o kɛ lɛ nɛ ho!”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Se Rut ha lɛ heto ke, “Mo ko nyɛ ye nɔ doo ke ma si mo; ha nɛ waa ho kɛkɛ. He tsuaa he nɛ o yaa a, ma ya; nɛ he tsuaa he nɛ o maa hi ɔ, lejɛ ɔ ma hi. O je kɛ wɛ maa pee imi hu ye je kɛ wɛ, nɛ o Mawu maa pee ye Mawu.

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: He nɛ o ma gbo ngɛ ɔ, lejɛ ɔ ma gbo ngɛ, nɛ lejɛ ɔ nɔuu a maa pu mi ngɛ. Ja gbenɔ pɛ lɛ ma ha nɛ ma si mo; ke pi ja lɛɛ Yawɛ kɛ mi nɛ ye sisiisi.”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Benɛ Naomi na kaa Rut muɔ e yi mi kpɔ kaa e kɛ lɛ maa ya a, e de we nɔ́ ko hu.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ mɛ ni enyɔ ɔmɛ a tsa nyɛɛmi ɔ nɔ kɛ ya si a ya su Betlehem. Benɛ a su Betlehem ɔ, ma a tsuo hoso, nɛ yi ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ gbafa bi ke, “Naomi ɔ ji nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Nɛ e he nɔ nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ ko tsɛ mi Naomi hu, se mohu nyɛ tsɛ mi Mara, ejakaa Ope ɔ kɛ mi ye sane nɛ dooɔ tsɔ.

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Ye he su kɛ je hiɛ ɔ kɛ ho, se Yawɛ kpale mi kɛ ba dɛ gu. Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ nyɛ tsɛɔ mi Naomi, be mi nɛ Ope ɔ te si wo mi, nɛ e ha i na nɔ kikɛ nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: One day, Ruth said to Naomi, “Let me see if I can find someone who will let me pick up the grain left in the fields by the harvest workers.” Naomi answered, “Go ahead, my daughter.” So immediately Ruth went out to pick up grain in a field. She didn't know it was owned by Boaz, a relative of Naomi's husband Elimelech, as well as a rich and important man.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Rut ho ngma ngmɔ ɔmɛ a mi ya nɛ e ya nyɛɛ ní kpali ɔmɛ a se kɛ kukuɔ bibliwi ɔmɛ. He ní a nya a, e ya je Boaz, nɛ je Elimelek weku ɔ mi ɔ e ngmɔ mi.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Saii mi ɔ, Boaz nitsɛ je ma a mi kɛ ba. E ha ní kpali ɔmɛ ayekoo, nɛ mɛ hu a he nɔ ke, “Aayee.”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Boaz bi e tsɔlɔ ɔ nɛ ji ní kpali ɔmɛ a nyatsɛ ɔ ke, “Jije zangmayo nɛ ɔ je?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ he nɔ ke, “Lɛ ji Moab yo nubwɔ ɔ nɛ e kɛ Naomi je Moab zugba a nɔ kɛ ba a nɛ.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: E bi ke ma ngmɛ lɛ blɔ nɛ e kukuɔ ngma bibliwi ngɛ ní kpali ɔmɛ a se. E bɔni ní tsumi kɛ je mɔtu kpla nɛ he jɔɔmi be mi, nɛ kpaako e kpa nɛ e yaa jɔɔ e he bɔɔ ngɛ gba a sisi.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Boaz de Rut ke, “Ye bi, o ngɛ tue bue? Ko ya kukuɔ ngma bibliwi ngɛ nɔ kpa ko ngmɔ mi pe hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ pɛ. Moo nyɛɛ yihewi ní tsuli ɔmɛ a se bɛbɛɛbɛ;

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: moo hyɛ he nɛ nyumu ɔmɛ ngɛ ngma a poe ngɛ ɔ, konɛ o nyɛɛ yihewi ní kpali ɔmɛ a se. I wo nihewi ɔmɛ si ke a ko doo o nya. Ke kuma ngɛ mo yee ɔ, yaa buɛ ɔmɛ a he nɛ o ya nu nyu nɛ nihewi ɔmɛ yɛ ɔ eko.”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Boaz he nɔ ke, “Níhi nɛ o pee ha o nganyɛ ngɛ o huno gbenɔ se ɔ, a bɔ mi lɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ; nɛ jehanɛ ɔ, o si o tsɛ kɛ o nyɛ, kɛ o ma kɛ ba je nihi nɛ o li mɛ a kpɛti.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ Israel Mawu ɔ, nɔ ngɔ nɛ o ba sa we ngɛ ɔ, lɛ nitsɛ nɛ e wo mo níhi nɛ o pee ɔ kulaa he hiɔ.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Rut he nɔ ke, “I naa mo si, ye nyɔmtsɛ. Hyɛ bɔ nɛ o munyu ngɔngɔɛ ɔmɛ wo mi gɛjɛmi, nɛ ye nɔ gbagba te ha, pohu tsa pi o mawayi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake ji mi.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Benɛ ní yemi be su ɔ, Boaz de Rut ke, “Hɛɛ mo kɛ ba nɛ o ba ngɔ abolo ɔ eko nɛ o kɛ sɔ flɔɔ ɔ mi.” Nɛ e ba nɛ e ba hi si ngɛ ní kpali ɔmɛ a kasa nya. Boaz ha lɛ ngma a nɛ a sí ɔ eko nɛ e ye kɛ ya si eko piɛ nɛ́ e nyɛ we yemi hu.

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Kikɛ nɛ ɔ Rut pee kɛ kukuɔ ngma bibliwi ngɛ ngmɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ ya si du bu. Nɛ benɛ e kɛ tso gbee nɔ́ nɛ e kukuɔ ɔ, e ná ngma maa pee kilo nyɔngma.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Rut tloo ngma a kɛ ho ma a mi ya, nɛ e kɛ ya tsɔɔ e nganyɛ ɔ kaa nɔ́ nɛ e nyɛ bua nya ji lɔ ɔ nɛ. E kɛ ní ɔ nɛ e ye piɛ ɔ hu ha lɛ.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Naomi bi Rut ke, “Jije o ya bua ngma fuu nɛ ɔ nya ngɛ? Mawu maa gbaa nɔmlɔ nɛ tsɔ e hɛ mi ha mo kikɛ nɛ ɔ.” Rut de e nganyɛ ɔ ke ngmɔ si he nɛ e ya tsu ní ngɛ ɔ, a tsɛɛ ngmɔtsɛ ɔ ke Boaz.

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Naomi de ke, “Yawɛ nɛ yeɔ e siwo nɔ kɛ haa hɛ kali, kɛ nihi nɛ gbo tsuo ɔ maa gbaa lɛ.” E ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Boaz nɛ ɔ, wa weku no pɔtɛɛ ji lɛ, nɛ kusumi nya hu e peeɔ wa nɔ hyɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Rut, Moab yo ɔ ya nɔ nɛ e de e nganyɛ ɔ ke, “Nɔ́ kake hu nɛ nyumu ɔ de ji kaa ma hi ní ɔ kukuɔe ngɛ ní tsuli ɔmɛ a se kɛ yaa si a ma kpa e ngma a tsuo gbe nya.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Naomi de e nganyɛ Rut ke, “Ye bi, e hi kaa o kɛ yihewi ɔmɛ ma tsu ní ngɛ Boaz ngmɔ mi pe kaa o maa ya nɔ kpa ko ngmɔ mi nɛ a ya doo o nya.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Rut pee ja, nɛ daa nɛ ɔ, e ya kukuɔɔ ngma bibliwi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ya si be nɛ a poo ngma slɔɔto ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ gbe nya. Nɛ e tsa nɔ nɛ e kɛ e nganyɛ ɔ hi si.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Be ko se ɔ, Naomi de Rut ke, “Ye bi, tse i ko hla gba ha mo konɛ níhi a mi nɛ e hi ha mo?

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Kaa bɔ nɛ o le ɔ, Boaz nɛ o kɛ e mawayi ɔmɛya kukuɔ ní ɔ, wa weku no ji lɛ. Gbɔkuɛ nɛ ɔ, e ma ya sa e ngma a mi.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Moo bu tue! Moo du o he, nɛ o kpa nu, nɛ o bu bo, nɛ o pue nɔ kɛ ya ngma mi sami he ɔ. Mo ko je o he si ha lɛ kɛ yaa si be nɛ e maa ye ní gbe nya nɛ e maa hwɔ si.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Bɔɔ mɔde nɛ o to he nɛ e maa hwɔ ɔ he hɛ, konɛ ke e ya hwɔ si ɔ, o ya nɛ o ya kpa bo ngɛ e nane he ngɛ kusumi nya, nɛ o hwɔ lejɛ ɔ; nɛ e maa tsɔɔ mo nɔ́ nɛ o pee.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Rut pue nɔ kɛ ho ngma mi sami he ɔ ya, nɛ e ya pee bɔ nɛ e nganyɛ ɔ de lɛ ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Benɛ Boaz ye ní nɛ e nu nɔ́ ko, nɛ e bua jɔ e he ɔ, e ho nɛ e ya hwɔ si ngɛ ngma nɛ a bua nya a kasa nya. Rut pee blɛuu nɛ e ya kpa bo ngɛ e nane he, nɛ e hwɔ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Kɛ yaa nyɔ mi kpɛti ɔ, Boaz hɛli si, nɛ benɛ e plɛ e he ɔ, e pee lɛ nyakpɛ kaa yo ko hwɔɔ si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: E bi ke, “Mo mɛnɔ?” Nɛ Rut he nɔ ke, “Imi Rut, o mawayo ɔ. Akɛnɛ o weku no yalɔyo ji mi he je ɔ, e ji o blɔ nya kaa o kɛ o bo ɔ haa ye nɔ ngɛ kusumi nya kɛ tsɔɔ kaa o maa ngɔ mi.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Nɛ Boaz de lɛ ke, “Yawɛ maa gbaa mo, ye bi, kaa o kɛ nɔ́ nɛ o pee nɛ ɔ tsɔɔ weku no kpakpa peemi he okadi pe níhi kulaa nɛ o pee ha o nganyɛ ɔ po, kaa o ya nyɛɛ we nihewi ohiatsɛmɛ, loo niatsɛmɛ a se.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: E ngɛ mi niinɛ kaa ngɛ kusumi nya a, i ngɛ he blɔ nɛ i ngɔɔ mo nɛ i hyɛɛ o nɔ lɛɛ, se kɛ̃ ɔ nɔ ko pa ngɛ blɔ nya pe imi.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, moo hi hiɛ ɔ kɛ yaa si mɔtu; nɛ ke nyumu nɛ ɔ kplɛɛ nɛ e pee kusumi ɔ, nɛ e ngɔ mo ɔ, kɛkɛ lɛɛ saminya. Se ke e kplɛɛ we ɔ, lɛɛ i ngɛ si woe ngɛ Mawu hɛ kalɔ ɔ biɛ mi kaa ma ngɔ mo. Moo hwɔ si ngɛ hiɛ ɔ kɛ yaa si je maa na.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e hwɔ Boaz nane si blɔ kɛ ya si mɔtu. Nɛ́ nɔ ko kó le kaa yo ko ba lejɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Rut te si loko je mi tsɔ.

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Boaz de lɛ ke, “Mo je o nɔ hami bo ɔ nɛ o bli mi.” Nɛ benɛ e pee ja a, Boaz ka ngma kilo nyingmi enyɔ nya kɛ wo mi, nɛ e ngɔ tloo lɛ, nɛ e kɛ tlomi ɔ kpale e se kɛ ho ma a mi ya.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: E ya nɔ nɛ e de lɛ ke, “E ke ma ko kpale dɛ gu kɛ ba ye nganyɛ ngɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, moo hyɛ ngma sɔuu nɛ e ha mi!”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Naomi de lɛ ke, “Moo to o tsui si, ye bi, kɛ yaa si o maa na sane nɛ ɔ nya; ejakaa ja Boaz gbe sane nɛ ɔ nya mwɔnɛ ɔ loko e maa jɔɔ e he.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Boaz ho ya hi si ngɛ kpe he ɔ ngɛ ma a agbo ɔ nya. Kɛkɛ nɛ e na Elimelek weku no ɔ nɛ e tu e he munyu ɔ nɛ bee. Boaz tsɛ lɛ nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ye huɛ, ba nɛ o ba hi si ngɛ hiɛ ɔ.” E ba nɛ e ba hi si.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Boaz tsɛ ma a mi nimeli ɔmɛ a ti nihi nyɔngma ke a ba hi si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ; nɛ mɛ hu a ba hi si.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Boaz de Elimelek weku no ɔ ke, “Nɛ Naomi kpale e se kɛ je Moab kɛ ba nɛ ɔ, e ngɛ hlae nɛ e jua zugba kpɔ ɔ nɛ ji wa nyɛmi Elimelek zugba a,

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: nɛ i susu kaa ma wo o tue nɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke o suɔ ɔ, kpɔ ngɛ nihi nɛ hii si ngɛ hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ a hɛ mi. Se ke o sume ɔ, de mi; ejakaa nɔ ko be he blɔ nɛ e kpɔɔ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ kaa ja mo, nɛ o se loko imi.” Nyumu ɔ de lɛ ke, “Ma kpɔ.”

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Boaz de lɛ ke, “Saminya! Ke o he zugba a ngɛ Naomi dɛ ɔ, ja o ngɔ Rut, Moab yo yalɔyo ɔ hulɔ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ o kɛ lɛ nɛ fɔ bimɛ, konɛ nɔ nɛ be je mi ɔ biɛ nɛ hi e gbosi ní ɔ he.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Elimelek weku no ɔ de lɛ ke, “Ke ja a lɛɛ i be zugba a kpɔe mɔ; ejakaa ke i pee ja a, imi nitsɛ ye nina a maa je mi dɛ gu. Lɛɛ mo kpɔ zugba a mɔ, ejakaa imi nitsɛ i be suɔe.”

english_verse: To make a sale legal in those days, one person would take off a sandal and give it to the other.
translation_verse: Blema a, kusumi ko nɛ Israel bi peeɔ kɛ maa weto ní kpɔmi kɛ tsakemi nɔ mi ji kaa nɔtsɛ ɔ ma je e tokota kɛ ha helɔ ɔ. Enɛ ɔ a kɛ yeɔ odase ngɛ Israel.

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, benɛ Elimelek weku no ɔ de lɛ ke, “Mo nitsɛ mo he” ɔ, e je e tokota a kɛ ha Boaz.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Boaz de ma nimeli ɔmɛ, kɛ ni ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ kpe ɔ ke, “I tsɛ nyɛ odase kaa mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, Elimelek nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ Naomi dɛ, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ji Kilion kɛ Malon a níhi ɔ, i he lɛ tsuo ngɛ Naomi dɛ.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ se ɔ, Rut, Moab yo ɔ, nɛ ji Malon yalɔyo ɔ, ba peeɔ ye yo. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, gbosi ní ɔ hu maa hi Malon weku ɔ dɛ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Elimelek biɛ ko laa ngɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti ngɛ e ma a mi. Nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ na mwɔnɛ ɔ, nyɛ ma nyɛ maa ye he odase hwɔɔ se.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ma a mi bi ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, kɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ de ke, “Wa kplɛɛ nɔ, Yawɛ nɛ ha yo nɛ ɔ ba pee kaa Rahel kɛ Lea nɛ a fɔ bimɛ fuu kɛ ha Yakob ɔ. Yawɛ nɛ pee mo niatsɛ ngɛ Efrat, nɛ o biɛ nɛ pɛ ngɛ Betlehem.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Ngmɛduhi nɛ Yawɛ ma ha mo kɛ gu yo nɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ, a ha nɛ o we ɔ hɛ mi nɛ ba nyami kaa Yuda kɛ Tamar a bi Perez we ɔ.” Boaz nina

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Nɛ huza a nɔ yi ɔmɛ de Naomi ke, “Nyɛ ha wa je Yawɛ yi kaa e ha mo bibi mwɔnɛ ɔ nɛ e ba ye o se. Yawɛ nɛ ha nɛ e na biɛ kpakpa ngɛ Israel.

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: O nganyɛ ɔ suɔ mo, nɛ e he jua wa ha mo pe binyumuwi kpaago. Jehanɛ lɛɛ e ha mo bibi, nɔ nɛ ma ha mo he wami he, nɛ e maa hyɛ o nɔ ngɛ o bwɔmi si.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Naomi wo jokuɛ ɔ kaa lɛ nitsɛ e bi nɛ e hyɛ lɛ.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Nɛ huza a nɔ yi ɔmɛ de ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ Naomi na binyumu.” A wo jokuɛyo ɔ biɛ ke Obed. Pee se ɔ, Obed fɔ binyumu, nɛ a wo lɛ biɛ ke Ishai. Ishai nɛ ɔ ji David tsɛ. David weku kpa

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Nyumu ko hi Rama, ngɛ Efraim yo ɔmɛ a nɔ. E je Efraim wɛtso ɔ mi, nɛ e biɛ ji Elkana. E tsɛ biɛ ji Yeroham; e nɛ̃ ji Elihu; e nɛnɛkasowa ji Tohu, nɛ Tohu tsɛ ji Zuf.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Elkana ngɛ yihi enyɔ; nɔ kake biɛ ji Hana, nɛ nɔ kake hu biɛ ji Penina. Penina ngɛ bimɛ, se Hana lɛɛ e fɔ we.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Daa jeha a, Elkana jeɔ Rama kɛ yaa Shilo ya jaa Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ, nɛ e sãã bɔ kɛ haa lɛ. Lejɛ ɔ Hofni kɛ Finehas, Eli binyumu enyɔ ɔmɛ ngɛ osɔfo yee ngɛ.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Be tsuaa be nɛ Elkana maa sã bɔ ɔ, e ma gba lo ɔ kɛ ha e yo Penina kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ kɛ e biyi ɔmɛ tsuo nɔ tsuaa nɔ kɛ e nɔ́.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Se Hana lɛɛ, e jeɔ blɔ haa lɛ e nɔ́ pɔtɛɛ; ejakaa Yawɛ tsi e fɔmi nya mohu, se e huno ɔ suɔ lɛ saminya.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: E hunoyo Penina yeɔ e he fɛu nɛ e yeɔ e tsui ngɛ fɔmi nɛ e fɔ we ɔ he.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ yaa nɔ daa jeha; be tsuaa be nɛ a ya Yawɛ we ɔ, Penina maa ye Hana tsui kɛ yaa si e ma fo ya nɛ e ma kua ní yemi.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ e huno Elkana ma bi lɛ ke, “Hana, mɛni he je o ngɛ ya foe? Mɛni he je o yi ní? Mɛni he je o pee mɔbɔmɔbɔ kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Anɛ i pi binyumuhi nyɔngma kɛ ha mo lo?” Hana kɛ Eli

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Hana wo si nɛ e de ke, “Yawɛ Ope, ke o maa hyɛ o mawayo haomi, nɛ o ma kai mi, nɛ o hɛ be ye nɔ jee, nɛ o ma ha o mawayo binyumu ɔ, i kɛ lɛ ma ha mo e wami ligbi tsuo, nɛ asoyi nya be e yi he sae.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Hana ngɛ munyu tue ngɛ e tsui mi; e gbi lɛɛ a nui, se e nya mi kɛkɛ nɛ e ngɛ pae nɛ e ngɛ mae. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Eli susu kaa e de dã,

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: nɛ e de ke, “Mɛni be o maa de dã kɛ yaa si? Ha dã nɛ je o hɛ mi!”

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Koo bu mi kaa yaka nɔ ko, ejakaa ye haomi, kɛ nɔ nami ɔmɛ a he i ngɛ kue fae ngɛ.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Eli de lɛ ke, “O kɛ he jɔmi nɛ ya; Israel Mawu ɔ ma ha mo nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o bi lɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Lɛ hu e he nɔ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o susu o mawayo he daa.” Kɛkɛ nɛ e ho nɛ e ya ye ní, nɛ aywilɛho ɔ je e hɛ mi. Samuel fɔmi

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, Elkana kɛ e yi ɔmɛ, kɛ e bimɛ ɔmɛ te si mla, nɛ benɛ a ja Yawɛ ta a, a kpale a se kɛ ho a we mi ya ngɛ Rama. Elkana kɛ e yo Hana na bɔmi, nɛ Yawɛ bu Hana kue fami ɔ tue.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Hana ngɔ hɔ, nɛ e fɔ binyumu, nɛ e wo lɛ biɛ ke Samuel; nɛ e de ke, “I wo lɛ kikɛmɛ a biɛ nɛ ɔ, ejakaa i bi Yawɛ nɛ e kɛ lɛ ha mi.”

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Jeha ba su ekohu, nɛ Elkana kɛ e we ɔ tsuo ho Shilo ya, konɛ a ya sã daa jeha bɔ ɔ, kɛ bɔ titli ko hu nɛ e wo Yawɛ he si ɔ.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Se Hana lɛɛ e yɛ, ejakaa e de e huno ɔ ke, “Ke i tsɔ jokuɛ ɔ nyɔ pɛ ma ngɔ lɛ kɛ ya Yawɛ we ɔ; nɛ lejɛ ɔ e maa hi e wami be tsuo.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: E huno Elkana de lɛ ke, “E da; nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o susu kaa e hi ɔ, moo pee; hii si ngɛ hiɛ ɔ kɛ yaa si o ma tsɔ lɛ nyɔ. Yawɛ nɛ e ha nɛ o pee kaa bɔ nɛ o wo si ɔ.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Hana hi si nɛ e hyɛ e bi ɔ kɛ ya si e tsɔ lɛ nyɔ.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: I bi Yawɛ bi nɛ ɔ, nɛ e ha mi nɔ́ nɛ i bi lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, imi hu i ngɔ lɛ ba ha Yawɛ. E maa pee Yawɛ nɔ́ e wami ligbi ɔmɛ tsuo.” Kɛkɛ nɛ a ja Yawɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Nɔ ko be nɛ ngɛ klɔuklɔu kaa Yawɛ. E se ɔ, nɔ ko be. Ee, Mawu se ɔ, wesa he kpa ko be.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Nyɛ kpa fiami munyu puu tumi; he nɔ womi munyu nɛ ko je nyɛ nya mi. Yawɛ ji Mawu nɛ le níhi tsuo, nɛ e kojoɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ nimli peeɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Katsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a kɛ̃ɛ̃ ɔmɛ ku, nɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ a he wɛ ɔ na he wami he.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Ni nɛmɛ nɛ tɔ hyɛ ɔ, a bɔni apaa yemi nɛ a kɛ na a nya mi ngma; ni nɛmɛ nɛ hwɔ ye mɛ ɔ, a hwɔ ɔ se po. Yosa a ba fɔ bimɛ kpaago, nɛ bimɛ a nyɛ ɔ ba pee kaa yo nɛ fɔ we hyɛ.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Yawɛ gbeɔ nɔ, nɛ e haa nɔ wami ekohu; e kɛ nɔ yaa gbeje, nɛ e kpaleɔ lɛ kɛ baa wami mi ekohu.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Yawɛ lɛ peeɔ nɔ ohiatsɛ, nɛ e peeɔ nɔ niatsɛ. E baa nɔ si, nɛ e woɔ nɔ nɔ.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: E woɔ ohiatsɛmɛ a nɔ kɛ jeɔ tabo zu mi, nɛ e jeɔ ni nɛmɛ nɛ e fi mɛ kɛ jeɔ a haomihi a mi. E haa a kɛ ganɔhi hii si, nɛ e kɛ mɛ toɔ hɛ mi nyami blɔ hehi. Yawɛ níhi ji je ɔ titima amɛ; a nɔ nɛ e fia je ɔ kɛ fɔ.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: “E baa ni nɛmɛ nɛ yeɔ lɛ anɔkuale ɔ a yi. Se yayami peeli lɛɛ a hɛ mi kpataa ngɛ diblii mi; tsa pi adesa nitsɛ he wami nya nɛ e yeɔ manye.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: A ma kpata Yawɛ he nyɛli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi pɛsɛpɛsɛ; hiɔwe ma si wo mɛ. Yawɛ maa kojo je ɔ tsuo; e kɛ he wami ma ha e matsɛ ɔ, nɛ e ma ha matsɛ nɛ a pɔ lɛ nu ɔ maa ye kunimi.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Elkana kpale e se kɛ ho we mi ya ngɛ Rama, se jokuɛyo Samuel ɔ hi osɔfo Eli ngɔ nɛ e sɔmɔ Yawɛ. Eli binyumu ɔmɛ

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: loo blɔ nya tomi nɛ ngɛ kɛ ha osɔfo ɔmɛ a blɔ fa mi ní nɛ sa kaa a he ngɛ ma a dɛ ɔ. Mohu ɔ, ke nɔ ko ba ngɛ bɔ sãe ɔ, osɔfo ɔ tsɔlɔ ɔ maa ba kɛ e dɛ mi gbowe kɛ e nya gbla etɛ. Nɛ benɛ a ngɛ lo ɔ hooe ɔ,

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: e kɛ gbowe ɔ maa wo dadesɛ, loo ngɛyu, loo kutu ɔ mi, nɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ gbowe ɔ maa bɛ ɔ, maa pee osɔfo ɔ nɔ́. Bɔ nɛ a peeɔ Israel bi tsuo nɛ baa Shilo ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Anɔkuale mi ɔ, be mi nɛ a na we nɛ a sã zɔ ɔ tete ɔ, osɔfo ɔ tsɔlɔ ɔ maa ba nɛ e ma ba de nɔ nɛ ngɛ bɔ ɔ sãe ɔ ke, “Ha mi lo ɔ eko nɛ ma kɛ ya ha osɔfo ɔ nɛ e si; ejakaa e be lo nɛ a hoo momo hee ngɛ o dɛ, ja lo mumu.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Ke nɔ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Ha nɛ a sã zɔ ɔ kekle kaa bɔ nɛ mlaa a tsɔɔ ɔ, konɛ lɔ ɔ se nɛ o ngɔ bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ o suɔ” ɔ, e ma de ke, “Dɛbi! Ha mi nɔuu! Ke pi ja a, ma ngɔ pani nya!”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Eli binyumu ɔmɛ pee yayami agbo ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi, ejakaa a bui Yawɛ bɔ sami ɔ. Samuel ngɛ Shilo

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, jokuɛyo Samuel ɔ lɛɛ e ngɛ Yawɛ sɔmɔe, nɛ a kɛ kploba efɔd fi e kpɛti.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Daa jeha a, e nyɛ kpɛɔ tade bɔbɔyoo ko kɛ ya haa lɛ, ke e kɛ e huno ɔ ya nɛ a ya sã jeha bɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ Eli maa gbaa Elkana kɛ e yo ɔ, nɛ e ma de Elkana ke, “Yawɛ nɛ e ha nɛ o kɛ o yo ɔ nɛ na bimɛ kpahi, nɛ a ba ye nɔ nɛ o ngɔ kɛ ba ha lɛ ɔ nane mi.” Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a maa kpale a se kɛ ho a ma mi ya.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Yawɛ gbaa Hana niinɛ, nɛ e fɔ binyumu kpahi etɛ kɛ yihi enyɔ. Jokuɛyo Samuel ɔ ba wa, nɛ e ya nɔ nɛ e sɔmɔ Yawɛ. Eli kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Dɛbi, ye bimɛ, nyɛ kpa! Níhi nɛ i ngɛ nue nɛ Yawɛ ma a ngɛ dee ngɛ nyɛ he ɔ, pi ní kpakpahi.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Ke nɔ ko pee e nyɛmi adesa yayami ɔ, Mawu maa da mi ha lɛ; se ke nɔ ko pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ ɔ, mɛnɔ maa da mi ha lɛ?” Se a bui a tsɛ ɔ munyu ɔmɛ tue; ejakaa Yawɛ to momo kaa e maa gbe mɛ.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Jokuɛyo Samuel ɔ lɛɛ e ngɛ wae ngɛ nɔmlɔ tso mi; nɛ Yawɛ kɛ nimli adesahi tsuo na e he bua jɔmi. Eli we ɔ hɛ mi kpatami

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, gbalɔ ko ngɔ sɛ gbi kɛ je Yawɛ ngɔ ba ha Eli ke, “Benɛ o nɛ̃ Aaron, kɛ e weku li ɔmɛ ngɛ nyɔguɛ si himi mi ngɛ Egipt ɔ, i je ye he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ Aaron.

english_verse: Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar. But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
translation_verse: Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ nyɛ peeɔ jiklɔɔ ngɛ bɔ ɔmɛ nɛ i fa ke a kɛ ba ha mi ɔ he? Eli, mɛni he je o buu o binyumu ɔmɛ pe mi ɔ? Mɛni he je o ngmɛ blɔ nɛ a ngɔ bɔ ɔmɛ nɛ ye ma Israel kɛ ba haa mi ɔ e mi kpakpa amɛ kɛ ngɛ a he lɛe, nɛ a ngɛ plɔkee kikɛ nɛ ɔ?

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Imi Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ, i wo si be ko ke o kɛ o weku li ma sɔmɔ mi kaa osɔfohi kɛ maa ya neneene. Se jehanɛ ɔ, i ngɛ dee ke i kpale ye nya se! Mohu ɔ, nihi nɛ woɔ ye hɛ mi nyami ɔ, ma wo a hɛ mi nyami; nɛ nihi nɛ hiee mi ɔ, imi hu ma hie mɛ.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Bu tue, be ma nɛ ma kpata nihewi nɛ ngɛ o we ɔ, kɛ o weku ɔ mi tsuo a hɛ mi, nɛ nɔmoyo ko be o we ɔ mi hie hu.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: O maa hao, nɛ o kɛ hɛkɔ maa hyɛ gbaamihi nɛ i kɛ ma ha Israel bi kpa amɛ, se o we ɔ mi lɛɛ nɔmoyo ko nɔmoyo ko be mi hie hu.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Se kɛ̃, ma ha o nina ko yi ma na wami, nɛ e ma sɔmɔ mi kaa osɔfo. Lɛɛ e hɛ ma yu nɛ e maa hao, se ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ lɛɛ a kɛ klaate maa gbe mɛ tsuo.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Nɛ nɔ́ nɛ o kɛ maa le kaa nɔ́ nɛ i de ɔ tsuo maa ba mi ji lss ma ha o binyumu enyɔ ɔmɛ nɛ ji Hofni kɛ Finehas tsuo ma gbo ligbi kake too.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Ma hla osɔfo ko nɛ maa ye mi anɔkuale; nɛ lɛ ji nɔ nɛ maa pee níhi nɛ ngɛ ye tsui nɔ, kɛ níhi nɛ ngɛ ye juɛmi mi ɔ ha mi. Ma bɔ we saminya ha lɛ, nɛ a ma sɔmɔ ngɛ ye matsɛ ɔ nɛ i pɔ lɛ nu ɔ e hɛ mi daa.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ maa piɛ ngɛ o we ɔ mi ɔ, ja a ya jamɛ a osɔfo ɔ ngɔ nɛ a ya ba sika, loo niye ní; aloo ja a ya kpa pɛɛ kaa a ngmɛ mɛ blɔ nɛ a piɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ a he kɛ tsu ní, loko a ma na a nya mi ngma!”

english_verse: Samuel served the Lord by helping Eli the priest, who was by that time almost blind. In those days, the Lord hardly ever spoke directly to people, and he did not appear to them in dreams very often. But one night, Eli was asleep in his room,
translation_verse: Ligbi ko nyɔ mi, benɛ Eli, nɛ lɔ ɔ ji e hɛngmɛ yu ta, hwɔɔ si ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e tsu ɔ mi ɔ,

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: Samuel lɛɛ e hwɔɔ si ngɛ Yawɛ sɔlemi we ɔ he nɛ Mawu somi daka a ngɛ ɔ. Benɛ je mi tsɔ we lolo, nɛ kane ɔ hu na we nɛ e gbo ɔ,

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Samuel tu fo kɛ ho Eli ngɔ ya nɛ e ya de lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, i ba; i nu nɛ o tsɛ mi.” Se Eli de lɛ ke, “I tsɛ we mo; yaa nɛ o ya hwɔ si ekohu.” Nɛ Samuel ho nɛ e ya hwɔ si.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ tsɛ Samuel ekohu, nɛ Samuel te si kɛ ho Eli ngɔ ya nɛ e ya de lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, i ba; i nu nɛ o tsɛ mi.” Se Eli de lɛ ke, “I tsɛ we mo, ye bi; yaa nɛ o ya hwɔ si ekohu.”

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, Samuel li Yawɛ lolo; ejakaa Yawɛ kɛ lɛ tui munyu hyɛ.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Yawɛ tsɛ Samuel ekohu si etɛne, nɛ Samuel te si kɛ ho Eli ngɔ ya nɛ e ya de lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, i ba; i nu nɛ o tsɛ mi.” Jehanɛ Eli yɔse kaa Yawɛ nɛ ngɛ jokuɛ nyumuyo ɔ tsɛe ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e de Samuel ke, “Yaa hwɔ si, nɛ ke e tsɛ mo ekohu ɔ, de ke, ‘Moo tu munyu, Yawɛ; o tsɔlɔ ngɛ mo tue bue.’ ” Nɛ Samuel ho nɛ e ya hwɔ si.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ ba da si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e tsɛ lɛ kaa kekle ɔ ke, “Samuel! Samuel!” Nɛ Samuel he nɔ ke, “Moo tu munyu, o tsɔlɔ ngɛ mo tue bue.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Samuel ke, “I miɔ nɛ ma pee nɔ́ ko ngɛ Israel, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa nu he ɔ, e tue mi maa pee lɛ heii.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: I de lɛ momo ke ma gbla e we ɔ tue kɛ maa ya neneene, ejakaa e le kaa e bimɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ musu bɔe kɛ ngɛ Mawu sie, se e kua we nɔ́ ha mɛ.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i ngɛ Eli kɛ e we mi bi ɔmɛ kita kae kaa yayami agbo nɛ a pee nɛ ɔ, a kɛ sami bɔ, loo niye ní bɔ ko be nyɛe ma kpata mi kɔkɔɔkɔ.”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Samuel ho ya hwɔ si kɛ ya si mɔtu; nɛ e te si nɛ e bli Yawɛ we ɔ sinya amɛ. Samuel ye gbeye kaa e ma de Eli nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Se Eli tsɛ lɛ nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ye bi Samuel!” Nɛ e he nɔ ke, “Tsaatsɛ!”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Eli bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni Yawɛ de mo ɔ? De mi nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́. Ke o laa mi ba a, Mawu maa gbla o tue!”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Samuel de lɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́; e si we nɔ́ ko nɛ e de we lɛ. Eli de ke, “Lɛ ji Yawɛ ɔ nɛ; nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ sa e hɛ mi ɔ, e pee!”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Nɛ́ Samuel ngɛ wae ɔ, Yawɛ kɛ lɛ ngɛ, nɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Samuel de ɔ, Yawɛ haa e baa mi ja pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Israel ma a tsuo, kɛ je Dan kɛ ya si Beersheba ba na le kaa Samuel ɔ, Yawɛ nitsɛ gbalɔ ji lɛ.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, Filisti bi ɔmɛ ya bua a he nya ngɛ Afek, konɛ a ya tua Israel bi ɔmɛ. Israel bi ɔmɛ hu ya bua a he nya ngɛ Ebenezer, konɛ a kɛ mɛ nɛ hwu.

english_verse: The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about
translation_verse: Ta a mi wa saminya. Filisti bi ɔmɛ ye Israel bi ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ a gbe a ta buli maa pee akpe eywiɛ.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a tsɔ ya ngɔ Yawɛ somi daka a ngɛ Shilo kɛ ba. Somi daka a daa si ha Yawɛ Ope ɔ matsɛ sɛ. Eli binyumu enyɔ ɔmɛ, Hofni kɛ Finehas piɛ nihi nɛ ngɔ somi daka a kɛ ba a a he.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Benɛ ta buli ɔmɛ kpale a se kɛ ba ma sito he ɔ, Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ bi ke, “Mɛni he je nɛ Yawɛ ha Filisti bi ɔmɛ gbe wɔ mwɔnɛ ɔ kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Nyɛ ha wa ya ngɔ Yawɛ somi daka a ngɛ Shilo kɛ ba konɛ Yawɛ ba hi wa ngɔ, nɛ e ba kpɔ wɔ kɛ je wa he nyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yawɛ somi daka a ba su ma sito he ɔ, Israel tsuo hwɔ lele wawɛɛ, nɛ lɔ ɔ ha zugba mimiɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Filisti bi ɔmɛ nu lele hwɔmi ɔ, nɛ a bi ke, “Lele nɛ a hwɔ wawɛɛ ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a sito he ɔ, kɛ ji e sisi kɛɛ?” Benɛ a na le kaa Yawɛ somi daka a ba su Hebri bi ɔmɛ a sito he ɔ,

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: sawale nu Filisti bi ɔmɛ, nɛ a de ke, “Mawu komɛ ba ni ɔmɛ a sito he ɔ! Akuanyɛ! Nɔ nɛ ɔ eko tsa bɛ hyɛ.

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Wa yi ta! Mɛnɔ ma kpɔ wɔ kɛ je kikɛmɛ a mawu kpetekpleenyɛ nɛ ɔmɛ a dɛ mi? Mɛ ji mawuhi nɛ kɛ haomi slɔɔtohi gba Egipt bi ɔmɛ a nya ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ nɛ!

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Nyɛ wlua nyɛ, nɛ nyɛɛ pee kã kaa nyumuhi; ke pi ja a, nyɛ ma ba plɛ pee Hebri bi ɔmɛ a nyɔguɛhi kaa bɔ nɛ mɛ hu a sɔmɔ nyɛ be ko mi ɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ hwu ta kaa nyumuhi!”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: A kpɔ Mawu somi daka a, nɛ Hofni kɛ Finehas, Eli binyumu enyɔ ɔmɛ hu gbo. Eli gbenɔ

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Nyumu ko nɛ je Benyamin wɛtso ɔ mi gbɔ fo kɛ je ta nga a nɔ kɛ ba Shilo jamɛ a ligbi ɔ nɔuu kɛ e he tade nɛ hía, kɛ e yi mi zu.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Benɛ e ba a, Eli hii si ngɛ sɛ nɔ ngɛ agbo ɔ nya, nɛ e ngɛ blɔ ɔ mi hyɛe; ejakaa e ngɛ e tsui yee ngɛ somi daka a he. Benɛ nyumu ɔ ba su ma a mi, nɛ e ba gba sane nɛ ba a, ma a tsuo kpa bubuubui.

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Tsɔlɔ ɔ ha lɛ heto ke, “Israel tu fo ngɛ ta a nya, nɛ a gbe a ti nihi babauu. Hofni kɛ Finehas, o binyumu enyɔ ɔmɛ gbo; nɛ a kpɔ Mawu somi daka a hu kɛ je!”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Nɛ́ nyumu ɔ wo somi daka a nɔ ta kikɛ nɛ ɔ, Eli kpa kɛ je e sɛ ɔ nɔ kɛ ya nɔ e se ngɛ agbo ɔ kasa nya. Nɛ akɛnɛ nɔmlɔ ɔ bwɔ nɛ e jiɔ he je ɔ, e kuɛ ku nɛ e gbo. Eli hi Israel ma a nya jeha nyingmi eywiɛ. Finehas yo ɔ gbenɔ

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Eli nganyɛ nɛ ji Finehas yo ɔ mi wa, nɛ e fɔmi be su ta. Benɛ e nu kaa a kpɔ Mawu somi daka a, nɛ e ngatsɛ ɔ, kɛ e huno ɔ tsuo gbo ɔ, e kpatu nu kɔɔmi, nɛ e fɔ.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Benɛ e maa ho gbomi ya a, yi ɔmɛ nɛ daa si ngɛ e he ɔ de lɛ ke, “Koo ye gbeye! O fɔ binyumu!” Se e pui a nya mi, nɛ e ha we mɛ heto hulɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Benɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ kpɔ somi daka a, a wo lɛ kɛ je Ebenezer kɛ ho Ashdod ya,

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: nɛ a kɛ lɛ ya ma a wɔ ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Dagon ɔ kasa nya ngɛ piɛ ɔ mi.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena mɔtu mla benɛ Ashdod bi ɔmɛ te si ɔ, o nɛ Dagon nɛ kuɛli nɔ si, nɛ e hɛ mi bu si ngɛ Yawɛ somi daka a hɛ mi. A wo e nɔ kɛ ma e ma he ɔ ekohu.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena kpa mɔtu mla benɛ a ke a teɔ si ekohu ɔ, o nɛ Dagon nɛ kuɛli nɔ si ekohu, nɛ e hɛ mi bu si ngɛ Yawɛ somi daka a hɛ mi. Dagon yi, kɛ e nine enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo kplɔ pue si ngɛ kpoku ɔ nya; e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ pɛ lɛ piɛ.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
