translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ he je ɔ, kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ, Dagon wɔnɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ nihi tsuo nɛ yaa wɔ piɛ ɔ mi ngɛ Ashdod ɔ kɛ nane mɛ kpoku ɔ nɔ; pe a haneɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Yawɛ gbla Ashdod bi ɔmɛ a tue wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ e kɛ tslɔɔ kpata a kɛ a huza a nɔ bi ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Ashdod bi ɔmɛ na bɔ nɛ níhi ngɛ nɔ yae ha a, a de ke, “Israel Mawu ɔ ngɛ waa kɛ wa wɔ Dagon ɔ tsuo tue gblae. Wa ko ha nɛ somi daka a nɛ hi wa ngɔ hu.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a tsɛ Filisti matsɛmɛ enuɔ ɔmɛ tsuo kpe, nɛ a bi mɛ ke, “Kɛ wa maa pee Israel Mawu ɔ somi daka a kɛɛ?” A he nɔ ke, “Nyɛɛ ngɔ Israel Mawu ɔ somi daka a kɛ ya Gat.” Nɛ a wo daka a kɛ ho lejɛ ɔ ya.

english_verse: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
translation_verse: Se benɛ daka a ya su Gat ɔ, Yawɛ gbla ma a tue. E ha tslɔɔ fuu ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo, jokuɛwi kɛ nikɔtɔmahi; nɛ sawale nu nɔ tsuaa nɔ.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a wo Yawɛ somi daka a kɛ ho Ekron ya. Se benɛ Mawu somi daka a ya su Ekron ɔ, Ekron bi ɔmɛ kpa bubuubui, nɛ a de ke, “A wo Israel Mawu ɔ somi daka a kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ, konɛ e ba gbe wɔ, kɛ wa ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo!”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mɛ hu a tsɛ Filisti matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsuo kpe, nɛ a de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ wo Israel Mawu ɔ somi daka a kɛ je hiɛ ɔ kɛ ya ha nɔtsɛmɛ, konɛ e ko ba gbe wɔ, kɛ wa ma mi bi ɔmɛ.” Sawale nu ma a tsuo, ejakaa gbenɔ hiɔ ɔ bɔni ní puɛmi momo.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Ni nɛmɛ nɛ gbo we ɔ po, tslɔɔ fuu mɛ; nɛ ma a kpa bubuubui kɛ ba yemi kɛ buami ngɛ a wɔ ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Benɛ Yawɛ somi daka a na nyɔhiɔ kpaago ngɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ ɔ,

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: ni ɔmɛ ya tsɛ wɔnɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ kunya yeli ɔmɛ, nɛ a bi mɛ ke, “Kɛ wa maa pee Yawɛ somi daka a kɛɛ? Mɛni waa kɛ maa piɛ he kɛ ho e je he ya?”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: A he nɔ ke, “Ke nyɛɛ kɛ Israel Mawu ɔ somi daka a maa ya a, nyɛɛ kɛ lɛ ko ya dɛ gu; e hia doo kaa nyɛɛ ngɔ fɔ yemi bɔ kɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya kpata lɛ. Ke nyɛ pee ja loko nyɛ ma na he wami, kɛkɛ nyɛ maa le nɔ́ nɛ he je nɛ Mawu ngɛ nyɛ tue gblae ɔ.”

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Ma a bi ke, “Mɛni fɔ yemi bɔ waa kɛ maa ya a?” Nɛ a ha heto ke, “Sika tsu tslɔɔ enuɔ, kɛ sika tsu kɔkue enuɔ, ngɛ Filisti matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a hiɛmi nya; ejakaa haomi kake ɔ nɔuu lɛ ba nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ matsɛmɛ enuɔ ɔmɛ tsuo nyɛ nɔ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ pee sika tsu tslɔɔ nɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ sika tsu kɔkue nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ daa si ha kɔkuehi nɛ ba ngɛ nyɛ zugba a hɛ mi kpatae ɔ, konɛ nyɛ ya wo Israel Mawu ɔ hɛ mi nyami kaa, alini e maa jɔɔ nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ wɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ nyɛ zugba a tue gblami lo.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Mɛni he je nyɛ maa kplii nyɛ tsui kaa bɔ nɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Farao ɔ kplii a tsui ɔ? Nyɛ kai kaa Mawu kɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ to ní wawɛɛ nitsɛ kɛ ya si be nɛ a ngmɛɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a he nɛ a ho.

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ kpɛ tlɔɔke he kake, nɛ nyɛɛ fi na nyɔ hali enyɔ nɛ a wui mɛ kuɛ pã tso hyɛ kɛ wo he; na bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ nyɛɛ po mɛ ya wo tsu mi.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Nyɛ wo Yawɛ somi daka a kɛ ma tlɔɔke ɔ mi, nɛ sika tsu ní ɔmɛ nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ ma ha Yawɛ kaa fɔ yemi bɔ ɔ, nyɛɛ ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo daka ko mi kɛ ma somi daka a kasa nya. Nyɛɛ ngɔ tlɔɔke ɔ ngɔ ma blɔ ɔ nɔ, nɛ lɛ nitsɛ e ho.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, nyɛɛ hi lɛ hyɛe; ke e ba mi kaa tlɔɔke ɔ nyɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ̃ kɛ ya su lɛ nitsɛ e zugba a nɔ ngɛ Bet Shemesh ɔ, lɛɛ Israel Mawu ɔ ji nɔ nɛ kɛ amanehlu nguaa nɛ ɔ ba wa nɔ ɔ nɛ. Se ke e pee we ja a, lɛɛ wa maa na kaa tsa pi lɛ nɛ e gbla wa tue, se mohu matahu kɛkɛ nɛ ba po wɔ.” Somi daka a ya su Bet Shemesh

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Ni ɔmɛ pee kaa bɔ nɛ a de mɛ ɔ; a ya nu na nyɔ hali enyɔ, nɛ a fi mɛ kɛ wo tlɔɔke ɔ he. Se na bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ a nga a yi wo tsu mi.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: A kɛ somi daka a, kɛ daka nɛ sika tsu kɔkue ɔmɛ, kɛ sika tsu tslɔɔ ɔmɛ ngɛ mi ɔ wo tlɔɔke ɔ mi.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, Bet Shemesh bi ɔmɛ ngɛ ngma pooe ngɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi; nɛ benɛ a na somi daka a, a nya saminya.

english_verse: The cows left the road and pulled the cart into a field that belonged to Joshua from Beth-Shemesh, and they stopped beside a huge rock. Some men from the tribe of Levi were there. So they took the chest off the cart and placed it on the rock, and then they did the same thing with the bag of gold rats and sores. A few other people chopped up the cart and made a fire. They killed the cows and burned them as sacrifices to the Lord. After that, they offered more sacrifices.
translation_verse: Levi bi ɔmɛ je Yawɛ somi daka a, kɛ daka nɛ maa si ngɛ e kasa nya nɛ sika ní ɔmɛ ngɛ mi ɔ ngɔ ma tɛ sa agbo ɔ nɔ. Bet Shemesh bi ɔmɛ sã sami bɔhi, kɛ bɔ kpahi kɛ ha Yawɛ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Filisti matsɛmɛ enuɔ ɔmɛ hyɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ bɔɔ, nɛ a kpale a se kɛ ho Ekron ya jamɛ a ligbi ɔ nɔuu.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Filisti bi ɔmɛ ngɔ sika tsu tslɔɔ enuɔ ɔmɛ ya ha Yawɛ kaa fɔ yemi bɔ kɛ ha a ma nguaa enuɔ ɔmɛ. Ma amɛ ji Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gat, kɛ Ekron.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Sika tsu kɔkue ɔmɛ lɛɛ a kɛ mɛ kpata Mawu kɛ ha Filisti ma nguaa amɛ nɛ a fia gbogbo ngɔ wo a he ɔ, kɛ ma wawihi nɛ a fiɛ gbogbo ngɔ wui a he, nɛ ji mahi nɛ Filisti matsɛmɛ enuɔ ɔmɛ yeɔ a nɔ ɔ tsuo. Tɛ sa agbo ɔ nɛ a kɛ Yawɛ somi daka a ma nɔ ngɛ Yoshua ngmɔ ɔ mi ngɛ Bet Shemesh ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ kaa nɔ́ nɛ ba a he odase.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Bet Shemesh bi ɔmɛ bi ke, “Mɛnɔ po ma nyɛ Yawɛ, Mawu klɔuklɔu nɛ ɔ hɛ mi maa da? Nɛ jije wa ma je lɛ kɛ je wa ngɔ kɛ ya?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: A tsɔ nihi kɛ ho Kiriat Yearim bi ɔmɛ a ngɔ ya ya de mɛ ke, “Filisti bi ɔmɛ kpale Yawɛ somi daka a kɛ ba. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ ba nɛ nyɛ ba ngɔ kɛ ho.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Kiriat Yearim bi ɔmɛ ba nɛ a ba ngɔ Yawɛ somi daka a kɛ ho nyumu ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Abinadab ɔ we mi ya, ngɛ yoku ko nɔ. A wo e binyumu Eleazar osɔfo, konɛ e hyɛ Yawɛ somi daka a nɔ. Samuel hyɛ Israel ma a nɔ

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Samuel de Israel bi ɔmɛ ke, “Ke nyɛ maa kpale ba nyɛɛ Yawɛ se niinɛ kɛ nyɛ tsui tsuo ɔ, lɛɛ nyɛ je ma se mawu ɔmɛ, kɛ yo wɔ Ashtarot ɔ kɛ je nyɛ kpɛti. Nyɛ dla nyɛ tsui mi kɛ ha Yawɛ, nɛ nyɛ sɔmɔ lɛ nɔ kake too, nɛ e ma je nyɛ kɛ je Filisti bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ ngmɛɛ a Baal ɔmɛ, kɛ Ashtarot ɔ he, nɛ a sɔmɔ Yawɛ pɛ.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Samuel de ke, “Nyɛ bua Israel ma a tsuo nya ngɛ Mizpa, nɛ ma kpa Yawɛ pɛɛ ha mɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma a tsuo ba bua a he nya ngɛ Mizpa. A yɛ nyu kɛ pue si ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi, nɛ a ha hwɔ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ tsuo, nɛ a de ke, “Wa pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ.” Mizpa ji he nɛ Samuel hyɛɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti sanehi a mi haa mɛ ngɛ.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Filisti bi ɔmɛ nu kaa Israel bi ɔmɛ ya bua a he nya ngɛ Mizpa, nɛ Filisti matsɛmɛ enuɔ ɔmɛ hia konɛ a ya tua mɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nu he ɔ, a ye gbeye,

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: nɛ a de Samuel ke, “Moo hi kue fae kɛ hi Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ hae, konɛ e je wɔ kɛ je Filisti bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Benɛ Samuel ngɛ sami bɔ ɔ sãe ɔ, Filisti bi ɔmɛ hɛ mɛ kɛ ba, konɛ a ba tua Israel. Se Yawɛ ha hiɔwe si wawɛɛ kɛ wo Filisti bi ɔmɛ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ; nɛ e ha basabasa sɛ a kpɛti, nɛ a kɛ sawale tu fo.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ hia kɛ je Mizpa kɛ nyɛɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a se, nɛ a gbe mɛ hluu kɛ ya si e piɛ bɔɔ nɛ a maa su Bet Kar.

english_verse: The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them. For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ a plɛ kɛ ye Filisti bi ɔmɛ a nɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Samuel yi nɔ ɔ, Yawɛ ngmɛ́ blɔ nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ ya tua Israel ngɛ a zugba a nɔ hu.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, ma amɛ nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ kpɔ ngɛ Israel dɛ kɛ je Ekron kɛ ya si Gat kɛ a he zugba amɛ ɔ, a kpale mɛ tsuo ngɔ ha Israel ekohu. Nɛ tue mi jɔmi ba Israel bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Amor bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samuel hyɛ Israel ma a nɔ e wami ligbi ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Daa jeha a, e kpaa si kɛ yaa Betel, Gilgal, kɛ Mizpa ya hyɛɛ sanehi a mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e kpaleɔ kɛ baa e ma mi Rama, nɛ e ba kojoɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ hulɔ. E ma bɔ sami la tɛ hu ha Yawɛ ngɛ Rama.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: nɛ a kojo ngɛ Beersheba. E bitɛte ɔ biɛ ji Yoel, nɛ e binyumu enyɔne ɔ biɛ ji Abiya.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ a be kaa a tsɛ ɔ; mɛɛ a ya di sika se, nɛ a heɔ nyɔ mi ní, nɛ a plɛɔ sane hɛ mi ngɔ buɔ si.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ ba Rama, nɛ a kɛ Samuel ba pee kpe,

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: nɛ a de lɛ ke, “O nɛ, o bwɔ, nɛ o binyumu ɔmɛ ya wo we o nane; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, moo wo matsɛ ha wɔ nɛ e ye wa nɔ kaa bɔ nɛ je ma kpa amɛ ngɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Se e ngɔɛ Samuel nya kaa ni ɔmɛ bi ke a ha mɛ matsɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Samuel fa kue ha Yawɛ;

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ma a bi mo ɔ, moo pee ha mɛ. Pi mo nɛ a kua a; imi mohu nɛ a kua ke ma ko ye a nɔ matsɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Kɛ je be mi nɛ i je mɛ kɛ je Egipt ɔ, a je ye se ya ngɛ mawu kpahi jae. Nɔ́ nɛ a pee mi ɔ, lɔ ɔ a ngɛ mo hu pee ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Samuel ya bɔ ma a nɛ bi ke a ha mɛ matsɛ ɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: E de mɛ ke, “Matsɛ ɔ nɛ ma ba ye nyɛ nɔ ɔ, bɔ nɛ e maa pee nyɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. E maa ngɔ nyɛ binyumu ɔmɛ ngɔ pee e ta buli; ni komɛ maa hi e ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ a mi, ni komɛ maa hi e ta okpɔngɔ ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ ni komɛ hu maa hi fo tue ngɛ ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Nyɛ bi yi ɔmɛ hu e maa ngɔ mɛ kɛ pee e nu via peeli, ní hooli, kɛ abolo sali.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: E maa ngɔ nyɛ ngmɔ ɔmɛ, wai ngmɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ oliv abɔɔ kpakpa amɛ kɛ ha e mɔ mi ní tsuli ɔmɛ.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: E maa ngɔ nyɛ ngma, kɛ nyɛ wai ngmɔ ɔmɛ a mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka kɛ ha e mɔ mi ní tsuli, kɛ e tsɔli.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Nyɛ nyɔguɛ nyumuhi kɛ yihi, nyɛ nahi, kɛ nyɛ teji kpakpa amɛ ɔ, e maa ngɔ mɛ kɛ ya tsu lɛ nitsɛ e ní tsumi.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: E maa ngɔ nyɛ to ɔmɛ a mi dlami nyɔngma mi kake, nɛ nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ ma plɛ pee e nyɔguɛhi.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, nyɛ maa wo yana ngɛ matsɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ hla a e ní peepee he, se Yawɛ be nyɛ nya mi poe.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: kaa bɔ nɛ je ma amɛ tsuo ngɛ ɔ. Wa matsɛ ɔ maa kojo wɔ, nɛ e maa nyɛɛ wa hɛ mi kɛ hwu ta amɛ ha wɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Benɛ Samuel nu nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ma a de ɔ, e ho ya bɔ Yawɛ.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Moo bu mɛ tue nɛ o wo matsɛ ha mɛ.” Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Samuel ha Israel bi ɔmɛ nane, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ kpale kɛ ho e ma mi ya.

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Benyamin no niatsɛ ko hi si. E biɛ ji Kish; e tsɛ biɛ ji Abiel; e nɛ̃ ji Zeror; e nɛnɛkasowa ji Bekorat, nɛ Bekorat hu e tsɛ biɛ ji Afia.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Kish ngɛ binyumu ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Saul. E ji niheyo nɛ he ngɛ fɛu saminya, nɛ nyumu ko nyumu ko be Israel nɛ ka, nɛ e he hu ngɛ fɛu kɛ lɛ sɔ.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Saul tsɛ Kish teji komɛ laa; nɛ Kish de e bi ɔ ke, “Ngɔɔ tsɔli ɔmɛ a kpɛti nɔ kake kɛ piɛ o he nɛ o ya hla teji ɔmɛ.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: A ya kpa Efraim yo ɔ nɔ, kɛ Shalisha zugba a nɔ, se a nɛ teji ɔmɛ. A tsa nɔ kɛ ya gu Shaalim zugba a nɔ, se teji ɔmɛ be lejɛ ɔ hulɔ. Jehanɛ, a ya gu Benyamin zugba a nɔ, se a nɛ mɛ.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Benɛ a su Zuf zugba a nɔ ɔ, Saul de tsɔlɔ ɔ nɛ e kɛ lɛ ngɛ nyɛɛe ɔ ke, “Ha waa kpale wa se, ke pi ja a, tsaatsɛ hɛ maa je teji ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ e ma bɔni e tsui yemi ngɛ wɔ mohu wa he.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Se tsɔlɔ ɔ de lɛ ke, “O nɛ, ní nalɔ ko ngɛ ma nɛ ɔ mi nɛ a buu lɛ saminya; ejakaa nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e deɔ ɔ, baa mi. Ha wa ya na lɛ; eko piɔ e maa tsɔɔ wɔ he nɛ wa maa na lohwe ɔmɛ ngɛ.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Saul bi tsɔlɔ ɔ ke, “Ke wa ya a, mɛni wa ma ha nyumu ɔ?” E ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Abolo ɔ nɛ ngɛ wa kotoku ɔmɛ a mi ɔ ta, nɛ nɔ́ ko be nɛ wa ma ha ní nalɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Tsɔlɔ ɔ de Saul ekohu ke, “I hɛɛ sika hiɔ nyafii ko. I kɛ lɔ ɔ ma ha ní nalɔ ɔ, konɛ e tsɔɔ wɔ he nɛ wa maa na lohwe ɔmɛ ngɛ.”

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Saul de ke, “Mo! O le demi; ha nɛ waa ho.” Nɛ a pue nɔ kɛ ho ma a mi he nɛ Mawu nɔmlɔ ɔ ngɛ ɔ ya. Benɛ a ngɛ yoku ɔ kuɔe kɛ yaa a, a kɛ yihewi komɛ kpe nɛ a yaa yɛ nyu. A bi yihewi ɔmɛ ke, “Ní nalɔ ɔ ngɛ ma a mi lo?”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Saul kɛ e tsɔlɔ ɔ pue nɔ kɛ ho ma a mi ya. Benɛ a sɛ ma a mi ɔ, a na Samuel nɛ lɛɛ e je ma a mi kɛ yaa jami he ɔ.

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Hwɔɔ, maa pee be nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, ma tsɔ nyumu ko nɛ je Benyamin wɛtso ɔ mi kɛ ba o ngɔ. Moo pɔ lɛ nu nɛ e ba ye ganɔ ngɛ ye ma, Israel ɔ nya, nɛ e kpɔ mɛ kɛ je Filisti bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi, ejakaa i na a nɔ nami ɔ, nɛ i nu a kue fami ɔ hulɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Samuel na Saul ɔ, Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Nyumu ɔ nɛ i gba mo e he sane ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Lɛ ji nɔ nɛ ma ba ye ye ma a nɔ.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Saul hɛ lɛ kɛ su Samuel he ngɛ agbo ɔ nya, nɛ e bi lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, jije ní nalɔ ɔ we mi ngɛ?”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Samuel de Saul ke, “Imi ji ní nalɔ ɔ nɛ; moo nyɛɛ ye hɛ mi nɛ waa ho jami he ɔ ya; ejakaa mwɔnɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ kɛ mi maa ye ní, nɛ hwɔɔ mɔtu ɔ, ma de mo níhi nɛ o ngɛ hlae nɛ o le ɔ tsuo, loko ma wo mo blɔ nɛ o ho.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Teji ɔmɛ nɛ laa mwɔnɛ ɔ ji ligbi etɛ ɔ, koo ye o tsui ngɛ a he; a na mɛ. Se mɛnɔ ji nɔ nɛ Israel ma a ngɛ hlae wawɛɛ kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Mo tutuutu; o kɛ o tsɛ we ɔ.”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Saul he nɔ ke, “I je Benyamin, Israel wɛtso nɛ ji nyafii pe kulaa a mi; nɛ ye weku ɔ hu ji weku nyafii pe kulaa ngɛ wɛtso ɔ mi. Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ o kɛ mi ngɛ munyu tue kikɛ nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Ní hoolɔ ɔ ngɔ lo fiɔ ɔ, kɛ bo mi fiɔ ɔ ba ma Saul hɛ mi. Nɛ Samuel de ke, “O nɛ, lo nɛ a kɛ to ha mo ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Moo ye, ejakaa i je blɔ ngɔ to ha mo nɛ o ba ye kikɛmɛ a be nɛ ɔ kɛ nibwɔ ɔmɛ nɛ i kpee ɔ.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul kɛ Samuel ye ní jamɛ a ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Benɛ a kple si kɛ je jami he ɔ kɛ ba ma a mi ɔ, a pee sa ha Saul ngɛ tsu ɔ yi mi,

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: nɛ e hwɔ lejɛ ɔ. Samuel pɔ Saul nu Makɛ ɔ, Samuel tsɛ Saul ngɛ tsu ɔ yi mi nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Tee si nɛ ma wo mo blɔ nɛ o ho.” Saul te si, nɛ e kɛ Samuel tsuo je kpo.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Benɛ a maa ho ma a nya sumi ya a, Samuel de Saul ke, “De o tsɔlɔ ɔ nɛ e be kɛ sɛ wa hlami. Mo nitsɛ lɛɛ moo mlɛ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ bɔɔ nɛ ma de mo sɛ ko nɛ je Mawu ngɔ.”

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Ke o je ye ngɔ mwɔnɛ ɔ, o kɛ nyumuhi enyɔ maa kpe ngɛ Rahel yɔkɔ ɔ kasa nya ngɛ Zelza, ngɛ Benyamin zugba a nɔ. A ma de mo ke teji ɔmɛ nɛ nyɛ ho hlami ya a, a na mɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, o tsɛ jɔɔ a he susumi, se o he mohu e ngɛ tsui yee ngɛ, nɛ e ngɛ bie kpami ke, ‘Jije ma na ye bi ɔ ngɛ?’

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ ya nyɛ hɛ mi saii nɛ nyɛ ya su Tabor tso ngua a he ɔ, nyɛɛ kɛ nyumuhi etɛ maa kpe nɛ a yaa sã bɔ ha Mawu ngɛ Betel. Nɔ kake hɛɛ apletsi ku etɛ, nɔ kake hɛɛ abolo bɔbɔɛ etɛ, nɛ nɔ kake hu hɛɛ wai lohwe he womi tɔ kake.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, nyɛ maa ya Mawu yo ɔ nɔ ngɛ Gibea, he nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a ta a pueɔ si ngɛ ɔ. Nyɛ ma a mi sɛmi pɛ nyɛɛ kɛ gbali a kuu ko maa kpe nɛ a kple si kɛ je yoku ɔ nɔ kɛ ma kɛ a dɛ mi kpa saku, miɛ, kɛ bɛ. Nyɛ maa na kaa a ngɛ doe, nɛ a ngɛ huhui kpae.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Yawɛ mumi ɔ maa ba o nɔ; o maa do, nɛ o ma kpa huhui kaa mɛ, nɛ o ma plɛ pee nɔmlɔ kpa.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Ke ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ba mi ɔ, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Mawu ma de mo ke o pee ɔ, moo pee; ejakaa e kɛ mo ngɛ.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: O maa sɛ ye hlami kɛ ho Gilgal ya. Ma ba na mo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ ma sã sami bɔ, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔ. O maa mlɛ mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ligbi kpaago kɛ yaa si ma ba nɛ ma ba tsɔɔ mo nɔ́ nɛ o pee.”

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul kɛ Samuel ye sɛ nɛ a mi gba a, Mawu ha Saul tsui he; nɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Samuel de lɛ ɔ ba mi jamɛ a ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul kɛ e tsɔlɔ ɔ ya su Gibea a, e kɛ gbali a kuu ko kpe; nɛ tlukaa a, Mawu mumi ɔ ba e nɔ, nɛ e kɛ mɛ bɔni domi, kɛ huhui kpami.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Benɛ nihi nɛ le lɛ saminya a na e ní peepee ngɛ gbali ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ, a bi a he ke, “Mɛni lɛ ba Kish binyumu ɔ nɔ? Anɛ Saul hu ba plɛ pee gbalɔ lo?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ nɔ ko nɛ je lejɛ ɔ bi ke, “Gbali kpa amɛ ɔ, mɛnɔ bimɛ ji mɛ?” Nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ba pee nɔ́ ko nɛ a kɛ tuɔ munyu ke, “Anɛ Saul hu ba plɛ pee gbalɔ lo?”

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul do nɛ e kpa huhui ɔ se ɔ, e pue nɔ kɛ ho we mi ya.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Saul tsɛ nyɛminyumu ɔ bi Saul kɛ e tsɔlɔ ɔ ke, “Jije nyɛ je?” Saul he nɔ ke, “Wa ho ya hla teji ɔmɛ, nɛ nɛ́ wa nɛ mɛ ɔ, wa ya Samuel ngɔ.”

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Saul tsɛ nyɛminyumu ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Kɛ Samuel de nyɛ kɛɛ?”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Saul he nɔ ke, “E de wɔ ke a na teji ɔmɛ.” Se Saul de we e tsɛ nyɛminyumu ɔ ke Samuel de lɛ ke e ma ba ye matsɛ. A wo Saul matsɛ

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Samuel ha Israel ma a tsuo ba bɔ gua ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi ngɛ Mizpa,

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Imi lɛ i kpaka nyɛ kɛ je Egipt kɛ ba. Imi lɛ i kpɔ nyɛ ngɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ, kɛ ma kpa amɛ tsuo nɛ ngɛ nyɛ yi mi wae ɔ a dɛ mi.

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Imi ji nyɛ Mawu nɛ jeɔ nyɛ kɛ jeɔ haomi, kɛ nɔ́ nami tsuo mi. Se mwɔnɛ ɔ, nyɛ kua mi, nɛ nyɛ bi ke ma ha nyɛ matsɛ. Yoo, nyɛ ba bua nyɛ he nya wɛtso nya wɛtso nya, kɛ weku nya weku nya ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi.’ ”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Samuel tsɛ wɛtso ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi, nɛ a fɔ sɔ kɛ hla Benyamin wɛtso ɔ.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Samuel ha Benyamin wɛtso ɔ ba weku nya weku nya, nɛ a fɔ sɔ kɛ hla Matri weku ɔ. Nyagbe ɔ, nyumuhi nɛ je Matri weku ɔ mi hu ba kakaaka, nɛ a fɔ sɔ kɛ hla Saul, Kish binyumu ɔ. Se benɛ a ngɛ lɛ hlae ɔ, a nɛ lɛ.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a ya bi Yawɛ ke, “Jije nɔmlɔ ɔ ngɛ?” Nɛ Yawɛ de mɛ ke, “Saul ya laa e he ngɛ nito he ɔ.”

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a tu fo nɛ a ya nu lɛ kɛ ba. Benɛ e daa si ngɛ ni ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ, a na kaa e ka pe nɔ tsuaa nɔ.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Samuel de ma a tsuo ke, “Nyumu ɔ nɛ Yawɛ hla ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Nɔ ko nɔ ko be kaa lɛ ngɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo a kpɛti.” Kɛkɛ nɛ ma a tsuo hwɔ lele nɛ a de ke, “Matsɛ yi nɛ e na wa!”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Samuel tsɔɔ ma a bɔ nɛ matsɛ yemi ɔ blɔ nya tomi ngɛ ha, matsɛ ɔ blɔ nya nɛ e hɛɛ, kɛ e ní tsumi. E ngma nɔ́ nɛ ɔ kɛ wo womi mi, nɛ e ngɔ ya fɔ Yawɛ hɛ mi. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Samuel ha ma a nane, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ ho e we mi ya.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Saul hu kpale e se kɛ ho e ma mi, Gibea ya. Benɛ e yaa a, Mawu je nyumuhi oblai komɛ ha lɛ, nɛ a kɛ lɛ ho.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Se yaka nimli komɛ bi ke, “Kɛ nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ maa pee kɛ he wa yi wami kɛɛ?” A gbe e he guɛ, nɛ mɛɛ a ya ki lɛ ní. Se Saul pui a nya mi.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Maa pee hlami kake se ɔ, Matsɛ Nahash nɛ je Amon, kɛ e ta buli ya sa Yabesh Gilead yi. Nyumu ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ Yabesh ɔ de Nahash ke, “Ha waa kɛ mo nɛ so, konɛ wa sɔmɔ mo.”

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Se Nahash de mɛ ke, “Loko i kɛ nyɛ maa so ɔ, ma ta nɔ tsuaa nɔ hiɔ hɛngmɛ, nɛ i kɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ma pue Israel tsuo hɛ mi si.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Yabesh ma nimeli ɔmɛ de lɛ ke, “Ha wɔ ligbi kpaago nɛ waa tsɔ kɛ ya Israel ma amɛ tsuo a mi. Ke wa nɛ nɔ ko nɛ ma kpɔ wɔ ɔ, lɛɛ wa ma ha yi.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Tsɔli ɔmɛ ba su Gibea, he nɛ Saul ngɛ ɔ. Benɛ a bɔ ma a amaniɛ ɔ, ma a wo yana yuuyuuyuu.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Se benɛ a maa hyɛ ɔ, Saul ji nɛ ɔ nɛ e nyɛɛ e nahi a se kɛ je ngmɔ mi kɛ ma. Saul bi ke, “Mɛni ba loko ma a tsuo wo yana kikɛ nɛ ɔ?” A de lɛ sɛ gbi nɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ hɛɛ kɛ je Yabesh kɛ ba a.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul nu munyu nɛ ɔ, Mawu mumi ɔ ba e nɔ, nɛ e mi mi fu wawɛɛ nitsɛ.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: E nu na enyɔ nɛ e poo a mi kpɔ nya kpɔ nya, nɛ e ngɔ ha tsɔli ke a ya kpa Israel ma amɛ tsuo a mi nɛ a de ke, “Nɔ nɛ be bae nɛ e ba nyɛɛ Saul kɛ Samuel a se ɔ, jamɛatsɛ ɔ, bɔ nɛ a maa pee e nahi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ!” Yawɛ ha sawale nu ma a, nɛ mɛ tsuo kulaa a je kpo kɛ ba; e píɛ nɔ ko.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: A de tsɔli ɔmɛ nɛ je Yabesh Gilead kɛ ba a ke, “Nyɛ ya de nyɛ bi ɔmɛ ke, ‘Hwɔɔ, loko pu maa da a, a ma he nyɛ yi wami!’ ” Benɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ ya bɔ Yabesh bi ɔmɛ amaniɛ ɔ, a bua jɔ,

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: nɛ a de Nahash ke, “Hwɔɔ ɔ, wa ma ha yi, nɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ suɔ ɔ, nyɛɛ pee wɔ.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, Saul gba ma a mi kɛ wo tabo etɛ a mi. Makɛ ɔ, a ya sɛ he nyɛli ɔmɛ a ta a mi, nɛ a tua Amon bi ɔmɛ. A gbe Amon hluu kɛ ya si be nɛ pu da. Ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ gbɛ fĩa, nɛ o be a ti nihi enyɔ po nae ngɛ he kake.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ma a de Samuel ke, “Mɛnɔmɛ lɛ a de ke, ‘Anɛ Saul hu ma nyɛ wa nɔ matsɛ maa ye’ ɔ? Nyɛɛ ngɔ ni ɔmɛ ha wɔ nɛ waa gbe mɛ!”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Se Saul de ke, “Dɛbi, a be nɔ ko nɔ ko gbee mwɔnɛ ɔ, ejakaa mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, Yawɛ he Israel yi wami.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Samuel de ma a ke, “Nyɛ ha waa ya Gilgal nɛ wa ya ma matsɛ yemi ɔ nɔ mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Ma a tsuo ho nɛ a ya wo Saul matsɛ ngɛ Gilgal ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. A sã tue mi jɔmi bɔhi ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ Saul kɛ Israel ma a tsuo nyá babauu.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Samuel de Israel tsuo ke, “Nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ bi mi ɔ, i pee ha nyɛ; i wo matsɛ ha nyɛ.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, lɛ nɛ e maa nyɛɛ nyɛ hɛ mi. Imi lɛɛ i bwɔ, nɛ ye yi bwɔmi hiɛ futaa, nɛ ye binyumuhi ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti. I nyɛɛ nyɛ hɛ mi kɛ je ye nihe mi kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Imi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Ke i pee nɔ́ ko nɛ dɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ po ye nya ngɛ Yawɛ, kɛ nɔ nɛ a wo lɛ matsɛ ɔ a hɛ mi. Anɛ i kpɔ nɔ ko na, loo nɔ ko teji? Anɛ i ye nɔ ko amimi, aloo i wa nɔ ko yi mi? Anɛ i he nyɔ mi ní ngɛ nɔ ko dɛ bɔ nɛ pee nɛ ma ye e sane ɔ ha lɛ lo? Nyɛ de, konɛ ma to nyɛ nane mi.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Samuel ya nɔ nɛ e de ma a ke, “Yawɛ lɛ hla Mose kɛ Aaron, nɛ lɛ ji nɔ nɛ kpaka nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ kɛ ba.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ da si dii, konɛ ma po nyɛ nya ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi, nɛ ma kai nyɛ ní nguahi nɛ Yawɛ pee kɛ he nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ a yi wami.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yakob kɛ e bimɛ ɔmɛ ya Egipt, nɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ ngɛ mɛ yi mi wae ɔ, nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ fa kue ha Yawɛ, nɛ e tsɔ Mose kɛ Aaron nɛ a ya je mɛ kɛ je Egipt kɛ ba hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Se a hɛ je Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ nɔ. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, lɛ hu e ngɔ mɛ ngɔ wo Hazor tatsɛ Sisera, kɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Moab matsɛ ɔ a dɛ mi, nɛ a kɛ mɛ hwu ta.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a fa kue ha Yawɛ, nɛ a de ke, ‘Wa pee yayami, ejakaa wa je Yawɛ se nɛ wa ya ja Baal amaga amɛ, kɛ yo wɔ Ashtarot ɔ hu e we amaga amɛ. Mo kpɔ wɔ kɛ je wa he nyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi, nɛ wa ma sɔmɔ mo!’

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Se benɛ nyɛ na kaa Amon matsɛ, Nahash ma nyɛ tuami ɔ, nyɛ de mi ke, ‘Dɛbi, ja wa ná matsɛ nɛ e ye wa nɔ,’ be mi nɛ Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ ji nyɛ matsɛ.

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ne matsɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛ hla a; nyɛ bi ke a ha nyɛ matsɛ, nɛ Yawɛ ngɔ lɛ ngɔ ha nyɛ.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ maa ye Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ gbeye, nɛ nyɛ ma sɔmɔ lɛ, nɛ nyɛ be e hɛ mi atuã tsɔe, se nyɛ maa ye e mlaa amɛ a nɔ, nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ matsɛ ɔ maa nyɛɛ e se ɔ, lɛɛ e maa hi ha nyɛ.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Se ke nyɛ bui Yawɛ tue, nɛ nyɛ tsɔ atuã kɛ si e mlaa amɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ, kɛ nyɛ matsɛ ɔ tsuoyawɛ kɛ nyɛ maa ye saminya.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ da si dii, nɛ nyɛ maa na nyakpɛ ní nguaa nɛ Yawɛ ma tsu.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Anɛ pi ngma kpami be ji nɛ ɔ? Se ma tsɛ Yawɛ nɛ e ma ha hiɔwe ma si, nɛ hiɔmi maa nɛ konɛ nyɛ na nyɛɛ le kaa nyɛ pee Yawɛ yayami agbo kaa nyɛ bi ke a ha nyɛ matsɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Samuel fa kue ha Yawɛ, nɛ Yawɛ ha hiɔwe si, nɛ hiɔmi nɛ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ. Nɛ ma a tsuo ye Yawɛ kɛ Samuel gbeye wawɛɛ nitsɛ;

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: nɛ a de Samuel ke, “Kpa Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ pɛɛ ha wɔ, konɛ wa ko gbo; ejakaa wa na jehanɛ kaa ngɛ wa yayami kpa amɛ a se ɔ, wa pee yayami kaa wa bi ke a ha wɔ matsɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Se Samuel de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ ko ye gbeye. E ngɛ mi kaa nyɛ ná pee kikɛmɛ a yayami nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo lɛɛ, se kɛ̃, nyɛ ko je Yawɛ se; mohu nyɛ sɔmɔ lɛ kɛ nyɛ tsui tsuo.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko ya nyɛɛ yaka níhi nɛ a he be se nami, nɛ a be nyɛ yi wami nyɛe ma he ɔ a se; ejakaa yaka níhi kɛkɛ ji mɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Yawɛ be e ma nɛ e hla a he ngmɛɛe. Ke e pee ja pɛ kɛkɛ e biɛ kpetekpleenyɛ ɔ puɛ; ejakaa e sa e hɛ mi kaa e kɛ nyɛ maa pee lɛ nitsɛ e ma.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Imi lɛɛ ma kpa Yawɛ pɛɛ ha nyɛ daa, nɛ ma tsɔɔ nyɛ nɔ́ nɛ hi, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ da, konɛ ma ko pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ sa nyɛ peemi kɛkɛ ji nyɛɛ ye Yawɛ gbeye, nɛ nyɛ kai ní nguahi nɛ e pee ha nyɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Se ke nyɛ tsa nɔ pee yayami ɔ, lɛɛ e ma kpata nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ matsɛ ɔ tsuo nyɛ hɛ mi.”

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Israel tsuo nu kaa Saul gbe Filisti bi a nyatsɛ ɔ, nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha Filisti bi ɔmɛ a hɛ dɔ wo mɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma a bua a he nya, nɛ a bu Saul nɔ kɛ ho Gilgal ya.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: A ya tua Israel bi ɔmɛ wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ na kaa a yi fi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a ya laa a he ngɛ tɛ puɔhi, muɔhi, yɔkɔhi, vuhi, kɛ tɛ sahi a mi;

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: ni komɛ hu po Yordan pa a kɛ ho Gad kɛ Gilead zugba amɛ a nɔ ya. Se Saul lɛɛ e ngɛ Gilgal jamɛ a be ɔ kɛ mwɔɔ, nɛ sawale nu nihi nɛ nyɛɛ e se ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: E mlɛ ligbi kpaago kaa bɔ nɛ Samuel to lɛ ɔ, se Samuel bɛ Gilgal, nɛ ma a bɔni gbɛmi ngɛ e he.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e de ma a ke, “Nyɛɛ ngɔ sami bɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔ ɔmɛ kɛ ba.” Nɛ e sã sami bɔ ɔ.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Benɛ e sã sami bɔ ɔ ta pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ Samuel ba hia si. Saul je kpo ya kpee lɛ, nɛ e fɔ lɛ.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Se Samuel bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni o pee nɛ ɔ?” Saul he nɔ ke, “Ma a ngɛ gbɛe kɛ ngɛ fĩae ngɛ ye he, nɛ mo hu o bɛ be nɛ o to mi ɔ. Jehanɛ se hu, Filisti bi ɔmɛ ngɛ a he nya buae ngɛ Mikmash.

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i de ke, ‘Filisti bi ɔmɛ ma mi tuami ngɛ Gilgal be mi nɛ i bi we Yawɛ yemi kɛ buami.’ Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kɛ he hiami sã sami bɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuel de Saul ke, “O je kuasia; o yi Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ mlaa nɛ e wo mo ɔ nɔ; kaa o ye nɔ jinɛ o matsɛ yemi ngɛ Israel ɔ, Yawɛ ma ha nɛ e da si kɛ ya neneene.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Se amlɔ nɛ ɔ lɛɛ o matsɛ yemi ɔ be si dae. Yawɛ hla lɛ nitsɛ e tsui nya nɔmlɔ, nɛ e wo lɛ ganɔ ngɛ e ma a nya; ejakaa o yi mlaa nɛ e wo mo ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Samuel je Gilgal nɛ e pue nɔ kɛ ho Gibea ya ngɛ Benyamin. Benɛ Saul kane nihi nɛ kɛ lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, e ná maa pee nyumuhi lafa ekpa.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Saul kɛ e binyumu Yonatan, kɛ nihi nɛ piɛ a he ɔ ya bua a he nya ngɛ Geba ngɛ Benyamin; se Filisti bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ a ya bua a he nya ngɛ Mikmash.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Ní hali a kuu etɛ je Filisti bi ɔmɛ a sito he ɔ kɛ ya ha ní. Kuu kake ya Ofra ngɛ Shual zugba a nɔ;

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: kuu enyɔne ɔ gu Bet Horon blɔ, nɛ kuu nɛ ji etɛ ɔ hu gu Geba blɔ, ngɛ huzu ɔ nɛ ngɛ kɛ yaa Zeboim kɔ̃ ɔ mi blɔ ɔ kɛ ho nga a nɔ ya.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Sɔlɔ ko sɔlɔ ko be Israel zugba a nɔ tsuo; ejakaa Filisti bi ɔmɛ fia pɛɛ si kaa a be hae nɛ Hebri bi ɔmɛ nɛ a sɔ klaatehi, loo akplɔhi kɛ ha a he.

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Ke a duɔ gbiɛ nya, loo a dla a na tsɔmi dade ɔ, a heɔ kaplɛ nyafii kake. Se na kpakplaa, loo kpakplaa nitsɛ lɛɛ a heɔ kaplɛ nyafii enyɔ.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ta hwumi ligbi ɔ, a nɛ klaate, loo akplɔ ngɛ ta bulɔ ko dɛ; blɔɔ Saul kɛ e binyumu Yonatan pɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ hɛɛ klaate, loo akplɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Tɛ sa a kake ngɛ omleyi je ngɛ Mikmash hanɔ, nɛ kake hu ngɛ leneyi je ngɛ Geba hanɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Yonatan de niheyo ɔ nɛ hɛɛ e ta hwumi ní ɔmɛ ke, “Ha waa ho mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a sito he ɔ ya. Eko piɔ, Yawɛ ma tsu nyakpɛ ní ha wɔ; ejakaa nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko tsi Yawɛ nya kaa e kɛ nihi fuu, loo bɔɔ ma he nihi a yi wami.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Yonatan de lɛ ke, “Yoo, waa ho nɛ wa ya je wa he kpo kɛ tsɔɔ Filisti bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Ke a de wɔ ke waa mlɛ kɛ yaa si a maa ba wa ngɔ ɔ, wa maa da si dii ngɛ he nɛ wa ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Se ke a ke waa kuɔ kɛ ba a ngɔ ɔ, lɛɛ wa maa ya; ejakaa lɔ ɔ maa tsɔɔ wɔ kaa Yawɛ je mɛ kɛ wo wa dɛ mi.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, a de Yonatan kɛ e ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ ɔ ke, “Nyɛɛ kuɔ kɛ ba wa ngɔ; wa ngɛ nɔ́ ko nɛ wa ma de nyɛ.” Yonatan de e ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ ɔ ke, “Moo kuɔ kɛ nyɛɛ ye se, ejakaa Yawɛ ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo Israel dɛ mi.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Yonatan waa ngɛ e nine kɛ e nakutso nya kɛ kuɔ, nɛ e ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ ɔ nyɛɛ e se. Yonatan ya tua Filisti bi ɔmɛ nɛ e tsɛ̃ mɛ ko si; nɛ e ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ ɔ gbe mɛ ngɛ e se.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, kaa ma a ye ní nɛ a kpɔ ngɛ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ ɔ saminya a, jinɛ tse a ko gbe Filisti bi babauu pe kikɛ nɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo bua a he nya kɛ ya sɛ ta a mi; se basabasa a ha Filisti bi ɔmɛ wo klaate nɔ ngɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a sibi a nɔ.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Sawale nu Filisti bi ɔmɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ. Ta buli ɔmɛ, kɛ ní hali ɔmɛ tsuo a tsui po. Jehanɛ hu zugba mimiɛ, nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha sawale nɛ nu mɛ ɔ nya ba wa pe kekle ɔ. A gbe Filisti bi ɔmɛ

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Saul e buli ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Gibea ngɛ Benyamin ɔ na Filisti bi ɔmɛ nɛ a gbɛ fĩa, nɛ́ a ngɛ fo tue nɛ a li he nɛ a yaa.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul de e we bi ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ kane ta buli ɔmɛ nɛ waa le nɔ nɛ be hiɛ ɔ.” Benɛ a kane mɛ ɔ, a na kaa Yonatan kɛ e ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ ɔ be lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, osɔfo Ahiya ji nɔ nɛ ngɛ Mawu somi daka a nɔ hyɛe. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul de lɛ ke, “Yaa ngɔ Mawu somi daka a kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Se benɛ Saul kɛ osɔfo ɔ ngɛ munyu tue ɔ, basabasa nɛ te si ngɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ nya wa pe nine. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul de lɛ ke, “Koo ya hu; deka ko be kulaa!”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Hebri bi komɛ nɛ ya piɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a he ngɛ a sito he ɔ, a yi mi tsake nɛ a ba piɛ Saul kɛ Yonatan a he.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ hu, Israel bi tsuo nɛ ya laa a he ngɛ Efraim yo ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ, benɛ a nu kaa Filisti bi ɔmɛ ngɛ fo tue ɔ, mɛ hu a ba piɛ a nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a he nɛ a kɛ nyɛɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a se

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ na nɔ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, ejakaa Saul ka kita pue ma a nɔ ke, “Nɔ nɛ li peemi nɛ e maa ye nɔ́ ko loko je maa jɔ, be mi nɛ i na we ma ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a he lue lolo ɔ, a gbiɛ jamɛatsɛ ɔ.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ ko nɔ ko sɛ e nya nɔ́ ko ligbi ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Lejɛ ɔ tsuo pee kɛ hwo sɔuu, se nɔ ko nɔ ko yi; ejakaa ma a tsuo ngɛ kita nɛ Saul ka a gbeye yee.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Se Yonatan lɛɛ kita a nɛ e tsɛ ka fɔ ma a nɔ ɔ, e nui he, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e kɛ tso nɛ e hɛɛ ngɛ e dɛ ɔ nya sɔ hwo gbaku ɔ mi, nɛ e kɛ sa e nya; nɛ e na he wami he.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ ni ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake de lɛ ke, “Wɔ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ wa pee gbedee kɛ hwɔ; se o tsɛ ka kita ngɔ fɔ ma a nɔ ke, ‘Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ye nɔ́ ko mwɔnɛ ɔ, a gbiɛ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Yonatan he nɔ ke, “Mɛni haomi tsaatsɛ kɛ ba ma a nɔ nɛ ɔ. Nɛ i sa ye nya hwo bɔbɔyoo nɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ hyɛ bɔ nɛ i ba nɔmlɔ mi ha!

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ gbe Filisti bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Mikmash hluu kɛ ya su Aiyalon tɔɔ; nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ pee gbedee kɛ hwɔ.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a sa fo kɛ ho ta yibu ní ɔmɛ nɛ a ha a he ya. A ya nuu tohi kɛ nahi nɛ a gbe ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɔuu, nɛ a ye lo ɔ kɛ muɔ ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ nɔ ko ya de Saul ke, “Hyɛ, ma a ngɛ yayami pee kɛ ngɛ Yawɛ sie kaa a ngɛ lo kɛ muɔ tsuo yee.” Saul de ke, “Nyɛ tɔ̃! Nyɛ kpɛne tɛ agbo ko ba ha mi ngɛ hiɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: E ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Nyɛɛ gbɛ fĩa nɛ nyɛ ya de ma a ke, ‘Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ngɔ e na, loo e to kɛ ba nɛ e ba gbe ngɛ hiɛ ɔ nɛ e ye, konɛ nyɛ ko ye lo kɛ muɔ nɛ nyɛ ba pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ.’ ” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ hɛɛ e na kɛ ba jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ba gbe ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Saul puɛ bɔ sami la tɛ kɛ ha Yawɛ, nɛ lɔ ɔ ji kekleekle bɔ sami la tɛ nɛ e puɛ.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Saul de e we bi ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ ha waa ho nɛ wa ya tua Filisti bi ɔmɛ nyɔ mi; waa ha a níhi kɛ yaa si mɔtu, nɛ waa gbe mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.” Ma a he nɔ ke, “Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o suɔ kaa o maa pee ɔ, mo pee.” Se osɔfo ɔ de ke, “Nyɛ ha wa bi Mawu ga womi lolo.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul bi Mawu ke, “Ma ya tua Filisti bi ɔmɛ lo? Anɛ o maa ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo Israel dɛ mi lo?” Se Mawu ha we lɛ heto jamɛ a ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul de ma nikɔtɔma amɛ ke, “Nyɛ tsuo nyɛɛ ba hiɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛ ba hyɛ kaa nɔ ko pee yayami mwɔnɛ ɔ lo.

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: I na Yawɛ Israel yi wami helɔ ɔ, kaa ke ji ye bi Yonatan po nɛ pee yayami nɛ ɔ, ja a gbe lɛ.” Se nɔ ko nɔ ko de we nɔ́ ko.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Saul de Israel ma a tsuo ke, “Nyɛ ya da he kake, konɛ imi hu i kɛ ye bi Yonatan wa ya da he kake.” Ma a he nɔ ke, “Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o suɔ kaa o maa pee ɔ, moo pee.”

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Saul de ke, “Yawɛ Israel Mawu lee, mɛni he je o pui ye nya mi mwɔnɛ ɔ? Ha mi heto kɛ tɛ klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ. Yawɛ Israel Mawu lee, ke imi, loo ye bi Yonatan le nɔ́ nɛ ɔ he nɔ́ ko ɔ, moo tsɔɔ Urim; se ke o ma, Israel nɛ pee yayami ɔ, lɛɛ moo tsɔɔ Tumim.” Sɔ ɔ ya nɔ Saul kɛ e bi Yonatan a nɔ, nɛ Israel he je mi.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Saul de ke, “Nyɛɛ fɔ sɔ ngɛ i kɛ ye bi Yonatan wa nɔ.” Nɛ sɔ ɔ nɔ Yonatan nɔ.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul de Yonatan ke, “De mi nɔ́ nɛ o pee ɔ.” Yonatan de lɛ ke, “I ngɔ tso ɔ nɛ i hɛɛ ɔ nya kɛ sɔ hwo mi nɛ i lɔ. Imi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; i dla ye he kɛ ha gbenɔ.”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Saul de lɛ ke, “Yonatan, ja o gbo; ke a gbi mo fii, Mawu kɛ mi nɛ e ye!”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Se ma a de Saul ke, “Anɛ e sa kaa Yonatan nɛ́ ye kunimi nguaa nɛ ɔ kɛ ha Israel ɔ nɛ gbo lo? Dɛbi, e ko ba mi ja! Wa na Yawɛ hɛ kalɔ ɔ kaa Yonatan yi bwɔmi kake po be jee kɛ nɔ zugba; ejakaa ní nɛ e tsu mwɔnɛ ɔ, Mawu nine ngɛ mi.” Nɛ ma a he Yonatan yi wami, nɛ a gbi lɛ.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Saul jɔɔ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a se nyɛɛmi, nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ kpale kɛ ho mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba a nɔ ya.

english_verse: When Saul became king, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, the Philistines, and the Amalekites had all been robbing the Israelites. Saul fought back against these enemies and stopped them from robbing Israel. He was a brave commander and always won his battles. Saul's Family
translation_verse: E pee ka saminya, nɛ e ye Amalek bi ɔmɛ po a nɔ, nɛ e kpɔ Israel kɛ je nihi nɛ ye a nɔ ɔ tsuo a dɛ mi.

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Saul be ɔ mi ɔ, daa nɛ ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ ngɛ ta nɛ nya wa hwue. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, be tsuaa be nɛ Saul na nyumu oblai, loo katsɛ ko pɛ e ngɔ lɛ ngɔ piɛ e he.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Samuel de Saul ke, “Imi lɛ Yawɛ tsɔ nɛ i ba pɔ mo nu kɛ wo mo tsɛ ngɛ Israel ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Yawɛ maa gbla Amalek bi ɔmɛ a tue, ejakaa a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ya po Israel bi ɔmɛ blɔ benɛ a je Egipt kɛ ma a.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Yaa nɛ o ya tua Amalek bi ɔmɛ, nɛ o kpata a nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ hɛ mi. Ko si nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko; se mohu o gbe nyumuhi kɛ yihi, jokuɛwi kɛ bimwɔwi, nahi kɛ tohi, kɛ afukpɔngɔhi kɛ tejihi tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Saul bua e ta buli ɔmɛ a nya ngɛ Telem, nɛ benɛ a kane mɛ ɔ, a ná nihi akpe lafa enyɔ nɛ je Israel, kɛ akpe nyɔngma nɛ je Yuda.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Samuel ke,

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul ba Amalek ma a mi, nɛ e ba wo ka ngɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Saul tsɔ ya de Ken bi ɔmɛ nɛ ji ni komɛ nɛ a nɛmɛ na Israel bi ɔmɛ mɔbɔ benɛ a je Egipt kɛ ma a ke, “Nyɛɛ je Amalek bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti, konɛ ma ko kpata nyɛɛ kɛ mɛ tsuo nyɛ hɛ mi.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Ken bi ɔmɛ je Amalek bi ɔmɛ a he.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Saul gbe Amalek bi ɔmɛ kɛ je Havila kɛ ya si Shur ngɛ Egipt beleku je.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Saul kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ baa Agag yi, nɛ na kɛ na bi, jijɔ kɛ jijɔ bi kpakpa amɛ, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ hi ɔ, a kpataa we a hɛ mi; se níhi nɛ a hiee, kɛ níhi nɛ a he be se nami ɔ lɛɛ a kpata lɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ hɛ mi. Mawu kua Saul

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: “I pia ye he kaa i wo Saul matsɛ; ejakaa e je ye se nɛ e yi ye mlaa amɛ a nɔ.” Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ dɔ Samuel, nɛ e fa kue ha Yawɛ nyɔ ɔ mi tsuo.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: E nɔ jena mɔtu mla a, Samuel te si, konɛ e ya hla Saul. Se a de lɛ ke Saul ho Karmel, he nɛ e ma manye yemi kaimi nɔ́ kɛ ha lɛ nitsɛ e he ngɛ ɔ ya, nɛ e se kpalemi mi ɔ, e po mi kɛ ho Gilgal ya.

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Samuel ba su Saul ngɔ ɔ, Saul fɔ lɛ nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Yawɛ nɛ e gbaa mo! I ye Yawɛ fami ɔ nɔ.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Samuel bi ke, “Kɛ peeɔ kɛɛ nɛ i ngɛ jijɔhi, kɛ nahi a pɛmi he nue nɛ ɔ mɔ?”

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Saul he nɔ ke, “Ye we bi ɔmɛ kpɔ mɛ kɛ je Amalek bi ɔmɛ a dɛ. A baa jijɔ, kɛ na kpakpa amɛ a yi, konɛ a kɛ mɛ ba sã bɔ ha Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ; se ní nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ lɛɛ wa kpata mɛ tsuo a hɛ mi.”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Samuel de Saul ke, “Da si nɛ ma bɔ mo nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ de mi nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi.” Saul de lɛ ke, “Yaa o nya nɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuel de lɛ ke, “E ngɛ mi kaa o peeɔ o he humi mohu, se Israel wɛtso ɔmɛ a nyatsɛ ji mo. Yawɛ wo mo matsɛ ngɛ Israel.

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: E tsɔ mo, nɛ e de mo ke, ‘Yaa nɛ o kɛ Amalek yayami peeli ɔmɛ ya hwu nɛ o kpata a hɛ mi, nɛ e ko piɛ a ti nɔ kake po.’

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Mɛni he je nɛ o bui Yawɛ tue? Mɛni he je nɛ o he ya sɔ kɛ ha ta yibu ní, nɛ o pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Saul de Samuel ke, “I bu Yawɛ tue; tsɔmi nɛ e tsɔ mi ɔ, i ya. I kɛ Amalek matsɛ, Agag ɔ ba, nɛ i gbe Amalek bi ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Se ta yibu ní ɔmɛ a kpɛti jijɔ, kɛ na kpakpa amɛ nɛ a ke a kpata a hɛ mi ɔ, mɛɛ lɛɛ ma a muɔ mɛ kɛ ba Gilgal, konɛ a kɛ ba sã bɔ ha Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ.”

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Samuel bi ke, “Anɛ Yawɛ nyaa sami bɔ, kɛ bɔ kpahi a he pe e munyu ɔ tue bumi lo? O nɛ, tue bumi hi pe bɔ sami, nɛ munyu ngɔmi hi pe jijɔhi a zɔ.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Atuã tsɔmi ɔ, e ji yayami; e ngɛ kaa klaami, nɛ tue wami hu ngɛ kaa wɔ jami. Akɛnɛ o bui Yawɛ fami ɔ tue he je ɔ, lɛ hu e kua mo kaa matsɛ.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Saul de Samuel ke, “Niinɛ, i pee yayami; ejakaa i bui Yawɛ fami ɔ, kɛ mo hu o munyu ɔmɛ tue. I ya ye ma a gbeye, nɛ i bu mɛ tue.

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Se Samuel de Saul ke, “I kɛ mo be yae; o bui Yawɛ fami ɔ tue, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, lɛ hu e kua mo kaa matsɛ ngɛ Israel.”

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Benɛ Samuel plɛ nɛ e yaa a, Saul nu e bo ɔ nya; nɛ bo ɔ hía.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuel de lɛ ke, “Yawɛ hía Israel matsɛ yemi ɔ kɛ je o he mwɔnɛ ɔ, nɛ e ngɔ kɛ ha o nyɛmi ko nɛ hi pe mo.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Mawu nɛ ji Israel hɛ mi nyami ɔ, e yi lakpa, nɛ e tsakee we e yi mi tomi hulɔ; ejakaa tsa pi nɔmlɔ ji lɛ nɛ e ma tsake e yi mi tomi.”

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Saul de ke, “I pee yayami; se kɛ̃, moo wo ye hɛ mi nyami ngɛ ye ma nimeli, kɛ Israel tsuo a hɛ mi, nɛ o kɛ mi nɛ ya nɛ ma ya ja Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Samuel de ke, “Nyɛɛ ngɔ Amalek matsɛ, Agag ɔ kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ.” Agag ba kɛ bua jɔmi, nɛ e de ke, “Niinɛ, gbenɔ doomi ɔ be.”

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Se Samuel de lɛ ke, “Kaa bɔ nɛ o klaate ɔ ha binyɛmɛ kpatu plɛ pee nihi nɛ be bimɛ ɔ, ja nɔuu o nyɛ hu ma plɛ pee yosa ngɛ yihi a kpɛti.” Nɛ Samuel poo Agag mi kpɔ nya kpɔ nya ngɛ Yawɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ hɛ mi ngɛ Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Samuel pue nɔ kɛ ho Rama ya, nɛ Matsɛ Saul hu kpale kɛ ho e we mi ya ngɛ Gibea.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuel nɛ́ Saul hu kɛ ya si e gbenɔ ligbi; se daa nɛ ɔ, e yeɔ e he kɔmɔ. Nɛ Yawɛ pia e he kaa e wo Saul matsɛ ngɛ Israel.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ bi Samuel ke, “Mɛni be o maa ye Saul he kɔmɔ kɛ yaa si? O nɛ kaa i kua lɛ kaa matsɛ ngɛ Israel lo? Wo o koli ɔ mi nu nɛ e hyi tɔ, nɛ ma tsɔ mo Betlehem no, Ishai ɔ ngɔ; ejakaa i hla ye matsɛ ɔ kɛ je e binyumu ɔmɛ a kpɛti.”

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Se Samuel de ke, “Kɛ ma plɛ kɛ ya kɛɛ? Ke Saul nu he ɔ, e maa gbe mi.” Yawɛ ha heto ke, “Moo hɛɛ na bi kɛ to dɛ, nɛ o de ke, ‘I ba nɛ ma ba sã bɔ ha Yawɛ.’

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Moo kpee Ishai kɛ ba bɔ sami ɔ, nɛ ma tsɔɔ mo nɔ́ nɛ o pee. O maa pɔ nɔmlɔ nɛ ma tsɔɔ mo ɔ nu, nɛ o wo lɛ matsɛ ha mi.”

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samuel pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ɔ. E ya Betlehem, nɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ kɛ lɛ ba kpe kɛ he domi, nɛ a bi ke, “O ba ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi lo?”

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: E he nɔ ke, “Ee, i ba nɛ ma ba sã bɔ ha Yawɛ. Nyɛɛ tsukɔ nyɛ he nɛ waa ho bɔ sami he ɔ ya.” E tsukɔ Ishai kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e kpee mɛ hu kɛ ya bɔ sami he ɔ.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Benɛ a ya su lejɛ ɔ, Samuel na Eliab, nɛ e de ngɛ e yi mi ke, “Niinɛ, nɔ nɛ Yawɛ hla a nɛ daa si ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ de Samuel ke, “Koo hyɛ e kami, loo e he fɛu; i sume lɛ, ejakaa i hyɛ we nɔ́ kaa bɔ nɛ nɔmlɔ hyɛɛ nɔ́ ɔ. Nɔmlɔ lɛɛ nɔ hɛ mi e hyɛɛ; se imi Yawɛ lɛɛ tsui mi i hyɛɛ.”

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Ishai tsɛ e binyumu Abinadab, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ba be ngɛ Samuel hɛ mi. Se Samuel de ke, “Dɛbi, nɔ nɛ ɔ hu Yawɛ hlɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Ishai ha Shama ba. Se Samuel de ke, “Dɛbi, nɔ nɛ ɔ hu Yawɛ hlɛ lɛ.”

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
