translation_verse: Ishai tsa nɔ kikɛ nɛ ɔ kɛ ya si e ngɔ e binyumuhi kpaago kɛ ba Samuel hɛ mi. Se Samuel de Ishai ke, “Yawɛ hlɛ a ti nɔ ko nɔ ko.”

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Samuel bi Ishai ke, “O binyumu ɔmɛ tsuo ji nɛ ɔ lo?” E he nɔ ke, “E piɛ a kpɛti nɔ wayoo pe kulaa a, se lɛɛ e ngɛ tohi hyɛe.” Samuel de Ishai ke, “Tsɔ nɛ a ya ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba; ejakaa wa be si hie, ja e ba hiɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Ishai tsɔ nɛ a ya ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba. Ke o hyɛ lɛ ɔ, e tsuɔ papaapa; e hɛngmɛ nɔ tsɔ, nɛ e he hu ngɛ fɛu. Yawɛ de Samuel ke, “Tee si nɛ o pɔ lɛ nu, ejakaa lɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ!”

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Samuel wo nu kɛ koli ɔ, nɛ e pɔ David nu ngɛ e nyɛminyumu ɔmɛ a hɛ mi. Nɛ Yawɛ mumi ɔ ba David nɔ kɛ je jamɛ a ligbi ɔ. Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Samuel kpale e se kɛ ho Rama ya. David ba sɔmɔ Saul

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Yawɛ mumi ɔ je Saul nɔ, nɛ Yawɛ ha mumi yayami ko ba hao lɛ.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul tsɔli ɔmɛ de lɛ ke, “Wa kpa mo pɛɛ, mumi yayami ko lɛ Mawu kɛ ngɛ mo haoe nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Wa nyɔmtsɛ, mo fa wɔ, o tsɔli ɔmɛ mɔ, nɛ wa ya hla nɔ ko nɛ le saku fiami saminya kɛ ba, konɛ ke Mawu ha mumi yayami ɔ ba o nɔ ɔ, nɛ e fia saku ɔ, nɛ o na he wami ekohu.”

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Saul de e tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya hla nɔ ko nɛ le saku fiami saminya, nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba ye ngɔ.”

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Nihewi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake de lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, i le Ishai, Betlehem no ɔ binyumuyo ko nɛ le saku fiami saminya. Nyumu katsɛ kɛ ta hwulɔ ji lɛ. E nya mi tsɔ, nɛ e he ngɛ fɛu, nɛ Yawɛ kɛ lɛ ngɛ.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul tsɔ ya de Ishai ke, “Ha nɛ o bi David, to hyɛlɔ ɔ nɛ ba.”

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Ishai fi abolo, kɛ wai lohwe he womi tɔ kake, kɛ apletsi bi ngɔ fɔ teji se mi, nɛ e kɛ ha e binyumu David ke e ngɔ kɛ ya ha Saul.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: David ba Saul ngɔ nɛ e ba bɔni lɛ sɔmɔmi. Saul suɔ David sane saminya, nɛ e ngɔ lɛ kɛ pee e ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Saul tsɔ ya de Ishai ke, “I suɔ David sane; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ha nɛ e hi hiɛ ɔ nɛ e sɔmɔ mi.”

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ bua a tabo ɔmɛ a nya kɛ ha ta hwumi ngɛ Yuda ma ko nɛ a tsɛɛ Soko ɔ, nɛ a ya to si ngɛ Efes Damim, ngɛ Soko kɛ Azeka a kpɛti.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Filisti bi ɔmɛ wo zã ngɛ yoku kake nɔ, nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ hu wo zã ngɛ yoku kake nɔ; nɛ kɔ̃ ngɛ a kpɛti.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ tatsɛ kpanaa ko je Filisti bi ɔmɛ a ta a mi kɛ ba. A tsɛɛ lɛ Goliat; e je Gat, nɛ e kami ji nine mi blimi nyɔngma kɛ etɛ.

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: E wo akɔblee dama ngɛ e nane hulɔ, nɛ akɔblee tsɛ̃i ngɛ e konɔ.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, benɛ David gbe Goliat nɛ e kpale e se kɛ ba ta a mi ɔ, Abner kpaka lɛ ya ha Saul; nɛ David hɛɛ Filisti no ɔ yi tɔ ɔ kɛ mwɔɔ.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: E we akplɔ ɔ nya tso ngɛ kaa bo lolɔ gba tso, nɛ e we akplɔ ɔ yi dade jiimi ji kilo kpaago; nɛ e tsɛ̃i hɛɛlɔ ɔ nyɛɛ e hɛ mi.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Goliat ba da si ngɛ Israel tabo ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ e kpa huhui ke, “Mɛni he nyɛ gba ta ngɛ? Pi Filisti no ji mi? Nɛ nyɛ hu pi Saul tsɔli ji nyɛ? Nyɛɛ hla nyɛ kpɛti nɔ kake nɛ e kɛ mi ba kpe.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Ke e nyɛ nɛ e kɛ mi nɔ kunɔ nɛ e gbe mi ɔ, wa maa pee nyɛ nyɔguɛhi; se ke i ye e nɔ, nɛ i gbe lɛ ɔ, lɛɛ nyɛ maa pee wa nyɔguɛhi, nɛ nyɛ ma sɔmɔ wɔ.”

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul kɛ Israel tsuo nu munyuhi nɛ Filisti no ɔ ngɛ tue ɔ, a ye gbeye wawɛɛ nitsɛ. David ngɛ Saul ta a mi

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Efraim no ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Ishai ɔ binyumu ji David. E je Betlehem ngɛ Yuda. Ishai ngɛ binyumuhi kpaanyɔ; nɛ benɛ Saul ngɛ matsɛ yee ɔ, lɛɛ e bwɔ momo.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: Se David lɛɛ ke e sɔmɔ Saul bɔɔ kɛkɛ e je kɛ ho Betlehem ya ya hyɛ e tsɛ to ɔmɛ hu bɔɔ.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Daa mɔtu kɛ gbɔkuɛ ɔ, Goliat maa ba nɛ e ma ba tsɔ̃ Israel bi ɔmɛ a nya; e pee ja ligbi nyingmi eywiɛ sɔuu.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ngɔ e dɛma tso kɛ ma e dɛ, nɛ e ho ya kukuɔ dongo tɛ enuɔ ngɛ pa a mi, nɛ e kɛ wo e to hyɛlɔ kotoku ɔ mi. E hɛɛ e we amlami ɔ ngɛ e dɛ, nɛ e hɛ lɛ kɛ su Filisti no ɔ he. David gbe Goliat

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Ishai de e binyumu David ke, “Ngɔɔ ngma nɛ a si nɛ ɔ kilo nyɔngma, kɛ abolo bɔbɔɛ nyɔngma nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ya ha o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ ta nga a nɔ esɔesɔ.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, moo hɛɛ wagasi nyɔngma nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ya ha tatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma nɛ ngɛ a nya a. Slaa o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ o hyɛ bɔ nɛ a ngɛ, nɛ o kɛ okadi ko nɛ je a ngɔ kɛ ba.

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: David te si mɔtu mla, nɛ e si to ɔmɛ ha to hyɛlɔ kpa, nɛ e ngɔ niye ní ɔ, nɛ e pue nɔ kɛ ho kaa bɔ nɛ Ishai fa lɛ ɔ. E ya su ta nga a nɔ be mi nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ he ose kɛ je kpo kɛ yaa ta a nya.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ pe Israel tabo ɔ kɛ Filisti tabo ɔ kpe hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: David si ní ɔmɛ ha tlomi nɔ hyɛlɔ ɔ, nɛ e gbɔ fo kɛ ho ta a nya ya ya fɔ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ́ e kɛ hyɛ a hwɔhwɔɛ.

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: Benɛ e kɛ mɛ ngɛ munyu tue ɔ, Filisti bi a tatsɛ kpanaa a nɛ je Gat, nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Goliat ɔ hia kpo kɛ ba nɛ e ba tu munyu kaa kekle ɔ. Nɛ David nu nɔ́ nɛ e de ɔ.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ na nyumu ɔ, sawale nu mɛ, nɛ mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a tu fo.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ de a he ke, “Tse nyɛ na nyumu nɛ ɔ? Hyɛ, Israel ahlua nɛ e ma bɔmi nɛ ɔ nɛ. Matsɛ Saul wo si kaa nɔ nɛ ma nyɛ maa gbe lɛ ɔ, e maa wo lɛ ní babauu. Jehanɛ hu e kɛ e biyo ma ha lɛ, nɛ e tsɛ weku li maa ye a he kɛ je ma tó tsumi kɛ sɔmɔmi mi.”

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: David bi nyumu ɔmɛ nɛ daa si ngɛ e kasa nya a ke, “Nɔ nɛ maa gbe Filisti no nɛ ɔ, nɛ́ e ma je Israel kɛ je ahlua bɔmi nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, mɛni a maa pee ha lɛ? Mɛnɔ ji kikɛmɛ a Filisti no mɔmlɔtɔtsɛ nɛ ɔ, nɛ e ngɛ Mawu hɛ kalɔ ɔ tabo ɔmɛ ahlua bɔe kikɛ nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔmɛ he nɔ nɛ a tsɔɔ lɛ nɔ́ nɛ a maa pee kɛ ha nɔ nɛ maa gbe Goliat ɔ.

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Benɛ Davidmɛ awetsɛ Eliab nu nɛ David kɛ nyumu ɔmɛ ngɛ munyu tue ɔ, e mi mi fu David, nɛ e de ke, “Mɛni o ma hlami ngɛ hiɛ ɔ? Nɛ mɛnɔ o si to ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ kɛ ha? I le o nɔ buimi, kɛ o tsui wami kaa ta hwumi ɔ nɛ o ma hyɛmi nɛ ɔ nɛ!”

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: David bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni i pee? Pi munyu kɛkɛ nɛ i bi nɔ!”

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: David je e he, nɛ e ya na ni kpa komɛ. E bi mɛ jamɛ a munyu ɔ nɔuu, nɛ mɛ hu a ha lɛ heto kaa bɔ nɛ kekle ni ɔmɛ de lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Benɛ nyumu ɔmɛ na David juɛmi ɔ, a ya bɔ Saul amaniɛ, nɛ lɛ hu e tsɔ nɛ a ya ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: David de Saul ke, “Nɔ ko nɔ ko kó ye tsui ngɛ Filisti no nɛ ɔ he; i yaa nɛ i kɛ lɛ ya kpe.”

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Se Saul de lɛ ke, “Dɛbi, o be Filisti no nɛ ɔ nyɛe, ejakaa niheyo kɛkɛ ji mo; lɛɛ ta hwulɔ ji lɛ kɛ je e nihe mi.”

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Se David de Saul ke, “I hyɛɛ tsaatsɛ tohi; nɛ ke e ba mi kaa jata, loo osisiblisi ko ba nu to bi ko ngɛ to ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: i nyɛɛɔ e se nɛ i ya fiaa lɛ nɔ, nɛ i jeɔ to bi ɔ ngɛ e nya mi. Ke e plɛ kɛ wo mi ɔ, i nuɔ e tsitsa nɛ i fiaa lɛ nɔ́ kɛ ya siɔ e gboɔ.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: I gbe jatahi kɛ osisiblisihi hyɛ, nɛ ja nɔuu ma pee kikɛmɛ a Filisti no mɔmlɔtɔtsɛ nɛ ɔ, ejakaa e bɔ Mawu hɛ kalɔ ɔ tabo ɔmɛ ahlua.”

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: David ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Yawɛ nɛ́ je mi kɛ je jatahi kɛ osisiblisihi a dɛ mi ɔ ma je mi kɛ je Filisti no nɛ ɔ dɛ mi.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul de David ke, “Yaa, Yawɛ maa piɛ o he.”

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Saul ngɔ lɛ nitsɛ e ta hwumi ní ɔmɛ ngɔ ha David; e bu lɛ akɔblee pɛɛ, nɛ e wo lɛ dama.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: David fi Saul klaate ɔ kɛ wo dama a he, nɛ e ka nyɛɛmi, se e yɛ nya; ejakaa e kpla we jamɛ a ní ɔmɛ eko hyɛ. David de Saul ke, “I be nyɛe ma kpla ní nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ya, ejakaa a dɛ́ mi.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David je ní ɔmɛ pue si.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Filisti no ɔ hu bɔni nyɛɛmi kɛ ma David ngɔ, nɛ e ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ ɔ ngɛ e hɛ mi.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Benɛ e hyɛ David nɛ e na kaa niheyo tsutsuutsu papaapa nɛ he ngɛ fɛu kɛkɛ ji lɛ ɔ, e bui lɛ fɛɛ.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: E bi David ke, “Anɛ gbe ji mi nɛ o ma ye ngɔ kɛ tso ɔ?” E ya nɔ nɛ e tsɛ wɔ pue David nɔ, nɛ e gbiɛ lɛ,

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ba hiɛ ɔ, nɛ ma ngɔ o he lo ɔ ngɔ ha lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ, kɛ pu mi lohwehi.”

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: David de Filisti no ɔ ke, “Moo lɛɛ o kɛ klaate, akplɔ, kɛ kɛ̃ɛ̃ ma ye ngɔ; se imi lɛɛ i ma ngɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ, Israel tabo ɔmɛ a Mawu ɔ nɛ o ngɛ lɛ ahlua bɔe ɔ biɛ mi.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, Yawɛ ma je mo ngɔ wo ye dɛ mi; ma gbe mo, nɛ ma po o yi. Nɛ ma ngɔ Filisti ta buli ɔmɛ a gbogboehi kɛ ha lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ, kɛ pu mi lohwehi nɛ a ye. Nɛ je ɔ tsuo maa le kaa Mawu ko ngɛ Israel,

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: nɛ ma a nɛ bua ngɛ hiɛ ɔ hu maa le kaa pi klaate kɛ akplɔ nɛ Yawɛ kɛ heɔ nɔ yi wami. Yawɛ ye kunimi momo ngɛ ta a nya, nɛ e ma je nyɛ kɛ wo wa dɛ mi.”

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: David kɛ e nine wo kotoku ɔ mi, nɛ e je tɛ kake kɛ wo amlami ɔ mi, nɛ e fɔ. Tɛ ɔ ya na Filisti no ɔ hɛ nya, nɛ e sɛ lo ɔ mi; nɛ Goliat nɔ si bum, nɛ e hɛ mi ya bu si.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David hɛɛ we klaate lɛɛ, se e kɛ amlami kɛ amlami tɛ gbe Filisti no ɔ.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: David sa fo ya da Goliat nɔ. E hia Goliat klaate ɔ kɛ je kpo ɔ mi, nɛ e kɛ po e yi nɛ e gbe lɛ. Benɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ na kaa a tatsɛ kpanaa a gbo ɔ, a tu fo.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Israel kɛ Yuda tabo ɔmɛ hwɔ lele kɛ nyɛɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a se kɛ ya si Gat kɛ Ekron agbo ɔ nya tɔɔ. Filisti bi ɔmɛ plaa pue si ngɛ Sharaim blɔ ɔ he hluu kɛ ya si Gat kɛ Ekron tɔɔ.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ kpale ngɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a se kɛ ba a, a ba ha ní ngɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a ta a mi.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: David ngɔ Goliat yi ɔ kɛ ho Yerusalem ya; se Goliat ta hwumi ní ɔmɛ lɛɛ e ngɔ ya to lɛ nitsɛ e bo tsu mi. A kɛ David ya tsɔɔ Saul

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Benɛ David yaa nɛ e kɛ Filisti no ɔ ya kpe ɔ, Saul bi e tatsɛ, Abner ke, “Abner, mɛnɔ bi ji kikɛmɛ a niheyo nɛ ɔ?” Abner he nɔ ke, “Nɛnɛ, i na o nane kaa i li.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Saul bi lɛ ke, “Niheyo, mɛnɔ bi ji mo?” Nɛ David ha heto ke, “O tsɔlɔ Ishai, Betlehem no ɔ bi ji mi.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Saul tsi David nya kɛ je jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, nɛ e ngmɛ́ lɛ blɔ nɛ e kpale kɛ ho e tsɛ we ya hu.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Yonatan kpa e he bo kɛ ha David. E kɛ e ta hwumi ní ɔmɛ, e klaate ɔ, e kɛ̃ɛ̃ ɔ, kɛ e mlɛ mi fimi nɔ́ ɔ hu piɛ he ha lɛ.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: He tsuaa he nɛ Saul tsɔ David ɔ, e ya yeɔ manye. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, Saul wo lɛ asafoatsɛ, nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ sa Saul tsɔli, kɛ nihi tsuo a hɛ mi. Saul hɛ kɔ David nɔ

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Benɛ David gbe Goliat nɛ e kɛ ta buli ɔmɛ kpale a se kɛ ma a, Israel yi ɔmɛ je a ma amɛ tsuo a mi kɛ ba, nɛ a kɛ bua jɔmi la, kɛ do, kɛ kpa saku ba kpee Matsɛ Saul.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Benɛ yi ɔmɛ ngɛ nyae ɔ, a je la nɛ a he nɔ ke, “Saul gbe akpehi, se David lɛɛ e gbe akpe nyɔngmahi.”

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Munyu nɛ ɔ ngɔɛ Saul nya. E mi mi fu wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ e de ke, “A ngɔ akpe nyɔngmahi ngɔ ha David; se imi lɛɛ a ha mi akpehi pɛ. Mɛni pa piɛ mɔ nɛ e ma na pe matsɛ yemi ɔ?”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, mumi yayami ko nɛ je Mawu ngɔ ba Saul nɔ, nɛ e bɔni munyu tumi basabasa ngɛ e we ɔ mi kaa godotsɛ. Jamɛ a be ɔ, David ngɛ kpa saku ɔ fiae kaa bɔ nɛ e peeɔ daa ligbi ɔ. Saul hɛɛ e we akplɔ ɔ ngɛ e dɛ mi,

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: nɛ e de ngɛ e yi mi ke, “Ma hɛ David akplɔ kɛ pi gbogbo ɔ.” Kɛkɛ nɛ e hɛ lɛ akplɔ ɔ si enyɔ; se David yu e he nɛ e je mi slɔkee.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Saul ye David gbeye, ejakaa Yawɛ kɛ David ngɛ; se lɛ Saul ɔ lɛɛ Yawɛ je e se.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: nɛ e yeɔ manye ngɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ mi; ejakaa Yawɛ kɛ lɛ ngɛ.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Se Israel kɛ Yuda tsuo suɔ lɛ saminya, ejakaa ma hɛ mi nyɛɛlɔ kpakpa ji lɛ. David ngɔ Saul biyo

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Saul de David ke, “O nɛ, ye biyo nɔkɔtɔma Merab ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Ke o maa pee kã, nɛ o maa hwu Yawɛ ta amɛ ha mi ɔ, i kɛ lɛ ma ha mo.” Saul susu kaa ke e pee ja a, Filisti bi ɔmɛ a nine maa su David nɔ nɛ a maa gbe lɛ, nɛ lɛɛ e nine be e he sae.

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: David he nɔ ke, “Mɛnɔ ji mi, nɛ ye tsɛ we ɔ hu mɛnɔmɛ ji mɛ ngɛ Israel, nɛ́ imi nɛ ɔ i ba peeɔ matsɛ lɛɛ e ngatsɛ?”

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Se benɛ e su be nɛ a kɛ Saul biyo Merab ma ha David ɔ, a ngɔ lɛ ngɔ ha Adriel, Mehola no ɔ mohu.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul biyo Mikal ba suɔ David sane; benɛ Saul nu he ɔ, e na he bua jɔmi.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Saul susumi ji e kɛ e biyo Mikal ma ha David nɛ e kɛ tsɔ lɛ klama, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a nine nɛ su e nɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul de David si enyɔne ɔ ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ o maa pee ye ngatsɛ.”

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Saul tsɔli ɔmɛ ya sɛɛ ní nɛ ɔ ha David, nɛ David de ke, “Matsɛ e ngatsɛ peemi ɔ, e ji hɛ mi nyami agbo! Imi ohiatsɛ nɛ i be blɔ nya ko ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ ɔ kle pe mi.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Saul tsɔli ɔmɛ ya bɔ Saul nɔ́ nɛ David de ɔ.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Saul fa mɛ ke a ya de David ke, “Matsɛ ɔ hla we yo se ní kpa ko pe Filisti bi a mɔmlɔtɔ lafa kɛkɛ nɛ e kɛ ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a he lue.” Saul to kikɛmɛ a ga nɛ ɔ bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a nine nɛ su David nɔ nɛ a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul tsɔli ɔmɛ ya bɔ David amaniɛ nɛ ɔ, e ngɔ David nya saminya kaa e maa pee matsɛ ɔ ngatsɛ. Loko be nɛ a to ɔ su ɔ,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Saul ba yɔse faii kaa Yawɛ kɛ David ngɛ, nɛ e biyo Mikal ɔ hu suɔ lɛ.

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e ye David gbeye pe kekle ɔ po, nɛ David ba plɛ pee e he nyɛlɔ e wami ligbi tsuo.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Ke pee ɔ, Filisti ganɔ ɔmɛ ba tuaa Israel bi ɔmɛ. Se be tsuaa be nɛ ta ko maa te si ɔ, David yeɔ kunimi pe Saul tsɔli kpa amɛ tsuo. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha David na biɛ wawɛɛ nitsɛ.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Saul de e binyumu Yonatan kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ kulaa ke a gbe David. Se suɔmi babauu nɛ Yonatan ngɛ kɛ ha David he je ɔ,

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: Imi lɛɛ ma ya nɛ ma ya da tsaatsɛ kasa nya ngɛ nga a nɔ he nɛ o ngɛ ɔ, nɛ i kɛ lɛ maa tu munyu ngɛ o he; nɛ bɔ nɛ e ma ya ba ha a, ma ha nɛ o le.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: E ngɔ e wami ngɔ ke, benɛ e gbe Filisti no ɔ, nɛ Yawɛ ye kunimi nguaa kɛ ha Israel tsuo. O na, nɛ o bua jɔ he. Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ o ngɛ hlae nɛ o gbe David yaka gu nɛ e pee we mo yayami ko ɔ?”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Saul bu Yonatan munyu ɔ tue; nɛ e kɛ Yawɛ biɛ ka kita ke e be David gbee.

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Yonatan ya tsɛ David nɛ e bɔ lɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e kɛ lɛ ba Saul ngɔ, nɛ David sɔmɔ Matsɛ Saul kaa kekle ɔ.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Se ta te si ekohu, nɛ David ya nɛ e kɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ ya hwu, nɛ e gbe mɛ basabasa; nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ tu fo kɛ je ta a nya.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: Saul ka kaa e maa hɛ David akplɔ ɔ kɛ wo gbogbo ɔ he, se David yu e he nɛ akplɔ ɔ ya pi gbogbo ɔ. Nɛ David tu fo kɛ je.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, Saul tsɔ nihi kɛ ho David we ɔ mi ya nɛ́ a ya huɔ lɛ, konɛ mɔtu nɛ a gbe lɛ. Se David yo Mikal de lɛ ke, “Ke o ji hiɛ ɔ nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi nɛ o he o yi wami ɔ, hwɔɔ ɔ, a maa gbe mo.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Mikal ngɔ David kɛ gu saflɛ mi kɛ kple si; nɛ e tu fo kɛ je.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Mikal ngɔ amaga ko kɛ fɔ sa a nɔ, nɛ e ngɔ sɔnue nɛ a kɛ apletsi he bwɔmi pee fɔ e yi je, nɛ e ngɔ bo ha he.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul tsɔli ɔmɛ ba konɛ a ba nu David kɛ ho ɔ, Mikal de mɛ ke e be he wami.

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Saul de tsɔli ɔmɛ ke a kpale nɛ a ya hyɛ kaa a maa na David ɔ lo. E fa mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ngɔ lɛ kɛ sa a tsuo ba ha mi nɛ ma gbe lɛ.”

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Benɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ kpale kɛ ba a, a ba na amaga a ngɛ sa a nɔ nɛ sɔnue nɛ a kɛ apletsi he bwɔmi pee fɔɔ si ngɛ e yi je.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Saul bi Mikal ke, “Mɛni he je nɛ o sisi mi kikɛ nɛ ɔ, nɛ o ha ye he nyɛlɔ ɔ tu fo kɛ je ɔ?” Mikal he nɔ ke, “E de mi ke ke i ha we lɛ blɔ nɛ e ho ɔ, e maa gbe mi.” David kɛ Samuel ngɛ Rama

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: David tu fo kɛ ho Samuel ngɔ ya ngɛ Rama, nɛ e ya bɔ lɛ nɔ́ nɛ Saul pee lɛ ɔ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ. David kɛ Samuel ho Nayot ya, nɛ a ya hi lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul nu kaa David ngɛ Nayot ngɛ Rama a,

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: e tsɔ nihi ke a ya nu lɛ kɛ ba. Se benɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ na gbali a kuu ɔ nɛ a ngɛ doe, nɛ a ngɛ huhui kpae, nɛ Samuel hu ngɛ a kpɛti kaa a nyatsɛ ɔ, Mawu mumi ɔ ba Saul tsɔli ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ mɛ hu a bɔni domi kɛ huhui kpami.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul nu he ɔ, e tsɔ ni kpahi kɛ ho; se mɛ hu a do nɛ a kpa huhui ja nɔuu. Saul kpale tsɔ nihi kɛ ho si etɛne; nɛ mɛ hu a pee ja nɔuu.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul nitsɛ pue nɔ kɛ ho Rama ya, nɛ benɛ e ya su vu nguaa a he ngɛ Seku ɔ, e bi ke, “Jije Samuel kɛ David ngɛ?” Nɛ nɔ ko ha lɛ heto ke, “A ngɛ Nayot ngɛ Rama.”

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Benɛ e je lejɛ ɔ kɛ yaa Nayot ngɛ Rama a, Mawu mumi ɔ ba lɛ hu e nɔ; nɛ e do nɛ e kpa huhui kɛ nyɛɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ ya su Nayot.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: E jé e he tade ɔmɛ, nɛ e do nɛ e kpa huhui ngɛ Samuel hɛ mi, nɛ e hɛɛ e he gu jamɛ a ligbi ɔ piani kɛ nyɔ mi tsuo. Nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ba pee nɔ́ ko nɛ a kɛ tuɔ munyu “Anɛ Saul hu ba plɛ pee gbalɔ lo?”

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, David tu fo kɛ je Nayot ngɛ Rama kɛ ba Yonatan ngɔ, nɛ e ba bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni i pee? Mɛni ji ye tɔmi? Mɛni yayami i pee o tsɛ loko e ngɛ mi hlae nɛ e gbe ɔ?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Yonatan he nɔ ke, “Dɛbi! O be gboe. Hyɛ, tsaatsɛ pee we nɔ́ ko nguaa, loo bɔbɔyoo nɛ e wo we ye tue nɔ ngɛ he. E be mi!”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Se David he nɔ ke, “O tsɛ le saminya kaa o suɔ ye sane; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e pee e juɛmi kaa e be hae nɛ o le nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ e ko hao mo. Se anɔkuale, i na Yawɛ hɛ kalɔ ɔ kaa nane hiami kake pɛ lɛ ngɛ i kɛ gbenɔ wa kpɛti.”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Yonatan de David ke, “Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ hlae ɔ, de mi nɛ ma pee ha mo.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: David de Yonatan ke, “Hyɛ, hwɔɔ ji Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be ɔ nɛ, nɛ jinɛ e sa kaa i kɛ matsɛ ya ye ní. Se ha nɛ ma ya laa ye he ngɛ nga a nɔ kɛ yaa si ligbi etɛne ɔ gbɔkuɛ nya si.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Ke o tsɛ bi ye si ɔ, de lɛ ke, ‘David bi mi blɔ wawɛɛ ke e maa po e he bɔɔ kɛ ya e ma mi ngɛ Betlehem nɛ e ba; ejakaa a ngɛ jeha bɔ sãe ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ha weku ɔ tsuo.’

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Ke e de ke, ‘Yoo!’ ɔ, o tsɔlɔ yi ma na wami; se ke e mi mi fu ɔ, lɛɛ o na nɛ o le kaa e muɔ e yi mi kpɔ kaa e maa pee mi yayami.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, naa mi mɔbɔ, nɛ o ye somi nɛ o kɛ mi so ngɛ Yawɛ biɛ mi ɔ nɔ. Se ke i yeɔ fɔ ɔ, lɛɛ mo nitsɛ moo gbe mi. Mɛni he je o maa ngɔ mi kɛ ya ha o tsɛ?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Se Yonatan de ke, “Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ nɛ ko ba o juɛmi mi kulaa! Ke i le kaa tsaatsɛ to kaa e maa pee mo yayami ko ɔ, i ko de we mo lo?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Yonatan he nɔ ke, “Ha nɛ waa ho nga a nɔ ya.” Mɛ ni enyɔ ɔmɛ a pue nɔ kɛ ho nga a nɔ ya.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Yonatan de David ke, “I ngɛ mo si woe ngɛ Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ biɛ mi kaa hwɔɔ, loo hwɔɔ se maa pee be nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, ma hla juɛmi nɛ tsaatsɛ ngɛ ngɛ o he. Ke e ngɛ o he juɛmi kpakpa a, ma tsɔ ba de mo.

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Se ke tsaatsɛ to kaa e maa pee mo yayami, nɛ i wo we o tue nɔ nɛ ma wo mo blɔ nɛ ó ya ngɛ he jɔmi mi ɔ, lɛɛ Yawɛ kɛ imi, Yonatan nɛ e ye sisiisi. Yawɛ kɛ mo nɛ e hi si kaa bɔ nɛ e kɛ tsaatsɛ hi si ɔ.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: ko ha o mi mi himi ɔ se nɛ e po ngɛ ye weku li a nɔ ligbi ko ligbi ko. Ke Yawɛ kpata o he nyɛli ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ,

english_verse: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
translation_verse: ko ha Yonatan biɛ nɛ e laa ngɛ David weku ɔ mi. Ke o pee ja a, Yawɛ kɛ mo maa ye.”

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Yonatan ha David kpale ka lɛ kita ekohu kaa e suɔ lɛ, ejakaa lɛ, Yonatan ɔ nitsɛ e suɔ David kaa bɔ nɛ e suɔ lɛ nitsɛ e he.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Yonatan de David ke, “Hwɔɔ ji Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be ɔ nɛ. A ma bi o si, ejakaa o sɛ ɔ maa fɔ si gu.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Hwɔɔ se lɛɛ a ma pa bi o si tsɔ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, yaa he nɛ o ya laa o he ngɛ ligbi ɔ benɛ sane ɔ ba a, nɛ o ya laa o he ngɛ tɛhi nɛ a bua nya a a se.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Ma tsɛ̃ kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi etɛ kɛ ya lejɛ ɔ kaa nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ ye dɛ nya dami kae.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ma ha nɛ ye tsɔlɔ ɔ ya kukuɔ mɛ kɛ ba. Ke i de ke, ‘Hyɛ, kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi ɔmɛ ngɛ hiɛ blɔ; yaa nɛ o ya kukuɔ mɛ’ ɔ; e tsɔɔ kaa o ma nyɛ maa ba, ejakaa gbeye ko be. I na Yawɛ, hɛ kalɔ ɔ kaa nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be mo pee.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Se ke i de niheyo ɔ ke, ‘Hyɛ, kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi ɔmɛ ngɛ o hɛ mi’ ɔ, lɛɛ yaa; ejakaa Yawɛ nɛ e ke o je hiɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Si nɛ wa wo wa sibi ɔ, Yawɛ nɛ e ha waa ye nɔ daa.”

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David ho ya laa e he ngɛ nga a nɔ. Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be ɔ, Matsɛ Saul ba ní yemi he ɔ,

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: nɛ e hi e sɛ ɔ nɔ ngɛ gbogbo ɔ he he nɛ e hii daa a. Yonatan hi e hɛ mi, nɛ Abner hi e kasa nya. Se David lɛɛ e blɔ he ɔ fɔɔ si.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Saul de we nɔ́ ko jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, ejakaa e de ngɛ e yi mi ke, “Be nɛ ɔ mi matahu ko ya po lɛ, nɛ e he tsɔ we.”

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: E nɔ jena nɛ ji ligbi nɛ nyɛɛ Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be ɔ se ɔ, David blɔ he ɔ fɔɔ si ekohu. Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul bi Yonatan ke, “Mɛni he je Ishai binyumu ɔ ba yi ní hiɛ kɛ mwɔnɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: E ke, ‘I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o ha ma ya, ejakaa wa weku ɔ ngɛ bɔ sãe ngɛ ma a mi, nɛ ye nyɛminyumu ɔmɛ sɛ ba de mi ke ma ba dãã. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke o suɔ mi ɔ, ha ma ya nɛ ma ya na ye nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ.’ Nɔ́ nɛ he je nɛ e bɛ matsɛ ɔ okplɔɔ he ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Saul mi mi fu Yonatan wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Mo, yo ajuama kɛ atuã tsɔlɔ mi bi! O bu kaa i li kaa o ngɔ Ishai binyumu ɔ ngɔ pee o huɛ, nɛ o kɛ pue mo nitsɛ kɛ o nyɛ tsuo nyɛ hɛ mi si!

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Anɛ o li kaa ligbi abɔ nɛ David ngɛ je mi ɔ, o be matsɛ yee gblegbleegble ngɛ zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ lo? Yaa nɛ o ya ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ; ja e gbo!”

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Yonatan bi e tsɛ Saul ke, “Mɛni he je a maa gbe lɛ? Mɛni e pee?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul fɔ e we akplɔ ɔ, konɛ e kɛ gbe Yonatan. Nɛ Yonatan kɛ yɔse kaa e tsɛ muɔ e yi mi kpɔ kaa e maa gbe David.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Yonatan kɛ abofu nɛ nya wa te si kɛ je okplɔɔ ɔ he, nɛ e yi nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko ngɛ Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be ɔ we ligbi enyɔne ɔ nɔ. David he pee lɛ mɔbɔ wawɛɛ nitsɛ, ejakaa Saul pue e hɛ mi si.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: E nɔ jena mɔtu ɔ, Yonatan ho nga a nɔ ya, konɛ e kɛ David ya kpe kaa bɔ nɛ a de to momo ɔ. E kɛ niheyo wayoo ko ho,

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: nɛ e de niheyo ɔ ke, “Tuu fo nɛ o ya kukuɔ kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bihi nɛ ma tsɛ̃ ɔ kɛ ba!” Benɛ niheyo ɔ wo fo pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ Yonatan tsɛ̃ kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi kake kɛ be e he.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Se niheyo ɔ li nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ nɔ yae; blɔɔ Yonatan kɛ David pɛ nɛ a le.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Yonatan kɛ e ta hwumi ní ɔmɛ ha niheyo ɔ, nɛ e de lɛ ke e ngɔ kɛ ho ma a mi ya.

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Benɛ niheyo ɔ je ɔ, David te si kɛ je tɛ nɛ a bua nya a se. E ba kpla si nɛ e kɛ e hɛ mi bu si si etɛ; nɛ e kɛ Yonatan fua a sibi, nɛ a fo ya ngɔ pue a sibi a nɔ. Se David aywilɛho ɔ nya wa pe Yonatan nɔ́ ɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yonatan de David ke, “Yaa ngɛ he jɔmi mi. Kita a nɛ i kɛ mo tsuo wa ka wa he ngɛ Yawɛ biɛ mi ɔ, Yawɛ ma ha nɛ i kɛ mo, kɛ o nina, kɛ imi hu ye nina wa maa ye nɔ kɛ maa ya neneene.” Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, David je lejɛ ɔ, nɛ Yonatan hu kpale e se kɛ ho ma a mi ya.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: David ba Nob ngɛ osɔfo Ahimelek ngɔ. Ahimelek kɛ he domi ba kpee David, nɛ e bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he je nɛ mo nɔ kake too o nyɛɛ, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko piɛ we o he ɔ?”

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: David de osɔfo Ahimelek ke, “Matsɛ tsɔ mi, nɛ e de mi ke ma ko ha nɛ nɔ ko nɛ le nɔ́ nɛ he nɛ e tsɔ mi ngɛ ɔ. Ye we bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ i kɛ mɛ so kaa a kɛ mi nɛ e kpe ngɛ he ko.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, mɛni ngɛ o dɛ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ? Ha mi abolo enuɔ, loo nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ o dɛ.”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Osɔfo ɔ de David ke, “I be abolo gu ko ngɛ hiɛ ɔ; abolo klɔuklɔu lɛ ngɛ. Ke o we bi ɔmɛ ya tɛ yihi a he ɔ, lɛɛ ma nyɛ ma ha nyɛ.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: David de osɔfo ɔ ke, “Niinɛ, be nɛ wa ngɛ ní tsumi ko nɔ ɔ, wa tɛ yihi a he. Nihewi ɔmɛ hyɛɛ a he nɔ saminya ke wa nyɛɛ nyɛɛmi gu po. Anɛ mwɔnɛ ɔ nɛ wa ngɛ ní tsumi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ ɔ, a be a he pee klɔuklɔu lo?”

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, osɔfo ɔ ngɔ abolo klɔuklɔu ɔ ngɔ ha lɛ; ejakaa abolo kpa ko be lejɛ ɔ, pe abolo klɛdɛɛ ɔ nɛ a je kɛ je Yawɛ hɛ mi ligbi ɔ nɛ a kɛ abolo kala a tsake ɔ.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, Saul tsɔli ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ a tsi e nya ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. E biɛ ji Doeg; e je Edom, nɛ Saul lohwehi a hyɛli ɔmɛ a nɔkɔtɔma ji lɛ.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: David bi Ahimelek ke, “O be akplɔ, loo klaate ko ngɛ hiɛ ɔ lo? Matsɛ tsɔmi ɔ he esɔ nɛ i ngɛ yee ɔ ha nɛ i je ye klaate kɛ ta hwumi ní kpa amɛ a he.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Osɔfo ɔ he nɔ ke, “Goliat, Filisti no ɔ nɛ o gbe ngɛ Ela kɔ̃ ɔ mi ɔ, e klaate ɔ fɔɔ si ngɛ efɔd ɔ se nɛ a ha he bo. Ke o suɔ ɔ, ngɔɔ; ejakaa klaate kpa ko be hiɛ ɔ hu.” David de ke, “Ngɔɔ lɛ ha mi; klaate ko be nɛ hi kɛ lɛ sɔ.”

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, David tu fo kɛ je Saul he kɛ ho Gat matsɛ, Akish ngɔ ya.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Akish tsɔli ɔmɛ ya de Akish ke, “Anɛ pi David, zugba a nɔ matsɛ ɔ ji nɛ ɔ lo? Anɛ yihi la we nɛ a do, nɛ a de ngɛ e he ke, ‘Saul gbe akpehi, se David gbe akpe nyɔngmahi lo?’ ”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: David susu munyu nɛ ɔmɛ a he saminya, nɛ e ye Gat matsɛ, Akish gbeye wawɛɛ nitsɛ.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e tsake e ní peepee, nɛ e buá pee e he godotsɛ ngɛ a kpɛti. E maa ngma ní ngɛ matsɛ we agbo ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e maa la lada kɛ kpa e kpɛni he kpɔtɔɔ.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Akish bi e tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “Nɛ nyɛ na kaa nɔ ɔ nu godo ɔ, mɛni he je nyɛɛ kɛ lɛ ba ye ngɔ mɔ?

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: David tu fo kɛ je Gat kɛ ho Adulam tɛ puɔ ɔ mi ya. Benɛ e nyɛminyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ e weku li tsuo nu e he ɔ, a bu e nɔ kɛ ya na lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Ni kpa komɛ hu ba piɛ David he. Mɛ ji nihi nɛ a ngɛ mɛ yi mi wae, nihi nɛ hɛɛ hiɔ, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ a pee mɛ nidɔ níhi, nɛ David pee a nyatsɛ. Nihi nɛ nyɛɛ e se ɔ a yibɔ maa pee lafa eywiɛ.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: David je lejɛ ɔ kɛ ho Mizpa ya ngɛ Moab, nɛ e ya de Moab matsɛ ɔ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, ha nɛ tsaatsɛ kɛ maa nɛ a ba hi nyɛ ngɔ kɛ yaa si ma le nɔ́ nɛ Mawu maa pee ha mi.”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David si e fɔli ɔmɛ ngɔ ha Moab matsɛ ɔ, nɛ a hi e ngɔ be mi nɛ e ngɛ e he lae ngɛ tɛ puɔ ɔ mi ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Gbalɔ Gad ba de David ke, “Koo hi tɛ puɔ nɛ ɔ mi; moo je hiɛ ɔ esɔ kɛ ho Yuda zugba a nɔ ya.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David je kɛ ho Heret hue ɔ mi ya.

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Saul ba nu kaa a ya na David kɛ nyumuhi nɛ piɛ e he ɔ. Jamɛ a be ɔ, Saul hii si ngɛ tso nguaa ko sisi ngɛ yoku ko nɔ ngɛ Gibea. E hɛɛ e we akplɔ ɔ ngɛ e dɛ, nɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo daa si kɛ bɔle lɛ.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul de e tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ Benyamin bi, nyɛɛ bu tue! Pe nyɛ susu kaa Ishai binyumu ɔ ma ha nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ zugba kɛ wai ngmɔ, nɛ e maa pee nyɛ tsuo kulaa asafoatsɛmɛ ngɛ nihi akpehi kɛ lafahi a nya,

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: loko nyɛ tsuo nyɛ so kɛ wo ye he kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Nɔ ko nɔ ko wo we ye tue nɔ kaa ye binyumu ɔ kɛ David so somi ko. Nɔ ko nɔ ko be nyɛ kpɛti nɛ ye sane dɔɔ lɛ, nɛ e ma wo ye tue nɔ kaa imi nitsɛ ye binyumu ha nɛ ye tsɔlɔ te si wo mi, nɛ mwɔnɛ ɔ, e ngɛ ye he blɔ hlae nɛ e gbe mi.”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Doeg, Edom no ɔ nɛ lɛ hu e daa si ngɛ Saul tsɔli ɔmɛ a kasa nya a, he nɔ nɛ e de ke, “I na Ishai binyumu ɔ benɛ e ba Ahitub binyumu Ahimelek ngɔ ngɛ Nob.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Ahimelek bi Yawɛ ga womi ha David. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ha lɛ ní, nɛ e ngɔ Goliat, Filisti no ɔ klaate ɔ hu ngɔ ha lɛ.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Matsɛ Saul tsɔ nɛ a ya tsɛ osɔfo Ahimelek, Ahitub binyumu ɔ, kɛ e weku li nɛ ji osɔfohi nɛ ngɛ Nob ɔ tsuo kulaa kɛ ba.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Saul de Ahimelek ke, “Ahitub binyumu, bu tue!” Nɛ e he nɔ ke, “I ngɛ tue bue, ye nyɔmtsɛ.”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Saul bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he je nɛ o kɛ Ishai binyumu ɔ nyɛ so wo ye he ɔ? Mɛni he je o ha lɛ niye ní, kɛ klaate, nɛ jehanɛ hu o bi Mawu ga womi ha lɛ ɔ? Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, e te si wo mi, nɛ e ngɛ ye he blɔ hlae nɛ e gbe mi!”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Ahimelek he nɔ ke, “O tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo a kpɛti ɔ, mɛnɔ lɛ e yeɔ anɔkuale kɛ o ngatsɛ David sɔ? O he buli ɔmɛ a nyatsɛ ji lɛ, nɛ a buu lɛ saminya ngɛ o we ɔ mi.

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Anɛ mwɔnɛ ɔ nɛ i bɔni Mawu ga womi bimi kɛ lɛ hami lo? Dɛbi! Nɛnɛ, koo po sane ngɔ fɔ o tsɔlɔ, loo o tsɔlɔ weku li a nɔ; ejakaa i li nɔ́ nɛ ɔ he nɔ ko kulaa.”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ de ke, “Mo Ahimelek, ja o gbo; mo, kɛ o weku li tsuo.”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Nɛ matsɛ ɔ de e he buli nɛ daa si ngɛ e kasa nya a ke, “Nyɛɛ gbe Yawɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ, ejakaa a kɛ David so; a le e fo tumi ɔ he nɔ́ ko, se a wo we ye tue nɔ.” Se matsɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ kplɛɛ we kaa a ma wo a nine nɔ ngɛ Yawɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ a nɔ nɛ a gbe mɛ.

english_verse: Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!” On that same day, Doeg killed
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, matsɛ ɔ de Doeg ke, “Moo gbe mɛ!” Nɛ Doeg, Edom no ɔ gbe osɔfohi nɛ a woɔ efɔd ɔ nyingmi kpaanyɔ kɛ enuɔ sɔuu jamɛ a ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Saul ha a kɛ klaate kpata nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ hɛ mi ngɛ Nob nɛ ji osɔfohi a ma a mi. A gbe nyumuhi kɛ yihi, jokuɛwi kɛ bimwɔwi, nahi kɛ tejihi, kɛ tohi tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ. Abiatar tu fo

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Se Abiatar nɛ ji Ahimelek binyumu ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake lɛɛ a nine sui e nɔ; nɛ e tu fo kɛ ho David ngɔ ya

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: ya bɔ lɛ amaniɛ kaa Saul gbe Yawɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Moo hi ye ngɔ; koo ye gbeye, ejakaa nɔ nɛ ngɛ hlae nɛ e gbe mi ɔ ngɛ hlae nɛ e gbe mo hulɔ. Ke o ngɛ ye ngɔ ɔ, o yi ma na wami.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: David nu kaa Filisti bi ɔmɛ ya tua Keila bi ɔmɛ, nɛ a ngɛ Keila bi ɔmɛ a blɛfo he nɛ a kpɔ ɔ hae.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David bi Yawɛ ke, “Ma ya nɛ ma ya tua Filisti bi ɔmɛ lo?” Yawɛ he nɔ ke, “Ee, yaa nɛ o ya tua mɛ nɛ o kɛ he Keila yi wami.”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Se David we bi ɔmɛ de lɛ ke, “O nɛ, wa ngɛ Yuda ma a mi hiɛ ɔ po wa ngɛ gbeye yee; lɛɛ ke wa ya Keila nɛ waa kɛ Filisti bi a tabo ɔmɛ ya kpe ɔ, kɛ wa maa pee kɛɛ?”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David kpale bi Yawɛ ga womi ekohu. Nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya tua Keila; ejakaa ma ngɔ Filisti bi ɔmɛ kɛ wo o dɛ mi.”

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Benɛ David na le kaa Saul ngɛ nɔ́ yayami soe kɛ wo e he ɔ, e de osɔfo Abiatar ke, “Ngɔɔ efɔd ɔ kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David de ke, “Yawɛ Israel Mawu lee, i nu kaa Saul ngɛ hlae nɛ e ba Keila nɛ e ba kpata ma a hɛ mi ngɛ imi, o tsɔlɔ ɔ, ye he.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Anɛ Keila bi ɔmɛ ma je mi kɛ wo e dɛ mi lo? Anɛ Saul maa ba niinɛ kaa bɔ nɛ o tsɔlɔ nu ɔ lo? Yawɛ Israel Mawu lee, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o ha mi heto.” Yawɛ he nɔ ke, “Ee, Saul maa ba.”

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: David kpale bi lɛ ke, “Anɛ Keila bi ɔmɛ maa ngɔ imi, kɛ ye we bi ɔmɛ kɛ wo Saul dɛ mi lo?” Yawɛ he nɔ ke, “Ee, a maa pee ja.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: David ya laa e he ngɛ tɛ puɔhi a mi ngɛ yoku ko nɔ, ngɛ Zif nga a nɔ. Daa ligbi ɔ, Saul hlaa David he blɔ; se Mawu je we lɛ ngɔ wui e dɛ mi.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: David tsui po, ejakaa e na kaa Saul ma lɛ gbemi. David ngɛ Horesh ngɛ Zif nga a nɔ.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Saul binyumu Yonatan ba e ngɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ba wo e hemi kɛ yemi ngɛ Mawu mi he wami.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: E de David ke, “Koo ye gbeye, ejakaa tsaatsɛ Saul nine be o nɔ sue. E le kaa mo lɛ o ma ba ye matsɛ ngɛ Israel, nɛ ma pee o se yelɔ.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Mɛ ni enyɔ ɔmɛ ka a he kita ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Yonatan je kɛ ho we mi ya; se David lɛɛ e tlɔ Horesh.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Zif bi komɛ ya Saul ngɔ ngɛ Gibea nɛ a ya de lɛ ke, “David ba laa e he ngɛ wa zugba a nɔ ngɛ Horesh, ngɛ Hakila yo ɔ nɔ, ngɛ Yudea nga kplanaa a leneyi je.

english_verse: If you come, we will help you catch him.”
translation_verse: Nɛnɛ, be tsuaa be nɛ o suɔ ɔ, ba nɛ wa je lɛ kɛ wo o dɛ mi.”

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Saul de mɛ ke, “Yawɛ maa gbaa nyɛ kaa nyɛ na mi mɔbɔ.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya hla mi saminya, nɛ nyɛɛ le he tutuutu nɛ e ngɛ, kɛ nɔ nɛ na lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ejakaa a de mi ke e hɛ mi tɛ̃ saminya.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya hyɛ e laami he ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ nɛ nyɛɛ to a he hɛ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, nyɛɛ ba nɛ nyɛ ba bɔ mi amaniɛ, konɛ i kɛ nyɛ waa ho. Ke ji kaa e ngɛ huza a nɔ niinɛ ɔ, lɛɛ ke e hia kaa ma hla lɛ kɛ kpa Yuda zugba a tsuo nɔ po, ma pee ja.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a sɛ Saul hlami, nɛ a kpale a se kɛ ho Zif ya. Jamɛ a be ɔ, David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ngɛ Maon nga a nɔ ngɛ kɔ̃ ko mi, ngɛ Yudea nga kplanaa a leneyi je.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ba nɛ a ba ngɛ David hlae ɔ, nɔ ko ba wo David tue nɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e je lejɛ ɔ nɛ e ya hi tɛ sa yoku nɛ ngɛ Maon nga a nɔ ɔ mi. Benɛ Saul nu he ɔ, e nyɛɛ David se kɛ ho lejɛ ɔ ya.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Saul kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ngɛ yoku ɔ kasa kake, nɛ David hu kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ngɛ yoku ɔ kasa kake. A ngɛ esɔ yee nɛ a je Saul kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi, ejakaa Saul kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ miɔ nɛ a ma sá David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ a yi, nɛ a nuu mɛ.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Tlukaa a, tsɔlɔ ko ba Saul ngɔ ba de lɛ ke, “Moo kpale kɛ ba esɔesɔ, ejakaa Filisti bi ɔmɛ ba tua ma a.”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul jɔɔ David se nyɛɛmi, nɛ e ho nɛ e kɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ ya kpe. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Mi gbami yoku.

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: David je lejɛ ɔ nɛ e ya hi tɛ puɔ mi ngɛ Engedi.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul kpale kɛ je Filisti bi ɔmɛ a se nyɛɛmi kɛ ba a, a de lɛ ke David ngɛ Engedi nga a nɔ.

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul su to tsu komɛ a he ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ ɔ, e gba ya sɛ tɛ puɔ ko mi, nɛ e ya nane nɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ hu laa a he ngɛ jamɛ a tɛ puɔ ɔ nɔuu mi ngɛ se blɔ.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David we bi ɔmɛ de lɛ ke, “Yawɛ de mo ke, ‘Ma je o he nyɛlɔ ɔ kɛ wo o dɛ mi nɛ o pee lɛ nɔ́ nɛ o suɔ.’ O nɛ, be ɔ su.” David pee blɛuu nɛ e ya po Saul bo ɔ nya nigii.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David he nile bɔni lɛ haomi,

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: David kɛ munyu nɛ ɔmɛ jɔɔ e we bi ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e ngmɛ́ mɛ blɔ nɛ a pee Saul nɔ́ ko. Pee se ɔ, Saul je tɛ puɔ ɔ mi, nɛ e ma e blɔ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: David hu je kpo kɛ je tɛ puɔ ɔ mi, nɛ e kpa huhui kɛ tsɛ Saul yi se, nɛ e de ke, “Ye nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ!” Nɛ benɛ Saul plɛ nɛ e hyɛ e se ɔ, David kpla si nɛ e kɛ e hɛ mi bu si ngɛ zugba kɛ tsɔɔ bumi.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: David de Saul ke, “Mɛni he je nɛ nihi ngɛ mo dee ke i ngɛ hlae ma ye mo awi, nɛ o ngɛ mɛ tue bue ɔ?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, mo nitsɛ o na kɛ o hɛngmɛ bɔ nɛ Yawɛ je mo kɛ wo ye dɛ mi ngɛ tɛ puɔ ɔ mi, bɔ nɛ ni komɛ de mi ke ma gbe mo, se i kɛ o wami ke mo, nɛ i de ke, ‘I be ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ awi yee, ejakaa Yawɛ nɛ hla lɛ kaa e ba ye matsɛ!’

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ tsaatsɛ hyɛ, o bo ɔ nya nɛ ngɛ ye dɛ mi nɛ ɔ nɛ. Kaa i nyɛ po o bo ɔ nya, se i gbi mo ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ ɔ maa tsɔɔ mo kaa nɔ́ yayami, loo atuã tsɔmi ko be ye mi.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Yawɛ maa kojo i kɛ mo wa kpɛti, nɛ e maa wo mo hiɔ ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ mi pee nɛ ɔ he; imi lɛɛ ye nine be o he sae.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Nimeli bu abɛ ke, ‘Nimli yayamihi a dɛ mi nɛ nɔ́ yayami jeɔ.’ Se imi lɛɛ ye nine be o he sae.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Mɛni se lɛ Israel matsɛ nyɛɛ nɛ ɔ? Mɛni o ngɛ fiee? Gbe gbogboe, aloo malɛɛ?

english_verse: “David, my son—is that you?” Saul asked. Then he started crying
translation_verse: Benɛ David tu munyu ta a, Saul bi lɛ ke, “Ye bi David, mo ji nɛ ɔ?” Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul wo ya,

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: nɛ e de David ke, “O da pe mi; ejakaa benɛ i pee mo yayami ɔ, moo o pee mi kpakpa kɛ to nane mi.

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Mwɔnɛ ɔ, o na mi mɔbɔ agbo; ejakaa be mi nɛ Yawɛ je mi kɛ wo o dɛ mi ɔ, o gbi mi.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Ke nɔ ko nine su e he nyɛlɔ nɔ ɔ, anɛ e ngmɛɛɔ e he nɛ e yaa slɔkee lo? Yawɛ nɛ e gbaa mo ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ o pee ha mi mwɔnɛ ɔ he.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ lɛɛ i le kaa bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, o ma ba ye matsɛ, nɛ a maa ngɔ Israel matsɛ yemi ɔ kɛ wo o dɛ.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mo ka mi kita ngɛ Yawɛ biɛ mi kaa ke i gbo ɔ, o be ye nina hɛ mi kpatae, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ ye biɛ, kɛ ye weku li a biɛ ko laa.”

english_verse: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
translation_verse: David nu ngɛ nga a nɔ kaa Nabal ngɛ e to ɔmɛ a he bwɔmi sãe.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: nɛ a de lɛ ke, “He manye, ye nyɛmi. He jɔmi nɛ ba o we ɔ, kɛ o nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɔ.

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: I nu kaa o ngɛ o to ɔmɛ a he bwɔmi sãe. I ngɛ hae nɛ o le kaa o to hyɛli ɔmɛ kɛ wɔ ba hi si, nɛ wa pee we mɛ yayami ko. Jehanɛ hu, ligbi abɔ nɛ a ye ngɛ Karmel ɔ, a nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko laa we.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Bi o nihewi ɔmɛ, nɛ a ma de mo. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, akɛnɛ nyami ligbi nɔ wa ba ngɛ he je ɔ, mo he wɔ atuu. I kpa mo pɛɛ, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ o dɛ ɔ, mo ha o tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ o binyumu David hu eko.”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: David we bi ɔmɛ ngɔ sɛ gbi ɔ ya ha Nabal ngɛ David biɛ mi; nɛ lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a mlɛ.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Se Nabal he nɔ nɛ e de David tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “Mɛnɔ ji jamɛ a David ɔ? Nɛ mɛnɔ hu ji Ishai binyumu nɛ ɔ? Ligbi etɛ nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, tsɔli nɛ tsɔ a nyɔmtsɛmɛ a hɛ mi atuã ba ngɛ hiɛe tsɔ.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma ngɔ ye abolo, ye nyu, kɛ lohwehi nɛ i gbe ha ye to he bwɔmi sali ɔ ngɔ ha nihi nɛ i li he nɛ a je ɔ lo?”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: David we bi ɔmɛ kpale a se nɛ a ya gba David nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Nabal de ɔ.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mo susu he, konɛ o hyɛ nɔ́ nɛ sa peemi; ejakaa sane yobu lɛ ma wa nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kɛ e weku li a nɔ nɛ ɔ nɛ. Nɔmlɔ ɔ tsui wa, nɛ a wui lɛ ga.”

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: E de e tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ nyɛɛ waa ho; i ngɛ nyɛ se kɛ ma.” Se e sɛ́ e huno Nabal.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Abigail hi e teji ɔ nɔ kɛ ngɛ yo ɔ kplee nɛ e kɛ David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ya bua tlukaa nɛ mɛ hu a ma e ngɔ blɔ.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: David de e he ke, “I tsu yaka ní pɛ kaa i bu nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ níhi a he ha lɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ nɛ e nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko laa we. Yayami mohu e kɛ to kpakpa nɛ i pee lɛ ɔ nane mi.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: I na Mawu, benɛ je ke e naa a, ke nyumu kake ngmelu piɛ ngɛ e we bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti fii!”

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: I kpa mo pɛɛ, ke i pee mo yayami ko ɔ, kɛ pa mi. Yawɛ maa wo mo matsɛ, nɛ e maa pee o we ɔ matsɛ we kɛ maa ya neneene; ejakaa Yawɛ tahi lɛ o ngɛ hwue ɔ nɛ; nɛ yayami ko yayami ko be o he sae kɛ yaa si o gbenɔ ligbi.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Nɛ ke nɔ ko maa te si kɛ wo mo, nɛ e ma hla kaa e gbe mo ɔ, Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ maa bu o he kaa bɔ nɛ nɔmlɔ adesa buu june nɛ he jua wa he ɔ. Se o he nyɛli ɔmɛ lɛɛ e ma sake mɛ ngɔ fɔ he kaa bɔ nɛ a fɔɔ amlami tɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Ní kpakpahi tsuo nɛ Yawɛ wo mo a he si ɔ, ke e na pee ha mo nɛ e wo mo ganɔ ngɛ Israel ɔ,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: ko pia o he, nɛ ko ha nɛ o he nile hu nɛ hao mo kaa o pue muɔ si yaka gu, aloo kaa o ye mo nitsɛ o he lue. I kpa mo pɛɛ, ke Yawɛ gbaa mo ɔ, mo kai imi, o mawayo ɔ.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: David de Abigail ke, “Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ, nɔ nɛ tsɔ mo mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ ke o kɛ mi nɛ ba kpe ɔ, a je e yi.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Niinɛ, Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ tsi ye nya ke ma ko pee mo yayami ko. Se i na Mawu, kaa o pee we esɔ nɛ o kɛ mi ba kpe, jinɛ hwɔɔ benɛ je ke e naa a, nɔ kake ngmelu be piɛe ha Nabal.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David he nike ní ɔ ngɛ e dɛ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Koo ye gbeye; moo kpale kɛ ho we mi ya. Nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ hlae ɔ, ma pee ha mo.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Benɛ Abigail kpale e se kɛ ba we ɔ mi ɔ, o nɛ Nabal nɛ ngmɛ okplɔɔ kaa matsɛ. Nabal de dã kpɔtɔɔ, nɛ e bua jɔ e he, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Abigail bɔɛ lɛ amaniɛ ko kɛ ya si je na.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Mɔtu benɛ dã a je Nabal hɛ mi ɔ, e yo ɔ gba lɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ya nɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ Nabal tsui kpa tsɔ, nɛ e hule pue si.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Maa pee ligbi nyɔngma se ɔ, Yawɛ fia Nabal nɔ nɛ e gbo.

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Abigail te si esɔesɔ nɛ e ya hi e teji ɔ nɔ, nɛ e kɛ e mawayi enuɔ ɔmɛ nyɛɛ David tsɔli ɔmɛ a se kɛ ho, nɛ e ya pee e yo.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: David ngɔ Ahinoam nɛ je Yezreel ɔ hu kɛ piɛ e yo Abigail ɔ he.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: David yo Mikal lɛɛ e tsɛ Saul ngɔ lɛ ngɔ ha Laish binyumu Palti nɛ je Galim ɔ.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Zif bi ɔmɛ ba Saul ngɔ ngɛ Gibea ba bɔ lɛ amaniɛ ke David ba laa e he ngɛ Hakila yo ɔ nɔ ngɛ Yuda nga a nya.

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Saul kɛ e tabo ɔ ya bua a he nya ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɛ gu Hakila yoku ɔ nɔ ɔ he, ngɛ Yeshimon hanɔ. Jamɛ a be ɔ, David ngɛ laami tso mi ngɛ nga a nɔ. Benɛ David nu kaa Saul ba lɛ hlami ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ,

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: e tsɔ slaali ngɛ laami mi nɛ e kɛ ná le kaa Saul ngɛ lejɛ ɔ niinɛ.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David be kɛ ho he nɛ Saul ta buli ɔmɛ bua a he nya ngɛ ɔ ya. David ya na he nɛ Saul kɛ e tatsɛ nguaa Abner, Ner bi ɔ hwɔɔ si ngɛ ɔ. Saul hwɔɔ si ngɛ ta a mi, nɛ e ta buli ɔmɛ pue si kɛ bɔle lɛ.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: David bi Ahimelek, Hit no ɔ, kɛ Yoab nyɛminyumu Abishai, Zeruya binyumu ɔ ke, “Nyɛ ti mɛnɔ kɛ mi maa ya Saul ta a mi?” Abishai he nɔ ke, “I kɛ mo maa ya.”
