english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David kɛ Abishai ho ta a mi ya jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi, nɛ a ya na Saul nɛ hwɔ mahe kɛ e we akplɔ ɔ nɛ a kɛ gbɔ si ngɛ e yi tetle mi. Abner kɛ ta buli ɔmɛ hwɔɔ si kɛ bɔle lɛ.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Abishai de David ke, “Mawu je o he nyɛlɔ ɔ kɛ wo o dɛ mi mwɔnɛ ɔ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ha nɛ ma hɛ lɛ akplɔ ɔ si kake pɛ kɛ ya pi zugba, nɛ e be hiae kaa a hɛ lɛ enyɔne.”

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: David ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “I na Yawɛ, hɛ kalɔ ɔ kaa lɛ Yawɛ nitsɛ e maa fia Saul nɔ, loo Saul gbenɔ be maa su nɛ e ma gbo, loo e ma gbo ngɛ ta nya.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Yawɛ hiɔ kaa nɔmlɔ nɛ lɛ, Yawɛ nitsɛ e wo lɛ matsɛ ɔ, ma pue e muɔ si. Ha waa kɛ̃ akplɔ ɔ nɛ ngɛ e yi tetle mi ɔ, kɛ nyu kɛ kplu ɔ, nɛ waa ho.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: David kɛ̃ akplɔ ɔ, kɛ nyu kɛ kplu ɔ nɛ ngɛ Saul yi tetle mi ɔ, nɛ a je lejɛ ɔ. Nɔ ko nɔ ko nɛ mɛ; nɔ ko nɔ ko li nɔ́ nɛ ba, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko hɛ tsɛ̃ hulɔ. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ hwɔ mahe; ejakaa Yawɛ ha mahe vii ko ba nɔ mɛ tsuo a nɔ.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, David po mi kɛ ho, nɛ e ya da yoku ɔ yi mi tsitsaa lokoo,

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: David he nɔ ke, “Pi nyumu ji mo? Mɛnɔ kɛ mo sɔ ngɛ Israel? Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ o bui o nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ ɔ he? Nɔ ko ba ta a mi piɔ, nɛ jinɛ e ko kpata o nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ ɔ hɛ mi.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Nyɛ pee we nɛ hi kulaa. I na Mawu, ja a gbe nyɛ tsuo kulaa; ejakaa nyɛ bui nyɛ nyɔmtsɛ ɔ, nɔ nɛ Yawɛ pɔ lɛ nu ɔ he. Jehanɛ, hyɛ he nɛ matsɛ ɔ akplɔ ɔ ngɛ! Nyu kɛ kplu ɔ hu nɛ ngɛ matsɛ ɔ yi tetle mi ɔ, hyɛ he nɛ e ba je!”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Saul yɔse David gbi, nɛ e bi ke, “Ye bi David, mo ji nɛ ɔ?” David he nɔ ke, “Ee, ye nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ, imi!”

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: David ya nɔ nɛ e bi lɛ ke, “Ye nyɔmtsɛ, mɛni he je o ngɛ ye se nyɛɛe kɛ mwɔɔ? Mɛni i pee mo? Mɛni yayami i pee?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Ye nyɔmtsɛ, moo bu nɔ́ nɛ o tsɔlɔ ma de mo nɛ ɔ tue. Ke Yawɛ lɛ pee loko o ngɛ ye se blɔ hlae ɔ, lɛɛ e ngmɛ mi blɔ nɛ ma sã bɔ kɛ kpata lɛ. Se ke nimli adesahi a ní tsumi ɔ, lɛɛ Yawɛ nɛ e gbiɛ mɛ; ejakaa mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, a fie mi kɛ je Yawɛ zugba a nɔ kɛ ho ma kpa nɔ ya nɛ ma ya ja mawu kpahi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Mo ko ha nɛ ma gbo nɛ ye muɔ nɛ pue si ngɛ zugba kpa nɔ kɛ je Yawɛ hɛ mi. Mɛni he je Israel matsɛ hia ta kɛ ma mi tuami, imi nɛ i ngɛ kaa malɛɛ kɛkɛ ɔ? Mɛni he je e ngɛ mi dae kaa a daa hɔne ngɛ yoku nɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Saul he nɔ ke, “I tɔ̃! Ye bi David, moo kpale kɛ ba; i be mo nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko pee hu, ejakaa o kɛ ye wami ke mi mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ. I je kuasia nɛ i tɔ̃ babauu.”

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Yawɛ gbaa nihi nɛ yeɔ anɔkuale, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ da. Yawɛ je mo kɛ wo ye dɛ mi mwɔnɛ ɔ, se mo nɔmlɔ nɛ Yawɛ pɔ mo nu ɔ, i tɛ o he.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ i kɛ o wami ke mo mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, Yawɛ nɛ e ngɔ ye wami kɛ ke mi, nɛ e je mi kɛ je amanehlu tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ mi.”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Saul de David ke, “Mawu nɛ e gbaa mo, ye bi David! O maa ye manye ngɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ mi.” Kɛkɛ nɛ David je lejɛ ɔ, nɛ Saul hu kpale e se kɛ ho we mi ya.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: David de ngɛ e yi mi ke, “Saul maa gbe mi tlukaa ligbi kake, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ sa mi peemi ji ma tu fo kɛ ho Filisti bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ ya. Saul nine mi maa je wu, nɛ e maa jɔɔ ye se nyɛɛmi ngɛ Israel huza amɛ a nɔ, nɛ ye yi ma na wami.”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Benɛ a ya bɔ Saul ke David tu fo kɛ ho Gat ya a, e jɔɔ e se nyɛɛmi.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: David de Akish ke, “Ke o suɔ mi ɔ, lɛɛ ha nɛ a ha mi he ko ngɛ kɔpe ɔ kake mi nɛ ma hi lejɛ ɔ; ejakaa e sɛ kaa imi, o tsɔlɔ ɔ, i kɛ mo hii matsɛ ma a mi.”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Akish ngɔ ma nɛ a tsɛɛ Ziklag ɔ ngɔ ha lɛ. Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ Ziklag ma a ba pee Yuda matsɛmɛ a nɔ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: David ye jeha kake kɛ hlami eywiɛ ngɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Ke pee ɔ, David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ maa hia ya tua nihi nɛ ngɛ Geshur, Girzi, kɛ Amalek. Nimli nɛ ɔmɛ ji zugbatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ hi zugba a nɔ kɛ je Shur kɛ ya si Egipt kɛ je teteete.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: David ma kpata nɔ tsuaa nɔ hɛ mi, nɛ nyumu, loo yo kake po be piɛe hɛ ngmengmle. E maa muɔ tohi, nahi, tejihi, afukpɔngɔhi, kɛ tadehi po. Kɛkɛ e maa kpale e se kɛ ba Akish ngɔ.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Ke Akish bi lɛ ke, “Mɛnɔmɛ o ya tua mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ?” David ma de lɛ ke e ya tua Yuda leneyi je, aloo Yerameel bi ɔmɛ a zugba a, aloo Ken bi ɔmɛ a zugba a.

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Ke David ya tua ni ɔmɛ kikɛ nɛ ɔ, e maa gbe nɔ tsuaa nɔ, nyumuhi kɛ yihi tsuo, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ nɔ ko nɛ ko be kɛ ya Gat nɛ e ya bɔ ni ɔmɛ bɔ nɛ e kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ puɛ ní ha. Ligbi abɔ nɛ David ye ngɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ ɔ, ní tsumi nɛ e tsu ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Akish he David ye saminya, nɛ e deɔ ngɛ e yi mi ke, “Lɛ nitsɛ e nyɛmimɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ sume lɛ pɛsɛpɛsɛ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, hiɛ ɔ kɛkɛ e maa hi nɛ e ma sɔmɔ mi daa.”

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Filisti bi ɔmɛ bua a he nya ngɛ Shunem, nɛ Saul hu bua Israel tsuo nya ngɛ Gilboa.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul na Filisti bi ɔmɛ a tabo ɔ, e ye gbeye wawɛɛ nitsɛ,

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e ya bi Yawɛ ga womi. Se Yawɛ pui e nya mi. E na we sɛ gbi ko kɛ gui nlami mi. Urim kɛ Tumim de we lɛ nɔ́ ko, nɛ e nui nɔ́ ko kɛ ji gbalɔ ko gbalɔ ko nya.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul de e tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ hla yo ko nɛ peeɔ ní ha mi nɛ ma ya e ngɔ ya bi ní.” E tsɔli ɔmɛ de lɛ ke, “Wa kpa mo pɛɛ, yo ní peelɔ ko ngɛ Endor.” Endor yo ní peelɔ ɔ

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul tsake e he nɛ e wo tade kpa, nɛ gbɔkuɛ ɔ, e kɛ nyumuhi enyɔ pue nɔ kɛ ho yo ɔ ngɔ ya. E de yo ɔ ke, “Moo pee ní ha mi, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ma tsɛ e biɛ ɔ, o ha nɛ nɔ ɔ susuma nɛ ba.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Se yo ɔ de lɛ ke, “Tse mo nitsɛ o le nɔ́ nɛ Matsɛ Saul pee ɔ, kaa e kpata ní peeli, kɛ klamɔhi nɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ a hɛ mi. Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ o ngɛ mi klama tsɔe nɛ o ha nɛ a gbe mi ɔ?”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul kɛ Yawɛ biɛ ka yo ɔ kita ke, “I na Yawɛ kaa nɔ ko nɔ ko be o tue gblae ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ he.”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Yo ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Mɛnɔ ma tsɛ ha mo?” Nɛ Saul he nɔ ke, “Tsɛ Samuel ha mi.” Samuel kpade

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Benɛ yo ɔ na Samuel ɔ, e kpa bubuubui nɛ e de Saul ke, “Mɛni he je o sisi mi ɔ? Matsɛ Saul ji mo!”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Koo ye gbeye! Mɛni o na?” Yo ɔ he nɔ ke, “I na kpade ko nɛ hia kɛ je zu ɔ mi kɛ ma.”

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Samuel bi Saul ke, “Mɛni he je o hao mi kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Mɛni he je o ba tsɛ mi?” Saul he nɔ ke, “Ye yi fi. Lɔ ɔ ji Filisti bi ɔmɛ kɛ mi ngɛ ta hwue, nɛ Mawu je ye se. Ke i tsɛ lɛ ɔ, e he we nɔ; jehanɛ hu i nui e he kɛ gui gbali ɔmɛ a nɔ, loo nlami mi. Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ i ba tsɛ mo, konɛ o tsɔɔ mi bɔ nɛ ma pee.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Samuel bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he je o ba ngɛ mi tsɛe be mi nɛ Yawɛ je o se, nɛ e plɛ pee o he nyɛlɔ ɔ?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ gu ye nɔ de mo ɔ, lɔ ɔ e pee nɛ ɔ nɛ. Yawɛ kpɔ matsɛ yemi ɔ ngɛ o dɛ nɛ e kɛ ha o he nɔ David.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Akɛnɛ o bui Yawɛ tue, nɛ fami nɛ e kɛ mi mi fumi nɛ nya wa fa mo ngɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ a he ɔ hu o yi nɔ ɔ, enɛ ɔ he je nɛ Yawɛ pee mo nɔ́ nɛ ɔ mwɔnɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ se hu, Yawɛ maa ngɔ mo, kɛ Israel tsuo kɛ wo Filisti bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi; nɛ hwɔɔmɛ a je hwɔɔ ɔ, o kɛ o binyumu ɔmɛ ma ba piɛ ye he. Israel tabo ɔ hu Yawɛ maa ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo Filisti bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul kuɛli nɔ zugba amlɔ; ejakaa Samuel munyu ɔmɛ wo e he gbeye wawɛɛ nitsɛ. Nɛ akɛnɛ e yi nɔ́ ko piani kɛ nyɔ mi tsuo he je ɔ, e gbɔjɔ.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ yo ɔ ba Saul ngɔ, nɛ e na kaa e tsui po, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e de lɛ ke, “O nɛ, o mawayo bu mo tue; i ngɔ ye wami ngɔ ke, nɛ i pee nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ hlae ɔ ha mo.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ mo hu o bu o mawayo ɔ tue. Ha ma pee nɔ́ ko ha mo nɛ o ye, konɛ o na he wami nɛ o kɛ hia blɔ.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Saul kplɛɛ we, nɛ e ke, “Dɛbi, i be ní yee.” Se e tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ yo ɔ nyɛ e nɔ kɛ ya si e bu mɛ tue. E te si ngɛ zugba, nɛ e hi sa a nɔ.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Yo ɔ ngɛ na bi ko nɛ wo zɔ ngɛ we ɔ mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e pee esɔ nɛ e ya gbe lɛ. E pɔtɔ mamu nɛ e kɛ sã abolo kplolo,

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: nɛ e ngɔ niye ní ɔ ya ma Saul kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi nɛ a ye. Nɛ a je lejɛ ɔ jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi nɔuu.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Se Filisti tatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a mi mi fu Akish, nɛ a de lɛ ke, “Ha nɛ nyumu ɔ nɛ kpale e se kɛ ya he nɛ o ngɔ ha lɛ ɔ. Waa kɛ lɛ be ta yae nɛ e ba plɛ wo wɔ ngɛ ta a mi nɛ e fia wɔ senya kɔ. Mɛni nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ kɛ ma kpata e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ, nɛ maa sa e hɛ mi pe nimli nɛ ngɛ hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ a yi koklodohi?

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: David ɔ, nɔ nɛ he nɛ yi ɔmɛ do, nɛ a la ke, ‘Saul gbe akpehi, se David gbe akpe nyɔngmahi’ ɔ, pi lɛ ji nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Akish tsɛ David, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “I na Israel Mawu, hɛ kalɔ ɔ kaa o yeɔ mi anɔkuale, nɛ jinɛ imi lɛɛ i ko suɔ kaa o kɛ mi nɛ ya ta nɛ ɔ; ejakaa kɛ je ligbi ɔ nɛ o ba ye ngɔ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ, i nɛ nɔ́ yayami ko ngɛ o he. Se matsɛmɛ kpa amɛ sume kaa o kɛ wɔ nɛ ya.

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: David bi Akish ke, “Mɛni i pee? Kɛ je ligbi ɔ nɛ i ba bɔni mo sɔmɔmi kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ, mɛni o na ngɛ o tsɔlɔ ɔ he loko e sɛ kaa i yaa nɛ i kɛ ye nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ ɔ he nyɛli ya hwuɔ ta a?”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Akish ha David heto ke, “Imi lɛɛ i le kaa nɔ́ ko be o he; o ngɛ kaa Mawu bɔfo. Filisti tatsɛmɛ kpa amɛ nɛ a de ke, ‘Waa kɛ lɛ be ta yae’ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David, hwɔɔ mɔtu ɔ, o kɛ Saul tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ piɛ o he ɔ maa te si mla; nɛ benɛ je mi ke e tsɔɔ ɔ, kɛkɛ nyɛ je hiɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ te si mɔtu mla nɛ a kpale kɛ ho Filistia ya; nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ hu pue nɔ kɛ ho Yezreel ya.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji etɛ ɔ, be nɛ David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ke a suu Ziklag ɔ, Amalek bi ɔmɛ ba ha ní ngɛ Yuda leneyi je, nɛ a tua Ziklag. A kɛ la sã Ziklag,

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Benɛ David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ba su ma a mi ɔ, a na kaa a sã ma a, nɛ jehanɛ hu a nuu a yi ɔmɛ, a binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ a biyi ɔmɛ kɛ je.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ wo yana hluu kɛ ya si a he wami ta.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: A nuu David yi enyɔ ɔmɛ hu kɛ ho. Mɛ ji Ahinoam, Yezreel no ɔ, kɛ Abigail, Nabal nɛ je Karmel yalɔyo ɔ.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: David hao wawɛɛ nitsɛ; ejakaa e we bi ɔmɛ a hɛ dɔ ngɛ a bimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a be ɔ a he. Jehanɛ hu a de ke a maa fia lɛ tɛ. Se Yawɛ, David Mawu ɔ wo lɛ he wami.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: David de osɔfo Abiatar, Ahimelek binyumu ɔ ke, “Ngɔɔ efɔd ɔ kɛ ba ha mi.” Nɛ Abiatar ngɔ efɔd ɔ kɛ ba ha lɛ.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: David bi Yawɛ ke, “Ma nyɛɛ ní hali ɔmɛ a se lo? Anɛ ye nine maa su a nɔ lo?” Yawɛ he nɔ ke, “Ee, moo nyɛɛ a se; ejakaa o ma ya na mɛ, nɛ bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, o ma kpɔ ni ɔmɛ.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: David we bi ɔmɛ ya na Egipt niheyo ko ngɛ nga a nɔ, nɛ a kɛ lɛ ba David ngɔ. A ha lɛ ní nɛ e ye, nɛ a ha lɛ nyu nɛ e nu.

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a ha lɛ ngmɔkɔ kɛ wai yiblii sau enyɔ nɛ e ye, kɛkɛ nɛ e hɛ mi tsɔ lɛ; ejakaa e yi ní, nɛ e nui nyu ligbi etɛ sɔuu.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: David bi lɛ ke, “Mɛnɔ ngɔ bi ji mo? Nɛ jije o je?” Niheyo ɔ he nɔ ke, “Egipt no ji mi, se ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ lɛɛ Amalek no ji lɛ. Ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ je ye he ngɛ hiɛ ɔ mwɔnɛ ɔ ji ligbi etɛ; ejakaa i be he wami.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Wa ya tua Keret bi a zugba a nɛ ngɛ Yuda leneyi je ɔ, kɛ Kaleb bi a zugba a, nɛ wa sã Ziklag ma a.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: David bi lɛ ke, “Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa tsɔɔ mi he nɛ nimli nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ lo?” Niheyo ɔ he nɔ ke, “Ke o maa wo si ngɛ Mawu biɛ mi kaa o be mi gbee, nɛ jehanɛ hu, o be mi jee kɛ wo ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ dɛ mi ɔ, lɛɛ i kɛ mo maa ya.”

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena makɛ ɔ, David ya tua mɛ, nɛ e kɛ mɛ hwu kɛ ya si gbɔkuɛ. Nɔ ko nɔ ko he ji mi, kaa ja nihewi lafa eywiɛ nɛ mɛɛ a hi afukpɔngɔ nɔ kɛ tu fo pɛ.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: David kpɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ ba ha kɛ ho ɔ. E nine su e yihi enyɔ ɔmɛ hu a nɔ,

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: nɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko laa we. David kpɔ e we bi ɔmɛ a binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ a biyi ɔmɛ, kɛ ta yibu ní nɛ Amalek bi ɔmɛ muɔ ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ David muɔ to ɔmɛ, kɛ na amɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ. E we bi ɔmɛ kpaka lohwe ɔmɛ kɛ nyɛɛ a hɛ mi be mi nɛ a ngɛ dee ke, “David ta yibu ní ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ!” Ta yibu ní dlami

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Se amimitsɛmɛ kɛ yaka nimli nɛ nyɛɛ David se ɔ de ke, “Akɛnɛ a kɛ wɔ yɛ he je ɔ, wa be mɛ ta yibu ní ɔmɛ nɛ wa ya kpɔ ɔ eko hae. A ba ngɔ a yi ɔmɛ, kɛ a bimɛ ɔmɛ kɛkɛ nɛ a ho.”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Se David de mɛ ke, “Ye nyɛmimɛ, nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ ha wɔ ɔ, nyɛ ko pee lɛ ja. Yawɛ baa wa yi nɛ e je ni nɛmɛ nɛ ba tua wɔ ɔ kɛ wo wa dɛ mi.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Mɛnɔ maa kplɛɛ nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ de nɛ ɔ nɔ? Bɔ nɛ ta yalɔ ko ma na a, ja nɔuu nɔ nɛ buu ní ɔmɛ a he ɔ ma na; mɛ tsuo a ma na sɔsɔɛ.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: David pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ mlaa, nɛ a ngɛ nɔ yee ngɛ Israel kɛ je jamɛ a be ɔ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Benɛ David kpale kɛ ba Ziklag ɔ, e tsɔ nɛ a kɛ ta yibu ní ɔ eko ya ha e huɛmɛ Yuda ma nimeli ɔmɛ, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nike ní nɛ wa ngɔ kɛ ba ha nyɛ nɛ ɔ ji ta yibu ní nɛ wa ngɔ kɛ je Yawɛ he nyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi ɔ eko.”

english_verse: This is a list of the towns where David sent gifts: Bethel, Ramoth in the Southern Desert, Jattir, Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa, Racal, the towns belonging to the Jerahmeelites and the Kenites, Hormah, Bor-Ashan, Athach, and Hebron. He also sent gifts to the other towns where he and his men had traveled.
translation_verse: kɛ Hebron ma amɛ a mi. He tsuaa he nɛ David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ya kpa a, e mane nihi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ta yibu ní ɔ eko.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Filisti bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ hwu ta ngɛ Gilboa yo ɔ nɔ. A gbe Israel bi ɔmɛ babauu nitsɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ Saul, kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ tu fo.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Se Filisti bi ɔmɛ ya na mɛ, nɛ a gbe Saul binyumu etɛ ɔmɛ, Yonatan, Abinadab, kɛ Malkishua.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Ta nɛ nyɛɛ Saul se ɔ mi wa wawɛɛ nitsɛ. Kɛ̃ɛ̃ tsɛli ɔmɛ a nine su e nɔ, nɛ a plaa lɛ wawɛɛ.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Saul de e ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ ɔ ke, “Moo hia o klaate ɔ nɛ o kɛ gbe mi, nɛ́ mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ nɛ ɔmɛ ko ba gbe mi nɛ a bɔ mi ahlua.” Se niheyo ɔ ye gbeye, nɛ e nyɛ we nɛ e pee ja. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Saul nitsɛ kɛ̃ e klaate ɔ, nɛ e kɛ gbe e he.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ ɔ na kaa Saul gbo ɔ, lɛ hu e kɛ lɛ nitsɛ e klaate ɔ gbe e he.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Nɛ Saul kɛ e binyumu etɛ ɔmɛ, e ta hwumi ní hɛɛlɔ ɔ, kɛ e ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo gbo ligbi kake too.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Yezreel kɔ̃ ɔ se je, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ Yordan pa a beleku je ɔ nu kaa Israel ta a gbɛ, nɛ jehanɛ hu, Saul kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ gbo ɔ, a tu fo kɛ je a ma amɛ a mi; nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ ba nɛ a ba hi lejɛ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena benɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ ba nɛ a ba ha ní ngɛ ni gbogboe ɔmɛ a he ɔ, a na Saul kɛ e binyumu etɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a gbo fɔɔ si ngɛ Gilboa yo ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines cut off Saul's head and pulled off his armor. Then they put his armor in the temple of the goddess Astarte, and they nailed his body to the city wall of Beth-Shan. They also sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the good news in the temples of their idols and among their people.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a ngɔ e ta hwumi ní ɔmɛ ya to yo mawu ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Ashtarot ɔ we ɔ, nɛ a kɛ e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ ya kpla Bet Shan gbogbo ɔ he.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yabesh Gilead bi ɔmɛ nu nɔ́ nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ pee Saul ɔ,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: nyumuhi katsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsuo nyɛɛ nyɔnyɔɔnyɔ kɛ ya Bet Shan ya je Saul gbogboe ɔ, kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ a ní ɔmɛ kɛ je gbogbo ɔ he, nɛ a ngɔ mɛ kɛ ba Yabesh, nɛ a ba sã mɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a muɔ wu ɔmɛ ya pu ngɛ tso nguaa ko sisi ngɛ Yabesh ma a mi, nɛ a ha hwɔ ligbi kpaago.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Ligbi etɛne ɔ, nyumu ko je Saul ta a mi kɛ ba. E hía e tade ɔmɛ ngɛ e he, nɛ e ngɔ zu ngɔ pue e yi mi kɛ tsɔɔ kaa e ngɛ kɔmɔ yee. E ba David ngɔ, nɛ e kɛ bumi ba kpla si ngɛ e hɛ mi.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: David bi lɛ ke, “Jije o je?” Nɛ e he nɔ ke, “I ku kɛ je Israel ta a mi.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: David de lɛ ke, “Moo bɔ mi bɔ nɛ níhi ya nɔ ha.” Nyumu ɔ de David ke, “Wa ta buli ɔmɛ tu fo ngɛ ta a nya, nɛ a gbe a ti nihi babauu. Saul kɛ e bi Yonatan hu gbo.”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Niheyo ɔ he nɔ ke, “I ya je Gilboa yo ɔ nɔ tlukaa, nɛ i na Saul nɛ e buu si ngɛ e we akplɔ ɔ nɔ. E he nyɛli ɔmɛ a ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ a we okpɔngɔ nɔ hili ɔmɛ su e he haa.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Saul plɛ hyɛ e se, nɛ e na mi. E tsɛ mi, nɛ i he nɔ ke, ‘Nɛnɛ!’

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: E bi mi ke, ‘Mɛnɔ ji mo?’ Nɛ i ha lɛ heto ke, ‘Amalek no ji mi.’

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i hɛ kɛ su e he nɛ i gbe lɛ; ejakaa i le sa kaa si nɛ e nɔ ɔ, e be je mi tlɔe. I je matsɛ pɛɛ ɔ nɛ e bu ɔ, kɛ ga nɛ ngɛ e kɔni si ɔ, nɛ i hɛɛ kɛ ma mo, ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ha mi.”

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David kɛ aywilɛho hía tade ɔ ngɛ e he, nɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo pee ja nɔuu.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: A wo yana, nɛ a ye kɔmɔ, nɛ a ha hwɔ kɛ ya si gbɔkuɛ. A wo yana kɛ ha Saul kɛ e bi Yonatan, kɛ Israel, Yawɛ ma a; ejakaa nimli babauu gbo ngɛ ta a mi.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: David bi niheyo ɔ nɛ ba bɔ lɛ amaniɛ ɔ ke, “Jije o je?” E he nɔ ke, “Amalek no ko nɛ ba to nubwɔ ngɛ Israel bi ji mi.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: David de Amalek no ɔ ke, “O musu tloo mo; ejakaa mo nitsɛ o kɛ o nya ye odase ke, ‘I gbe nɔmlɔ nɛ Yawɛ pɔ lɛ nu ɔ.’ ” David kɔmɔ yemi la kɛ ha Saul kɛ Yonatan

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: David la aywilɛho la nɛ ɔ kɛ nyɛ ya ha Saul kɛ e bi Yonatan,

english_verse: and he ordered his men to teach the song to everyone in Judah. He called it “The Song of the Bow,” and it can be found in The Book of Jashar. This is the song:
translation_verse: nɛ e fa kaa a tsɔɔ Yuda bi ɔmɛ tsuo. A ngma la nɛ ɔ ngɛ Yashar Womi ɔ mi. E la ke,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: “A gbe wa ta hɛ mi nyɛɛli ɔmɛ ngɔ pue Israel yo ɔmɛ a nɔ. Wa ta buli kpanaa amɛ gbo!

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko tu munyu nɛ ɔ nɛ Gat bi ba nu. Nyɛ ko sɛɛ ngɛ Ashkelon gbɛjegbɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ. Ke pi ja a, Filisti yi ɔmɛ ma na bua jɔmi. Ke pi ja a, wɔ jali a biyi ɔmɛ ma nya.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: Nyɛ Gilboa yohi, bɔ́, loo hiɔmi nɛ ko nɛ ngɛ nyɛ nɔ; nyɛ ngmɔ ko ngmɔ ko nɛ kó ba ní. Ejakaa lejɛ ɔ nyɛ katsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a tsɛ̃i ɔmɛ a hɛ mi pue si ngɛ; Saul tsɛ̃i ɔ fɔɔ si nɛ a pɔɛ he nu hu!

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Jinɛ Yonatan kɛ̃ɛ̃ ɔ, duɔ ngɛ nya; jinɛ Saul klaate ɔ nya ba. A kɛ gbe a he nyɛli kpanakuhi ngɛ ta mi kɛ be.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: “Saul kɛ Yonatan a he ngɛ bua jɔmi; a suɔ mɛ saminya. Wami mi jio, gbenɔ mi jio, a mi gba we. A he sɔɔ pe kɔle; nɛ a he wa pe jata.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: “Nyɛ Israel yihi, nyɛɛ ye kɔmɔ ha Saul! Lɛ nɛ e bu nyɛ bo tsu kpakpahi, nɛ e ha nyɛ bua jɔmi. Lɛ nɛ e kɛ sika tsu, kɛ june dla nyɛ he!

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: “Oo, hyɛ bɔ nɛ katsɛmɛ kpanaa amɛ gbo kɛ pueɔ si ngɛ ta mi ha! Oo, hyɛ bɔ nɛ Yonatan gbo kɛ fɔɔ si ngɛ yoku ɔmɛ a nɔ ha!

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: “Ye nyɛmi Yonatan, i ngɛ mo kɔmɔ yee; o suɔ mi saminya! Suɔmi nɛ o je kpo ngɔ ha mi ɔ, e nya wa pe yihi a suɔmi po!

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, David bi Yawɛ ke, “Ma kpale kɛ ya Yuda ma amɛ eko mi lo?” Yawɛ he nɔ ke, “Ee, moo ya.” David bi lɛ ekohu ke, “Jije ma ya?” Nɛ Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Yaa Hebron.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David kɛ e yi enyɔ ɔmɛ pue nɔ kɛ ho Hebron ya. Mɛ ji Ahinoam nɛ je Yezreel ɔ, kɛ Abigail nɛ ji Karmel no, Nabal yalɔyo ɔ.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ hu David ngɔ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ, kɛ a yihi, kɛ a bimɛ kɛ ho; nɛ a ya hi Hebron ma amɛ a mi.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Yuda ma nimeli ɔmɛ ba Hebron ba pɔ David nu nɛ a wo lɛ Yuda matsɛ. Benɛ David nu kaa Yabesh Gilead bi ɔmɛ ya pu Saul ɔ,

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: e tsɔ nɛ a kɛ sɛ gbi ya ha mɛ ke, “Yawɛ maa gbaa nyɛ kaa nyɛ je nyɛ suɔmi kpo ngɔ ha Saul, nyɛ nyɔmtsɛ ɔ, nɛ nyɛ pu lɛ!

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Yawɛ nɛ e na nyɛ mɔbɔ nɛ e je e mi mi himi kpo kɛ tsɔɔ nyɛ! Imi hu ma pee nyɛ kpakpa ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ pee nɛ ɔ he.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛ wlua nyɛ, nɛ nyɛɛ pee kã. Nyɛ matsɛ Saul ɔ gbo, nɛ Yuda ma a pɔ mi nu nɛ a wo mi a nɔ matsɛ.” A wo Ishboshet Israel matsɛ

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Se Saul tatsɛ Abner, Ner binyumu ɔ ku Saul binyumu Ishboshet kɛ tu fo kɛ po Yordan pa a kɛ ho Mahanaim ya.

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: Abner ya wo lɛ matsɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ha Gilead, Asher, Yezreel, Efraim, Benyamin, kɛ Israel ma amɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Nɛ David ye matsɛ ngɛ Hebron kɛ ha Yuda wɛtso ɔ jeha kpaago kɛ nyɔhiɔ ekpa. Israel kɛ Yuda ta a

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Ner bi Abner, kɛ Saul bi Ishboshet tsɔli ɔmɛ hia kɛ je Mahanaim kɛ ho Gibeon ya.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Zeruya binyumu Yoab kɛ David tsɔli ɔmɛ hu hia kɛ je kpo nɛ a kɛ mɛ ya kpe ngɛ Gibeon taku ɔ nya. Kuu kake bua a he nya ngɛ taku ɔ hɛ mi, nɛ kuu kake hu bua a he nya ngɛ taku ɔ se.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Abner de Yoab ke, “Ha nɛ nihewi ɔmɛ nɛ a te si nɛ a ka a he mi kɛ je wa hɛja.” Yoab he nɔ ke, “Yoo, i kplɛɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nu e nyɛmi yi, nɛ e kɛ e klaate ɔ gbɔ e kasa, nɛ mɛ tsuo a nɔ si nɛ a gbo si kake too. Lɔ ɔ he nɛ a wo Gibeon lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke, “Klaate nga nɔ” ɔ nɛ. Asahel gbenɔ

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, a hwu ta nguaa ko jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, nɛ David kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ ye Abner kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Zeruya binyumu etɛ ɔmɛ hu ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Mɛ ji Yoab, Abishai, kɛ Asahel. Asahel nane nya sɔɔ kaa alɔngɔ.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Abner plɛ kɛ hyɛ e se nɛ e bi ke, “Asahel, mo lo?” Nɛ e he nɔ ke, “Ee, imi.”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Abner de lɛ ke, “Jɔɔ ye se nyɛɛmi! Tuu fo ya na nihewi ɔmɛ, nɛ o nu a ti nɔ kake, nɛ o kpɔ e ta yibu ní ɔ ngɛ e dɛ.” Se loloolo ɔ, Asahel nyɛɛ e se.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Abner de lɛ ekohu ke, “Kpale ngɛ ye se nɛ o ko ha ma fia mo nɔ́ nɛ ma gbe. Ke i pee ja a, kɛ ma plɛ kɛ hyɛ o nyɛmi Yoab hɛ mi kɛɛ?”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Se loloolo ɔ, Asahel kplɛɛ we. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Abner kɛ e we akplɔ ɔ se je ɔ gbɔ Asahel muklii mi, nɛ akplɔ ɔ nya ya hia kpo ngɛ Asahel se mi. Asahel nɔ si nɛ e gbo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɔuu, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ba su he nɛ e fɔɔ si ngɛ ɔ, ba da si dii.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Yoab kɛ Abishai nyɛɛ Abner se, nɛ benɛ pu maa ho si nɔmi ya a, a ya su Ama yoku ɔ he, ngɛ Giya kasa nya, kɛ yaa Gibeon nga a nɔ.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Abner kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ nɛ je Benyamin wɛtso ɔ mi ɔ ya bua a he nya ekohu ngɛ yoku ko yi mi.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Abner kpa ngmlaa kɛ tsɛ Yoab nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Anɛ waa ya nɔ waa hi wa he gbee kɛ mwɔɔ lo? Anɛ o li kaa nyagbenyagbe ɔ, wɔ tsuo wa hɛ mi ma kpata lo? Mɛni be o ngɛ mlɛe loko o fa o we bi ɔmɛ nɛ a jɔɔ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a nyɛmimɛ a se nyɛɛmi lo?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Yoab he nɔ ke, “I na Mawu hɛ kalɔ ɔ, jinɛ kaa o tu we munyu po ɔ, kɛ yaa si hwɔɔ mɔtu ɔ, ye we bi ɔmɛ ma kpa nyɛ se nyɛɛmi!”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yoab kpa titimati nɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo jɔɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ a se nyɛɛmi; nɛ ta a se po.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Abner kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ kpale a se kɛ ya gu Yordan kɔ̃ ɔ mi. A po Yordan pa a, nɛ e nɔ jena a, a nyɛɛ mɔtu ɔ tsuo kɛ ya si a su Mahanaim.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Yoab kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ngɔ Asahel nɛ a ya pu lɛ ngɛ e tsɛ yɔkɔ ɔ mi ngɛ Betlehem. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a nyɛɛ nyɔnyɔɔnyɔ, nɛ je ba na mɛ heii ngɛ Hebron.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul we ɔ, kɛ David we ɔ ngɛ ta hwue ɔ, Abner ba na blɔ nya ngɛ Saul we ɔ.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Saul ngɛ plã ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Rizpa, nɛ ji Aya biyo. Ligbi ko ɔ, Saul bi Ishboshet ya bi Abner ke, “Mɛni he je o kɛ tsaatsɛ plã a ya na bɔmi ɔ?”

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Abner muklii mi fu wawɛɛ nitsɛ ngɛ munyu ɔ nɛ Ishboshet bi lɛ ɔ he, nɛ e de ke, “Anɛ e peeɔ mo kaa kuasia ji mi lo? Hyɛ, i kɛ o tsɛ, kɛ e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ e huɛmɛ ɔmɛ hi si saminya. I je we mo kɛ wui David dɛ mi. Mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ, moo o ngɛ sane poe kɛ ngɛ ye nɔ fɔe ke i kɛ nɔ ko yo ya na bɔmi!

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: Yawɛ wo David si kaa e ma kpɔ matsɛ yemi ɔ ngɛ Saul kɛ e weku kɛ nina a dɛ, nɛ e maa to David matsɛ sɛ ɔ si, konɛ e ye Israel kɛ Yuda tsuo a nɔ kɛ maa je Dan kɛ yaa si Beersheba. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke i ha we nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ nɛ ba mi ɔ, lɛɛ Mawu nɛ fia mi nɔ́ nɛ e gbe!”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Ishboshet nyɛ we nɛ e de Abner nɔ kpa ko hu; ejakaa e ye lɛ gbeye.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Abner tsɔ kɛ ya Hebron he nɛ David ngɛ ɔ ke a ya bi lɛ ke, “Zugba a, mɛnɔ lɛ yeɔ nɔ?” E ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Mo ha nɛ waa so somi ko, nɛ ma piɛ o he kɛ gbla Israel tsuo kɛ ba o ngɔ.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Heto nɛ David ha kɛ mane ji, “Saminya! I kɛ mo maa so somi nɛ ɔ. Se nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ hlae nɛ o pee ha mi ji kaa ke o ma a, o kpaka Saul biyo Mikal ba ha mi. Ke pi ja a, lɛɛ i hla we nɛ ma na o hɛ mi.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: David tsɔ ke a ya de Saul bi Ishboshet hu ke, “Moo kpale ye yo Mikal ɔ ba ha mi; Filisti bi a mɔmlɔtɔ lafa kake nɛ i kɛ pee e he ní.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Ishboshet tsɔ ya kpaka yo ɔ kɛ je e huno Paltiel, Laish bi ɔ ngɔ kɛ ba.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Paltiel fo ya kɛ nyɛɛ yo ɔ se hluu kɛ ya su Bahurim tɔɔ. Se Abner de lɛ ke, “Kpale o se esɔesɔ!” Nɛ e kpale e se.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Abner tsɛ Israel nimeli ɔmɛ kpe, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Be saii ji nɛ ɔ, jinɛ nyɛ ngɛ David se blɔ hlae nɛ nyɛɛ wo lɛ matsɛ.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ lɛɛ be ɔ su; nyɛ tsu he ní. Nyɛ kai kaa Yawɛ wo David si ke, ‘Ma gu ye tsɔlɔ David nine nɔ kɛ kpɔ ye ma, Israel kɛ je Filisti bi ɔmɛ, kɛ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ tsuo a dɛ mi.’ ”

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Abner kɛ Benyamin wɛtso ɔ hu ya na ní sɛɛmi. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ya Hebron nɛ e ya bɔ David nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Israel kɛ Benyamin we ɔ wo si ke a maa pee ɔ.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Benɛ Abner ba David ngɔ ngɛ Hebron ɔ, nyumuhi nyingmi enyɔ piɛ e he kɛ ba; nɛ David tsɛ mɛ ní yemi.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Abner de David ke, “Jehanɛ, i yaa nɛ ma ya bua Israel ma a tsuo nya kɛ ba mo, ye nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ o ngɔ. A maa kplɛɛ nɛ o ye a nɔ matsɛ; kɛkɛ o nine maa su nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ hlae ɔ nɔ, nɛ o maa ye zugba a tsuo nɔ.” Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, David wo Abner blɔ; nɛ e ho ngɛ he jɔmi mi. A gbe Abner

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: E kɛ we nɛ Yoab kɛ David tsɔli kpa komɛ ba lejɛ ɔ. A ya tua ni komɛ nɛ a kpɔ a níhi babauu kɛ ba. Se a ba na we Abner ngɛ David ngɔ ngɛ Hebron, ejakaa David wo lɛ blɔ momo, nɛ e je ngɛ he jɔmi mi.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Yoab kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ a lejɛ ɔ sumi pɛ nɛ a bɔ lɛ amaniɛ ke Ner binyumu Abner ba Matsɛ David ngɔ, nɛ David wo lɛ blɔ kɛ ho ngɛ he jɔmi mi.

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Yoab ya nɛ e ya de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Mɛni o pee nɛ ɔ? Hyɛ kaa Abner ba o ngɔ! Mɛni he je o ngmɛɛ e he nɛ e ho ɔ?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Ná nɛ o le kaa Ner bi Abner ɔ, sisimi e ba sisi mo nɛ e kɛ le o yami kɛ bami, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ pee.”

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yoab je David ngɔ ɔ, e tsɔ nihi kɛ nyɛɛ Abner se. Ni ɔmɛ ya ná lɛ ngɛ Sira nyu vu ɔ he, nɛ a kpale lɛ kɛ ba. Se David li he nɔ́ ko.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Benɛ Abner kpale kɛ ba Hebron ɔ, Yoab nu e nine si nɛ e kɛ lɛ ho ma a agbo ɔ nya ya kaa nɔ́ nɛ e kɛ lɛ yaa dami. Yoab gbɔ Abner muklii mi nɔ́ nɛ e gbe lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ngɛ e nyɛmi Asahel muɔ nɛ Abner pue si ɔ he.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Pee se benɛ David ba nu sane ɔ he ɔ, e de ke, “Yawɛ le kaa Ner bi Abner muɔ si nɛ a pue nɛ ɔ he musu ko musu ko tloo we i kɛ ye nɔ yemi sisi bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Musu ɔ nɛ tloo Yoab kɛ e tsɛ we ɔ tsuo. Se tso mi hiɔtsɛ, loo nɔ ko nɛ he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya ngɛ e he, loo nyumu nɛ peeɔ e ní kaa yo, loo nɔ nɛ a gbe lɛ ngɛ ta mi, loo hwɔ yeyeetsɛ kó ta Yoab kɛ e nina a we mi gblegbleegble.”

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Yoab kɛ e nyɛminyumu Abishai gbe Abner, ejakaa lɛ hu e gbe a nyɛminyumu Asahel ngɛ Gibeon ta a mi. A pu Abner

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: David fa Yoab kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ hía tade ɔmɛ ngɛ nyɛ he, nɛ nyɛ bu kpekpe ya bo kɛ nyɛ ya, nɛ nyɛɛ wo yana ha Abner.” Matsɛ David nitsɛ nyɛɛ gbogboe ɔ se.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Benɛ a ya pu Abner ngɛ Hebron ɔ, matsɛ ɔ fo ya yuuyuuyuu ngɛ yɔkɔ ɔ he; nɛ ma a tsuo wo yana kɛ piɛ e he.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Matsɛ David la aywilɛho la nɛ ɔ kɛ nyɛ ya ha Abner: “Anɛ e sa kaa o gbo kaa kuasia gboɔ lo?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: O nine ɔmɛ ɔ, a tsa fi we mɛ; o nane ɔmɛ hu, a wui mɛ pã. Bɔ nɛ dikali taneɔ nɔ yi ɔ, ja pɛ a gbe mo nɛ ɔ nɛ.” Ma a tsuo wo yana ha Abner ekohu.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Ma a nyɛ David nɔ ligbi ɔ tsuo ke e ye nɔ́ ko. Se David ka kita nɛ e de ke, “Ke i wo ye nya mi nɔ́ ko loko pu nɔ si ɔ, Mawu nɛ fia mi nɔ́ nɛ e gbe!”

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Ma a yɔse nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, nɛ e sa a hɛ mi. Niinɛ, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ matsɛ ɔ pee ɔ sa ma a hɛ mi saminya.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David we bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Israel tsuo na le jamɛ a ligbi ɔ kaa David li Ner bi Abner gbenɔ ɔ he nɔ́ ko.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, matsɛ ɔ de e tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ ná nɛ nyɛɛ le kaa ganɔ kɛ nɔmlɔ nguaa ko nɔ ngɛ Israel mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Imi lɛɛ a pɔ mi nu nɛ a wo mi matsɛ mohu, se mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, i pee kaa nɔ nɛ be he wami. Kikɛmɛ a Zeruya binyumu nɛ ɔmɛ a sane wa pe mi. Yawɛ nɛ wo yayami peelɔ ɔ hiɔ bɔ nɛ sa lɛ!”

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul bi Ishboshet nu kaa a gbe Abner ngɛ Hebron ɔ, e nine mi je wu; nɛ Israel tsuo dɛ yaa.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ishboshet ngɛ asafoatsɛmɛ enyɔ; nɔ kake biɛ ji Baana, nɛ nɔ kake hu biɛ ji Rekab. Beerot no Rimon nɛ je Benyamin wɛtso ɔ mi ɔ bimɛ ji mɛ. (A buu Beerot ngɔ siɔ Benyamin nɔ.

english_verse: The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
translation_verse: Beerot bi ɔmɛ nitsɛ lɛɛ a tu fo kɛ ya dumɔ Gitaim, nɛ a tlɔ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ.)

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Saul bi Yonatan ngɛ bi akpaketsɛ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Mefiboshet. Benɛ Saul kɛ Yonatan gbenɔ sane ɔ pɛ ngɛ Yezreel ɔ, jamɛ a be ɔ, Mefiboshet ye jeha enuɔ. A tsɔɔ kaa benɛ sane ɔ ba a, bimɛanyɛ nɛ ngɛ e nɔ hyɛe ɔ ngɔ lɛ kɛ tu fo. Se nɛ e ngɛ esɔ yee ɔ, jokuɛ ɔ je e dɛ nɔ si nɛ e hule.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Beerot no Rimon bimɛ Rekab kɛ Baana ya Ishboshet we ɔ mi piani katakata benɛ Ishboshet kpasa si bɔɔ.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Benɛ a sɛ we ɔ mi ɔ, a na Ishboshet nɛ hwɔɔ si ngɛ sa nɔ ngɛ e se tsu ɔ mi. Nɛ a fia lɛ nɔ́ nɛ a gbe ngɔ wo sa mi. A po e yi nɛ a kɛ yi ɔ nyɛɛ nyɔnyɔɔnyɔ kɛ ya gu Yordan kɔ̃ ɔ mi.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: A kɛ Ishboshet yi ɔ ba ha Matsɛ David ngɛ Hebron, nɛ a de lɛ ke, “O he nyɛlɔ Saul nɛ hla kaa e ma kpata o hɛ mi ɔ, e bi Ishboshet yi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, Yawɛ ha nɛ wa nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ ye lue ngɛ Saul kɛ e nina a nɔ.”

english_verse: David answered: I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble!
translation_verse: Se David ha mɛ heto ke, “I na Yawɛ, hɛ kalɔ ɔ nɛ he ye yi wami kɛ je amanehluhi tsuo a mi ɔ!

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: Benɛ nɔ ko ba bɔ mi amaniɛ ngɛ Ziklag ke Saul gbo, nɛ e pee lɛ kaa manye munyu nɛ e hɛɛ kɛ ba a, i nu lɛ nɛ i gbe lɛ. Lɔ ɔ ji sina nɛ e na kɛ je ye dɛ ngɛ munyu ɔ nɛ e kɛ ba a he.

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Lɛɛ ke nyɛ dikali nyɛ ya gbe nɔ ko nɛ pee we yayami ko kɛ wo sa mi ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e we mi ɔ, anɛ e sɛ kaa i yeɔ e gbenɔ ɔ he lue, nɛ ma kpata nyɛ hɛ mi kɛ je zugba a nɔ lo?”

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David fa e we bi ɔmɛ nɛ a gbe Rekab kɛ Baana; a poo a ninehi kɛ a nanehi, nɛ a ngɔ mɛ ngɔ kpla si ngɛ Hebron taku ɔ kasa nya. Se Ishboshet yi ɔ lɛɛ a ya pu ngɛ Abner yɔkɔ ɔ mi ngɛ Hebron.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Tiro matsɛ, Hiram wo tsɔli blɔ kɛ ba David ngɔ. A kɛ seda tsohi ba. Kapitɛhi, kɛ tɛ tsu fiali hu piɛ a he; nɛ a ba po we ha David.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: E hi Hebron kɛ ye Yuda nɔ matsɛ jeha kpaago kɛ fa; nɛ e hi Yerusalem kɛ ye Israel kɛ Yuda tsuo a nɔ matsɛ jeha nyingmi etɛ kɛ etɛ. David pee Yerusalem e matsɛ ma (Kronika I,

english_verse: David told his troops, “You will have to go up through the water tunnel to get those Jebusites. I hate people like them who can't walk or see.” That's why there is still a rule that says, “Only people who can walk and see are allowed in the temple.” David captured the fortress on Mount Zion, then he moved there and named it David's City. He had the city rebuilt, starting with the landfill to the east.
translation_verse: David hi mɔ nguaa a mi, nɛ e wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke “David ma.” David po ma kɛ bɔle si; e to ma a sisi kɛ je he nɛ a tloo zu ngɔ pue ɔ, kɛ ba mi blɔ.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Matsɛ David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ho ya tua Yerusalem. Yebus bi ɔmɛ nɛ ji zugba a nɔ bi ɔ, de David ke, “O be nyɛe maa ba hiɛ ɔ; hɛ yuyuili kɛ akpaketsɛmɛ po maa fie mo kɛ je hiɛ ɔ.” Blɔɔ a susumi ji David be nyɛe nɛ e ya lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: David ya nɔ wawɛɛ nitsɛ; ejakaa Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ Mawu ɔ kɛ lɛ ngɛ.

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: David yɔse kaa Yawɛ to lɛ si kaa Israel matsɛ, nɛ e ha e matsɛ yemi ɔ ya nɔ ngɛ e ma Israel ɔ he.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Benɛ David hia kɛ je Hebron kɛ ba Yerusalem ɔ, e ba ngɔ yihi babauu, nɛ e su plahi fuu; nɛ a fɔ binyumuhi kɛ biyihi ha David kɛ piɛ kekle ni ɔmɛ a he.

english_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
translation_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nefeg, Yafia,

english_verse: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. David Fights the Philistines (
translation_verse: Elishama, Elyada, kɛ Elifelet. A ye Filisti bi ɔmɛ a nɔ (Kronika I,

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Benɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ nu kaa a pɔ David nu nɛ a wo lɛ Israel matsɛ ɔ, mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a ba nɛ a ba hla lɛ nɛ a nu lɛ. Se David nu he nɛ e ya sɛ e mɔ nguaa a mi.

english_verse: So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Filisti bi ɔmɛ ba nɛ a ba gba wo Refaim kɔ̃ ɔ mi.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: David bi Yawɛ ke, “Ma ya tua Filisti bi ɔmɛ lo? O ma je mɛ kɛ wo ye dɛ mi lo?” Yawɛ ha David heto ke, “Ee, moo ya! Bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, ma je Filisti bi ɔmɛ kɛ wo o dɛ mi.”

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Filisti bi ɔmɛ je a wɔ ɔmɛ a he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ba muɔ kɛ ho.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Se Filisti bi ɔmɛ kpale a se nɛ a ya pue si ngɛ Refaim kɔ̃ ɔ mi ekohu.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Benɛ David ya bi Yawɛ ga womi ekohu ɔ, Yawɛ de lɛ ke, “Dɛbi, ko tua mɛ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ; yaa lɔgɔ kɛ gu a se je, nɛ o ya tua mɛ ngɛ tso ɔmɛ a he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Ke o nu nɔ́ ko nɛ ngɛ pɛe ngɛ tso ɔmɛ a yi mi kaa tabohi a nyɛɛmi ɔ, yaa nɛ o ya tua Filisti bi ɔmɛ; ejakaa Yawɛ nyɛɛ o hɛ mi kɛ yaa nɛ e ya gbe Filisti ta buli ɔmɛ.”

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: David pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa lɛ ɔ; nɛ e kpata Filisti bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi kɛ je Geba kɛ ya si Gezer tɔɔ.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Benɛ ni ɔmɛ nɛ hɛɛ Yawɛ daka a hia nane ekpa a, David ha nɛ a wa, nɛ e gbe na kɛ to nɛ wo zɔ nɛ e kɛ sã bɔ ha Yawɛ.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: David wo kploba efɔd, nɛ e do kɛ e he wami tsuo kɛ wo Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: David kɛ Israel tsuo ngɔ Yawɛ daka a kɛ ba kɛ lele hwɔmi kɛ koli kpami.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Benɛ daka a ba su David ma a mi ɔ, Mikal, Saul biyo ɔ je e hɛ mi kpo ngɛ saflɛ mi nɛ e na Matsɛ David nɛ e ngɛ tuue nɛ e ngɛ doe kɛ ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami woe; nɛ David he pee lɛ tai.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: A ya ngɔ somi daka a ngɛ Abinadab we ɔ mi ngɛ yoku ɔ nɔ, nɛ a kɛ ma tlɔɔke he mi. Abinadab binyumuhi Uza, kɛ Ahio ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ tlɔɔke ɔ nɛ Mawu daka a ngɛ mi ɔ blɔ tsɔɔe;

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: E kɛ mɛ tsuo ho Baala ya ngɛ Yuda, konɛ a ya ngɔ Mawu somi daka a ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba. Somi daka nɛ ɔ, a kɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ nɛ ngɛ tsɛ yee ngɛ kerub ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ biɛ tsɛɔ lɛ.

english_verse: with Ahio walking in front of it.
translation_verse: nɛ Ahio nyɛɛ daka a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, David kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ lae nɛ a ngɛ doe kɛ a he wami tsuo kɛ ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami woe. A fiɛ do, nɛ a fia kpa saku slɔɔtohi, kɛ ngmlɛhi, kɛ gɔgɔhi.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Benɛ a su Nakon ngma gbeemi he ɔ, na amɛ nɛ ngɛ tlɔɔke ɔ gblae ɔ a nanehi tɛ si, nɛ daka a mimiɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Uza nu daka a ngɔ da si.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Se Yawɛ Mawu mi mi fu Uza, nɛ e fia lɛ nɔ́ nɛ e gbe ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ejakaa e nine ta daka a he.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: E dɔ David kaa Yawɛ ngɔ abofu kɛ gbla Uza tue. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke Perez Uza, nɛ jã a tsɛɛ lɛ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: David ye Yawɛ gbeye jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, nɛ e bi ke, “Lɛɛ kɛ ma pee kɛ ngɔ somi daka a kɛ ya we mi kɛɛ?”

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, David to e yi mi kaa e kɛ Yawɛ daka a be Yerusalem yae hu. Kɛkɛ nɛ e gba kɛ je blɔ ɔ nɔ nɛ e kɛ daka a ho Obed Edom nɛ je Gat ɔ we mi ya.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Benɛ Matsɛ David nu kaa Mawu daka a he je ɔ, Yawɛ gbaa Obed Edom kɛ e we ɔ, kɛ e nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e ngɛ ɔ, David ho nɛ e ya ngɔ Mawu daka a ngɛ Obed Edom we ɔ mi, nɛ e kɛ daka a ba Yerusalem kɛ nyami.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: A ngɔ Yawɛ daka a ya ma e ma he ngɛ bo tsu nɛ David pee kɛ ha lɛ ɔ mi, nɛ David sã sami bɔhi, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔhi kɛ ha Yawɛ.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Benɛ David sã bɔ ɔmɛ gbe nya a, e gbaa ma a ngɛ Yawɛ Ope ɔ biɛ mi.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: David dla niye ní ha Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ, nyumuhi kɛ yihi tsuo. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ ná abolo bɔbɔɛ kake, kɛ lo nɛ a sã kpɔ kake, kɛ wai yiblii gbigbli nɛ a kɛ si tatale. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a je kɛ ho a wehi a mi ya.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Benɛ David ba su we mi, nɛ e ba fɔ e yi ɔmɛ, kɛ e bimɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, Saul biyo Mikal je kpo ba kpee lɛ; nɛ e de David ke, “Lɔ ɔ ji Israel matsɛ wo lɛ nitsɛ e hɛ mi nyami mwɔnɛ ɔ nɛ! Matsɛ hɛɛ e he gu ngɛ e tsɔli a mawayi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi kaa kuasia peeɔ nɔ!”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: David he nɔ ke, “I do kɛ wo Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami. Lɛ nɛ e hla mi ngɛ o tsɛ kɛ e weku kɛ nina nane mi, nɛ e wo mi ganɔ kɛ ha Israel ma a. Ee, ma do kɛ wo Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami daa,

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: nɛ ye hɛ mi ma pue si pe kikɛ nɛ ɔ po. E maa pee mo kaa pi nɔ ko ji mi; se mawayi ɔmɛ nɛ o tu a he munyu ɔ, mɛɛ lɛɛ a maa bu mi saminya.”

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Se ye suɔmi kɛ mɔbɔ nami ɔ lɛɛ i be jee ngɛ e nɔ gblegbleegble. I be lɛ pee kaa bɔ nɛ i pee Saul, nɔ nɛ i je kɛ je o blɔ mi nɛ o ba ye matsɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: David de gbalɔ Natan ke, “Hyɛ kaa imi lɛɛ i ngɛ we nɛ a ma kɛ seda mi, be mi nɛ Mawu somi daka a lɛɛ bo tsu mi lɛ e ngɛ!”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Natan de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o to kaa o maa pee ɔ, moo pee; ejakaa Yawɛ kɛ mo ngɛ.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Se jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Yawɛ de Natan ke,

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Yaa nɛ o ya de ye tsɔlɔ David ke Yawɛ ke, ‘Pi mo nɛ o maa po we ha mi nɛ ma hi mi.

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Kɛ je ligbi nɛ i ya kpɔ Israel ma a kɛ je Egipt kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, i hí we ko mi hyɛ; bo tsu ji we nɛ i hii mi.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Ngɛ hehi tsuo nɛ i kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ya gu ɔ, Israel hɛ mi nyɛɛli nɛ i hia ke a hɛɛ ye ma Israel kaa bɔ nɛ to hyɛlɔ hyɛɛ e tohi ɔ, anɛ i bi a ti nɔ ko hyɛ ke mɛni he je e kɛ seda ma we tsu ha mi lo?’

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mo de ye tsɔlɔ David ke, imi Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ, i ngɛ lɛ dee ke, ‘Imi nɛ i ya ngɔ mo kɛ je lohwe lɛmi he, kɛ je tohi a se, konɛ o ba ye ganɔ ngɛ ye ma, Israel nɔ.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Imi lɛ i kɛ mo nyɛɛ kɛ ya kɛ ba; nɛ imi nɔuu lɛ i kpata o he nyɛli ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi ngɛ o blɔ ɔ nɔ. Ma ha nɛ o ma na biɛ kaa nimli nguahi nɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ a ti nɔ ko.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Ke o gbo, nɛ a ya dla mo ngɛ o nɛmɛ ɔmɛ a hwɔ he ɔ, ma tle nɔ ko si ngɛ o se, nɛ ji mo nitsɛ o mi mi bi; nɛ ma to e matsɛ yemi ɔ sisi.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Lɛ ji nɔ nɛ ma ba po we kɛ wo ye biɛ ɔ hɛ mi nyami; nɛ ma ha e matsɛ yemi ɔ maa hi si kɛ maa ya neneene.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Ma pee e tsɛ, nɛ e maa pee ye bi. Ke e pee nɔ́ nɛ dɛ ɔ, ma gbla e tue kaa bɔ nɛ tsɛ gblaa e bi tue ɔ.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ Israel Mawu! O je tsɔɔ o tsɔlɔ ɔ kaa e matsɛ yemi ɔ se be poe gblegbleegble; lɔ ɔ he nɛ o tsɔlɔ ɔ nɔ gbagba te, nɛ e ngɛ kue nɛ ɔ fae ha mo ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Matsɛ David ya sɛ bo tsu ɔ mi, nɛ e ya hi si ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi, nɛ e de ke, “Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, mɛnɔ ji mi, nɛ ye we ɔ hu mɛnɔmɛ ji mɛ loko o hɛɛ mi kɛ ba su he nɛ i ngɛ nɛ ɔ?

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Lɛɛ mɛni pa ngɛ imi David, ye nya nɛ ma de mo? Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, o le imi o tsɔlɔ ɔ saminya!

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: O ngɛ ní nguangua nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo pee nɛ ma kɛ le kaa o wo si ko, nɛ o suɔ kaa o maa pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Yawɛ Mawu lee, o kle agbo! Nɔ ko nɔ ko be nɛ ngɛ kaa mo; níhi nɛ wa nu ɔ tsɔɔ kaa mo pɛ ji Mawu.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Ma kpa ko be zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ nɛ pe o ma Israel nɛ mo Mawu o ya kpɔ kɛ je nyɔguɛ si himi mi kɛ ba pee mo nitsɛ o ma a. Ní nguangua, kɛ nyakpɛ níhi nɛ o tsu ha o ma a, ha o biɛ pɛ kɛ kpe je ɔ mi tsuo. Benɛ o ma a nɛ o kpɔ kɛ je Egipt ɔ hia kɛ ma a, o fie je ma kpa amɛ, kɛ a mawu ɔmɛ kɛ je a blɔ mi.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: O to o ma Israel sisi, nɛ o ngɔ lɛ ngɔ pee mo nitsɛ o ma kɛ yaa neneene. Nɛ mo, Yawɛ o ba pee a Mawu.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: O biɛ maa jije kɛ maa ya neneene, nɛ nihi ma de ke, Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ ji Israel Mawu. Nɛ o ma ha imi, o tsɔlɔ David, ye matsɛ yemi ɔ maa hi si kɛ maa ya neneene.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: “Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, mo ji Mawu, nɛ o yeɔ o siwohi a nɔ daa. Mo ji nɔ nɛ wo mi si kpakpa nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o ya nɔ nɛ o gbaa imi, o tsɔlɔ ɔ, ye nina daa. Mo Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ o wo si; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, o gbaami maa hi imi, o tsɔlɔ ɔ, ye nina nɔ kɛ maa ya neneene.”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Yehoyada binyumu Benaya ji Keret kɛ Pelet bi ɔmɛ a nyatsɛ. Keret kɛ Pelet bi ɔmɛ ji David we bi a tabo. David binyumu ɔmɛ ji osɔfohi.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: E ya tua Moab bi ɔmɛ hulɔ nɛ e ye a nɔ. E ha nɛ ni ɔmɛ hwɔ si ngɛ zugba, nɛ e gba a mi etɛɛtɛ. Ni etɛ tsuaa ni etɛ mi ɔ, e gbe ni enyɔ, nɛ e kɛ nɔ kake he ke lɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Moab bi ɔmɛ ba pee David sɔmɔli, nɛ a tsuɔ tó kɛ haa lɛ.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ se, David ya ye Rehob binyumu Hadadezer, nɛ ji Zoba matsɛ ɔ nɔ kunimi. Jamɛ a be ɔ, Hadadezer ngɛ blɔ nɔ kɛ yaa, konɛ e ya kpɔ e zugba a nɛ ngɛ Yufrate pa a he ɔ ekohu.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: David to tabohi a hi hehi ngɛ Damasko; nɛ Siria bi ɔmɛ ba plɛ pee David sɔmɔli, nɛ a tsuɔ tó kɛ haa lɛ. Yawɛ ha nɛ David ye kunimi ngɛ he tsuaa he.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: David kpɔ sika tsu tsɛ̃i ɔmɛ nɛ Hadadezer tsɔli ɔmɛ hɛɛ ɔ ngɛ a dɛ, nɛ e kɛ ho Yerusalem ya.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ hu, David ya muɔ akɔblee babauu nitsɛ ngɛ Beta kɛ Berotai nɛ ji mahi nɛ matsɛ Hadadezer yeɔ a nɔ ɔ.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: e tsɔ e binyumu Yoram ya nga David, nɛ e ha lɛ ayekoo kaa e kɛ Hadadezer hwu ta nɛ e ye e nɔ kunimi; ejakaa lɛ Toi ɔ nitsɛ e kɛ Hadadezer hwu ta hluu. Yoram hɛɛ sika hiɔ, sika tsu, kɛ akɔblee nike níhi kɛ ho.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
