translation_verse: Matsɛ David gbaa ní nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ kɛ ha Yawɛ kɛ piɛ sika hiɔ kɛ sika tsu nɛ e kpɔ ngɛ je ma amɛ nɛ e ye a nɔ ɔ a dɛ ɔ he.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Ahitub binyumu Zadok, kɛ Abiatar binyumu Ahimelek ji osɔfohi; nɛ Seraya ji David nitsɛ e pɛdiyo.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Yoab, nɛ e nyɛ biɛ ji Zeruya a, ji tatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma; Ahilud binyumu Yehoshafat ji sanehi ngmalɔ;

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, David bi si ke, “Anɛ Saul nina ko piɛ lo? Ke nɔ ko ngɛ ɔ, ma suɔ nɛ ma na lɛ mɔbɔ ngɛ Yonatan he.”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Tsɔlɔ ko ngɛ Saul we ɔ mi nɛ e biɛ ji Ziba; nɛ a tsɛ lɛ kɛ ba David hɛ mi. Matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Mo ji Ziba a lo?” Nɛ e he nɔ ke, “Ee imi, ye nyɔmtsɛ.”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ekohu ke, “Anɛ Saul nina ko be, nɛ ma na lɛ mɔbɔ kaa bɔ nɛ i wo Mawu si ɔ lo?” Ziba de matsɛ ɔ ke, “E piɛ Yonatan binyumu kake; se lɛɛ akpaketsɛ ji lɛ.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Jije e ngɛ?” Ziba he nɔ ke, “E ngɛ Amiel binyumu Makir we ɔ mi ngɛ Lodebar ma a mi.”

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Saul bibi Mefiboshet, nɛ ji Yonatan bi ɔ ba David ngɔ ɔ, e kpla si nɛ e kɛ e hɛ mi bu si kɛ tsɔɔ bumi. David tsɛ e biɛ ke, “Mefiboshet!” Nɛ e he nɔ ke, “Ye nyɔmtsɛ.”

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: David ya nɔ nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Koo ye gbeye; ejakaa o tsɛ Yonatan he ɔ, ma na mo mɔbɔ. Ma kpale o nɛ̃, Saul zugba amɛ tsuo kɛ ha mo, nɛ ye okplɔɔ he o maa ye ní ngɛ daa.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Mefiboshet kpla si ngɛ David hɛ mi ekohu, nɛ e de ke, “Mɛnɔ po ji mi nɛ o naa mi mɔbɔ kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Imi, o tsɔlɔ nɛ i ngɛ kaa gbe gbogboe ɔ!”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, matsɛ ɔ tsɛ Saul tsɔlɔ Ziba, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “I ngɔ Saul gbosi ní tsuo kɛ ngɛ o nyɔmtsɛ ɔ bibi Mefiboshet hae.

english_verse: Ziba replied, “Your Majesty, I will do exactly what you tell me to do.” So Ziba's family and servants worked for Mephibosheth. Mephibosheth was lame, but he lived in Jerusalem and ate at David's table, just like one of David's own sons. And he had a young son of his own, named Mica.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Mefiboshet nɛ e nane enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo kplɔ ngɛ e sisi ɔ, lɛɛ e hi Yerusalem; nɛ e yeɔ ní ngɛ matsɛ okplɔɔ he daa ligbi.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Benɛ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Hadadezer sɔmɔe ɔ ná le kaa Israel bi ɔmɛ ye a nɔ ɔ, a kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ya kpata, nɛ a sɔmɔ mɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Siria bi ɔmɛ ye gbeye kaa a ma ya piɛ Amon bi ɔmɛ a he ekohu.

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: Amon ganɔ ɔmɛ bi a matsɛ Hanun ɔ ke, “O susu kaa David tsɔ nihi ba ha mo lakpoo, konɛ e kɛ wo o tsɛ hɛ mi nyami lo? Dɛbi! Ni ɔmɛ nɛ David tsɔ kɛ ba o ngɔ ɔ, pe a ba nɛ a ba slaa ma a, nɛ a kɛ kpa níhi si loko a ba tua wɔ.”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Hanun nuu David tsɔli ɔmɛ nɛ e sɛ a kpɛni kasa fa kake, nɛ e hía a tade ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ kpɛti tutuutu kɛ ba su a mlɛ mi, nɛ e ngmɛɛ a he nɛ a ho.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Benɛ David nu nɔ́ nɛ ba a; e tsɔ ya de mɛ ke a mlɛ ngɛ Yeriko kɛ yaa si a kpɛni ɔmɛ maa hɛ loko a ba, ejakaa e ngɛ mɛ zo pee kaa a maa kpale kɛ ba bɔ nɛ a ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Benɛ Amon bi ɔmɛ na kaa a ya hla munyu ngɛ David he ɔ, a tsɔ ya bɔ Siria ta buli akpe nyingmi enyɔ apaa kɛ je Bet Rehob kɛ Zoba. Jehanɛ hu, a ya bɔ Maaka matsɛ, kɛ e we bi akpe apaa kɛ piɛ Tob bi akpe nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ a he.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Moo pee kã, nɛ o ha nɛ waa da si kaa nyumuhi kɛ ha wa nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ wa Mawu ɔ ma amɛ. Nɔ́ nɛ sa Yawɛ hɛ mi ɔ, e pee.”

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: Benɛ David nu he ɔ, e wo Yoab kɛ Israel tabo ɔ blɔ nɛ a kɛ mɛ ya kpe.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Amon bi ɔmɛ hia nɛ a ya gba ta ngɛ a ma nguaa a nɛ a tsɛɛ Raba a agbo ɔ nya. Se ni kpa amɛ nɛ ji Siria bi ɔmɛ, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ je Tob kɛ Maaka a, mɛɛ lɛɛ a tsɔ a he kɛ ho nga a nɔ ya.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Yoab na bɔ nɛ a gba ta a ha, kaa a ma lɛ tuami kɛ je hɛ mi kɛ se blɔ tsuo. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e hla Israel ta buli komɛ nɛ a kɔni si wa, nɛ e ngɔ mɛ ngɔ kpee Siria bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ, e ngɔ mɛ ngɔ wo e nyɛminyumu Abishai dɛ mi, konɛ mɛ hu a kɛ Amon bi ɔmɛ ya kpe.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Yoab de lɛ ke, “Ke e ba mi kaa i ya nyɛ we Siria bi ɔmɛ ɔ, lɛɛ o ba nɛ o ba piɛ ye he. Se ke Amon bi ɔmɛ ngɛ mo gbee ɔ, lɛɛ imi ma ba piɛ o he.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Yoab kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ hia kɛ ba na Siria bi ɔmɛ, konɛ a kɛ mɛ nɛ ba hwu; se Siria bi ɔmɛ tu fo.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Benɛ Amon bi ɔmɛ na kaa Siria bi ɔmɛ tu fo ɔ, mɛ hu a tu fo ngɛ ta nɛ a kɛ Abishai ngɛ hwue ɔ nya kɛ ho ma a mi ya. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yoab jɔɔ Amon bi ɔmɛ a se nyɛɛmi, nɛ e kpale kɛ ho Yerusalem ya.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Benɛ Siria bi ɔmɛ na kaa Israel bi ɔmɛ ye a nɔ ɔ, a ya bua a he nya.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Hadadezer tsɔ nɛ a ya ngɔ Siria bi nɛ ngɛ Yufrate pa a se ɔ kɛ ba, nɛ Hadadezer we asafoatsɛ Shobak nyɛɛ a hɛ mi kɛ ba Helam.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
translation_verse: Benɛ David nu he ɔ, e bua Israel tsuo nya, nɛ e kɛ mɛ po Yordan pa a kɛ ho Helam ya. Siria bi ɔmɛ gba ta wo David, nɛ a kɛ lɛ hwu.

english_verse: It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Gbo be mi nɛ́ matsɛmɛ pɔɔ ta gbami ɔ, David tsɔ Yoab kɛ e we asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ Israel tabo ɔ tsuo kɛ ho nɛ a ya kpata Amon bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ a sa Raba ma a yi. Jamɛ a be ɔ, David nitsɛ lɛɛ e ngɛ Yerusalem.

english_verse: he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?
translation_verse: nɛ e ba mi kaa e mi mi fu nɛ e bi mo ke, ‘Mɛni he je nyɛ ya su ma a he haa kikɛ nɛ ɔ kɛ hwu ta a? Anɛ nyɛ li kaa a ma tsɛ̃ nyɛ kɛ̃ɛ̃ kɛ je gbogbo ɔ nɔ lo?

english_verse: But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, yo ɔ na kaa e hɛɛ mi, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e tsɔ ya de David.

english_verse: David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” Joab sent Uriah
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David tsɔ nɛ a kɛ sɛ gbi ya ha Yoab ke, “Ha nɛ Uria, Hit no ɔ nɛ ba.” Nɛ Yoab wo Uria blɔ kɛ ba David ngɔ.

english_verse: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
translation_verse: Benɛ Uria ba a, David bi lɛ Yoab kɛ tabo ɔmɛ a hwɔhwɔɛ, kɛ bɔ nɛ ta a ngɛ nɔ yae ha.

english_verse: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, David de Uria ke, “Yaa o we ɔ mi nɛ o ya jɔɔ o he bɔɔ.” Benɛ Uria je matsɛ we ɔ mi ɔ, matsɛ ɔ tsɔ nɛ a kɛ nike ní nyɛɛ e se.

english_verse: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
translation_verse: Se Uria yɛ we mi; mohu e kɛ e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo ya hwɔ matsɛ we ɔ agbo ɔ nya.

english_verse: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
translation_verse: Benɛ David nu kaa Uria yɛ we mi ɔ, e de Uria ke, “O hia blɔ be saii ji nɛ ɔ, nɛ piɔ pɛ o kpale kɛ ba. Mɛni he je nɛ o yɛ we mi ɔ?”

english_verse: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
translation_verse: Uria he nɔ ke, “Israel kɛ Yuda tsuo ngɛ ta hwue, nɛ somi daka a ngɛ a ngɔ. Jehanɛ, ye nyɔmtsɛ Yoab kɛ e we asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ hu pueɔ si ngɛ nga a nɔ; nɛ imi lɛɛ ma ya we mi nɛ ma ya ye ní, nɛ ma nu dã, nɛ i kɛ ye yo ya hwɔ si lo? I na o nane kaa i be nɔ́ nɛ ɔ pee!”

english_verse: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
translation_verse: David de Uria ke, “Lɛɛ moo hi hiɛ ɔ mwɔnɛ ɔ hulɔ, konɛ ma wo mo blɔ hwɔɔ nɛ o ho.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Uria hi si ngɛ Yerusalem jamɛ a ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, David tsɛ lɛ ní yemi; nɛ e ha e ye ní nɛ e nu dã saminya kɛ ya si e de. Se e yɛ we mi; gbɔkuɛ ɔ, e ho ya hwɔ e sa a nɔ ngɛ e nyɔmtsɛ ɔ tsɔli ɔmɛ a ngɔ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena mɔtu ɔ, David ngma Yoab womi, nɛ e ngɔ ha Uria kɛ ho.

english_verse: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ e ngma ngɛ womi ɔ mi ji, “Moo ngɔ Uria kɛ ya da ta a nya he nɛ mi he wa pe kulaa. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, nyɛɛ gbla nyɛ he si kɛ je e he, nɛ a fia lɛ ní nɛ e gbo.”

english_verse: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, benɛ Yoab ngɛ ma a yi sae ɔ, e ngɔ Uria ya da he nɛ e le kaa he nyɛli ɔmɛ a mi wa ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
translation_verse: He nyɛli ɔmɛ je kpo nɛ a kɛ Yoab we bi ɔmɛ ba hwu ta. David asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ekomɛ gbo; nɛ Uria, Hit no ɔ hu a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Yoab tsɔ nɛ a ya bɔ David nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ya nɔ ngɛ ta a mi.

english_verse: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
translation_verse: E je blɔ de tsɔlɔ ɔ ke, “Ke o bɔ matsɛ ɔ ta a mi sane ɔ tsuo gbe nya,

english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Nyɛ kaii we bɔ nɛ a gbe Gideon binyumu Abimelek ɔ? Anɛ pi Tebez nɛ yo ko ngɔ wɛ tɛ kɛ gu gbogbo nɔ kɛ ko e yi mi ngɛ nɛ e gbo lo? Mɛni he je nyɛ ya su gbogbo ɔ he haa kikɛ nɛ ɔ?’ Ke matsɛ ɔ bi mo kikɛmɛ a munyu nɛ ɔ, mo de lɛ ke, ‘O tsɔlɔ Uria, Hit no ɔ hu gbo.’ ”

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Tsɔlɔ ɔ ya bɔ David nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Yoab fa lɛ ke e ya de ɔ.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: E de David ke, “Wa he nyɛli ɔmɛ a he wa pe wɔ. A je ma a mi ba tua wɔ ngɛ nga a nɔ; se wa fie mɛ kɛ ho ma agbo ɔ nya ya.

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: A tsɛ̃ wɔ kɛ̃ɛ̃ kɛ je gbogbo ɔ nɔ. Nɛnɛ, asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ekomɛ gbo, nɛ o tsɔlɔ Uria, Hit no ɔ hu a gbe lɛ.”

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: David de tsɔlɔ ɔ ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya wo Yoab he wami, nɛ o de lɛ ke e ko ha nɛ sane nɛ ɔ nɛ hao lɛ; ejakaa klaate ngɛ nɛ ɔ, e hlɛ nɔ mi nɛ e gbee. De lɛ ke e ngɔ e he wami tsuo kɛ tua ma a, nɛ e ngɔ ma a.”

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Benɛ Uria yo ɔ nu kaa e huno Uria gbo ɔ, e nyɛ ya ha lɛ.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: Benɛ e nyɛ ya ha lɛ gbe nya a, David tsɔ ya ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba e we ɔ mi, nɛ e ba pee e yo; nɛ e fɔ binyumu ha lɛ. Se nɔ́ nɛ David pee nɛ ɔ ngɔɛ Yawɛ nya.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Niatsɛ ɔ ngɛ tohi kɛ nahi babauu nitsɛ;

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, nubwɔ ko ba to niatsɛ ɔ. Niatsɛ nɛ ɔ sume kaa e maa nu lɛ nitsɛ e to, loo na nɛ e gbe kɛ pee niye ní ha nubwɔ ɔ; se mohu e ya nu ohiatsɛ ɔ jijɔ bi ɔ nɛ e gbe kɛ ha e nubwɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: David mi mi fu jamɛ a niatsɛ ɔ wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ e de Natan ke, “I na Yawɛ kaa nɔmlɔ nɛ pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, ja e gbo!

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ se hu, kaa e nyɛ pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ nɛ mɔbɔ nami ko be e mi ɔ, e sa kaa e to jijɔ bi ɔ nane mi totoe eywiɛ.” David tue gblami

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Natan de David ke, “Mo tutuutu ji jamɛ a nyumu ɔ nɛ! Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Imi nɛ i pɔ mo nu nɛ i wo mo Israel matsɛ, nɛ i je mo kɛ je Saul dɛ mi.

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: Imi nɛ i ngɔ o nyɔmtsɛ Saul matsɛ yemi ɔ, kɛ e yi ɔmɛ ngɔ wo o dɛ mi; imi nɛ i wo mo Israel kɛ Yuda tsuo matsɛ. Ke ní nɛ ɔmɛ pi ha mo ɔ, jinɛ ma ngɔ totoe enyɔ ngɔ piɛ he ha mo.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ o tɔ Yawɛ mlaa a nɔ, nɛ o pee yayami kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ ngɛ e hɛ mi? O ha Amon bi ɔmɛ gbe Uria, Hit no ɔ ngɛ ta nga a nɔ, nɛ o ngɔ e yo ɔ kɛ ba pee o yo!

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, akɛnɛ o bui mi, nɛ o ya ngɔ Uria yo ɔ kɛ ba pee o yo he je ɔ, klaate nya gbenɔ fɔɔ si ha o weku kɛ nina kɛ yaa neneene.’

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ ngɛ mo dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Ma ha mo nitsɛ o we ɔ mi no ko ma tsɔ atuã kɛ wo mo. Ma kpɔ o yi ɔmɛ ngɛ o dɛ hɛ mi paa, nɛ ma ngɔ mɛ ngɔ ha o nyɛmi ko; nɛ e kɛ mɛ maa hwɔ piani katakata.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Moo o pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ngɛ laami mi; se imi lɛɛ ma pee nɔ́ nɛ i de nɛ ɔ piani katakata, konɛ Israel tsuo nɛ na.’ ” David pia e he

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ o kɛ nɔ́ nɛ o pee nɛ ɔ pue Yawɛ hɛ mi si he je ɔ, bi nɛ a fɔ ha mo ɔ ma gbo.”

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Natan je kɛ ho we mi ya. David binyumu ɔ gbo Yawɛ ha nɛ binyumu ɔ nɛ Uria yo ɔ kɛ David fɔ ɔ wo hiɔ.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: David kpa Mawu pɛɛ nɛ́ e ha nɛ jokuɛ ɔ nɛ na he wami. David kua ní yemi; nɛ daa nyɔ mi ɔ, e hwɔɔ zugba kɛ ya siɔ je nami.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: David we ɔ mi nimeli ɔmɛ maa ya e ngɔ, nɛ a ma ya fa kue ha lɛ kaa e maa te si ngɛ zugba a lo; se e kplɛɛ we, nɛ e kɛ mɛ yi ní hulɔ.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Otsi se ɔ, jokuɛ ɔ gbo, nɛ David tsɔli nikɔtɔma amɛ ye gbeye kaa a ma de lɛ ke jokuɛ ɔ gbo. A de ke, “Benɛ jokuɛ ɔ na we nɛ e gbo lolo ɔ, ke wa de lɛ nɔ́ ko ɔ, e pui wa nya mi; lɛɛ ke wa de lɛ ke jokuɛ ɔ gbo ɔ, tse e maa ye e he awi ngɔ fɔ wa nɔ!”

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Benɛ David na kaa e tsɔli ɔmɛ kɛ a he ngɛ ablɛgbi tue ɔ, e yɔse kaa jokuɛ ɔ gbo, nɛ e bi mɛ ke, “Jokuɛ ɔ gbo lo?” Nɛ a he nɔ ke, “Ee, e gbo.”

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ bi lɛ ke, “Kɛ ji nɔ́ nɛ o pee nɛ ɔ sisi kɛɛ? Benɛ jokuɛ nɛ ɔ ngɛ wami mi ɔ, o ha hwɔ nɛ o fo ya ha lɛ. Se benɛ jokuɛ ɔ gbo mohu ɔ, o te si nɛ o ye ní.”

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: David ha mɛ heto ke, “Benɛ jokuɛ ɔ na we nɛ e gbo lolo ɔ, i ha hwɔ nɛ i fo ya; ejakaa i susu kaa, alini Yawɛ maa na mi mɔbɔ nɛ jokuɛ ɔ yi ma na wami.

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Se piɔ nɛ e gbo ɔ, mɛni he je e sa kaa ma ha hwɔ ekohu? Anɛ ma nyɛ ma kpale lɛ kɛ ba wami mi ekohu lo? Imi mohu nɛ ma bu e nɔ ligbi ko; se lɛɛ e be kpalee kɛ ba ye ngɔ hu gblegbleegble.” A fɔ Salomo

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, David ba to e yo Batsheba tsui nɔ nine. E kɛ lɛ na bɔmi, nɛ e fɔ binyumu; nɛ David wo lɛ biɛ ke Salomo. Yawɛ suɔ jokuɛ ɔ saminya,

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (
translation_verse: nɛ e fa gbalɔ Natan ke e ya wo jokuɛ ɔ biɛ ke Yedidia; e sisi ji, “Nɔ nɛ Yawɛ suɔ lɛ.” David ye Raba bi a nɔ (Kronika I,

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Yoab gba ta wo Raba, Amon bi a ma nguaa a he, nɛ e miɔ nɛ e ngɔ ma a.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Yoab tsɔ ya de David ke, “I kɛ Raba bi hwu ta nɛ i kpɔ a nyu yɛmi he ɔ ngɛ a dɛ.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mo bua ta nɛ piɛ ɔ nya nɛ o ya tua ma a, konɛ mo nitsɛ o nine nɛ su ma a tsuo nɔ. Ke o pee we ja, nɛ i ya ye ma a nɔ ɔ, a maa ngɔ ye biɛ kɛ wo ma a.”

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, David ya bua e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo a nya, nɛ e ya tua Raba, nɛ e ngɔ ma a.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Ma a mi bi ɔmɛ nitsɛmɛ lɛɛ e muɔ mɛ kɛ ba nɛ e ba ha mɛ ní tsumi kpakpataa komɛ nɛ a kɛ sauhi kɛ dade gbiɛ slɔɔtohi tsuɔ. Jehanɛ se hu, e nyɛ ni ɔmɛ a nɔ nɛ a sã bliikisi. David pee Amon bi ɔmɛ a ma kpa amɛ tsuo kikɛ nɛ ɔ nɔuu. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, David kɛ ma a tsuo kpale kɛ ba Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: David binyumu Absalom ngɛ nyɛmiyo ko nɛ he ngɛ fɛu saminya. E biɛ ji Tamar. E ba mi kaa Tamar tsɛbi Amnon ba na suɔmi wawɛɛ kɛ ha e nyɛmiyo nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Suɔmi nɛ Amnon ngɛ kɛ ha e nyɛmiyo ɔ nya wa saminya, nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ba wo lɛ hiɔ. Amnon le kaa bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, e be e nyɛmiyo ɔ he blɔ nae; ejakaa yomiyo ji lɛ, nɛ a ngmɛ́ lɛ blɔ nɛ e kɛ nyumu nɛ na bɔmi.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Se Amnon ngɛ huɛ ko nɛ le nɔ́ he ga tomi saminya. E biɛ ji Yonadab, nɛ e kɛ Amnon peeɔ tsɛngua kɛ tsɛwayo bimɛ; ejakaa Yonadab tsɛ Shimea kɛ David peeɔ nɔ kɛ e senɔ.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Yonadab bi Amnon ke, “Mo matsɛbi mluku ɔ, mɛni ba loko o ngɛ flaae jenajena kikɛ nɛ ɔ?” Amnon he nɔ ke, “I suɔ Tamar, ye tsɛbi Absalom nyɛmiyo ɔ sane saminya.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Yonadab de lɛ ke, “Yaa hwɔ si nɛ o buá nɛ o pee kaa o be he wami. Ke o tsɛ ba slaa mo ɔ, de lɛ ke, ‘Mo ha nɛ ye nyɛmiyo Tamar ba ha mi niye ní nɛ ma ye. Ha nɛ e ba pee niye ní ɔ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ nɛ ma na; konɛ e hɛɛ ngɛ e dɛ mi nɛ ma ye.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Amnon ho ya hwɔ si nɛ e buá pee kaa nɔ nɛ e be he wami. Matsɛ David ya slaa lɛ, nɛ Amnon de lɛ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o ngmɛ ye nyɛmiyo Tamar blɔ nɛ e ba hiɛ ɔ nɛ e ba si tatale enyɔ ko ha mi, konɛ e hɛɛ ngɛ e dɛ mi nɛ ma ye.”

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: David tsɔ ya de Tamar ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ mi ke, “Yaa o nyɛminyumu Amnon we ɔ mi, nɛ o ya pee niye ní ha lɛ.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Tamar ba Amnon we ɔ mi, nɛ e ba na lɛ nɛ e hwɔɔ si. Tamar pɔtɔ ma ngɛ Amnon hɛ mi nɛ e kɛ pee tatale nɛ e si.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e plɛ tatale ɔ ngɛ nisi kã a mi, nɛ e ngɔ kɛ ya ma Amnon hɛ mi; se e kua yemi. Amnon de ke, “Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ e je hiɛ ɔ!” Nɛ ni ɔmɛ tsuo je lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Amnon de Tamar ke, “Moo hɛɛ niye ní ɔ ngɛ o dɛ mi nɛ o kɛ ba ha mi ngɛ se tsu ɔ mi nɛ ma ye.” Tamar ngɔ tatale nɛ e si ɔ ya ha e nyɛminyumu Amnon ngɛ se tsu ɔ mi.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Benɛ e kɛ niye ní ɔ su Amnon ngɔ pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ Amnon nu lɛ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ye nyɛmiyo, ba nɛ o kɛ mi ba hwɔ!”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Se Tamar de lɛ ke, “Dɛbi, ye nyɛminyumu, ko pue ye hɛ mi si; ejakaa a pee we nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ngɛ Israel. Ko tsu zo ní kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Zo nɛ ɔ, jije ma kɛ gu? Se moo lɛɛ o maa pee kaa Israel yakayaka nimli ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ, yaa nɛ o ya na matsɛ ɔ; ejakaa i heɔ yeɔ kaa e maa kplɛɛ kaa e kɛ mi ma ha mo.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Se Amnon bui nɔ́ nɛ e nyɛmi ɔ ngɛ de ɔ tue; nɛ akɛnɛ e he wa pe lɛ he je ɔ, e nu lɛ pani nya, nɛ e kɛ lɛ hwɔ.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Tamar he tai bɔni Amnon peemi; nɛ ninyɛ nɛ Amnon na kɛ ha lɛ ɔ nya wa kulaa pe suɔmi nɛ e kɛ suɔ lɛ kekle ɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ Amnon de lɛ ke, “Tee si nɛ o ho!”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Se Tamar de lɛ ke, “Mo ko de mi ja! Fiemi nɛ o ngɛ mi fiee nɛ ɔ, e ji yayami nɛ kle pe kekle nɔ́ nɛ o pee mi ɔ po.” Se Amnon bui nɔ́ nɛ e ngɛ de ɔ tue.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: E tsɛ niheyo ɔ nɛ sɔmɔɔ lɛ ɔ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Je yo nɛ ɔ kpo; fie lɛ kɛ je hiɛ ɔ, nɛ o la sinya a se!”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Tsɔlɔ ɔ pee ja, nɛ e la sinya a se. Tamar wo tade klɔii saminyayoo; ejakaa blema a, ja ji bɔ nɛ matsɛmɛ a biyihi nɛ a gbɛ lolo ɔ dlaa a he.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Tamar muɔ la zu kɛ pue e yi mi, nɛ e hía tade klɔii saminyayoo ɔ nɛ e wo ɔ. E kɛ e nine kpla e yi, nɛ e ma blɔ; nɛ e ngɛ ya foe boboobo kɛ ho.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Benɛ e nyɛminyumu Absalom na lɛ ɔ, e bi lɛ ke, “Anɛ o nyɛminyumu Amnon ta o he lo? Ye nyɛmiyo, mo ma o nya kɛkɛ; mo ko ye o tsui, ejakaa o nyɛminyumu ji lɛ.” Tamar hi si mɔbɔmɔbɔ ngɛ e nyɛminyumu Absalom we ɔ mi.

english_verse: When David heard what had happened to Tamar, he was very angry. But Amnon was his oldest son and also his favorite, and David would not do anything to make Amnon unhappy.
translation_verse: Benɛ Matsɛ David nu sane nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo a he ɔ, e muklii mi fu wawɛɛ nitsɛ.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Absalom hu na ninyɛ agbo kɛ ha Amnon, nɛ e kɛ lɛ hiɔ nya kaa e nyɛ e nyɛmiyo Tamar nɔ pani nya, nɛ e kɛ lɛ hwɔ. Absalom lue yemi

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Jeha enyɔ se ɔ, e ba mi kaa a ya ngɛ Absalom tohi a he bwɔmi sãe ngɛ Baal Hazor, ngɛ Efraim kasa nya; nɛ Absalom fɔ matsɛbinyumu ɔmɛ tsuo nine.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Absalom ba matsɛ ɔ ngɔ nɛ e ba de lɛ ke, “A ma o tsɔlɔ ɔ to ɔmɛ a he bwɔmi sami. I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o kɛ o tsɔli ɔmɛ nɛ ba, nɛ nyɛ ba hyɛ ye kuɛ se mi.”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Se matsɛ ɔ de Absalom ke, “Dɛbi, ye bi, ke wɔ tsuo wa ba a, wa ma ba pee tlomi ngɛ o kuɛ nɔ.” Absalom nyɛ e nɔ hluu, se e kplɛɛ we; se kɛ̃, matsɛ ɔ gbaa lɛ.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Absalom de ke, “Ke o kplɛɛ we ɔ, lɛɛ i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o ha nɛ ye nyɛminyumu Amnon ba sɛ wɔ mɔ.” Matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he je o ngɛ Amnon hlae ɔ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Se Absalom nyɛ e nɔ hluu kɛ ya si e kplɛɛ kaa Amnon kɛ matsɛbinyumu ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ a ya. Absalom ngmɛ okplɔɔ gbidii kaa a ngmɛɛ okplɔɔ ha matsɛ.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Absalom fa e tsɔli ɔmɛ ke, “Ke Amnon nu wai nɛ e bua jɔ e he ɔ, nyɛɛ hi lɛ huɔe konɛ ke i de ke, ‘Nyɛɛ fia Amnon nɔ́,’ pɛ nɛ nyɛɛ gbe lɛ. Imi nɛ i fa nyɛ ɔ nɛ. Nyɛ ko ye gbeye! Nyɛɛ pee kã; nɛ nyɛ ha nɛ a na kaa nyumuhi ji nyɛ.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Absalom tsɔli ɔmɛ tsu Amnon he ní kaa bɔ nɛ Absalom fa mɛ ɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛbinyumu ɔmɛ tsuo te si, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ ya kuɔ e teji okpɔngɔ; nɛ a tu fo.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Benɛ a ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ yaa a, nɔ ko ya bɔ David amaniɛ ke, “Absalom gbe matsɛbinyumu ɔmɛ tsuo, nɛ a ti nɔ kake po píɛ.”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ te si nɛ e kɛ aywilɛho hía e tade ɔmɛ ngɛ e he, nɛ e hwɔ si ngɛ zugba; nɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ daa si ngɛ e kasa nya a hu hía a tade ɔmɛ ngɛ a he.

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, Absalom tu fo kɛ je momo. Kɛkɛ nɛ bulɔ ɔ na nimli babauu ngɛ Horonaim blɔ ɔ nɔ nɛ a ngɛ yo ɔ kplee kɛ ma.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Yonadab de matsɛ ɔ ke, “O nɛ, matsɛbinyumu ɔmɛ nɛ a ma a nɛ. Nɔ́ nɛ o tsɔlɔ de ɔ, lɔ ɔ nɛ e ba mi nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Benɛ e gbe e munyu ɔ nya pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛbinyumu ɔmɛ ba hia si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. A hɛ dɔ, nɛ a wo yana. Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo wo yana kɛ piɛ a he.

english_verse: David was sad for a long time because Amnon was dead. David Lets Absalom Come Home Absalom had run away to Geshur, where he stayed for three years with King Talmai the son of Ammihud.
translation_verse: Absalom tu fo kɛ ho Geshur matsɛ Talmai, nɛ ji Amihud binyumu ɔ ngɔ ya; nɛ e ya hi lejɛ ɔ jeha etɛ. David ye e binyumu Amnon he kɔmɔ be babauu.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Se benɛ kɔɔhiɔ fia Amnon gbenɔ ɔ mi bɔɔ ɔ, David hɛ ja ngɛ Absalom he; nɛ e ná nɛ e na lɛ ekohu.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Zeruya binyumu Yoab ba yɔse kaa Matsɛ David ngɛ e tsui yee ngɛ Absalom he,

english_verse: and he sent someone to bring in the wise woman who lived in Tekoa. Joab told her, “Put on funeral clothes and don't use any makeup. Go to the king and pretend you have spent a long time mourning the death of a loved one.” Then he told her what to say.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, yaa matsɛ ɔ ngɔ nɛ o ya de lɛ nɔ́ nɛ ma de mo nɛ ɔ.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Yoab de yo ɔ nɔ́ nɛ e ya de matsɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Benɛ Tekoa yo ɔ ba matsɛ ɔ ngɔ ɔ, e kpla si nɛ e kɛ e hɛ mi bu si, nɛ e de ke, “Nɛnɛ lee! Moo ye bua mi!”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni ji o sane ɔ?” Yo ɔ he nɔ ke, “Taflaatsɛ, yalɔyo ji mi; ye huno gbo.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: I kpa mo pɛɛ, i ngɛ binyumuwi enyɔ. Ligbi ko ɔ, pɛ ba sɛ a kpɛti ngɛ nga nɔ. Akɛnɛ nɔ ko be lejɛ ɔ nɛ ma kpata mɛ he je ɔ, nɔ kake fia e nyɛmi ɔ nɔ nɛ e gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, weku ɔ tsuo te si wo mi nɛ a ngɛ ye nɔ nyɛe ke ma ngɔ ye bi ɔ nɛ tane e nyɛmi ɔ yi ɔ ngɔ ha mɛ nɛ a gbe lɛ kɛ ye e nyɛmi ɔ nɛ e gbe ɔ he lue. Ke a pee ja kɛkɛ a kpata gbosi ní yelɔ ɔ hu hɛ mi; kɛkɛ pe a gbe ye la tso ku nɛ piɛ ngɛ la mi ɔ ji lɔ ɔ nɛ. Lɛɛ tse ye huno biɛ maa laa gbidigbidi; nɛ e nina ko hu be piɛe ngɛ zugba a nɔ.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ de yo ɔ ke, “Moo kpale kɛ ho we mi ya; ma ye o sane ɔ ha mo.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Tekoa yo ɔ de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Nɛnɛ, ke fɔ yemi ko ba a, e pee imi kɛ ye tsɛ we ɔ wa nɔ; nɛnɛ kɛ e sɛ ɔ lɛɛ e sɛ́ kaa nɔ ko nɔ ko piaa mɛ.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Ke nɔ ko wo o susuma he gbeye ɔ, ngɔɔ lɛ ba ha mi; nɛ e be o he tae hu gblegbleegble.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ yo ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ e ba moo o yi mi kaa o pee kikɛmɛ a yayami nɛ ɔ nɔuu kɛ si Mawu ma a? Si abɔ nɛ nɛnɛ nyɛ we nɛ e kpale lɛ nitsɛ e binyumu nɛ a je lɛ we ɔ kɛ ba nɛ ɔ, nɛnɛ kɛ nɔ́ nɛ e de nɛ ɔ bu lɛ nitsɛ e he fɔ.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Gbenɔ fɔɔ si kɛ ha wɔ tsuo; wa ngɛ kaa nyu nɛ a kpa pue si nɛ be hie muɔmi hu. Mawu lɛɛ e kpataa we susuma hɛ mi; se mohu e toɔ ga, konɛ nɔ ko nɛ a je lɛ we ɔ, e ko ba pee nɔmlɔ nɛ tlɔ nga pɛsɛpɛsɛ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɛnɛ, nɔ́ nɛ he je nɛ i ba nɛ i kɛ mo ba ngɛ munyu nɛ ɔ tue ɔ ji kaa ma a wo ye susuma he gbeye, nɛ i de ngɛ ye yi mi ke, ke i ba nɛ i ba bɔ nɛnɛ amaniɛ nɛ ɔ, alini nɛnɛ maa pee nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ hlae ɔ ha mi.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: I le sa kaa nɛnɛ maa bu nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ dee ɔ tue, nɛ nɔmlɔ nɛ ngɛ hlae kaa e kpata i kɛ ye bi tsuo wa hɛ mi, konɛ Mawu weto ní nɛ e laa wɔ ɔ, e ma kpɔ mi kɛ je e dɛ mi.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: I heɔ yeɔ kaa munyu nɛ nɛnɛ maa tu ɔ maa jɔɔ ye bua; ejakaa mo nɛnɛ ɔ, o ngɛ kaa Mawu bɔfo; o le slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ kpakpa kɛ yayami a kpɛti. Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ nɛ e gbaa mo.”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ de yo ɔ ke, “Nɔ́ nɛ ma bi mo nɛ ɔ, moo tu mi anɔkuale.” Yo ɔ de lɛ ke, “Nɛnɛ, mo de.”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Anɛ Yoab le ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo a he nɔ́ ko lo?” Yo ɔ he nɔ ke, “I na nɛnɛ, kaa nɔ ko nɔ ko be nyɛe maa je nɔ́ nɛ o de nɛ ɔ he nɔ́. O tsɔlɔ Yoab tutuutu ji nɔ nɛ tsɔ mi; nɛ lɛ nɔuu nɛ e tsɔɔ mi nɔ́ nɛ ma ba de mo ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: O tsɔlɔ Yoab to ga nɛ ɔ, nɛ́ e dla sane ɔ he. Se nɛnɛ lɛɛ e ngɛ kaa Mawu bɔfo; e le nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ngɛ je ɔ mi.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, matsɛ ɔ de Yoab ke, “Yoo, i kplɛɛ nɔ́ nɛ o bi ɔ nɔ. Jehanɛ, yaa nɛ o ya hla niheyo Absalom ɔ, nɛ o ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Yoab ba pue nɔ kɛ ho Geshur ya nɛ e ya ngɔ Absalom kɛ ba Yerusalem.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Se matsɛ ɔ de ke, “É ho nɛ e ya hi lɛ nitsɛ e we ɔ mi banee; i hla we nɛ ma na e hɛ mi.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Absalom ho ya hi lɛ nitsɛ e we ɔ mi; nɛ e yɛ matsɛ ɔ ngɔ. Absalom kɛ David tsa ekohu

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Absalom fɔ binyumuhi etɛ kɛ biyo kake. Yoyo ɔ biɛ ji Tamar, nɛ e he ngɛ fɛu saminya.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Absalom hi Yerusalem jeha enyɔ sɔuu nɛ e nɛ matsɛ ɔ hɛ mi.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Absalom tsɔ ke a tsɛ Yoab ha lɛ nɛ e tsɔ lɛ matsɛ ɔ ngɔ; se Yoab bɛ. E tsɔ si enyɔne; se Yoab bɛ.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yoab ba Absalom ngɔ ngɛ e we ɔ mi, nɛ e ba bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he nɛ o tsɔli ɔmɛ ya sã ye ngmɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Absalom he nɔ ke, “Ejakaa i tsɔ ba tsɛ mo, nɛ o bɛ. Jinɛ i ngɛ hlae nɛ ma tsɔ mo matsɛ ɔ ngɔ nɛ o ya bi lɛ ha mi ke, ‘Mɛni he je i je Geshur kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ? Kaa i ngɛ lejɛ ɔ mohu kɛ ba si piɔ jinɛ i ko suɔ.’ ” Absalom ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “I suɔ nɛ o ya sɛ mi matsɛ ɔ ngɔ; nɛ ke e ba mi kaa i ye fɔ ɔ, lɛɛ e gbe mi.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yoab ya matsɛ ɔ ngɔ nɛ e ya bɔ lɛ amaniɛ. Matsɛ ɔ tsɔ ya tsɛ Absalom; nɛ benɛ e ba a, e kpla si ngɛ matsɛ ɔ hɛ mi, nɛ e kɛ e hɛ mi bu si. Nɛ matsɛ ɔ fua lɛ atuu.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Absalom ba na lɛ nitsɛ e ta zugba lɛ kɛ e he okpɔngɔhi, kɛ nyumuhi nyingmi enuɔ nɛ maa hi fo tue ngɛ e hɛ mi.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Daa ligbi ɔ, Absalom maa te si mla, kɛkɛ e ho ya da si ngɛ blɔ ɔ mi ngɛ ma agbo ɔ nya. Ke nɔ ko hɛɛ munyu ko kɛ ma matsɛ ɔ ngɔ nɛ a ye ha lɛ ɔ, Absalom ma tsɛ nɔ ɔ nɛ e ma bi lɛ ke, “Jije ma mi o je?” Ke nɔ ɔ tsɔɔ lɛ Israel wɛtso nɔ́ nɛ mi nɛ e je ɔ,

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Absalom ma de lɛ ke, “Hyɛ, o sane ɔ da, se matsɛ ɔ nane mi dalɔ ko be hiɛ ɔ nɛ maa ye o sane ɔ ha mo.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Be tsuaa be nɛ nɔ ko ma ya su e kasa nya nɛ e ma kpla si ha lɛ ɔ, Absalom ma sɔle e nine nɛ e maa fua lɛ atuu.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Absalom peeɔ Israel no tsuaa Israel no nɛ kɛ munyu ko ba matsɛ ɔ ngɔ nɛ a ye ha lɛ ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Kɛ gu enɛ ɔ peemi mi ɔ, Absalom dɔ Israel ma a tsuo a tsui kɛ ba e he.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Jeha eywiɛ se ɔ, Absalom de matsɛ ɔ ke, “I kpa mo pɛɛ, ha nɛ ma ya Hebron konɛ si ko nɛ i wo Yawɛ ɔ, ma ya ye nɔ.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Benɛ i ngɛ Geshur ngɛ Siria a, i wo Yawɛ si kaa ke e maa kpale mi kɛ ba Yerusalem ekohu ɔ, lɛɛ ma ya ja lɛ ngɛ Hebron.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: David de e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ e kɛ mɛ ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ ke, “Nyɛɛ te si nɛ waa tu fo; ke pi ja lɛɛ Absalom nine maa su wa nɔ. Nyɛ ha nɛ waa ho esɔ nɛ e ko ba na wɔ tlukaa. Ke e ba mi ja lɛɛ sane yobu maa ye wɔ, nɛ e kɛ klaate ma kpata ma a hɛ mi.”

english_verse: David left behind ten of his wives to take care of the palace, but the rest of his family and his officials and soldiers went with him. They stopped at the last house at the edge of the city.
translation_verse: Benɛ matsɛ ɔ kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo ya su nyagbe we ɔ he ɔ, mɛ tsuo a da si.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: David bi Itai, Gat no ɔ ke, “Mɛni he je mo hu o kɛ wɔ yaa a? Moo kpale o se nɛ o kɛ matsɛ he ɔ nɛ e ya hi si. Nubwɔ ji mo; jehanɛ se hu, pe a fie mo kɛ je o ma mi.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Mo nɛ hiɛ pɛ o ba a, mɛni he je ma ngɔ mo kɛ ya wo lalaalo be mi nɛ imi nitsɛ i li he nɛ i yaa a? Moo kpale o se nɛ o kɛ o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ho. Yawɛ nɛ na mo mɔbɔ nɛ e kɛ mo nɛ hi si.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Se Itai he nɔ ke, “I na Yawɛ, nɛ i na nɛnɛ kaa he tsuaa he nɛ o yaa a, i kɛ mo maa ya, gbenɔ mi jio, wami mi jio.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: David de Itai ke, “Saminya, ba be kɛ ho!” Kɛkɛ nɛ Itai, Gat no ɔ, kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo, kɛ jokuɛwi tsɔwi ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ piɛ e he ɔ ba be.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Ma a tsuo wo yana benɛ David we bi ɔmɛ je kɛ yaa a. Matsɛ ɔ ya po Kidron pa a, nɛ e we bi ɔmɛ nyɛɛ e se; nɛ mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a pue nga a nɔ blɔ.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Abiatar, Zadok, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ ya ngɔ Mawu somi daka a kɛ ba ma si kɛ ya si nɔ tsuaa nɔ je ma a mi.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, matsɛ ɔ de Zadok ke, “Moo kpale Mawu somi daka a kɛ ho ma a mi ya. Ke Yawɛ suɔ ɔ, e maa kpale mi kɛ ba nɛ ma ba na daka a kɛ e hi he ɔ ekohu.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Se ke Yawɛ sume ɔ, lɛɛ imi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e suɔ ɔ, e pee mi.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ ya nɔ nɛ e de osɔfo Zadok ke, “Hyɛ, moo kpale o se kɛ ho ma a mi ya ngɛ he jɔmi mi; mo kɛ Abiatar, kɛ o binyumu Ahimaaz, kɛ Abiatar binyumu Yonatan.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Imi lɛɛ ma mlɛ ngɛ pa pomi he ɔ ngɛ nga a nɔ kɛ yaa si ma nu sɛ gbi ko kɛ je nyɛ ngɔ.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Zadok kɛ Abiatar kpale Mawu somi daka a kɛ ho Yerusalem ya; nɛ a ya hi lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: David ha e yi nɔ, nɛ e nyɛɛ nane gu kɛ ya kuɔ Oliv yo ɔ. Benɛ e yaa a tsuo e ngɛ ya foe. Nihi nɛ piɛ e he ɔ tsuo ha a yi nɔ; nɛ benɛ a ngɛ yo ɔ kuɔe ɔ, mɛ hu a wo yana.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Benɛ a ya bɔ David amaniɛ ke Ahitofel hu ya piɛ Absalom atuã tsɔli ɔmɛ a he ɔ, e sɔle ke, “Yawɛ lee, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o plɛ Ahitofel ga womi ɔ kɛ pee kuasiahi a sane.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Benɛ David ya su yo ɔ yi mi he nɛ a dla kɛ ha Mawu jami ɔ, Hushai, Arki no ɔ ba kpee lɛ kɛ e hiɔwe tade nɛ hía, kɛ e yi mi zu.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: David de lɛ ke, “Ke o nyɛɛ ye se ɔ, o maa pee tlomi ha mi.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Moo kpale kɛ ho ma a mi ya nɛ o ya de Absalom ke, ‘Matsɛ, ma sɔmɔ mo kaa bɔ nɛ i sɔmɔ o tsɛ be ko nɛ be ɔ.’ Enɛ ɔ peemi mohu nɛ o kɛ ma puɛ Ahitofel ga womi ɔ ha mi.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Osɔfo Zadok, kɛ osɔfo Abiatar ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o maa nu kɛ je matsɛ we ɔ mi ɔ, mo de mɛ.

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: David huɛ Hushai ba su Yerusalem be mi nɛ Absalom hu maa ho ma a mi sɛmi ya.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Benɛ David po mi ngɛ yo ɔ yi mi bɔɔ ɔ, Mefiboshet tsɔlɔ Ziba kɛ lɛ ba kpe. E hɛɛ teji enyɔ kɛ a se tlomi: abolo bɔbɔɛ lafa enyɔ, wai yiblii gbigbli sau lafa, tso yiblii lafa, kɛ wai lohwe he womi tɔ kake.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Jije o kɛ ní nɛ ɔmɛ yaa?” Ziba he nɔ ke, “I ngɔ teji ɔmɛ kɛ ba, konɛ o we bi ɔmɛ nɛ a hi a nɔ. I ngɔ abolo ɔ kɛ tso yiblii ɔmɛ kɛ ba konɛ nihewi ɔmɛ nɛ a ye. Jehanɛ, i kɛ wai hu ba, konɛ ke pɔ tɔ nihewi ɔmɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ nɛ a nu.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ke, “O nyɔmtsɛ ɔ bibi Mefiboshet ɔ, jije e ngɛ?” Ziba he nɔ ke, “E ngɛ Yerusalem, ejakaa e susu kaa be su nɛ Israel ma a maa kpale e nɛ̃ matsɛ yemi ɔ kɛ ha lɛ.”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ de Ziba ke, “O nɛ, Mefiboshet nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ba peeɔ o nɔ jehanɛ.” Ziba de lɛ ke, “Ye nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ, i kɛ he si bami ngɛ mo tsumi haae; moo pɛtɛ ye he daa.” David kɛ Shimei

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Benɛ David ba su Bahurim ɔ, Gara binyumu Shimei, Saul weku no ɔ kɛ lɛ ba kpe; benɛ e ma a tsuo, e ngɛ David gbiɛe.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e muɔ tɛ nɛ e kɛ fiaa Matsɛ David, kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ e we bi a tabo ɔ, kɛ ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ bɔle lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Benɛ Shimei ngɛ David gbiɛe ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ e ngɛ dee ji, “Jee hiɛ ɔ! Jee hiɛ ɔ! Mo muɔ si puelɔ, kɛ yakayaka nɔmlɔ!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: O kpɔ Saul matsɛ yemi ɔ, se piɔ lɛɛ Yawɛ ngɛ o tue gblae ngɛ Saul we mi bimɛ babauu a muɔ si nɛ o pue ɔ he. Yawɛ ngɔ matsɛ yemi ɔ ngɔ wo o binyumu Absalom dɛ. Hyɛ, o hɛ mi kpata pɛ, ejakaa muɔ si puelɔ ji mo.”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Abishai nɛ e nyɛ biɛ ji Zeruya a, bi matsɛ ɔ ke, “Ye nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ, mɛni he je nɛ o ngmɛ blɔ nɛ gbe gbogboe nɛ ɔ ngɛ mo gbiɛe kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Ha nɛ ma ya nɛ ma ya po e yi.”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Se matsɛ ɔ de Abishai, kɛ e nyɛminyumu Yoab ke, “Nyɛ Zeruya bimɛ, mɛni sane nɛ ɔ kɔɔ ngɛ nyɛ he? Ke Yawɛ nɛ de lɛ ke e gbiɛ mi, nɛ e ngɛ mi gbiɛe ɔ, mɛnɔ ngɛ he blɔ nɛ e biɔ ke mɛni he je e ngɛ ja pee lo?”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, David de Abishai, kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo ke, “Nyɛɛ hyɛ, ke imi nitsɛ ye bi fɔfɔɛ ngɛ ye wami se blɔ hlae ɔ, lɛɛ Benyamin no nɛ ɔ, mɛni tsiɔ lɛ blɔ? Nyɛɛ ngmɛɛ e he nɛ e gbiɛ mi faa, ejakaa Yawɛ nɛ de lɛ ke e pee ja a nɛ.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Eko ɔ, Yawɛ maa hyɛ ye nɔ́ nami ɔ, nɛ e kɛ kpakpa maa to ahlua nɛ a ngɛ mi bɔe mwɔnɛ ɔ nane mi ha mi.”

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Benɛ matsɛ ɔ kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ nyɛɛ e se ɔ su Yordan pa a he ɔ, pɔ tɔ mɛ nyanyaanya; nɛ a jɔɔ a he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Absalom ba su Yerusalem

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Absalom kɛ Israel ma a tsuo ba Yerusalem, nɛ Ahitofel hu piɛ a he.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Benɛ David huɛ Hushai, Arki no ɔ ba su Absalom ngɔ ɔ, e hwɔ lele, nɛ e de ke, “Manye oo, manye! Manye oo, manye!”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Absalom bi Hushai ke, “Bɔ nɛ o jeɔ o suɔmi kpo kɛ tsɔɔ o huɛ David ɔ ji nɛ ɔ lo? Mɛni he je o kɛ lɛ yɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Hushai he nɔ ke, “Dɛbi, imi lɛɛ nɔmlɔ nɛ Yawɛ kɛ ma nɛ ɔ, kɛ Israel tsuo hla lɛ ɔ, e nɔ ji mi; nɛ lɛ i kɛ maa hi si.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Jehanɛ se hu, ke i sɔmɔ we ye nyɔmtsɛ ɔ binyumu ɔ nɛɛ, mɛnɔ ma sɔmɔ mɔ?”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Absalom de Ahitofel ke, “Moo wo ga koo; kɛ wa maa pee kɛɛ?”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Ahitofel de Absalom ke, “Yaa nɛ o kɛ o tsɛ plã amɛ nɛ e si ke a hi we ɔ nɔ hyɛe ɔ ya hwɔ. Ke o pee ja a, Israel tsuo maa na kaa o kɛ o tsɛ ɔ, nyɛ plɛ he nyɛli. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ maa fɔ o se nyɛɛli ɔmɛ tsuo a kɔni nɔ kpa.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a pee bo tsu ha Absalom ngɛ tsu ɔ yi mi, nɛ Absalom ya tsɛ e tsɛ plã amɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ngɛ Israel ma a tsuo a hɛ mi.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Wa ma ya hla David ngɛ he tsuaa he nɛ e ngɛ ɔ, nɛ wa ma tua lɛ benɛ e li e he be kaa bɔ nɛ bɔ́ nɛɔ kɛ pueɔ zugba a. E kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo a ti nɔ kake ngmelu po be piɛe.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: Ma ya ná lɛ be mi nɛ pɔ tɔ lɛ, nɛ e nine mi je wu. Ma wo e he gbeye, kɛkɛ ma a tsuo nɛ piɛ e he ɔ maa tu fo. Ma gbe matsɛ ɔ pɛ,

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: nɛ ma kpaka e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ba ha mo kaa ayɛflo nɛ ma e huno we mi. Nɔmlɔ kake too pɛ wami se blɔ o ngɛ hlae; ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ, mɛɛ lɛɛ a maa ye a he.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Ga nɛ a wo nɛ ɔ sa Absalom, kɛ Israel nimeli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Absalom de ke, “Nyɛ ya tsɛ Hushai, Arki no ɔ hu kɛ ba nɛ waa bu tue nɔ́ nɛ lɛ hu e ma de.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Benɛ Hushai ba a, Absalom de lɛ ke, “Bɔ nɛ Ahitofel de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; waa ye e ga womi ɔ nɔ lo? Ke e hí ɔ, lɛɛ mo hu mo de wɔ nɔ́ ko.”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Hushai he nɔ ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ ga nɛ Ahitofel wo ɔ, ga a hí.”

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Hushai ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Mo nitsɛ o le kaa o tsɛ kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ɔ, katsɛmɛ ji mɛ, nɛ a hɛ mi pee klamaklama kaa osisiblisi nɛ nɔ ko ya muɔ e bimɛ ngɛ nga nɔ. Jehanɛ se hu, o tsɛ ɔ, ta bulɔ kpanaa ji lɛ; e hí e we bi a kpɛti nyɔ mi.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Hyɛ, nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ po, ke o li peemi, be nɛ ɔ mi e ya laa ngɛ tɛ puɔ ko mi, aloo ngɛ he kpa ko. Ke e ba mi kaa mɛɛ a tua wɔ kekle, nɛ wa we bi ɔmɛ ekomɛ nɔ ngɛ ta a mi, nɛ nihi nu he ɔ, a ma de ke, ‘A kpata Absalom we bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi.’

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Ke e ba mi ja a, nɔmlɔ nɛ lɛɛ e tsui wa kaa jata po sawale maa nu lɛ, ejakaa Israel tsuo le kaa o tsɛ ɔ, tatsɛ nguaa ji lɛ, nɛ e we bi ɔmɛ hu katsɛmɛ ji mɛ.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Imi lɛɛ, ga nɛ ma wo mo ji kaa o ha nɛ a bua Israel tsuo nya ha mo kɛ je Dan kɛ yaa si Beersheba. A he nɛ hiɛ babauu kaa wo nya zia, nɛ mo nitsɛ o nyɛɛ a hɛ mi kɛ ya ta a.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Ke e ba mi kaa e tu fo kɛ ho ma ko mi ya a, Israel tsuo maa ngɔ kpahi, nɛ wa maa gbla ma a kɛ ya wo kɔ̃ ɔ mi kɛ yaa si a be tɛ kake po nae ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Absalom kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ tsuo de ke, “Ga nɛ Hushai, Arki no ɔ wo ɔ hi pe Ahitofel nɔ́ ɔ.” Blɔɔ Yawɛ to momo kaa ga kpakpa a nɛ Ahitofel wo ɔ, a ko ye nɔ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ lɛ, Yawɛ ɔ e kɛ amanehlu nɛ ba Absalom nɔ. Nɔ ko ya naa David nane nɔ, nɛ e tu fo

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Ga nɛ Ahitofel wo Absalom kɛ Israel ma nimeli ɔmɛ ɔ, Hushai ho nɛ e ya bɔ osɔfo Zadok kɛ osɔfo Abiatar. E de mɛ lɛ nitsɛ hu e ga nɛ e wo ɔ.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Hushai ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Nyɛɛ tsɔ esɔ, nɛ a ya de David ke, nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, e ko hwɔ pa pomi he ɔmɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ; se mohu, bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, e po Yordan pa a nɔuu. Ke pi ja a, a ma kpata lɛ matsɛ ɔ nitsɛ, kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi.”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, Yonatan kɛ Ahimaaz ngɛ mlɛe ngɛ Enrogel pa a he ngɛ Yerusalem kasa nya. Nɛ́ nɔ ko kó na mɛ he je ɔ, a yɛ ma a mi. Ke pee ɔ, mawayo ko kɛ sɛ gbi ya haa mɛ, kɛkɛ mɛ hu a ya de David.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Se ligbi ko ɔ, niheyo ko na mɛ, nɛ e ya de Absalom. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mɛ ni enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo a je lejɛ ɔ mla kɛ ho nyumu ko we mi ya ngɛ Bahurim. Nyumu ɔ ngɛ vu ko ngɛ kpo ɔ nɔ, nɛ a ya sɛ mi.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ yo ɔ ngɔ nɔ́ kɛ ha vu ɔ nya, nɛ e fĩa ngma kɛ pue nɔ bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a ko le kaa ni komɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Benɛ Absalom tsɔli ɔmɛ ba su we ɔ mi ɔ, a bi yo ɔ ke, “Jije Ahimaaz kɛ Yonatan ngɛ?” Yo ɔ he nɔ ke, “A po pa a kɛ ho.” Ni ɔmɛ hla mɛ hluu, se a nɛ mɛ; kɛkɛ nɛ a kpale a se kɛ ho Yerusalem ya.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Benɛ a je ɔ, Ahimaaz kɛ Yonatan je kpo kɛ je vu ɔ mi, nɛ a ho nɛ a ya bɔ Matsɛ David amaniɛ. A de lɛ ke, “Tee si esɔ nɛ o po pa a.”

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ David kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo bɔni Yordan pa a pomi hluu kɛ ya si je nanɛɛ nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ po pa a ta.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Benɛ Ahitofel na kaa a yi ga nɛ e wo ɔ nɔ ɔ, e wo e teji nɔ ní, nɛ e je kɛ ho lɛ nitsɛ e ma mi ya. Benɛ e to e níhi a blɔ nya gbe nya a, e ho nɛ e ya wo e kuɛ kpa; nɛ a pu lɛ ngɛ e tsɛ yɔkɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Benɛ Absalom kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ tsuo ke a poɔ Yordan pa a, David su Mahanaim momo.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Absalom pee Amasa tatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma ngɛ Yoab nane mi. Amasa nɛ ɔ, Israel no ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Itra a bi ji lɛ. E nyɛ Abigail, nɛ ji Yoab nyɛ Zeruya nyɛmiyo ɔ, Nahash biyo ji lɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Absalom kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ ya pue si ngɛ Gilead zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Benɛ David ba su Mahanaim ɔ, Nahash binyumu Shobi nɛ je Amon bi a ma, Raba a, kɛ Amiel bi Makir nɛ je Lodebar a, kɛ Barzilai nɛ je Rogelim ngɛ Gilead ɔ kɛ lɛ ba kpe.

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: hwo, nyami, wagasi, kɛ jijɔhi. A de ke, “Be nɛ ɔ mi pɔ tɔ ni ɔmɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ; be nɛ ɔ mi hwɔ ngɛ mɛ yee, nɛ kuma hu ngɛ mɛ yee.”

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, David gba tabo ɔ tsuo mi etɛ, nɛ e ngɔ Yoab ngɔ to kekleekle nɔ́ nya. Yoab senɔ Abishai, Zeruya bi ɔ ji kuu enyɔne ɔ nyatsɛ; nɛ etɛne ɔ lɛɛ e kɛ wo Itai, Gat no ɔ dɛ mi. Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ de e we bi ɔmɛ ke, “Imi nitsɛ i kɛ nyɛ maa ya.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Nyumu ko ya na lɛ, nɛ e ba bɔ Yoab amaniɛ ke, “O nɛ, i ya na Absalom nɛ kplaa si ngɛ tso ngua a ko he.”

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Ta a gbɛ fĩa lejɛ ɔ zugba a nɔ tsuo, nɛ nimli babauu a hɛ mi kpata ngɛ hue ɔ mi jamɛ a ligbi ɔ pe ni nɛmɛ nɛ gbo ngɛ klaate nya po.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Absalom kɛ David tsɔli ɔmɛ ya kpe tlukaa. Absalom hi e teji okpɔngɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ ya gu tso ngua a ko sisi. E yi ya bɛ tso kɔni kusuu ɔmɛ, nɛ e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ kplaa si ngɛ kɔɔhiɔ mi be mi nɛ teji okpɔngɔ ɔ lɛɛ e je e sisi kɛ ho.

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Kaa i ya pee lɛ nɔ́ yayami ko, nɛ munyu nɛ ɔ ba su matsɛ ɔ, akɛnɛ matsɛ tue kle he je ɔ, mo nitsɛ po o ko fa we ye he.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Yoab de lɛ ke, “I pa be be ko puɛe ngɛ o he hu.” Kɛkɛ nɛ e ya ngɔ akplɔ etɛ, nɛ e fɔ kɛ gbɔ Absalom gugue mi, be mi nɛ e kplaa si ngɛ tso ɔ mi nɛ e gbo we lolo ɔ.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Yoab kpa titimati ɔ, nɛ e we bi ɔmɛ jɔɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ a se nyɛɛmi, nɛ a kpale kɛ ba.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: A je Absalom nɛ a sake lɛ ngɔ fɔ muɔ agbo ko mi ngɛ hue ɔ mi, nɛ a muɔ tɛ babauu ngɔ pue e nɔ. Israel bi ɔmɛ tsuo tu fo, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ pue lɛ nitsɛ e ma mi blɔ.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Benɛ Absalom ngɛ je mi ɔ, e ma kaimi titima ko kɛ ha e he ngɛ Matsɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi; ejakaa e de ke, “I be binyumu ko nɛ a kɛ ma kai ye biɛ.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e kɛ lɛ nitsɛ e biɛ wo titima a; nɛ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ɔ, a tsɛɛ lɛ Absalom kaimi nɔ́. A ya bɔ David Absalom gbenɔ ɔ

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Zadok bi Ahimaaz de Yoab ke, “Ha nɛ ma tu fo nɛ ma ya bɔ matsɛ ɔ amaniɛ kaa Yawɛ wo lɛ nguɔ, nɛ e je lɛ kɛ je e he nyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Se Yoab de lɛ ke, “Dɛbi! Ko ya bɔ lɛ amaniɛ mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ. Ligbi kpa konɛ o ya bɔ lɛ amaniɛ ɔ, se pi mwɔnɛ ɔ; ejakaa matsɛbi ɔ yi ta.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yoab de nyumu ko nɛ je Kush ɔ ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya bɔ matsɛ ɔ nɔ́ nɛ o na kɛ o hɛngmɛ.” Kush no ɔ kpla si ngɛ Yoab hɛ mi, kɛkɛ nɛ e sa fo kɛ je.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Ahimaaz, Zadok bi ɔ kpale de Yoab ke, “Nɔ́ nɛ maa ba nɛ e ba! Ha nɛ imi hu ma gbɔ fo kɛ nyɛɛ Kush no ɔ se.” Yoab de lɛ ke, “Ye bi, mɛni he je nɛ o ngɛ hlae doo kaa mo hu o maa ya a? O be hiɔwo ko nae ngɛ sɛ gbi nɛ ɔ nɛ o kɛ maa ya a he oo!”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Se Ahimaaz de ke, “Nɔ́ nɛ maa ba nɛ e ba! Ma gbɔ fo kɛ ya!” Yoab de lɛ ke, “Moo ya koo!” Kɛkɛ nɛ Ahimaaz wo fo kɛ gu nga a nɔ blɔ, nɛ e ya be Kush no ɔ nya.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, David hii si ngɛ he ko ngɛ ma agbo enyɔ ɔmɛ a kpɛti. Kɛkɛ nɛ bulɔ ɔ kuɔ gbogbo ɔ nɛ e ya da si ngɛ agbo ɔ yi mi. Benɛ e maa hyɛ ɔ, nyumu ko ji nɛ ɔ nɛ lɛ nɔ kake too e ngɛ fo tue kɛ ma.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Bulɔ ɔ kpa ngmlaa nɛ e kɛ de matsɛ ɔ. Matsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Ke nɔ kake ɔ, lɛɛ e hɛɛ amaniɛ kɛ ma.” Benɛ tsɔlɔ ɔ su a ngɔ ta a,

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Bulɔ ɔ de ke, “E peeɔ mi kaa nɔ nɛ ngɛ hɛ mi ɔ ngɛ fo tue kaa Zadok bi Ahimaaz.” Matsɛ ɔ de ke, “Nɔmlɔ kpakpa ji lɛ, nɛ e hɛɛ manye munyu kɛ ma.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ahimaaz kpa ngmlaa nɛ e de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Manye oo, manye!” Kɛkɛ nɛ e ba kpla si ngɛ matsɛ ɔ hɛ mi nɛ e kɛ e hɛ mi bu si, nɛ e de ke, “Nɛnɛ! A je Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ yi. Nihi nɛ te si ngɔ wo mo ɔ, Yawɛ ha o ye a nɔ.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Niheyo Absalom ɔ ngɛ saminya lo?” Ahimaaz he nɔ ke, “Benɛ o tsɔlɔ Yoab tsɔ mi ɔ, i na kaa lejɛ ɔ pee gidigidi wawɛɛ nitsɛ; se i li nɔ́ nɛ ba.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Ba be nɛ o ya da si ngɛ hiɛ ɔ!” Nɛ e ho ya da si dii.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: E kɛ we nɛ Kush no ɔ hu ba nɛ e ba de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Nɛnɛ, mo he manye! Mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, Yawɛ je mo kɛ je nihi tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ nɛ te si ngɔ wo mo ɔ a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ bi Kush no ɔ ke, “Niheyo Absalom ɔ ngɛ saminya lo?” Kush no ɔ he nɔ ke, “Nɛnɛ, i ná nɛ a pee o he nyɛli ɔmɛ, kɛ ni nɛmɛ tsuo nɛ te si ngɔ wo mo, ye nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ a pee jamɛ a niheyo ɔ pɛ.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ hɛ dɔ, nɛ e kuɔ kɛ ho e se tsu ɔ mi ya ngɛ agbo ɔ yi mi nɛ e ya fo ya. Benɛ e yaa a, e ngɛ ya foe nɛ e ngɛ dee ke, “Ao, ye bi ɔ! Ye bi Absalom! Ye bi Absalom! I na nɛ imi mohu i gbo ngɛ o nane mi. Absalom, ye bi, ye bi!”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: A ya bɔ Yoab amaniɛ ke matsɛ ɔ ngɛ ya foe, nɛ e ngɛ kɔmɔ yee ha Absalom.

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, jamɛ a ligbi ɔ manye yemi ɔ plɛ pee kɔmɔ yemi kɛ ha ma a tsuo; ejakaa ma a nu jamɛ a ligbi ɔ kaa matsɛ ɔ ngɛ kɔmɔ yee ha e bi ɔ.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Tabo ɔmɛ nyɛɛ blɛuu blɛuu kɛ ba sɛ ma a mi kaa nihi nɛ tu fo ngɛ ta nya, nɛ́ zo ngɛ mɛ pee.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ kɛ nɔ́ ha e hɛ mi, nɛ e fo ya boboobo, nɛ e de ke, “Ao ye bi ɔ! Ye bi Absalom! Ye bi Absalom!”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yoab ya matsɛ ɔ ngɔ ngɛ e we ɔ mi, nɛ e ya de lɛ ke, “Mwɔnɛ ɔ, o tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ he mo, kɛ o binyumu ɔmɛ, o biyi ɔmɛ, o yi ɔmɛ, kɛ o plã amɛ a yi wami ɔ, o pue mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a hɛ mi si,
