english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: ejakaa o suɔ nihi nɛ nyɛɛ mo, nɛ o nyɛɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ suɔ mo mohu. O tsɔɔ paa mwɔnɛ ɔ kaa o tatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ o tabo ɔmɛ ɔ, a pi ni komɛ kulaa ha mo; ejakaa i kpa si mwɔnɛ ɔ kaa e ji Absalom yi na wami, nɛ wɔ tsuo wa gbo jinɛ e ko ngɔ o nya.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, tee si esɔ, nɛ o ya nɛ o ya jɔɔ o tsɔli ɔmɛ a bua. I na Yawɛ kaa ke o yɛ ɔ, nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi ke e piɛ nyumu kake ngmelu ngɛ o he fii! Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ma ba pee haomi agbo kɛ ha mo pe haomi ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ ba o nɔ kɛ je o nihe mi kɛ ba si amlɔ nɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ te si nɛ e ho ya hi si ngɛ ma agbo ɔ nya. Nɛ benɛ e we bi ɔmɛ tsuo nu kaa matsɛ ɔ hii si ngɛ ma agbo ɔ nya a, mɛ tsuo a ya na lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. David kpale e se kɛ yaa Yerusalem Jamɛ a be ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ tu fo kɛ ho lɛ nitsɛ e ma mi ya.

english_verse: everyone in Israel started arguing. They were saying to each other, “King David rescued us from the Philistines and from our other enemies. But then we chose Absalom to be our new leader, and David had to leave the country to get away. Absalom died in battle, so why hasn't something been done to bring David back?”
translation_verse: Absalom ɔ nɛ wa pɔ lɛ nu nɛ wa wo lɛ matsɛ ɔ, lɛ hu e gbo ngɛ ta mi. Mɛni he je nɔ ko yɛ nɛ e ya ngɔ Matsɛ David ɔ kɛ ba mɔ?”

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Benɛ Matsɛ David nu nɔ́ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɛ dee ɔ, e tsɔ osɔfo Zadok kɛ osɔfo Abiatar ke a ya nɛ a ya bi Yuda ma nimeli ɔmɛ ke, “Mɛni he je nyɛ mohu nyɛ de we kekle ke nyɛ yaa ngɔ matsɛ ɔ kɛ ba we ɔ?

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Ye nyɛmimɛ nitsɛnitsɛmɛ ji nyɛ; mɛni he je nyɛ mohu nyɛ de we kekle ke nyɛ ma ba ngɔ mi kɛ ba we ɔ?”

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: David sɛ mɛ ke a ya de Amasa hu ke, “Ye nyɛmi tutuutu ji mo. Kɛ je mwɔnɛ ɔ kɛ yaa a, i pee mo ye tabo ɔ nyatsɛ ngɛ Yoab nane mi. Mawu nɛ fia mi nɔ nɛ e gbe ke i pee we nɔ́ nɛ ɔ!”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Sɛ nɛ David kɛ mane Yuda bi ɔmɛ ɔ ha a yi mi plɛ, nɛ a pee kake. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a tsɔ kɛ ba de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Moo kpale o se kɛ ba kɛ o tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo.”

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ nɔuu ɔ, Benyamin no ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Shimei, nɛ ji Gera nɛ je Bahurim binyumu ɔ he sɔ nɛ e kɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ ho, nɛ lɛ hu e ya kpee Matsɛ David.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: I le kaa i pee yayami; nɛ enɛ ɔ he je nɛ imi ji kekleekle nɔ nɛ je omleyi je wɛtso ɔmɛ nɛ ji Yosef we ɔ mi kɛ ma mo nɛnɛ kpeemi mwɔnɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: A ngɔ matsɛ ɔ we mi bi ɔmɛ kɛ po pa a; nɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ matsɛ ɔ ngɛ hlae ɔ, a pee ha lɛ. David na Shimei mɔbɔ Benɛ matsɛ ɔ maa ho pa a pomi ya a, Gera binyumu Shimei ya kpla si ngɛ e hɛ mi nɛ e nu matsɛ ɔ nane,

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Nɛnɛ, yayami nɛ i pee mo ligbi ɔ nɛ o je Yerusalem ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o kɛ pa mi. Mo ko ngɔ kɛ to ha mi, nɛ mo ko kai hu gblegbleegble.

english_verse: But Abishai shouted, “You should be killed for cursing the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Zeruya bi Abishai de ke, “E sa kaa a gbe Shimei, ejakaa e gbiɛ nɔmlɔ nɛ Mawu pɔ lɛ nu ɔ.”

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Se David de ke, “Nyɛ Zeruya bimɛ, mɛni sane nɛ ɔ kɔɔ ngɛ nyɛ he, loko nyɛ ngɛ hlae nɛ nyɛɛ doo ye nya mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ? Anɛ e sa kaa a gbe nɔ ko ngɛ Israel mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ lo? Anɛ i li kaa mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, imi ji matsɛ ngɛ Israel lo?”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ de Shimei ke, “I ngɛ mo kita kae kaa a be mo gbee!” David na Mefiboshet mɔbɔ

english_verse: Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
translation_verse: Benɛ e je Yerusalem kɛ ba nɛ e kɛ matsɛ ɔ ba kpe ɔ, matsɛ ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Mefiboshet, mɛni he je nɛ o kɛ mi yɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: E he nɔ ke, “Ye nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ, kaa bɔ nɛ o le ɔ, akpaketsɛ ji mi. I fa ye tsɔlɔ ɔ ke e wo ye teji ɔ nɔ ní ha mi nɛ ma hi nɔ nɛ i kɛ mo nɛ ya. Se ye tsɔlɔ ɔ sisi mi,

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: nɛ e ba po ye nya ha mo. Mo nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ ɔ, moo lɛɛ o ngɛ kaa Mawu bɔfo, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ da ha mo ɔ, moo pee.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Jinɛ tsaatsɛ we ɔ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ sa gbenɔ; se kɛ̃ o ngɔ o tsɔlɔ ɔ ngɔ piɛ nihi nɛ yeɔ ní ngɛ o we okplɔɔ ɔ he ɔ a he. Lɛɛ mɛni he blɔ i ngɛ kaa ma bi nɛnɛ ekohu ke e na mi mɔbɔ?”

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “E hia we kaa o pa deɔ nɔ́ ko hu. I to ye yi mi kaa o kɛ Ziba maa dla Saul zugba a fiee.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Se Mefiboshet de ke, “Oo, ha nɛ e ngɔ lɛ tsuo kɛkɛ; nɛ́ ye nyɔmtsɛ matsɛ ná ba su we fiafiaafia nɛ ɔ kɛkɛ e hiɛ ha mi.” David na Barzilai mɔbɔ

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Barzilai, Gilead no ɔ hu je Rogelim kɛ ba Yordan pa a nya, konɛ lɛ hu e ba po David pa.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ de Barzilai ke, “Ha nɛ waa ho Yerusalem ya nɛ ma ya hyɛ o nɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Se Barzilai de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Dɛbi, be bɔɔ pɛ nɛ piɛ ha mi nɛ ma hi je mi; mɛni he je i kɛ mo maa ya Yerusalem mɔ?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Mɛni he je matsɛ maa pee nɔ́ kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ kɛ to nɔ́ ko bɔbɔyoo nɛ i pee ha lɛ ɔ nane mi? Oo, ma je mo blɔ kɛ po Yordan pa a kɛkɛ.

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ he nɔ ke, “Yoo, i kɛ Kimham maa ya, nɛ ma pee ha lɛ kaa bɔ nɛ o ngɛ hlae ɔ. Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o ma bi mi ɔ, ma ha mo.”

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Benɛ matsɛ ɔ po pa a ta a, Yuda bi ɔmɛ tsuo kulaa, kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ fa ngɔ lɛ kɛ ho Gilgal ya. Kimham hu piɛ a he.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ tsuo ba matsɛ ɔ ngɔ nɛ a ba bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni he je wa nyɛmimɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ ya ju mo, nɛ a ngɔ mo, kɛ o we ɔ ltsuo, kɛ o we bi ɔmɛ kɛ po Yordan pa a?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ de Israel bi ɔmɛ ke, “Matsɛ ɔ, wa weku no tutuutu ji lɛ. Mɛni he je nɔ́ nɛ ɔ dɔɔ nyɛ? Anɛ matsɛ ɔ jé lɛ nitsɛ e sika ko kɛ pee niye ní ha wɔ nɛ wa ye lo? Anɛ e ha wɔ nike ní ko lo?”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ he nɔ ke, “Wɛtso nyɔngma lɛ ngɛ Israel; nɛ matsɛ blɔ fa mi hu wa blɔ nya hiɛ pe nyɛ. Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ nyɛ nyɛɛ wɔ? Anɛ pi wɔ nɛ wa sɛ hlami kɛ de ke a ya ngɔ matsɛ ɔ kɛ ba lo?” A hɛɛ sane nɛ ɔ mi kɛ ya kɛ ba; se Yuda bi ɔmɛ a nya wa pe Israel bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: E ba mi kaa yakayaka nɔmlɔ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Sheba ba je Gilgal. Benyamin no, Bikri bi ji lɛ. Sheba kpa titimati nɛ e de ke, “Wa be blɔ nya ko ngɛ David ngɔ; Ishai binyumu ɔ, pi e ní yeli ji wɔ. Israel bi, nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ho lɛ nitsɛ e we mi ya!”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha Israel bi ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ gbla a he si kɛ je David he nɛ a ya nyɛɛ Bikri bi Sheba se; se Yuda bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ a mɛtɛ a matsɛ ɔ he kpɛii, nɛ a nyɛɛ e se kɛ je Yordan ɔ he kɛ ho Yerusalem ya.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Benɛ Matsɛ David ba su e we ɔ mi ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ, e kɛ yihi nyɔngma amɛ, nɛ ji e plahi nɛ e si nɛ a hi we ɔ nɔ hyɛe ngɛ e se ɔ ya wo tsu mi. E hyɛɛ a nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, se e kɛ mɛ na we nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi. A tsi a nya nɛ a hi si kaa yalɔyihi kɛ ya si a gbenɔ ligbi.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ de Amasa ke, “Yaa nɛ o ya bua Yuda bi ɔmɛ tsuo a nya, nɛ hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ ligbi etɛ ɔ, o kɛ mɛ nɛ ba hiɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Amasa ho, konɛ e ya kpee Yuda bi ɔmɛ kɛ ba; se e se ya fia si bɔɔ, nɛ e bɛ be nɛ a to lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ de Abishai ke, “Sheba ma ba hao wɔ kulaa pe Absalom tete. Ngɔɔ ye tsɔli ɔmɛ, nɛ́ nyɛɛ nyɛɛ e se; ke pi ja a, e ma ya sɛ mahi nɛ a fia gbogbo ngɔ wo a he ɔ ekomɛ a mi, nɛ e maa hao wɔ.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Abishai kɛ Yoab we bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Keret bi ɔmɛ kɛ Pelet bi ɔmɛ, kɛ ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo hia kɛ je Yerusalem kɛ nyɛɛ Sheba se.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Benɛ a su Gibeon tɛ agbo ɔ he ɔ, a kɛ Amasa ya bua. Jamɛ a be ɔ, Yoab lɛɛ e wo ta hwumi tade kɛ mlɛ mi fimi nɔ́ nɛ a fi e klaate nɛ ngɛ kpo mi ɔ kɛ wo he. Benɛ e yaa a, klaate ɔ pɛne nɔ si.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Yoab de Amasa ke, “Ye nyɛmi, kɛ o ngɛ kɛɛ?” Yoab kɛ e hiɔ nine nu Amasa kpɛni, konɛ e fiɔ e nya he.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Nɛ pee ja a, Amasa nɛ́ klaate ɔ nɛ Yoab hɛɛ ngɛ e muɔ nine mi ɔ; kɛkɛ nɛ Yoab kɛ klaate ɔ gbɔ e muklii mi, nɛ e pã e mi ní kɛ pue zugba. E gbo amlɔ nɔuu nɛ e he hia we kaa Yoab nɛ fia lɛ nɔ́ si enyɔne hu. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Yoab kɛ e nyɛmi Abishai pue nɔ kɛ nyɛɛ Bikri bi Sheba a se.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Yoab we bi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake ho ya da si ngɛ Amasa he, nɛ e de ke, “Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ngɛ Yoab, kɛ David blɔ fa mi ɔ, e ba nɛ e ba nyɛɛ Yoab se.”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Amasa hwɔɔ si ngɛ muɔ ɔ mi ngɛ gbɛjegbɛ ɔ kpɛti tutuutu; nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ma ba be nɛ na lɛ ɔ, kɛkɛ e da si. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, benɛ niheyo ɔ na kaa ni ɔmɛ tsuo ba ngɛ si dae ɔ, e gbla Amasa kɛ je gbɛjegbɛ ɔ nɔ kɛ sɛ nga a mi, nɛ e ngɔ bo ngɔ ha e nɔ.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Benɛ e je lɛ kɛ je gbɛjegbɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ, ni ɔmɛ tsuo ya piɛ Yoab he nɛ a kɛ nyɛɛ Sheba se.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Sheba ya kpa Israel wɛtso ɔmɛ tsuo a nɔ kɛ ya si Abel ngɛ Bet Maaka, nɛ Bikri bi ɔmɛ tsuo bua a he nya nɛ a nyɛɛ e se kɛ ho ma a mi ya.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Benɛ Yoab we bi ɔmɛ nu kaa Sheba ngɛ Abel ngɛ Bet Maaka a, a ya sa ma a yi. A kɛ zu fia kpoku wo ma a he kɛ ya su gbogbo nɛ bɔle ma a yi mi tɔɔ, nɛ a bɔni gbogbo ɔ nɔ́ fiami, konɛ a hule lɛ.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ yo ní lelɔ ko kpa bubuubui kɛ je ma a mi, nɛ e de ke, “Nyɛɛ bu tue! Nyɛɛ bu tue! Nyɛ ya de Yoab ke e ba hiɛ ɔ nɛ i kɛ lɛ waa tu munyu.”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Yoab ba a, yo ɔ bi lɛ ke, “Mo ji Yoab ɔ lo?” E he nɔ ke, “Ee, imi.” Kɛkɛ nɛ yo ɔ de lɛ ke, “Moo bu imi, o mawayo ɔ munyu ɔmɛ tue.” Nɛ lɛ hu e he nɔ ke, “I ngɛ mo tue bue.”

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Yo ɔ ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “A pɔɔ demi blema be ɔ mi ke, ‘Ha nɛ a ya Abel nɛ a ya bi ga womi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ’; ke a pee ja kɛkɛ sane ɔ he jɔ.

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Wa ma nɛ ɔ, ma nguaa ji lɛ; tue mi jɔmi ngɛ mi, nɛ e ji mahi nɛ yeɔ Israel anɔkuale ɔ a kpɛti kake. Nɛ moo o ngɛ hlae nɛ o kpata ma a hɛ mi! Mɛni he je o ngɛ hlae nɛ o puɛ Yawɛ nitsɛ blɔ fa mi nɔ́ ɔ?”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Yoab he nɔ ke, “Kpaoo! Kpaoo! I bɛ nyɛ ma a puɛmi, aloo e hɛ mi kpatami.

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Tsa pi ja ji sane ɔ. Nyumu ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ ke Sheba, nɛ ji Bikri binyumu ɔ nɛ je Efraim yo ɔ nɔ ɔ, lɛ nɛ e te si ngɔ wo Matsɛ David. Nyɛ je nyumu nɛ ɔ pɛ ngɔ wo ye dɛ mi, kɛkɛ ma kpale ye se!” Yo ɔ de Yoab ke, “Hyɛ, wa maa fɔ e yi kɛ gu gbogbo ɔ nɔ kɛ mane mo.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ yo ɔ ho nɛ e ya wo ma mi bi ɔmɛ ga; nɛ a po Sheba yi nɛ a fɔ ngɔ mane Yoab. Yoab kpa titimati, nɛ e we bi ɔmɛ gbɛ kɛ je ma a he; nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ ho e ma mi ya. Yoab kpale kɛ ba matsɛ ɔ ngɔ ngɛ Yerusalem. David ma ní tsuli

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Yoab ji Israel tatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma; Yehoyada bi Benaya ji Keret bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Pelet bi ɔmɛ a nyatsɛ.

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Ni nɛmɛ nɛ a nyɛɔ a nɔ nɛ a tsuɔ ní kɛ haa ma nɛ a wui mɛ hiɔ ɔ, mɛɛ a nyatsɛ ji Adoniram.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Ahilud bi Yehoshafat ji sanehi ngmalɔ; Sheva ji pɛdiyo; Zadok kɛ Abiatar ji osɔfohi,

english_verse: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_verse: nɛ Ira, Yair no ɔ, lɛ hu David osɔfo ji lɛ.

english_verse: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, matsɛ ɔ tsɛ Gibeon bi ɔmɛ nɛ e kɛ mɛ tu munyu. Gibeon bi nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, pi Israel bi ji mɛ; Amor bi nɛ piɛ ɔ ekomɛ ji mɛ. Jinɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ka Gibeon bi kita kaa a maa baa a yi; se be mi nɛ Saul hɛ dɔ ngɛ Israel kɛ Yuda he ɔ, e hla kaa e ma kpata a hɛ mi.

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: David bi Gibeon bi ɔmɛ ke, “Mɛni ma pee ha nyɛ? Mɛni ma ngɔ kɛ kpata nyɛ konɛ nyɛɛ gbaa Yawɛ ma a?”

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: A he nɔ ke, “Saul to kaa e ma kpata wa hɛ mi, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a ko nu wa he ngɛ Israel zugba amɛ ekoeko nɔ hu.

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, á ngɔ nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ binyumuhi kpaago ba ha wɔ nɛ waa sɛu mɛ ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi ngɛ Gibeon, ngɛ Yawɛ yo ɔ nɔ.” Matsɛ ɔ he nɔ ke, “Yoo, ma ngɔ mɛ ba ha nyɛ.”

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Ngɛ kita nɛ David kɛ Saul bi Yonatan ka a he he je ɔ, matsɛ ɔ tɛ Yonatan bi Mefiboshet nɛ ji Saul bibi ɔ he.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: David ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo Gibeon bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi, nɛ a ya sɛu mɛ ngɛ yo ɔ nɔ, ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. Mɛ ni kpaago ɔmɛ tsuo a gbo si kake too. Benɛ ní kpami be su, nɛ́ a bɔni ngma poomi ɔ, jamɛ a be ɔ nɛ a gbe ni ɔmɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Rizpa, Aya biyo ɔ ngɔ kpekpe kɛ pee bo tsu ngɛ tɛ sa a nɔ. Nɛ kɛ je be mi nɛ a bɔni ní kpami kɛ ya si hiɔmi bɔni nɛmi ɔ, e huɔ gbogboe ɔmɛ nyɔ kɛ pia; e ngmɛ́ blɔ nɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ ba maa a nɔ piani; nɛ nyɔ mi ɔ, e fieɔ lohwe awi yeli kɛ jeɔ a he.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: e ho nɛ e ya ngɔ Saul kɛ e bi Yonatan a wuhi ngɛ Yabesh Gilead bi ɔmɛ a dɛ. Ligbi ɔ nɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ gbe Saul ngɛ Gilboa, nɛ a ngɔ e kɛ Yonatan kpla si ngɛ a kpe he ɔ ngɛ Bet Shan ɔ, Yabesh Gilead bi ɔmɛ ya ju mɛ.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: A ya pu Saul kɛ e bi Yonatan a wu ɔmɛ ngɛ Benyamin zugba a nɔ ngɛ Zela, ngɛ e tsɛ Kish yɔkɔ ɔ mi; nɛ a pee nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ kaa bɔ nɛ matsɛ ɔ fa mɛ ɔ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Mawu bu a kue nɛ a fa kɛ ha ma a tue. Tahi nɛ a kɛ Filisti oblai komɛ hwu (Kronika I,

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, a hwu ta ekohu ngɛ Gat, he nɛ nyumu oblai kpanaa ko ngɛ ɔ. E ngɛ nine nguɛ ekpa kɛ nane nguɛ ekpa; nɛ lɛ tsuo peeɔ nyingmi enyɔ kɛ eywiɛ.

english_verse: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
translation_verse: Filisti bi ɔmɛ gba ta kɛ wo Israel bi ɔmɛ ekohu; nɛ David kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ ho nɛ a kɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ ya hwu; se pɔ tɔ David.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ oblai ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Ishbibenob ɔ susu kaa e nine gbe David ta. Ishbibenob hɛɛ akɔblee akplɔ ko nɛ e jiimi maa pee kilo etɛ kɛ fa, nɛ e fi klaate ehe hu ngɛ e mlɛ mi.

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Se Zeruya bi Abishai ba piɛ David he; e tua Filisti no ɔ, nɛ e gbe lɛ. Kɛkɛ nɛ David we bi ɔmɛ ka David kita ke, “O kɛ wɔ be ta yae hu gblegbleegble. Israel hɛngmɛ ji mo; koo pee nɛ wa hɛngmɛ ɔ ba pɛ.”

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, a kɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ hwu ta ekohu ngɛ Gob, nɛ Sibekai nɛ je Husha a gbe oblai ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Saf.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ pa hwu ta ekohu ngɛ Gob; nɛ Yair binyumu Elhanan nɛ je Betlehem ɔ gbe Goliat, Gat no ɔ nɛ e akplɔ nya tso ngɛ kaa bo lolɔ gba tso ɔ.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: Nyumu nɛ ɔ bɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ ahlua, nɛ Yonatan nɛ ji David nyɛminyumu Shama binyumu ɔ gbe lɛ.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Ni eywiɛ nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, Gat oblaihi a nina ji mɛ; nɛ mɛ tsuo a nɔ ngɛ David kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ a klaate nya.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: E je mi kɛ je ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ nyɛɔ mi ɔ a dɛ mi; ejakaa a he wa tsɔ pe mi.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Benɛ Yawɛ je David kɛ je Saul kɛ e he nyɛli ɔmɛ tsuo a dɛ mi ɔ, David la la nɛ ɔ kɛ ha Yawɛ:

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: Yawɛ, enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, ma je o yi ngɛ je ma amɛ a kpɛti; ma la kɛ je o biɛ ɔ yi.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ji ye tɛ sa nɛ baa ye yi.

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: Ye Mawu ɔ ji nɔ nɛ baa ye yi; e ngɔ nɛ i saa we ngɛ. Ye Mawu ɔ ji ye tsɛ̃i, ye wesa he, kɛ ye mɔ; lɛ nɛ e heɔ ye yi wami.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: Ma fa kue ha Yawɛ; e ma kpɔ mi ngɛ ye he nyɛli a dɛ mi. A je Yawɛ yi.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Gbenɔ oslɔke ɔmɛ bɔle mi kɛ kpe; pa yayamihi hia kɛ wo mi.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: Gbenɔ oslaa amɛ bɔle mi kɛ kpe, nɛ yɔkɔ hu tsɔ̃ mi klama.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: Benɛ e fi mi ɔ, i fa kue ha Yawɛ; ee, i tsɛ ye Mawu ɔ. E nu ye gbi kɛ je e sɔlemi we ɔ; nɛ e bu ye kue fami ɔ tue.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ zugba a mimiɛ nɛ e hoso; hiɔwe sisi tomi ɔmɛ hɛ a he, nɛ a mimiɛ; ejakaa Mawu mi mi fu!

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: La su ku je kpo kɛ je e gugwɔ mi; la nɛ ngɛ tsoe je e nya mi, nɛ e sã níhi.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: E gba hiɔwe mi enyɔ; nɛ e nyɛɛ bɔku kpii ko nɔ kɛ ba zugba.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: E hi kerub nɔ kɛ fli kɛ je; e hi kɔɔhiɔ pɛlihi a nɔ kɛ te.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: E ngɔ diblii ngɔ ha e he; bɔku nɛ nyu hyi lɛ tɔ bɔle lɛ.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: La nɛ pã kɛ bɔle lɛ ɔ ha je ɔ mi tsɔ heii.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ si si ngɛ hiɔwe nɛ Hiɔwe No ɔ wo gbi.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yawɛ mi mi fu nɛ e kuɛ wo e he nyɛli ɔmɛ ɔ, wo nyu dɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ je ɔ sisi tomi ɔmɛ je kpo.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: Yawɛ juale e nine kɛ je hiɔwe, nɛ e pɛtɛ ye he; e gbla mi kɛ je pa nɛ mi kuɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: Benɛ i ngɛ amanehlu mi ɔ, a tua mi; se Yawɛ he ye yi wami.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: E je mi kɛ je amanehlu mi. E he ye yi wami, ejakaa e suɔ mi.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: Ní kpakpahi nɛ i peeɔ ɔ, Yawɛ woɔ mi a he hiɔ; e gbaa mi, ejakaa i pee we nɔ ko yayami.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: I ye Yawɛ mlaa amɛ a nɔ; i ji ye Mawu ɔ se.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: I le e mlaa amɛ tsuo kulaa; i ye mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: E le kaa i da kɛ pi si; e le kaa i pee we yayami ko.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: Yawɛ gbaa mi; ejakaa e le kaa i peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da; ejakaa e le kaa yayami ko be ye he.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ yeɔ mo anɔkuale ɔ, mo hu o yeɔ mɛ anɔkuale; ni nɛmɛ nɛ da a, o naa mɛ mɔbɔ.

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ a he tsɔ ɔ, o tsɔɔ mɛ kaa o he tsɔ; se ni nɛmɛ nɛ a yi mi wa lɛɛ o kɛ mɛ toɔ ní.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ baa a he si ɔ, o heɔ a yi wami. Ni nɛmɛ nɛ woɔ a he nɔ ɔ, o baa mɛ si.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: Yawɛ, mo ji ye kane. Ye Mawu, mo nɛ o fieɔ diblii ngɛ ye blɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: Mawu nɛ ɔ lɛɛ e blɔ ɔmɛ tsuo da; e siwo ɔmɛ hu anɔkuale sɔuu! E ngɛ kaa tsɛ̃i kɛ ha nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ba saa we ngɛ e ngɔ.

english_verse: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
translation_verse: Yawɛ pɛ ji wa Mawu; lɛ pɛ ji wa he bulɔ.

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Mawu nɛ ɔ ji ye mɔ ngua nɛ baa ye yi. E bli blɔ gbajaa ha mi.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: E haa nɛ i nyɛɛɔ yoku ɔmɛ a nɔ kɛ gɛjɛmi kaa yo nɔ apletsi, nɛ i sane we nɔɛ si.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: E haa mi ta hwumi he nile, kɛ he wami nɛ ma kɛ tsɛ̃ akɔblee kɛ̃ɛ̃ po.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: Yawɛ lee, o baa ye yi, nɛ o kpɔ mi; o yemi kɛ buami ɔ pee mi nɔmlɔ agbo.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: O ha we nɛ ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a nine nɛ su ye nɔ; i sane we nɔɛ si hyɛ.

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: I fia mɛ ni, nɛ i gbe mɛ pue si ngɛ ye nane nya, nɛ a nyɛ we nɛ a te si hu.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: Mo lɛ o ha mi he wami nɛ i kɛ hwu ta; mo lɛ o ha nɛ i ye ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a nɔ kunimi.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: A hyɛ yemi kɛ buami blɔ, se kpɔlɔ ko bɛ. A fa kue ha Yawɛ, se e pui a nya mi.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: I wɛɛ mɛ mɔnyɔmɔnyɔ nɛ a pee kaa tabo zu; i naa a nɔ, nɛ i gbɛ mɛ fĩa kaa gbɛjegbɛ nɔ mɔsɔ.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: O je mi kɛ je ye ma mi bi atuã tsɔli a dɛ mi; o baa ye yi, nɛ i ba pee je ma amɛ a nyatsɛ. Mahi nɛ i li mɛ po ba plɛ pee ye sɔmɔli.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Sawale maa nu ma je li ɔmɛ; a kɛ he kpokpomi maa hia kɛ maa je a laami he ɔmɛ kɛ ba.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: Yawɛ hɛ ngɛ! Tɛ sa a nɛ baa ye yi ɔ, a je e yi. Ye Mawu ɔ nɛ he ye yi wami ɔ, a wo e biɛ ta kaa e kle, nɛ e he wa.

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Lɛ nɛ e ha i ye ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a nɔ; nɛ e ngɔ ma amɛ ngɔ wo ye sisi,

english_verse: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
translation_verse: Mawu haa nɛ e matsɛ ɔ yeɔ kunimi nguahi. E jeɔ e suɔmi nɛ be nyagbe ɔ kpo kɛ tsɔɔ David, nɔ nɛ a pɔ lɛ nu ɔ, kɛ e nina kɛ yaa neneene.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: Yawɛ mumi ɔ tuɔ munyu kɛ guu ye nɔ, nɛ e sɛ gbi ɔ ngɛ ye nya he.

english_verse: is like the sunrise on a cloudless day, or like rain that sparkles on the grass.”
translation_verse: e ngɛ kaa pu nɛ ngɛ tsoe mɔtu be mi nɛ bɔku be hiɔwe; aloo hiɔmi nɛ haa nga tsɛ̃ɔ kɛ jeɔ zu mi.”

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: Kikɛ nɛ ɔ Mawu maa gbaa ye weku kɛ nina. Mawu kɛ mi so neneene somi, somi nɛ a be mi poe gblegbleegble. Nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ hlae ɔ pɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; e maa pee ye kunimi yemi, nɛ Yawɛ ma ha nɛ e ba mi.

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: David ta buli kpanaa amɛ a biɛhi ji nɛ ɔmɛ: Kekleekle nɔ ɔ ji Yosheb Bashebet, Takemon no ɔ; lɛ ji “Ni etɛ ɔmɛ” a nyatsɛ. E kɛ nimli lafa kpaanyɔ ya bua si kake, nɛ e kɛ e we akplɔ ɔ gbe mɛ tsuo.

english_verse: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
translation_verse: Nɔ nɛ nyɛɛ e se ngɛ katsɛmɛ etɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti ji Eleazar, Ahohi bi Dodo bi ɔ. Ligbi ko benɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ ya bua a he nya nɛ a gba ta a, Eleazar kɛ David ya tsɔ a nya. Jamɛ a be ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ a gbla a he si kɛ je lejɛ ɔ momo.

translation_verse: Benɛ ní kpami be su ta a, katsɛmɛ nyingmi etɛ ɔmɛ a ti ni etɛ pue nɔ kɛ ya na David ngɛ Adulam tɛ puɔ ɔ mi, be mi nɛ Filisti ojo fiali a kuu ɔ hu ya bua a he nya ngɛ Refaim kɔ̃ ɔ mi.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, David ngɛ tɛ puɔ ɔ mi, nɛ Filisti ta buli ɔmɛ ekomɛ ngɛ Betlehem.

english_verse: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: David kɛ he hiami bi ke, “Mɛnɔ po ma ya yɛ nyu ngɛ vu ɔ nɛ ngɛ agbo ɔ kasa nya ngɛ Betlehem ma a mi ɔ ba ha mi nɛ ma nu?”

translation_verse: Katsɛmɛ etɛ ɔmɛ pee nyumu ka; a ya gu Filisti bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti, nɛ a ya yɛ nyu ngɛ vu ɔ mi kɛ ba ha David. Se e kua numi; e plɛ nyu ɔ pue si ha Yawɛ mohu,

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Yehoyada bi Benaya, Kabzeel no ɔ, lɛ hu katsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake ji lɛ; nɛ e tsu ní tsumi nguahi. Lɛ nɛ e gbe Ariel nɛ je Moab ɔ binyumu enyɔ ɔmɛ, nɛ lɛ nɔuu nɛ e ya sɛ muɔ ko mi nɛ e gbe jata ligbi ko nɛ snoo ngɛ nɛe ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: Benaya nɛ ɔ nɔuu gbe Egipt no kpanaa ko. Egipt no ɔ hɛɛ akplɔ ngɛ e dɛ mi, se Benaya ho nɛ e ya na lɛ kɛ e dɛma tso ɔ kɛkɛ. E kpɔ akplɔ ɔ ngɛ e dɛ, nɛ e ngɔ Egipt no ɔ nitsɛ e akplɔ ɔ kɛ gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
translation_verse: E hɛ mi ngɛ nyami pe mɛ, se kekleekle ni etɛ ɔmɛ lɛɛ e na we mɛ. David kɛ lɛ pee e we bi a tabo ɔ nyatsɛ.

english_verse: in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
translation_verse: Ní lelɔ ji mo, nɛ o le nɔ́ nɛ sa nɛ o pee; ko ha nɛ e gbo lɛ nitsɛ e gbenɔ ngɛ he jɔmi mi.

english_verse: Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him.
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ, Gera binyumu Shimei nɛ je Bahurim ma a mi ngɛ Benyamin wɛtso ɔ mi ɔ hu ngɛ. Lɛ ji nɔ nɛ gbiɛ mi kadikadi ligbi ɔ nɛ i ya Mahanaim ɔ nɛ. Se benɛ e kɛ mi ba kpe ngɛ Yordan pa a nya a, i ka lɛ kita ngɛ Yawɛ biɛ mi ke i be lɛ gbee.

english_verse: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
translation_verse: Se kɛ̃ ɔ, ko ha nɛ e ye e he. Ní lelɔ ji mo, nɛ o le nɔ́ nɛ sa nɛ o pee; hyɛ nɛ a gbe lɛ.” David gbenɔ

english_verse: he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: e mia e teji ɔ, nɛ e pue nɔ kɛ ho Akish ngɔ ya ngɛ Gat, nɛ́ e ya hla mɛ. E ya na mɛ, nɛ e kɛ mɛ kpale kɛ ba we.

english_verse: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
translation_verse: A muɔ yi sɔ̃ ɔ maa ba Yoab kɛ e nina a nɔ kɛ maa ya neneene. Se David kɛ e nina nɛ ma ba hi e sɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ, mɛɛ Yawɛ ma ha mɛ tue mi jɔmi kɛ maa ya neneene.”

english_verse: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
translation_verse: Salomo ba ye matsɛ ngɛ e tsɛ David se, nɛ e matsɛ yemi ɔ ma si saminya. Adoniya gbenɔ

english_verse: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Adoniya nɛ a tsɛɛ e nyɛ ke Hagit ɔ, ba Salomo nyɛ Batsheba ngɔ. Batsheba bi lɛ ke, “O ba kɛ tue mi jɔmi lo?” E he nɔ ke, “Ee!

english_verse: I just want to talk with you.” “All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
translation_verse: Se i ngɛ nɔ́ ko nɛ ma de mo.” Batsheba de lɛ ke, “Mo de!”

english_verse: “You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed.
translation_verse: Adoniya de lɛ ke, “Kaa bɔ nɛ o le ɔ, jinɛ imi lɛ i yeɔ matsɛ; Israel ma a tsuo hyɛ blɔ kaa imi lɛ ma ba ye matsɛ ɔ nɛ. Se e ya bɛ lɛ ja, nɛ ye senɔ mohu ba ye matsɛ; ejakaa Yawɛ lɛ ha nɛ e ba mi ja.

english_verse: Would you do me a favor?” “What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
translation_verse: Se i ngɛ nɔ́ kake nɛ ma bi mo; mo ko kua.” Batsheba de lɛ ke, “Mo bi mi faa.”

english_verse: Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?” Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Batsheba de ke, “I kɛ hiami nɔ́ nyafii ko ma o hɛ mi fɔmi nɛ o pee ha mi; mo ko kua.” Matsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke, “Maa, mo bi mi faa; i be kuae.”

english_verse: Solomon said: What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
translation_verse: Matsɛ Salomo bi e nyɛ ɔ ke, “Mɛni he je o bi mi ke ma ngɔ Abishag kɛ ha Adoniya a? Bi nɛ ma ngɔ matsɛ yemi ɔ hu ngɔ ha lɛ mɔ. Wa wetsɛ ji lɛ! Pi kɛ ha lɛ pɛ; se mohu bi kɛ ha osɔfo Abiatar, kɛ Zeruya binyumu Yoab hulɔ!”

english_verse: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Matsɛ Salomo ka Yawɛ kita nɛ e de ke, “I na Mawu kaa ke Adoniya kɛ e wami ha we ngɛ munyu nɛ e tu nɛ ɔ he fii, Mawu nɛ gbe mi!

english_verse: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ngɔ mi ngɔ hi tsaatsɛ David sɛ ɔ nɔ. Yawɛ ye e siwo nɔ, nɛ e ngɔ matsɛ yemi ɔ ngɔ ha imi, kɛ ye nina. I na Mawu hɛ kalɔ ɔ kaa ja Adoniya gbo mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ nɔuu!”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Matsɛ Salomo tsɔ Yehoyada binyumu Benaya, nɛ e ya fia Adoniya nɔ́ nɛ e gbe lɛ. A je Abiatar we

english_verse: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Matsɛ Salomo de osɔfo Abiatar ke, “Moo ho mo nitsɛ o ma mi ya ngɛ Anatot. Jinɛ e sa kaa a gbe mo, se i be hae nɛ a gbe mo piɔ; ejakaa benɛ o kɛ tsaatsɛ David ngɛ ɔ, mo lɛ o hyɛɛ Yawɛ Mawu somi daka a nɔ. Jehanɛ se hu, amanehlu slɔɔtohi tsuo nɛ tsaatsɛ na a, o kɛ lɛ nɛ na.”

english_verse: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Salomo kpa Abiatar osɔfo yemi, nɛ e yi osɔfo ha Yawɛ hu; nɛ nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ de ngɛ Shilo ngɛ osɔfo Eli, kɛ e nina a he ɔ ba mi.

english_verse: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Yoab nu sane nɛ ba a. . Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e tu fo ya sɛ Yawɛ bo tsu ɔ mi ya fua bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he koli ɔmɛ.

english_verse: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
translation_verse: Benɛ a ya bɔ Matsɛ Salomo amaniɛ ke Yoab tu fo ya sɛ Yawɛ bo tsu ɔ mi, nɛ e ya sa we ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he ɔ, Salomo tsɔ Yehoyada binyumu Benaya ke e ya fia lɛ nɔ́ nɛ e gbe.

english_verse: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
translation_verse: Benaya ya Yawɛ bo tsu ɔ mi, nɛ e ya de Yoab ke, “Matsɛ ɔ fa ke, o je kpo nɛ o ba!” Yoab he nɔ ke, “Dɛbi, ma gbo ngɛ hiɛ ɔ.” Benaya kpale kɛ ho matsɛ ɔ ngɔ ya ya de lɛ nɔ́ nɛ Yoab de ɔ.

english_verse: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
translation_verse: Yawɛ maa wo Yoab hiɔ ngɛ nihi nɛ e gbe nɛ tsaatsɛ David li he nɔ́ ko ɔ a he. Yoab gbe nyumuhi enyɔ nɛ a da pe lɛ yaka gu. Mɛ ji Israel tatsɛ Abner, Ner binyumu ɔ, kɛ Yuda tatsɛ Amasa, Yeter binyumu ɔ.

english_verse: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yehoyada binyumu Benaya ya sɛ Yawɛ bo tsu ɔ mi, nɛ e fia Yoab nɔ́ nɛ e gbe, nɛ e ya pu lɛ ngɛ e we mi ngɛ nga a nɔ.

english_verse: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ wo Yehoyada binyumu Benaya tatsɛ ngɛ Yoab nane mi, nɛ e ngɔ osɔfo Zadok hu ngɔ to osɔfo Abiatar blɔ he ɔ. Shimei gbenɔ

english_verse: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, matsɛ ɔ tsɔ ya tsɛ Shimei kɛ ba, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ba ma tsu ngɛ hiɛ ɔ ngɛ Yerusalem, nɛ o hi mi. Koo je hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ kɛ ya he ko he ko.

english_verse: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
translation_verse: Ligbi ɔ nɛ o maa je hiɛ ɔ, nɛ o maa po Kidron pa a, ná nɛ o le kaa ja o gbo, nɛ sɔ̃ ɔ maa tloo mo nitsɛ.”

english_verse: “That's fair, Your Majesty,” Shimei answered. “I'll do that.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem from then on.
translation_verse: Shimei he nɔ ke, “Saminya! Ma pee kaa bɔ nɛ o de ɔ.” Nɛ Shimei hi Yerusalem be babauu.

english_verse: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
translation_verse: Se jeha etɛ se ɔ, Shimei nyɔguɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti ni enyɔ tu fo kɛ ho Gat matsɛ, Akish, Maaka binyumu ɔ ngɔ ya. Benɛ Shimei nu kaa e nyɔguɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ Gat ɔ,

english_verse: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
translation_verse: Benɛ Salomo nu nɔ́ nɛ Shimei pee ɔ he ɔ,

english_verse: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
translation_verse: e tsɔ nɛ a ya tsɛ lɛ kɛ ba, nɛ e bi lɛ ke, “Anɛ i ha we nɛ o ka Yawɛ kita kaa o be Yerusalem jee gblegbleegble lo? Anɛ i ha we nɛ o nu sisi faii kaa ligbi nɛ o maa je Yerusalem ɔ, ja o gbo lo?

english_verse: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ o tɔ kita nɛ o ka Yawɛ ɔ, nɛ o yi mlaa a nɛ i wo mo ɔ hu nɔ ɔ?

english_verse: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
translation_verse: Mo nitsɛ o le yayamihi tsuo nɛ o je blɔ pee tsaatsɛ David. Yawɛ maa wo mo he hiɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
translation_verse: Se imi Matsɛ Salomo lɛɛ Yawɛ maa gbaa mi, nɛ e ma ha David matsɛ yemi ɔ maa ma si kpɛii kɛ maa ya neneene.”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, matsɛ ɔ fa Yehoyada binyumu Benaya, nɛ e je kpo nɛ e ya fia Shimei nɔ́ nɛ e gbe. Jehanɛ lɛɛ Salomo matsɛ yemi ɔ ma si kpɛii.

english_verse: At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, a na we nɛ a ma we ha Yawɛ lolo; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma a ya nɔ nɛ a sã bɔ ngɛ wɔ piɛ ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, nɔ́ nɛ o bi we tete hu ma ha mo; o wami ligbi ɔmɛ tsuo ɔ, ma ha o ma na ní, nɛ o hɛ mi maa ba nyami bɔ nɛ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛ mo be sɔe.

english_verse: Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
translation_verse: Salomo suɔ Yawɛ, nɛ e ye e tsɛ David mlaa amɛ a nɔ; se e gbe lohwe, nɛ e sã tsopa kɛ e he via ngɛ wɔ piɛ ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: Jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Yawɛ je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ Salomo ngɛ nlami mi, nɛ e bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni o suɔ nɛ ma ha mo?”

english_verse: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ye Mawu lee, o ha nɛ i ba ngɛ tsɛ yee ngɛ tsaatsɛ David se, be mi nɛ jokuɛ bɔbɔyoo kɛkɛ ji mi, nɛ́ i li nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko.

english_verse: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
translation_verse: Ne mi ngɛ nimli nɛ o je blɔ hla mɛ kɛ pee mo nitsɛ o ma, nimli kpekpemi nɛ nɔ ko be nyɛe maa kane mɛɔ a kpɛti.

english_verse: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ, ha mi nile nɛ ma kɛ ye o ma a nɔ ngɛ dami sane yemi mi; nɛ ma le slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ da, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ dɛ a kpɛti. Ke pi ja a, lɛɛ kɛ ma pee kɛ ye o ma kpekpemi nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ kɛɛ?”

english_verse: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Mawu de lɛ ke, “Akɛnɛ o bi nile nɛ o kɛ ye dami sane, se o bi we ke o wami se nɛ kɛ, aloo o ma na ní, aloo a gbe o he nyɛli ha mo he je ɔ,

english_verse: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
translation_verse: Nɛ ke o maa bu mi tue, nɛ o maa ye ye mlaa amɛ a nɔ kaa bɔ nɛ o tsɛ David pee ɔ, ma ha o wami se maa kɛ.”

english_verse: Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials. Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
translation_verse: Salomo hɛ tsɛ, nɛ e na kaa nlami lɛ e nla. E ya Yerusalem, nɛ e ya da si ngɛ Yawɛ somi daka a hɛ mi, nɛ e sã sami bɔhi, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔhi. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ngmɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo okplɔɔ. Salomo kojo sane ko nɛ he wa

english_verse: One day two women came to King Solomon,
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, yi ajuamahi enyɔ ba Matsɛ Salomo ngɔ kɛ sane ko.

english_verse: and one of them said: Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home,
translation_verse: Nɔ kake de lɛ ke, “Nɛnɛ, i kɛ yo nɛ ɔ tsuo ngɛ we kake mi; nɛ i ba fɔ binyumu ngɛ we ɔ mi ngɛ e hɛ mi.

english_verse: One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died.
translation_verse: Ligbi ko nyɔ mi ɔ, yo nɛ ɔ hwɔ e binyumu ɔ nɔ, nɛ jokuɛ ɔ gbo.

english_verse: Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
translation_verse: Nyɔ mi kɔ̃kɔ̃ɔ̃kɔ̃ benɛ i hwɔ mahe ɔ, yo nɛ ɔ te si nɛ e ba wo ye binyumuyo ngɛ ye kasa nya, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ya hɔ e mi si; nɛ e wo lɛɛ e binyumuyo ɔ nɛ gbo ɔ kɛ ba hɔ ye mi si.

english_verse: In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
translation_verse: Mɔtu benɛ i te si nɛ ma ha ye bi ɔ nyɔ ɔ, i na kaa e gbo. Se benɛ i hyɛ lɛ saminya a, i na kaa pi ye bi ɔ.”

english_verse: “No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!” “The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!” They argued back and forth in front of Solomon,
translation_verse: Se yo kaketsɛ ɔ de ke, “Dɛbi! Ye bi ji nɔ nɛ hɛ ngɛ ɔ nɛ; o bi ji nɔ nɛ gbo ɔ nɛ!” Nɔ kake ɔ hu de ke, “Dɛbi! O bi ji nɔ nɛ gbo ɔ, nɛ ye bi ji nɔ nɛ hɛ ngɛ ɔ nɛ!” Bɔ nɛ a hua sane ɔ he kɛ ya kɛ ba ngɛ matsɛ ɔ hɛ mi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Someone bring me a sword.” A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered,
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Saminya, nyɛ ha mi klaate!” Benɛ a kɛ klaate ɔ ba a,

english_verse: “Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
translation_verse: e de ke, “Nyɛɛ dla bi nɛ hɛ ngɛ ɔ mi enyɔ, nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ fa ngɔ ha nɔ kake, nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ fa hu ngɔ ha nɔ kake.”

english_verse: “Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.” The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ nɔ tutuutu nɛ ji bi nɛ hɛ ngɛ ɔ nyɛ ɔ tsui mi sã lɛ ngɛ e bi ɔ he, nɛ e de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Nɛnɛ, i kpa mo pɛɛ, koo gbe jokuɛ ɔ. Ngɔɔ lɛ ngɔ ha yo ɔ kɛkɛ.” Se yo kaketsɛ ɔ de ke, “Dɛbi! E be ye nɔ́ pee, nɛ e be mo hu o nɔ́ pee; a dla e mi enyɔ.”

english_verse: Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Salomo de ke, “Koo gbe jokuɛ ɔ! Ngɔɔ lɛ kɛ ha kekleekle yo ɔ; ejakaa lɛ ji bi ɔ nyɛ nitsɛnitsɛ.”

english_verse: Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_verse: Benɛ Israel ma a tsuo nu bɔ nɛ Matsɛ Salomo buá sane ɔ he ha a, a bu lɛ wawɛɛ nitsɛ; ejakaa a yɔse kaa Mawu ha lɛ nile nɛ e kɛ kojo ngɛ dami sane yemi nya.

english_verse: Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Salomo pee nyumuhi nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ amlaalohi ngɛ Israel zugba a tsuo nɔ. Mɛ lɛ a ba haa matsɛ ɔ, kɛ e we ɔ niye ní; nɔ tsuaa nɔ ba haa niye ní hlami kake ngɛ jeha mi.

english_verse: These were the twelve officers: The son of Hur was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Amlaalo ɔmɛ a biɛ, kɛ hehi nɛ a hyɛɛ nɔ ɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: Benhur nɔ́ mi ji Efraim yo ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
translation_verse: Bendeker nɔ́ mi ji Makaz, Shaalbim, Bet Shemesh, Elon, kɛ Bet Hanan.

english_verse: The son of Abinadab was in charge of Naphath-Dor and was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath.
translation_verse: Benabinadab nɛ ngɔ Salomo biyo nɛ a tsɛɛ Tafat ɔ, e nɔ́ mi ji Dor tsuo.

english_verse: The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had
translation_verse: Bengeber nɔ́ mi ji Ramot ngɛ Gilead, kɛ Manase binyumu Yair kɔpehi nɛ ngɛ Gilead ɔ. Lɛ kɛ̃ e nɔ́ mi ji Argob zugba a nɛ ngɛ Bashan ɔ nɛ. Ma nguangua nyingmi ekpa ngɛ zugba a nɔ; a fia gbogbo ngɔ wo a he, kɛ a nya agbohi nɛ a kɛ akɔblee pee.

english_verse: Ahinadab son of Iddo was in charge of the territory of Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Ido binyumu Ahinadab nɔ́ mi ji Mahanaim.

english_verse: Ahimaaz was in charge of the territory of Naphtali and was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath.
translation_verse: Ahimaaz nɛ ngɔ Salomo biyo ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Basemat ɔ, e nɔ́ mi ji Naftali.

english_verse: Baana son of Hushai was in charge of the territory of Asher and the town of Bealoth.
translation_verse: Hushai binyumu Baana nɔ́ mi ji Asher kɛ Bealot.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in charge of the territory of Issachar.
translation_verse: Parua binyumu Yehoshafat nɔ́ mi ji Isakar.

english_verse: Shimei son of Ela was in charge of the territory of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ela binyumu Shimei nɔ́ mi ji Benyamin.

english_verse: Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived. And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah. The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
translation_verse: Uri binyumu Geber nɔ́ mi ji Gilead, nɛ ji Amor Matsɛ Sihon, kɛ Bashan Matsɛ Og a zugba a. Nimli nɛ ɔmɛ a se ɔ, amlaalo kake ngɛ nɛ hyɛɛ zugba a tsuo nɔ. Salomo ye tsɛ ngɛ kplɔkɔtɔ mi

english_verse: Solomon ruled every kingdom between the Euphrates River and the land of the Philistines down to Egypt. These kingdoms paid him taxes as long as he lived.
translation_verse: Nɛ Salomo ye tsɛ ngɛ ma amɛ tsuo a nɔ, kɛ je Yufrate pa a nya kɛ ya si Filisti bi ɔmɛ a zugba a, kɛ ya pue Egipt bi ɔmɛ a huzu ɔ nya tɔɔ. Je ma nɛ ɔmɛ wo tó ha lɛ, nɛ a sɔmɔ lɛ e wami be ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: Everyone living in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, was safe as long as Solomon lived. Each family sat undisturbed beneath its own grape vines and fig trees.
translation_verse: Salomo yi nɔ ɔ, Yuda kɛ Israel tsuo hi si ngɛ he jɔmi mi kɛ je Dan kɛ ya si Beersheba; nɔ tsuaa nɔ ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e wai tso kɛ ngmɔkɔ tso.

english_verse: Solomon was brilliant. God had blessed him with insight and understanding.
translation_verse: Mawu ha Salomo nile, nɔ́ sisi numi, kɛ juɛmi nɛ nya wa babauu nitsɛ bɔ nɛ a be nyɛe maa kale.

english_verse: He was wiser than anyone else in the world, including the wisest people of the east and of Egypt. He was even wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Mahol's three sons, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Solomon became famous in every country around Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: E le ní pe nɔ tsuaa nɔ; e le ní pe Etan, Ezrahi no ɔ; e le ní pe Mahol binyumuhi, Heman, Kalkol, kɛ Darda; nɛ e he biɛ ngɛ je ma amɛ tsuo nɛ bɔle lɛ kɛ kpe ɔ a mi.

english_verse: He could talk about all kinds of plants, from large trees to small bushes, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
translation_verse: E tu tsohi a he munyu kɛ je Lebanon seda tso ɔmɛ a nɔ hluu kɛ ya si nga tsɔwi nɛ puɛɔ ngɛ gbogbohi a nɔ ɔ a nɔ. E tu lohwe nane eywiɛtsɛmɛ, pɛlitsɛmɛ, kɛ ní nɛmɛ nɛ sãã si, kɛ lohi a he munyu.

english_verse: Kings all over the world heard about Solomon's wisdom and sent people to listen to him teach.
translation_verse: Zugba a nɔ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsuo nu e nile ɔ he, nɛ a woɔ nihi blɔ kɛ yaa ya buɔ lɛ tue.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre had always been friends with Solomon's father David. When Hiram learned that Solomon was king, he sent some of his officials to meet with Solomon.
translation_verse: Tiro matsɛ, Hiram kɛ David ɔ, huɛmɛ ji mɛ. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, benɛ e nu kaa a pɔ Salomo nu nɛ a wo lɛ matsɛ ngɛ David se ɔ, e tsɔ kɛ ya ha lɛ manye.

english_verse: I'd like you to send your workers to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. I will pay them whatever you say and will even have my workers help them. We both know that your workers are more experienced than anyone else at cutting lumber.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ha nɛ a hɛ seda tsohi ngɛ Lebanon ha mi. Ye tsɔli ɔmɛ ma ba piɛ o tsɔli ɔmɛ a he, nɛ ma wo o tsɔli ɔmɛ hiɔ bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ o maa tsɔɔ. Kaa bɔ nɛ mo nitsɛ o le ɔ, nɔ ko nɔ ko be Israel nɛ le tso hɛmi kɛ nyɛ Sidon bi ɔmɛ sɔ.”

english_verse: Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!”
translation_verse: Benɛ Hiram nu Salomo sɛ gbi ɔ, e ná bua jɔmi babauu, nɛ e de ke, “A gbaa Yawɛ mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, kaa e ha David binyumu ní lelɔ nɛ maa ye ma nguaa nɛ ɔ nɔ!”

english_verse: Then he sent back his answer: I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Hiram ngɔ sɛ gbi ngɔ mane Salomo ke, “O sɛ gbi ɔ ba su mi; nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ hlae ɔ, ma pee ha mo. Ma ha mo seda tsohi, kɛ sɛsɛo tsohi.

english_verse: My workers will carry them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea. They will tie the logs together and float them along the coast to wherever you want them. Then they will untie the logs, and your workers can take them from there. To pay for the logs, you can provide the grain I need for my household.
translation_verse: Ye tsɔli ɔmɛ maa muɔ tso ɔmɛ kɛ je Lebanon kɛ ba wo ɔ nya, nɛ ma ha a fi mɛ kɛ bla kɛ gu wo nɔ kɛ ya pue he nɛ o maa tsɔɔ mi. Ma ha nɛ a pɛne kpa a ngɛ a he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, konɛ o ha nɛ a ba muɔ kɛ ho. Ngɛ moo o blɔ fa mi ɔ, ma suɔ nɛ o ha ye we bi ɔmɛ niye ní.”

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise and made Solomon wise. Hiram and Solomon signed a treaty and never went to war against each other. Solomon's Workers
translation_verse: Yawɛ ye e siwo ɔ nɔ, nɛ e ha Salomo nile. Hiram kɛ Salomo hi si ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi; mɛ ni enyɔ ɔmɛ a so somi.

english_verse: He ordered the workers to cut and shape large blocks of good stone for the foundation of the temple.
translation_verse: Ngɛ Matsɛ Salomo fami nya a, a gba tɛ kpakpa nguanguahi nɛ a he jua wa kɛ ba fia sisi tomi ha Mawu we ɔ.

english_verse: Solomon's and Hiram's men worked with men from the city of Gebal, and together they got the stones and logs ready for the temple.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Salomo tsu mali, Matsɛ Hiram tsu mali, kɛ Gebal bi ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ kó tɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ́ a dla tso ɔmɛ a he kɛ ha Mawu we ɔ mami ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: The windows were narrow on the outside but wide on the inside.
translation_verse: Salomo pee saflɛhi nɛ blɔ ngɛ a mi ngɔ wo Yawɛ we ɔ he.

english_verse: The roof of the temple was made out of beams and cedar boards. The workers finished building the outside of the temple.
translation_verse: Benɛ Matsɛ Salomo ma we ɔ gbe nya a, e sɛu nɔ kɛ seda plai, kɛ gbegbeli.

english_verse: Along the sides and back of the temple, there were three levels of storage rooms. The rooms on the bottom level were just over two meters wide, the rooms on the middle level were over two and a half meters wide, and those on the top level were just over three meters wide. There were ledges on the outside of the temple that supported the beams of the storage rooms, so that nothing was built into the temple walls.
translation_verse: E ma tsu nɛ ɔmɛ siaudo etɛ; zugba tsu ɔ blimi ji nine mi blimi nyɔngma, kpɛti nɔ́ ɔ blimi nine mi blimi nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ, nɛ hiɔwe nɔ́ ɔ blimi ji nine mi blimi nyɔngma kɛ eywiɛ. E pee kpokuhi kɛ wo we ɔ gbogbo ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e kɛ plai ɔmɛ fɔ nɔ; se e kɛ wui gbogbo ɔ mi. Kikɛ nɛ ɔ Salomo pee nɛ e kɛ tsa tsu ɔmɛ kɛ wo gbogbo ɔ he.

english_verse: Solomon did not want the noise of hammers and axes to be heard at the place where the temple was being built. So he gave orders for the workers to shape the blocks of stone at the quarry.
translation_verse: Tɛ nɛ a kó momo ngɛ tɛ gbami he nɛ a kɛ ma tsu ɔ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, benɛ a ngɛ tsu ɔ mae ɔ, a nui hamle, loo gbiɛ, loo dade kpa ko nya ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Storage rooms just over two meters high were all around the temple, and they were attached to the temple by cedar beams.
translation_verse: E ma tsu tsɔwihi siaudo etɛ, nɛ e kɛ seda plai tsa mɛ kɛ wo gbogbo ɔmɛ a he kɛ kpe. Siaudo tsuaa siaudo hiɔwe yami ji nine mi blimi nyɔngma.

english_verse: The Lord told Solomon:
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Salomo ke,

english_verse: The floor of the temple was made out of pine, and the walls were lined with cedar from floor to ceiling.
translation_verse: Salomo ka seda gbegbeli ngɔ wo gbogbo ɔmɛ a he ngɛ we ɔ mi je, kɛ je zugba kɛ ya ta siaudo ɔ nya; zugba a nitsɛ lɛɛ e kɛ sɛsɛo ka mi.

english_verse: The most holy place was in the back of the temple, and it was nine meters square. Cedar boards standing from floor to ceiling separated it from the rest of the temple.
translation_verse: E ma se tsu ko nɛ a tsɛɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a ngɛ we ɔ se je. E kami ji gugue enuɔ, nɛ a kɛ seda gbegbeli po mi kɛ je siaudo ɔ nya kɛ ba ma zugba.

english_verse: The inside walls were lined with cedar to hide the stones, and the cedar was decorated with carvings of gourds and flowers.
translation_verse: Seda gbegbeli nɛ a ka ngɔ wo gbogbo ɔmɛ a he ngɛ we ɔ mi je ɔ ha tɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi; a je blɔ hlɔ tɔhi kɛ mɔmɔhi nɛ blɛke saminyawiiwi kɛ mɛtɛ he.

english_verse: The sacred chest was kept in the most holy place.
translation_verse: Salomo pee tsu ko ngɛ we ɔ kpɛti tutuutu, he nɛ a kɛ Yawɛ somi daka a maa ma.

english_verse: This room was nine meters long, nine meters wide, and nine meters high, and it was lined with pure gold. There were also gold chains across the front of the most holy place. The inside of the temple, as well as the cedar altar in the most holy place, was covered with gold.
translation_verse: E kɛ sika tsu ha we mluku ɔ tsuo he; bɔ sami la tɛ nɛ ngɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a hu e kɛ sika tsu ha he.

english_verse: Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made from olive wood to put in the most holy place. Each creature was four and a half meters tall
translation_verse: Salomo kɛ oliv tso pee kerub enyɔ ngɔ ma he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a; kerub kake kami ji nine mi blimi nyingmi enyɔ.

english_verse: The creatures were also covered with gold.
translation_verse: Salomo kɛ sika tsu ha kerub ɔmɛ a he.

english_verse: The walls of the two rooms were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: A je blɔ kpɛ níhi kaa kerubhi, tã, kɛ mɔmɔhi nɛ a blɛke saminyawiiwi ngɔ mɛtɛ gbogbo ɔmɛ a he kɛ kpe ngɛ we ɔ mi blɔ, kɛ kpo nɔ blɔ tsuo.

english_verse: Even the floor was covered with gold.
translation_verse: Zugba a nitsɛ po a kɛ sika tsu ha hɛ mi.

english_verse: The two doors to the most holy place were made out of olive wood and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures. The doors and the carvings were covered with gold. The door frame came to a point at the top.
translation_verse: A je blɔ hlɔ kerubhi, tãhi, kɛ mɔmɔhi nɛ a blɛke ngɔ mɛtɛ sinya amɛ a he; a kɛ sika tsu ha sinya amɛ, tã amɛ, kɛ mɔmɔ ɔmɛ a he.

english_verse: The doors were covered with gold and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: A je blɔ hlɔ kerubhi, tãhi, kɛ mɔmɔhi nɛ a blɛke ngɔ mɛtɛ he, nɛ a kɛ sika tsu ha he.

english_verse: The inner courtyard of the temple had walls made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams.
translation_verse: Kue ɔ nɛ Salomo ma ngɛ we ɔ kpɛti ɔ gbogbo ɔmɛ ɔ, tɛ nɛ a kó gbaka etɛ, kɛ seda plai gbaka kake nɛ a kɛ pee lɛ.

english_verse: Work began on the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year, four years after Solomon became king of Israel.
translation_verse: A to Yawɛ we ɔ sisi ngɛ Salomo yi nɔ jeha nɛ ji eywiɛ ɔ we nyɔhiɔ enyɔne ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Ziv ɔ mi.

translation_verse: Akɔblee kpɔ ɔmɛ nɛ a pee kaa mɔmɔ ɔ maa si ngɛ titima amɛ a yi mi. Bɔ nɛ a pee nɛ a kɛ gbe titima amɛ a he ní tsumi nya ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Akɔblee nyu nɔ́ ɔ (Kronika II,

english_verse: The section of the palace where Solomon lived was behind Justice Hall and looked exactly like it. He had a similar place built for his wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt.
translation_verse: Salomo hi he ɔ nitsɛ nɛ ngɛ kue kpa ko mi ngɛ kojomi kue ɔ se ɔ, e pee lɛ kaa tsu kpa amɛ nɔuu; nɛ e po jamɛ a we ɔ eko kɛ ha e yo nɛ ji Egipt matsɛ ɔ biyo ɔ.

english_verse: From the foundation all the way to the top, these buildings and the courtyard were made out of the best stones carefully cut to size, then smoothed on every side with saws.
translation_verse: Tsu nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo, kɛ kue nguaa a, tɛ nɛ he jua wa nɛ a kɛ pee mɛ kɛ je sisi tomi ɔ nɔ kɛ ya si siaudo ɔ he. A susu tɛ ɔmɛ loko a kó, nɛ a kɛ sau dla a hɛ mi, kɛ a se.

english_verse: The walls around the palace courtyard were made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams, just like the front porch and the inner courtyard of the temple. Hiram Makes the Bronze Furnishings (
translation_verse: Matsɛ we mi kue nguaa a, kpɛti kue ɔ nɛ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ, kɛ wayoo ɔ nɛ ngɛ agbo ɔ nya a, tɛ nɛ a kó gbaka etɛ, kɛ seda plai gbaka kake nɛ a kɛ pee gbogbo ɔmɛ. Huram ní tsumi

english_verse: The caps were decorated with seven rows of designs that looked like chains,
translation_verse: E pee ya enyɔ nɛ a lo, kɛ mɔmɔ jlasi nɛ a pee kaa kɔsɔkɔsɔ ngɔ ma titima enyɔ ɔmɛ a yi mi.

english_verse: Hiram was a skilled bronze worker from the city of Tyre. His father was now dead, but he also had been a bronze worker from Tyre, and his mother was from the tribe of Naphtali. King Solomon asked Hiram to come to Jerusalem and make the bronze furnishings to use for worship in the Lord's temple, and he agreed to do it.
translation_verse: Yalɔyo ko nɛ je Naftali wɛtso ɔ mi ɔ bi ji lɛ; e tsɛ lɛɛ e je Tiro, nɛ akɔblee ga ní tsulɔ ji lɛ. Huram hu akɔblee ga ní tsulɔ kpanaa ji lɛ; nɛ e ba Salomo ngɔ nɛ e ba tsu akɔblee ní tsumi ɔ tsuo. Akɔblee titima enyɔ ɔmɛ (Kronika II,

english_verse: For the top of each column, he also made a bronze cap just over two meters high.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, e pee akɔblee kpɔ enyɔ kɛ ma titima amɛ a yi mi; kake hiɔwe yami ji nine mi blimi nyɔngma.

english_verse: The caps for the columns of the porch were almost two meters high and were shaped like lilies.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɔmɛ nɛ maa si ngɛ titima amɛ a yi mi ɔ, a pee mɛ kaa mɔmɔ, nɛ eko tsuaa eko hiɔwe yami ji nine mi blimi kpaanyɔ.

english_verse: Hiram placed the two columns on each side of the main door of the temple. The column on the south side was called Jachin, and the one on the north was called Boaz.
translation_verse: Huram ngɔ akɔblee titima enyɔ nɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ ma Yawɛ we ɔ agbo ɔ nya; e wo nɔ́ nɛ maa si ngɛ leneyi je ɔ biɛ ke Yakin, nɛ e wo omleyi je nɔ́ ɔ biɛ ke Boaz.

translation_verse: A pee akɔblee tɔhi gbaka enyɔ kɛ bɔle nyu nɔ́ ɔ kuɔ si kɛ kpe; a sile akɔblee kɛ pee mɛ kɛ nyu nɔ́ ɔ tsuo kake.

english_verse: Hiram made ten movable bronze stands, each one over a meter high, almost two meters long, and almost two meters wide.
translation_verse: Huram pee akɔblee tlɔɔke nyɔngma; tlɔɔke kake kami ji nine mi blimi kpaanyɔ, e blimi nine mi blimi kpaanyɔ, kɛ e hiɔwe yami nine mi blimi ekpa.

english_verse: The sides were made with panels attached to frames decorated with flower designs. The panels themselves were decorated with figures of lions, bulls, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: E pee jatahi, na kuhi, kɛ kerubhi ngɛ akɔblee ní kɔ nya eywiɛɛywiɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ; nɛ e pee mɔmɔ jlasi saminyawiiwi ngɛ jata amɛ, kɛ na ku ɔmɛ a nɔ ngɛ hɛ mi, kɛ se tsuo.

english_verse: Hiram made the ten bronze stands from the same mold, so they were exactly the same size and shape.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ a pee tlɔɔke nyɔngma amɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. A sɔ̃ mɛ tsuo fiee; a hɛɛ susumi kake kɛ henɔ kake.

english_verse: Hiram also made ten small bronze bowls, one for each stand. The bowls were almost two meters across and could hold about
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Huram pee akɔblee kã nyɔngma, tlɔɔke tsuaa tlɔɔke kɛ e he kã. Kã tsuaa kã a, kpa nine mi blimi kpaanyɔ maa kpe he, nɛ nyu lita lafa kpaanyɔ maa ya mi.

english_verse: He put five stands on the south side of the temple, five stands on the north side, and the large bowl at the southeast corner of the temple.
translation_verse: E kɛ tlɔɔke enuɔ ma Yawɛ we ɔ leneyi je, nɛ e kɛ enuɔ ma omleyi je; e ngɔ nyu nɔ́ ɔ lɛɛ ngɔ ma we ɔ leneyi je kɛ beleku je a kpɛti kɔ nya he ko. Yawɛ we ɔ mi dlami níhi (Kronika II,

english_verse: near the Jordan River between Succoth and Zarethan by pouring melted bronze into clay molds.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ ha nɛ a sɔ̃ ní ɔmɛ ngɛ akɔblee galɔ ní tsumi he nɛ ngɛ Sukot kɛ Zaretan a kpɛti, ngɛ Yordan kɔ̃ ɔ mi ɔ.

english_verse: There were so many bronze things that Solomon never bothered to weigh them, and no one ever knew how much bronze was used.
translation_verse: Salomo ha we nɛ a ngmɛ akɔblee ní ɔmɛ nɛ a pee ɔ, ejakaa a hiɛ tsɔ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ ko nɔ ko li akɔblee ɔ nya.

english_verse: Solomon gave orders to make the following temple furnishings out of gold: the altar; the table that held the sacred loaves of bread;
translation_verse: Salomo ha a kɛ sika tsu ngmingmiingmi pee ní nɛ ɔmɛ hulɔ kɛ ma Yawɛ we ɔ mi: bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ, okplɔɔ ɔ nɛ a kɛ abolo klɛdɛɛ ɔ maa nɔ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ,

english_verse: ten lampstands that went in front of the most holy place; flower designs; lamps and tongs;
translation_verse: kane tso nyɔngma amɛ nɛ maa he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a hɛ mi ɔ, enuɔ ngɛ leneyi je, kɛ enuɔ hu ngɛ omleyi je; mɔmɔ ɔmɛ, kane ɔmɛ, abɛɛle ɔmɛ,

english_verse: cups, lamp snuffers, and small sprinkling bowls; dishes for incense; fire pans; and the hinges for the doors to the most holy place and the main room of the temple.
translation_verse: kplu ɔmɛ, la gbemi ní ɔmɛ, kã amɛ, kɛ ngɛyu ɔmɛ nɛ a kɛ jeɔ la a; he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a sinya amɛ a se asa amɛ, kɛ Yawɛ we ɔ kpo nɔ je sinya amɛ a se asa amɛ.

english_verse: After the Lord's temple was finished, Solomon put into its storage rooms everything that his father David had dedicated to the Lord, including the gold and the silver.
translation_verse: Benɛ Matsɛ Salomo gbe Yawɛ we ɔ he ní tsumi ɔ tsuo nya a, e ngɔ níhi tsuo nɛ e tsɛ David gbaa nɔ ngɔ ha Yawɛ ɔ ngɔ to nito hehi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Ní ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: sika hiɔ, sika tsu, kɛ ni kpa komɛ.

english_verse: Solomon and a crowd of people stood in front of the chest and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Matsɛ Salomo, kɛ Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo ya bua a he nya ngɛ somi daka a hɛ mi, nɛ a gbe to, kɛ na babauu nɛ a li nya kɛ sã bɔ.

english_verse: The poles were so long that they could be seen from right outside the most holy place, but not from anywhere else. And they stayed there from then on.
translation_verse: Tso ɔmɛ ka gagaa bɔ nɛ ke nɔ ko daa si ngɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a hɛ mi ɔ, e maa na a nya amɛ nɛ je kpo; se a nya ji kpo nɛ a maa na ngɛ kpo nɔ. Tso ɔmɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The only things kept in the chest were the two flat stones Moses had put there when the Lord made his agreement with the people of Israel at Mount Sinai, after bringing them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be somi daka a mi kaa ja tɛ tɛtlɛɛ enyɔ ɔmɛ nɛ Mose ngɔ wo mi kɛ je Sinai yo ɔ nɔ ɔ. Yawɛ kɛ Israel ma a so ngɛ lejɛ ɔ be mi nɛ a je Egipt zugba a nɔ kɛ ma a.

english_verse: Now I have built a glorious temple where you can live forever.” Solomon Speaks to the People (
translation_verse: Jehanɛ lɛɛ, i po we saminyayoo ko ha mo nɛ o hi lejɛ ɔ kɛ ya neneene.” Salomo kɛ ma a tu munyu (Kronika II,

english_verse: and said: Praise the Lord God of Israel! Long ago he brought his people out of Egypt. He did not choose a city from any tribe in Israel where his temple would be built, but he kept his promise to make my father David the king of Israel.
translation_verse: ‘Kɛ je be nɛ i je ye ma Israel kɛ je Egipt ɔ, i hla we ma ko ma ko kɛ ji Israel wɛtso ko mi nɛ a po we ha mi nɛ a ja mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Se i hla mo David, nɛ o ye ye ma, Israel ɔ nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: So when David wanted to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel,
