english_verse: In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors. Their advice led to his downfall.
translation_verse: Ahazia pee yayami, ejakaa e tsɛ gbenɔ se ɔ, Ahab weku li ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ woɔ lɛ ga; nɛ mɛ lɛ a kpata e nane.

english_verse: He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Mɛ nɔuu lɛ a wo lɛ ga nɛ e ya piɛ Israel matsɛ, Yoram, Ahab binyumu ɔ he nɛ a kɛ Siria matsɛ, Hazael ya hwu ta ngɛ Ramot nɛ ngɛ Gilead ɔ. Siria bi ɔmɛ plaa Yoram ngɛ ta a mi.

english_verse: and he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. And Ahaziah later went there to visit him.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e kpale e se kɛ ho Yezreel ma a mi ya konɛ e ya tsa e he. Yuda matsɛ, Ahazia, Yehoram binyumu ɔ hu bú e nɔ nɛ e ya slaa lɛ.

english_verse: It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death. When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family,
translation_verse: Se Mawu gu slaami nɛ Ahazia ya slaa Yoram ɔ nɔ nɛ e kɛ kpata Ahazia hɛ mi. Benɛ Ahazia ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, e kɛ Yoram je kpo ya na Nimshi binyumu nɛ a tsɛɛ Yehu ɔ. Lɛ ji nɔ nɛ Yawɛ hla kɛ to nɛ e ba kpata Ahab we ɔ hɛ mi.

english_verse: but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah.
translation_verse: Se Ahazia ngɛ nyɛmiyo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Yehosheba, nɛ gba osɔfo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Yehoyada. Yehosheba ku Ahazia binyumu ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Yoash ɔ kɛ je matsɛbinyumu ɔmɛ nɛ a yaa gbe ɔ a kpɛti. E ngɔ jokuɛ ɔ kɛ jokuɛ ɔ bimɛanyɛ ɔ ya laa ngɛ se tsu ko mi ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ. Kikɛ nɛ ɔ Yehosheba pee kɛ he Yoash yi wami, nɛ Atalia nine sui e nɔ.

english_verse: As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that,
translation_verse: Benɛ Matsɛ Ahazia nyɛ, Atalia na le kaa a gbe e binyumu ɔ, e ha nɛ a kpata Yuda matsɛ we mi bimɛ ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_verse: Yoash hi lejɛ ɔ ngɛ laami tso mi jeha ekpa sɔuu, be mi nɛ Atalia ngɛ manyɛ yee ngɛ zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛmɛ nɛ ɔmɛ ya kpa Yuda ma amɛ tsuo a mi, nɛ a ya kpee Levi bi, kɛ Israel we puɔ nya dali ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ba Yerusalem.

english_verse: Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, bɔ nɛ wa maa pee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Ke osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ ba ní tsumi Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ, a mi dlami etɛ mi kake ma ya bu Yawɛ we ɔ agbo ɔmɛ a nya,

english_verse: Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_verse: Ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ na bua jɔmi; nɛ kɛ je be nɛ a gbe Atalia se ɔ, ma a mi jɔ.

english_verse: After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
translation_verse: Manyɛ Atalia yi nɔ, jeha nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, osɔfo Yehoyada ba na kaa e su be nɛ sa kaa e pee nɔ́ ko. E kɛ asafoatsɛmɛ enuɔ so. Mɛ ji Yeroham bi Azaria, Yehohanan bi Ishmael, Obed bi Azaria, Adaya bi Maaseya, kɛ Zikri bi Elishafat.

english_verse: and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash. Jehoiada said to them: Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king.
translation_verse: Mɛ tsuo a ba bua a he nya ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ, nɛ a kɛ Yoash, matsɛbi ɔ ba so ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Yehoyada de mɛ ke, “Matsɛ ɔ binyumu ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ! Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, lɛ ji nɔ nɛ sa nɛ e ye matsɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ wo si ke David nina maa pee ɔ.

english_verse: one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards.
translation_verse: mi dlami etɛ mi kake ma ya bu ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ, nɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ maa hi sisi tomi agbo ɔ nya. Ma a tsuo ma bua a he nya ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ kue ɔ mi.

english_verse: Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Nɔ ko nɔ ko nɛ ko ya Yawɛ we ɔ kaa ja osɔfohi, kɛ Levi bi nɛ ngɛ sɔmɔe ɔ pɛ; mɛɛ lɛɛ a ma nyɛ maa ya lejɛ ɔ, ejakaa a ngɛ klɔuklɔu. Ma a nɛ piɛ ɔ, mɛɛ a ye Yawɛ mlaa amɛ a nɔ; a ko ya lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
translation_verse: Levi bi ɔmɛ nɛ a bɔle matsɛ ɔ, nɛ a hɛɛ a ta hwumi ní ɔmɛ ngɛ a dɛ mi; he tsuaa he nɛ matsɛ ɔ maa ya a, a kɛ lɛ nɛ ya. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ma hla kaa e maa sɛ Yawɛ we ɔ mi ɔ, a gbe lɛ.”

english_verse: The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty.
translation_verse: Levi bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Yuda ma a pee kaa bɔ nɛ osɔfo Yehoyada fa mɛ ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nihi nɛ ba tsu ní Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ nɛ sa kaa a ya we mi ɔ, osɔfo Yehoyada ha we nɛ a ngmɛɛ a he. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ná we bi babauu, nihi nɛ ma ní tsumi, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ kpa.

english_verse: Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders.
translation_verse: Osɔfo Yehoyada dla Matsɛ David akplɔhi, kɛ tsɛ̃ihi nɛ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ kɛ ha asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
translation_verse: E ngɔ nihi nɛ hɛɛ ta hwumi níhi ngɛ a dɛ mi ɔ ngɔ to Yawɛ we ɔ hɛ mi, kɛ je kɔ nya kake kɛ ya si kɔ nya kake, konɛ a bu matsɛ ɔ he.

english_verse: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
translation_verse: E maa hyɛ ɔ, matsɛ ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ daa si ngɛ titima a he kaa bɔ nɛ kusumi ɔ ngɛ ɔ. Asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ titimati kpali ɔmɛ daa si kɛ bɔle lɛ, nɛ ma a tsuo ngɛ lele hwɔe, nɛ a ngɛ titimati kpae. Lali ɔmɛ hu ngɛ lae, nɛ a ngɛ saku fiae kɛ nyɛɛ ma a hɛ mi kɛ ngɛ nyami ɔ he sɔ woe. Kɛkɛ nɛ Atalia hía tade ɔmɛ ngɛ e he, nɛ e kpa bubuubui, nɛ e de ke, “Nyɛ tsɔ atuã! Nyɛ tsɔ atuã!”

english_verse: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!”
translation_verse: Osɔfo Yehoyada sume kaa a gbe Atalia ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e fa asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ je lɛ kpo kɛ gu buli ɔmɛ a kpɛti; nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ka kaa e ma kpɔ lɛ ɔ, a gbe lɛ.”

english_verse: She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a nu Atalia pani nya kɛ ho matsɛ we ɔ mi ya, nɛ a ya gbe lɛ ngɛ okpɔngɔ agbo ɔ nya. Yehoyada tsake níhi (Matsɛmɛ II,

english_verse: Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ, kɛ ma a, kɛ matsɛ ɔ tsuo so kaa a maa pee Yawɛ ma.

english_verse: then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo ya sɛ Baal jami he ɔ, nɛ a gbɛ lɛ kɛ pue si. A ku bɔ sami la tɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ amaga amɛ dukuduku, nɛ a gbe Baal osɔfo ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Matan ɔ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing.
translation_verse: Yehoyada ngɔ Yawɛ we ɔ ní tsumi ɔ ngɔ wo osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi, konɛ a tsu ní ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ Matsɛ David dla ní tsumi ɔ ngɔ ha mɛ ɔ. Mɛ lɛ a maa sã bɔ ɔmɛ kɛ ha Yawɛ kaa bɔ nɛ a ngma ngɛ Mose mlaa a mi ɔ. Mɛ kɛ̃ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ maa hyɛ lami, kɛ nyami blɔ nya tomi ɔmɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah.
translation_verse: Nyagbe ɔ, osɔfo Yehoyada, asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, ma nimeli ɔmɛ, ma ní tsuli ɔmɛ, kɛ ma a tsuo kpaka matsɛ ɔ kɛ je Yawɛ we ɔ kɛ ba matsɛ we ɔ mi. A gu agbo ngua a mi kɛ ba, nɛ a kɛ matsɛ ɔ ya hi matsɛ sɛ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: While Jehoiada the priest was alive, Joash obeyed the Lord by doing right.
translation_verse: Yoash pee Yawɛ suɔmi nya ní, be mi nɛ osɔfo Yehoyada ngɛ je mi ɔ.

english_verse: Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ kɛ Yehoyada ngɔ sika a kɛ ha nihi nɛ a tu Yawɛ we ɔ dlami ní tsumi ɔ ngɔ wo a dɛ ɔ. Mɛ hu a ya bɔ tɛ gbali, kapitɛhi, dade ga ní tsuli, kɛ akɔblee ga ní tsuli apaa konɛ a ba dla Yawɛ we ɔ.

english_verse: and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple. Joash Turns Away from the Lord
translation_verse: A pu lɛ ngɛ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a pu he ɔ ngɛ David ma a mi. A pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ kɛ wo e hɛ mi nyami ngɛ ní tsumi nɛ e tsu kɛ ha Israel ma a, kɛ Mawu we ɔ he.

english_verse: Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
translation_verse: Yehoyada hla yihi enyɔ kɛ ha Matsɛ Yoash, nɛ Yoash kɛ mɛ fɔ binyumuhi, kɛ biyihi.

english_verse: He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.” But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders.
translation_verse: E fa osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ ke a ya Yuda ma amɛ a mi, nɛ a ya tsu sika ngɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo a dɛ kɛ ba nɛ a kɛ dla Yawɛ we ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ a peeɔ daa jeha a. E de mɛ ke a pee esɔ, se Levi bi ɔmɛ to tsle.

english_verse: So he sent for Jehoiada the high priest and asked, “Why didn't you send the Levites to collect the taxes? The Lord's servant Moses and the people agreed long ago that this tax would be collected and used to pay for the upkeep of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, matsɛ ɔ tsɛ Yehoyada, a nyatsɛ ɔ, nɛ e bi lɛ ke, “Tó ɔ nɛ Yawɛ tsɔlɔ Mose de ke ma a nɛ tsu konɛ a kɛ tsu Yawɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ he ní ɔ, mɛni he je o hyɛ we nɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ ya tsu ngɛ Yuda ma a amɛ a mi, kɛ Yerusalem ɔ?”

english_verse: Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ fa Levi bi ɔmɛ ke a kpɛ daka nɛ a kɛ ma tsu tó ɔ, nɛ a kɛ ma Yawɛ we ɔ agbo ɔ nya.

english_verse: He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
translation_verse: A fiɛ kɛ kpa Yerusalem, kɛ Yuda ma amɛ tsuo a mi ke, tó ɔ nɛ Mawu tsɔlɔ Mose tsu ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ngɔ e nɔ́ kɛ ba ha Yawɛ.

english_verse: The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box.
translation_verse: Sane nɛ ɔ ngɔ ma a, kɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ a nya saminya. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a ngɔ a tó ɔ kɛ ba ba wo daka a mi hluu kɛ ya si e hyi tɔ.

english_verse: Each day, after the Levites took the box into the temple, the king's secretary and the high priest's assistant would dump out the money and count it. Then the empty box would be taken back outside. This happened day after day, and soon a large amount of money was collected.
translation_verse: Daa ligbi ɔ, Levi bi ɔmɛ ma wo daka a kɛ ya ha matsɛ ní tsulɔ ɔ nɛ hyɛɛ nɔ ɔ. Ke daka a hyi ɔ, matsɛ pɛdiyo ɔ, kɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma a tsɔlɔ ko ma je sika a, kɛkɛ a kpale daka a ya ma e ma he ɔ ekohu. Kikɛ nɛ ɔ a pee nɛ a kɛ bua sika babauu nya.

english_verse: These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new.
translation_verse: Ní tsuli ɔmɛ tsuo tsu ní wawɛɛ nitsɛ kɛ ya si a dla Yawɛ we ɔ gbe nya, nɛ a pee lɛ ehe kaa bɔ nɛ e ngɛ sa a.

english_verse: They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple. Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived.
translation_verse: Benɛ a gbe ní tsumi ɔ nya a, a kɛ sika tsu, kɛ sika hiɔ nɛ piɛ ɔ ha matsɛ ɔ, kɛ Yehoyada, nɛ mɛ hu a kɛ pee kpluhi, kɛ ní kpa komɛ kɛ ma Yawɛ we ɔ mi. A tsake Yehoyada blɔ nya tomi ɔmɛ Yehoyada wami be ɔ tsuo ɔ, a sãã bɔhi daa ligbi ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ.

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted.
translation_verse: Se benɛ Yehoyada gbo se ɔ, Yuda ganɔ ɔmɛ ba a he si ha Matsɛ Yoash, nɛ lɛ hu e nu a munyu.

english_verse: The people of Judah soon stopped worshiping in the temple of the Lord God and started worshiping idols and the symbols of the goddess Asherah. These sinful things made the Lord God angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha nɛ a jɔɔ Yawɛ, a nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ we ɔ yami, nɛ a ya ja amagahi, kɛ yo mawu ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Ashera a. Yayami nɛ a pee nɛ ɔ ha nɛ Yawɛ mi mi fu Yuda, kɛ Yerusalem.

english_verse: but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
translation_verse: Yawɛ tsɔ gbali kɛ ba a ngɔ, konɛ a ba kpale mɛ kɛ ba lɛ Yawɛ ɔ ngɔ ekohu; se ma a bui mɛ tue.

english_verse: God's Spirit spoke to Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and Zechariah told everyone that God was saying: “Why are you disobeying me and my laws? This will only bring punishment! You have deserted me, so now I will desert you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Mawu mumi ɔ ba osɔfo Yehoyada binyumu Zakaria nɔ. E ho ya da si ngɛ he nɛ ma a maa na lɛ ngɛ, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Yawɛ Mawu ɔ ngɛ nyɛ bie ke, mɛni he je nyɛ kua e mlaa amɛ a nɔ yemi, nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ haomi ba nyɛ nɔ nɛ ɔ! Nyɛ kua Yawɛ, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, lɛ hu e kua nyɛ!”

english_verse: King Joash forgot that Zechariah's father had always been a loyal friend. So when the people of Judah plotted to kill Zechariah, Joash joined them and gave orders for them to stone him to death in the courtyard of the temple. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “I pray that the Lord will see this and punish all of you.” Joash Is Killed
translation_verse: Matsɛ Yoash hɛ je si himi kpakpa nɛ Zakaria tsɛ Yehoyada kɛ lɛ hi ɔ nɔ, nɛ e gbe e binyumu Zakaria. Benɛ Zakaria miɔ nɛ e ma gbo ɔ, e de ke “Yawɛ nɛ hyɛ nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ pee ɔ nɛ e gbla nyɛ tue!” Yoash matsɛ yemi ɔ nyagbe

english_verse: In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a jeha a nyagbe ɔ, Siria tabo ɔ ba tua Yuda kɛ Yerusalem; a gbe ganɔ ɔmɛ tsuo, nɛ a ngɔ ta yibu ní babauu kɛ ho Damasko ya.

english_verse: The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
translation_verse: Siria tabo ɔ, a he pi kulaa. Se Yawɛ ngɔ Yuda ta buli babauu ɔ ngɔ wo a dɛ mi; ejakaa ma a kua Yawɛ, a nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ. Blɔ nɔ nɛ a gu kɛ gbla Yoash tue ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Joash was severely wounded during the battle, and as soon as the Syrians left Judah, two of his officials, Zabad and Jehozabad, decided to revenge the death of Zechariah. They plotted and killed Joash while he was in bed, recovering from his wounds. Joash was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ so ngɔ wo e he ɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: Zabad, Amon yo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Shimeat ɔ binyumu, kɛ Yehozabad, Moab yo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Shimrit ɔ binyumu.

english_verse: The History of the Kings also tells more about the sons of Joash, what the prophets said about him, and how he repaired the temple. Amaziah son of Joash became king after his father's death.
translation_verse: Yoash binyumu ɔmɛ a he sanehi, gbamihi nɛ a gba kɛ si lɛ, kɛ bɔ nɛ e dla Yawɛ we ɔ nɛ e pee lɛ ehe ekohu ɔ, a ngma ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ Matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a Womi ɔ sisi tsɔɔmi womi ɔ mi. Yoash binyumu Amazia ba ye matsɛ ngɛ e tsɛ ɔ se.

english_verse: One of God's prophets said, “Your Majesty, don't let these Israelite soldiers march into battle with you. The Lord has refused to help anyone from the northern kingdom of Israel,
translation_verse: Se gbalɔ ko ba e ngɔ, nɛ e ba de lɛ ke, “Nɛnɛ, o kɛ Israel tabo ɔ ko ya ta, ejakaa Yawɛ je a se; Yawɛ je Efraim bi nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo a se.

english_verse: Amaziah replied, “What am I supposed to do about all the silver I paid those troops?” “The Lord will give you back even more than you paid,” the prophet answered.
translation_verse: Amazia bi gbalɔ ɔ ke, “Lɛɛ sika hiɔ nɛ jiɔmi ji kilo akpe etɛ kɛ e nya lafa eywiɛ nɛ i ngɔ kɛ ha Israel tabo ɔ, mɛni wa maa pee ngɛ he?” Gbalɔ ɔ he nɔ ke, “Yawɛ ma nyɛ ma ha mo nɔ́ nɛ hiɛ pe ja!”

english_verse: But before the prophet finished speaking, Amaziah interrupted and said, “You're not one of my advisors! Don't say another word, or I'll have you killed.” The prophet stopped. But then he added, “First you sinned and now you've ignored my warning. It's clear that God has decided to punish you!” Israel Defeats Judah (
translation_verse: Se benɛ gbalɔ ɔ ngɛ munyu tue kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ, Amazia po munyu ngɛ e nya, nɛ e bi lɛ ke, “Kɛ je mɛni be lɛ wa wo mo matsɛ ga wolɔ? Jɔɔ mo; ke pi ja a, ma ha a gbe mo piɔ!” Kɛkɛ nɛ gbalɔ ɔ kpa. Se loko e maa pee dii ɔ, e de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ i le kaa Mawu to e yi mi kaa e ma kpata o hɛ mi; ejakaa o bui ye ga womi ɔ tue, nɛ o ya tsu nɔ́ nɛ ɔ.” Amazia kɛ Israel bi hwu ta (Matsɛmɛ II,

english_verse: King Amaziah of Judah talked with his officials, then sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
translation_verse: Yuda matsɛ, Amazia kɛ e ga woli ɔmɛ so kɛ wo Israel he. Ligbi ko ɔ, e tsɔ ya de Israel matsɛ, Yehoash, Yehu bi Yehoahaz bi ɔ ke, “Ba nɛ o kɛ mi ba kpe hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi!”

english_verse: Jehoash sent back a reply that said: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon arranged the marriage between his son and the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
translation_verse: Israel matsɛ, Yehoash hu tsɔ ya de Yuda matsɛ, Amazia ke, “Be ko ɔ, Lebanon mio tso tsɔ ke a ya de Lebanon seda ke, ‘Ngɔɔ o biyo ɔ ngɔ ha ye binyumu ɔ nɛ e kɛ lɛ nɛ hi si!’ Kɛkɛ nɛ Lebanon pu mi lohwe ko ba be, nɛ e naa mio tso ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. But stay at home and do your celebrating. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Mo Amazia, nɛ o gbe Edom bi ɔmɛ he je ɔ, o ngɛ o he nɔ woe. I ngɛ mo ga woe ke o hi si ngɛ o we mi. Mɛni sane o ngɛ hlae nɛ o je ɔ? Anɛ o li kaa nɔ́ nɛ ɔ kɛ haomi maa ba o kɛ o ma Yuda tsuo nyɛ nɔ lo?”

english_verse: so Jehoash led his army to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Israel matsɛ, Yehoash hia nɛ e kɛ Yuda matsɛ Amazia ya bua ngɛ ta nga nɔ, ngɛ Yuda ma a nɛ a tsɛɛ Bet Shemesh ɔ.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Israel ye Yuda nɔ kunimi, nɛ Yuda ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo tu fo kɛ ho a wehi a mi ya.

translation_verse: Israel matsɛ, Yehoash nu Yuda matsɛ Amazia, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ba Yerusalem. Benɛ a ba su Yerusalem ɔ, Yehoash ha nɛ a ku Yerusalem gbogbo ɔ gugue lafa ngɔ pue si kɛ je Efraim agbo ɔ nya, kɛ ya si kɔ nya agbo ɔ nya.

translation_verse: Benɛ e kpale e se kɛ yaa Samaria a, e muɔ ta yibu ní nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ho: sika tsu, sika hiɔ tsuo nɛ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ, ní kpahi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ nɛ Obed Edom nina a hyɛɛ a nɔ ɔ, kɛ june ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ. Yehoash nuu ni komɛ hu kaa ta nyɔguɛhi kɛ je.

english_verse: Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Amazia he sane kpahi kɛ je sisije kɛ ya si e matsɛ yemi ɔ nyagbe ɔ, a ngma lɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ ngɛ Yuda Matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ Israel Matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a Blema Sanehi Womi ɔ mi.

english_verse: As soon as Amaziah started disobeying the Lord, some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there.
translation_verse: Kɛ je be mi nɛ Amazia je Yawɛ se ɔ, e ma mi bi ɔmɛ so ngɔ wo e he ngɛ Yerusalem. Nyagbenyagbe ɔ, e tu fo kɛ ho Lakish ma a mi ya; se e he nyɛli ɔmɛ nyɛɛ e se, nɛ a ya gbe lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Uzziah supplied his army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones used for slinging.
translation_verse: Uzia ha e ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo ta hwumi ní nɛ ɔmɛ: tsɛ̃i, akplɔ, dade pɛɛ, dade dama, kɛ̃ɛ̃, kɛ amlami tɛ.

english_verse: Uzziah had leprosy the rest of his life. He was no longer allowed in the temple or in his own palace. That's why his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: He womi nɔ hiɔ nɛ ɔ ngɛ Matsɛ Uzia he hluu kɛ ya si e gbenɔ ligbi. E ho ya hi lɛ nitsɛ e we ɔ mi, ejakaa a tsi e nya ke e ko ya Yawɛ we ɔ hu. A he e ní tsumi ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ e dɛ, nɛ e binyumu Yotam ba ye e nane mi kɛ hyɛ ma a nɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Uzziah did while he was king is in the records written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Uzia he sane kpahi nɛ piɛ, kɛ je sisije kɛ ya si nyagbe ɔ, gbalɔ Yesaya, Amoz binyumu ɔ ngma lɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Some of his skilled workers invented machines that could shoot arrows and sling large stones. Uzziah set these up in Jerusalem at his defense towers and at the corners of the city wall. God helped Uzziah become more and more powerful, and he was famous all over the world. Uzziah Becomes Too Proud
translation_verse: E ha nɛ e ga ní tsuli kpanaa amɛ pee klama komɛ ngɛ Yerusalem. A kɛ klama amɛ ma mɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ gbogbo kɔ̃ nya amɛ a nɔ, konɛ a kɛ tsɛ̃ kɛ̃ɛ̃, nɛ a kɛ kpɛne tɛ agboagbohi kɛ je lejɛ ɔmɛ. E matsɛ yemi ɔ he si, nɛ e biɛ pɛ kɛ ya lokoo, ejakaa Mawu piɛ e he. A gbla Uzia tue

english_verse: God helped him defeat the Philistines, the Arabs living in Gur-Baal, and the Meunites.
translation_verse: Mawu piɛ e he nɛ e kɛ ye Filisti bi, Arabia bi nɛ ngɛ Gurbaal ɔ, kɛ Meun bi ɔmɛ a nɔ kunimi.

english_verse: After the death of King Amaziah, the people of Judah crowned his son Uzziah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Uzia ba bɔni tsɛ yemi benɛ e ye jeha nyɔngma kɛ ekpa, nɛ e hi Yerusalem kɛ ye matsɛ jeha nyingmi enuɔ kɛ enyɔ. E nyɛ biɛ ji Yekolia, nɛ e je Yerusalem.

english_verse: Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall. One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him.
translation_verse: Se benɛ Uzia tsɛ yemi ɔ ba he si ɔ, e wo e he nɔ, nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha nɛ e hɛ mi kpata. E ya sã tsopa kɛ e he via ngɛ tsopa kɛ e he via sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ, nɛ e kɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ tɔ̃ Yawɛ, e Mawu ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: He obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: Uzia ya wo e tsɛ nane, nɛ e pee Yawɛ suɔmi nya ní.

english_verse: Zechariah was Uzziah's advisor and taught him to obey God. And so, as long as Zechariah was alive, Uzziah was faithful to God, and God made him successful.
translation_verse: Be mi nɛ Zakaria ngɛ je mi ɔ, Uzia sɔmɔ Yawɛ kɛ e tsui tsuo; enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Yawɛ hu gbaa lɛ. Zakaria ji nɔ nɛ tsɔɔ Uzia Mawu gbeye yemi.

english_verse: While Uzziah was king, he started a war against the Philistines. He smashed the walls of the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, then rebuilt towns around Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia.
translation_verse: Uzia kɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ ya hwu ta. E ku Gat, Yamnia, kɛ Ashdod gbogbo ɔmɛ kɛ pue si; nɛ e po mahi ngɛ Ashdod kasa nya, kɛ Filisti bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɛ piɛ ɔ tsuo nɔ.

english_verse: Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
translation_verse: Amon bi ɔmɛ tsuɔ tó kɛ haa Uzia. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha nɛ e matsɛ yemi ɔ ba he si, nɛ e biɛ pɛ wawɛɛ nitsɛ kɛ ya su Egipt tɔɔ.

english_verse: In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward.
translation_verse: Uzia fia gbogbo ngɔ wo Yerusalem he, nɛ e ma mɔ gagaagahi ngɛ kɔ̃ nya agbo ɔ, kɛ kɔ̃ agbo ɔ a nɔ, kɛ he nɛ gbogbo ɔ lɔgɔ si ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: He also built defense towers out in the desert. He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
translation_verse: E ma mɔhi ngɛ nga a nɔ hulɔ, nɛ e tsua vuhi fuu, ejakaa e ngɛ lohwehi babauu ngɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi, kɛ nga a nɔ. Akɛnɛ e suɔ humi he je ɔ, e wo e ma mi bi ɔmɛ he wami, nɛ a hu wai ngmɔhi ngɛ yoku ɔmɛ a nɔ, kɛ kɔ̃ ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials.
translation_verse: Uzia ngɛ ta buli babauu nɛ a tsɔse mɛ, nɛ a mia kɛ ha ta hwumi. A dla ta buli ɔmɛ ngɔ wo kuuhi a mi. Ni nɛmɛ nɛ pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ji matsɛ pɛdiyo Yeyel, e setsɔ Maaseya, kɛ a nyatsɛ Hanania, matsɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty, this isn't right! You are not allowed to burn incense to the Lord. That must be done only by priests who are descendants of Aaron. You will have to leave! You have sinned against the Lord, and so he will no longer bless you.”
translation_verse: nɛ a ya tsi e nya. A de lɛ ke, “Uzia, o be he blɔ nɛ o sãã tsopa kɛ e he via kɛ haa Yawɛ. Osɔfo ɔmɛ, nɛ ji Aaron nina a, mɛ pɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ a hla ngɔ to nɛ a tsu nɔ́ nɛ ɔ. Jee he klɔuklɔu nɛ ɔ. O tɔ̃ Yawɛ Mawu ɔ nɔ, nɛ e gbaami be o nɔ hu.”

english_verse: Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead!
translation_verse: Uzia daa si ngɛ tsopa kɛ e he via bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ kasa nya ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ kɛ e dɛ mi ngɛyu. E mi mi fu osɔfo ɔmɛ; kɛkɛ nɛ he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya ba pue e hɛ nya amlɔ nɔuu.

english_verse: Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
translation_verse: Benɛ Azaria, kɛ osɔfo kpa amɛ na hiɔ ɔ ngɛ e hɛ nya a, a tsitsɛɛ e yi se kɛ je Yawɛ we ɔ. Lɛ nitsɛ hu e he sɔ kɛ je kpo, ejakaa Yawɛ gbla e tue.

english_verse: Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_verse: Uzia ba gbo nɛ a pu lɛ ngɛ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a pu he ɔ; se e hiɔ ɔ he je ɔ, a pu we lɛ ngɛ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a yɔkɔ ɔmɛ eko mi. E binyumu Yotam ba ye matsɛ ngɛ e se.

english_verse: Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Yotam pee Yawɛ suɔmi nya ní kaa bɔ nɛ e tsɛ Uzia pee ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ; se lɛɛ e ya sɛ̃ tsopa kɛ e he via ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ. Se kɛ̃ ɔ, ma a ya nɔ pee yayami.

english_verse: Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
translation_verse: Yotam matsɛ yemi ɔ ba he si, ejakaa e bu Yawɛ, e Mawu ɔ tue ngɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ mi.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Yotam he sane kpahi nɛ piɛ, tahi nɛ e hwu, kɛ bɔ nɛ e to níhi a blɔ nya ha a, a ngma lɛ tsuo ngɛ Israel kɛ Yuda Matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a Blema Sanehi Womi ɔ mi.

english_verse: He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Yotam ba gbo nɛ a pu lɛ ngɛ David ma a mi, nɛ e binyumu Ahaz ba ye matsɛ ngɛ e se.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees. Syria and Israel Attack Judah (
translation_verse: Ahaz sã bɔ, kɛ tsopa kɛ e he via ngɛ jami he ɔmɛ, yoku ɔmɛ a nɔ, kɛ tsohi nɛ a bɔ kusuu ɔ a sisi. Ahaz kɛ Siria kɛ Israel hwu ta (Matsɛmɛ II,

english_verse: So Tiglath Pileser came to Judah, but instead of helping, he made things worse.
translation_verse: Se benɛ Asiria matsɛ, Tiglat Pileser ba a, e ba piɛ we Matsɛ Ahaz he; e ba hao lɛ mohu.

english_verse: and he offered sacrifices in Hinnom Valley. Worst of all, Ahaz sacrificed his own sons, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: E sã tsopa kɛ e he via ngɛ Hinom kɔ̃ ɔ mi. Pi lɔ ɔ kɛkɛ. E kɛ lɛ nitsɛ e bimɛ po sã sami bɔhi kɛ ha amagahi kaa bɔ nɛ je ma amɛ nɛ Yawɛ fie kɛ je Israel bi ɔmɛ a blɔ mi ɔ pee ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz and the people of Judah sinned and turned away from the Lord, the God their ancestors had worshiped. So the Lord punished them by letting their enemies defeat them. The king of Syria attacked Judah and took many of its people to Damascus as prisoners. King Pekah of Israel later defeated Judah and killed
translation_verse: Akɛnɛ Matsɛ Ahaz pee yayami he je ɔ, Yawɛ, e Mawu ɔ ha nɛ Siria matsɛ ɔ ba ye e nɔ kunimi, nɛ e nuu Yuda bi babauu nyɔguɛ kɛ ho Damasko ya. Jehanɛ hu, Yawɛ ha nɛ Israel matsɛ, Peka, Remalia binyumu ɔ ba ye Ahaz nɔ, nɛ e gbe Yuda ta buli kpakpahi akpe lafa kɛ nyingmi enyɔ ligbi kake. Yawɛ, a nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ ngmɛ blɔ nɛ a pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, ejakaa Yuda ma a kua lɛ.

english_verse: If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, nyɛ to kaa nyɛ maa pee nyumuhi kɛ yihi nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem kɛ Yuda a nyɛ nyɔguɛhi. Anɛ nyɛ li kaa nyɛ hu nyɛ pee yayamihi kɛ si Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ lo?

english_verse: About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong,
translation_verse: Efraim nikɔtɔma eywiɛ komɛ hu nɔ́ nɛ ta buli ɔmɛ pee ɔ ngɔɛ a nya. Mɛ ji Yehohanan binyumu Azaria, Meshilemot binyumu Berekia, Shalum binyumu Yehizkia, kɛ Hadlai binyumu Amasa.

english_verse: and they said: If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
translation_verse: A de ta buli ɔmɛ ke, “Nyɛ ko ngɔ ta nyɔguɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ! Wɔ nitsɛmɛ hu wa pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ; wa wo e mi mi la, nɛ tue gblami fɔɔ si ha wɔ momo. Jehanɛ, nyɛ pa ngɛ pee konɛ wa yayami ɔ nɛ hiɛ kɛ be nɔ!”

english_verse: So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ ta buli ɔmɛ ngɔ ta nyɔguɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ ta yibu ní ɔmɛ ngɔ wo ma a, kɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.

english_verse: The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria. translation_verse: A hla ni eywiɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a wo a biɛ ta a ke a hyɛ ta nyɔguɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ. Nihi tsuo nɛ hɛɛ a he gu, nɛ e hia kaa a ha mɛ bo nɛ a bu ɔ, a ha mɛ bo; ni nɛmɛ nɛ e hia kaa a ha mɛ tade nɛ a wo hu, a ha mɛ tade. Ta yibu ní ɔmɛ nɛ a ha a ekomɛ ji bo ɔmɛ, kɛ tade ɔmɛ ɔ nɛ. english_verse: Some time later, the Edomites attacked the eastern part of Judah again and carried away prisoners. And at the same time, the Philistines raided towns in the western foothills and in the Southern Desert. They conquered the towns of Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, including the villages around them. Then some of the Philistines went to live in these places. Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria and begged for help.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, Filisti bi ɔmɛ hu ba tua mahi nɛ ngɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi ngɛ bonyoku je ɔ, kɛ mahi nɛ ngɛ Yuda leneyi je ɔ. Filisti bi ɔmɛ ngɔ ma nɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ a hi a mi: Bet Shemesh, Aiyalon, kɛ Gederot. A ngɔ Soko kɛ Timna, kɛ Gimzo, kɛ kɔpehi nɛ bɔle ma nɛ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning.
translation_verse: Yuda matsɛ, Ahaz he ɔ, Yawɛ kɛ haomi ba Yuda ma a tsuo nɔ; ejakaa Ahaz ngmɛɛ ma a he kɛ fɔ si, nɛ e pee yayami babauu hu kɛ si Yawɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz. The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
translation_verse: Ahaz ya muɔ sika tsu ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ, matsɛ we ɔ, kɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ a we ɔmɛ a mi, nɛ e kɛ ha Asiria matsɛ ɔ. Se kɛ̃ ɔ, Tiglat Pileser piɛ we e he. Ahaz he yayamihi

english_verse: Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before.
translation_verse: Kikɛmɛ a Matsɛ Ahaz nɛ ɔ, benɛ e yi ba fi wawɛɛ nitsɛ po, e pee yayami babauu kɛ si Yawɛ pe kekle ɔ.

english_verse: He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
translation_verse: E sãã bɔhi kɛ haa Siria mawu ɔmɛ nɛ ba ye e nɔ kunimi ɔ. E deɔ ke, “Siria mawu ɔmɛ piɛɔ Siria matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a he. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke i sã bɔ kɛ ha mɛ ɔ, a maa piɛ imi hu ye he.” Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ kɛ haomi ba e kɛ e ma a tsuo nɔ.

english_verse: Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ahaz bua Yawɛ we ɔ mi ní ɔmɛ tsuo a nya, nɛ e ywia mɛ dukuduku. E ngmɛ Yawɛ we ɔ nya; nɛ e ma bɔ sami la tɛhi ngɛ he tsuaa he ngɛ Yerusalem.

english_verse: In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
translation_verse: E po jami hehi ngɛ Yuda mahi, kɛ kɔpehi tsuo a mi, konɛ a sã tsopa kɛ e he via ngɛ lejɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ha ma se mawuhi. Bɔ nɛ e pee kɛ wo Yawɛ, e nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ mi mi la ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Ahaz he sane kpahi nɛ piɛ, kɛ je e matsɛ yemi ɔ sisije kɛ ya si nyagbe ɔ, a ngma lɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ ngɛ Yuda kɛ Israel Matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a Blema Sanehi Womi ɔ mi.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Ahaz ba gbo, nɛ a pu lɛ ngɛ Yerusalem; se a pu we lɛ ngɛ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a pu he ɔ. E bi Hezekia ba ye matsɛ ngɛ e se.

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done. The Temple Is Purified
translation_verse: Hezekia ya wo e nɛ̃ David nane, nɛ e pee Yawɛ suɔmi nya ní. A tsukɔ Yawɛ we ɔ he

english_verse: they went back to Hezekiah and said: Your Majesty, we have finished our work. The entire temple is now pure again, and so is the altar and its utensils, as well as the table for the sacred loaves of bread and its utensils.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ ba Matsɛ Hezekia ngɔ, nɛ a ba bɔ lɛ amaniɛ ke, “Wa pee kusumi kɛ tsukɔ Yawɛ we ɔ tsuo gbe nya. La tɛ ɔ nɛ a sãã sami bɔ ngɛ nɔ ɔ, kɛ okplɔɔ ɔ nɛ a kɛ abolo klɔuklɔu ɔ maa nɔ ɔ, kɛ a he ní ɔmɛ tsuo, wa tsukɔ a he.

english_verse: Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan.
translation_verse: Mlaahi nɛ Yawɛ wo Matsɛ David kɛ gu lɛ David ɔ gbalɔ Gad, kɛ gbalɔ Natan a nɔ ɔ, Matsɛ Hezekia ye mlaa amɛ a nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. E ngɔ Levi bi ɔmɛ ya da si ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ kɛ a dɛ mi gɔgɔhi, bɛhi, kɛ sakuhi

english_verse: After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Matsɛ Hezekia kɛ ma a tsuo kpla si nɛ a ja Mawu.

english_verse: Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple
translation_verse: E kpee osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ kɛ ba kue ɔ mi ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ beleku je,

english_verse: and said: It's time to purify the temple of the Lord God of our ancestors. You Levites must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean, then go into the temple and bring out everything that is unclean and unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: nɛ e kɛ mɛ ba tu munyu ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. E de mɛ ke, “Nyɛ Levi bi, nyɛɛ bu mi tue! Nyɛɛ tsukɔ nyɛ he, nɛ nyɛɛ tsukɔ Yawɛ, nyɛ nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ we ɔ hu he. Nyɛ je nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ bleɔ Yawɛ we ɔ kɛ je hiɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple.
translation_verse: Wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ yi Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ anɔkuale; a pee yayami kɛ si lɛ. A kua Yawɛ, nɛ e we ɔ hu a yɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ a ya ja lɛ.

english_verse: They locked the doors, then let the lamps go out and stopped burning incense and offering sacrifices to him.
translation_verse: A nga Yawɛ we ɔ sinya amɛ, nɛ a gbe kane ɔmɛ. Tsopa kɛ e he via, kɛ sami bɔ pohu a kpa sami ngɛ Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ we ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord became terribly angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and everyone was shocked and horrified at what he did to punish them. Not only were
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Yawɛ mi mi fu Yuda kɛ Yerusalem, nɛ nɔ́ nɛ e pee mɛ ɔ ha nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ he mi po, nɛ a ye gbeye. Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ na nɔ́ nɛ ɔ kɛ nyɛ hɛngmɛ.

english_verse: our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
translation_verse: Wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɔ ngɛ ta mi, nɛ wa yi ɔmɛ, kɛ wa bimɛ ɔmɛ lɛɛ a nuu mɛ nyɔguɛ kɛ je.

english_verse: So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us.
translation_verse: “Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, i to ye yi mi kaa i kɛ Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ maa so, konɛ e mi mi nɛ fu wɔ wawɛɛ ɔ se nɛ po.

english_verse: Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ye bimɛ! Nyɛ ko puɛ be ko hu. Nyɛ ji nihi nɛ Yawɛ hla nɛ nyɛɛ sã tsopa kɛ e he via kɛ ha lɛ. Yawɛ hla nyɛ nɛ nyɛɛ nyɛɛ ma a hɛ mi kɛ sɔmɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: When Hezekiah finished talking, the following Levite leaders went to work: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the Kohath clan; Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel from the Merari clan; Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah from the Gershon clan; Shimri and Jeuel from the Elizaphan clan; Zechariah and Mattaniah from the Asaph clan; Jehuel and Shimei from the Heman clan; Shemaiah and Uzziel from the Jeduthun clan.
translation_verse: Levi bi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ jamɛ a be ɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: Kohat weku: Amasai binyumu Mahat, kɛ Azaria binyumu Yoel. Merari weku: Abdi binyumu Kish, kɛ Yehalelel binyumu Azaria. Gershon weku: Zimna binyumu Yoa, kɛ Yoa binyumu Eden. Elizafan weku: Shimri kɛ Yeuel. Asaf weku: Zakaria kɛ Matania. Heman weku: Yehuel kɛ Shimei. Yedutun weku: Shemaya kɛ Uziel.

english_verse: These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.
translation_verse: Nyumu nɛ ɔmɛ ya bua a nyɛmimɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ a nya, nɛ mɛ tsuo a tsukɔ a he. Kɛkɛ ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ matsɛ ɔ fa mɛ ke a pee ngɛ Yawɛ munyu ɔ nya a, a bɔni Yawɛ we ɔ he tsukɔmi.

english_verse: The priests went into the temple and carried out everything that was unclean. They put these things in the courtyard, and from there, the Levites carried them outside the city to Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Osɔfo ɔmɛ ya sɛ Yawɛ we ɔ mi nɛ a tsukɔ lejɛ ɔ. A muɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ he tsɔ we kɛ je lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba kue ɔ mi. Levi bi ɔmɛ hu muɔ ní ɔmɛ kɛ je kpo nɛ a ya sake ngɔ pue Kidron pa a mi.

english_verse: The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month
translation_verse: A je ní tsumi ɔ sisi ngɛ kekleekle nyɔhiɔ ɔ we kekleekle ligbi ɔ nɔ. Ligbi kpaanyɔne ɔ, a ya su kue ɔ nɛ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ hɛ mi ɔ he. A tsu ní ligbi kpaanyɔ kɛ piɛ he. Nɛ nyɔhiɔ ɔ we ligbi nɛ ji nyɔngma kɛ ekpa a, a tsukɔ Yawɛ we ɔ tsuo he gbe nya. A bli Yawɛ we ɔ nya ekohu

english_verse: And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar. Worship in the Temple
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, ní klɔuklɔuhi tsuo nɛ Matsɛ Ahaz hɛ ngɔ fɔ he benɛ e kpa Yawɛ se nyɛɛmi ɔ, wa bua tsuo nya nɛ wa pee mɛ klɔuklɔu ekohu. Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, ní ɔmɛ pueɔ si ngɛ Yawɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ hɛ mi.”

english_verse: At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Matsɛ Hezekia pee esɔ ya kpee ma nimeli ɔmɛ, nɛ e kɛ mɛ tsuo ya sɛ Yawɛ we ɔ mi.

english_verse: They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
translation_verse: A ngɔ na ku kpaago, agbosu kpaago, jijɔ kpaago, kɛ to akpakpo kpaago kɛ ya sã yayami pami bɔ kɛ ha matsɛ ɔ, Yawɛ we ɔ, kɛ Yuda ma a. Matsɛ ɔ fa osɔfo ɔmɛ, nɛ ji Aaron nina a ke a gbe lohwe ɔmɛ nɛ a kɛ sã bɔ ngɛ Yawɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals.
translation_verse: Nyagbe ɔ, a ngɔ to akpakpo ɔmɛ kɛ ba matsɛ ɔ kɛ ma a tsuo a hɛ mi, nɛ a ngɔ a nine ngɔ pue a nɔ.

english_verse: The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, osɔfo ɔmɛ gbe to akpakpo ɔmɛ, nɛ a kɛ a muɔ ɔ pue bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ kaa yayami pami bɔ kɛ ha Israel ma a tsuo; ejakaa matsɛ ɔ fa ke a sã sami bɔ, kɛ yayami pami bɔ kɛ ha Israel tsuo.

english_verse: The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
translation_verse: nɛ ngɛ kaa matsɛ David ní ɔmɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Osɔfo ɔmɛ hu daa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ a titimati ɔmɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Hezekia fa ke a sã sami bɔ ɔ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ. Benɛ a bɔni bɔ ɔ sami pɛ, ma a la kɛ je Yawɛ yi; titimati kpali ɔmɛ kpa titimati, nɛ saku fiali ɔmɛ hu fia saku.

english_verse: Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ, kɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ fa Levi bi ɔmɛ ke, yi jemi lahi nɛ David, kɛ gbalɔ Asaf po ɔ, a la jamɛ a la amɛ kɛ je Yawɛ yi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, be mi nɛ a kpla si nɛ a ngɛ Mawu jae ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ la kɛ bua jɔmi.

english_verse: Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.” The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices.
translation_verse: Hezekia de ma a ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ nyɛ pee nyɛ he klɔuklɔu. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ ngɔ bɔhi, kɛ sina bɔ ba ha Yawɛ.” A pee ja, nɛ a ti ni komɛ je a tsui mi faa nɛ a ngɔ lohwehi kɛ ba konɛ a kɛ sã sami bɔhi.

english_verse: There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned.
translation_verse: Akɛnɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ a he pi bɔ nɛ a ma nyɛ maa gbe lohwe nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo he je ɔ, a nyɛmimɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ ba piɛ a he kɛ tsu ní ɔ kɛ ya si a gbe nya. Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, osɔfo ɔmɛ babauu pee a he klɔuklɔu. .

english_verse: Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar. So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Ngɛ lohwehi babauu nɛ a ngɔ kɛ ba sã sami bɔ ɔmɛ a se ɔ, a kɛ zɔ ba sã tue mi jɔmi bɔ, nɛ a ngɔ wai bɔhi hu kɛ piɛ sami bɔ ɔmɛ a he. Bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a bɔni Yawɛ jami ngɛ e we ɔ mi ekohu ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Hezekia kɛ ma a tsuo na bua jɔmi, ejakaa Mawu piɛ a he kɛ tsu ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ be kuku mi.

english_verse: Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a to kaa á ya kpee Israel bi ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ba Yerusalem, konɛ a ba ye Hetsɔmi ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ mlaa a tsɔɔ ɔ. Á je Dan ngɛ omleyi je, kɛ Beersheba ngɛ leneyi je kɛ ba, nɛ a he nɛ hiɛ babauu pe bɔ nɛ a baa daa a.

english_verse: Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter: People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. If you do this, he will stop being angry.
translation_verse: Tsɔli ɔmɛ ngɔ matsɛ ɔ, kɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ a sɛ gbi ɔ kɛ ya kpa Israel kɛ Yuda tsuo, nɛ a de ke, “Israel ma! Asiria bi ba tua nyɛ, nɛ nyɛ je a dɛ mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ kpale kɛ ba Yawɛ, Abraham, Isak, kɛ Yakob a Mawu ɔ ngɔ, konɛ lɛ hu e kpale nɛ e he nyɛ.

english_verse: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry,
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko wa tue kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ pee ɔ; mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ bu Yawɛ tue. Nyɛɛ ba Yawɛ we ɔ ngɛ Yerusalem, we nɛ e pee klɔuklɔu kɛ yaa neneene ɔ. Nyɛ ba ja lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, konɛ e mi mi nɛ fu nyɛ wawɛɛ ɔ se nɛ po.

english_verse: and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
translation_verse: Ke nyɛ kpale kɛ ba Yawɛ ngɔ ɔ, nyɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ nyɛ bimɛ ɔmɛ a ní maa pee nihi nɛ ba nuu mɛ nyɔguɛ kɛ ho ɔ mɔbɔ. A maa ngmɛɛ a he, nɛ a maa kpale kɛ ba we ekohu. Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ mi mi jɔ, nɛ e naa mɔbɔ. Ke nyɛ kpale kɛ ba e ngɔ ɔ, e ma he nyɛ atuu.”

english_verse: Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Se kɛ̃ ɔ, Asher, Manase, kɛ Zebulun bi ɔmɛ a ti nihi bɔɔ ba a he si, nɛ a kplɛɛ kaa a maa ba Yerusalem.

english_verse: In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread.
translation_verse: Nyɔhiɔ nɛ ji enyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, nihi babauu nitsɛ ba bua a he nya ngɛ Yerusalem konɛ a ye Abolokplolo nyami be ɔ.

english_verse: Most of the people that came from Ephraim, West Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not made themselves clean, but they ignored God's Law and ate the Passover lambs anyway. Hezekiah found out what they had done and prayed, “Lord God, these people are unclean according to the laws of holiness. But they are worshiping you, just as their ancestors did. So, please be kind and forgive them.”
translation_verse: “Yawɛ, wa nɛmɛ a Mawu nɛ o naa mɔbɔ lee! Nihi tsuo nɛ a ngɛ mo jae kɛ a tsui tsuo, se kɛ̃ ɔ a he tsɔ we ɔ, ngɔɔ a he yayami ɔmɛ kɛ pa mɛ.”

english_verse: The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments.
translation_verse: Israel bi nɛ bua a he nya ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ ye Abolokplolo nyami be ɔ ligbi kpaago sɔuu kɛ bua jɔmi nɛ nya wa. Daa ligbi ɔ, Levi bi ɔmɛ, kɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ fiaa kpa saku, nɛ a laa kɛ jeɔ Yawɛ yi kɛ a tsui tsuo.

english_verse: Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration. The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Hezekia je Levi bi ɔmɛ a yi wawɛɛ nitsɛ, ejakaa a je a he kpo kaa nihi nɛ le Yawɛ sɔmɔmi ní tsumi ɔ saminya. A ye Hetsɔmi ɔ si enyɔne Ma a ye Abolokplolo nyami be ɔ ligbi kpaago sɔuu; a sã tue mi jɔmi bɔhi, nɛ a na Yawɛ, a nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ si. Ligbi kpaago ɔmɛ a se ɔ,

english_verse: Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Nɔ tsuaa nɔ bua jɔ e he; Yuda bi ɔmɛ, osɔfo ɔmɛ, Levi bi ɔmɛ, nihi nɛ je omleyi je kɛ ba a, kɛ nibwɔhi nɛ ngɛ Israel kɛ Yuda a.

english_verse: It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David.
translation_verse: Yerusalem ma a mi pee hoo kɛ nyami sɔuu, ejakaa kɛ je Matsɛ Salomo, David binyumu ɔ yi nɔ ɔ, nɔ́ ko kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ bɛ hyɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah divided the priests and Levites into groups, according to their duties. Then he assigned them the responsibilities of offering sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He also appointed people to serve at the temple and to sing praises at the temple gates.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Hezekia kpale dla ní tsumi kɛ ha osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ kɛ e ní tsumi pɔtɛɛ. Ní tsumi slɔɔto ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: sami bɔ sami, tue mi jɔmi bɔ sami, sɔmɔmi ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ, kɛ Yawɛ yi jemi kɛ si nami.

english_verse: The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
translation_verse: A kane osɔfo ɔmɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ, a bimɛ tsɔwitsɔwi ɔmɛ, a yi ɔmɛ, a binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ a biyi ɔmɛ; ejakaa mɛɛ lɛɛ be tsuaa be ɔ, e sa kaa a dla a he kɛ ha a ní tsumi klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ a tsumi.

english_verse: He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, matsɛ ɔ fa Yerusalem ma mi bi ɔmɛ ke a ngɔ osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ a blɔ nya ní ɔmɛ ba ha mɛ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a ngɔ a juɛmi tsuo kɛ fɔ a ní tsumi ɔmɛ a nɔ kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ mlaa a tsɔɔ ɔ.

english_verse: After the Festival, the people went to every town in Judah and smashed the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. They destroyed all the local shrines and foreign altars in Judah, as well as those in the territories of Benjamin, Ephraim, and West Manasseh. Then everyone went home. Offerings for the Priests and Levites
translation_verse: Benɛ a ye nyami be ɔmɛ ta a, Israel bi tsuo nɛ ba lejɛ ɔ pue nɔ kɛ ho Yuda ma amɛ a mi ya. A gbɛ jami he ɔmɛ; a ku amagahi nɛ a puɛ kɛ ha yo mawu ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Ashera a ngɔ pue si, nɛ a ywia bɔ sami la tɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ jami he ɔmɛ ngɛ Yuda ma amɛ tsuo a mi. A tsu kikɛmɛ a ní nɛ ɔ nɔuu ngɛ Benyamin, Efraim, kɛ Manase zugba amɛ a nɔ, loko a kpale kɛ ho a wehi a mi ya ngɛ a mahi a mi.

english_verse: Hezekiah provided animals from his own herds and flocks to use for the morning and evening sacrifices, as well as for the sacrifices during the Sabbath celebrations, the New Moon Festivals, and the other religious feasts required by the Law of the Lord.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ nitsɛ ha lohwehi nɛ a kɛ sã sami bɔhi daa mɔtu kɛ gbɔkuɛ. E ha lohwehi nɛ a kɛ sã bɔ Hejɔɔmi ligbi, Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be, kɛ nyami be kpahi kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ mlaa a tsɔɔ ɔ.

english_verse: As soon as the people heard what the king wanted, they brought a tenth of everything they owned, including their best grain, wine, olive oil, honey, and other crops.
translation_verse: Benɛ a fa kikɛ nɛ ɔ pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ nike ní nɛ ɔmɛ ba babauu nitsɛ: blɛfo kpokploku, wai, oliv nu, hwo, kɛ ngmɔ niba ní kpahi. Jehanɛ, níhi tsuo nɛ ngɛ a dɛ ɔ, a ngɔ a mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka hu kɛ ba.

english_verse: The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Yuda ma amɛ a mi ɔ, ngɔ a na amɛ, kɛ a jijɔ ɔmɛ a mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka kɛ ba. A ngɔ nike níhi hu babauu kɛ ba, nɛ a ba pee mɛ klɔuklɔu kɛ ha Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ.

english_verse: The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later.
translation_verse: Nyɔhiɔ etɛne ɔ mi ɔ, a bɔni nike ní ɔmɛ tomi kuukuu kɛ pue si; nɛ nyɔhiɔ nɛ ji kpaago ɔ mi ɔ, a gbe nya.

english_verse: When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
translation_verse: Benɛ Matsɛ Hezekia, kɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ ba na nike ní babauu nɛ a kɛ ba a, a je Yawɛ kɛ e ma Israel ɔ a yi.

english_verse: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ bi osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ nike ní ɔmɛ a he sane,

english_verse: The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
translation_verse: nɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma Azaria, Zadok nina a de lɛ ke, “Kɛ je be nɛ ma a kɛ nike ní ɔmɛ bɔni Yawɛ we ɔ mi bami ɔ, wa yeɔ ní nɛ wa tɔɔ, nɛ babauu piɛɔ ngɛ se. Niinɛ, Yawɛ gbaa e ma a babauu nitsɛ, nɛ nɔ́ nɛ a ye nɛ piɛ ɔ ji níhi nɛ pueɔ si ngɛ hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed,
translation_verse: Hezekia fa ke a dla nito hehi ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ. Benɛ a pee ja a,

english_verse: all the extra offerings were taken there. Hezekiah and Azariah then appointed Conaniah the Levite to be in charge of these storerooms. His brother Shimei was his assistant, and the following Levites worked with them: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah.
translation_verse: A he piɛli ji ni nyɔngma nɛ ɔmɛ: Yehiel, Azazia, Nahat, Asahel, Yerimot, Yozabad, Eliel, Ismakia, Mahat, kɛ Benaya. Matsɛ Hezekia, kɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa Azaria ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ to kikɛmɛ a blɔ nya nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: Kore son of Imnah was assigned to guard the East Gate, and he was put in charge of receiving the offerings voluntarily given to God and of dividing them among the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Nike ní ɔmɛ nɛ a kɛ ba ha Yawɛ, nɛ ji bɔhi nɛ je tsui mi faa a, nɔ nɛ a to nɛ ma he ngɛ ma a dɛ, nɛ lɛ nɔuu e maa dla ji Imna binyumu Kore, Levi no ɔ. Kore ji Yawɛ we ɔ beleku je agbo ɔ nya buli ɔmɛ a nɔkɔtɔma.

english_verse: He had six assistants who were responsible for seeing that all the priests in the other towns of Judah also got their share of these offerings. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah. Every priest and every Levite over
translation_verse: se pi ngɛ weku nya. Nyumuhi tsuo nɛ ye jeha nyingmi etɛɛtɛ, loo nɔ́ nɛ pe ja, nɛ a ya sɔmɔɔ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ mi daa ligbi ɔ, a dla niye ní ha mɛ hulɔ kaa bɔ nɛ blɔ nya nɛ a hɛɛ ɔ tsɔɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah also appointed other men to take food and supplies to the priests and Levites whose homes were in the pastureland around the towns of Judah. But the priests had to be descendants of Aaron, and the Levites had to be listed in the official records.
translation_verse: Osɔfohi nɛ ngɛ mahi nɛ a ngɔ kɛ ha Aaron nina a, kɛ kɔpehi nɛ bɔle jamɛ a ma amɛ a mi ɔ, a hla a ti ni komɛ nɛ a hɛ mi ka si. Mɛ lɛ a dlaa niye ní kɛ haa nyumuhi tsuo ngɛ osɔfohi a weku ɔmɛ a mi, kɛ Levi no tsuaa Levi no nɛ a ngma e biɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Everything Hezekiah did while he was king of Judah, including what he did for the temple in Jerusalem, was right and good. He was a successful king, because he obeyed the Lord God with all his heart.
translation_verse: Hezekia ya nɔ saminya, ejakaa nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e ngɛ pee ɔ, e peeɔ kɛ e tsui tsuo, kɛ Mawu gbeye yemi, Yawɛ we ɔ he ní tsumi jio, mlaa a nɔ yemi jio.

english_verse: You've heard what my ancestors and I have done to other nations. Were the gods of those nations able to defend their land against us?
translation_verse: Anɛ nɔ́ nɛ ye nɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ imi nitsɛ wa pee je ma kpa amɛ ɔ, nyɛ li lo? Anɛ jamɛ a je ma amɛ a mawu ɔmɛ nyɛ́ kpɔ mɛ kɛ je imi, Asiria matsɛ, ye dɛ mi lo?

english_verse: he and his officials worked out a plan to cut off the supply of water outside the city, so that the Assyrians would have no water when they came to attack. The officials got together a large work force that stopped up the springs and streams near Jerusalem.
translation_verse: e kɛ e ma nimeli ɔmɛ, kɛ e ta buli ɔmɛ na kpe, nɛ a to kaa a maa tsi vuhi nɛ ngɛ ma a nya a. A juɛmi ji, ke a tsi vu ɔmɛ nɛ Asiria bi ɔmɛ ba sɛ ma a mi ɔ, a be nyu nae. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma nimeli ɔmɛ ya bua nihi babauu a nya nɛ a kɛ mɛ ya tsi vu ɔmɛ tsuo; pa nɛ bee ngɛ zugba a mi ɔ hu a tsi lɛ, nɛ nyu bi ngɛ mi hu.

english_verse: Hezekiah's workers also repaired the broken sections of the city wall. Then they built defense towers and an outer wall to help protect the one already there. The landfill on the east side of David's City was also strengthened. He gave orders to make a large supply of weapons and shields,
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ dla Yerusalem ma a he fami ní ɔmɛ; gbogbohi nɛ ku ɔ, e kpale fia mɛ ekohu, nɛ e ma mɔhi ngɛ a nɔ; e fia gbogbo enyɔne hulɔ kɛ wo ma a he. Jehanɛ se hu, e dla Milo mɔ ɔ nɛ ngɛ David ma a mi ɔ, nɛ e sɔ kɛ̃ɛ̃hi kɛ tsɛ̃ihi babauu.

english_verse: and he appointed army commanders over the troops. Then he gathered the troops together in the open area in front of the city gate and said to them:
translation_verse: E ngɔ tatsɛmɛ ngɔ to ma a nya, nɛ e bua a nya ngɛ ma agbo ɔ nya. E de mɛ ke,

english_verse: Be brave and confident! There's no reason to be afraid of King Sennacherib and his powerful army. We are much more powerful,
translation_verse: “Nyɛ wlua nyɛ, nɛ nyɛɛ pee kã. Nyɛ ko ye Asiria matsɛ ɔ kɛ e ta babauu ɔ gbeye; ejakaa nɔ nɛ kɛ wɔ ngɛ ɔ, e he wa kulaa pe nɔ nɛ kɛ mɛ ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: When Sennacherib and his troops were camped at the town of Lachish, he sent a message to Hezekiah and the people in Jerusalem. It said:
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, benɛ Senakerib kɛ e tabo ɔ tsuo ngɛ Lakish kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ, e tsɔ nɛ a kɛ sɛ gbi nɛ ɔ ya ha Hezekia, kɛ Yuda ma a ngɛ Yerusalem ke,

english_verse: I am King Sennacherib of Assyria, and I have Jerusalem surrounded. Do you think you can survive my attack?
translation_verse: “Imi Asiria matsɛ, Senakerib, i ngɛ nyɛ bie ke mɛni nɔ nyɛ ngɔ nyɛ hɛ kɛ fɔ loko nyɛ hii si ngɛ Yerusalem kɛ mwɔɔ be mi nɛ a sa ma a yi ɔ?

english_verse: The Assyrian officials said terrible things about the Lord God and his servant Hezekiah.
translation_verse: Senakerib tsɔli ɔmɛ nitsɛmɛ hu tu munyuhi babauu kɛ si Yawɛ Mawu, kɛ e tsɔlɔ Hezekia.

english_verse: Sennacherib's letter even made fun of the Lord. It said, “The gods of other nations could not save their people from Assyria's army, and neither will the God that Hezekiah worships.”
translation_verse: Asiria matsɛ ɔ bɔ Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ ahlua ngɛ womi ɔ nɛ e ngma ba ha Hezekia a mi ke, “Je ma amɛ a mawu ɔmɛ nyɛ we nɛ a je a ma amɛ kɛ je ye dɛ mi. Hezekia Mawu ɔ hu be nyɛe ma je e ma a kɛ je ye dɛ mi.”

english_verse: People brought offerings to Jerusalem for the Lord and expensive gifts for Hezekiah, and from that day on, every nation on earth respected Hezekiah. Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies (
translation_verse: Nihi babauu ba Yerusalem, ba sã bɔ ha Yawɛ, nɛ a ke Matsɛ Hezekia hu níhi nɛ a he jua wa. Nɛ kɛ je jamɛ a be ɔ kɛ yaa a, je ma amɛ tsuo buɔ Hezekia saminya. Hezekia hiɔ kɛ e he nɔ womi (Matsɛmɛ II,

english_verse: About this same time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. He prayed, and the Lord gave him a sign that he would recover.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, Matsɛ Hezekia ba nu hiɔ, nɛ e piɛ nguɛ nya nɛ e gbo. E fa kue ha Yawɛ, nɛ Yawɛ ha lɛ okadi kɛ tsɔɔ kaa e ma na he wami.

english_verse: But Hezekiah was so proud that he refused to thank the Lord for everything he had done for him. This made the Lord angry, and he punished Hezekiah and the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Se kpakpa nɛ ɔ nɛ a pee Hezekia a, e nɛ Yawɛ si, nɛ e je we Yawɛ yi kɛ to nane mi; mohu ɔ, e wo e he nɔ. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Yawɛ mi mi fu lɛ, kɛ Yuda, kɛ Yerusalem.

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people later felt sorry and asked the Lord to forgive them. So the Lord did not punish them as long as Hezekiah was king. Hezekiah's Wealth (
translation_verse: Se nyagbe ɔ, Hezekia kɛ Yerusalem ma mi bi ɔmɛ ba a he si. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yawɛ gbla we ma a tue kɛ ya si Hezekia gbenɔ se. Hezekia ní kɛ agboje

english_verse: Hezekiah was very rich, and everyone respected him. He built special rooms to store the silver, the gold, the precious stones and spices, the shields, and the other valuable possessions.
translation_verse: Hezekia ba na ní babauu nitsɛ, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ buɔ lɛ. E pee nito hehi, nɛ e to ní nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔmɛ: sika tsu, sika hiɔ, tɛhi nɛ a he jua wa, tsopahi kɛ a he via, tsɛ̃ihi, kɛ ní kpa komɛ nɛ a he jua wa.

english_verse: Storehouses were also built for his supply of grain, wine, and olive oil; barns were built for his cattle, and pens were put up for his sheep.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ hu, e pee nito hehi kɛ ha e blɛfo, wai, kɛ oliv nu; nɛ e po piɛ kɛ ha e nahi kɛ tohi.

english_verse: God made Hezekiah extremely rich, so he bought even more sheep, goats, and cattle. And he built towns where he could keep all these animals.
translation_verse: Mawu ha Hezekia to, na, kɛ ní kpahi babauu nitsɛ, nɛ lɔ ɔ he je ɔ, e po mahi babauu.

english_verse: It was Hezekiah who built a tunnel that carried the water from Gihon Spring into the city of Jerusalem. In fact, everything he did was successful!
translation_verse: Matsɛ Hezekia nɛ ɔ nɔuu tsi Gihon pa a ngɛ yiti je nɛ e ha nɛ nyu ɔ ba be ngɛ David ma a bonyoku je. Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Hezekia pee ɔ, e ye manye ngɛ mi.

english_verse: Even when the leaders of Babylonia sent messengers to ask Hezekiah about the sign God had given him, God let Hezekiah give his own answer to test him and to see if he would remain faithful. Hezekiah Dies (
translation_verse: Benɛ ni ɔmɛ nɛ Babilonia ganɔ ɔmɛ tsɔ kɛ ba Hezekia ngɔ ba bi lɛ sane ngɛ nyakpɛ níhi nɛ ba zugba a nɔ ɔ a he pohu ɔ, Mawu ngmɛɛ Hezekia jemi he ngɔ ha lɛ. Mawu pee kikɛmɛ a nɔ́ nɛ ɔ konɛ e kɛ ka lɛ, nɛ e kɛ na nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ e tsui mi. Hezekia matsɛ yemi ɔ nyagbe (Matsɛmɛ II,

english_verse: Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including how faithful he was to the Lord, is included in the records kept by Isaiah the prophet. These are written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Hezekia he sane kpahi, kɛ ní kpakpahi tsuo nɛ e pee ɔ, a ngma ngɛ gbalɔ Yesaya, Amoz binyumu ɔ nina a nɛ ngɛ Yuda kɛ Israel Matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a Blema Sanehi Womi mi ɔ mi.

english_verse: When Hezekiah died, he was buried in the section of the royal tombs that was reserved for the most respected kings, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem honored him. His son Manasseh then became king.
translation_verse: Hezekia ba gbo, nɛ a pu lɛ ngɛ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a gɔ ɔ mi, ngɛ yiti je ɔ. Benɛ e gbo ɔ, Yuda kɛ Yerusalem tsuo wo e hɛ mi nyami. Hezekia bi Manase ba ye matsɛ ngɛ e se.

english_verse: But the people of Judah and Jerusalem listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
translation_verse: Se Manase mlɔɔ Yuda kɛ Yerusalem ma mi bi ɔmɛ, nɛ a ya pee yayami nɛ kle kulaa pe yayami nɛ je ma amɛ nɛ Yawɛ fie kɛ je Israel bi ɔmɛ a blɔ mi ɔ pee ɔ po. Manase tsake e tsui

english_verse: Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his prayer to the Lord God and the warnings from his prophets, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Manase he sane kpahi nɛ piɛ, kɛ kue nɛ e fa ha e Mawu, kɛ gbali ɔmɛ nɛ kɛ lɛ ba tu munyu ngɛ Israel Mawu ɔ biɛ mi ɔ a sɛ gbi ɔmɛ ɔ, a ngma ngɛ Israel Matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a Blema Sanehi Womi ɔ mi.

english_verse: While Manasseh was held captive there, he asked the Lord God to forgive him and to help him.
translation_verse: Benɛ e ngɛ haomi mi ɔ, e ba e he si, nɛ e fa kue ha Yawɛ, e nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ.

english_verse: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. And he continued to worship the stars.
translation_verse: Jami hehi nɛ e tsɛ Hezekia gbɛ ɔ, e kpale po mɛ ekohu. E ma bɔ sami la tɛhi kɛ ha Baal, nɛ e pee amagahi kɛ ha yo mawu ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Ashera a. E ja dodoehi hulɔ.

english_verse: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
translation_verse: Yawɛ we ɔ ngɛ Yerusalem, he nɛ Yawɛ to nɛ a ja lɛ ngɛ daa a, Manase puɛ bɔ sami la tɛhi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ha Baal ɔmɛ.

english_verse: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courtyards of the temple
translation_verse: Jehanɛ e puɛ bɔ sami la tɛhi ngɔ ma kue enyɔ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ a mi, konɛ a ja dodoehi ngɛ lejɛ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: and even set up a stone image of a foreign god. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own sons in Hinnom Valley. He did many other sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago, God had told David and Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there in the temple I will be worshiped forever.
translation_verse: E puɛ amaga ko ya ma Yawɛ ɔ we. Mawu, kɛ David, kɛ e binyumu Salomo tu we nɛ ɔ he munyu hyɛ, nɛ e de ke, “I hla we nɛ ɔ ngɛ Yerusalem kɛ je Israel wɛtso ɔmɛ tsuo a kpɛti ngɔ to kaa he nɛ sa nɛ a ja mi ngɛ daa.

english_verse: If my people will faithfully obey all the laws and teaching I gave to my servant Moses, I will never again force them to leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke Israel bi ɔmɛ maa pee nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ i fa mɛ ke a pee ɔ, nɛ a maa ye mlaa amɛ tsuo nɛ ye tsɔlɔ Mose wo mɛ ɔ a nɔ ɔ, i be hae nɛ a fie mɛ kɛ je zugba a nɛ i ngɔ kɛ ha a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ɔ nɔ hu.”

english_verse: The Lord tried to warn Manasseh and the people about their sins, but they ignored the warning.
translation_verse: Yawɛ bɔ Manase kɛ e ma a kɔkɔ, se a bui tue.

english_verse: So he let Assyrian army commanders invade Judah and capture Manasseh. They put a hook in his nose and tied him up in chains, and they took him to Babylon.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Yawɛ ha nɛ Asiria tabo ɔ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ba tua Yuda. A kɛ gbowehi nu Manase nɛ a wo lɛ kɔsɔkɔsɔ, nɛ a ngɔ lɛ kɛ ho Babilon ya.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Manasseh's prayer and saw how sorry he was, and so he let him go back to Jerusalem and rule as king. Manasseh knew from then on that the Lord was God.
translation_verse: Mawu bu Manase kue fami ɔ tue, nɛ e ha nɛ e kpale kɛ ya Yerusalem ya ye matsɛ ekohu. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha nɛ Manase na kaa Yawɛ ɔ, Mawu ji lɛ niinɛ.

english_verse: Later, Manasseh rebuilt the eastern section of Jerusalem's outer wall and made it taller. This section went from Gihon Valley north to Fish Gate and around the part of the city called Mount Ophel. He also assigned army officers to each of the fortified cities in Judah.
translation_verse: Ní nɛ ɔmɛ a se ɔ, Manase fia gbogbo enyɔne ɔ ngɛ David ma a we beleku je ɔ nɔ kɛ ya hiɔwe. E fia nɔ kɛ je kɔ̃ ɔ mi ngɛ Gihon pa a kasa nya ngɛ omleyi je kɛ ya si lo agbo ɔ nya, hluu kɛ ya bɔle ma a nɛ a tsɛɛ Ofel ɔ. Jehanɛ hu, e ngɔ tatsɛmɛ ngɔ to Yuda mahi nɛ a fia gbogbo ngɔ wo a he ɔ tsuo a mi.

english_verse: Manasseh also removed the idols and the stone image of the foreign god from the temple, and he gathered the altars he had built near the temple and in other parts of Jerusalem. He threw all these things outside the city.
translation_verse: E je ma se mawu ɔmɛ, kɛ amaga a nɛ e ngɔ ya ma Yawɛ we ɔ kɛ je lejɛ ɔ. Bɔ sami la tɛhi nɛ a pee ha mawuhi nɛ ngɛ yoku ɔ nɔ, he nɛ Yawɛ ɔ we ɔ ngɛ ɔ, kɛ ní nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ he kpahi ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ, e je mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ. E muɔ mɛ kɛ ho ya sake ngɔ pue ma a nya.

english_verse: Then he repaired the Lord's altar and offered sacrifices to thank him and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He gave orders that everyone in Judah must worship the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: E dla bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɛ ngɛ he nɛ a jaa Yawɛ ngɛ ɔ, nɛ e sã tue mi jɔmi bɔhi, kɛ sina bɔhi ngɛ nɔ. E fa Yuda ma a tsuo ke a sɔmɔ Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ.

english_verse: Manasseh died and was buried near the palace, and his son Amon became king. King Amon of Judah (
translation_verse: Manase ba gbo, nɛ a pu lɛ ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ mi, nɛ e bi Amon ba ye matsɛ ngɛ e se. Yuda matsɛ, Amon (Matsɛmɛ II,

english_verse: Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done, and he worshiped and offered sacrifices to the idols his father had made.
translation_verse: E ya wo e tsɛ Manase nane, nɛ e pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ; amaga amɛ nɛ e tsɛ puɛ ɔ, e sɔmɔ mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Manasseh had turned back to the Lord, but Amon refused to do that. Instead, he sinned even more than his father.
translation_verse: Se Amon bɛ e he si, nɛ e kpale we kɛ bɛ Yawɛ ngɔ kaa bɔ nɛ e tsɛ pee ɔ; lɛɛ e pee yayamihi babauu pe e tsɛ ɔ po.

english_verse: Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace.
translation_verse: Amon tsɔli ɔmɛ so ngɔ wo e he, nɛ a gbe lɛ ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ.

english_verse: But the people of Judah killed the murderers of Amon and made his son Josiah king.
translation_verse: Se Yuda bi ɔmɛ gbe nihi tsuo nɛ so ngɔ wo e he ɔ, nɛ a wo e bi Yosia matsɛ ngɛ e se.

english_verse: Hilkiah and the four other men left at once and went to talk with Huldah the prophet. Her husband was Shallum, who was in charge of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in the northern part of Jerusalem, and when they met in her home,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Hilkia, kɛ nihi nɛ matsɛ ɔ tsɔ ɔ pue nɔ kɛ ho nɛ a ya bi gbalɔyo ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Hulda a ní ngɛ Yerusalem ma he ɔ mi he nɛ e hii ɔ. Hulda huno ji Tikva bi Shalum, Harhas bibi ɔ; nɛ Shalum nɛ ɔ ji nɔ nɛ hyɛɛ tadehi a nɔ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ. Osɔfo Hilkia kɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ ngɔ matsɛ ɔ sɛ gbi ɔ ya ha gbalɔyo ɔ.

english_verse: In the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah, after he had removed all the sinful things from the land and from the Lord's temple, he sent three of his officials to repair the temple. They were Shaphan son of Azaliah, Governor Maaseiah of Jerusalem, and Joah son of Joahaz, who kept the government records.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Yosia yi nɔ jeha nɛ ji nyɔngma kɛ kpaanyɔ ɔ, e julaa zugba a, nɛ e tsukɔ Yawɛ, e Mawu ɔ we ɔ he. Be nɛ e gbe nya a, e tsɔ nihi etɛ konɛ a ya dla Yawɛ, e Mawu ɔ we ɔ.
