english_verse: When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them. Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ ma a tsuo ho a we ɔmɛ a mi ya. A ya ngmɛ okplɔɔ nɛ a kɛ a sibi ye ní kɛ bua jɔmi, ejakaa a nu nɔ́ nɛ a kane ha mɛ ɔ sisi saminya. Gbasisihimi nyami be ɔ

english_verse: On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, we puɔ nyatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, osɔfo ɔmɛ kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ ba bua a he nya ngɛ Ezra, mlaa tsɔɔlɔ ɔ ngɔ, nɛ a kase mlaa a.

english_verse: that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year.
translation_verse: A na kaa mlaa a nɛ Yawɛ wo kɛ gu Mose nɔ kɛ ha Israel bi ɔmɛ ɔ tsɔɔ kaa a hi gbahi a sisi kɛ ye nyami be nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ni ɔmɛ ya poo tso, nɛ a ba ma gbahi ngɛ a tsu ɔmɛ a yi mi, kɛ a we ɔmɛ a mi, kɛ Mawu we ɔ kpo ɔ nɔ, kɛ ma kpe he ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Nyu Agbo ɔ kɛ Efraim Agbo ɔ, nya a.

english_verse: On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
translation_verse: Kɛ je kekleekle ligbi ɔ nɔ kɛ ya si be nɛ a gbe nyami be ɔ nya a, a kaneɔ Mawu mlaa a fa ko daa ligbi. A ye Gbasisihimi nyami be nɛ ɔ ligbi kpaago, nɛ ligbi kpaanyɔne ɔ, a pee nyagbe kpe kaa bɔ nɛ mlaa a tsɔɔ ɔ.

english_verse: For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: A kane Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ mlaa a ngmlɛfia etɛ, nɛ ngmlɛfia etɛ nɛ tsa nɔ ɔ, a jaje a he yayami ɔmɛ, nɛ a ja Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ.

english_verse: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God.
translation_verse: A pee kpoku ko ha Levi bi ɔmɛ, nɛ lɔ ɔ nɔ nɛ Yeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebania, Buni, Sherebia, Bani, kɛ Kenani da si ngɛ. A sɔle boboobo kɛ ha Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ.

english_verse: You alone are the Lord, Creator of the heavens and all the stars, Creator of the earth and those who live on it, Creator of the ocean and all its creatures. You are the source of life, praised by the stars that fill the heavens.
translation_verse: Nɛ a sɔle ke, “Yawɛ, mo nɔ kake pɛ ji Yawɛ, mo nɛ o pee hiɔwe ɔ, kɛ dodoe ɔmɛ ngɛ kɔɔhiɔ mi. Mo nɛ o pee zugba kɛ wo, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ a mi, nɛ o ha mɛ tsuo wami. Hiɔwe ta a kplaa si haa mo, nɛ a jaa mo.

english_verse: You are the Lord our God, the one who chose Abram— you brought him from Ur in Babylonia and named him Abraham.
translation_verse: Yawɛ Mawu, mo nɛ o hla Abram, nɛ o kpaka lɛ kɛ je Ur ngɛ Babilonia; o tsake e biɛ ngɔ pee Abraham.

english_verse: Because he was faithful, you made an agreement to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites and Hittites, of the Amorites and Perizzites, and of the Jebusites and Girgashites. Now you have kept your promise, just as you always do.
translation_verse: O na kaa e ye mo anɔkuale, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, o kɛ lɛ so. O wo lɛ si ke o maa ngɔ Kanaan, Hit, Amon, Periz, Yebus, kɛ Girgash bi ɔmɛ a zugba a kɛ ha e nina. O ye o siwo ɔ nɔ, ejakaa o yeɔ anɔkuale.

english_verse: When our ancestors were in Egypt, you saw their suffering; when they were at the Red Sea, you heard their cry for help.
translation_verse: “O na bɔ nɛ wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ na amanehlu ngɛ Egipt, o nu a kue fami ɔ ngɛ Wo Tsu ɔ nya.

english_verse: You knew that the King of Egypt and his officials and his nation had mistreated your people. So you worked fearsome miracles against the Egyptians and earned a reputation that still remains.
translation_verse: O pee okadihi, kɛ nyakpɛ níhi ngɛ Farao ɔ, kɛ e ma ní tsuli ɔmɛ, kɛ e ma a tsuo a hɛ mi, ejakaa o le bɔ nɛ a wa o ma a yi mi. O he biɛ kɛ je jamɛ a be ɔ mi tɔɔ kɛ ba su mwɔnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: You divided the deep sea, and your people walked through on dry land. But you tossed their enemies in, and they sank down like a heavy stone.
translation_verse: O je blɔ kɛ gu wo ɔ mi kɛ ha o ma a, nɛ o kpaka mɛ kɛ nyɛɛ wo ɔ mi ngɛ zugba gbigbli nɔ. Nihi nɛ nyɛɛ a se ɔ gbo tlɔ nyu nɛ mi kuɔ ɔ sisi, kaa bɔ nɛ tɛ muɔ kɛ yaa wo nɛ gli sisi ɔ.

english_verse: Each day you led your people with a thick cloud, and at night you showed the way with a flaming fire.
translation_verse: O ngɔ bɔku kɛ tsɔɔ mɛ blɔ piani; se nyɔ mi lɛɛ o ha mɛ la nɛ a kɛ hyɛ a blɔ mi.

english_verse: At Sinai you came down from heaven, and you gave your people good laws and teachings that are fair and honest.
translation_verse: O kple si kɛ je hiɔwe kɛ ba Sinai yo ɔ nɔ, nɛ o kɛ o ma a ba tu munyu; o ha mɛ mlaa kpakpahi, kɛ ní tsɔɔmi nɛ hi kɛ pi si.

english_verse: You commanded them to respect your holy Sabbath, and you instructed your servant Moses to teach them your laws.
translation_verse: O tsɔɔ mɛ kaa a ye Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ klɔuklɔu, nɛ o gu o tsɔlɔ Mose nɔ kɛ ha mɛ o mlaa amɛ.

english_verse: When they were hungry, you sent bread from heaven, and when they were thirsty, you let water flow from a rock. Then you commanded them to capture the land that you had solemnly promised. *
translation_verse: “Benɛ hwɔ ye mɛ ɔ, o ha mɛ niye ní kɛ je hiɔwe, nɛ benɛ kuma ye mɛ ɔ, o ha mɛ nyu kɛ je tɛ sa mi. O de mɛ ke zugba a nɛ o wo si ke o ma ha mɛ ɔ, a ya ngɔ nɛ a hi nɔ.

english_verse: Our stubborn ancestors refused to obey— they forgot about the miracles you had worked for them, and they were determined to return to Egypt and become slaves again.
translation_verse: Se wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ba wo a he nɔ nɛ a wa tue, nɛ a yi o mlaa amɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: not even when they made an idol shaped like a calf and insulted you by claiming, “This is the god who rescued us from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Benɛ a puɛ amaga ko nɛ ngɛ kaa na ku, nɛ a de ke amaga nɛ ɔ nɛ kpaka mɛ kɛ je Egipt kɛ ba a, a bɔ musu babauu kɛ si mo Yawɛ.

english_verse: Because of your great mercy, you never abandoned them in the desert. And you always guided them with a cloud by day and a fire at night.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi po, o ngmɛɛ we a he ngɛ nga kplanaa a nɔ; ejakaa o naa mɔbɔ saminya. O je we bɔku ɔ nɛ tsɔɔ mɛ blɔ piani ɔ, kɛ la a hu nɛ tsɔɔ mɛ blɔ nyɔ mi ɔ kɛ ji a he.

english_verse: Your gentle Spirit instructed them, and you gave them manna to eat and water to drink.
translation_verse: O ha nɛ o mumi kpakpa a tsɔɔ mɛ ní, nɛ o ha mɛ a nya mi ngma, kɛ nyu nɛ a nu.

english_verse: You took good care of them, and for forty years they never lacked a thing. Their clothes didn't wear out, and their feet were never swollen.
translation_verse: Jeha nyingmi eywiɛ sɔuu nɛ a nyɛɛ nga kplanaa a nɔ ɔ, o ha mɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ he hia mɛ: a tadehi gba we ngɛ a he, nɛ a nanehi hu fuu we.

english_verse: You brought them into the land that you had promised their ancestors, and you blessed their nation with people that outnumbered the stars in the sky.
translation_verse: O ha nɛ a bimɛ ɔmɛ hu a he hiɛ babauu kaa dodoehi ngɛ hiɔwe; nɛ zugba a nɛ o de a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ke a ya ngɔ ɔ, o kpaka mɛ kɛ ya lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: They captured strong cities and rich farmland; they took furnished houses, as well as cisterns, vineyards, olive orchards, and numerous fruit trees. They ate till they were satisfied, and they celebrated your abundant blessings.
translation_verse: A ngɔ ma nguahi nɛ a fia gbogbo ngɔ wo a he ɔ zugba nɛ baa ní, kɛ wehi nɛ hyi tɔ kɛ ní kpakpahi tsuo; a ngɔ nyu vuhi nɛ a tsua momo, oliv tsohi, tsohi nɛ woɔ yiblii, kɛ wai ngmɔhi. A ye ní ɔmɛ nyamanyama; a tɔ nɛ a plɔke. Ní kpakpa amɛ nɛ o ha mɛ ɔ, a nya he.

english_verse: So you handed them over to their enemies, who treated them terribly. But in their sufferings, they begged you to help. From heaven you listened to their prayers and because of your great mercy, you sent leaders to rescue them.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, o ha a he nyɛli ba ye a nɔ, nɛ a hao mɛ. Ngɛ a fimi be ɔ mi ɔ, a fa kue kɛ tsɛ mo, nɛ o bu mɛ tue kɛ je hiɔwe. O mɔbɔ nami babauu ɔ nya a, o ha mɛ hɛ mi nyɛɛli nɛ kpɔ mɛ kɛ je a he nyɛli a dɛ.

english_verse: But when they were at peace, they would turn against you, and you would hand them over to their enemies. Then they would beg for help, and because you are merciful, you rescued them over and over again.
translation_verse: Benɛ a na tue mi jɔmi ɔ, a pee yayami ekohu; kɛkɛ nɛ o je a se, nɛ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ ba ye a nɔ ekohu. Se benɛ a tsake a tsui, nɛ a fa kue kɛ tsɛ mo ekohu ɔ, o bu mɛ tue kɛ je hiɔwe; nɛ o na mɛ mɔbɔ, nɛ o kpɔ mɛ si abɔ.

english_verse: For years, you were patient, and your Spirit warned them with messages spoken by your prophets. Still they refused to listen, and you handed them over to their enemies.
translation_verse: O to o tsui si, nɛ o bɔ mɛ kɔkɔ jeha babauu. O ngɔ o mumi ɔ ngɔ wo o gbali ɔmɛ a mi, konɛ a tu munyu ngɔ tsɔɔ mɛ; se o ma a wa tue. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, o ngmɛɛ a he ha ma kpahi nɛ a ye a nɔ.

english_verse: But you are merciful and kind, and so you never forgot them or let them be destroyed.
translation_verse: O kua we mɛ; o na mɛ mɔbɔ, nɛ o kpataa we a hɛ mi hulɔ. Ejakaa Mawu mɔbɔ nalɔ kɛ dloolɔ ji mo!

english_verse: You have always been fair when you punished us for our sins.
translation_verse: O ye dami sane kaa o gbla wa tue, ejakaa o ye anɔkuale, be nɛ wɔɔ lɛɛ wa pee yayami.

english_verse: You blessed them with a kingdom and with an abundance of rich, fertile land, but they refused to worship you or turn from their evil.
translation_verse: O gbaa matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ye o ma a nɔ ɔ, kɛ zugba kpakpa nɛ baa ní saminya a. Se kɛ̃ ɔ, a kpa we yayami peemi ɔ, konɛ a ba sɔmɔ mo.

english_verse: Its plentiful harvest is taken by kings you placed over us because of our sins. Our suffering is unbearable, because they do as they wish to us and our livestock. The People Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Zugba a baa ní babauu ha matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a ngɔ to wa nya a mohu, se akɛnɛ wa pee yayami kɛ si mo ɔ, a pee wɔ nimli ɔmɛ, kɛ wa lohwe ɔmɛ yayami bɔ nɛ a suɔ, nɛ wa yi fi wawɛɛ nitsɛ!” A ngma biɛhi ngɔ wo somi womi ɔ sisi

english_verse: As governor, I signed the agreement together with Zedekiah and the following priests:
translation_verse: Kekleekle nɔ nɛ ngma e biɛ ji ɔ, Hakalia bi Nehemia, amlaaho ɔ. Nɔ nɛ nyɛɛ e se ji Zedekia.

english_verse: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah, Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch, Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah.
translation_verse: Osɔfohi nɛ ngma a biɛhi ji: Seraya, Azaria, Yeremia, Pashur, Amaria, Malkiya, Hatush, Shebania, Haluk, Harim, Meremot, Obadia, Daniel, Gineton, Baruk, Meshulam, Abiya, Miyamin, Maazia, Bilgai, kɛ Shemaya.

english_verse: All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
translation_verse: wa piɛ wa ma nimeli ɔmɛ a he kɛ ngɛ kita kae ke gbiɛmi nɛ ba wa nɔ ke wa tɔ kita a. Wa ngɛ kita kae ke Mawu mlaa a nɛ e wo wɔ kɛ gu e tsɔlɔ Mose nɔ ɔ, wa maa ye nɔ. Wa ngɛ kita kae ke níhi tsuo kulaa nɛ Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ fa wɔ ke waa pee ɔ, wa maa pee. Wa ngɛ kita kae ekohu ke wa maa ye e mlaa amɛ, kɛ blɔ nya tomi ɔmɛ tsuo a nɔ.

english_verse: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
translation_verse: Ke nibwɔhi ba jua niye ní, loo nɔ́ kpa ko ha wɔ ngɛ Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ nɔ, loo nyami be kpa ko mi ɔ, wa be hee. Daa jeha kpaago ɔ, wa be ngmɔ hue. Jehanɛ hu, hiɔhi nɛ nihi hɛɛ wɔ ɔ tsuo wa be jee hu; wa maa ngɔ kɛ ke mɛ.

english_verse: This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
translation_verse: Wɔ tsuo wa maa ngɔ ní nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ba nɛ a kɛ sɔmɔ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ: abolo klɔuklɔu ɔ, niye ní bɔ nɛ a sãã daa ligbi ɔ, lohwehi nɛ a kɛ sãã bɔ daa ligbi ɔ, bɔ klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ nɛ a sãã Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔmɛ ɔ, kɛ Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be ɔ, kɛ nyami be kpa amɛ a nɔ ɔ. Wa ma ha níhi nɛ a kɛ sãã bɔ klɔuklɔu kpa amɛ hulɔ kaa yayami pami bɔ nɛ a kɛ kpataa Yawɛ ha Israel kikɛ nɛ ɔ, kɛ nɔ́ ko saisaa nɛ he hia nɛ a kɛ ma sɔmɔ ngɛ wa Mawu ɔ we ɔ.

english_verse: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ hu, wa ngɛ si woe ke daa jeha a, wɔ ma a, kɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ, waa kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ maa fɔ sɔ kɛ na wekuhi nɛ maa ngɔ lɛ́ kɛ ba nɛ a kɛ sã bɔhi ha Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ mlaa a tsɔɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
translation_verse: Wa ngɛ si woe hu ke daa jeha a, wa maa ngɔ blɛfo, kɛ kekleekle tso yiblii nɛ wa ma na a kɛ maa ba lɛ, Yawɛ e we ɔ.

english_verse: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
translation_verse: Wa ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ maa ngɔ e kekleekle binyumu kɛ ba osɔfo ɔmɛ a ngɔ ngɛ wa Mawu ɔ we ɔ, konɛ a pee mɛ klɔuklɔu kɛ ha Mawu kaa bɔ nɛ mlaa a tsɔɔ ɔ. Jehanɛ, wa maa ngɔ wa na amɛ, kɛ wa to ɔmɛ a kekleekle bihi hu kɛ ba.

english_verse: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
translation_verse: Daa jeha a, wa maa ngɔ ma nɛ a pee kɛ je blɛfo he mi kɛ ba ha osɔfo ɔmɛ ngɛ wa Mawu ɔ we ɔ. Nike ní kpahi nɛ maa piɛ he ji wai, oliv nu, kɛ tso yiblii nɛ a yeɔ slɔɔtohi tsuo. Levi bi nɛ tsuɔ ngmɔ nɔ niba níhi a mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka ngɛ kɔpe ɔmɛ a mi ɔ hu, wa ma ha mɛ ngmɔ nɔ niba ní mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka.

english_verse: A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom,
translation_verse: Osɔfohi nɛ ji Aaron nina a, ke benɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ ngɛ mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka amɛ tsue ɔ, a kɛ mɛ nɛ hi lejɛ ɔ. Levi bi ɔmɛ nɛ a ngɔ mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka amɛ nɛ a bua nya a tsuo a mi dlami nyɔngma mi kake kɛ to ngɛ wa Mawu we ɔ nito he ɔmɛ.

english_verse: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Israel ma a, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ a blɔ nya ji kaa a ngɔ blɛfo, dã, kɛ oliv nu nɛ a tsu ngɛ ni ɔmɛ a dɛ ɔ kɛ ba nito he ɔmɛ ngɛ Mawu we ɔ. Lejɛ ɔ a toɔ níhi nɛ a kɛ sɔmɔɔ ɔ ngɛ. Osɔfohi nɛ ngɛ ní tsue, buli, kɛ lali ɔmɛ hu lejɛ ɔ nɔuu ji he nɛ a hii. Wa maa hyɛ wa Mawu ɔ we ɔ nɔ saminya.

english_verse: The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there.
translation_verse: Ma nimeli ɔmɛ hi Yerusalem ma klɔuklɔu ɔ mi, nɛ ma a mi bi ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ fɔ sɔ kɛ hla nɔ kake ngɛ ni nyɔngma a kpɛti kɛ piɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ a he; se nihi nɛ piɛ ɔ lɛɛ a ya hi ma kpa amɛ kɛ kɔpe ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni kpahi nɛ a si a gugue ke a maa hi Yerusalem ɔ, Israel ma a je a yi saminya.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families. The Judah Tribe
translation_verse: Israel ma a, osɔfo ɔmɛ, Levi bi ɔmɛ, sɔlemi we ɔ ní tsuli ɔmɛ, kɛ Salomo tsɔli ɔmɛ a nina amɛ lɛɛ a hi mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɔ, ngɛ a ma amɛ kɛ kɔpe ɔmɛ a mi. Yuda zugba a nɔ ma nimeli nɛ hi Yerusalem ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.

english_verse: From the Benjamin tribe, three leaders settled in Jerusalem. The first was Sallu son of Meshullam, and the others were Gabbai and Sallai. Sallu's ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah. Altogether, there were
translation_verse: Gabai kɛ Salai; a weku no pɔtɛɛ ji Salu. Benyamin bi tsuo nɛ hi Yerusalem ɔ a hiɛmi ji

english_verse: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command. Priests
translation_verse: A nyatsɛ ji Zikri bi Yoel; nɛ Hasenua bi Yuda ji ma a nɔ hyɛlɔ ɔ setsɔ.

english_verse: The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest.
translation_verse: Hilkia bi Seraya, Meshulam bibi ɔ. E nɛmɛ ji Zadok, Merayot, kɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa Ahitub.

english_verse: from his clan who served in the temple. The third priest to settle there was Adaiah son of Jeroham. His ancestors were Pelaliah, Amzi, Zechariah, Pashhur, and Malchijah.
translation_verse: . Yeroham bi Adaya, Pelalia bibi ɔ. E nɛmɛ ji Amzi, Zakaria, Pashur, kɛ Malkiya.

english_verse: clan leaders among his relatives. The fourth priest to settle there was Amashsai son of Azarel. His ancestors were Ahzai, Meshillemoth, and Immer.
translation_verse: , nɛ mɛ tsuo we puɔ nyatsɛmɛ ji mɛ. Azarel bi Amashsai, Azai bibi ɔ. E nɛmɛ ji Meshilemot, kɛ Imer.

english_verse: brave warriors from their clans, and their leader was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim. Levites
translation_verse: je we puɔ nya nɛ ɔ, nɛ ta hwuli kpanakpanaa ji mɛ. A nyatsɛ ji Hagedolim bi Zabdiel.

english_verse: Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
translation_verse: Levi bi ɔmɛ: Hashub bi Shemaya, Azrikam bibi ɔ. E nɛmɛ ji Hashabia kɛ Buni.

english_verse: Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
translation_verse: Shabetai kɛ Yozabad ji Levi bi nɛ hyɛɛ Mawu we ɔ kpo nɔ je ní tsumi ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant. Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
translation_verse: Mika bi Matania, Asaf nina ko nɛ a tsɛɛ Zabdi ɔ bibi ɔ. Lɛ ji nɔ nɛ jeɔ la nɛ a kɛ jeɔ si nami sɔlemi sisi. Bakbukia, Matania setsɔ ɔ, kɛ Shamua bi Abda, Yedutun nina Galal bibi ɔ.

english_verse: One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
translation_verse: Agbo nya buli: Akub, kɛ Talmon, kɛ a weku li. Mɛ tsuo a yibɔ ji

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah.
translation_verse: Israel ma nɛ piɛ ɔ, a kɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi nɛ piɛ ɔ hi mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɔ ngɛ Yuda ma kpa amɛ a mi.

english_verse: But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
translation_verse: Sɔlemi we ɔ he ní tsuli ɔmɛ hi Yerusalem he ko nɛ a tsɛɛ Ofel ɔ, nɛ a nyatsɛmɛ ji Ziha kɛ Gishpa.

english_verse: Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services,
translation_verse: Nɔ nɛ hyɛɛ Levi bi nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ a nɔ ji Bani bi Uzi, Hashabia bibi ɔ. E nɛmɛ ji Matania kɛ Mika. E je Asaf we puɔ nya. We puɔ nya nɛ ɔ blɔ nya ji kaa e hyɛ la nɛ a laa kɛ sɔmɔɔ ngɛ Mawu we ɔ nɔ saminya.

english_verse: though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
translation_verse: Matsɛ David wo mlaa nɛ tsɔɔ bɔ nɛ lali ɔmɛ maa hi a sibi tsakee kɛ lami, kɛ hiɔwo nɛ sa nɛ a haa mɛ daa ligbi.

english_verse: The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe. The People in the Other Towns and Villages
translation_verse: Meshezabel bi Petahia nɛ je Zera we puɔ nya, kɛ Yuda we puɔ nya a, daa Israel ma a nya ngɛ ma a sane yemihi a mi. Nihi nɛ hi ma kpa amɛ a mi

english_verse: Some of the people of Judah lived in the following towns near their farms: Kiriath-Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel,
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ babauu hi a kɔpe ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ ngmɔ si. Yuda wɛtso ɔ mi bi ɔmɛ hi Kiriat Arba, Dibon, Yekabzeel, kɛ a he kɔpe ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: Enrimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
translation_verse: kɛ Enrimon, Zora, Yarmut,

english_verse: The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages,
translation_verse: Benyamin wɛtso ɔ mi bi ɔmɛ hi Geba, Mikmash, Ai, Betel, kɛ a he kɔpe ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
translation_verse: Hazor, Rama, Gitaim,

english_verse: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
translation_verse: Hadid, Zeboyim, Nebalat,

english_verse: Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley.
translation_verse: Lod, Ono, kɛ ga ní tsuli a kɔ̃ ɔ mi.

english_verse: Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Levi bi ɔmɛ ekomɛ nɛ hi Yuda zugba a nɔ ɔ kɛ Benyamin bi ɔmɛ ya hi si.

english_verse: Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
translation_verse: Osɔfohi kɛ Levi bi nɛ kpale kɛ je ma se kɛ ba a, a kɛ Shaeltiel bi Zerubabel, kɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa nɛ a tsɛɛ Yoshua a nɛ ba. A biɛhi ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: Osɔfo ɔmɛ:

english_verse: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
translation_verse: Seraya, Yeremia, Ezra, Amaria, Maluk, Hatush, Shekania, Rehum, Meremot, Ido, Ginetoi, Abiya, Miyamin, Maadia, Bilga, Shemaya, Yoyarib, Yedaya, Salu, Amok, Hilkia, kɛ Yedaya. Mɛ ji a nyɛmimɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ tsuo a nya dali ngɛ Yoshua yi nɔ.

english_verse: The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise,
translation_verse: Levi bi: Nihi nɛ hyɛɛ nɛ a la sina lahi ji Yeshua, Binui, Kadmiel, Sherebia, Yuda, kɛ Matania.

english_verse: while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses. Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
translation_verse: Lali a kuu nɛ heɔ la nɔ ji Bakbukia, Uno, kɛ e nyɛmimɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ. Osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa Yoshua nina

english_verse: Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada.
translation_verse: Yoshua bi ji Yoyakim; Yoyakim bi ji Eliashib, nɛ Eliashib hu bi ji Yoyada.

english_verse: Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua. Leaders of the Priestly Clans
translation_verse: Yoyada bi ji Yonatan, nɛ Yonatan bi ji Yadua. Osɔfo weku ɔmɛ a nyatsɛmɛ

english_verse: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
translation_verse: A ngma Levi bi ɔmɛ a weku ɔmɛ a nyatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ a weku ɔmɛ a nyatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ hu a biɛhi ngɔ wo womi mi ngɛ osɔfo nikɔtɔma pe kulaa nɛ ɔmɛ a wami be mi: Eliashib, Yoyada, Yonatan, kɛ Yadua. A ya nɔ ngma biɛ nɛ ɔmɛ hluu kɛ ya si Persia matsɛ, Darius yi nɔ.

english_verse: However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
translation_verse: Levi bi ɔmɛ a weku ɔmɛ a nyatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a biɛ ɔmɛ lɛɛ a ngma kɛ wo Blema Sanehi Womi ɔ mi kɛ ba su Eliashib bibi Yonatan be ɔ mi pɛ. Bɔ nɛ a dla sɔlemi we ɔ mi ní tsumi ɔmɛ

english_verse: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
translation_verse: Buli nɛ ɔmɛ ji nihi nɛ buu ngɛ nito hehi nɛ ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ agbo ɔmɛ a nya: Matania, Bakbukia, Obadia, Meshulam, Talmon, kɛ Akub.

english_verse: All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest. Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ a wo a ta nɛ ɔ hi si ngɛ Yeshua bi Yoyakim, Yehozadak bibi ɔ yi nɔ. Jamɛ a be ɔ kɛ̃ nɛ Nehemia ye amlaalo, nɛ osɔfo Ezra hu ji mlaa tsɔɔlɔ ɔ nɛ. Nehemia julaa ma a gbogbo ɔ

english_verse: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Benɛ a maa julaa Yerusalem gbogbo ɔ, a ya kpee Levi bi ɔmɛ kɛ je hehi tsuo nɛ a ngɛ ɔ kɛ ba. A ba piɛ Yerusalem ma mi bi ɔmɛ a he, nɛ a fia gɔgɔ, kɛ saku, nɛ a la sina lahi nɛ a kɛ ye nyami ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
translation_verse: Osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ pee kusumi kɛ julaa mɛ nitsɛmɛ a he. A julaa ma a, kɛ agbo ɔmɛ, kɛ ma gbogbo ɔ hulɔ.

english_verse: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, i bua Yuda ma nimeli ɔmɛ a nya ngɛ gbogbo ɔ nɔ, nɛ i ngɔ mɛ ngɔ to kuu agboagbo enyɔ a nya, konɛ a hyɛ nɛ a to kɛ nyɛɛ, nɛ a la Mawu yi jemi lahi kɛ bɔle ma a. Kekleekle kuu ɔ nyɛɛ hiɔ nɔ, ngɛ gbogbo ɔ nɔ, kɛ yaa Dwɔmi Agbo ɔ nya.

english_verse: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them.
translation_verse: Hoshaya nyɛɛ lali ɔmɛ a se, nɛ Yuda ma nimeli ɔmɛ fa nyɛɛ e se.

english_verse: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
translation_verse: Ni kpahi nɛ je e weku ɔ mi nɛ nyɛɛ e se ji Shemaya, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Netanel, Yuda, kɛ Hanani. Sakuhi nɛ Matsɛ David, nɛ a pɔɔ lɛ tsɛmi ke Mawu nɔmlɔ ɔ fiaa a, ni nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo hɛɛ jamɛ a saku ɔmɛ ekomɛ. Mlaa tsɔɔlɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Ezra a, nyɛɛ kuu nɛ to ɔ a hɛ mi.

english_verse: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
translation_verse: A gu Nyu Vu Agbo ɔ nya kɛ kuɔ kpoku ɔmɛ nɛ yaa David ma a mi ɔ, kɛ ya be ngɛ David mɔ ɔ he, kɛ kpale kɛ ba Nyu Agbo ɔ nya, ngɛ ma a beleku je.

english_verse: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
translation_verse: Kuu enyɔne ɔ nyɛɛ muɔ nɔ ngɛ gbogbo ɔ nɔ, nɛ i kɛ ma a fa nyɛɛ a se. Wa to kɛ nyɛɛ kɛ ya gu Flɔɔnɔɔ Mɔ ɔ nɔ, kɛ ya su Gbogbo Gbajaa he.

english_verse: Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard,
translation_verse: Wa tsa nɔ kɛ ya gu Efraim Agbo ɔ nɔ, Yeshana Agbo ɔ nɔ, Lo Agbo ɔ nɔ, Hananel Mɔ ɔ he, kɛ Lafa Mɔ ɔ he, hluu kɛ ya su To Agbo ɔ nɔ. Wa ba gbe nya ngɛ Buli Agbo ɔ nya.

english_verse: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ɔ, lali a kuu enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ ngɛ lae kɛ ngɛ Mawu si nae ɔ ba bua ngɛ Mawu we ɔ. I kɛ ma nimeli nɛ nyɛɛ ye se ɔ hu ya su lejɛ ɔ,

english_verse: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
translation_verse: kɛ osɔfo nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ a bɛ ɔmɛ kpae: Eliakim, Maaseya, Miniamin, Mikaya, Elioenai, Zakaria, kɛ Hanania.

english_verse: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
translation_verse: Ni nɛ ɔmɛ hu tsa nɔ: Maaseya, Shemaya, Eleazar, Uzi, Yehohanan, Malkiya, Elam, kɛ Ezer. Lali ɔmɛ, kɛ a nyatsɛ Yezrahia la wawɛɛ.

english_verse: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
translation_verse: A sã bɔhi babauu jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, nɛ ma a nyá saminya; ejakaa Mawu ha nɛ a bua jɔ wawɛɛ nitsɛ. Yi ɔmɛ, kɛ jokuɛwi ɔmɛ hu piɛ he kɛ ye nyami ligbi ɔ; nɛ a nu ngmlaa a he ngɛ se lokoo. A ke ní nɛ a kɛ sɔmɔ ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ

english_verse: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, nito hehi nɛ ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ, nɛ a toɔ nike níhi ngɛ a mi ɔ, a ngɔ ni komɛ ngɔ to a nya, nɛ́ a hyɛ mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka ɔmɛ, kɛ jeha mi kekleekle blɛfo ɔ, kɛ kekleekle tso yiblii nɛ fu ɔ a nɔ. Ni nɛ ɔmɛ a ní tsumi ji kaa a hyɛ nɛ a bua nike ní ɔmɛ a nya ngɛ ngmɔ ɔmɛ nɛ bɔle ma amɛ a nɔ, nɛ a kɛ ba ha osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ kaa bɔ nɛ mlaa a tsɔɔ ɔ. Yuda ma a tsuo bua jɔ osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ a he saminya;

english_verse: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
translation_verse: ejakaa a pee he julaami, kɛ kusumi kpahi nɛ Mawu fa ke a pee ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Jã kɛ̃, sɔlemi we ɔ lali ɔmɛ, kɛ buli ɔmɛ hu tsu a blɔ nya ní tsumi ɔmɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Matsɛ David kɛ e bi Salomo tsɔɔ kaa a pee ɔ.

english_verse: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
translation_verse: Lali a kuu nɛ laa yi jemi, kɛ sina lahi kɛ haa Mawu ɔ, Matsɛ David, kɛ la polɔ Asaf be ɔ mi tɔɔ nɛ a to nikɔtɔmahi ngɛ a nya.

english_verse: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_verse: Zerubabel yi nɔ, kɛ Nehemia be ɔ mi ɔ, Israel ma a tsuo ngɔɔ nike ní kɛ ba haa nɛ a kɛ hyɛ sɔlemi we ɔ lali ɔmɛ, kɛ buli ɔmɛ a nɔ daa ligbi. Ma a ngɔɔ bɔ klɔuklɔu kɛ ba haa Levi bi ɔmɛ, nɛ mɛ hu a ngɔɔ bɔ ɔ mi fa, nɛ ji osɔfo ɔmɛ a blɔ nya a kɛ haa osɔfo ɔmɛ.

english_verse: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
translation_verse: Benɛ a ngɛ mlaa a kanee, nɛ ma a tsuo ngɛ tue bue ɔ, a na he nɛ a ngma ngɛ ke a ko ngmɛ Amon no, loo Moab no ko blɔ nɛ e ba futu Mawu ma a mi bi ɔmɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
translation_verse: Benɛ ma a nu mlaa a nɛ a kane ɔ, a je nibwɔ ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ je Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti. Nehemia tsake níhi

english_verse: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
translation_verse: Osɔfo Eliashib, nɔ nɛ hyɛɛ wa Mawu ɔ we ɔ nito he tsu ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ, e huɛ ji Tobia.

english_verse: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
translation_verse: Eliashib dla tsu agbo ko ngɔ to Tobia. Jinɛ ní nɛ ɔmɛ pɛ nɛ a toɔ ngɛ tsu ɔ mi: niye ní bɔ, mimɛ, níhi nɛ a kɛ tsuɔ ní ngɛ Mawu we ɔ, bɔhi nɛ a haa osɔfo ɔmɛ, blɛfo mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka amɛ, wai, kɛ oliv nu nɛ a kɛ haa Levi bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Mawu we ɔ lali ɔmɛ, kɛ buli ɔmɛ ɔ.

english_verse: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
translation_verse: Be nɛ ɔ mi tsuo ɔ, i be Yerusalem; ejakaa Babilonia matsɛ, Artaherhes yi nɔ jeha nyingmi etɛ kɛ enyɔne ɔ mi ɔ, i ya e ngɔ nɛ i ya bɔ lɛ amaniɛ. Pee se ɔ, e ngmɛ mi blɔ,

english_verse: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
translation_verse: nɛ i kpale kɛ ba Yerusalem. Lejɛ ɔ nɛ i ya na yayami nɛ Eliashib pee kaa e je Mawu we ɔ tsu kake he gbi ha Tobia. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha nɛ ye mi mi fu wawɛɛ nitsɛ,

english_verse: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
translation_verse: nɛ i kɛ hɛdɔ ya je Tobia ní ɔmɛ tsuo kpo ngɔ hɛ pue he.

english_verse: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
translation_verse: I fa ke a sá tsu ɔmɛ a mi saminya, nɛ a ngɔ níhi nɛ a kɛ tsuɔ ní ngɛ Mawu we ɔ, kɛ ngma bɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ mimɛ ɔ kɛ ya to a hi hehi.

english_verse: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
translation_verse: I na le hu kaa Mawu we ɔ lali ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi kpa amɛ je Yerusalem kɛ ho a ngmɔhi a mi ya; ejakaa niye ní nɛ a to kaa a ha mɛ ɔ, a ha we mɛ.

english_verse: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
translation_verse: I ka ma ní tsuli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi wawɛɛ kaa a hyɛ we Mawu we ɔ nɔ bɔ nɛ sa. Jehanɛ, i kpale Levi bi ɔmɛ, kɛ lali ɔmɛ kɛ ba to a ní tsumi ɔmɛ a nya ngɛ Mawu we ɔ ekohu.

english_verse: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Israel ma a tsuo ngɔ a blɛfo, wai, kɛ oliv nu mi dlami nyɔngmanyɔngma mi kakaaka amɛ kɛ ba nito he ɔmɛ ekohu.

english_verse: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
translation_verse: I ngɔ nimli nɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ to nito he tsu ɔmɛ a nya: osɔfo Shelemia, mlaa tsɔɔlɔ Zadok, kɛ Levi no ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Pedaya a. A he piɛlɔ ji Zakur bi Hanan, Matania bibi ɔ. I le mɛ kaa anɔkuale yeli nɛ a ní tsumi ji kaa a maa dla niye ní ɔ ha a sibi ní tsuli ɔmɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
translation_verse: Mawu, i kpa mo pɛɛ, mo kai ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ i pee ɔ. Ni kpakpahi tsuo nɛ i pee kɛ ha o we ɔ, kɛ bɔ nɛ i sɔmɔ mo ɔ, o hɛ ko je nɔ.

english_verse: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, i na ni komɛ ngɛ Yuda nɛ a ngɛ wai yiblii ngae ngɛ Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ nɔ. Ni komɛ hu ngɛ tlomi fie kɛ ngɛ a tejihi a nɔ woe kɛ yaa Yerusalem. Tlomi ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ: blɛfo, wai, wai yiblii, ngmɔkɔ, kɛ ní kpa komɛ. I bɔ mɛ kɔkɔ ke Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ, a ko jua ní.

english_verse: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Tiro bi komɛ nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ, mɛ hu a ngɔɔ pa mi lo, kɛ nijua ní slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi babauu kɛ baa ma a mi, nɛ a ba juaa kɛ haa wa nyɛmimɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ ngɛ Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
translation_verse: I ka Yuda ma nimeli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ i de mɛ ke, “Nɔ́ yayami nyɛ ngɛ pee nɛ ɔ nɛ! Nyɛ ngɛ Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ blee.

english_verse: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
translation_verse: Pi níhi nɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ pee, nɛ Mawu gbla nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ Yerusalem ma a tue ɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ lo? Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ blee kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ? Anɛ nyɛ li kaa nɔ́ nɛ ɔ kɛ Mawu mi mi fumi nɛ nya wa maa ba Israel nɔ lo?”

english_verse: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i fa ke ke pu yaa nɔ si nɛ a maa je Hejɔɔmi ligbi tsuaa Hejɔɔmi ligbi yemi sisi ɔ, a nga ma agbo ɔmɛ, nɛ a ko bli kɛ yaa si Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ maa be. I ngɔ ye tsɔli ɔmɛ ekomɛ ngɔ to agbo ɔmɛ a nya, konɛ a hyɛ nɛ a ko ngɔ tlomi ko kɛ ba ma a mi Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
translation_verse: Jua yeli nɛ juaa ní slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi ba hwɔ ma a gbogbo ɔmɛ a se Soha nyɔ mi si kake loo si enyɔ.

english_verse: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ i fa Levi bi ɔmɛ ke a tsukɔ a he, nɛ a ya bu agbo ɔmɛ a nya, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a ye Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ klɔuklɔu. Ye Mawu lee, mo kai mi ngɛ enɛ ɔ hu he, nɛ o baa ye yi ngɛ o suɔmi agbo nɛ ngɛ daa a he.

english_verse: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi kɛ̃ nɛ i ná le kaa Yuda bi ɔmɛ babauu ya ngɔ yihi ngɛ Ashdod, Amon, kɛ Moab.

english_verse: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
translation_verse: A bimɛ ɔmɛ fa tuɔ Ashdod gbi, loo gbi kpa ko, nɛ a tu we Yuda gbi ɔ.

english_verse: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i ka nyumu ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ i gbiɛ mɛ; i fia ni komɛ ní, nɛ i hiaa a yi bwɔmi. Jehanɛ, i ha a kɛ Mawu biɛ ka kita ke mɛ nitsɛmɛ, kɛ a binyumu ɔmɛ be nibwɔhi a biyi ɔmɛ ngɔe, nɛ a biyi ɔmɛ hu be nibwɔhi gbae kɔkɔɔkɔ hu.

english_verse: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
translation_verse: Anɛ waa nyɛɛ nyɛ se, nɛ wa ya ngɔ ma se yihi, nɛ wa tɔ Mawu nɔ lo?”

english_verse: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
translation_verse: Osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa Eliashib bi ji Yoyada; se Yoyada bimɛ ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake ya ngɔ Sanbalat nɛ je Bet Horon ɔ biyo. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i fie Yoyada kɛ je Yerusalem.

english_verse: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Ye Mawu, mo kai bɔ nɛ jamɛ a ni ɔmɛ ble osɔfo yemi, kɛ somi nɛ o kɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ Levi bi ɔmɛ so ɔ hulɔ.

english_verse: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_verse: I to blɔ nya, konɛ a ngɔ lɛ́ nɛ a kɛ maa sã bɔ ɔ kɛ ba ngɛ be nɔ. I to be hu nɛ a maa ngɔ a kekleekle ngmɔ niba ní ɔmɛ kɛ ba. Ye Mawu, mo kai ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo, nɛ o ha nɛ e hi ha mi.

english_verse: King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled
translation_verse: Be ko ɔ, Persia matsɛ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Ahasuerus ɔ ba ye tsɛ. E matsɛ ma biɛ ji Susa. Matsɛ nɛ ɔ ye ma

english_verse: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
translation_verse: Benɛ e ngɛ tsɛ yee ɔ, jeha etɛne ɔ, e tsɛ e ganɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo ní yemi. E kpee Persia kɛ Media tabo ɔmɛ, amlaalo ɔmɛ, kɛ odehe ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ba.

english_verse: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
translation_verse: Pee se ɔ, matsɛ ɔ tsɛ Susa ma a mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo ní yemi, niatsɛmɛ kɛ ohiatsɛmɛ tsuo. A ye ní nɛ a nu ní ngɛ abɔɔ ɔ mi ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ mi otsi.

english_verse: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
translation_verse: A wo dã ha ni ɔmɛ ngɛ sika tsu kplu slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi a mi; nɛ matsɛ ɔ dã a hiɛ bɔ nɛ sa.

english_verse: and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
translation_verse: Dã nɛ a nu ɔ hiɛ babauu nitsɛ; ejakaa matsɛ ɔ wo e tsɔli ɔmɛ mlaa ke a ha nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ nu dã a bɔ nɛ e suɔ.

english_verse: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, Manyɛ Vashti hu tsɛ yi ɔmɛ ní yemi ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ mi.

english_verse: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, benɛ matsɛ ɔ nu dã nɛ e bua jɔ saminya a, e tsɛ e he buli kpaago ɔmɛ nɛ a puɛ mɛ ɔ. Mɛ ji Mehunan, Bizta, Habona, Bigta, Abagta, Zeta, kɛ Kakas.

english_verse: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: E fa mɛ ke a ya ngɔ Manyɛ Vashti kɛ ba kɛ e yi jlasi ɔ. Manyɛ Vashti he ngɛ fɛu saminya; nɛ matsɛ ɔ ngɛ hlae nɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ ni ɔmɛ nɛ e kpee kɛ ba a tsuo nɛ a na bɔ nɛ manyɛ ɔ he ngɛ fɛu ha.

english_verse: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
translation_verse: Se benɛ tsɔli ɔmɛ ya de Manyɛ Vashti ke matsɛ ɔ ke a ba ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba a, e kua bami. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha matsɛ ɔ mi mi fu wawɛɛ nitsɛ.

english_verse: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
translation_verse: E he nihi nɛ e pɔɔ tsɛmi ji Kashena, Shetar, Admata, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, kɛ Memukan. Nimli kpaago nɛ ɔmɛ ji Persia kɛ Media nɔ yemi ɔ mi ganɔhi nɛ hɛɛ blɔ nya nguaa pe kulaa.

english_verse: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
translation_verse: E de mɛ ke, “Imi Matsɛ Ahasuerus, i tsɔ nihi ke a ya ngɔ Manyɛ Vashti kɛ ba a, e kua bami. Wa mlaa a nya a, kɛ wa maa pee lɛ kɛɛ?”

english_verse: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Memukan de matsɛ ɔ, kɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ nɛ pueɔ si ɔ ke, “Pi mo matsɛ ɔ kɛkɛ o nɔ nɛ Manyɛ Vashti tɔ̃, se mohu e tɔ̃ ganɔ ɔmɛ tsuo a nɔ. Anɔkuale mi ɔ, e tɔ̃ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɔ ngɛ o nɔ yemi he ɔ!

english_verse: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
translation_verse: Yihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ o nɔ yemi he ɔ ma ba nu nɔ́ nɛ Manyɛ Vashti pee nɛ ɔ, nɛ a be a hunomɛ bue hu. A ma de ke, ‘Matsɛ Ahasuerus nitsɛ po fa ke a ya ngɔ Manyɛ Vashti kɛ ba, nɛ e kua bami’.

english_verse: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
translation_verse: Ke matsɛ ɔ ganɔhi nɛ ngɛ Persia kɛ Media a a yi ɔmɛ nu nɔ́ nɛ manyɛ ɔ pee nɛ ɔ, a ma ya sɛɛ ha a hunomɛ mwɔnɛ ɔ loko du ma bu. Jehanɛ, yigbayihi ngɛ he tsuaa he be a hunomɛ bue hu; nɛ nyumu ɔmɛ hu a mi mi ma fu a yi ɔmɛ wawɛɛ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɛnɛ, ke e sa o hɛ mi ɔ, wo mlaa ngɛ o he wami ɔ nya ke Vashti kó ba matsɛ ɔ hɛ mi gblegbleegble hu. Fa nɛ a ngma ngɔ wo Persia kɛ Media mlaa amɛ a mi, konɛ a ko tsake mlaa nɛ ɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ngɔɔ e blɔ nya kaa manyɛ ɔ ngɔ ha yo kpa nɛ ngɛ subai kpakpa pe lɛ.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Ke o wo mlaa nɛ ɔ, nɛ a fiɛ kɛ kpa o nɔ yemi he nguaa nɛ ɔ tsuo ɔ, yigbayihi tsuo maa bu a hunomɛ, nimli nguahi jio, nimli wawi jio.”

english_verse: King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said,
translation_verse: Ga nɛ Memukan wo nɛ ɔ sa matsɛ ɔ, kɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ matsɛ ɔ pee ja.

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: E tsɔ nɛ a kɛ womihi ya matsɛ ɔ nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ tsuo; a ngma munyu ɔmɛ ngɛ zugba tsuaa zugba e ningma kɛ e gbi mi ke nyumu tsuaa nyumu nɛ pee wetsɛ, nɛ ke e de nɔ́ ko ɔ, nɔ ko nɔ ko kó de nɔ́ kpa ko hu.

english_verse: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
translation_verse: Pee se, benɛ matsɛ ɔ tsui jɔ ɔ, e kai nɔ́ nɛ Vashti pee ɔ, kɛ mlaa nɛ e wo ngɛ e he ɔ.

english_verse: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e ga woli kpakpa amɛ a ti ni komɛ de lɛ ke, “Nɛnɛ, ha nɛ a hla yihewi komɛ nɛ a he ngɛ fɛu ba ha mo.

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: Ha nɛ a to nihi ngɛ o nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ tsuo, nɛ a bua yihewi nɛ a he ngɛ fɛu nɛ ɔ a nya kɛ ba matsɛ yi ɔmɛ a hi he ɔ, ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ ngɛ Susa. Ha nɛ Hegai, nyumu nɛ a puɛ lɛ, nɛ hyɛɛ o yi ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ nɛ hyɛ a nɔ. Ha nɛ a pɔ mɛ nu kɛ dla mɛ saminya.

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ngɔɔ yiheyo nɛ o suɔ pe kulaa ngɛ a kpɛti, nɛ o wo lɛ manyɛ ngɛ Vashti nane mi.” Ga nɛ a wo nɛ ɔ sa matsɛ ɔ hɛ mi, nɛ e pee ja.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Yuda no ko hi Susa ma a mi nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Mordekai. E je Benyamin wɛtso ɔ mi. E tsɛ biɛ ji Yair, e nɛ̃ ji Simei, nɛ e nɛnɛkasowa ji Kish.

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Benɛ Babilon matsɛ, Nebukadnezar ba nuu Yuda matsɛ, Yehoyakin, kɛ ni komɛ ngɛ Yerusalem kɛ ho ɔ, Mordekai hu piɛ he.

english_verse: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
translation_verse: Mordekai tsɛ nyɛminyumu ngɛ bi yiheyo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Ester; e Hebri biɛ ji Hadasa. E ji yiheyo nɛ he ngɛ fɛu, nɛ zangma pue e nɔ. Benɛ e tsɛ kɛ e nyɛ gbo ɔ, Mordekai ngɔ lɛ kaa lɛ nitsɛ e bi nɛ e hyɛ lɛ.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Benɛ matsɛ ɔ mlaa a je kpo ɔ, a ngɔ yihewi babauu kɛ ba Susa; nɛ Ester hu piɛ a he kɛ ba matsɛ we ɔ. A kɛ lɛ wo Hegai nɛ hyɛɛ matsɛ yi ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ dɛ, nɛ́ e hyɛ e nɔ.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Hegai suɔ Ester sane, nɛ e na e he bua jɔmi. E yi be ko nɛ e ha a bɔni lɛ nu pɔmi nɛ a kɛ dla lɛ; a ha lɛ niye ní kpakpa hulɔ. Hegai ngɔ Ester ya to he ko nɛ hi pe kulaa ngɛ matsɛ yi ɔmɛ a hi he ɔ, nɛ e je blɔ hla yihewi kpaago kɛ je matsɛ we ɔ, nɛ́ a sɔmɔ lɛ.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Be nɛ ɔ mi tsuo ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ Mordekai wo lɛ ga a, Ester ha we nɛ a le kaa Yuda no ji lɛ.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Daa ligbi ɔ, Mordekai ya slaa si ngɛ kue ɔ nɛ ngɛ matsɛ yi ɔmɛ a hi he ɔ hɛ mi, nɛ e kɛ hyɛɔ kaa Ester ngɛ saminya, aloo sane ko ba e nɔ lo.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ a peeɔ kɛ dlaa yi ɔmɛ a he nɛ a he peeɔ fɛu ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: a pɔɔ mɛ nu, nɛ a kpaa mɛ mimɛ nyɔhiɔ ekpa; nɛ a pɔɔ mɛ nu kɛ e he via nyɔhiɔ ekpa ekohu; lɛ tsuo peeɔ jeha kake. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a toɔ be ha yihewi ɔmɛ, nɛ a kɛ mɛ yaa Matsɛ Ahasuerus ngɔ kakaaka.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: Ke e su be nɛ yiheyo ko maa je yi ɔmɛ a hi he ɔ kɛ ya matsɛ we ɔ, a ma ha lɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e suɔ nɛ e kɛ dla e he.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: E maa ya matsɛ we ɔ gbɔkuɛ, nɛ ke je na mɔtu ɔ, a kɛ lɛ maa ya matsɛ yi ɔmɛ a hi he kpa, ya ha Shaashgaz. Shaashgaz nɛ ɔ ji nyumu nɛ a puɛ lɛ nɛ hyɛɛ matsɛ plã amɛ a nɔ. Yiheyo nɛ ɔ be matsɛ ɔ ngɔ yae hu, ja matsɛ ɔ ná e he bua jɔmi, nɛ e wo e biɛ ta, nɛ e tsɔ ke a ya ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba ekohu.

english_verse: Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
translation_verse: Benɛ Matsɛ Ahasuerus ngɛ tsɛ yee ɔ we jeha kpaagone ɔ we nyɔhiɔ nyɔngmane ɔ nɛ a kɛ Ester ba e ngɔ ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ nɛ. Nyɔhiɔ nɛ ɔ biɛ ji Tebet.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ suɔ Ester pe yihewi kpa amɛ tsuo, nɛ e bua jɔ Ester he pe mɛ tsuo. Matsɛ Ahasuerus ngɔ jlasi ɔ ngɔ bu Ester, nɛ e wo lɛ manyɛ ngɛ Vashti nane mi.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, matsɛ ɔ tsɛ e ganɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ ní yemi ko nɛ sɔ saminya, nɛ e kɛ wo Manyɛ Ester hɛ mi nyami. E ha a fiɛ ngɛ e nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ tsuo ke a jɔɔ a he; nɛ e dla nike ní bɔ nɛ sa matsɛ ngɔ ha mɛ. Mordekai he matsɛ ɔ yi wami

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Benɛ a ma bua yihewi ɔmɛ a nya si enyɔne ɔ, jamɛ a be ɔ, matsɛ ɔ ha Mordekai ba pee tsɔlɔ nɔkɔtɔma.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Mordekai nu nɔ́ nɛ ɔ he, nɛ e ya sɛɛ ha Manyɛ Ester, nɛ lɛ hu e ya de matsɛ ɔ nɔ́ nɛ Mordekai ba de lɛ ɔ.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Benɛ a hla sane ɔ mi ɔ, a na kaa sane ɔ ngɛ mi niinɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a sɛu ni enyɔ nɛ ɔmɛ. Matsɛ Ahasuerus fa nɛ a ngma sane nɛ ɔ ngɔ wo e yi nɔ sanehi womi ɔ mi.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔmɛ a se ɔ, Matsɛ Ahasuerus wó nyumu ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Haman nɔ, nɛ e pee lɛ e ganɔ ɔmɛ a nɔkɔtɔma. Hamedata bi Haman ɔ, Agag nina ji lɛ.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Matsɛ ɔ fa e tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ ngɛ e sisi ɔ ke a bu Haman, nɛ a kpla si kɛ ha lɛ. Ni ɔmɛ tsuo peeɔ ja, se Mordekai kpla we si ha lɛ fɛɛ!

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Ester kɛ matsɛ ɔ tu munyu. E kpla si kɛ e hɛ mi vo nyu ngɛ matsɛ ɔ nane nya, nɛ e kpa lɛ pɛɛ ke e pee nɔ́ ko kɛ tsi yi mi tomi yaya nɛ Agag nina Haman to ngɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ a he ɔ nya.

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: “Ke nɛnɛ suɔ ye sane, nɛ e sa nɛnɛ hɛ mi, nɛ e da ha lɛ ɔ, lɛɛ i kpa nɛnɛ pɛɛ, nɛ e ha nɛ a fiɛ kɛ tsi mlaa yaya nɛ Agag nina, Hamedata bi Haman wo ɔ nya. Mlaa a ke a kpata Yuda bi tsuo a hɛ mi ngɛ nɛnɛ nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ke amanehlu nɛ ɔ ba ma a nɔ, nɛ́ a ma kpata imi nitsɛ ye nyɛmimɛ a hɛ mi ɔ, kɛ ma pee kɛɛ?”

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Matsɛ Ahasuerus de Manyɛ Ester kɛ Mordekai, Yuda no ɔ ke, “Nyɛɛ hyɛ, i ha a sɛu Haman ngɛ yi mi yaya nɛ e to ngɔ wo Yuda bi ɔmɛ a he ɔ he, nɛ i ngɔ e weto ní ngɔ ha Manyɛ Ester.

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Mordekai hyɛ nɛ a ngma womi ɔmɛ ngɛ Matsɛ Ahasuerus biɛ mi, nɛ a sɔu nya kɛ matsɛ ɔ womi nya sɔumi ga a. Tsɔli nɛ hi okpɔngɔhi nɛ le fo tumi saminya a nɔ ya dla womi ɔmɛ kɛ fo. A hla okpɔngɔ ɔmɛ kɛ je matsɛ ɔ nitsɛ we okpɔngɔ tsu ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: In these letters the king said: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies. A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
translation_verse: Mlaa a tsɔɔ kaa á fiɛ blɔ nya tomi nɛ ɔ ngɛ nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ a dla a he kɛ to, konɛ ke be ɔ su ɔ, a kɛ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ nɛ hwu, nɛ a kɛ ye a he lue.

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Benɛ Mordekai je matsɛ we ɔ kɛ ma a, e wo ablade tade bluu kɛ futaa, nɛ sika tsu jlasi ngɛ e yi. E wo ablade tade wuyaa nɛ a kɛ kɔbɛi kpa kpakpa lo hulɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ a he ose ngɛ Susa ma a mi; nɛ blɔ ɔmɛ tsuo a nɔ pee hoo kɛ bua jɔmi.

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ a bua jɔ kaa a je haomi mi, nɛ a nya ejakaa a hɛ mi ba nyami.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Ma tsuaa ma mi, ngɛ nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ tsuo, he nɛ a maa kane matsɛ ɔ fiɛmi ɔ ngɛ ɔ, Yuda bi ɔmɛ tsuo a bua jɔɔ a he, nɛ a yeɔ nyami ligbi; a tsɛɔ ní yemi, nɛ a nyaa wawɛɛ. Anɔkuale mi ɔ, ni kpahi babauu ba pee a he Yuda bi, ejakaa jehanɛ lɛɛ, a ngɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ gbeye yee.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Nyɔhiɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Adar a we ligbi nyɔngma kɛ etɛne ɔ ba su. Kikɛmɛ a ligbi nɛ ɔ ji be nɛ a to nɛ a kɛ mlaa nɛ matsɛ ɔ wo nɛ a fiɛ ha ma a ma bɔni ní tsumi. Ligbi nɛ ɔ kɛ̃ ji ligbi nɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ to kaa a ma kpata Yuda bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi ɔ nɛ. Se nɔ́ nɛ ba mohu ji kaa Yuda bi ɔmɛ ye a he nyɛli ɔmɛ a nɔ kunimi.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Anɔkuale mi ɔ, nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ a ganɔ ɔmɛ tsuo, amlaalo ɔmɛ, ma nɔ hyɛli ɔmɛ, kɛ tsɔli nɛ ngɛ nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ piɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ a he; ejakaa Mordekai he sawale nu mɛ tsuo.

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Mordekai ba pee nɔmlɔ ngua ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ, nɛ e biɛ pɛ ngɛ nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ tsuo; ejakaa blɔ nya nɛ e hɛɛ ɔ ngɛ nɔ kuɔe, nɛ e nɔ gbɔ we gblee.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Yuda bi ɔmɛ pee a he nyɛli ɔmɛ bɔ nɛ a suɔ. A ya tua mɛ, nɛ a kɛ klaate kpata a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, benɛ matsɛ ɔ na le nihi abɔ nɛ a gbe ngɛ matsɛ ma nɛ a tsɛɛ Susa a mi ɔ,

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Ester he nɔ ke, “Nɛnɛ, i kpa mo pɛɛ, nɔ́ nɛ a ha Yuda bi ɔmɛ pee mwɔnɛ ɔ, ha nɛ a pee ja ekohu hwɔɔ. Jehanɛ, fa nɛ a sɛu Haman binyumu nyɔngma amɛ ngɛ sɛumi tsohi a nɔ.”

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Susa a, mɛɛ lɛɛ a kɛ ligbi nyɔngma kɛ enuɔne ɔ pee a nyami ligbi, nɛ a jɔɔ a he. Ejakaa ligbi nyɔngma kɛ etɛne ɔ, kɛ nyɔngma kɛ eywiɛne ɔ, a hɛ dɔ kɛ ngɛ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi kpatae.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Yuda bi nɛ ngɛ ma wawi a mi ɔ yeɔ nyɔhiɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Adar a we ligbi nɛ ji nyɔngma kɛ eywiɛ ɔ kaa a nyami ligbi, nɛ a bua jɔɔ a he. A yeɔ ní nɛ a nuɔ ní, nɛ a kee a sibi niye ní. Nyami be nɛ a tsɛɛ Purim ɔ

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: E de mɛ ke, daa jeha a, á ye ligbi nyɔngma kɛ eywiɛne ɔ, kɛ nyɔngma kɛ enuɔne ɔ ngɛ nyɔhiɔ Adar a mi kaa he jɔɔmi ligbihi.

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: Ligbi nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ nɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ kpata a he nyɛli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi ɔ nɛ. Jinɛ nyɔhiɔ nɛ ɔ maa pee aywilɛho kɛ kɔmɔ yemi be, se e ba plɛ pee bua jɔmi kɛ nyami be mohu. Bɔ nɛ a tsɔɔ mɛ ke a ye nyami ligbi nɛ ɔmɛ ji a tsɛ nihi ní yemi, nɛ a nya; a ke a sibi, kɛ ohiatsɛmɛ niye ní, kɛ ohiatsɛmɛ hu ní kpakpahi.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ pee bɔ nɛ Mordekai tsɔɔ mɛ kaa a pee ɔ, nɛ nyami be nɛ ɔ ba plɛ pee kusumi ko nɛ a peeɔ daa jeha.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Hamedata bi Haman, Agag nina a ji Yuda bi ɔmɛ tsuo a he nyɛlɔ. E so Yuda bi ɔmɛ a yi nɔ nɛ e ma kpata mɛ tsuo a hɛ mi. E fɔ sɔ konɛ e na ligbi pɔtɛɛ nɛ a ma tsu yi wu tso ní nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Se Ester ba na matsɛ ɔ, nɛ matsɛ ɔ ngma womi kɛ tsi ga yaya nɛ Haman to kɛ ha Yuda bi ɔmɛ ɔ nya. Bɔ nɛ e ya ba ha ji kaa nɔ́ nɛ e hla kaa e maa pee Yuda bi ɔmɛ ɔ, a kɛ pee lɛ nitsɛ mohu. Lɔ ɔ ji kaa a sɛu lɛ kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, Manyɛ Ester, Abihail biyo ɔ hu ngma womi, nɛ e kɛ e he wami tsuo pi nɔ́ nɛ Mordekai ngma momo nɛ kɔɔ Purim he ɔ se kpɛii.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: E tsɔɔ hu kaa mɛ nitsɛmɛ, kɛ a nina tsuo a ye Purim ligbi ɔmɛ ngɛ a be ɔ mi tutuutu kaa bɔ nɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a wo mlaahi kɛ ha hwɔ hami, nɛ a to behi nɛ a kɛ yeɔ kɔmɔ ɔ. Bɔ nɛ Mordekai kɛ Manyɛ Ester tsuo fa ke a pee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Mlaa nɛ Manyɛ Ester wo nɛ ɔ ma Purim blɔ nya tomi ɔmɛ a nɔ mi. Nɛ a ngma kɛ wo womi mi.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Matsɛ Ahasuerus ha nɛ nihi nɛ ngɛ e nɔ yemi he ɔ ngɛ wo nya je, kɛ hue mi je tsuo tsu ní kpakpataa.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: Ní nguahi, kɛ nyakpɛ níhi tsuo nɛ e pee, kɛ sanehi tsuo nɛ kɔɔ bɔ nɛ e wo Mordekai nɔ nɛ e pee lɛ nɔkɔtɔma a, a ngma ngɛ Persia kɛ Media matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a yi nɔ sanehi womi ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Yuda no, Mordekai ji Matsɛ Ahasuerus nitsɛ e se yelɔ. E hɛɛ blɔ nya nguaa ngɛ ma, Yuda bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti, nɛ a suɔ lɛ saminya. E hlaa kaa e ma mi bi ɔmɛ nɛ a ya nɔ, nɛ e daa mi ha mɛ konɛ níhi a mi nɛ hi ha mɛ.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Nyumu ko hi si ngɛ Uz zugba a nɔ; e biɛ ji Hiob. E jaa Mawu, nɛ e yeɔ lɛ anɔkuale. Nyumu nɛ ɔ, nɔmlɔ kpakpa ji lɛ; e pee we nɔ́ nɛ dɛ blɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ bi Satan ke, “Jije o je?” Satan he nɔ ke, “I ya kpa je ɔ mi tsuo kɛ ya kɛ ba.”

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ke pee ɔ, Hiob binyumu ɔmɛ tsɛɔ ní yemi kakaaka ngɛ a we ɔmɛ a mi, nɔ tsuaa nɔ kɛ e be, nɛ a kpeeɔ a nyɛmimɛ yi etɛ ɔmɛ kɛ baa ní yemi ɔ.

english_verse: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
translation_verse: Ke a gbe ní yemi ɔ tsuo nya kikɛ nɛ ɔ, jena mɔtu ɔ, Hiob maa te si mla nɛ e maa sã sami bɔ kɛ ha e bimɛ ɔmɛ kakaaka, nɛ e kɛ maa pee mɛ klɔuklɔu. Hiob peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ daa, ejakaa e susuɔ kaa eko ɔ, e bimɛ ɔmɛ pee yayami kaa a jɛ Mawu nɛ a li a he be.

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Mawu bimɛ ɔmɛ ba bua a he nya ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi, nɛ Satan hu piɛ a he kɛ ba.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ bi lɛ ke, “Anɛ o to ye tsɔlɔ Hiob he hɛ kaa nɔ ko nɔ ko be je ɔ mi nɛ da, nɛ yeɔ anɔkuale kɛ lɛ sɔ lo? E jaa mi, nɛ e pee we nɔ́ nɛ dɛ blɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ.”

english_verse: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
translation_verse: O baa Hiob yi, kɛ e we mi bimɛ, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e ngɛ, nɛ nɔ́ ko hia we lɛ. O gbaa e ní tsumi, nɛ o wo lɛ ní babauu ngɛ zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Moo lɛɛ mo he ní ɔmɛ ngɛ e dɛ kaa e be mo gbiɛe ngɛ o hɛ mi lo!”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Satan ke, “Saminya! Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ Hiob dɛ ɔ, i ngɔ kɛ wo o dɛ. Se lɛ nitsɛ e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ lɛɛ o nine ko ta he.” Kɛkɛ nɛ Satan je Mawu he. Hiob bimɛ ɔmɛ kɛ e níhi tsuo a hɛ mi kpata

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Ligbi ko benɛ Hiob binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ e biyi ɔmɛ ngɛ ní yee nɛ a ngɛ ní nue ngɛ a nyɛminyumu nɔkɔtɔma a we ɔ mi ɔ,

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,
translation_verse: tsɔlɔ ko gbɔ fo kɛ ba Hiob ngɔ, nɛ e ba de lɛ ke, “Na amɛ ngɛ hue, nɛ teji yi ɔmɛ ngɛ ní yee ngɛ a kasa nya.

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Tlukaa a, Sabea bi ɔmɛ ba yu a nɔ, nɛ a muɔ lohwe ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ho. A gbe o tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo; imi nɔ kake too lɛ i je mi, nɛ i ba konɛ ma ba bɔ mo amaniɛ.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Benɛ e ngɛ munyu ɔ tue kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ, tsɔlɔ kpa ba nɛ e ba de ke, “Oslabai gba pue to ɔmɛ kɛ to hyɛli ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ e gbe mɛ tsuo. Imi nɔ kake too lɛ i je mi, nɛ i ba konɛ ma ba bɔ mo amaniɛ.”

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: E nya na we nɛ e nɔ si nɛ tsɔlɔ kpa ba nɛ e ba de ke, “Kaldea ní hali a kuu etɛ ba tua wɔ. A gbe o tsɔli ɔmɛ tsuo, nɛ a ngɔ afukpɔngɔ ɔmɛ kɛ je. Imi nɔ kake too lɛ i je mi, nɛ i ba konɛ ma ba bɔ mo amaniɛ.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: Benɛ lɛ hu e ngɛ munyu ɔ tue kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ, tsɔlɔ kpa ba nɛ e ba de ke, “O binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ o biyi ɔmɛ ngɛ ní yee nɛ a ngɛ ní nue ngɛ a nyɛminyumu nɔkɔtɔma a we ɔ mi.

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Hiob te da si, nɛ e kɛ aywilɛho hía tade ɔmɛ ngɛ e he, nɛ e sã e yi nɔ. E kpla si, nɛ e ngɔ e hɛ mi ngɔ bu si, nɛ e ja Mawu.

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: Hiob de ke, “Maa fɔ mi kɛ ba he gu, nɛ ma kpale kɛ ya he gu. Yawɛ lɛ ha, nɛ Yawɛ lɛ ba ngɔ kɛ ho. A je Yawɛ biɛ ɔ yi!”

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ tsuo mi ɔ, Hiob pee we yayami ko; e pia we Mawu.

english_verse: When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Ligbi ko benɛ Mawu bimɛ ɔmɛ ba bua a he nya ekohu ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi ɔ, Satan piɛ a he kɛ ba.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ bi Satan ke, “Jije o je?” Satan he nɔ ke, “I ya kpa je ɔ mi tsuo kɛ ya kɛ ba.”

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ bi lɛ ke, “Anɛ o to ye tsɔlɔ Hiob he hɛ kaa nɔ ko be je ɔ mi nɛ da, nɛ yeɔ anɔkuale kɛ lɛ sɔ lo? E jaa mi, nɛ e pee we nɔ́ nɛ dɛ blɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ. O ba nyɛ ye nɔ ke ma ha mo blɔ nɛ o ya hao lɛ, be mi nɛ e pee we yayami ko kulaa. Se kɛ ba si piɔ ɔ, Hiob ngɛ anɔkuale yee kɛ mwɔɔ.”

english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Satan he nɔ ke, “Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ nɔ ko dɛ ɔ, e ma nyɛ ngɔ kɛ ha, ke e yi ma na wami kɛkɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Moo lɛɛ moo ye e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ awi kaa e be mo gbiɛe ngɛ o hɛ mi lo!”

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de Satan ke, “Saminya! E ngɛ o dɛ mi; e hɛ mi kɛkɛ nɛ o ko kpata.”

english_verse: Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Satan si Yawɛ, nɛ e ya ha nɛ tslɔɔ fuu Hiob nɔmlɔ tso ɔ tsuo, kɛ je e nane sisi kɛ ya si e yi mi.

english_verse: Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery,
translation_verse: Hiob ho ya hi la zu mi, nɛ e ngɔ ngɛyu kɛ ngɛ e he hluae.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, e yo ɔ de lɛ ke, “Tse o ngɛ anɔkuale ɔ yee kɛ mwɔɔ! Gbiɛ Mawu, nɛ o gbo!”

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Hiob he nɔ ke, “O ngɛ munyu tue kaa bɔ nɛ yihi kuasia amɛ a ti nɔ ko maa tu munyu pɛ. Ke Mawu ha wɔ nɔ́ kpakpa a, tse wa heɔ. Lɛ ke e ha wɔ nɔ́ yaya a, wa ko ngɔ lo?” Enɛ ɔ tsuo mi ɔ, Hiob pee we yayami; e de we nɔ́ ko kɛ si we Mawu. Hiob huɛmɛ ɔmɛ

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Amanehlu nɛ ba Hiob nɔ ɔ, e huɛmɛ etɛ komɛ nu he, nɛ a je he slɔɔtohi kɛ ba konɛ a ba ye lɛ kɔmɔ nɛ a wo lɛ bua. Huɛmɛ ɔmɛ ji Elifaz nɛ je Teman ma a mi, Bildad nɛ je Shua zugba a nɔ, kɛ Zofar nɛ je Naama zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Benɛ a ma ngɛ tsitsaa a, a na Hiob, se a yo we lɛ. Benɛ a ba yo lɛ ɔ, a wo yana nɛ a nya awe. A kɛ aywilɛho hía tade ɔmɛ ngɛ a he, nɛ a fĩa bunyuku kɛ ho hiɔwe ya kɛ pue a yi mi.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a ba hi si ngɛ e kasa nya ngɛ zugba nyɔ kɛ pia ligbi kpaago sɔuu. Nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛ lɛ tu we munyu jamɛ a be ɔ tsuo, ejakaa a na kaa e ngɛ nɔ́ nae wawɛɛ nitsɛ.

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: Á gbiɛ ligbi ɔ nɛ a fɔ mi ɔ; á gbiɛ nyɔ ɔ nɛ a wo ye hɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Ha nɛ jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ nɛ pee nyɔ ku; bua jɔmi la ko nɛ ko pɛ.

english_verse: Darken its morning stars and remove all hope of light,
translation_verse: Ha nɛ nɔkɔ ɔ nɛ wo diblii; je mi nɛ ko tsɔ, nɛ je hu ko na.

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: Á gbiɛ jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ nɛ a fɔ mi ɔ, kaa e kɛ mi wo haomi kɛ aywilɛho mi.

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Mɛni he je maa ngɔ mi kɛ fɔ e tɛ nɔ? Mɛni he je lɛ e ha mi nyɔ?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: I gbo kpoo jamɛ a be ɔ mi, jinɛ amlɔ nɛ ɔ, ye he mi jɔ mi.

english_verse: with kings and their advisors whose palaces lie in ruins,
translation_verse: Jinɛ i kɛ matsɛmɛ, kɛ nɔ yeli nɛ ma mɔhi blema ko ɔ hwɔɔ si mwɔnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: Mɛni he je i gbo we ngɛ muɔ nɔ, nɛ i ko nɛ́ pu la a?

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Ngɛ gbeje ɔ, yiwutsotsɛmɛ jɔɔ nɔ haomi, nɛ nihi nɛ pɔ tɔ mɛ ɔ, jɔɔ a he.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Nimli wawi kɛ nimli nguahi tsuo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ nyɔguɛ hu ye e he.

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: A hyɛɛ gbenɔ blɔ, se gbenɔ bɛ; a hlaa yɔkɔ mohu se blɔ pe juetli.

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: Ja a gbo nɛ a pu mɛ, loko a naa bua jɔmi.

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: Mɛni he je e sa kaa a fɔ nɔ ko nɛ e ba na nɔ́ yaka, be mi nɛ níhi nɛ maa ba e nɔ hwɔɔ se ɔ, Mawu ngɔ kɛ laa lɛ?

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: I be tue mi jɔmi; i be he jɔmi; ye haomi ɔmɛ a se pui gblegbleegble.

english_verse: But now you feel discouraged when struck by trouble.
translation_verse: Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, haomi ba o nɔ nɛ o jija, nɛ o nyɛ we nya nɛ o da.

english_verse: In my experience, only those who plant seeds of evil harvest trouble,
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ imi i le ji kaa nihi nɛ huɔ yayami ngmɔ, nɛ a duɔ yayami wu ɔ, yayami yiblii lɛ a kpaa.

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Mawu ngɔɔ abofu kɛ kpataa a hɛ mi kaa bɔ nɛ ahumi puɛɔ ní ɔ.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Yiwutsotsɛmɛ huãã, nɛ a pɛɛ kaa jata, se Mawu jɔɔ a he nɛ e kũɔ a lunguhi.

english_verse: they starve, and their children are scattered. A Secret Was Told to Me
translation_verse: A gboɔ kaa jata nɛ nɛ lohwe nɛ e gbe nɛ e ye, nɛ a bimɛ ɔmɛ tsuo gbɛɛ kɛ fĩaa.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: Nɔ ko ju si ba tu mi munyu ko zaa ngɛ ablɛgbi mi be ko.

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ mumi ko ba po ye hɛ mi fli, nɛ gbeye sɔuu ha nɛ fĩɛ ngmangu pue ye nɔ.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
