translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ i kɛ̃ womi kpo kpa kɛ ha Baruk, womi ngmalɔ ɔ, nɛ e ngma munyuhi tsuo nɛ i tsɛ kɛ ha lɛ ɔ kɛ wo mi. Lɔ ɔmɛ ji munyuhi tsuo nɛ a ngma kɛ wo kekle womi kpo ɔ nɛ Yuda matsɛ, Yehoyakim sã a mi, kɛ munyu kpahi babauu nɛ piɛ he.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
translation_verse: Babilonia matsɛ, Nebukadnezar wo Zedekia, Yosia bi ɔ Yuda matsɛ ngɛ Yehoyakim bi Yehoyakin nane mi.

english_verse: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Se sɛ gbi nɛ Yawɛ kɛ ha mi ɔ, lɛ Zedekia a, kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ, kɛ ma a tsuo bui tue fɛɛ.

english_verse: Later, the Babylonian army attacked Jerusalem, but they left after learning that the Egyptian army was headed in this direction. One day, Zedekiah sent Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah to talk with me. At that time, I was free to go wherever I wanted, because I had not yet been put in prison. Jehucal and Zephaniah said, “Jeremiah, please pray to the Lord our God for us.”
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ nɔuu ɔ, Babilonia tabo ɔ ba sa Yerusalem ma a yi momo. Se benɛ a nu kaa Farao ɔ tabo ɔ je Egipt kɛ ma a, a gbee senyasenya kɛ je Yerusalem.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
translation_verse: ma ya de Zedekia ke, “Farao ɔ tabo ɔ nɛ ba piɛ o he ɔ maa kpale a se kɛ ya mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɔ ngɛ Egipt.

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Ke a je ɔ, Babilonia bi ɔmɛ maa kpale kɛ ba, nɛ a ma ba tua ma nɛ ɔ ekohu. A maa ngɔ ma a, nɛ a maa mɛ he la.

english_verse: Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before.
translation_verse: Imi Yawɛ i ngɛ nyɛ dee ke nyɛ ko sisi nyɛ he; nyɛ ko susu kaa Babilonia bi ɔmɛ be kpalee kɛ ba hu. A maa ba kokooko!

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Ke e ba mi kaa nyɛ ye Babilonia tabo ɔ tsuo nɔ, nɛ e piɛ nihi nɛ plaa kɛ pueɔ si ngɛ a bo tsuhi a mi po, jamɛatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ maa te si nɛ a maa sã ma nɛ ɔ kɛ̃.” A nu Yeremia kɛ wo tsu

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Benɛ Egipt tabo ɔ ma, nɛ Babilonia bi ɔmɛ je Yerusalem ɔ,

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: jamɛ a be ɔ, imi hu i je Yerusalem kɛ yaa Benyamin zugba a nɔ, konɛ weku weto ní ɔ nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, ma ya ngɔ ye blɔ fa mi nɔ́.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: Se benɛ i su Benyamin agbo ɔ nya a, bulɔ ko nu mi nɛ e po ye nya ke, “Babilonia bi ɔmɛ a ngɔ o tu fo kɛ yaa nɛ ɔ nɛ!” Bulɔ ɔ nɛ nu mi ɔ biɛ ji Iriya, nɛ Hanania bi Shelemia lɛɛ e bi ji lɛ.

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: I he nɔ ke, “Dɛbi! Pi Babilonia bi ɔmɛ a ngɔ nɛ i tu fo kɛ yaa!” Se Iriya bui mi tue. Mohu ɔ, e nu mi kɛ ya ha ma nimeli ɔmɛ.

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: Be ko se ɔ, Matsɛ Zedekia tsɔ nɛ a ba ngɔ mi kɛ ba e ngɔ. Nɛ e bi mi ngɛ laami mi zaa ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ mi ke, “Anɛ sɛ gbi ko je Yawɛ ngɔ lo?” I he nɔ ke, “Ee, sɛ gbi ko ba!” I ya nɔ nɛ i de lɛ ke, “A maa ngɔ mo kɛ wo Babilonia matsɛ ɔ dɛ mi.”

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, i bi Matsɛ Zedekia ke, “Mɛni yayami i pee mo, loo o tsɔli ɔmɛ, loo ma nɛ ɔ, loko nyɛ wo mi tsu ɔ?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: O gbali ɔmɛ nɛ de mo ke Babilonia matsɛ ɔ be bae nɛ e ba tua mo, loo zugba nɛ ɔ, jije a ngɛ?

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Matsɛ Zedekia fa, nɛ a ya wo mi tsu ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ kue ɔ mi. Daa ligbi ɔ a jeɔ abolo sali ɔmɛ a hi he ɔ, ba haa mi abolo bɔbɔɛ kake. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ya nɔ hluu kɛ ya si abolo ta ma a mi tsuo.

english_verse: One day, Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jehucal, and Pashhur heard me tell the people of Judah
translation_verse: Shefatia, Matan bi ɔ, Gedalia, Pashur bi ɔ, Yehukal, Shelemia bi ɔ, kɛ Pashur, Malkia bi ɔ ba nu kaa i ngɛ ma a dee ke

english_verse: that the Lord had said, “If you stay here in Jerusalem, you will die in battle or from disease or hunger, and the Babylonian army will capture the city anyway. But if you surrender to the Babylonians, they will let you live.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, a nu nɛ i de ma a ke Yawɛ de ke, “I kɛ ma nɛ ɔ ma ha Babilonia tabo ɔ, nɛ a maa ngɔ ma a.”

english_verse: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ ho nɛ a ya de matsɛ ɔ ke, “Ha nɛ a gbe nyumu nɛ ɔ. Munyuhi nɛ e ngɛ tue ɔ ha nɛ ta buli nɛ piɛ ngɛ ma a mi, kɛ nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ ma a mi ɔ a kɔni mi ngɛ jɔe. Nyumu nɛ ɔ, ma a si gbeemi e ngɛ hlae, se pi ma a nɔ yami.”

english_verse: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a nu mi nɛ a kɛ kpa siu mi kɛ wo matsɛbinyumu ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Malkia a e vu mi ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ kue ɔ mi. Nyu be vu ɔ mi; mɔsɔ kɛkɛ lɛ ngɛ mi. Nɛ i pu ngɛ mɔsɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: “Nɛnɛ, nɔ́ nɛ nimli nɛ ɔmɛ pee nɛ ɔ dɛ. Vu ɔ mi nɛ a ngɔ gbalɔ Yeremia ya wo nɛ ɔ, hwɔ maa gbe lɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ; ejakaa niye ní ta ma a mi.”

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Ebedmelek kɛ nyumu ɔmɛ ya matsɛ we ɔ, nɛ a ya hla tako piɛ, kɛ bo gbagbɛ ngɛ daka ko mi ngɛ nito he ɔ. A kɛ kpa fi ní nɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ a siu kɛ ba ha mi ngɛ vu ɔ mi.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: Ebedmelek, Etiopia no ɔ de mi ke ma ngɔ tako piɛ ɔ, kɛ bo gbagbɛ ɔ kɛ wo ye ngasi, ngɛ kpa a sisi. I pee ja,

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: kɛkɛ nɛ a kɛ tangme kpa gbla mi kɛ je vu ɔ mi, nɛ a ya wo mi tsu ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ kue ɔ mi. Zedekia bi Yeremia ga womi

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
translation_verse: Ligbi ko ɔ, Matsɛ Zedekia tsɔ nɛ a ba ngɔ mi kɛ ba e ngɔ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ agbo etɛne ɔ nya. Matsɛ ɔ de mi ke, “Ma bi mo munyu ko. O kɛ nɔ́ ko kó laa mi.”

english_verse: “Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
translation_verse: I he nɔ ke, “Ke i tu anɔkuale ɔ, o maa gbe mi, nɛ ke i wo mo ga hu, o be tue bue.”

english_verse: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Matsɛ Zedekia ka mi kita ngɛ laami mi ke, “I na Yawɛ hɛ kalɔ ɔ nɛ ha wɔ wami ɔ kaa i be mo gbee; nimli nɛ ngɛ mo hlae nɛ a gbe ɔ, mɛ hu i be mo ngɔe kɛ wo a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ i de Zedekia ke, “Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ, de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Ke o maa ya nɛ o ya nu Babilonia matsɛ ɔ ma nimeli ɔmɛ a nane ɔ, a maa ngɔ o wami kɛ ke mo, nɛ a be ma nɛ ɔ sãe. A ma he o kɛ o we ɔ tsuo nyɛ yi wami.

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Se Matsɛ Zedekia de mi ke, “Wa nyɛmimɛ Hebri bi ɔmɛ nɛ tu fo kɛ ya piɛ Babilonia bi ɔmɛ a he ɔ, i ngɛ gbeye yee kaa a maa ngɔ mi kɛ wo mɛ mohu a dɛ, nɛ a maa pee mi basabasa.”

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: I de lɛ ke, “Dɛbi, a be mo ngɔe kɛ wo a dɛ. I kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o bu Yawɛ sɛ gbi nɛ i kɛ ha mo nɛ ɔ tue. Ke o pee ja a, e maa hi ha mo, nɛ o yi ma na wami.

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: I na nɛ a ngɔ yi ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ piɛ ngɛ Yuda matsɛ we ɔ mi ɔ kɛ yaa Babilonia matsɛ ɔ ma nimeli ɔmɛ a ngɔ. Benɛ a yaa a, nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ‘Matsɛ ɔ huɛmɛ kpakpa amɛ sisi lɛ nɛ a ye e nɔ. Se amlɔ nɛ ɔ nɛ e nane pu mɔsɔ lɛɛ e huɛmɛ ɔmɛ je e he?’ ”

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, i de matsɛ ɔ ke, “A ma kpaka o yi ɔmɛ, kɛ o bimɛ ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ya ha Babilonia bi ɔmɛ, nɛ mo nitsɛ hu o be a dɛ mi jee. Babilonia matsɛ ɔ maa nu mo, nɛ ma nɛ ɔ lɛɛ a maa sã.”

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Zedekia de mi ke, “Ko ha nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko nɛ le nɔ́ nɛ i kɛ mo sɛɛ nɛ ɔ. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a be mo gbee.

english_verse: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
translation_verse: Ke ma nimeli ɔmɛ nu kaa i kɛ mo sɛɛ ní ɔ, a ma ba bi mo nɔ́ nɛ i kɛ mo sɛɛ ɔ. A maa wo mo si ke o de mɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́, kɛkɛ a be mo gbee.

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: Ke a ba o ngɔ kɛ munyu kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ, moo lɛɛ de mɛ ke pe o ba fa kue ha mi nɛ ma ko ha nɛ a ngɔ mo kɛ ya wo tsu hu, nɛ o ba gbo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Ma nimeli ɔmɛ tsuo ba nɛ a ba bi mi munyu, nɛ imi hu i ha mɛ heto pɛpɛɛpɛ kaa bɔ nɛ matsɛ ɔ tsɔɔ mi ke ma de mɛ ɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ a kpa ye nya doomi, ejakaa ní ɔ nɛ i kɛ matsɛ ɔ sɛɛ ɔ, nɔ ko nɔ ko nui he.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: I hi tsu ɔ mi ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ kue ɔ mi kɛ ya si a ba ngɔ Yerusalem.

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Benɛ Yuda matsɛ, Zedekia kɛ e ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo na mɛ ɔ, a tu fo kɛ je ma a mi nyɔ ɔ mi. A gu matsɛ abɔɔ ɔ mi, kɛ ya be ngɛ agbo ɔ nɛ ngɛ gbogbo enyɔ ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ, nɛ a tu fo kɛ yaa Yordan kɔ̃ ɔ mi je.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: ke ma ya de Ebedmelek, Etiopia no ɔ ke bɔ nɛ lɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ, de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Kaa bɔ nɛ i de to ɔ, ma ha nɛ haomi maa ba ma nɛ ɔ nɔ, se pi nɔ́ kpakpa. Nɛ ke nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ba a, o maa na paa kɛ o hɛngmɛ.

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: “Yaa nɛ o ya ngɔ Yeremia, nɛ o hyɛ e nɔ saminya. Koo pee lɛ yayami ko; se mohu nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e ngɛ hlae ɔ, pee ha lɛ.”

english_verse: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
translation_verse: Se Babilonia tabo ɔ nyɛɛ a se, nɛ a ya nu Zedekia ngɛ Yeriko nga a nɔ. A ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba ha Matsɛ Nebukadnezar ngɛ Ribla, ngɛ Hamat zugba a nɔ. Nɛ lejɛ ɔ Nebukadnezar kojo lɛ nɛ e bu lɛ fɔ ngɛ.

english_verse: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.
translation_verse: Babilonia matsɛ ɔ gbe Zedekia bimɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ Zedekia hɛ mi. E gbe Yuda ma nimeli ɔmɛ tsuo ja nɔuu.

english_verse: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ta Zedekia hɛngmɛ. E ha nɛ a bɔ lɛ pã, nɛ a ngɔ lɛ kɛ ho Babilonia ya.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Babilonia bi ɔmɛ sã matsɛ we ɔ, kɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ a wehi, nɛ a ku Yerusalem gbogbo ɔmɛ ngɔ pue si.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan, tatsɛ ɔ nuu nihi nɛ piɛ ngɛ ma a mi ɔ, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ ku kɛ ba piɛ e he ɔ kɛ ho Babilonia ya.

english_verse: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Se Nebuzaradan, tatsɛ ɔ si ohiatsɛmɛ komɛ nɛ weto ní be a dɛ ngɛ Yuda zugba a nɔ, nɛ e ha mɛ wai ngmɔhi kɛ zugba. A je Yeremia ngɛ tsu mi

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan:
translation_verse: Babilonia matsɛ, Nebukadnezar fa Nebuzaradan, tatsɛ ɔ fami nɛ ɔ nɛ kɔɔ Yeremia he ke,

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, Nebushazban, Nergal Sharezer, and the other officers of King Nebuchadnezzar
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Nebuzaradan, tatsɛ ɔ, kɛ asafoatsɛnguahi Nebushazban kɛ Nergal Sarezer, kɛ Babilonia matsɛ we asafoatsɛngua kpa amɛ tsuo

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: ba ngɔ mi kɛ je tsu ɔ mi ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ. A ngɔ mi kɛ wo Shafan bi Ahikam bi Gedalia dɛ, konɛ e hyɛ nɛ ma ya su we mi. Nɛ i hi ye ma mi bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti. Hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi ngɛ ha Ebedmelek

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Benɛ i ngɛ tsu mi ngɛ matsɛ we ɔ kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ, Yawɛ de mi

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ma baa o yi, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be mo gbee. O maa ye o he, ejakaa o ngɔ o hɛ kɛ fɔ ye nɔ. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan, tatsɛ ɔ, ngɔ mi ngɛ pã mi kɛ ya Rama. I piɛ Yuda ma a, kɛ Yerusalem ma mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ a nuu kɛ yaa Babilonia a a he. Se imi lɛɛ e ngmɛɛ ye he ngɛ Rama, nɛ Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan said: Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land.
translation_verse: Tatsɛ ɔ tsɛ mi kɛ ya se, nɛ e de mi ke, “Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ de to ke e ma kpata zugba nɛ ɔ hɛ mi.

english_verse: But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
translation_verse: Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, Yawɛ ná pee nɔ́ nɛ e de to ke e maa pee ɔ. Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ba nyɛ nɔ, ejakaa nyɛ pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ, nɛ nyɛ bui lɛ tue.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i ngɛ pã nɛ ɔ jee ngɛ o kɔni si mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ. Ke o suɔ kaa o kɛ mi maa ya Babilonia a, i kɛ mo maa ya nɛ ma ya hyɛ o nɔ saminya ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Se ke e dɛ ha mo kaa o kɛ mi maa ya a, lɛɛ mo ko ya. Hyɛ, zugba a tsuo lɛ ngɛ o hɛ mi nɛ ɔ nɛ. He tsuaa he nɛ hi ha mo nɛ o suɔ kaa o maa ya a, yaa.”

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ i je kɛ ho Ahikam bi Gedalia ngɔ ya ngɛ Mizpa, nɛ i kɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ ya hi si. Gedalia, Yuda amlaalo ɔ (Matsɛmɛ II,

english_verse: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, together with Johanan and Jonathan, the two sons of Kareah, had been officers in Judah's army. And so had Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah from Maacah. They and their troops had been stationed outside Jerusalem and had not been captured. They heard that Gedaliah had been chosen to rule Judah, and that the poorest men, women, and children had not been taken away to Babylonia. So they went to Mizpah and met with their new ruler.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nimli nɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ a we bi ɔmɛ tsuo ba Gedalia ngɔ ngɛ Mizpa. Mɛ ji Ishmael, Natania bi ɔ, Yohanan, Karea bi ɔ, Seraya, Tanhumet bi ɔ, Efai nɛ je Netofa a bimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ Yezania nɛ je Maaka a.

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Gedalia de mɛ ke, “I ngɛ nyɛ kita kae kaa nyɛ ko ye gbeye kaa nyɛ maa ngɔ nyɛ he ya ha Babilonia bi ɔmɛ. Nyɛɛ hi zugba a nɔ, nɛ nyɛ sɔmɔ Babilonia matsɛ ɔ, kɛkɛ e maa hi ha nyɛ.

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Imi nitsɛ lɛɛ ma hi Mizpa kaa nyɛ nya dalɔ, nɛ ke Babilonia bi ɔmɛ ba hiɛ ɔ, ma tu munyu ha nyɛ. Se nyɛɛ lɛɛ nyɛ ya bua wai, kɛ tso yibliihi, kɛ oliv nu nya kɛ to, nɛ nyɛɛ hi mahi nɛ nyɛ ngɔ ɔ a mi.”

english_verse: Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. So the Jews in these other countries came back to Judah and helped with the grape and fruit harvest, which was especially large that year. Gedaliah Is Murdered
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a je hehi tsuo nɛ a fie mɛ kɛ ho ɔ, nɛ a kpale kɛ ba Yuda zugba a nɔ. A ba Gedalia ngɔ ngɛ Mizpa, nɛ a ba bua wai kɛ tso yibliihi babauu nya ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. A gbe Gedalia (Matsɛmɛ II,

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, Yohanan, Karea bi ɔ, kɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ ta nga a nɔ nɛ mɛɛ lɛɛ a ngɔɛ a he ya ha we Babilonia bi ɔmɛ ɔ, ba Gedalia ngɔ ngɛ Mizpa.

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: A ba de lɛ ke, “Anɛ o li kaa Amon matsɛ, Baalis tsɔ Netania bi Ishmael kɛ ba nɛ a ba gbe mo lo?” Se Gedalia he we mɛ yi.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yohanan de lɛ ngɛ laami mi ke, “Ha nɛ ma ya nɛ ma ya gbe Ishmael, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be lee. Mɛni he je e sa kaa e gbe mo ɔ? Ke e pee ja a, Yuda bi tsuo nɛ ba bua a he nya ngɛ o ngɔ ɔ maa gbɛ fĩa, nɛ Yuda ma nɛ piɛ ɔ a hɛ mi ma kpata.”

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Se Gedalia he nɔ ke, “Koo pee ja! Nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ dee ngɛ Ishmael he ɔ be mi!”

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a jeha a mi nɔuu, nyɔhiɔ kpaago ɔ mi ɔ, Elishama bi Netania bi Ishmael kɛ nyumuhi nyɔngma ba Gedalia ngɔ ngɛ Mizpa. Ishmael je matsɛ we mi, nɛ matsɛ tsɔli nikɔtɔma amɛ a kpɛti nɔ kake ji lɛ. Benɛ mɛ tsuo a bua nɛ a ngɛ ní yee ɔ,

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Ishmael kɛ nyumuhi nyɔngma nɛ piɛ e he ɔ hia klaate wo Gedalia he, nɛ a gbe lɛ.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Israel bi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Gedalia ngɔ ngɛ Mizpa, kɛ Babilonia ta buli nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, Ishmael gbe mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: E nɔ jena benɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko nui he lolo kaa a gbe Gedalia a,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Ishmael, Netania bi ɔ je Mizpa ya kpee mɛ; benɛ e yaa a tsuo, e ngɛ ya foe ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ. Benɛ e kɛ mɛ ya bua a, e de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ba waa ho Ahikam bi Gedalia ngɔ ya.”

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Benɛ a ba su ma a mi pɛ, Ishmael kɛ e we bi ɔmɛ gbe mɛ, nɛ a sake a gbogboe ɔmɛ kɛ wo vu ko mi.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Se a ti ni nyɔngma de Ishmael ke, “Koo gbe wɔ! Wa ngɔ ngma, blɛfo, oliv nu, kɛ hwo ngɔ laa ngɛ nga a mi.” Kɛkɛ nɛ e ngmɛɛ a he, nɛ e gbi mɛ ngɔ piɛ a nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a he.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Vu ɔ nɛ Ishmael sake nihi tsuo nɛ e gbe ɔ a gbogboe ɔmɛ kɛ wo mi ɔ, jamɛ a vu ɔ, Matsɛ Asa lɛ tsua. Matsɛ ɔ tsua vu nɛ ɔ be mi nɛ Israel matsɛ, Baasha ba tua lɛ ɔ. Vu nɛ ɔ mi lɛ Netania bi Ishmael sake ni gbogboe ɔmɛ kɛ wo tɔ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Ishmael nuu nihi tsuo nɛ piɛ ngɛ Mizpa a kɛ je. Matsɛbiyi ɔmɛ, kɛ nihi tsuo nɛ tatsɛ Nebuzaradan ngɔ kɛ wo Ahikam bi Gedalia dɛ mi po, Ishmael nuu mɛ, nɛ e kɛ mɛ pue nɔ kɛ yaa Amon bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: a ngɔ a ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ nyɛɛ e se konɛ a kɛ lɛ ya hwu ta. A ya na lɛ ngɛ taku agbo ɔ nɛ ngɛ Gibeon ɔ kasa nya.

english_verse: When Ishmael's prisoners saw Johanan and the officers, they were happy
translation_verse: Benɛ ni ɔmɛ nɛ Ishmael nuu ɔ na Karea bi Yohanan, kɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ e he ɔ, a nya.

english_verse: and turned around and ran toward Johanan.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a tu fo kɛ ba Yohanan ngɔ.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Se Ishmael kɛ e we bi kpaanyɔ komɛ lɛɛ a je Yohanan dɛ mi, nɛ a tu fo kɛ ho Amon bi ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ ya.

english_verse: Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, ni ɔmɛ nɛ Netania bi Ishmael nuu kɛ je Mizpa kɛ yaa benɛ e gbe Ahikam bi Gedalia se ɔ, Yohanan kɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ e he ɔ ba ngɔ mɛ: ta buli, yihi, jokuɛwi, kɛ nyumuhi nɛ a puɛ mɛ.

english_verse: toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar. The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_verse: A ye Babilonia bi ɔmɛ gbeye, ejakaa Netania bi Ishmael gbe Ahikam bi Gedalia, nɔ nɛ Babilonia matsɛ ɔ nitsɛ ngɔ to a nya kaa amlaalo ɔ. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a plɛ a hɛ mi ngɔ ka Egipt blɔ, konɛ a tu fo kɛ je Babilonia bi ɔmɛ a nya. Benɛ a yaa a, a ya to si ngɛ Kimham, ngɛ Betlehem kasa nya.

english_verse: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Karea bi Yohanan, Heshaya bi Azaria, kɛ tatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ ma a tsuo; nimli wawi kɛ nimli nguahi

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: Kpa Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ pɛɛ konɛ e tsɔɔ wɔ blɔ nɛ wa maa nyɛɛ nɔ, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ sa wɔ peemi.”

english_verse: even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
translation_verse: Wa suɔ jio, wa sume jio, wa maa bu Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ nɛ wa tsɔ mo e ngɔ ɔ tue, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ e hi ha wɔ. Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ, wa maa bu lɛ tue.” Yawɛ ha Yeremia heto

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Ligbi nyɔngma se ɔ, Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu;

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: nɛ i de mɛ ke, “Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ nɛ nyɛ tsɔ mi e ngɔ ke ma ya kpa lɛ pɛɛ ha nyɛ ɔ, bɔ nɛ e de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ:

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: ‘Ke nyɛ maa hi zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ, lɛɛ ma gbaa nyɛ, nɛ i be nyɛ hɛ mi kpatae; ma to nyɛ si, nɛ i be nyɛ hiae hu. E dɔ mi babauu kaa i gbla nyɛ tue kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him,
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko ye Babilonia matsɛ ɔ gbeye hu. I kɛ nyɛ ngɛ, nɛ ma je nyɛ kɛ je e dɛ mi.

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: Ma na nyɛ mɔbɔ, nɛ lɛ hu e maa na nyɛ mɔbɔ, nɛ e ma ha nɛ nyɛɛ kpale kɛ ya nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ zugba a nɔ. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.’

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ti nihi tsuo nɛ maa pee a yi mi kaa a ma ya hi Egipt ɔ, ke a nɔɛ ta a, lɛɛ mi mi hwɔ, loo gbenɔ hiɔ maa gbe mɛ. Tue gblami nɛ i kɛ maa ba jamɛatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ, nɔ ko nɔ ko be piɛe, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko hu he be mi jee.’

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: “Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ ke, ‘Bɔ nɛ i ngɔ ye mi mi la nɛ nya wa a kɛ kple Yerusalem ma mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ, ja pɛ ma pee nyɛ ke nyɛ je kɛ ho Egipt ya. Nyɛ ma plɛ pee kita kami nɔ́, gbeye nɔ́, gbiɛmi nɔ́, kɛ ahlua nɔ́. Nyɛ be hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ nae hu.’ ”

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: I ya nɔ nɛ i de ke, “Nyɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ nyɛ piɛ ngɛ Yuda a, Yawɛ de nyɛ ke, ‘Nyɛ ko ya Egipt.’ Nyɛ ná nɛ nyɛɛ le kaa i bɔ nyɛ kɔkɔ mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ,

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: kaa blɔ nɛ nyɛ hia a, blɔ ɔ dɛ, nɛ tue gblami nɛ maa nyɛɛ se ɔ, nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ wami ma he. Nyɛ de mi ke ma kpa Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ pɛɛ ha nyɛ, nɛ nyɛ wo si ke nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ ma fa nyɛ ke nyɛɛ pee ɔ, nyɛ maa pee.

english_verse: I told the people everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: I bɔ ma a níhi tsuo nɛ Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ tsɔ mi ke ma ba de mɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: Benɛ i gbe nya a, Hoshaya bi Azaria, Karea bi Yohanan, kɛ nyumuhi he nɔ woli kpa amɛ tsuo de mi ke, “Lakpa munyu o ngɛ tue nɛ ɔ nɛ. Yawɛ, wa Mawu ɔ tsɔ we mo ke o ba de wɔ ke wa ko ya hi Egipt.

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Neria bi Baruk ji nɔ nɛ wo o yi mi nɛ e su mo kɛ wo wa he. E pee enɛ ɔ konɛ e ngɔ wɔ kɛ wo Babilonia bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi nɛ a gbe wɔ, loo a nuu wɔ kɛ ya Babilonia.”

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, fami ɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa ke a hi Yuda zugba a nɔ ɔ, nɔ ko nɔ ko bui fɛɛ, Karea bi Yohanan jio, asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ jio, ma a jio.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yohanan, kɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɔ nihi tsuo nɛ piɛ ngɛ Yuda a kɛ ho Egipt ya. Ni nɛmɛ nɛ a fie kɛ ho je ma amɛ a nɔ ya nɛ a kpale kɛ ba a, jamɛatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ hu piɛ he,

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: nyumuhi, yihi, jokuɛwi, kɛ matsɛbiyihi. Imi Yeremia, Neria bi Baruk, kɛ nihi tsuo nɛ tatsɛ Nebuzaradan si ha Gedalia nɛ e ngɛ a nɔ hyɛe ɔ, wɔ hu wa piɛ nihi nɛ a ngɔ kɛ ho ɔ a he.

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: A bui Yawɛ munyu ɔ tue, nɛ a je kɛ ho Egipt zugba a nɔ ya, kɛ ya su Tapanhes tɔɔ.

english_verse: when the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Benɛ wa ngɛ Tapanhes ɔ, Yawɛ de mi ke,

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: “Yaa hla tɛ agboagbo komɛ nɛ o pu ngɛ zu mi ngɛ he nɛ a ka tɛ ngɛ, ngɛ Egipt matsɛ ɔ we ɔ hɛ mi ɔ. Ke o ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ pee ɔ, ha nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ a na mo.

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: De mɛ ke imi Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ, i yaa ngɔ Babilonia matsɛ Nebukadnezar, ye tsɔlɔ ɔ kɛ ba hiɛ ɔ. E maa ngɔ e matsɛ sɛ ɔ ba ma tɛ nɛ nyɛ pu ɔ nɔ, nɛ e kɛ e we akatabai ɔ maa ma lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I will let him set Egypt's temples on fire, and he will either burn or carry off their idols. He will destroy the sacred monuments at the temple of the sun-god. Then Nebuchadnezzar will pick the land clean, just like a shepherd picking the lice off his clothes. And he will return safely home.
translation_verse: E maa ku amagahi nɛ a kɛ tɛ pee, nɛ maa si ngɛ Heliopolis ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ, nɛ e maa sã Egipt mawu ɔmɛ a jami he ɔmɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Yawɛ ha mi sɛ gbi nɛ ɔ nɛ kɔɔ Israel bi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Egipt ɔ a he, nihi nɛ ngɛ Migdol, Tapanhes, kɛ Memfis ma amɛ a mi, kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ zugba a leneyi je ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ ke, “Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ na bɔ nɛ i kpata Yerusalem, kɛ Yuda ma kpa amɛ a hɛ mi. Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, ma amɛ pee ma dokuhi nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be a mi,

english_verse: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
translation_verse: ejakaa ma amɛ a mi bi ɔmɛ pee yayami, nɛ a wo ye mi mi la. A sã bɔhi nɛ a kɛ sɔmɔ mawu kpahi nɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ, loo nyɛ, loo nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ po li gblee.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: Daa nɛ ɔ, i tsɔɔ ye tsɔli gbali ɔmɛ kɛ baa nyɛ ngɔ, nɛ a ba deɔ nyɛ ke nyɛ ko pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, ejakaa i hie.

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Se kɛ ba si mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, nyɛ bɛ nyɛ he si. Nyɛ wui ye hɛ mi nyami, nɛ mlaahi tsuo nɛ i wo nyɛ, kɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, nyɛ yi mlaa amɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Yuda bi nɛ piɛ, nɛ a to a yi mi kaa a maa ya Egipt nɛ a ya hi lejɛ ɔ, ma hyɛ nɛ a kpata mɛ tsuo a hɛ mi. Mɛ tsuo a ma gbo ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ, nimli wawi, kɛ nimli nguahi tsuo. Ni komɛ ma gbo ngɛ ta mi, nɛ hwɔ maa gbe ni komɛ. Nihi maa hie mɛ; a maa bɔ mɛ ahlua, nɛ a kɛ a biɛ maa gbiɛ nɔ.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ ta, hwɔ, kɛ gbenɔ hiɔ kɛ gbla nihi nɛ ngɛ Egipt ɔ a tue kaa bɔ nɛ i gbla Yerusalem tue ɔ.

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Yuda bi nɛ piɛ, nɛ a ho Egipt ya nɛ a ya hi lejɛ ɔ, a ti nɔ ko he be mi jee, nɛ nɔ ko yi be wami nae. Yuda zugba a nɛ a ko suɔ nɛ a ba hi mi ekohu ɔ, a ti nihi bɔɔ kɛkɛ lɛ a maa kpale kɛ ba lejɛ ɔ; pi mɛ tsuo.”

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Nyumuhi tsuo nɛ le kaa a yihi sãã tsopa kɛ e he via kɛ haa mawu kpahi, yihi tsuo nɛ daa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, kɛ Israel bi nɛ ngɛ Egipt leneyi je ɔ, nimli babauu nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo de mi ke,

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: “Munyu ɔ nɛ o kɛ wɔ tu ngɛ Yawɛ biɛ mi ɔ, wa be tue bue fɛɛ.

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Níhi tsuo nɛ wa de ke wa maa pee ɔ, lɔ ɔmɛ wa maa pee. Wa maa sã tsopa kɛ e he via kɛ ha wa yo mawu ɔ nɛ ji hiɔwe manyɛ ɔ, nɛ wa maa sã wai bɔ ha lɛ kaa bɔ nɛ waa kɛ wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ, wa matsɛ ɔ, kɛ wa ma nimeli ɔmɛ pee be ko ngɛ Yuda ma amɛ a mi, kɛ Yerusalem gbɛjegbɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ. Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, wa ngɛ niye ní babauu; wa plɔke, nɛ haomi ko be wa nɔ.

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Se kɛ je be mi nɛ wa kpa tsopa kɛ e he via, kɛ wai bɔ sami kɛ ha hiɔwe manyɛ ɔ, wa yi fi wawɛɛ nitsɛ; nɛ ta, kɛ mi mi hwɔ ngɛ wɔ gbee.”

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Yi ɔmɛ de kɛ piɛ he ke, “Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, tse wa bɔɔ keeki kaa bɔ nɛ hiɔwe manyɛ ɔ su ngɛ ɔ, nɛ́ wa sãã? Tse wa sãã tsopa kɛ e he via kɛ haa hiɔwe manyɛ ɔ, nɛ wa sãã wai bɔ haa lɛ? Anɛ tsa pi wa hunomɛ ɔmɛ a gbi nɔ nɛ wa peeɔ níhi kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔmɛ lo?”

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: “Tsopa kɛ e he via nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ, nyɛ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, nyɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ, kɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ sã ngɛ Yuda ma amɛ a mi, kɛ Yerusalem gbɛjegbɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ, anɛ nyɛ susu kaa Yawɛ li lo? Nyɛ bu kaa e hɛ je nɔ?

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: Mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, nyɛ zugba a hɛ mi kpata, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be nɔ. Nyɛ zugba a plɛ pee nɔ́ ko nɛ a hiee, nɛ nihi kɛ e biɛ gbiɛɛ nɔ; ejakaa nyɛ yi wu tso ní peemi ɔmɛ, kɛ nyɛ yayami ɔmɛ ba ti Yawɛ.

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: Se jehanɛ, nyɛ Israel bi tsuo nɛ nyɛ ngɛ Egipt, nyɛɛ bu kita nguaa nɛ imi, Yawɛ hu i ka ye he, ngɛ ye biɛ kpetekpleenyɛ ɔ mi ɔ tue. Kɛ je mwɔnɛ ɔ kɛ yaa a, i be nyɛ ti nɔ ko nɔ ko blɔ ngmɛe hu nɛ e ngɔ ye biɛ kɛ ka kita nɛ e de ke, ‘I na Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, hɛ kalɔ ɔ!’

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Se nyɛ ti nihi bɔɔ ko kɛ̃ a he maa je mi, nɛ a maa kpale kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ kɛ ya Yuda zugba a nɔ. Jamɛ a be ɔ loko nihi nɛ a yi na wami ɔ maa le kaa imi lɛ ye munyu ba mi, aloo mɛ.

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
translation_verse: Yuda matsɛ, Yehoyakim, Yosia bi ɔ yi nɔ jeha nɛ ji eywiɛ ɔ mi ɔ, Neria bi Baruk ngma munyu ɔ nɛ i de lɛ ke e ngma a. Kɛkɛ nɛ i de lɛ ke,

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: munyu nɛ ngɛ o nya jee ji, ‘Jehanɛ lɛɛ ye yi ta pɛ! Ejakaa Yawɛ pa ngɔ aywilɛho kɛ piɛ ye haomi ɔ he. Ye kɛmɛmi ɔ nya ba wa tsɔ, nɛ i be he jɔmi!’

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Moo lɛɛ ní nguahi o ngɛ hlae ha o he? Ko hla! Ejakaa ma ngɔ haomi kɛ ba adesahi tsuo a nɔ. Se moo lɛɛ he tsuaa he nɛ o maa gu ɔ, o he maa je mi. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: e je sisi kɛ je Egipt nɔ. Egipt matsɛ, Neko tabo ɔ nɛ Babilonia matsɛ, Nebukadnezar ye a nɔ ngɛ Karkemish, ngɛ Yufrate pa a nya a, bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ngɛ a he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Sane nɛ ɔ ba ngɛ Yuda matsɛ, Yehoyakim yi nɔ jeha eywiɛne ɔ mi.

english_verse: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
translation_verse: “Egipt asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ kpa ngmlaa ke, ‘Nyɛ dla nyɛ he kɛ nyɛ tsɛi ɔmɛ, nɛ nyɛɛ hia ta!

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ a he sɔɔ wawɛɛ po, a he be mi jee; ta buli kpanakpanaa amɛ hu, ja nɔuu. A ma tɛ nɔ́, nɛ a maa nɔɔ si ngɛ omleyi je, ngɛ Yufrate pa a nya.

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: Mɛnɔ lɛ ma nɛ ɔ, kaa Nilo pa a, kaa pa nɛ hia lalaala kɛ ha zugba a tsuo hɛ mi ɔ?

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Nyɛ okpɔngɔhi, nyɛɛ ya nyɛ hɛ mi esɔ. Nyɛ zugba lɛhi, nyɛ sa fo! Nyɛ katsɛmɛ, nyɛɛ je kpo: Sudan kɛ Libia tsɛi hɛɛli, kɛ Lidia kɛ̃ɛ̃ tsɛ̃li nɛ nyɛ nine nya da.’ ”

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ ligbi ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ; mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, Yawɛ maa ye e he lue; mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, e maa gbla e he nyɛli ɔmɛ a tue. Yawɛ klaate ɔ maa pee kaa nɔ ko nɛ ye ní nɛ e tɔ, aloo nɔ ko nɛ nu muɔ nɛ e de kaa dã. Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ ngɔ e he nyɛli ɔmɛ kɛ ngɛ bɔ sãe ngɛ omleyi je, ngɛ Yufrate pa a tue.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Je ma amɛ nu kaa nyɛ hɛ mi pue si; nɔ tsuaa nɔ nu ngmlaa nɛ nyɛ ngɛ kpae ɔ. Katsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ a sibi tɛe, nɛ a ngɛ si nɔɔe. Nebukadnezar ba

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: “Nyɛɛ fiɛ ngɛ Egipt ma amɛ a mi, ngɛ Migdol, Memfis, kɛ Tapanhes ke, ‘Nyɛɛ mia, nɛ nyɛɛ pee klaalo, ejakaa ta ngɛ ní puɛe ngɛ mahi nɛ bɔle nyɛ ɔ a mi kɛ ma!

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: Imi Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ, imi ji Mawu hɛ kalɔ ɔ nɛ. Kaa bɔ nɛ Tabor yo ɔ daa si gagaa ngɛ yo ɔmɛ a kpɛti, aloo kaa bɔ nɛ Karmel yo ɔ daa si ngɛ wo tue ɔ, jã ji bɔ nɛ nɔ nɛ ma mo tuami ɔ e he wami ngɛ.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Nyɛ Egipt bi, nyɛ dla nyɛ he, ejakaa a ma ba nuu nyɛ kɛ ho ma se ya. Nyɛ ma a nɛ a tsɛɛ Memfis ɔ, a ma kpata e hɛ mi. Memfis maa pee ma doku, nɛ nɔ ko be mi hie hu.

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: Egipt ngɛ kaa na yo saminyayoo nɛ pwɔlwɛ je omleyi je ba kɔ lɛ.

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: Egipt bi ɔmɛ tu fo ngɛ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ a nya kɛ a nɔ ngmlaa kaa sinɔ nɛ ngɛ si sãe kɛ yaa. He nyɛli ɔmɛ ba tua lɛ kɛ gbiɛhi kaa nihi nɛ ngɛ tso hɛɛe,

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: aloo nihi nɛ ngɛ hue tso gbae. A ta buli ɔmɛ ɔ, nɔ ko li a nya; a he hiɛ babauu pe baalɛhi po.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: A bɔ Egipt bi ɔmɛ ahlua; nihi nɛ je omleyi je ɔ ye a nɔ kunimi. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ ke, “Ma gbla Amon, Tebes mawu ɔ, kɛ Egipt mawu kpa amɛ tsuo a tue. Farao ɔ, kɛ nihi tsuo nɛ ngɔɔ a hɛ kɛ fɔɔ e nɔ ɔ, mɛ hu ma gbla a tue.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo nihi nɛ ngɛ mɛ hlae nɛ a gbe ɔ, Babilonia matsɛ, Nebukadnezar, kɛ e tsɔli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi. Se pee se ɔ, nihi ma ba hi Egipt ekohu kaa sa a. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.” Yawɛ ma he e ma a yi wami

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ye ma, nyɛ tsui ko po, ejakaa i kɛ nyɛ ngɛ. Je ma amɛ, hehi nɛ i fie nyɛ kɛ ho ɔ, ma kpata mɛ tsuo a hɛ mi; se nyɛɛ lɛɛ i be nyɛ hɛ mi kpatae. Se kɛ̃ ɔ, i be hae nɛ nyɛɛ ye nyɛ he kulaa; ma gbla nyɛ tue bɔ nɛ sa kɛkɛ. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Loko Egipt matsɛ ɔ ya tua Filistia a, Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu nɛ kɔɔ Filistia he.

english_verse: I, the Lord, tell you that your land will be flooded with an army from the north. It will destroy your towns and sweep you away, moaning and screaming.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ke, “Hyɛ! Nyu babauu je omleyi je kɛ ma kaa pa nɛ hia lalaala. Nyu nɛ ɔ ma ba ha zugba a nɔ tsuo; e maa ha mahi, nimli, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɔ. Ngmlaa maa je nyumuhi po a nya, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ maa wo yana ngɛ zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
translation_verse: A maa nu nɛ okpɔngɔhi a nane kokloto ngɛ si sie glɛi, glɛi, glɛi! A maa nu nɛ zugba lɛhi a nane ngɛ pɛe kplakatsa, kplakatsa, kplakatsa! Tsɛmɛ be plɛe nɛ a hyɛ a bimɛ; a nine mi maa je wu.

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: Be ɔ su nɛ a ma kpata Filisti bi ɔmɛ, kɛ a huɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ piɛ ɔ, Tiro, kɛ Sidon a hɛ mi. Imi, Yawɛ nitsɛ ma kpata Filisti bi ɔmɛ, ni nɛmɛ tsuo nɛ je Kreta wo ɔ nya kɛ ba a a hɛ mi.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Amanehlu agbo ba Gaza bi ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ Ashkelon bi ɔmɛ pee dii. Filisti bi ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ, mɛni be a maa ye kɔmɔ kɛ ya si?

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: Ngmlaa je nyɛ nya nɛ nyɛ bi ke, ‘Yawɛ klaate, mɛni be o ma kpa ní tsumi? Yaa sɛ o kpo ɔ mi, nɛ o jɔɔ o he, nɛ o pee dii!’

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ de ngɛ Moab he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Musu tloo Nebo bi ɔmɛ, ejakaa a kpata a ma a hɛ mi! A pue Kiriataim hɛ mi si, nɛ a ngɔ ma a. A ku mɔ ngua a ngɔ pue si, nɛ a bɔ lɛ ahlua.

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Moab hɛ mi nyami ɔ ta. He nyɛli ɔmɛ ngɔ Heshbon, nɛ a to kaa a ma kpata Moab zugba a hɛ mi. Madmen ma a hu, a ma ya tua lɛ, nɛ a ma kpata ma a hɛ mi.

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Horonaim bi ɔmɛ jé ngmlaa, ejakaa a ngɛ níhi a hɛ mi kpatae basabasa ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: “Moab jokuɛ tsɔwitsɔwi ɔmɛ wo yana ke, a kpata Moab ma a hɛ mi.

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ hyɛ bɔ nɛ a wo yana kɛ yaa, benɛ a ngɛ Luhit yoku ɔ kuɔe ɔ. Nyɛɛ hyɛ mɛ nɛ a ngɛ awe nyae, benɛ a ngɛ kplee kɛ ma Horonaim ɔ.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: A ke, ‘Nyɛɛ tu fo esɔ, kaa nga mi teji yo, nɛ nyɛ kɛ he nyɛ yi wami!’

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: He nyɛlɔ ɔ ma kpata mahi tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a hɛ mi; ma ko ma ko he be mi jee. A ma kpata kɔ̃ kɛ nga kplanaa tsuo a hɛ mi. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ ma kaimi nɔ́ ko ha Moab; ejakaa e be kɛe nɛ a ma kpata ma a hɛ mi. Moab ma amɛ maa pee ma dokuhi nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be a mi hie hu.”

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: A kpata Moab zugba a, kɛ ma amɛ tsuo a hɛ mi; a gbe Moab nihewi kpakpa amɛ tsuo. Imi matsɛ ɔ, Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ, imi lɛ i de.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: Moab amanehlu be ɔ su ta; Moab hɛ mi kpatami be ɔ ma kɛ fo.

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
translation_verse: “Nyɛ nihi tsuo nɛ nyɛ bɔle Moab, nyɛ ni nɛmɛ tsuo nɛ nyɛ nu bɔ nɛ e biɛ pɛɛ be ko ɔ, nyɛɛ ye lɛ kɔmɔ. Nyɛ de ke, ‘E nɔ yemi kpetekpleenyɛ ɔ se po; e hɛ mi nyami, kɛ e he wami ɔ ta.’

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: Nyɛ Moab bi, nyɛ je nyɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ ngɔ fɔ si; nyɛ ba hi si ngɛ zia mi ngɛ zugba. Moab he nyɛli ɔmɛ ma ba tua nyɛ hulɔ, nɛ a ma kpata nyɛ mɔ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi.

english_verse: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
translation_verse: Nyɛ Aroer bi, nyɛ ya da blɔ he nɛ nyɛɛ huɔ! Nyɛ bi nihi nɛ ngɛ fo tue kɛ yaa a ke, ‘Mɛni sane ba?’

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: A ma he nɔ ke, ‘A bɔ Moab ahlua; a kpata Moab hɛ mi. Nyɛɛ wo yana nɛ nyɛ nya awe! Nyɛɛ fiɛ ngɛ Arnon pa a nya ke a kpata Moab hɛ mi!’

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: “A gbla ma nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ nga kplanaa a nɔ ɔ a tue: Holon, Yaza, Mefat,

english_verse: Dibon, Nebo, Beth-Diblathaim,
translation_verse: Dibon, Nebo, Bet Diblataim,

english_verse: Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
translation_verse: Kiriataim, Betgamut, Betmeon,

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Moab he wami kpetekpleenyɛ ɔ je e dɛ; a kpata Moab hɛ mi. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.” A maa ba Moab si

english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Nyɛ ha nɛ Moab nɛ pee kaa nɔ ko nɛ tɔ dã, ejakaa e te si kɛ si mi. Moab ma kokloo si ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e vie mi, nɛ nihi maa muɔ lɛ.

english_verse: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma fo ya ha nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Moab zugba a nɔ ɔ, nɛ ma ye kɔmɔ ha Kir Heres bi ɔmɛ.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: Nyɛ Sibma bi, ma fo nyɛ kulaa pe bɔ nɛ ma fo Yazer bi. Sibma ma, o ngɛ kaa wai tso nɛ kɔnihi gba kɛ ya be ngɛ Ngo wo ɔ he kɛ ya su Yazer tɔɔ. Se amlɔ nɛ ɔ, a kpata o tso yiblii ɔmɛ, kɛ o wai yiblii ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: “Heshbon kɛ Eleale bi ngɛ awe nyae, nɛ a ngɛ ngmlaa a he nue ngɛ Yahaz tɔɔ. Ngmlaa a ngɛ pɛe ngɛ Zoar, Horonaim, kɛ Eglat Shelishiya tɔɔ. Nimrim pa a po gbli.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ma ha nɛ Moab bi ɔmɛ ma kpa sami bɔ sami ngɛ a jami he ɔmɛ, nɛ tsopa kɛ e he via nɛ a sãã ha a mawu ɔmɛ hu se maa po. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ a kpaa ya la mɔbɔmɔbɔ ngɛ bɛ mi ɔ, ja nɛ i ngɛ tsui yee ha Moab, kɛ Kir Heres ma mi bi ɔmɛ, ejakaa a ní nɛ a na a tsuo hɛ mi kpata.

english_verse: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
translation_verse: Ngɛ tsuhi a yi mi, kɛ blɔhi a nɔ ngɛ Moab zugba a nɔ ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ o maa nu kɛkɛ ji kɔmɔ yemi, ejakaa i ha nɛ Moab pee kaa buɛ nɛ ywia wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ nɛ nɔ ko sume hu.

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: A maa ngɔ ma amɛ, kɛ mɔ ɔmɛ. Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, sawale maa nu Moab ta buli ɔmɛ kaa yo nɛ nu kɔɔmi.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: A ma kpata Moab hɛ mi pɛsɛpɛsɛ, nɛ e be ma pee hu; ejakaa e te si kɛ si mi.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ke nɔ ko tu fo kɛ je haomi ɔ nya a, e ma ya nɔ muɔ mi. Nɛ ke e je muɔ ɔ mi ɔ, e ma ya du klama. Ní nɛ ɔmɛ maa ba mi, ejakaa Yawɛ to be nɛ a kɛ ma kpata Moab hɛ mi.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ a he wami ta maa ka kaa a maa tu fo nɛ a ya laa a he ngɛ Heshbon mɔ ɔ mi, he nɛ Matsɛ Sihon ye tsɛ ngɛ be ko ɔ. Se la sã Moab zugba a tsuo; atuã tsɔli nɛ ɔmɛ a zugba a sã kɛ je zugba a nya he kake kɛ ya si he kake.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Moab bi, due! Nyɛ nihi nɛ nyɛ sɔmɔɔ Kemosh ɔ, a kpata nyɛ hɛ mi, nɛ a nuu nyɛ binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ nyɛ biyi ɔmɛ kɛ je.”

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ngɛ Amon he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Jije Israel nyumu ɔmɛ ngɛ? Anɛ nɔ ko be nɛ ma fa a zugba a he lo? Mɛni he je mɔ nɛ a ngmɛɛ Gad bi ɔmɛ a zugba a he ngɔ ha Milkom jali ɔmɛ nɛ a ba ngɔ zugba a kɛ pee a nɔ́ ɔ?

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Se be ma nɛ ma ha nɛ nihi nɛ ngɛ Amon matsɛ ma Raba a maa nu nɛ a he ose kɛ ma. A ma kpata ma a hɛ mi, nɛ kɔpehi nɛ bɔle ma a, a maa mɛ a he la. Jamɛ a be ɔ, zugba a nɛ he nyɛli ɔmɛ ba kpɔ ngɛ Israel dɛ ɔ, Israel nine maa su nɔ ekohu.

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: Nyɛ Heshbon bi, nyɛɛ wo yana, ejakaa a kpata Ai hɛ mi. Raba yihi, nyɛ nya awe! Nyɛ bu kpekpe ya bo, nɛ nyɛɛ ye kɔmɔ. Nyɛɛ hi fo tue kɛ hi bee basaa kɛkɛ. Nyɛ mawu ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Milkom ɔ, a ma ba ngɔ lɛ kɛ ho ma se ya, kɛ e we osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ ganɔ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: Nyɛ nihi nɛ nyɛ je Mawu se, mɛni he je nyɛ ngɛ fĩae? Nyɛ he wami ɔ ta. Mɛni he je nyɛ ngɔ nyɛ hɛ ngɔ fɔ nyɛ sika nɔ, nɛ nyɛ deɔ ke nɔ ko nɔ ko be nyɛe nɛ e ba tua nyɛ ɔ?

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: Imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ, ma ngɔ haomi kɛ ba nyɛ nɔ. Mahi nɛ bɔle nyɛ ɔ tsuo maa fie nyɛ kɛ fo kpatakpata kɛ je nyɛ zugba a nɔ, nɛ nɔ ko be nɛ ma bua nyɛ nya ekohu.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: “Se pee se ɔ, ma ha nɛ Amon ma ba na e he ekohu. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.” Yawɛ maa gbla Edom tue

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Nyɛ Dedan bi, nyɛ plɛ nɛ nyɛɛ tu fo! Nyɛ ya laa nyɛ he ngɛ muɔhi a mi. Ma kpata Esau nina a hɛ mi, ejakaa be ɔ nɛ ma kɛ gbla a tue ɔ, be ɔ su.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Ke nihi ngɛ wai yiblii nya buae ɔ, anɛ a si we eko ngɛ tso ɔ nɔ lo? Ke juli ma jumi nyɔ mi ɔ, pi nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ hlae ɔ pɛ nɛ a muɔɔ kɛ yaa lo?

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Se imi lɛɛ i kpakpaa Esau nina a he ní, nɛ i pee mɛ pasaa. A laami he ɔmɛ hu i je mɛ kpo, nɛ a be he ko nɛ a laa a he ngɛ hu. A kpata Edom bi ɔmɛ tsuo a hɛ mi; a ti nɔ kake ngmelu po píɛ.

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: “Nihi nɛ sɛ́ tue gblami, nɛ a gbla a tue ɔ, moo o susu kaa o maa ye o he lo? Dɛbi! Jamɛ a tue gblami kplu ɔ, ja mo hu o nu kɛ̃!

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Imi nitsɛ i ka ye he kita ke ma ha nɛ Bozra ma a maa pee ma doku; nihi maa ye a he fɛu, nɛ a kɛ ma a biɛ maa gbiɛ nɔ. Kɔpehi nɛ bɔle ma a tsuo a hɛ mi ma kpata kɛ ya neneene. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: O he nɔ womi ɔ sisi mo. Nɔ ko nɔ ko pa yi mo gbeye hu kaa bɔ nɛ o susuu ɔ. O hi he ji tɛ sa amɛ a kpɛ, ngɛ yo ɔmɛ a yi mi. E ngɛ mi kaa o hi he ngɛ hiɔwe lokoo kaa kɔle hi he mohu, se kɛ̃ Yawɛ ma je mo kɛ je lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e maa ba mo si. Yawɛ lɛ de.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Kaa bɔ nɛ jata hiaa kpo vlai kɛ jeɔ pu mi ngɛ Yordan pa a he kɛ baa lohwehi a ní yemi he ɔ, ja ma ba tlukaa, nɛ ma ba fie Edom bi ɔmɛ kɛ je a zugba a nɔ kɛ fo. Kɛkɛ ɔ, hɛ mi nyɛɛlɔ ɔ nɛ ma hla a, lɛ ji nɔ nɛ maa ye ma a nɔ. Mɛnɔ lɛ e kɛ mi sɔ? Mɛnɔ ma nyɛ nɛ e kɛ mi maa to ní? Te nɔ yelɔ nɛ ma nyɛ ye hɛ mi maa da nɛɛ?

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: He nyɛlɔ ɔ ma ba tua Bozra tlukaa kaa kɔle nɛ gbɛ e pɛlihi a mi kɛ ma. Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, Edom ta buli ɔmɛ maa nu sawale kaa yo nɛ nu kɔɔmi.” Yawɛ maa gbla Damasko tue

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ngɛ Damasko he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Hamat ma mi bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Arpad ma mi bi ɔmɛ hao, ejakaa a nu sane yaya. A tsui po, nɛ a he mi ngɛ mɛ hiae kaa wo nɛ ngɛ fiae gudugudu nɛ he jɔɔmi be mi.

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Damasko ma mi bi ɔmɛ a he wami ta, nɛ a kɛ sawale tu fo kɛ je. A ngɛ haomi, kɛ he hiami mi kaa yo nɛ nu kɔɔmi.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Kɛ ba lɛ kɛɛ loko ma nɛ he biɛ, kɛ e mi bua jɔmi babauu ɔ, a je ma a he kikɛ nɛ ɔ?

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, a maa gbe ma nihe ɔ tsuo ngɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ, nɛ a ma kpata ta buli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: Ma mɛ Damasko gbogbo ɔ he la, nɛ ma sã Matsɛ Benhadad mɔ ɔmɛ. Imi, Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ lɛ i de.” A maa gbla Kedar wɛtso ɔ kɛ Hazor ma a tue

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Kedar wɛtso ɔ, kɛ Hazor nɔ yemi he ɔmɛ nɛ Babilonia matsɛ, Nebukadnezar ba ye a nɔ ɔ, bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ngɛ a he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya tua Kedar, ma a, nɛ nyɛ kpata beleku je wɛtso ɔ hɛ mi!

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: ‘Jamɛ a ma a nɛ e mi bi ngɛ he jɔmi, kɛ tue mi jɔmi mi ɔ, nyɛ ha nɛ wa ya tua mɛ! Ma a fɔɔ si gu, agbo be he ɔ, dade se lami nɔ́ hu be he.’

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: “Nyɛɛ ha a we afukpɔngɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ a na amɛ tsuo! Nihi nɛ sɛɛ a yi kasa fa a, ma gbɛ mɛ ngɔ fĩa je ɔ tsuo, nɛ ma ha haomi maa je hehi munomuno kɛ ba na mɛ.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: Hazor maa pee ma doku kɛ nga mi gbehi a hi he kɛ ya neneene. Nɔ ko nɔ ko be lejɛ ɔ hie hu. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.” A maa gbla Elam tue

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Ma gbe Elam kɛ̃ɛ̃ tsɛ̃li ɔmɛ tsuo; mɛ ji Elam he wami ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ma kpata a matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ ma to imi nitsɛ ye matsɛ yemi sisi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: Se pee se ɔ, ma ha nɛ Elam bi ɔmɛ ma ba na a he ekohu. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Sɛ gbi nɛ Yawɛ ha mi nɛ kɔɔ Babilon ma a, kɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ a he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ:

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: “Je ma ko hia kɛ je omleyi je kɛ ma nɛ e ba tua Babilonia. A ma kpata zugba a hɛ mi, nɛ a maa pee lɛ butuu; nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be lejɛ ɔ hie hu. Nimli kɛ lohwehi tsuo maa tu fo kɛ je.” Israel maa kpale kɛ ba

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ke, “Jamɛ a be ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ tsuo maa wo yana kɛ ba, nɛ a ma ba hla imi, a Mawu ɔ, ye se blɔ.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa na mɛ ɔ ma tua mɛ. Nɔ́ nɛ a he nyɛli ɔmɛ deɔ ji ‘Wɔɔ lɛɛ wa tɔ we. Mɛ lɛ a pee yayami kɛ si Yawɛ, Mawu dami sane yelɔ ɔ nɛ a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ a hɛ ngɔ fɔ e nɔ ɔ.’

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: Ma ya sú je mahi babauu nɛ a he wa kɛ je omleyi je kɛ wo Babilonia he. A ma gba ta kɛ wo zugba a, nɛ a maa ngɔ lɛ. Ta buli kpanakpanaahi ji mɛ. A dɛ nya da, nɛ ke a tsɛ̃ kɛ̃ɛ̃ ɔ, e bi nɔ́ he kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: A maa ha ní ngɛ Babilonia zugba a nɔ kɛ yaa si nɔ tsuaa nɔ ma na bɔ nɛ e suɔ. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.” A ma kpata Babilonia hɛ mi

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Babilonia bi, nyɛ kpata ye zugba a hɛ mi. Nyɛ kle tɔfutɔfu kaa na yihi nɛ ye niye ní kpakpa, nɛ nyɛ kpaa ngmlaa kɛ he wami kaa okpɔngɔ. Nyɛ bua jɔɔ nyɛ he, nɛ nyɛ nyaa.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Imi Yawɛ, ye mi mi fu Babilon, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be lejɛ ɔ hie hu; e maa pee ma doku kulaa, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ ma ba be ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, e he mi maa po, nɛ e nya maa kpɛ e he.

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ fie ní duli, kɛ ní kpali kɛ a dɛ mi ha kɛ je Babilon. Nibwɔhi nɛ ngɛ ma a mi ɔ, a maa ye ta nɛ ba tua mɛ ɔ gbeye, nɛ a maa je kɛ ho mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɔ ya.” Israel maa kpale kɛ ba

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Israel bi ngɛ kaa tohi nɛ jatahi fie mɛ, nɛ a gbɛ mɛ ngɔ fĩa. Kekleekle ɔ, Asiria matsɛ ba tua mɛ, nɛ e ye mɛ; lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Babilonia matsɛ, Nebukadnezar ba kpe a wuhi.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, imi Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ, ma gbla matsɛ Nebukadnezar kɛ e zugba a tue kaa bɔ nɛ i pee Asiria matsɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ma kpale Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ ba mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba a nɔ ekohu. A maa ye niye ní nɛ baa ngɛ Karmel yo ɔ nɔ, kɛ Bashan zugba a nɔ ɔ. A ma na ní maa ye bɔ nɛ a suɔ ngɛ Efraim kɛ Gilead zugba a nɔ.

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: Ke jamɛ a be ɔ su ɔ, a ma hla kaa a maa na Israel he yayami ko lo, se a be nae. Yuda hu a be yi wu tso nɔ́ ko nae ngɛ he e, ejakaa ni nɛmɛ nɛ i he a yi wami ɔ, ma ngɔ a he yayami ɔmɛ kɛ pa mɛ. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.” Mawu maa gbla Babilonia tue

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Nyɛ ya tua Merataim, kɛ Pekod bi ɔmɛ. Nyɛɛ gbe mɛ, nɛ nyɛ kpata a hɛ mi. Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ i fa nyɛ ke nyɛɛ pee ɔ, nyɛɛ pee. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Ta ose pɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ, nɛ níhi babauu a hɛ mi kpata.

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Babilonia, o kɛ imi, Yawɛ hwu ta. Nɛ klama nɛ i tsɔ mo ɔ, o du klama a; ejakaa o li tete kaa i tsɔ mo klama ko.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Nyɛ ya tua Babilonia kɛ je he tsuaa he, nɛ nyɛɛ ywia ngma tomi he ɔmɛ. Nyɛɛ to ta yibu ní ɔmɛ kaa ngma nɛ a to lɛ glekugleku! Nyɛ kpata zugba a hɛ mi! Nyɛ ko si nɔ ko nɔ ko ngɛ nɔ!

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ gbe a ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo! Nyɛ kpata a hɛ mi pɛsɛpɛsɛ! Babilonia bi ɔmɛ a yi fi wawɛɛ nitsɛ. A tue gblami be ɔ su!”

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: Ni komɛ tu fo kɛ je Babilonia kɛ ba Yerusalem nɛ a ba bɔ ma a amaniɛ bɔ nɛ Yawɛ ye e he lue ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ Babilonia bi ɔmɛ pee lɛ Yawɛ e we ɔ he.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: “Babilonia bi, nyɛ woɔ nyɛ he nɔ. Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ, i kɛ nyɛ maa to ní. Nyɛ be ɔ su; be ɔ nɛ ma gbla nyɛ tue ɔ su.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Nyɛ, ma he nɔ woli nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, nyɛ ma tɛ nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ maa nɔɔ si, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be nyɛ nɔ woe. Ma mɛ nyɛ ma amɛ a he la, nɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ bɔle mɛ kɛ kpe ɔ hɛ mi ma kpata.”

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Ta ma ba na lakpa gbali ɔmɛ, nɛ a ma plɛ pee kuasiahi! Ta ma ba na ta buli ɔmɛ, nɛ sawale maa nu mɛ!

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Ta ma ba na okpɔngɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ zugba lɛ ɔmɛ; ta ma ba na ma se ta buli tsuo nɛ ngɛ Babilonia a; a he wami maa ta, nɛ a maa pee kaa yihi pɛ! A maa ha a juetli tsuo!

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Pahi tsuo a mi nyu maa mii ta, nɛ nyu hwɔ maa ba zugba a nɔ! Amaga gbeyegbeyehi sɔuu ji zugba a nɔ, nɛ lɔ ɔmɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ ngɔ a tsui kɛ ha.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ma kpata Babilon hɛ mi pɛsɛpɛsɛ kaa bɔ nɛ i pee Sodom, kɛ Gomora, kɛ kɔpehi nɛ bɔle ɔ. Nɔ ko nɔ ko be lejɛ ɔ hie hu. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: “Ma ko je omleyi je kɛ ma. Je ma agbo ko, kɛ matsɛmɛ babauu hia kɛ je tsitsaa lokoo kɛ ma.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: A hɛɛ kɛ̃ɛ̃ kɛ akplɔ; a yi mi wa, nɛ mɔbɔ nami ko kulaa be a mi. A he ose, nɛ a hi okpɔngɔhi a nɔ kɛ ma; nɛ lejɛ ɔ tsuo pee hoo kaa wo nɛ ngɛ fiae gudugudu. A mia kɛ ma nɛ a kɛ Babilonia ba hwu ta.

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: Benɛ Babilonia matsɛ ɔ nu sane nɛ ba a, e nine mi je wu. E tsui po wawɛɛ nitsɛ, nɛ e kpatu pee kaa yo nɛ nu kɔɔmi.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: “Kaa bɔ nɛ jata hiaa kpo vlai kɛ jeɔ pu mi ngɛ Yordan pa a he kɛ baa lohwehi a ní yemi he ɔ, ja imi Yawɛ, ma ba tlukaa nɛ ma ba fie Babilonia bi ɔmɛ kɛ je a ma a mi kɛ fo. Kɛkɛ ɔ, hɛ mi nyɛɛlɔ ɔ nɛ ma hla a, lɛ ji nɔ nɛ maa ye ma a nɔ. Mɛnɔ lɛ e kɛ mi sɔ? Mɛnɔ ma nyɛ nɛ e kɛ mi maa to ní? Te nɔ yelɔ nɛ ma nyɛ ye hɛ mi maa da?

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Ma ha nɛ kɔɔhiɔ nɛ puɛɔ ní maa fia ngɛ Babilonia zugba a nɔ, nɛ e ma kpata nihi a hɛ mi.

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Nyɛ ko ngmɛ a ta buli ɔmɛ blɔ nɛ a kpla a gbaja amɛ. Nyɛ ko ngmɛ mɛ blɔ nɛ a tsɛ̃ a kɛ̃ɛ̃ ɔmɛ. Nyɛ ko ha nɛ a nihewi ɔmɛ a yi nɛ na wami! Nyɛ kpata tabo ɔ tsuo hɛ mi!

english_verse: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
translation_verse: A maa plaa mɛ ngɔ pue si ngɛ Kaldea gbɛjegbɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ a ma gbo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Niinɛ, Israel kɛ Yuda pee yayami kɛ si imi, Israel Nɔ Klɔuklɔu ɔ. Se imi Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ Mawu ɔ, imi lɛɛ i kua we mɛ.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ tu fo kɛ je Babilonia nɛ nyɛ kɛ he nyɛ yi wami. Nyɛ ko ha nɛ a gbe nyɛ ngɛ Babilonia bi ɔmɛ a he yayami ɔ he. Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, i ngɛ ye he lue yee ngɛ a nɔ, nɛ i ngɛ a tue gblae bɔ nɛ sa mɛ.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Babilonia ngɛ kaa sika tsu kplu ko ngɛ ye dɛ mi nɛ ha je ɔ tsuo tɔ dã. Je ma amɛ tsuo nu wai ngɛ kplu nɛ ɔ mi, nɛ a fo godo.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Babilonia nɔ si tlukaa, nɛ e hɛ mi kpata. Nyɛ nya awe ha lɛ! Nyɛɛ to e pa amɛ a nɔ tsopa kaa alini e ma na he wami lo.

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Nibwɔhi nɛ ngɛ Babilonia a de ke, ‘Jinɛ wa ka kaa wa maa piɛ a he, se wa ya nyɛ we. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛ ha nɛ waa je e he; nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ pue e ma mi blɔ. Mawu gbla Babilonia tue wawɛɛ nitsɛ; Mawu kpata zugba a hɛ mi pɛsɛpɛsɛ.’ ”

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Pahi fuu ngɛ jamɛ a zugba a nɔ, nɛ a juetli hu hiɛ babauu. Se a nyagbe ɔ su; a po a wami kpa a.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Yawɛ Tabohiatsɛ ɔ ka e he kita ke e maa ngɔ nihi babauu kaa baalɛhi kɛ ba tua Babilonia. A maa ye kunimi, nɛ a ma hwɔ lele. Mawu yi jemi la
