translation_verse: A maa hi sɛ saminyayoo nɔ; a maa ngɔ okplɔɔ kɛ e nɔ ní kpakpahi kɛ ya ma si ngɛ a hɛ mi. Tsopa kɛ e he via, kɛ oliv nu nɛ i ha mɛ ɔ hu piɛ he.

english_verse: and I noticed that the men were eager to have sex with these women, though they were exhausted from being prostitutes.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ i de ye he ke, hyɛ kaa yo nɛ bwɔ kikɛ nɛ ɔ ngɛ ajuama bɔmi mi ɔ, nyumuhi kɛ lɛ pa ngɛ si hwɔe!

english_verse: In fact, the men had sex over and over with Oholah and Oholibah, the two sinful sisters.
translation_verse: Nyumuhi ngɛ a ngɔ yae kaa bɔ nɛ a yaa yihi yaholi a ngɔ. Ee, ja pɛpɛɛpɛ a ngɛ Ohola kɛ Oholiba nɔ puee; a pee a he ajamɛatsɛmɛ!

english_verse: But honest judges will someday accuse those two of murder and of being unfaithful, because they are certainly guilty.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ peeɔ nɔ nɛ da maa bu mɛ fɔ kaa a puɛ gba, nɛ a pue muɔ si hulɔ; ejakaa a ngɔ yahomi kɛ pee a ní tsumi, nɛ a pue muɔ si.”

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters: I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Yawɛ ngɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Ma ha yakayaka nimli babauu ma ba wo a he gbeye, nɛ a maa ha a níhi.

english_verse: They will stone you to death and cut you to pieces; they will kill your children and burn down your houses.
translation_verse: Yakayaka nimli nɛ ɔmɛ maa fia mɛ tɛ, nɛ a ma ja mɛ klaate; a maa gbe a bimɛ, nɛ a maa mɛ a we ɔmɛ a he la.

english_verse: I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have.
translation_verse: Ma ha yahomi se maa po ngɛ zugba a nɔ, konɛ a kɛ bɔ yihi tsuo kɔkɔ nɛ a ko tsu yahomi ní nɛ nyɛmiyi enyɔ ɔmɛ tsu ɔ gblegbleegble.

english_verse: You will be punished for becoming prostitutes and for worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Nɛ nyɛ, nyɛmiyi enyɔ nɛ ɔmɛ, ma gbla nyɛ tue kaa nyɛ bɔ ajuama nɛ nyɛ ya ja amagahi. Lɔ ɔ loko nyɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Benɛ a nuu wɔ kɛ ho ma se ya a, jeha nɛɛne ɔ we nyɔhiɔ nyɔngma a we ligbi nyɔngma a, Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ekohu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: E fa mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, kadi mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ biɛ ngɛ womi mi kɛ to! Ejakaa mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ nɔuu Babilonia matsɛ ɔ bɔni Yerusalem he ka womi.

english_verse: These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ngɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Musu tloo ma nɛ muɔ si pɛ a pueɔ ngɛ mi ɔ! Ma a ngɛ kaa buɛ ko nɛ e mi nɔ kana, nɛ́ kana a ma ngɛ mi. A tá e mi lo ɔmɛ kakaaka ta; ekoeko piɛ ngɛ mi!

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground.
translation_verse: A pue muɔ si ngɛ ma a mi. Pi zugba nɛ muɔ ɔ pue nɛ a maa ngɔ tabo zu kɛ tsi nɔ, se tɛ sa kpataa nɔ.

english_verse: so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ lɛ́ babauu kɛ ba! Ma ha la a maa tso wawɛɛ, nɛ lo ɔ maa be saminya! Hwonyu ɔ maa si, nɛ wu ɔmɛ tete ma ngla!

english_verse: Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, ma ha buɛ ɔ mi gu maa ma la hleii ɔ nɔ, konɛ e dɔ la kɛ yaa si akɔblee ɔ maa tsu paa; kɛkɛ ɔ, e mi mu ɔ tsuo maa sile, nɛ e mi kana a tsuo maa ta pɛsɛpɛsɛ!

english_verse: That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Ezekiel's Wife Dies
translation_verse: Imi, Yawɛ nitsɛ lɛ i de. Be ɔ su jehanɛ; bɔ nɛ i de ɔ, ja ma pee. I be ye nya se kpalee; i be mɔbɔ nae, nɛ i be ye he piae hulɔ. Yayamihi nɛ o pee ɔ a he ɔ, ma gbla o tue bɔ nɛ sa mo.” Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ de. Gbalɔ ɔ yo ɔ gbenɔ

english_verse: The Lord said,
translation_verse: Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ekohu.

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry.
translation_verse: E ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, tlukaa a, ma ha gbenɔ hiɔ ma ba fia o suɔlɔ pe kulaa a, nɛ e ma gbo. Ke e ba mi ja a, koo ye kɔmɔ; ko fo ya, nɛ koo nga vo nyu hulɔ.

english_verse: Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
translation_verse: A ko nu o huu fami he; se fi o yi duku, nɛ o wo tokota. Koo ngɔ nɔ́ kɛ ha o nya nɔ, nɛ koo ye ya nɔ niye ní kɛ tsɔɔ kaa o ngɛ ya nyɛe.”

english_verse: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
translation_verse: Mɔtu kpla a, i kɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ tu munyu. Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ gbɔkuɛ nɔuu nɛ ye yo ɔ gbo. E nɔ jena mɔtu ɔ, i pee kaa bɔ nɛ a de mi ke ma pee ɔ.

english_verse: and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ bi mi ke, “Mɛni he je o ngɛ níhi pee kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ɔ, nyɛ maa pee kaa bɔ nɛ i pee nɛ ɔ: nyɛ be nɔ́ ngɔe kɛ ha nyɛ nya nɔ, nɛ nyɛ be ya nɔ ní hu yee.

english_verse: You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
translation_verse: Nyɛ yi fimi ní ɔmɛ maa fi nyɛ yi; nyɛ tokota amɛ maa hi nyɛ nane; nyɛ be kɔmɔ yee, nɛ nyɛ be ya foe. Se yayamihi nɛ nyɛ pee ɔ ma ha nyɛ maa ta he lo, nɛ nyɛ ma kɛmɛ kɛ tsɔɔ nyɛ sibi.

english_verse: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
translation_verse: Nɛ imi Ezekiel, ma pee nɔ́ hyɛmi nɔ́ ha nyɛ; bɔ nɛ i pee ɔ, ja pɛpɛɛpɛ nyɛ maa pee. Yawɛ ke, ke nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ba mi ɔ, nyɛ maa le kaa lɛ ji Yawɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, nɔ ko nɛ yi na wami kɛ je hɛ mi kpatami ɔ mi ma ba bɔ mo amaniɛ.

english_verse: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, o kɛ nɔ nɛ yi na wami ɔ maa sɛɛ ní. O maa tu munyu, nɛ o be mumui pee hu. O ma plɛ pee okadi ha mɛ, konɛ a le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ekohu.

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma ngɔ nyɛ kɛ wo nihi nɛ je beleku je ɔ a dɛ mi. A maa ngɔ nyɛ zugba a kɛ pee a nɔ́. A ma ba po wehi ngɛ he nɛ nyɛ ngɛ ɔ, nɛ a kɛ nyɛ maa hi si. A maa ye nyɛ tso yiblii, nɛ a maa nu nyɛ na nyɔ nyu.

english_verse: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Raba ma a ma plɛ pee nga nɔ he nɛ afukpɔngɔhi maa ye ní ngɛ. Ma ha Amon bi ɔmɛ a zugba a tsuo ma plɛ pee to lɛmi he. Lɔ ɔ loko nyɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kɛ mo ná; ma ngɔ mo ngɔ ha je ma amɛ nɛ a ha o níhi. A ma je mo ngɔ hɛ ngɔ fɔ, nɛ o hɛ mi ma kpata pɛsɛpɛsɛ kɛ maa je je ɔ mi. Kɛkɛ ɔ, o maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.” A ma kpata Moab hɛ mi

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ngɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Moab bi ɔmɛ de ke Yuda ngɛ kaa je ma kpa amɛ tsuo,

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: Ma gbla Moab tue wawɛɛ; kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.” A ma kpata Edom hɛ mi

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i ngɛ dee ke ma gbla Edom tue wawɛɛ; ma kpata nimlihi, kɛ lohwehi tsuo a hɛ mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Nihi babauu maa nɔ ngɛ ta mi kɛ maa je Teman kɛ yaa si Dedan tɔɔ. Nɛ Edom zugba a ma ba pee ma doku.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: Ma ha ye ma Israel hu kɛ Edom maa to ní; nɛ Edom maa na bɔ nɛ ye we abofu nya wa ha ke i ngɛ nɔ́ ko tue gblae ɔ.” Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ de. A ma kpata Filistia hɛ mi

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ma gbla a tue wawɛɛ nitsɛ. Ma ngɔ abofu kɛ gbla a tue, nɛ a maa nu he. Lɔ ɔ loko a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Benɛ a nuu wɔ kɛ ho ma se ya a se jeha nyɔngma kɛ kakene ɔ we kekleekle ligbi ngɛ nyɔhiɔ ko mi ɔ, Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: E ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, bɔ nɛ Tiro bi ɔmɛ ngɛ nyae, nɛ a ngɛ dee ngɛ Yerusalem he ji, ‘Yiɛɛ! A ku Yerusalem ngɔ pue si! E jua yemi, kɛ ní nɛ e na a tsuo ma ba je wa ngɔ.’

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, bɔ nɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ dee ji: Tiro, i kɛ mo ná. Ma ha je mahi babauu ma ba tua mo; a maa ba nɔtonɔto kaa bɔ nɛ wo oslɔkehi kuɔ kɛ baa wo dɔ mi.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: A ma kpata o ma a hɛ mi; a maa ku gbogbo ɔmɛ, kɛ mɔ gojogojo ɔmɛ kɛ pue si. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, imi nitsɛ ma bɛɛ zu ɔ tsuo kɛ je lejɛ ɔ kɛ ho, nɛ e maa piɛ tɛ sa kpataa kɛkɛ.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: nɛ a kɛ a klaate maa gbe nimli ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ ngɛ ma amɛ a mi ngɛ zugba a nɔ. Lɔ ɔ loko Tiro maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “Ma ha Nebukadnezar, Babilonia matsɛ nguaa pe kulaa a ma ba tua Tiro. E kɛ e tabo babauu nitsɛ, nihi nɛ hi okpɔngɔhi a nɔ, nihi nɛ ngɛ ta zugba lɛhi a mi, kɛ nihi nɛ nyɛɛ nane maa je omleyi je kɛ ba.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ ngɛ o ma amɛ a mi ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ, ma kpata a hɛ mi. Ma ha o he nyɛlɔ ɔ maa tsua muɔ kɛ bɔle mo; e maa fia kpoku kɛ wo o he, nɛ e kɛ tsɛ̃i maa ma si kaa gbogbo kɛ bɔle mo.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: E maa ngɔ e gbogbo kumi ní ɔmɛ kɛ si o gbogbo ɔmɛ, nɛ o mɔ gojogojo ɔmɛ hu, e maa ngɔ e dade ɔmɛ kɛ ku mɛ kɛ pue si.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: E we okpɔngɔhi maa hiɛ babauu nɛ a se bunyuku ɔ maa laa o nɔ. Okpɔngɔ ɔmɛ, e ní gblami tlɔɔke ɔmɛ, kɛ e ta zugba lɛ ɔmɛ maa sɛ agbo ɔmɛ a mi gidigidi kaa a sɛɔ ma ko nɛ a ye e nɔ momo mi. A hoo peemi ɔ ma mimiɛ o gbogbo ɔmɛ tete.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: O he nyɛli ɔmɛ ma kpɔ ní nɛ o ná a ngɛ o dɛ, nɛ a maa ha o guɛ ní. A maa ku o gbogbo ɔmɛ kɛ, o we saminyawiiwi ɔmɛ. A maa muɔ tɛ ɔmɛ kɛ tso ɔmɛ, kɛ zu ɔ tsuo kɛ ya pue wo mi.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: Ma ha o la amɛ a se maa po; a be o saku ɔmɛ a he nue hu.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: Ma pee mo tɛ sa kpataa, he nɛ wo hɛli ma ka a yahi ngɛ. A be mo dlae kɛ pee ma hu. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Se jehanɛ lɛɛ, ma amɛ a he maa do blibliibli kaa mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, a kpata o hɛ mi! Niinɛ, wo nya ma amɛ tsuo a tsui maa po kaa a kpata o hɛ mi kikɛ nɛ ɔ!”

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: O ma kple si kɛ ya su gbeje nitsɛ, he nɛ blematsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a be je mi hu ɔ ngɛ ɔ. Lejɛ ɔ o kɛ mɛ maa hi ngɛ blema níhi nɛ a kpata a hɛ mi ɔ a mi ngɛ je ɔ sisi tɔɔ. Kɛkɛ ɔ, o be nyɛe maa pee ma nɛ nɔmlɔ adesa maa hi mi ngɛ je nɛ ɔ mi hu!

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ma ha o nyagbe maa pee gbeye; o be je mi hie hu. Ke a bi o si ɔ, a be mo nae; o maa laa gbidii kɛ yaa neneene.” Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ de.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ adesa, la mɔbɔ la kɛ nyɛ ya ha Tiro ma a.

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: Tiro ji wo nya ma nguaa, nɛ e kɛ je mahi tsuo yeɔ jua kɛ yaa wo se tsitsaa. De lɛ ke bɔ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ngɛ lɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Tiro ma, o wo o he nɔ, nɛ o fĩa ke, ‘Ye he ngɛ fɛu kɛ pi si.’

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Lɛ ɔ nitsɛ tsuo ɔ, Hermon yo ɔ nɔ sɛsɛo tso sɔuu a kɛ kpɛ. O mi abalaa tso ɔmɛ ɔ, seda tso nɛ je Lebanon a kɛ pee mɛ.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Akɔfa amɛ lɛɛ, Bashan tso nguaa amɛ a kɛ hlɔ mɛ. Lɛ nɔ tsu bi ɔ, nga nɔ tso tlɔmɔɔ nɛ je Kipro a kɛ pee lɛ. A topɛ́ tso ɔ mi, nɛ a wo mi suɔ wu.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Sidon bi, kɛ Arvad bi ji o lɛ hluili; mo Tiro nitsɛ o mi bi nɛ le ga saminya ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ kudɔɔ o lɛ ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: “Ta buli nɛ je Persia, Lidia, kɛ Libia hu ba piɛ o ta buli ɔmɛ a he. A kɛ a tsɛ̃i ɔmɛ, kɛ dade pɛɛ ɔmɛ ha nɛ o ye kunimi.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Ta buli nɛ je Arvad bu o gbogbo ɔmɛ a he kɛ kpe, nɛ Gamad bi hu bu o mɔ ɔmɛ a he. Ni nɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ a tsɛ̃i ɔmɛ kɛ kpla o gbogbo ɔmɛ a he kɛ kpe. Mɛ lɛ a ha o he pee fɛu kɛ pi si ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
translation_verse: “Spania kɛ mo ye jua, ejakaa o ngɛ guɛ ní babauu, nɛ a kɛ sika hiɔ, dade, sanylaa, kɛ sumui ba tsakee o guɛ ní ɔmɛ.

english_verse: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
translation_verse: O kɛ Hela, Tubal, kɛ Meshek hu ye jua. A ngɔɔ nɔmlɔ adesa po, akɔblee níhi, okpɔngɔhi, kɛ teji okpɔngɔhi kɛ ba tsakee o guɛ ní ɔmɛ.

english_verse: and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ je Bet Togarma kɛ okpɔngɔhi, ta okpɔngɔhi, kɛ teji okpɔngɔhi ba tsakee o guɛ ní.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: Rodo bi hu kɛ mo ye jua. A ngɔɔ suɔ wu, kɛ tɛ tso kɛ ba tsakee o guɛ ní.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Yuda kɛ Israel zugba amɛ hu kɛ mo ye jua. Ke a ba he ní ɔ, níhi nɛ a kɛ woɔ hiɔ ji ngma, hwo, oliv nu, kɛ tsopa kɛ e he via.

english_verse: while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats.
translation_verse: Arabia bi kɛ Kedar ganɔ ɔmɛ tsuo o kɛ mɛ ye jua; mɛɛ níhi nɛ a kɛ woɔ hiɔ ji agbosuhi, jijɔhi, kɛ akpakpohi.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Sheba kɛ Raama bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ níhi nɛ a kɛ ba tsakee o guɛ ní ɔmɛ ji juetli, sika tsu, kɛ tsopa kɛ e he via kpakpa.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: Haran, Kane, kɛ Eden ma amɛ, kɛ jehanɛ jua yeli nɛ je Sheba, Asur kɛ Kilmad ma amɛ a mi ɔ, mɛ tsuo a kɛ mo ye jua.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: O guɛ ní hyiɔ lɛ agbohi babauu. O pee kaa lɛ ngɛ wo nɔ, lɛ nɛ a wo lɛ tlomi tɔtɔɔtɔ.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: O lɛ kudɔɔ nuli ɔmɛ kpa ngmlaa wawɛɛ; a nu ngmlaa a he ngɛ wo ɔ nya tsuo.

english_verse: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
translation_verse: “Lɛ hluili ɔmɛ tsuo je a lɛ ɔmɛ a mi: lɛ ɔmɛ a mi bi tsuo ba kpo nɔ.

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: Mɛ tsuo a ngɛ ya foe wawɛɛ ha mo; a ngɔ zu kɛ pue a yi mi, nɛ a ngɛ si wuwluae ngɛ la zu mi.

english_verse: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
translation_verse: A sɛ a yi kpalokpalo; a ha kpekpe ya bo kɛ ngɛ aywilɛho yee; a ngɛ ya nyɛe wawɛɛ ha mo.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: A la hɛdo la ko kɛ nyɛ ya ha mo: ‘Tiro nɛ e nɔ jɔ ngɛ wo kpɛti kikɛ nɛ ɔ? Mɛnɔ he a kɛ lɛ maa to?

english_verse: “Nations that received your merchandise were always pleased; kings everywhere got rich from your costly goods.
translation_verse: Benɛ o guɛ ní ɔmɛ yaa ma se tsitsaa a, o haa ma amɛ tɔɔ kɛ ní kpakpahi. Matsɛmɛ ná a he kɛ je o ní nami ɔ mi.

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: “Bɔ nɛ o nyagbe ba ji nɛ ɔ? E pee nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ wo nya ma amɛ a mi ɔ nyakpɛ; a matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ po ye gbeye, nɛ a hɛ mi pee mɛ yaa.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Sawale nu jua yeli nɛ ngɛ je ɔ mi ɔ tsuo; a ngɛ gbeye yee kaa mɛ hu a hɛ mi ma kpata ja nɔuu; o laa kɛ yaa neneene.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ adesa, de Tiro ganɔ ɔ ke, bɔ nɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ lɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: O wo o he nɔ gojoo ke mawu ji mo. O hii si ngɛ matsɛ sɛ nɔ; nɛ wo bɔle mo. Mo nɔmlɔ adesa a, o pee o he kaa mawu ko ji mo.

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: O nile, kɛ o nɔ́ sisi numi ha nɛ o ná ní kpɔtɔɔ: o bua sika tsu, kɛ sika hiɔ babauu nya kɛ to.

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: O ngɛ jua yemi he juɛmi saminya, nɛ o ná ní babauu. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, o wo o he nɔ gojoo ke niatsɛ ji mo!

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: ma ha nibwɔhi yiwutsotsɛmɛ kpanakuhi maa je je ma amɛ a mi ma ba tua mo. Afɛu ní babauu nɛ o gu o nile, kɛ o ga a nɔ kɛ ná a tsuo hɛ mi ma kpata.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: A maa gbe mo, nɛ a ma sake mo ngɔ fɔ gbeje ngɛ wo ɔ sisi tɔɔ.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Ke e ba mi ja a, anɛ o ma nyɛ ma de ngɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ mo gbee ɔ a hɛ mi ke mawu ji mo lo? O maa le kaa nɔmlɔ adesa kɛkɛ ji mo.

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Nibwɔhi nɛ li imi Mawu ɔ ma kpata o hɛ mi; a maa gbe mo kaa a gbeɔ gbe. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.” Tiro matsɛ ɔ hɛ mi kpata

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
translation_verse: Eden, Mawu ngmɔ ɔ nitsɛ mi nɛ o hi. Tɛ kpakpa nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo o kɛ dla o he: rubi, daimond, topaz, beril, kanelian, yaspi, safiro, emerald, kɛ garnet. O ngɛ sika tsu he dlami níhi, kɛ heha ní babauu. Ligbi ɔ nɛ a bɔ mo ɔ, jamɛ a ligbi ɔ nɔuu lɛ a dla mo saminyayoo jã.

english_verse: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
translation_verse: I ngɔ Mawu bɔfo ko nɛ he ngɛ gbeye kɛ to lejɛ ɔ, konɛ e bu o he. O hi ye yo klɔuklɔu ɔ nɔ; o slaa si ngɛ tɛhi nɛ ngɛ kpɛe nylamnylam ɔ a kpɛti.

english_verse: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
translation_verse: Kɛ je be nɛ a bɔ mo ɔ, o ba o je mi pɛpɛɛpɛ, nɛ a nɛ́ tɔmi ko kulaa ngɛ o he kɛ ya su be ko, kɛkɛ nɛ o bɔni yayami peemi.

english_verse: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
translation_verse: Be nɛ jua yemi ba ngɛ nɔ yae ɔ, amimi yemi hu ba hyi o mi tɔ, nɛ o pee yayami. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i ha o je ye yo klɔuklɔu ɔ nɔ; nɛ Mawu bɔfo nɛ bu o he ɔ fie mo kɛ je tɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ kpɛe kɛ la nylamnylam ɔ a kpɛti.

english_verse: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
translation_verse: O he fɛu ɔ he ɔ, o wo o he nɔ gojoo, nɛ o je kuasia. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i tsɛ̃ mo ngɔ fia si ngɛ zugba bum. Bɔ nɛ o nyagbe ba ha nɛ ɔ maa pee kɔkɔ bɔmi nɔ́ ha matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsuo.

english_verse: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
translation_verse: O pee yayami babauu ngɛ o jua yemi ɔ mi, nɛ o kɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ble hehi nɛ o ya jaa Mawu ngɛ ɔ. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, i mɛ o he la, nɛ i sã mo pioo, nɛ o pee la zu ngɛ nihi tsuo a hɛ mi.

english_verse: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
translation_verse: Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, o be hu; o laa gbidii. Je mahi tsuo nɛ le mo ɔ, jehanɛ lɛɛ sawale nu mɛ. A ngɛ gbeye yee kaa mɛ hu a hɛ mi ma kpata ja nɔuu.” A ma kpata Sidon ma a hɛ mi

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ adesa, plɛ o hɛ mi kɛ kpee Sidon ma a, nɛ o gba kɛ si mɛ.

english_verse: and tell its people: I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: De mɛ ke imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ke i kɛ mɛ ná. Je ma amɛ maa wo ye hɛ mi nyami ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ ma pee Sidon ma a he. Ma gbla Sidon tue, konɛ a na bɔ nɛ i ngɛ klɔuklɔu ha. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ma ha gbenɔ hiɔ ma ba sɛ ma a mi; a maa ye awi ngɛ gbɛjegbɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ. A ma ba sa ma a yi, nɛ a kɛ klaate maa gbe ma a mi bi ɔmɛ. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.” A maa gbaa Israel

english_verse: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
translation_verse: Yawɛ ke, “Je ma amɛ nɛ bɔle Israel kɛ kpe nɛ a pue e hɛ mi si ɔ, ekoeko be e he pee kaa mio, loo mio tso kɛ plaa Israel hu. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le kaa imi ji Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ngɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Ma kpale ye ma Israel kɛ je je ma amɛ a kpɛti he nɛ i gbɛ mɛ kɛ fĩa a, nɛ je ma amɛ tsuo maa le kaa nɔ klɔuklɔu ji mi. Israel ma a ma ba hi mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɛ i ngɔ ha ye tsɔlɔ Yakob ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: A maa hi si ngɛ tue mi jɔmi, kɛ he jɔmi mi. A maa ma tsuhi, nɛ a ma hu wai ngmɔhi. Nihi tsuo nɛ pue Israel hɛ mi si ɔ, ma gbla a tue, nɛ Israel ma na he jɔmi, kɛ tue mi jɔmi kulaa. Lɔ ɔ loko a ma na maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Benɛ a nuu wɔ kɛ ho ma se ya a, jeha nyɔngmane ɔ we nyɔhiɔ nyɔngma a we ligbi nyɔngma kɛ enyɔne ɔ, Yawɛ de mi ke,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ adesa, plɛ o hɛ mi kɛ kpee Egipt matsɛ ɔ, nɛ o de lɛ ke a maa gbla e kɛ e ma a tsuo a tue.

english_verse: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
translation_verse: De lɛ ke bɔ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ngɛ Egipt matsɛ ɔ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: Mo wo mi lohwe gbeyegbeye, i kɛ mo ná. O ke Nilo pa a o nɔ, nɛ mo lɛ o pee.

english_verse: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
translation_verse: Ma wo o nya mi gbowe, nɛ e maa la o tsitsa; kɛkɛ ɔ, lo ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ pa a mi maa mɛtɛ o he toto ɔmɛ a he. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ma gbla mo kɛ je Nilo pa a mi, kɛ lo ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ mɛtɛ o he ɔ.

english_verse: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
translation_verse: Ma sake mo, kɛ lo ɔmɛ tsuo ngɔ fɔ nga a nɔ. O ma ya nɔ si, nɛ o ma gbo kɛ fɔ lejɛ ɔ. A be mo pue; ma ha lohwe awi yeli, kɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ mohu maa ye mo.

english_verse: Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord. You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ɔ, Egipt ma a tsuo maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.” Yawɛ ke, “Egipt ngɛ kaa gla nɛ Israel kɛ pee dɛma tso.

english_verse: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
translation_verse: Benɛ a pɛtɛ he ɔ, e ku, nɛ e plaa a konɔ tsuo. A ke a ma kpasa lɛ ɔ, e ku nɛ e ha a nanehi hluã.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, jehanɛ lɛɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ dee ke imi nitsɛ ma ha ta ma ba tua ma a. A maa gbe nɔ tsuaa nɔ; a ma kpata lohwehi tsuo a hɛ mi.

english_verse: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
translation_verse: Nɔ ko nɔ ko be Egipt zugba a nɔ hie hu; zugba a maa pee ma doku nɛ e maa fɔ si gu. Lɔ ɔ loko a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ. “Akɛnɛ o ke Nilo pa a o nɔ́, nɛ́ mo nitsɛ lɛ o pee he je ɔ,

english_verse: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
translation_verse: i kɛ mo ná, nɛ i kɛ o Nilo pa a hu ná. Ma ha Egipt zugba a tsuo nɔ maa je gu; e maa pee ma dokuhi sɔuu kɛ je Migdol ngɛ omleyi je kɛ yaa su Aswan ngɛ leneyi je, hluu kɛ ma ya su Sudan bi ɔmɛ a huzu ɔ nya tɔɔ.

english_verse: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
translation_verse: Nane ko nane ko be zugba a nɔ nyɛɛe hu, nɔmlɔ nɔ́ jio, lohwe nɔ́ jio. Lejɛ ɔ maa fɔ si gu jeha nyingmi eywiɛ sɔuu.

english_verse: They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom
translation_verse: Ma ha a ma ba hi a hi he momo ɔ ngɛ Egipt leneyi je. A ma ba to nɔ yemi ko nɛ he wɛ kulaa sisi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past.
translation_verse: E maa pee nɔ yemi nɛ he wɛ pe kulaa. Ma pee mɛ ma wayoo, bɔ nɛ a be nyɛe maa ye je ma amɛ ekoeko nɔ hu.

english_verse: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
translation_verse: Ke e ba mi ja a, e be ma nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ maa ngɔ a hɛ kɛ fɔ e nɔ pee hu. Ejakaa a ma kai kaa e ji tɔmi agbo kaa Israel ngɔ e hɛ kɛ fɔ Egipt nɔ. Kɛkɛ ɔ, Israel maa le kaa imi ji Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ.” Matsɛ Nebukadnezar maa ngɔ Egipt zugba a

english_verse: Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Benɛ a nuu wɔ kɛ ho ma se ya a, jeha nyingmi enyɔ kɛ kpaagone ɔ we kekleekle nyɔhiɔ ɔ we kekleekle ligbi ɔ, Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu, nɛ e de mi ke,

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ adesa, Nebukadnezar, Babilonia matsɛ ɔ ya tua Tiro. E ha e ta buli tsu ní kpakpataa ngɛ ta nɛ e kɛ Tiro ngɛ hwue ɔ he: a tloo tlomi nɛ jiɔ; nɔ tsuaa nɔ yi mi kpa, nɛ e konɔ kpɔ. Se matsɛ ɔ kɛ e tabo ɔ na we se ko kɛ ji dengme nɛ a gbo ɔ mi.

english_verse: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: I ngɔ Egipt zugba a kɛ ha lɛ kaa e hiɔwo; ejakaa imi lɛ e tabo ɔ tsu ní ɔ kɛ ha. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: “Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, ma ha Israel ma na he wami he, nɛ ma ha Ezekiel maa tu munyu wawɛɛ ngɛ ma a tsuo hɛ mi, konɛ a le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ adesa, gbaa nɛ o ha nɛ a le nɔ́ nɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ dee ɔ. Wo yana nɛ o de ke, Ligbi yaya! Ligbi yaya ko ma!

english_verse: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
translation_verse: Ligbi ɔ su ta. Ligbi ɔ nɛ Yawɛ ma tsu nyakpɛ ní ɔ maa pee aywilɛho, kɛ amanehlu be nitsɛ kɛ ha ma amɛ.

english_verse: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
translation_verse: A maa hwu ta ngɛ Egipt; nɛ Sudan maa hao wawɛɛ. A maa gbe nihi babauu ngɛ Egipt; a maa muɔ e juetli kɛ je; nɛ ma a maa pee ma doku posoposo.

english_verse: All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Mahi nɛ piɛɔ Egipt he kɛ je Migdol ngɛ omleyi je kɛ ya su Aswan ngɛ leneyi je ɔ, a mi bi tsuo a hɛ mi ma kpata ngɛ ta a mi. Tabo ɔ nɛ Egipt kɛ fĩaa a hɛ mi ma kpata kulaa. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
translation_verse: E zugba a maa pee pasaa kulaa ngɛ je ɔ mi, nɛ e ma amɛ ma plɛ pee ma dokuhi.

english_verse: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke i mɛ Egipt he la, nɛ i kpata e he piɛli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi ɔ, kɛkɛ a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
translation_verse: “Ke be ɔ nɛ ma kpata Egipt hɛ mi ɔ su ɔ, ma tsɔ nihi nɛ a he sɔɔ kɛ gu wo ɔ nɔ kɛ ya wo Sudan bi ɔmɛ nɛ a hɛ be a he nɔ ɔ he gbeye, konɛ sawale nɛ nu mɛ. Jamɛ a be ɔ su ta!”

english_verse: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Ma ha Nebukadnezar, Babilonia matsɛ ɔ ma ba muɔ Egipt ma a tsuo kɛ ho.

english_verse: He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
translation_verse: E kɛ e tabo yiwutsotsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ma ba kpata zugba a hɛ mi. A kɛ klaate ma ba tua Egipt. Zugba a nɔ ma hyi tɔ kɛ ni gbogboehi.

english_verse: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
translation_verse: Ma ha Nilo pa a maa mii. Ma jua Egipt zugba a tsuo kɛ ha yiwutsotsɛmɛ ɔmɛ. Ma ha nibwɔhi ma kpata zugba a, kɛ e nɔ bi tsuo a hɛ mi. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Ma kpata wɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ amaga amɛ nɛ ngɛ Memfis ɔ a hɛ mi. Ganɔ ko be Egipt zugba a nɔ yee hu; lejɛ ɔ maa pee gbeye. Ma ha nɛ sawale maa nu nɔ tsuaa nɔ.

english_verse: The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed!
translation_verse: Ma ha Egipt leneyi je maa pee ma doku pasaa; nɛ Zoan nɛ ngɛ omleyi je ɔ, ma mɛ he la. Ma gbla Tebes ma a tue.

english_verse: The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
translation_verse: Pelusium, Egipt ma a nɛ a fia gbogbo kɛ bɔle lɛ ɔ hu, ye mi mi maa wo la kɛ wo e he. Ma kpata Tebes ma a tsuo a hɛ mi.

english_verse: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
translation_verse: Ma mɛ Egipt he la, nɛ Pelusium maa hao wawɛɛ. Ma ku Tebes gbogbo ɔmɛ kɛ pue si, nɛ ma a mi ma hyi tɔ kɛ nyu.

english_verse: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
translation_verse: Heliopolis, kɛ Bubastis ma amɛ a mi nihewi ma gbo ngɛ ta mi, nɛ nihi nɛ maa piɛ ɔ lɛɛ a maa nuu mɛ nyɔguɛ.

english_verse: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
translation_verse: Ma kpɔ Egipt he wami ɔ ngɛ e dɛ, nɛ e he nɔ womi babauu ɔ se maa po; jamɛ a be ɔ, diblii maa wo ngɛ Tafanes piani katakata. Amanehlu maa pee kaa bɔku nɛ ha Egipt zugba a nɔ, nɛ a maa nuu e ma amɛ a mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo nyɔguɛ.

english_verse: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
translation_verse: Ke i gbla Egipt tue wawɛɛ kikɛ nɛ ɔ, kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.” Egipt matsɛ ɔ he wami ɔ ta

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Benɛ a nuu wɔ kɛ ho ma se ya a, jeha nyɔngma kɛ kakene ɔ we kekleekle nyɔhiɔ ɔ we ligbi kpaagone ɔ, Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword.
translation_verse: E de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, i ku Egipt matsɛ ɔ kɔni. Nɔ ko nɔ ko to we nɔ tsopa; a fi we hulɔ, konɛ e kɔni ɔ nɛ tsa, nɛ́ e na he wami nɛ e kɛ pɛtɛ klaate he ekohu.

english_verse: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, bɔ nɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ dee ji, i kɛ Egipt matsɛ ɔ ná. Ma kplɔ e kɔni enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo. Ma ku kake ɔ kɛ piɛ nɔ́ nɛ ku momo ɔ he; kɛkɛ ɔ, e klaate ɔ maa je e dɛ kɛ nɔ si.

english_verse: and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
translation_verse: Ma gbɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ ngɔ fĩa je ɔ mi tsuo.

english_verse: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ee, Egipt matsɛ ɔ kɔnihi ma kplɔ ngɛ e he; se Babilonia matsɛ ɔ lɛɛ, ma wo lɛ he wami. Ke i wo e dɛ mi klaate, nɛ e wo nɔ kɛ tsɔɔ Egipt blɔ ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ ma ná maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_verse: Ma gbɛ Egipt bi ɔmɛ kɛ fĩa je ɔ mi tsuo. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a ma ná maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
translation_verse: Benɛ a nuu wɔ kɛ ho ma se ya a, jeha nyɔngma kɛ kakene ɔ we nyɔhiɔ etɛ ɔ we kekleekle ligbi ɔ, Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
translation_verse: E de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, de Egipt matsɛ ɔ, kɛ e ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo ke: O he wa saminya! Mɛni he po ma ngɔ mo kɛ to?

english_verse: There was once a cedar tree in Lebanon with large, strong branches reaching to the sky.
translation_verse: O ngɛ kaa seda tso ko nɛ bɔ kusuu ngɛ Lebanon, e kɔni saminyawiiwi ɔmɛ pee hɔ; e ka gagaa kɛ su bɔku mi tɔɔ.

english_verse: This tree had plenty of water to help it grow tall, and nearby streams watered the other trees in the forest.
translation_verse: Nyu babaaba ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, kɛ zugba a mi tsuo; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e na niye ní bɔ nɛ sa. Nyu ɔ ha tso kpa amɛ tsuo bɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Birds built nests in its branches, and animals were born beneath it. People from all nations lived in the shade of this strong tree.
translation_verse: Lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ slɔɔtoslɔɔto ya pee a tsuhi ngɛ e kɔni nguangua amɛ a nɔ. Nga mi lohwehi tsuo ya fɔ a bimɛ ngɛ e kɔni wawi ɔmɛ a sisi, nɛ je ma nguanguahi tsuo ya hii si ngɛ e sisi hɔ̃ ɔ mi.

english_verse: It had beautiful, long branches, and its roots found water deep in the soil.
translation_verse: E he pee fɛu; e nɔ kuɔ gojoo, kɛ e kɔnihi gagaaga; ejakaa e sipoku na nyu babaaba kɛ je zu mi.

english_verse: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
translation_verse: I ha nɛ e pee fɛu saminya kɛ e kɔnihi babauu. Tsohi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Mawu ngmɔ ɔ mi ngɛ Eden ɔ, a hɛ kɔ e nɔ.

english_verse: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ lɛɛ, jamɛ a tso ɔ nɛ bɔ kusuu, nɛ e nɔ kuɔ gojoo kɛ su bɔku mi tɔɔ ɔ, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ nitsɛ ma tsɔɔ mo nɔ́ nɛ maa ba e nɔ. Akɛnɛ e nɔ kuɔ gojoo he je ɔ, e wo e he nɔ nɛ e fĩa;

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
translation_verse: lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kua lɛ. Ma ha nubwɔ ko nine maa su e nɔ. E kɛ lɛ maa ye sisiisi; e maa pee lɛ bɔ nɛ sa lɛ ngɛ yi wu tso níhi nɛ e pee ɔ a he.

english_verse: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
translation_verse: Nibwɔhi nɛ ji je ma amɛ a kpɛti yiwutsotsɛmɛ pe kulaa maa hɛ lɛ ngɔ fɔ si, nɛ a maa je e he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. E kɔni wawi ɔmɛ ma ya pue yo ɔmɛ a nɔ, kɛ kɔ̃ ɔmɛ a mi; nɛ e kɔni agbo ɔmɛ maa ku kɛ pue nyu dɔ ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ zugba a nɔ tsuo. Je ma amɛ nɛ ngɛ e hɔ̃ ɔ mi ɔ maa je.

english_verse: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
translation_verse: Lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ ma ba ma tso nɛ a hɛ ngɔ fɔ si ɔ nɔ, nɛ pu mi lohwehi ma ba hi e kɔni ɔmɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, kɛ je mwɔnɛ ɔ kɛ yaa a, tso nɛ naa nyu saminya a ekoeko be kae kɛ ya hiɔwe ja hu, loo kaa e ma ha e yi mi ma ya su bɔku mi ploplooplo kikɛ nɛ ɔ. Mɛ tsuo a ma gbo kaa bɔ nɛ nɔmlɔ adesa gboɔ ɔ. Mɛ tsuo a ma ya piɛ nihi nɛ ho gbeje ya a a he.”

english_verse: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ngɛ dee ji, “Ligbi ɔ nɛ tso ɔ ma ya su gbeje ɔ, ma ha pahi nɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ maa ha e nɔ; a maa pee ja kɛ tsɔɔ kaa a ngɛ ya nyɛe ha lɛ. Ma tsi pa amɛ a nya nɛ a ko be hu, nɛ pa wawi, kɛ nyu dɔ ɔmɛ maa ta. Akɛnɛ tso ɔ gbo he je ɔ, ma ha diblii maa wo ngɛ Lebanon yo ɔmɛ a nɔ; pu mi tso ɔmɛ tsuo ma ngla.

english_verse: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
translation_verse: Ma ha e maa nɔ si haa bum kɛ maa ya gbeje; nɛ je ma amɛ ma mimiɛ, ke a nu e si nɔmi ɔ. Eden ngmɔ ɔ mi tso ɔmɛ tsuo, kɛ Lebanon tsohi nɛ a je blɔ ha mɛ nyu saminya, nɛ mɛɛ lɛɛ a ho gbeje ya momo ɔ, a bua maa jɔ wawɛɛ kaa tso nɛ ɔ nɔ si.

english_verse: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
translation_verse: A ma kpaka lɛ kɛ ho gbeje ya, konɛ e ya piɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ nɔ momo ɔ a he. Nɛ mahi tsuo nɛ hi e hɔ̃ ɔ mi ɔ maa gbɛ fĩa je ɔ mi tsuo.

english_verse: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Tso nɛ ɔ daa si ha Egipt matsɛ ɔ, kɛ e ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo. Tsohi nɛ ngɛ Eden ngmɔ ɔ mi po ka we, nɛ a he hu pee we fɛu kaa tso nɛ ɔ. Se jehanɛ lɛɛ kaa bɔ nɛ Eden ngmɔ ɔ mi tso ɔmɛ ya su gbeje ɔ, lɛ hu e maa ya lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e ma ya piɛ nihi nɛ a pui mɛ, kɛ nihi nɛ nɔ ngɛ ta mi ɔ a he. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
translation_verse: Benɛ a nuu wɔ kɛ ho ma se ya a, jeha nyɔngma kɛ enyɔne ɔ we nyɔhiɔ nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ ɔ we kekleekle ligbi ɔ, Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying: You act like a lion roaming the earth; but you are nothing more than a crocodile in a river, churning up muddy water with your feet.
translation_verse: E de ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, la hɛdo la nɛ o kɛ bɔ Egipt matsɛ ɔ kɔkɔ. Ngɔɔ ye sɛ gbi nɛ ɔ kɛ ha lɛ: O peeɔ o níhi kaa nɔ́ nɛ jata ji mo ngɛ je ma amɛ a kpɛti; se o ngɛ kaa nyaka nɛ ngɛ pa gudue mohu. O tuɔ kɛ sɛɛ o pa amɛ a mi tsulaoo; o kɛ o nane gbidii nyu ɔ kɛ puɛɔ pa amɛ.

english_verse: King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore.
translation_verse: Ke je ma amɛ ba bua a he nya babauu ɔ, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ nitsɛ ma fɔ ye ya a kɛ pue o nɔ; e maa du mo, nɛ je ma amɛ maa gbla mo kɛ ba kpo.

english_verse: I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh.
translation_verse: Ma sake mo ngɔ fɔ zugba; nɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ, kɛ nga mi lohwehi tsuo ma ba ye mo.

english_verse: I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys,
translation_verse: Ma sake o gbogboe ɔmɛ kɛ pue yo ɔmɛ a nɔ, kɛ kɔ̃ ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining.
translation_verse: Benɛ ma kpata o hɛ mi ɔ, ma tsi hiɔwe hɛ mi; dodoe ɔmɛ maa laa. Pu maa laa e hɛ mi ngɛ bɔku ɔmɛ a se; nɛ nyɔhiɔ be kpɛe hu.

english_verse: The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ma ha pu, nyɔhiɔ, kɛ dodoe ɔmɛ tsuo maa laa, nɛ diblii maa wo ngɛ je ɔ mi tsuo. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you.
translation_verse: “Je mahi babauu, ngɛ zugbahi a nɔ he nɛ o li tete po, ke a nu bɔ nɛ i kpata o hɛ mi ɔ, a maa ye tsui.

english_verse: The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt!
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ngɛ Egipt matsɛ ɔ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Ma ha Babilonia matsɛ ɔ kɛ mo maa hwu ta.

english_verse: Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed.
translation_verse: Ma ha o tabo kpekpemi ɔ maa nɔ ngɛ katsɛmɛ kpanakpanaa a klaate nya. O kɛ o ma a, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o ngɔɔ o hɛ kɛ fɔɔ nɔ ɔ nyɛ hɛ mi ma kpata.

english_verse: I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water.
translation_verse: Ma gbe o lohwe ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ pa amɛ a tue, nɛ nane ko nane ko be pa a gbidie hu; nɔmlɔ jio, lohwe jio.

english_verse: The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ, ma ha o nyu ɔ hɛ mi ma tsɔ, nɛ pa amɛ maa be kaa nu. Imi Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke i kpata Egipt ma a, kɛ e mi níhi, kɛ nimli tsuo nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ a hɛ mi kikɛ ɔ, kɛkɛ a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. A Sad Ending for Egypt
translation_verse: Kɔkɔ nɛ a ngɛ mo bɔe nɛ ɔ ma ba pee kɔmɔ yemi la nɛ a ma la. Yihi nɛ ngɛ je ma amɛ a mi ma la la nɛ ɔ kɛ nyɛ ya ha Egipt kɛ Egipt bi tsuo. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.” Gbeje

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations.
translation_verse: E ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, ye kɔmɔ ha Egipt ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo. Ngɔɔ a kɛ je ma amɛ nɛ a hɛ mi ngɛ nyami ɔ kɛ ya zugba a sisi tɔɔ kɛ ya piɛ nihi nɛ ngɛ gbeje ɔ a he.

english_verse: Say to them: You may be more beautiful than the people of other nations, but you will also die and join the godless in the world below.
translation_verse: De mɛ ke, “Pe nyɛ susuɔ kaa nyɛ he ngɛ fɛu pe nihi tsuo lo? Nyɛ ma ba be kɛ ho gbeje ya, nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ ma ya hi lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you.
translation_verse: “Egipt bi ɔmɛ, kɛ nihi nɛ nɔ ngɛ ta mi ɔ a nyagbe maa ba si kake. Ta ma ba kpata mɛ tsuo a hɛ mi.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Yɔkɔ nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ gbeje muɔ ɔ sisi tɔɔ. E ta buli ɔmɛ tsuo nɔ ngɛ ta mi; nɛ a yɔkɔ ɔmɛ bɔle e nɔ́ ɔ. Se be ko nɛ be ɔ, mɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ wo nihi a he gbeye wawɛɛ ngɛ je ɔ mi.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
translation_verse: Elam hwɔɔ si kɛ piɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ nɔ ngɛ ta mi ɔ a he. E ta buli kpekpemi ɔ a yɔkɔ ɔmɛ bɔle lɛ kɛ kpe. Ni nɛmɛ nɛ gbo ngɛ ta mi nɛ ɔ, mɛ tsuo mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ ji mɛ. Benɛ a ngɛ wami mi ɔ, a wo nihi a he gbeye wawɛɛ; se jehanɛ lɛɛ a gbo kɛ fɔɔ si kɛ zo kpɔtɔɔ.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Meshek kɛ Tubal tsuo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ a ta buli ɔmɛ a yɔkɔ ɔmɛ bɔle mɛ kɛ kpe. Mɛ tsuo mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ ji mɛ; a gbe mɛ ngɛ ta mi. Be ko ɔ, a wo je ɔ he gbeye wawɛɛ.

english_verse: They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
translation_verse: A pu we mɛ kaa bɔ nɛ a puɔ katsɛmɛ blema a. Blema a, a puɔ katsɛ kaa nɔ ko nɛ mia e ta hwumi ní kɛ yaa gbeje: a ngɔɔ e klaate kɛ hɔɔ e yi sisi, nɛ a kɛ e tsɛ̃i haa e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he. Katsɛmɛ nɛ a wo a hɛ mi nyami kikɛ nɛ ɔ ji nihi nɛ a he sawale nuɔ je ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
translation_verse: “Kikɛ nɛ ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ a maa ku Egipt bi ɔmɛ a mi kɛ pue mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ nɛ nɔ ngɛ ta mi ɔ a nɔ.

english_verse: The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Edom kɛ e matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ e ganɔ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Be ko ɔ, ta buli katsɛmɛ ji mɛ; se jehanɛ lɛɛ a ngɛ gbeje, nɛ a kɛ mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ nɛ nɔ ngɛ ta mi ɔ tsuo ngɛ he kake.

english_verse: The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Omleyi je ganɔ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Sidon bi ɔmɛ hu ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Be ko ɔ, a he wami ɔ haa sawale nuɔ je ɔ tsuo; se jehanɛ lɛɛ a kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ nɔ ngɛ ta mi ɔ, zo gbe mɛ tsuo kpɔtɔɔ. Mɛ tsuo mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ ji mɛ, nɛ a ya su gbeje muɔ voo ɔ sisi tɔɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God says: When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering.
translation_verse: “Ke Egipt matsɛ ɔ kɛ e tabo ɔ na nihi babauu nɛ a gbe ngɛ ta a mi nɛ ɔ, a bua maa jɔ.” Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ de.

english_verse: I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Imi nitsɛ lɛ i ha Egipt matsɛ ɔ hao je ɔ nɛ; se lɛ nitsɛ kɛ e tabo ɔ tsuo a hɛ mi ma kpata, nɛ a maa pu mɛ, kɛ mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a gbe ngɛ ta a mi ɔ.” Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ de.

english_verse: and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming.
translation_verse: Ke e na he nyɛli ɔmɛ nɛ a ma a, e ma kpa titimati kɛ wo ma a tue nɔ.

english_verse: Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
translation_verse: Yayami nɛ e pee ɔ, ma ngɔ kɛ pa lɛ, nɛ e yi ma na wami; ejakaa e pee nɔ́ nɛ da, nɛ e ye dami sane.

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
translation_verse: Benɛ a nuu wɔ kɛ ho ma se ya a, jeha nyɔngma kɛ enyɔne ɔ we nyɔhiɔ nyɔngmane ɔ we ligbi enuɔne ɔ, nyumu ko nɛ tu fo kɛ je Yerusalem, ba bɔ mi amaniɛ ke he nyɛli ba ywia Yerusalem ma a.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ekohu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying: Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch
translation_verse: E ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, tu munyu kɛ tsɔɔ o ma a mi bi ɔmɛ, nɛ o de mɛ nɔ́ nɛ maa ba ke i ha ta ba zugba ko nɔ ɔ. Ma a mi bi ɔmɛ maa hla a kpɛti nɔ kake kaa a ma a he bulɔ.

english_verse: If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
translation_verse: Ejakaa e nu titimati ɔ pɛmi, se e bui. E bu tue jinɛ e ko he lɛ nitsɛ e yi wami.

english_verse: But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ hu, ke bulɔ ɔ na he nyɛli ɔmɛ nɛ a ma, nɛ e kpa we titimati kɛ wo ma a tue nɔ ɔ, he nyɛli ɔmɛ ma ba gbe yayami peeli ɔmɛ lɛɛ, se ma bi a muɔ si ngɛ bulɔ ɔ dɛ.

english_verse: Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ adesa, jehanɛ bu tue, ma pee mo Israel ma a he bulɔ. Munyuhi nɛ ma tu kɛ bɔ mɛ kɔkɔ ɔ, de mɛ lɛ tsuo.

english_verse: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Ke i de ke yayami peelɔ ko ma gbo ngɛ e yayami nɛ e ngɛ pee ɔ he, se o bɔɛ lɛ kɔkɔ, konɛ e tsake kɛ je e blɔ yayami ɔ nɔ nɛ e yi nɛ na wami ɔ, e ma gbo ngɛ e yayami ɔmɛ a he lɛɛ, se ma bi e muɔ si ngɛ o dɛ.

english_verse: If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent. The Lord Is Always Fair (Ezekiel
translation_verse: Ke o bɔ yayami peelɔ kɔkɔ, se e tsakee we e tsui nɛ e kpa yayami nɛ e ngɛ pee ɔ, e ma gbo ngɛ e yayami ɔ he, se moo lɛɛ o maa ye o he.” Nɔ tsuaa nɔ maa bu e ní tsumi he akɔtaa

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Ke dalɔ kpale kɛ je e dami blɔ ɔ nɔ, nɛ e pee yayami ɔ, yayami ɔ he e ma gbo ngɛ.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, ke o ma a mi bi ɔmɛ ba kpe ngɛ ma a gbogbo ɔmɛ a he, loo a we agbo ɔmɛ a nya a, o he munyu sɔuu lɛ a hii tue. Bɔ nɛ a deɔ a sibi ji, ‘Nyɛɛ ba nɛ wa ya bu munyu nɛ kpale je Yawɛ ngɔ kɛ ba amlɔ nɛ ɔ tue.’

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me.
translation_verse: Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu. E ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, bɔ nɛ Israel ma a ngɛ dee ji, ‘Wa tɔmi ɔmɛ, kɛ wa he yayami ɔmɛ pee tlomi ngɛ wa nɔ, nɛ e ha wa ngɛ he lo tae. Kɛ wa maa pee kɛ hi je mi kɛɛ?’

english_verse: Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
translation_verse: De mɛ ke imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ ye he kita kae ke i na we yayami peelɔ gbenɔ he bua jɔmi, se mohu i suɔ kaa e kpa yayami peemi, konɛ e yi nɛ na wami. Israel, nyɛ kpa yayami nɛ nyɛ ngɛ pee ɔ. Mɛni he je nyɛ suɔ mohu kaa nyɛ ma gbo ɔ?

english_verse: Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ adesa, jehanɛ de Israel ma a ke, ke dalɔ pee yayami ɔ, kpakpa nɛ e pee be ko ɔ be nyɛe ma he e yi wami. Ke yayami peelɔ kpa yayami peemi ɔ, a be e tue gblae; nɛ ke dalɔ bɔni yayami peemi ɔ, a be e yi wami hee.

english_verse: Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Ke i de dalɔ ko ke bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, e yi ma na wami, kɛkɛ nɛ e bɔni kpakpa nɛ e pee be ko ɔ he susumi kaa e hiɛ babauu, nɛ jehanɛ e bɔni yayami peemi ɔ, i be kpakpa nɛ e pee be ko ɔ kaie. Yayamihi nɛ e pee ɔ a he e ma gbo ngɛ.

english_verse: Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right.
translation_verse: Ke i bɔ yayami peelɔ kɔkɔ kaa e ma gbo, kɛkɛ nɛ e kpa yayami peemi, nɛ e bɔni nɔ́ nɛ da peemi kɛ dami sane yemi ɔ, e be gboe; e yi ma na wami.

english_verse: For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ ji kaa nɔ́ ko nɛ a kɛ ba to awaba ngɛ e ngɔ ɔ, e kpale kɛ ya ha nɔtsɛ; aloo nɔ́ ko nɛ e ya ju ɔ, e kpale ya ha nɔtsɛ. Ke e kpa yayami peemi, nɛ e bɔni mlaahi nɛ haa nɔ wami ɔ a nɔ yemi ɔ, e be gboe; e yi ma na wami.

english_verse: Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair.
translation_verse: “Se o ma a mi bi ɔmɛ ke nɔ́ nɛ i peeɔ ɔ dɛ! Dɛbi, mɛ mohu lɛ a ní peepee ɔmɛ dɛ!

english_verse: And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Ke yayami peelɔ kpa yayami peemi, nɛ e pee nɔ́ nɛ da, nɛ e ye dami sane ɔ, e he e yi wami.

english_verse: But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done. The News of Jerusalem's Fall
translation_verse: Se kɛ̃ ɔ, Israel ma, nyɛ ke nɔ́ nɛ i peeɔ ɔ dɛ. Nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ peeɔ ɔ, lɔ ɔ nɔ ma da kɛ kojo lɛ.” A ywia Yerusalem ma a

english_verse: The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak. What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
translation_verse: Gbɔkuɛ ɔ nɛ e nɔ jena mɔtu loko amaniɛ bɔlɔ ɔ ba a, Yawɛ he wami ɔ ma ye nya. Se mɔtu maa pee benɛ e ba a, Yawɛ bli ye nya momo, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i nyɛ tu munyu. Ma a pee yayamihi babauu

english_verse: Then the Lord said:
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de mi ke,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
translation_verse: “Nɔmlɔ adesa, nihi nɛ ngɛ ma doku ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ Israel zugba a nɔ ɔ deɔ mi ke, ‘Abraham ɔ nɛ a ngɔ zugba a tsuo ngɔ ha lɛ ɔ, nɔ kake too ji lɛ, se wɔɔ lɛɛ wa he hiɛ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, zugba a, wɔ a kɛ ha kaa wa weto ní.’

english_verse: So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying: How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder
translation_verse: “De mɛ ke imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, bɔ nɛ i ngɛ dee ji, nyɛ yeɔ lo nɛ muɔ ngɛ mi. Nyɛ jaa amagahi. Nyɛ pueɔ muɔ si. Mɛni ha nɛ nyɛ susuɔ kaa nyɛ nɔ ji zugba a?

english_verse: and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
translation_verse: Nyɛ hiaa klaate kɛ woɔ nyɛ sibi a he. Nyɛ tsuɔ níhi nɛ a hiee babauu; nyɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ nyɛ puɛɔ gba. Mɛni kulaa lɛ haa nyɛ susuɔ kaa nyɛ nɔ́ ji zugba a?

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases.
translation_verse: “De mɛ ke imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ ye he kita kae ke bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, nihi nɛ ngɛ ma doku ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, a ma kpata mɛ tsuo a hɛ mi. Nihi nɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ, nga mi lohwe awi yeli maa ye mɛ. Nɛ nihi nɛ ya laa a he ngɛ yo ɔmɛ a nɔ, kɛ tɛ muɔhi a mi ɔ, gbenɔ hiɔ maa gbe mɛ.

english_verse: I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them.
translation_verse: Ma ha zugba a nɔ tsuo maa pee pasaa kulaa, kɛkɛ ɔ, zugba a mi he wami nɛ a ngɔ a hɛ kɛ fɔ nɔ ɔ se maa po. Yo ɔmɛ a nɔ maa je gu; lejɛ ɔmɛ maa pee gbeye, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be lejɛ ɔmɛ gue hu.

english_verse: I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord. The People Listen, but Don't Change The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ke i pee zugba a tsuo pasaa nɛ e pee ma doku ngɛ yayamihi babauu nɛ a pee ɔ a he ɔ, kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.” Nɔ́ nɛ ba ngɛ gbalɔ ɔ sɛ gbi ɔ se

english_verse: So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ye ma a baa o ngɔ, nɛ a ba hii si ngɛ o hɛ mi nɛ a buɔ munyu ɔmɛ tue, se nɔ́ nɛ o deɔ mɛ ke a pee ɔ, lɔ ɔ lɛɛ a pee we. Á yeɔ nɔ he fɛu, nɛ a se nami he pɛ a susuɔ.

english_verse: They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
translation_verse: A buɔ mo kaa nɔ ko nɛ laa suɔmi la kɛ gbi ngɔngɔɛ, aloo nɔ ko nɛ le saku fiami saminya. A ba buɔ o munyu ɔmɛ tue lɛɛ, se a yi nɔ.

english_verse: Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_verse: Níhi nɛ o de mɛ ɔ tsuo maa ba mi sisiisi. Ke a ba mi ɔ, kɛkɛ a maa le kaa gbalɔ ko kɛ mɛ ba hi si hyɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ekohu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them: I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep.
translation_verse: E ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, gbaa kɛ si Israel nɔ yeli ɔmɛ. De mɛ ke bɔ nɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ mɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Musu tloo nyɛ Israel to hyɛli! Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ he pɛ nyɛ ngɛ lɛe; nyɛ hyɛ we to ɔmɛ a nɔ! Anɛ pi to ɔmɛ mohu nɛ to hyɛlɔ hyɛɛ lo?

english_verse: You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock!
translation_verse: Se nyɛɛ lɛɛ nyɛ gbeɔ to nɛ wo zɔ ɔ nɛ nyɛ yeɔ; nyɛ ngɔɔ to he womi ɔ kɛ kpɛɔ tade nɛ nyɛ woɔ, se to ɔmɛ lɛɛ nyɛ ha we mɛ ní.

english_verse: You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep.
translation_verse: Ní nɛmɛ nɛ gbɔjɔ ɔ, nyɛ hyɛ we a nɔ bɔ nɛ sa; hiɔtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, nyɛ tsa we mɛ; ní nɛmɛ nɛ plaa a, nyɛ fi we pa amɛ a nɔ ha mɛ; ní nɛmɛ nɛ tla blɔ ɔ, nyɛ ya kpakaa we mɛ; nɛ ní nɛmɛ nɛ laa a, nyɛ ya hla we mɛ. Se yi mi mohu nyɛ waa mɛ.

english_verse: They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: To hyɛlɔ ko be; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, to ɔmɛ gbɛ fĩa, nɛ lohwe awi yeli ya nuu mɛ nɛ a ye.

english_verse: Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep.
translation_verse: Imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ ye he kita kae, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛ ta tue. Nga mi lohwe awi yeli nuu ye to ɔmɛ, a gbe mɛ nɛ a ye nyamanyama, ejakaa to hyɛlɔ ko be; ye to hyɛli ɔmɛ dí to ɔmɛ a se. To hyɛli ɔmɛ ngɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a he lɛe; a hyɛ we to ɔmɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
translation_verse: Imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ke i kɛ nyɛ ná. Ma kpɔ ye to ɔmɛ ngɛ nyɛ dɛ. I be hae nɛ nyɛɛ lɛ nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ he hu. Ma kpɔ ye to ɔmɛ kɛ je nyɛ dɛ; kɛkɛ ɔ, nyɛ be mɛ nae maa ye hu. To hyɛlɔ kpakpa a

english_verse: The Lord God then said: I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself,
translation_verse: “Imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ nyɛ dee ke, imi nitsɛ ma hla ye to ɔmɛ a se blɔ, nɛ ma hyɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ to hyɛlɔ hlaa e tohi nɛ gbɛ fĩa, nɛ e buaa a nya ekohu ɔ, jã ma hla ye to ɔmɛ a se blɔ. Ma kpaka mɛ kɛ je he tsuaa he nɛ a gbɛ fĩa ligbi ɔ nɛ jamɛ amanehlu kɔɔhiɔ yaya ba fia mɛ ɔ.

english_verse: and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields.
translation_verse: Ma je mɛ kɛ je je ma amɛ a kpɛti; ma bua a nya kɛ ba mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba a nɔ. Ma lɛ mɛ ngɛ yo ɔmɛ a nɔ, pa amɛ a he, kɛ he tsuaa he nɛ nga mumu ngɛ ngɛ Israel.

english_verse: to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right. Judgment on the Strong Sheep
translation_verse: “Tohi nɛ laa a, ma ya hla mɛ; ní nɛmɛ nɛ tla blɔ ɔ, ma ya tsɔ́ mɛ kɛ ba; ní nɛmɛ nɛ plaa a, ma fi a pa amɛ a nɔ ha mɛ; hiɔtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ hu ma tsa mɛ. Se ní nɛmɛ nɛ wo zɔ, kɛ ní nɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ he wami saminya a, ma kpata a hɛ mi; ejakaa i yeɔ dami sane.

english_verse: The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel: I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak.
translation_verse: “Jehanɛ, nyɛ ye to kuu, bɔ nɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ nyɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: Ma kojo jijɔ kake kɛ jijɔ kake a kpɛti; ma kojo akpakpo ɔmɛ kɛ agbosu ɔmɛ a kpɛti.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak.
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, jehanɛ lɛɛ tohi nɛ wo zɔ, kɛ tohi nɛ tã he lo ɔ, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ nitsɛ ma kojo a kpɛti.

english_verse: You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak,
translation_verse: Nyɛɛ lɛɛ nyɛ tsitsɛɛɔ to hiɔtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ nyɛ hɛɛ mɛ koli kɛ jee to kuu ɔ he kɛ yaa se.

english_verse: but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
translation_verse: Se imi lɛɛ ma he ye to ɔmɛ a yi wami, nɛ i be blɔ ngmɛe nɛ nɔ ko nɛ wa mɛ yi mi hu. Ma kojo jijɔ kɛ jijɔ a kpɛti.

english_verse: After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ to hyɛlɔ kake kɛ to a nya nɛ e hyɛ a nɔ. Lɛ ji ye tsɔlɔ David. E maa hyɛ a nɔ saminya.

english_verse: He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Imi Yawɛ, ma pee a Mawu, nɛ ye tsɔlɔ David maa ye ganɔ ha mɛ. Imi Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid.
translation_verse: I kɛ mɛ maa so tue mi jɔmi somi. Ma fie lohwe awi yeli tsuo kɛ je zugba a nɔ, konɛ a hi si ngɛ nga a nɔ ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi, nɛ a hwɔ mahe fuaa.

english_verse: to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Nga nɔ tso ɔmɛ maa wo yiblii, nɛ zugba a maa ba ní saminya; kɛkɛ ɔ, tue mi jɔmi maa ba zugba a nɔ. Ma kplɔ kɔsɔkɔsɔ ɔmɛ kɛ je a kuɛ mi, nɛ a ye a he kɛ je nyɔguɛ si himi mi. A ma ba hi mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɔ. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear.
translation_verse: Je ma amɛ ba be mɛ haoe nɛ a ha a ní hu. Lohwe awi yeli ba be mɛ nue nɛ a ye hu. A maa hi si ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be a he gbeye woe.

english_verse: I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ zugba nɛ baa ní saminya kɛ ha mɛ; nɛ ma ha hwɔ se maa po kulaa ngɛ zugba a nɔ; kɛkɛ ɔ, je ma amɛ be a he guɛ gbee ngɛ je ɔ mi hu.

english_verse: Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: A maa le kaa imi Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ, i kɛ mɛ ngɛ. Nɛ mɛ Israel bi ɔ, ye ma ji mɛ. Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ de.

english_verse: They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
translation_verse: “Nyɛ ye ma, nyɛ ji ye tohi nɛ i ngɛ lɛe, nɛ imi ji nyɛ Mawu.” Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ de.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ekohu.

english_verse: and say to them: I, the Lord God, am now your enemy! And I will turn your nation into an empty wasteland,
translation_verse: De lɛ ke bɔ nɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ dee ji, Edom, i kɛ mo ná! Ma pee mo pasaa.

english_verse: leaving your towns in ruins. Your land will be a desert, and then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ma pee o ma amɛ ma dokuhi; o zugba a tsuo maa pee pasaa; kɛkɛ ɔ, o maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins.
translation_verse: “O kɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ yi saasaa. Benɛ a pee yayami nɛ a ngɛ a tue gblae, nɛ a ngɛ amanehlu nae ɔ, o kɛ klaate gbe mɛ.

english_verse: And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ ye he kita kae ke a ma kpata o hɛ mi; o yi be wami nae kɔkɔɔkɔ. O pue muɔ si, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a ma pue mo hu o muɔ si.

english_verse: I will destroy your nation and kill anyone who travels through it.
translation_verse: Ma pee Edom yo ɔ nɔ pasaa kulaa. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa gu lejɛ ɔ, ma kpata e hɛ mi.

english_verse: and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ma pee mo pasaa kulaa. O ma amɛ maa pee ma dokuhi, nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be a mi hie hu. Kɛkɛ ɔ, o maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God,
translation_verse: “O de ke e ngɛ mi kaa imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, ye mahi ji Yuda, Israel, kɛ a he zugba amɛ lɛɛ, se o níhi ji mɛ tsuo, nɛ o maa ngɔ.

english_verse: just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Benɛ ye ma Israel nɔ si nɛ e pee pasaa a, o nya. Jehanɛ lɛɛ Seir yo ɔmɛ, kɛ Edom zugba a tsuo maa pee pasaa kulaa. Kɛkɛ ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel
translation_verse: Yawɛ de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, o kɛ Israel yo ɔmɛ nɛ tu munyu, nɛ o de mɛ ke sɛ gbi nɛ imi

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, am saying: Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ mɛ hae ɔ, a bu tue: Israel he nyɛli ɔmɛ pee pupuupu kɛ fĩa, nɛ a de ke, ‘Yiɛɛ! Blema yo ɔmɛ ba pee wa níhi.’

english_verse: So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛ Israel yohi, yokuhi, nyu dɔhi, kɔ̃hi, kɛ we dokuhi kɛ nyɛ he mahi nɛ a ha nyɛ mi ní nɛ nyɛ ba pee nɔ́ nɛ a yeɔ he fɛu ha mɛ, nyɛɛ bu nɔ́ nɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ i ngɛ nyɛ dee ɔ tue.

english_verse: But in my fierce anger, I will turn against those nations, and especially the Edomites, because they laughed at you the loudest and took over your pasturelands.
translation_verse: “Imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i kɛ hɛdɔ, kɛ abofu tu munyu kɛ si je ma amɛ, kɛ Edom zugba a tsuo. Mɛɛ lɛɛ a nya, nɛ a gbe ye ma a he guɛ; ejakaa a ngɔ ye zugba a, kɛ lohwe lɛmi he ɔmɛ ngɔ pee a weto ní.

english_verse: so I will now insult and disgrace them. That is my solemn promise.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ kita kae ke ma ba mɛ si kulaa, konɛ zo nɛ gbe mɛ kpɔtɔɔ.

english_verse: Trees will grow on you mountains of Israel and produce fruit for my people, because they will soon come home.
translation_verse: Se Israel yo ɔmɛ a nɔ lɛɛ tso ɔmɛ ma gba kɔnihi, nɛ a maa wo yiblii ha nyɛ ekohu. Be nɛ nyɛ maa kpale kɛ ba we ekohu ɔ su ta.

english_verse: I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes.
translation_verse: I kɛ nyɛ ngɛ. Ma hyɛ nɛ a ma hu nyɛ zugba amɛ ekohu, nɛ a ma du ní ngɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: The people of Israel will return and rebuild your ruined towns and live in them.
translation_verse: Ma ha nyɛ he maa hiɛ babauu. Nyɛ maa hi ma amɛ a mi, nɛ nyɛ ma dla maa ma doku ɔmɛ mɛ ekohu.

english_verse: Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Nimli, kɛ lohwehi a he ma ba hiɛ babauu ngɛ zugba a nɔ; a ma plɔke, nɛ a ma fɔ bimɛ. Ma ha a maa hi zugba a nɔ kaa bɔ nɛ a hi nyɛ zugba a nɔ sa a. Ma ha nyɛ maa bɔ pe kekle ɔ po. Kɛkɛ ɔ, nyɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve.
translation_verse: Ye ma Israel, ma kpale nyɛ kɛ ba zugba a nɔ, nɛ nyɛ ma ba hi lejɛ ɔ ekohu. Zugba a maa pee nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ nɔ́, nɛ nyɛ bimɛ hu i be hae nɛ a ma gbo gblegbleegble.

english_verse: It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve.
translation_verse: “Imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ke e ngɛ mi niinɛ kaa nihi deɔ ke zugba nɛ yeɔ nɔmlɔ ji mo, nɛ o ha we nɛ o mi bi a yi naa wami.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord Will Be Honored
translation_verse: He guɛ gbemi, kɛ ahlua bɔmi munyuhi nɛ je ma amɛ tuɔ ɔ, zugba a be tue bue hu. Zugba a be e bimɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi kpatae hu. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.” Israel ma na wami he

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean.
translation_verse: E ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, benɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɛ a zugba a nɔ ɔ, a ngɔ a ní peemi níhi, kɛ a blɔ yaya amɛ kɛ ble lejɛ ɔ. A je mi bami nɛ a kɛ ble a he ɔ ngɛ kaa bɔ nɛ yo nɛ ku nine nɛ e he tsɔ we ngɛ ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people
