translation_verse: I gbla a tue wawɛɛ, ejakaa ye mi mi wo la ngɛ muɔ si nɛ a pue ngɛ zugba a nɔ, kɛ amagahi nɛ a kɛ ble lɛ ɔ a he.

english_verse: Wherever they went, my name was disgraced, because foreigners insulted my people by saying I had forced them out of their own land.
translation_verse: He tsuaa he nɛ a ya a, nihi tuɔ munyu kɛ puɛɔ ye biɛ klɔuklɔu ɔ. A deɔ ke, ‘Yawɛ nitsɛ ma ji nɛ ɔ nɛ, se e fie mɛ kɛ je zugba nɛ e ha mɛ ɔ nɔ.’

english_verse: so tell the Israelites that I am saying: You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, de Israel bi ɔmɛ ke bɔ nɛ imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ i ngɛ dee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: Nɔ́ nɛ i yaa pee nɛ ɔ, pi nyɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nyɛ he, se mohu ye biɛ klɔuklɔu ɔ nɛ nyɛ ble ngɛ ma amɛ a mi he nɛ nyɛ ya a, lɔ ɔ he je.

english_verse: I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ nyu klɔuklɔu kɛ fĩa nyɛ nɔ, nɛ nyɛ he ma tsɔ. Ma tsu nyɛ he kɛ je amagahi, kɛ mu níhi tsuo nɛ nyɛ kɛ ble nyɛ he ɔ a mi.

english_verse: I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts,
translation_verse: Ma ha nyɛ tsui he, kɛ juɛmi he. Nyɛ tsui nɛ wlua kaa tɛ ɔ, ma je kɛ je nyɛ mi, nɛ ma ha nyɛ tsui nɛ he jɔ.

english_verse: because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ ye mumi ɔ kɛ wo nyɛ mi, konɛ nyɛɛ bu ye mlaa amɛ tsuo tue, nɛ nyɛɛ ye a nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ zugba a nɛ i ngɔ ha nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, nyɛ maa hi nɔ. Nyɛ maa pee ye ma, nɛ imi hu ma pee nyɛ Mawu.

english_verse: I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve.
translation_verse: Níhi tsuo nɛ bleɔ nyɛ ɔ, ma je nyɛ kɛ je a mi. Ma ha nɛ ngma maa ba ha nyɛ babauu, nɛ hwɔ be nyɛ yee hu.

english_verse: Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food.
translation_verse: Ma ha tso yiblii, kɛ ngmɔ niba ní maa hiɛ babauu, konɛ hwɔ ko ye nyɛ nɛ nyɛ pue nyɛ hɛ mi si ngɛ je ma amɛ a kpɛti hu.

english_verse: People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Israel, i ngɛ hae nɛ nyɛɛ le kaa tsa pi nyɛ he nɛ ma tsu ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo. Pe i suɔ kaa zo nɛ gbe nyɛ, nɛ nyɛ hɛ mi nɛ pue si ngɛ nyɛ je mi bami yaya a he. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: After I have made you clean, I will let you rebuild your ruined towns and let you live in them.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Ke i tsu nyɛ he kɛ je nyɛ he yayami ɔmɛ tsuo a mi ɔ, ma ha nyɛ ma ba hi nyɛ ma amɛ a mi ekohu, nɛ nyɛ ma dla maa ma we doku ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people.
translation_verse: A ma de ke zugba nɛ ɔ nɛ fɔ si gu kaa nga kplanaa a, lɔ ɔ lɛ ba pee kaa Eden ngmɔ nɛ ɔ. Ma amɛ nɛ a ku pueɔ si, nɛ a ha a mi níhi, nɛ a pee ma dokuhi ɔ, a kpale fia a gbogbo ɔmɛ ekohu, nɛ nihi ngɛ ma amɛ a mi.

english_verse: Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ɔ, je ma amɛ tsuo nɛ bɔle nyɛ kɛ kpe ɔ maa le kaa imi Yawɛ lɛ i dla ma we doku ɔmɛ, nɛ i du ní ngɛ zugba nɛ fɔ si gu ɔ nɔ. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de, nɛ ma pee hulɔ!”

english_verse: I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Nɔ́ kake nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ma bi mi nɛ ma pee ha mɛ ji, ma ha a he nɛ hiɛ babauu kaa to kuu.

english_verse: The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ma ha nɛ a ma amɛ ma hyi tɔ kɛ nimli kaa tohi nɛ a kɛ ba bɔ sami, loo nimli kpekpemi nɛ ba Yerusalem nɛ a ba ye nyami be. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones.
translation_verse: I nu Yawɛ he wami he wawɛɛ; nɛ e mumi ɔ ngɔ mi kɛ ya ma kɔ̃ ko mi. Lejɛ ɔ tsuo hyi kɛ wuhi babauu.

english_verse: The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out.
translation_verse: E kɛ mi bɔle kɔ̃ ɔ tsuo kɛ kpe; nɛ i na kaa wuhi babauu nitsɛ pueɔ si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, wuhi nɛ gbli kadokado sɔuu.

english_verse: He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?” I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e bi mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, anɛ wu nɛ ɔmɛ ma nyɛ ma na wami ekohu lo?” I he nɔ ke, “Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, mo lɛ o le!”

english_verse: He then told me to say: Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you,
translation_verse: E ya nɔ, nɛ e de mi ke, “Gbaa kɛ pue wu nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ. De wu gbigbli nɛ ɔmɛ ke á bu Yawɛ munyu ɔ tue.

english_verse: “I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live.
translation_verse: De mɛ ke imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ mɛ dee ke ma ngɔ mumi kɛ wo nyɛ mi, nɛ nyɛ maa ba wami mi ekohu.

english_verse: I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together!
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ i gba kaa bɔ nɛ a de mi ɔ. Benɛ i ngɛ munyu ɔ tue ɔ, i nu nɛ wu ɔmɛ bɔni a he mimiɛmi kɛ a sibi a he sami kpɛkpɛ kpɛkpɛ; nɛ wu kɛ wu tsa.

english_verse: I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
translation_verse: Pani kɛ lo ba ha wu ɔmɛ a he, nɛ he womi ba ha a nɔ. Se mumi be nimli tso nɛ ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
translation_verse: Jehanɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, gbaa kɛ tsɔɔ mumi ɔ. De lɛ ke Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke e je je ɔ kɔ nya eywiɛ ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ba, nɛ e ba wo mumi kɛ pue gbogboe nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ, konɛ a ba wami mi ekohu.”

english_verse: As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i gba kaa bɔ nɛ a de mi ɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ mumi ba gbogboe ɔmɛ a mi; a ba pee hɛ kali, nɛ a te da si ngɛ a nanehi a nɔ; a hiɛ babauu nitsɛ!

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, Israel ma a tsuo ngɛ kaa wu nɛ ɔmɛ. A ngɛ dee ke a gbli kadokado, nɛ a be hɛ nɔ kami ko kulaa; a kpata a hɛ mi pɛsɛpɛsɛ.

english_verse: So tell them, “I, the Lord God, promise to open your graves and set you free. I will bring you back to Israel,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, gbaa kɛ tsɔɔ ye ma Israel, nɛ o de mɛ ke imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ nitsɛ ma bli a yɔkɔ ɔmɛ a nya. Ma je mɛ kpo, nɛ ma ha a ma ba hi mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɔ ekohu.

english_verse: My Spirit will give you breath, and you will live again. I will bring you home, and you will know that I have kept my promise. I, the Lord, have spoken.” Judah and Israel Together Again
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ ye mumi ɔ ngɔ wo a mi, nɛ ma ha a maa ba wami mi ekohu. Ma ha a ma ba hi mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɔ ekohu. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ. Imi ji nɔ nɛ wo si ɔ, nɛ ma ye nɔ sisiisi. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.” Yuda kɛ Israel plɛ pee nɔ yemi kake

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ekohu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.”
translation_verse: E ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, yaa ngɔ tso, nɛ o ngma ngɛ nɔ ke, ‘Yuda nɔ yemi ɔ.’ Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, yaa ngɔ tso kpa nɛ o ngma ngɛ nɔ ke ‘Israel nɔ yemi ɔ.’

english_verse: Hold these two sticks end to end, so they look like one stick.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ bla tso enyɔ ɔmɛ kɛ pee kake, nɛ o hɛɛ ngɛ o dɛ mi.

english_verse: And when your people ask you what this means,
translation_verse: Ke o ma mi bi ɔmɛ bi mo nɔ́ nɛ ɔ sisi ɔ,

english_verse: tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
translation_verse: de ke, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, ma ngɔ tso ɔ nɛ daa si ha Israel ɔ, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ daa si ha Yuda a kɛ bla. Ma ngɔ tso enyɔ nɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ pee tso kake ngɛ ye dɛ mi.

english_verse: Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone
translation_verse: “Ha nɛ ma a nɛ na tso enyɔ ɔmɛ nɛ o ngma ní ngɛ a nɔ nɛ ngɛ o dɛ mi ɔ.

english_verse: and then say: I, the Lord God, will gather the people of Israel and bring them home from the foreign nations where they now live.
translation_verse: De mɛ ke he tsuaa he nɛ ye ma a ngɛ ngɛ je ma amɛ a mi hehi nɛ a ho ɔ, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, ma bua a nya, nɛ ma kpale mɛ tsuo kɛ je lejɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ba mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba nɔ.

english_verse: I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations.
translation_verse: Ma pee mɛ ma kake ngɛ zugba a nɔ ngɛ Israel yo ɔmɛ a nɔ. Matsɛ kake maa ye a nɔ. A be je ma enyɔ pee hu. A mi be gbae kɛ pee nɔ yemi enyɔ hu.

english_verse: They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ a be amaga jae hu, nɛ a be ní hiemi níhi, kɛ yayami pee kɛ ble a he hu. Se yayamihi gbegbeegbe nɛ a pee kɛ si mi ɔ, ma ngɔ kɛ pa mɛ. Ma tsu a he, nɛ a maa pee ye ma, nɛ imi hu ma pee a Mawu.

english_verse: Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: A maa hi zugba nɛ i ngɔ ha ye tsɔlɔ Yakob ɔ nɔ. Lejɛ ɔ lɛ a nɛmɛ ɔmɛ hi, nɛ lejɛ ɔ a bimɛ, kɛ a nina tsuo maa hi kɛ maa ya neneene. Ye tsɔlɔ David maa ye ganɔ kɛ maa ya neneene.

english_verse: I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time,
translation_verse: I kɛ mɛ maa so he jɔmi somi. E maa pee somi nɛ maa hi si daa. Ma baa a yi saminya. Ma gbaa ma a, nɛ a he maa hiɛ babauu. Ma ma ye we klɔuklɔu ɔ ngɛ zugba a nɔ he nɛ a ngɛ ɔ, nɛ we ɔ maa hi lejɛ ɔ daa.

english_verse: and I will live among my people and be their God.
translation_verse: I kɛ mɛ maa hi si. Ma pee a Mawu; nɛ mɛ hu a maa pee ye ma.

english_verse: Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
translation_verse: Ke i ma ye we ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ i ngɛ a kpɛti daa kɛ yaa neneene ɔ, kɛkɛ je ma amɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ; nɛ imi nitsɛ lɛ i hla Israel kaa ye ma a nɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yawɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ekohu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:
translation_verse: E ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, gbaa kɛ si Gog, ganɔ ngua a nɛ ngɛ Meshek, kɛ Tubal ngɛ Magog zugba a nɔ ɔ. Gbaa kɛ si lɛ.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, am your enemy,
translation_verse: De lɛ ke imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i kɛ lɛ ná.

english_verse: and I will make you powerless! I will put a hook in your jaw and drag away both you and your large army. You command cavalry troops that wear heavy armor and carry shields and swords.
translation_verse: Ma mlɔɔ e hɛ mi, nɛ ma ngɔ gbowe kɛ wo e tsitsa mi. Ma gbla e tabo ɔ, e we okpɔngɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ okpɔngɔ ta buli babauu nɛ a mia kɛ ha ta a kɛ je. Ta bulɔ tsuaa ta bulɔ hɛɛ tsɛ̃i, nɛ e mia kɛ klaate.

english_verse: So keep your troops prepared to fight,
translation_verse: De lɛ ke e pee e tabo ɔ, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ klaalo.

english_verse: because in a few years, I will command you to invade Israel, a country that was ruined by war. It was deserted for a long time, but its people have returned from the foreign nations where they once lived. The Israelites now live in peace in the mountains of their own land.
translation_verse: Jeha komɛ a se ɔ, ma ha e ma ya tua nihi ngɛ Israel yo ɔmɛ a nɔ. A kɛ ta kpata zugba nɛ ɔ hɛ mi be ko, nɛ a si lejɛ ɔ ngɔ fɔ si gu jeha babauu, se jehanɛ lɛɛ a bua nihi a nya ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi.

english_verse: But you and your army will attack them like a fierce thunderstorm and surround them like a cloud.
translation_verse: E kɛ e tabo ɔ, kɛ je mahi babauu ma ba tua lejɛ ɔ kaa ahumi; a maa ha zugba a nɔ kaa bɔku.”

english_verse: to take advantage of Israel, that weak and peaceful country where people live safely inside towns that have no walls or gates or locks.
translation_verse: O ma de ke o ma ya tua ma ko nɛ e mi bi hii si kpoo ngɛ tue mi jɔmi, kɛ he jɔmi mi. Gbogbo be ma amɛ a he ɔ, agbo se lami dade ko hu be.

english_verse: You will rob the people in towns that were once a pile of rubble. These people lived as prisoners in foreign nations, but they have returned to Israel, the most important place in the world, and they own livestock and property.
translation_verse: O ma ya tua ma amɛ, nɛ o maa ha a mi ní. O ma ya tua ma doku ɔmɛ nɛ amlɔ nɛ ɔ lɛɛ a mi hyi kɛ nimli ɔ. O ma ya tua ni ɔmɛ nɛ a bua a nya kɛ je je ma amɛ a mi ɔ. Nimli nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ na, to, kɛ weto ní babauu, nɛ a ngɛ he jɔmi mi ngɛ he nɛ je ɔ tsuo nya ba kpe ngɛ.

english_verse: The people of Sheba and Dedan, along with merchants from villages in southern Spain, will be your allies. They will want some of the silver and gold, as well as the livestock and property that your army takes from Israel.
translation_verse: Sheba bi, Dedan bi, kɛ jua yeli nɛ je Spania ma ba bi ke, ‘O ma nɛ o ba fia wɔ ojo lo? Anɛ o bua o tabo ɔ nya kɛ ba nɛ o ba ha ní pani nya, nɛ o muɔ wa lohwehi, wa sika tsu, wa sika hiɔ, kɛ wa weto ní tsuo kɛ ho lo?’ ”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, know that when you see my people Israel living in peace,
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ tsɔ mi ke ma ya de Gog ke, “Jehanɛ, benɛ ye ma Israel ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi ɔ, o maa hia blɔ

english_verse: You will attack my people like a storm-cloud that covers their land. I will let you invade my country Israel, so that every nation on earth will know that I, the Lord, am holy. Judgment on Gog
translation_verse: O ma ba tua ye ma Israel ɔ kaa ahumi nɛ ngɛ fiae huu kɛ nyɛɛ zugba a nɔ tsuo. Ke be ɔ su ɔ, ma ha o ma ba tua ye zugba a nɔ bi ɔmɛ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ je ma amɛ nɛ a na nɔ nɛ i ji, konɛ kɛ gu nɔ́ nɛ ma pee nɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ, a na kaa nɔ klɔuklɔu ji mi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Gog: Long ago, I ordered my prophets to warn the people of Israel that someday I would send an enemy to attack them. You, Gog, are that enemy, and that day is coming.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke blema lokoo nɛ i ha ye tsɔli, Israel gbali ɔmɛ gba jehahi babauu ke be ma nɛ ma ha nɔ ko ma ba ye ye ma Israel nɔ ɔ, anɛ mo o he i de ngɛ lo?” Mawu maa gbla Gog tue

english_verse: and in my anger I will send a terrible earthquake to shake Israel.
translation_verse: I ngɔ hunga, kɛ hɛdɔ kɛ ngɛ dee ke jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, Israel zugba a ma mimiɛ wawɛɛ.

english_verse: Every living thing on earth will tremble in fear of me—every fish and bird, every wild animal and reptile, and every human. Mountains will crumble, cliffs will fall, and cities will collapse.
translation_verse: Pa mi lohi, hiɔwe lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ, pu mi lohwe nane eywiɛɛywiɛtsɛmɛ kɛ sisali, kɛ nimli adesahi ngɛ zugba a nɔ tsuo maa pee yoyooyo ngɛ ye hɛ mi. Yohi maa hule kɛ pue si, tɛ sa nguanguahi maa nɔ si, nɛ gbogbo tsuaa gbogbo maa hule kɛ pue si.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will make the mountains of Israel turn against you. Your troops will be so terrified that they will attack each other.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ haomi slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi babauu kɛ wo Gog he gbeye. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de. A maa hwu ta gbeyegbeye ko ngɛ yo ɔmɛ a nɔ. Nimli maa hia klaate kɛ wo a sibi.

english_verse: I will do these things to show the world that I, the Lord, am holy.
translation_verse: Ke e ba mi kikɛ nɛ ɔ, je ma amɛ tsuo maa na kaa i kle, nɛ i ngɛ klɔuklɔu. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa le jehanɛ kaa imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog and tell him: You are the ruler of Meshech and Tubal, but I, the Lord, am your enemy!
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, gbaa kɛ si Gog, ganɔ ngua nɛ yeɔ Meshek kɛ Tubal je ma amɛ a nɔ ɔ, nɛ o de lɛ ke, i kɛ lɛ ná.

english_verse: I will turn you around and drag you from the north until you reach the mountains of Israel.
translation_verse: Ma dɔ e yi kɛ gu he kpa; ma ngɔ lɛ kɛ je tsitsaa omleyi je tɔɔ kɛ ba Israel yo ɔmɛ a nɔ.

english_verse: I will knock the bow out of your left hand and the arrows out of your right hand,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ ɔ, kɛ̃ɛ̃ nɛ ngɛ e muɔ nine mi ɔ, ma fia lɛ nɔ́ nɛ e nɔ zugba, nɛ kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bihi nɛ ngɛ e hiɔ nine mi ɔ ma pue si.

english_verse: of your dead bodies left lying in open fields. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: A ma gbo kɛ pue nga kplanaa a nɔ. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: I will set fire to the land of Magog and to those nations along the seacoast that think they are so secure, and they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Magog zugba a, kɛ wo nya ma amɛ nɛ a mi bi a tue mi jɔ mɛ ɔ, ma mɛ mɛ tsuo a he la; nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ ma na maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ.

english_verse: My people Israel will know me, and they will no longer disgrace my holy name. Everyone on earth will know that I am the holy Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ma ha ye ma Israel maa le ye biɛ klɔuklɔu ɔ; nɛ i be hae nɛ a ble ye biɛ nɛ he tsɔ ɔ hu. Kɛkɛ ɔ, je ma amɛ tsuo maa le kaa imi Yawɛ ji Israel Mawu Klɔuklɔu ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: The day is coming when these things will happen, just as I have promised.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Ligbi ɔ nɛ i to ɔ ji kikɛmɛ a ligbi nɛ ɔ nɛ. Hyɛ, e maa ba kokooko.

english_verse: When that day comes, the people in the towns of Israel will collect the weapons of their dead enemies. They will use these shields, bows and arrows, spears, and clubs as firewood, and there will be enough to last for seven years.
translation_verse: Israel ma mi bi ɔmɛ maa je kpo, nɛ a ma ya mɛ ta hwumi ní ɔmɛ a he la. A maa sã a tsɛ̃i wawi, kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bihi, akplɔhi, kɛ tso kpokuhi babauu nɛ he nyɛli ɔmɛ si ɔ. A kɛ maa pee lɛ́ nɛ a ma slɛ jeha kpaago sɔuu.

english_verse: They will burn these weapons instead of gathering sticks or chopping down trees. That's how the Israelites will take revenge on those who robbed and abused them. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Burial of Gog The Lord said:
translation_verse: E be hiae kaa a ya lɛ lɛ́, loo a ya poo tso kɛ pee lɛ́. Ejakaa ta hwumi ní nɛ a bua nya a, a kɛ maa pee lɛ́ nɛ a ma slɛ. Nihi nɛ ha a níhi, nɛ a fia mɛ ojo ɔ, Israel bi ɔmɛ hu maa ha a níhi, nɛ a maa fia mɛ ojo ja nɔuu.” Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ de. A maa pu Gog

english_verse: After Gog has been destroyed, I will bury him and his army in Israel, in Travelers' Valley, east of the Dead Sea. That graveyard will be so large that it will block the way of anyone who tries to walk through the valley, which will then be known as “The Valley of Gog's Army.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ ke, “Ke ní nɛ ɔmɛ na ba mi ɔ, ma ha a maa pu Gog ngɛ Israel zugba a mi, ngɛ ‘Blɔ hiali a kɔ̃’ ɔ mi, ngɛ Ngo wo ɔ beleku je. A maa pu Gog kɛ e ta a tsuo ngɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi, nɛ a maa wo lejɛ ɔ biɛ ke ‘Gog ta buli a kɔ̃.’

english_verse: The Israelites will spend seven months burying dead bodies and cleaning up their land.
translation_verse: Israel bi ɔmɛ maa ngɔ nyɔhiɔ kpaago kɛ pu gbogboe ɔmɛ tsuo, nɛ a kɛ maa tsu zugba a he ekohu.

english_verse: Everyone will help with the burial, and they will be honored for this on the day the brightness of my glory is seen.
translation_verse: Zugba a nɔ bi ɔmɛ tsuo ma bla kɛ pu mɛ. Ligbi ɔ nɛ a maa ye kunimi nɛ ɔ, a maa wo ye hɛ mi nyami. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: After those seven months, the people will appoint a group of men to look for any dead bodies left unburied. This must be done for seven months to make sure that the land is no longer unclean.
translation_verse: Nyɔhiɔ kpaago ɔ se ɔ, a maa hla ni komɛ nɛ maa kpa zugba a nɔ kɛ ya kɛ ba, konɛ gbogboehi nɛ piɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ, a pu mɛ, nɛ a tsu zugba a he.

english_verse: Whenever they find a human bone, they will set up a marker next to it. Then the gravediggers will bury it in “The Valley of Gog's Army”
translation_verse: Ke a ngɛ zugba a nɔ kpae, nɛ nɔ ko ya na wu ko ɔ, e pee okadi ngɛ wu ɔ he kɛ yaa si a maa ngɔ wu ɔ ya pu ngɛ Gog ta buli a kɔ̃ ɔ mi.

english_verse: near the town of “Gog's Army.” After that, the land will be pure again.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ a maa pee kɛ tsu zugba a he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to hold a feast on Israel's mountains and offer sacrifices there. So invite all the birds and wild animals to come from every direction and eat the meat of sacrifices and drink the blood. The birds and animals
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, tsɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ lohwe nane eywiɛɛywiɛtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ kɛ je he tsuaa he nɛ a ngɛ ɔ kɛ ba nɛ a ba ye ní. Ma sã bɔ nguaa ko ngɛ Israel yo ɔmɛ a nɔ ha mɛ, konɛ a ye lo, nɛ a nu muɔ.

english_verse: will feast on the bodies of warriors and foreign rulers that I will sacrifice like sheep, goats, and bulls.
translation_verse: A maa ye katsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a lo, nɛ a maa nu zugba a nɔ ganɔ ɔmɛ a muɔ. Ni nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ kaa Bashan agbosuhi, loo jijɔhi, loo akpakpohi, loo na kuhi nɛ wo zɔ.

english_verse: They will come to my table and stuff themselves with the flesh of horses and warriors of every kind. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Israel Will Be Restored The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ okpɔngɔhi, ta zugba lɛhi, katsɛmɛ, kɛ ta buli slɔɔtoslɔɔto babauu kɛ ngmɛ mɛ okplɔɔ; a maa ye ní nɛ a maa tɔ saminya. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.” Israel maa bɔ ekohu

english_verse: The people of Israel will know from then on that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Nɛ kɛ je jamɛ a ligbi ɔ kɛ yaa a, Israel bi ɔmɛ maa le kaa imi ji Yawɛ, a Mawu ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Foreign nations will realize that the Israelites were forced to leave their own land because they sinned against me. I turned my back on my people and let enemies attack and kill them.
translation_verse: Je ma amɛ hu maa le kaa imi lɛ i ha Israel bi ɔmɛ ya hi ma se kaa nyɔguɛhi, ejakaa a pee yayami kɛ si mi. I kua mɛ, i ha a he nyɛli ba ye a nɔ ngɛ ta mi, nɛ a gbe mɛ.

english_verse: Now I will show mercy to the people of Israel and bring them back from the nations where they are living. They are Jacob's descendants, so I will bless them and show that I am holy.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Jehanɛ lɛɛ, ma na Yakob nina a mɔbɔ; ma na Israel ma a tsuo mɔbɔ, nɛ ma ha a maa bɔ ekohu. Ma pee enɛ ɔ, konɛ a na kaa nɔ klɔuklɔu ji mi.

english_verse: They will live safely in their own land, but will be ashamed when they remember their evil ways and how they disgraced me.
translation_verse: Ke a kpale kɛ ba mɛ nitsɛmɛ a zugba a nɔ ngɛ tue mi jɔmi, kɛ he jɔmi mi, nɛ nɔ ko wui a he gbeye ɔ, a hɛ maa je nɔ kaa a pue a hɛ mi si, nɛ a tsɔ ye hɛ mi atuã.

english_verse: Foreign nations will watch as I take the Israelites from enemy lands and bring them back home, and those nations will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ pee nɛ je ma amɛ tsuo nɛ a le kaa i ngɛ klɔuklɔu ɔ, ma kpale ye ma a kɛ je a he nyɛli a zugba amɛ tsuo a nɔ kɛ ba.

english_verse: Never again will I turn my back on the people of Israel, and my Spirit will live in them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ma ngɔ ye mumi kɛ pue Israel ma a nɔ, nɛ i be mɛ kuae hu. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: He measured the entrance room at the far end of the passageway, and it was ten meters wide.
translation_verse: A guu tsu nɛ ngɛ nyagbe ɔ mi kɛ ya jee kpo ngɛ kue kpa mi. E susu jamɛ a tsu ɔ hulɔ; e blimi ji gugue enuɔ.

english_verse: In my vision the Lord took me closer, and I saw a man who was sparkling like polished bronze. He was standing near one of the gates and was holding a tape measure in one hand and a measuring stick in the other.
translation_verse: Mumi ɔ ngɔ mi kɛ ya su ma a he haa; nɛ i na nyumu ko nɛ e he ngɛ kpɛe kaa akɔblee. E hɛɛ nɔ́ susumi kpa, kɛ nɔ́ susumi tso ngɛ e dɛ mi kɛ daa si ngɛ agbo ko nya.

english_verse: Then he went to the east gate, where he walked up steps that led to a long passageway. On each side of this passageway were three guardrooms, which were three meters square, and they were separated by walls two and a half meters thick. The man measured the distance between the opening of the gate and the first guardroom, and it was three meters, the thickness of the outer wall. At the far end of this passageway, I saw an entrance room that faced the courtyard of the temple itself. There was also a distance of three meters between the last guardroom and the entrance room
translation_verse: Blɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ tsu etɛ ngɛ hiɔ nɔ, nɛ etɛ hu ngɛ muɔ nɔ. Tsu nɛ ɔmɛ a kami kɛ a blimi tsuo sɔ; eko tsuaa eko ngɛ gugue kake kɛ fa; nɛ gbogbo nɛ e timi ji gugue kake kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ tsa tsu kɛ tsu. Tsu wawi nɛ ɔmɛ a se ɔ, blɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ; blɔ ɔ kami ji gugue kake kɛ fa. Blɔ nɛ ɔ ya sɛ asa agbo ko mi.

english_verse: at the end of the passageway. The man measured this room: It was four meters from the doorway to the opposite wall, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one meter.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ susu tsu nɛ ɔ hulɔ; e ná gugue enyɔ. Agbo nɛ a guu mi kɛ yaa Yawɛ we ɔ mi ɔ ngɛ hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ; nɛ agbo ɔ timi ngɛ nyagbe ɔ ji gugue fa.

english_verse: Next, the man measured the width of the passageway, and it was six and a half meters, but the two doors of the gate were only five meters wide.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, nyumu ɔ susu agbo ɔ blimi; e ná gugue etɛ kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ; nɛ ke a bli agbo ɔ, e peeɔ gugue enyɔ kɛ fa.

english_verse: The man measured the distance from the back wall of one of these rooms to the same spot in the room directly across the passageway, and it was twelve and a half meters.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, e susu tsu ɔ kami kɛ gu gbogbo ɔ se; blɔ nɛ ngɛ tsu kake kɛ kake a kpɛti kami ji gugue ekpa kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ kɛ je tsu kake sinya nya kɛ ya na tsu nɛ tsa nɔ ɔ sinya.

english_verse: Finally, he measured the total length of the passageway, from the outer wall to the entrance room, and it was
translation_verse: Kɛ je gbogbo ɔ he ngɛ agbo ɔ nya kɛ ya su nyagbe tsu ɔ se tsuo peeɔ gugue nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ kɛ fa.

english_verse: The three walls in the guardrooms had small windows in them, just like the ones in the entrance room. The walls along the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. The Outer Courtyard
translation_verse: Saflɛ puɔ tsɔwitsɔwi ngɛ kpo nɔ je gbogbo ɔmɛ tsuo a mi; ekomɛ hu ngɛ gbogbo ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ po tsu ɔmɛ a mi ɔ a mi; nɛ tãhi nɛ a tɛni ngɛ sinya tso ɔmɛ a si mami ní ɔmɛ tsuo a he. Kue nɛ ngɛ kpo nɔ je ɔ

english_verse: The man then led me through the passageway and into the outer courtyard of the temple, where I saw
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ kɛ mi ya su kue ɔ nɛ ngɛ kpo nɔ je ɔ mi. Tsu nyingmi etɛ tsa a sibi a nɔ ngɛ gbogbo ɔ he. A ka tɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ zugba a tsuo

english_verse: In fact, everything along the passageway was also the same size, including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, the entrance room at the far end, and the windows. This gate, like the others, was
translation_verse: Tsu wawi ɔmɛ, tsu agbo ɔ, kɛ gbogbo nɛ po a mi ɔ tsuo ngɛ kaa agbo kpa amɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Saflɛhi ngɛ agbo nya tsu ɔmɛ a he. E susu enɛ ɔmɛ tsuo a kami; e pee gugue ekpa kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ, nɛ a blimi pee gugue kake kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ.

english_verse: This was known as the lower sidewalk, and it was
translation_verse: kɛ bɔle kue ɔ mi kɛ kpe. Kpɛti kue ɔ ya hiɔwe pe kpo nɔ je nɔ́ ɔ.

english_verse: I saw the gates that led to the inner courtyard of the temple and noticed that they were higher than those leading to the outer courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gates, and it was
translation_verse: A guu agbo nɛ ya hiɔwe ko mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ yaa kpɛti kue ɔ mi. Nyumu ɔ susu blɔ nɛ ngɛ agbo enyɔ nɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti, kɛ je yiti je nɔ́ ɔ he kɛ ya su sisi je nɔ́ ɔ he; nɛ e ná gugue nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enuɔ. Agbo nɛ ngɛ omleyi je ɔ

english_verse: This gate also had three guardrooms on each side of a passageway. The measurements of these rooms, the walls between them, and the entrance room at the far end of the passageway were exactly the same as those of the east gate. The north gate was also
translation_verse: Tsu wayowayo etɛ nɛ ngɛ muɔ nɔ kɛ etɛ nɛ ngɛ hiɔ nɔ ɔ, a klemi sɔ kaa bɔ nɛ kekle agbo ɔ ngɛ ɔ. E kami ji gugue nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ kɛ fa, nɛ e blimi ji gugue ekpa kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ.

english_verse: and the windows, the entrance room, and the carvings of palm trees were just like those in the east gate. The entrance room also faced the courtyard of the temple and had seven steps leading up to it.
translation_verse: Tsu agbo ɔ saflɛ ɔmɛ, e kue ɔ, kɛ tã amɛ ɔ, ke a susu mɛ ɔ, a ngɛ kaa agbo ɔ nɛ hɛ mi kpee beleku je ɔ ní ɔmɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. A kuɔɔ kpoku kpaago kɛ yaa he; nɛ e kue ɔ ngɛ mi mi je.

english_verse: Directly across the outer courtyard was a gate that led to the inner courtyard, just as there was for the east gate. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was
translation_verse: Kue ɔ nɛ ngɛ mi mi je ɔ we agbo ɔ, kɛ omleyi je nɔ́ ɔ ngɛ hanɔ kaa bɔ nɛ e kɛ leneyi je nɔ ɔ ngɛ ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nyumu ɔ susu kue enyɔ nɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti kami, nɛ e ná gugue nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enuɔ. Agbo nɛ ngɛ leneyi je ɔ

english_verse: The man then took me to the south gate. He measured the walls and the entrance room of this gate, and the measurements were exactly the same as those of the other two gates.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, nyumu ɔ kɛ mi ya leneyi je; agbo ko nya ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. E susu e sinya tso ɔmɛ, kɛ e kue ɔ. E na kaa a kɛ ekpa amɛ sɔ.

english_verse: Seven steps led up to the gate; the entrance room was at the far end of the passageway and faced the courtyard of the temple. Carvings of palm trees decorated the walls along the passageway.
translation_verse: A kuɔɔ kpoku kpaago kɛ ya sɛɛ tsu agbo ko mi ngɛ nyagbe ɔ; enɛ ɔ hu nya blɔ kpee kue ɔ mi je. A tɛni tãhi ngɛ agbo ɔ mi sinya tso ɔmɛ a he; kake ngɛ hiɛ, nɛ kake hu ngɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: And directly across the outer courtyard was a gate on the south side of the inner courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was also
translation_verse: Agbo ko ngɛ kue ɔ mi ngɛ leneyi je. E susu kɛ je agbo kake he kɛ ya su agbo kpa nɛ ngɛ leneyi je ɔ he, nɛ e ná gugue nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enuɔ. Kue nɛ ngɛ mi mi je ɔ: agbo nɛ ngɛ leneyi je ɔ

english_verse: We then went into the inner courtyard, through the gate on the south side of the temple. The man measured the gate, and it was the same size as the gates in the outer wall.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ kɛ mi ya gu agbo nɛ ngɛ leneyi je ɔ mi kɛ ya su kue nɛ ngɛ mi mi je ɔ mi. E susu agbo ɔ; enɛ ɔ hu kɛ agbo ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ kpo nɔ je ɔ sɔ.

english_verse: The entrance room of this gate faced the outer courtyard, and carvings of palm trees decorated the walls of the passageway. Eight steps led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Tsu agbo ko nɛ hɛ mi kpee kue kaketsɛ ɔ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ. A tɛni tãhi ngɛ gbogbo ɔmɛ a he ngɛ hiɔ nɔ kɛ muɔ nɔ tsuo. A kuɔɔ kpoku kpaanyɔ kɛ yaa agbo nɛ ɔ he. Mi mi je kue ɔ: agbo nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ

english_verse: Next, we went through the east gate to the inner courtyard. The man measured this gate, and it was the same size as the others.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ kɛ mi ya gu agbo nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ mi kɛ ya sɛ kue nɛ ngɛ we ɔ mi ɔ mi. E susu agbo ɔ, nɛ e ngɛ kaa ekpa amɛ nɔuu.

english_verse: The guardrooms, the walls separating them, and its entrance room had the same measurements as the other gates. The guardrooms and the entrance room had windows, and the gate was
translation_verse: Tsu wawi ɔmɛ, tsu agbo ɔ, kɛ gbogbo ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ kaa kekle ní ɔmɛ nɔuu. Saflɛhi ngɛ kue ɔmɛ a he kɛ kpe, nɛ saflɛhi ngɛ tsu agbo ɔ hu he. Enɛ ɔmɛ tsuo a kami ji gugue nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ kɛ fa, nɛ a blimi ji gugue ekpa kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ.

english_verse: The entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and the walls in the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
translation_verse: A tɛni tãhi ngɛ gbogbo ɔmɛ a he ngɛ hiɔ nɔ kɛ muɔ nɔ tsuo. A kuɔɔ kpoku kpaanyɔ kɛ yaa agbo nɛ ɔ he. Kue nɛ ngɛ mi mi je ɔ: agbo nɛ ngɛ omleyi je ɔ

english_verse: Then the man took me to the north gate. He measured it, and it was the same size as the others,
translation_verse: Jehanɛ nyumu ɔ kɛ mi ya agbo nɛ ngɛ omleyi je ɔ he. E susu enɛ ɔ hulɔ, nɛ e na kaa e kɛ ekpa amɛ sɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: and like the other inner gates, its entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and its walls were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate. The Rooms for Sacrificing Animals
translation_verse: Tsu agbo nɛ ɔ hɛ mi tsɔɔ agbo ɔ nya blɔ. A tɛni tãhi ngɛ gbogbo ɔmɛ a he ngɛ hiɔ nɔ kɛ muɔ nɔ tsuo. A kuɔɔ kpoku kpaanyɔ kɛ yaa agbo nɛ ɔ he. Agbo nɛ ngɛ omleyi je ɔ kasa nya tsuhi

english_verse: Inside the entrance room of the north gate, I saw four tables, two on each side of the room, where the animals to be sacrificed were killed. Just outside this room was a small building used for washing the animals before they were offered as sacrifices to please the Lord or sacrifices for sin or sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Okplɔɔ eywiɛ ngɛ tsu agbo nɛ ɔ mi; enyɔ ngɛ kasa hiɛ, nɛ enyɔ hu ngɛ kasa hiɛ. Okplɔɔ nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ a gbee lohwehi nɛ a kɛ maa sã bɔ ɔmɛ ngɛ: sami bɔhi jio, yayami pami bɔhi jio, fɔ yemi bɔhi jio.

english_verse: Four more tables were in the outer courtyard, two on each side of the steps leading into the entrance room.
translation_verse: Tsu ɔ se hu okplɔɔ eywiɛ nɛ ngɛ kaa enɛ ɔmɛ maa si. Enyɔ ngɛ hiɔ nɔ, nɛ enyɔ hu ngɛ muɔ nɔ ngɛ omleyi je agbo ɔ nya.

english_verse: So there was a total of eight tables, four inside and four outside, where the animals were killed,
translation_verse: Okplɔɔ kpaanyɔ nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ a gbeɔ lohwe ɔmɛ ngɛ; eywiɛ ngɛ tsu ɔ mi, nɛ eywiɛ hu ngɛ kpo ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: and where the meat was placed until it was sacrificed on the altar. Next to the tables in the entrance room were four stone tables
translation_verse: A ka gbowehi kɛ wo okplɔɔ ɔmɛ a tue kɛ kpe, eko tsuaa eko kami ji dɛ mi blimi kake. Lo ɔ tsuo nɛ a kɛ maa sã bɔ ɔmɛ ɔ, okplɔɔ nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ a kɛ pueɔ.

english_verse: The man then took me to the inner courtyard, where I saw two buildings, one beside the inner gate on the north and the other beside the inner gate on the south.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ nyumu ɔ kɛ mi ba mi mi je kue ɔ mi. Tsu enyɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ a bliɔ a sinya amɛ kɛ baa we ɔ mi je; kake ngɛ omleyi je agbo ɔ nya, nɛ e hɛ mi kpee leneyi je; nɛ kake hu ngɛ leneyi je agbo ɔ nya, nɛ e hɛ mi kpee omleyi je.

english_verse: He said, “The building beside the north gate belongs to the priests who serve in the temple,
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ de mi ke tsu nɛ hɛ mi kpee leneyi je ɔ, osɔfo ɔmɛ nɛ sɔmɔɔ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ a nɔ́ ji lɔ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: and the building beside the south gate belongs to those who serve at the altar. All of them are descendants of Zadok and are the only Levites allowed to serve as the Lord's priests.” The Inner Courtyard and the Temple
translation_verse: Kake ɔ hu nɛ hɛ mi kpee omleyi je ɔ, osɔfo ɔmɛ nɛ sɔmɔɔ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he ɔ, mɛ hu a nɔ́ ji lɔ ɔ nɛ. Zadok nina ji osɔfo nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo; nɛ mɛ pɛ ji Levi bi nɛ ngɛ he blɔ kaa a ba sɔmɔɔ ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. Yawɛ we ɔ kɛ kue nɛ ngɛ mi mi je ɔ

english_verse: We walked to the porch of the temple, and the man measured the doorway of the porch: It was seven meters long, two and a half meters wide, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one and a half meters.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ e kɛ mi ba Yawɛ we ɔ kue ɔ nya. E susu kue ɔ nya titima a; e blimi ji gugue kake kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ, nɛ e kami ji gugue etɛ kɛ fa. Gbogbo nɛ ngɛ hiɔ nɔ, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ muɔ nɔ ɔ, a timi sɔ, gugue fa kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ.

english_verse: The porch itself was ten meters by six meters, with steps leading up to it. There was a column on each side of these steps.
translation_verse: Kue ɔ kami ji gugue enuɔ, nɛ e blimi ji gugue etɛ. A kuɔɔ kpoku nyɔngma kɛ yaa sinya a nya. Titima hi maa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ; kake ngɛ hiɔ nɔ, nɛ kake hu ngɛ muɔ nɔ.

english_verse: Then the man walked to the far end of the temple's main room and said, “Beyond this doorway is the most holy place.” He first measured the doorway: It was one meter wide,
translation_verse: Jehanɛ e susu tsu ɔ mi nitsɛ. E ná gugue enuɔ ngɛ tsu ɔ kasa kake, nɛ e ná ja nɔuu ngɛ kasa kpa amɛ tsuo. Tsu nɛ ɔ ngɛ kpɛtikpɛti tsu ɔ se. Kɛkɛ nɛ e de mi ke, “Hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ ji he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa.” Yawɛ we ɔ gbogbo ɔmɛ a he tsuhi

english_verse: The distance across the front of the temple, including the open space on either side, was also
translation_verse: e blimi ngɛ beleku je kɛ kpo ɔ nɔ tsuo ji gugue nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enuɔ.

english_verse: were paneled with wood all the way from the floor to the windows, while the doorways, the small windows, and the three side rooms were trimmed in wood.
translation_verse: a ka tso kɛ wo lɛ tsuo he kɛ je zugba kɛ ya ta saflɛ ɔmɛ a nya. Saflɛ ɔmɛ hu a ha a he.

english_verse: The doorframe to the temple's main room was in the shape of a rectangle. The Wooden Altar In front of the doorway to the most holy place was something that looked like
translation_verse: A pee Yawɛ we ɔ he klɔuklɔu ɔ sinya tso ɔmɛ kɔ nya eywiɛɛywiɛ. Bɔ sami la tɛ nɛ a kɛ tso pee ɔ Ngɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa hɛ mi ɔ, nɔ́ ko maa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ ngɛ kaa

english_verse: a wooden altar. It was one and a half meters high and one meter square, and its corners, its base, and its sides were made of wood. The man said, “This is a reminder that the Lord is constantly watching over his temple.” The Doors in the Temple
translation_verse: bɔ sami la tɛ nɛ a kɛ tso pee. E hiɔwe yami ji gugue fa kɛ nine mi blimi enyɔ, nɛ e kami ji gugue fa, kɛ e blimi hu gugue fa. E kɔ nya amɛ, e nane ɔmɛ, kɛ e kasa nya amɛ tsuo tso a kɛ pee. Nyumu ɔ de mi ke, “Okplɔɔ nɛ maa Yawɛ hɛ mi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.” Sinya amɛ

english_verse: Both the doorway to the main room of the temple and the doorway to the most holy place had two doors,
translation_verse: A guu sinya kake mi kɛ sɛɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ, nɛ ngɛ tsu ɔ nyagbe ɔ, a guu sinya kpa mi kɛ sɛɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a.

english_verse: and each door had two sections that could fold open.
translation_verse: A pee sinya nɛ ɔmɛ blablɛ enyɔɔnyɔ; sinya amɛ eko tsuaa eko bliɔ ngɛ kpɛti.

english_verse: The doors to the main room were decorated with carvings of winged creatures and palm trees just like those on the walls, and there was a wooden covering over the porch just outside these doors.
translation_verse: A tɛni kerubhi, kɛ tãhi ngɛ sinya amɛ a he ngɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ a pee ngɛ gbogbo ɔmɛ a he ɔ. A kɛ tso pee gba ngɛ kue ɔ hɛ mi ngɛ kpo nɔ je.

english_verse: The walls on each side of this porch had small windows and were also decorated with carvings of palm trees.
translation_verse: Saflɛhi nɛ a pee puɔhi ngɛ a mi, nɛ a tɛni tãhi ngɛ a he ngɛ kue ɔ gbogbo ɔmɛ a he hiɛ kɛ hiɛ.

english_verse: After the man and I left the temple and walked back to the outer courtyard, he showed me a set of rooms on the north side of the west building. This set of rooms was
translation_verse: Kue nɛ ngɛ omleyi je nɛ ɔ kami ji gugue nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enuɔ, nɛ e blimi ji gugue nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ kɛ fa.

english_verse: and at the east end of this wall was the door leading from the courtyard to these rooms. There was also a set of rooms on the south side of the west building.
translation_verse: Tsu nɛ ɔmɛ a sisi kɛ yaa beleku je, he nɛ a fia gbogbo ɔ kɛ je ɔ, blɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ yaa kpo nɔ je kue ɔ mi. Tsu kpa ko nɛ je nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ beleku je ɔ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ leneyi je, nɛ e kɛ enɛ ɔ he kɛ we kulaa.

english_verse: with doors that opened toward the north, and in front of them was a walkway five meters wide and
translation_verse: Blɔ nɛ ngɛ omleyi je ɔ blimi ji gugue enyɔ kɛ fa, nɛ e kami ji gugue nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enuɔ kɛ ya na sinya nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The rooms on the top level were narrower than those on the middle level, and the rooms on the middle level were narrower than those on the bottom level.
translation_verse: Yiti tsu ɔmɛ a mi bli we kulaa; ejakaa ablanaa amɛ hé a blɔ he ɔmɛ pe sisi ní ɔmɛ, kɛ kpɛti ní ɔmɛ.

english_verse: These rooms were exactly like those on the north side, and they also had a walkway in front of them.
translation_verse: Blɔ ngɛ tsu nɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi kaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ omleyi je ɔ. E kami kɛ e blimi kɛ hehi nɛ a guu kɛ sɛɛ mi ɔ ngɛ kaa kaketsɛ ɔ nɔuu.

english_verse: The door to these rooms was at the east end of the wall that stood in front of them.
translation_verse: Sinya ko ngɛ tsu ɔmɛ a sisi kɛ yaa beleku je, he nɛ a fia gbogbo ɔ kɛ je ɔ.

english_verse: The man then said to me: These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ nyumu ɔ de mi ke, “Tsu enyɔ nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ klɔuklɔu. Osɔfohi nɛ baa Yawɛ we ɔ, tsu nɛ ɔmɛ a mi a yeɔ bɔ klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a ngɛ. Tsu nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ klɔuklɔu, nɛ a mi nɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ toɔ bɔ klɔuklɔu pe kulaa nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ: niye ní bɔ, yayami pami bɔ, kɛ fɔ yemi bɔ.

english_verse: When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people. The Size of the Temple Area
translation_verse: Ke osɔfo ɔmɛ sɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ, a be kpo jee kɛ ya kpo nɔ je kue ɔ mi; mohu a ma je a tade ɔmɛ nɛ a kɛ sɔmɔ ɔ kɛ pue si, ejakaa tade ɔmɛ ngɛ klɔuklɔu. A maa wo tade kpahi loko a maa je kpo kɛ ya he nɛ ma a ngɛ ɔ.” A susu Yawɛ we ɔ

english_verse: After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area.
translation_verse: Benɛ nyumu ɔ susu Yawɛ we ɔ mi ta a, e kɛ mi je kpo kɛ gu agbo nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ mi kɛ ba kpo ɔ nɔ; nɛ e ba susu lejɛ ɔ hulɔ.

english_verse: He used his measuring stick to measure the east side of this wall; it was
translation_verse: E ngɔ e tso ɔ kɛ susu kpo ɔ nɔ tsuo kɛ kpe. E ná gugue lafa kɛ nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enuɔ ngɛ beleku je ɔ.

english_verse: and so the temple area was a perfect square. The wall around this area separated what was sacred from what was ordinary.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ e susu omleyi je, leneyi je, kɛ bonyoku je tsuo; lɛ tsuo sɔ fiee, gugue lafa kɛ nyingmi enyɔ kɛ enuɔ. Gbogbo po he klɔuklɔu ɔ, kɛ he nɛ ji nihi tsuo a nɔ́ ɔ a kpɛti.

english_verse: The man took me back to the east gate of the temple,
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ kɛ mi ba agbo ɔ nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ nya.

english_verse: meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side. The Dedication of the Altar
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ i na Israel Mawu ɔ hɛ mi nyami ɔ nɛ ngɛ kpɛe plamplam kɛ je beleku je kɛ ma. Mawu gbi ngɛ pɛe hoo kɛ ma kaa wo nɛ gli; nɛ lejɛ ɔ tsuo pee hleii kɛ e hɛ mi nyami ɔ.

english_verse: This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River. I immediately bowed with my face to the ground,
translation_verse: Nina nɛ ɔ ngɛ kaa nina nɛ i na benɛ Mawu ba kpata Yerusalem hɛ mi, kɛ nina nɛ i na ngɛ Kebar pa a nya a. Kɛkɛ nɛ i ngɔ ye hɛ mi kɛ bu zugba.

english_verse: and the Lord's glory came through the east gate and into the temple.
translation_verse: Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ gu agbo nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ mi kɛ ya sɛ Yawɛ we ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
translation_verse: Yawɛ mumi ɔ wo ye nɔ, nɛ e kɛ mi ya ma mi mi je kue ɔ mi. E hɛ mi nyami ɔ hyi we ɔ tɔ.

english_verse: But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ lɛɛ a ma kpa mawu kpahi jami, nɛ a ma je a matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a gbogboe ɔmɛ kɛ je ye kasa nya kɛ ya se lokoo. Ke a pee ja a, ma hi a kpɛti kɛ maa ya neneene.”

english_verse: The people of Israel must suffer shame for sinning against me, so tell them about my holy temple. Let them think about it,
translation_verse: Yawɛ ya nɔ, nɛ e de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, bɔ nɛ imi Yawɛ ye we ɔ ngɛ ha a, kale fitsofitso kɛ tsɔɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ. Ha nɛ zo nɛ gbe mɛ ngɛ yayamihi nɛ a pee ɔ a he.

english_verse: The temple area on my holy mountain must be kept sacred! This is the most important law about the temple. The Altar
translation_verse: Mlaa nɛ kɔɔ imi Yawɛ ye we ɔ he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: yo ɔ yi mi tsuo kɛ bɔle si kɛ kpe ɔ maa pee he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa.” Bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ

english_verse: Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Ngɔɔ akpakpo kɛ ba nɛ a kɛ sã yayami pami bɔ daa ligbi kɛ yaa si ligbi kpaago. Ngɔɔ na ku kɛ agbosu hu nɛ kpa ko kpa ko be mɛ tsuo a he kɛ ba ja nɔuu.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do:
translation_verse: Mlaahi nɛ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ngɛ dee nɛ kɔɔ he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Ke a ma bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɛ a maa sã bɔ ngɛ nɔ, nɛ a maa ngɔ muɔ kɛ fĩa nɔ ɔ gbe nya a,

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Levi bi osɔfo ɔmɛ nɛ ji Zadok nina, nɛ mɛ pɛ lɛ a ba sɔmɔɔ mi ngɛ ye he klɔuklɔu ɔ, ha mɛ na ku nɛ a kɛ sã yayami pami bɔ.

english_verse: Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: Bɔ nɛ o maa pee kɛ tsukɔ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he, nɛ e pee klɔuklɔu ha Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: ngɔɔ muɔ ɔ eko nɛ o kɛ kpa koli eywiɛ ɔmɛ, la tɛ ɔ kpɛti mi dlami ɔ kɔ nya eywiɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ kla nɛ bɔle la tɛ ɔ he tsuo kɛ kpe ɔ.

english_verse: Then take the body of the bull outside the temple area and burn it at the special place.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ ngɔɔ na ku ɔ nɛ a kɛ maa sã yayami pami bɔ ɔ. Ha nɛ a sã lɛ ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ he, he nɛ a to nɛ a pee ngɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, ngɔɔ akpakpo nɛ kpa ko be e he kɛ ba sã yayami pami bɔ kɛ tsukɔ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he.

english_verse: Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them,
translation_verse: Ke o tsukɔ la tɛ ɔ he gbe nya a, ngɔɔ na ku kɛ agbosu nɛ kpa ko be a he kɛ ba.

english_verse: and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Ngɔɔ mɛ kɛ ba ha Yawɛ. Osɔfo ɔmɛ maa ngɔ ngo kɛ fĩa a nɔ, nɛ a kɛ mɛ maa sã sami bɔ kɛ ha imi Yawɛ.

english_verse: The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use.
translation_verse: A ngɔ ligbi kpaago kɛ tsukɔ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he, nɛ á gbaa nɔ kɛ ha bɔ sami.

english_verse: From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ke a gbe ligbi kpaago ní tsumi ɔ nya a, kɛ je ligbi kpaanyɔ ɔ hluu kɛ yaa a, osɔfo ɔmɛ nɛ a sã sami bɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔ ɔmɛ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ. Kɛkɛ ɔ, ye bua maa jɔ ma a tsuo he. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ nyumu ɔ kpale mi kɛ ba he klɔuklɔu ɔ we agbo ɔ nɛ hɛ mi kpee beleku je ɔ nya. A nga agbo ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said: I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it.
translation_verse: Yawɛ de mi ke, “A gbo nɛ ɔ, á nga daa; a ko bli gblegbleegble. Nɔ ko nɔ ko kó gu lejɛ ɔ kɛ sɛ we ɔ mi, ejakaa imi Yawɛ, Israel Mawu ɔ nitsɛ i gu lejɛ ɔ kɛ sɛ mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, á nga daa.

english_verse: The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate. People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
translation_verse: Ganɔ ɔ pɛ lɛ ngɛ he blɔ nɛ e yaa lejɛ ɔ. E ma nyɛ maa hi lejɛ ɔ kɛ ye ní ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. É gu kue ngua a nɛ ngɛ se je ɔ mi kɛ ya, nɛ é gu lejɛ ɔ nɔuu kɛ je kpo.” Blɔ nya tomi kɛ ha nihi nɛ maa ya Yawɛ we ɔ

english_verse: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, nyumu ɔ kɛ mi ya gu omleyi je agbo ɔ mi kɛ ba we ɔ hɛ mi, nɛ i na Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ nɛ hyi we ɔ tɔ. I ngɔ ye hɛ mi kɛ bu si.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, bli o hɛngmɛ nɛ o hyɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ pɛpɛɛpɛ; bu nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ tue saminya. Blɔ nya tomihi, kɛ mlaahi nɛ kɔɔ ye we ɔ he ɔ, kadi mɛ, konɛ o hɛ ko je a nɔ. Ná nɛ o le kaa pi nɔ tsuaa nɔ kɛkɛ nɛ yaa ye we ɔ.

english_verse: Tell those rebellious people of Israel: I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways!
translation_verse: “De Israel ma atuã tsɔli nɛ ɔmɛ ke imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ i be mɛ blɔ ngmɛe nɛ a pee ní hiemi níhi nɛ a ngɛ pee ɔ hu.

english_verse: My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: A ha nibwɔhi mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ, nihi nɛ a he tsɔ we, nɛ a bui mi tue ba sɛ ye we ɔ mi, benɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ ngɔ zɔ kɛ muɔ kɛ ngɛ bɔhi sãe ha mi ɔ. Ye ma a yi ye somi ɔ nɔ, nɛ a ngɔ a ní hiemi ní nɛ ɔmɛ hu kɛ tɔ ye nɔ.

english_verse: Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
translation_verse: Mɛ nitsɛmɛ a tsu we ye ní klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ a he ní ngɛ ye we ɔ, se mohu a ngɔ nibwɔhi kɛ to ní tsumi ɔmɛ a nya.

english_verse: And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel. The Levites Are Punished The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ dee ke nubwɔ mɔmlɔtɔtsɛ nɛ he tsɔ we, nɛ bui mi tue kó sɛ ye we ɔ mi kɔkɔɔkɔ; nibwɔhi nɛ ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti tete po a ko ya lejɛ ɔ.” Levi bi nɛ be he blɔ kaa a tsuɔ osɔfo ní tsumi

english_verse: Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished!
translation_verse: Yawɛ de mi ke, “Levi bi nɛ a kɛ Israel ma nɛ piɛ ɔ kua mi, nɛ a ya ja amagahi ɔ, ma gbla a tue.

english_verse: They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers.
translation_verse: A ma sɔmɔ ngɛ ye we ɔ; a maa bu agbo ɔmɛ a nya, nɛ a ma tsu ní ngɛ we ɔ. Lohwehi nɛ a kɛ ba sãã sami bɔ, kɛ bɔ kpahi ɔ, mɛ lɛ a maa gbe lohwe ɔ, nɛ mɛ nɔuu lɛ a ma sɔmɔ nihi nɛ ba bɔ sami ɔ.

english_verse: But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning,
translation_verse: Akɛnɛ a nyɛɛ Israel ma a hɛ mi kɛ ya ja amagahi, nɛ a ha a pee yayami kɛ si mi he je ɔ, imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ, i ngɛ ye he kita kae ke ma gbla a tue kokooko.

english_verse: and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins.
translation_verse: A ko sã kɛ su ye he, nɛ a ko ba tsu osɔfo ní tsumi ha mi. A ko ba ta ye ní klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ a he; nɛ a ko ya he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a hulɔ. Enɛ ɔ ji a tue gblami ngɛ ní hiemi níhi nɛ a pee ɔ a he.

english_verse: They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple. Rules for Priests The Lord said:
translation_verse: Se kɛ̃ ɔ, ma ha a maa hyɛ sɔlemi we ɔ nɔ. Sɔmɔmi ní tsumi, kɛ ní tsumi kpahi nɛ hia kaa a tsu ɔ, mɛ lɛ a ma tsu.” Osɔfo ɔmɛ

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Benɛ Israel ma a nɛ piɛ ɔ tsuo kua mi ɔ, Levi weku ɔ mi osɔfohi nɛ ji Zadok nina a, mɛɛ lɛɛ a sɔmɔ mi saminya ngɛ ye we ɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mɛ pɛ ji nihi nɛ maa ba ye hɛ mi nɛ a ba sɔmɔ mi. Mɛ ji nihi nɛ maa ngɔ zɔ, kɛ nu ɔ kɛ ba ha imi Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ.

english_verse: They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
translation_verse: Mɛ pɛ ji nihi nɛ maa ba ye he klɔuklɔu ɔ. A maa ba ye we okplɔɔ ɔ he, konɛ a ba sɔmɔ mi. Mɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ maa hyɛ nɛ a ja mi saminya.

english_verse: When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple.
translation_verse: Ke a maa ba Yawɛ we ɔ kpo nɔ je kue ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, a wo kploba tade. A ko wo kuutu nɔ́ ko kɛ ya sɔmɔ ngɛ kue ngua a nɛ ngɛ kpɛti ɔ mi; ye we ɔ nitsɛ mi hu, á pee ja kɛ.

english_verse: And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
translation_verse: Ke a maa je kpo kɛ ya agbo nya je kue ɔ mi, kɛ ya he nɛ ma a ngɛ ɔ, a je tade ɔmɛ nɛ a wo kɛ sɔmɔ ɔ kɛ pue tsu klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ a mi. A wo tade kpahi, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ heha ní klɔuklɔu nɛ ɔmɛ ko ye ma a awi.

english_verse: Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long.
translation_verse: “Osɔfo ɔmɛ ko sã a yi nɔ kpalokpalo, nɛ a ko ngmɛɛ a yi bwɔmi he nɛ e ka gagaa hulɔ. A dla a yi ɔ he bɔ nɛ sa kɛkɛ.

english_verse: They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Ke osɔfo ko maa ya he klɔuklɔu ɔ, e ko nu dã.

english_verse: A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
translation_verse: Osɔfo kó ngɔ yalɔyo, loo yo nɛ e kɛ e huno be hu; e ngɔ yomiyo kɛ je e ma Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti, aloo osɔfo ko nɛ be je mi ɔ e yo yalɔyo.

english_verse: Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean.
translation_verse: “Osɔfo ɔmɛ nɛ́ a tsɔɔ ye ma a slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ nɔ́ klɔuklɔu, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ be klɔuklɔu a kpɛti, kɛ slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ he tsɔ we, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ he tsɔ a kpɛti.

english_verse: They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ke sane ko ba a, osɔfo ɔmɛ nɔuu nɛ a hyɛ sane ɔ mi, nɛ á kojo ngɛ ye mlaa amɛ a nya. Mlaahi, kɛ blɔ nya tomihi nɛ kɔɔ nyami be ɔmɛ tsuo a he ɔ, a hyɛ nɛ a ye a nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, nɛ a pee Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔmɛ klɔuklɔu.

english_verse: Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister.
translation_verse: “Osɔfo ko kó ya gbogboe kasa nya nɛ e kɛ ba ble e he. Ke e he nɔ kɔklɔɔ kaa e tsɛ, loo e nyɛ, loo e binyumu, loo e biyo, loo e nyɛminyumu, loo e nyɛmiyo nɛ yɛ gba we kikɛ nɛ ɔ nɛ gbo lɛɛ e ma nyɛ ma ble e he faa.

english_verse: If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later,
translation_verse: Ke e tsukɔ e he se ɔ, a kane ligbi kpaago ha lɛ, kɛkɛ ɔ, e he ma tsɔ.

english_verse: he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, e ya Yawɛ we ɔ mi mi je kue ɔ mi, nɛ e ya sã yayami pami bɔ, konɛ e nyɛ nɛ e ya sɔmɔ mi ngɛ Yawɛ we ɔ ekohu. Imi, Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Osɔfo ɔmɛ a niye ní nɛ a maa ye ji niye ní bɔ ɔmɛ, yayami pami bɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ fɔ yemi bɔ ɔmɛ; jehanɛ hu, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ maa gbaa nɔ kɛ ke mi ɔ peeɔ osɔfo ɔmɛ a nɔ́.

english_verse: The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
translation_verse: Tso yiblii tsuaa tso yiblii kekleekle nɔ́, kɛ ní slɔɔtohi nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ ma ba sã bɔ ha mi ɔ a mi nɔ́ nɛ hi pe kulaa a peeɔ osɔfo ɔmɛ a nɔ́. Jehanɛ hu, ke a sã abolo ɔ, a ngɔ kekleekle nɔ́ nɛ a bɔ ɔ kɛ ba ha osɔfo ɔmɛ, konɛ ye gbaami nɛ hi we ɔmɛ a mi.

english_verse: Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_verse: Osɔfo kó ye lohwe ko nɛ lɛ nitsɛ e gbo, loo lohwe kpa ko tsɔtslɔɔ e mi kɔkɔɔkɔ, lohwe pɛlitsɛ jio, nane eywiɛtsɛ jio.”

english_verse: So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures.
translation_verse: “Nyɛɛ ngɔ sɛnihi nɛ hi, kɛ susumi níhi nɛ da kɛ tsu ní.

english_verse: The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
translation_verse: “A je Gbasisihimi nyami be ɔ yemi sisi kɛ je nyɔhiɔ kpaago ɔ we ligbi nyɔngma kɛ enuɔne ɔ. Ke be ɔ su ɔ, ganɔ ɔ nɛ ngɛ ma a nɔ yee ɔ maa sã jamɛ a bɔ ɔmɛ nɔuu daa ligbi otsi ɔ mi tsuo. A maa sã lohwe ɔ tsuo kɛ ha yayami pami; nɛ a kɛ blɛfo, kɛ oliv nu maa piɛ he.”

english_verse: kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem. Land for Israel's Ruler The Lord said:
translation_verse: Zugba nɛ ɔ mi fa nɛ e kami ji si tomi kpaanyɔ kɛ fa, nɛ e blimi ji si tomi etɛ kɛ fa maa pee he nɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa maa hi.

english_verse: The regions west and east of my sacred land and the city of Jerusalem will belong to the ruler of Israel. He will be given the region between the western edge of my land and the Mediterranean Sea, and between the eastern edge of my land and the Jordan River. This will mean that the length of his property will be the same as the sections of land given to the tribes. This property will belong to every ruler of Israel, so they will always be fair to my people and will let them live peacefully in the land given to their tribes. Israel's Rulers Must Be Honest
translation_verse: Zugba nɛ ganɔ nɛ ngɛ ma a nɔ yee ɔ ma na ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Ke nyɛ pee ja a, ganɔ ɔmɛ be ye ma a blɔ nya ní kpɔe ngɛ a dɛ, se mohu a maa dla zugba a mi kɛ ha wɛtso ɔmɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Mlaahi nɛ a wo ganɔ nɛ ngɛ ma a nɔ yee ɔ

english_verse: The Lord God said: You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ke, “Nyɛ Israel ganɔhi, e hiɛ oo e hiɛ! Nyɛ kpa amimi kɛ awi yemi! Nyɛɛ ye dami sane, nɛ nyɛɛ pee nɔ́ nɛ da. Nyɛ ko fie ye ma a kɛ je a zugba nɔ hu. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.

english_verse: The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
translation_verse: “Susumi nɔ́ nɛ a tsɛɛ ke efa, kɛ susumi nɔ́ nɛ a tsɛɛ ke bat ɔ, nyɛ ha nɛ a sɔ fiee; bat ɔ nyɔngma lɛ peeɔ susumi nɔ́ nɛ a tsɛɛ ke homer ɔ kake; jã kɛ̃ efa a hu nyɔngma lɛ peeɔ homer kake. Homer nɔ nyɛɛ da kɛ susu níhi.

english_verse: The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
translation_verse: Nyɔhiɔ ɔ we ligbi kpaago ɔ, pee jã kɛ̃ kɛ ha nɔ nɛ li e he be nɛ e tɔ̃, kɛ nɔ nɛ li kaa nɔ́ nɛ e pee ɔ peeɔ tɔmi ɔ. Blɔ nɔ nɛ o maa gu kɛ pee Yawɛ we ɔ klɔuklɔu ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people. The Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Sami bɔ ɔmɛ, niye ní bɔ ɔmɛ, kɛ wai bɔ ɔmɛ nɛ a kɛ baa Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be, Hejɔɔmi ligbi, kɛ nyami be kpa amɛ tsuo nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ yeɔ ɔ, ganɔ ɔ blɔ nya ji kaa e ha mɛ. Lɛ nɔuu lɛ e haa bɔ nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a kɛ peeɔ kusumi kɛ kpataa Yawɛ kɛ haa Israel ma a: yayami pami bɔ, niye ní bɔ, sami bɔ, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔ.” Nyami behi (Mose II,

english_verse: Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Ligbi kpaago ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ a ngɛ nyami be ɔ yee ɔ, daa ligbi ɔ, e ngɔ na ku kpaago, kɛ agbosu kpaago nɛ kpa ko be a he kɛ ba ha Yawɛ, nɛ e kɛ sã bɔ nɛ a sãã lohwe ɔ tsuo. E ngɔ to akpakpo kake hulɔ kɛ sã yayami pami bɔ daa ligbi.

english_verse: The Lord God said: On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Kekleekle nyɔhiɔ ɔ we kekleekle ligbi ɔ, ngɔɔ na niheyo nɛ kpa ko be e he nɛ o kɛ tsukɔ Yawɛ we ɔ he.

english_verse: The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ lohwe nɛ a kɛ maa pee kusumi kɛ kpa musu ɔ muɔ ɔ eko, nɛ e kɛ kpa we ɔ sinya tso ɔmɛ, bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ sisi kɔ nya eywiɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ we ɔ mi je kue ɔ agbo ɔ sinya tso ɔmɛ a he.

english_verse: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: “Kekleekle nyɔhiɔ ɔ we ligbi nyɔngma kɛ eywiɛne ɔ, nyɛ bɔni Hetsɔmi nyami be ɔ yemi. Nyɛɛ ye abolo kplolo ligbi kpaago.

english_verse: On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people.
translation_verse: Kekleekle ligbi ɔ, ganɔ ɔ nɛ ngɛ ma a nɔ yee ɔ nɛ ngɔ na ku nɛ e kɛ sã yayami pami bɔ kɛ ha lɛ nitsɛ e he, kɛ ma a tsuo.

english_verse: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Agbo nɛ a sɛɛ mi ngɛ beleku je kɛ baa kue ɔ mi ngɛ we ɔ mi je ɔ, a nga lɛ ní tsumi ligbi ekpa amɛ tsuo; se Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ, kɛ Nyɔhiɔhe he nyami be ɔmɛ lɛɛ a bli lɛ kɛ fɔ si.

english_verse: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
translation_verse: Benɛ osɔfo ɔmɛ ngɛ yayami pami, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔ ɔmɛ sãe ɔ, ganɔ ɔ nɛ ngɛ ma a nɔ yee ɔ nɛ gu jamɛ a agbo ɔ mi ngɛ kue ɔ kpo nɔ je kɛ ba, nɛ e ba da si ngɛ agbo ɔ sinya tso ɔ he. E ja Mawu ngɛ agbo ɔ nya ngɛ lejɛ ɔ loko e je kpo. A ko nga agbo ɔ kɛ yaa si gbɔkuɛ.

english_verse: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
translation_verse: Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ, kɛ Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be ɔmɛ ɔ, ma a tsuo nɛ ba ja Yawɛ ngɛ agbo ɔ nya.

english_verse: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: “Ganɔ nɛ ngɛ ma a nɔ yee ɔ nɛ ngɔ jijɔ ekpa, kɛ agbosu kake nɛ kpa be a he kɛ ba sã sami bɔ ha Yawɛ Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ.

english_verse: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: E ngɔ blɛfo lita nyɔngma kɛ kpaago kɛ fa kɛ piɛ agbosu ɔ he, se jijɔ ɔmɛ lɛɛ e ngɔ blɛfo ɔ bɔ nɛ e suɔ kaa e ma ha kɛ piɛ lohwe ɔmɛ a he kɛ ba sã bɔ ɔ. Oliv nu lita etɛ nɛ piɛ blɛfo lita nyɔngma kɛ kpaago kɛ fa he kɛ ba.

english_verse: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: E ngɔ na niheyo kake, jijɔ ekpa, kɛ agbosu kake nɛ kpa be ekoeko he kɛ ba sã bɔ Nyɔhiɔhe nyami be ɔ.

english_verse: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Blɛfo lita nyɔngma kɛ kpaago kɛ fa nɛ piɛ na ku ɔ he, nɛ lita nyɔngma kɛ kpaago kɛ fa nɛ piɛ agbosu ɔ hu he, se jijɔ ɔmɛ a nɔ́ ɔ lɛɛ e ha blɛfo ɔ bɔ nɛ e suɔ, nɛ e ngɔ oliv nu lita etɛ kɛ piɛ he kɛ ba sã niye ní bɔ.

english_verse: The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
translation_verse: Ganɔ ɔ nɛ gu agbo nɛ e kɛ sɛ mi ɔ nɔuu mi kɛ je kpo.

english_verse: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
translation_verse: “Nyami be tsuaa nyami be nɛ ma a tsuo ma Yawɛ jami ɔ, nihi nɛ maa gu omleyi je agbo ɔ mi kɛ sɛ we ɔ mi ɔ, á gu leneyi je agbo ɔ mi kɛ je kpo; nɛ nihi nɛ maa gu leneyi je agbo ɔ mi kɛ sɛ mi ɔ, á gu omleyi je nɔ́ ɔ mi kɛ je kpo. Nɔ ko nɔ ko kó gu blɔ nɛ e kɛ sɛ we ɔ mi ɔ kɛ je kpo; é gu agbo nɛ ngɛ e hɛ mi tɛɛ ɔ mi kɛ je kpo.

english_verse: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
translation_verse: Ke ma a ma ja Yawɛ ɔ, ganɔ ɔ kɛ mɛ nɛ ba; ke a maa kpale kɛ ya a, e kɛ mɛ nɛ ho.

english_verse: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Nyami be tsuaa nyami be nɛ a maa sã niye ní bɔ ɔ, blɛfo lita nyɔngma kɛ kpaago kɛ fa nɛ piɛ na ku kake he, nɛ lita nyɔngma kɛ kpaago kɛ fa nɛ piɛ agbosu kake he, se jijɔ ɔmɛ a nɔ́ ɔ lɛɛ a ha blɛfo ɔ bɔ nɛ a suɔ, nɛ a ngɔ oliv nu lita etɛ kɛ piɛ he kɛ ba.

english_verse: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
translation_verse: “Ke ganɔ ɔ je e tsui mi faa kɛ ma bɔ sami ha Yawɛ ɔ, bɔ nɛ e maa sã lɛ tsuo jio, sina bɔ jio, a bli agbo nɛ ngɛ beleku je ɔ ha lɛ. E sã e bɔ ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ e peeɔ Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ. Ke e gbe nya a, e je kpo, nɛ a nga agbo ɔ.” Bɔ nɛ a sãã daa ligbi

english_verse: Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ke, “Daa mɔtu ɔ, ganɔ ɔ nɛ ngɔ jijɔ nɛ ye jeha kake nɛ kpa ko be e he kɛ ba sã sami bɔ ha imi Yawɛ.

english_verse: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
translation_verse: E ngɔ niye ní nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ piɛ he daa mɔtu kɛ sã bɔ ha imi Yawɛ: mamu kilo enyɔ, kɛ oliv nu lita kake nɛ e kɛ pɔtɔ mamu ɔ. Blɔ nya tomi nɛ kɔɔ bɔ sami nɛ ɔ he ɔ, á ye nɔ daa.

english_verse: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
translation_verse: Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ ke, “Ke ganɔ ɔ ngɔ lɛ nitsɛ e zugba a fa ko kɛ ke e binyumu ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko ɔ, jamɛ a zugba a maa pee bimɛ ɔmɛ a weto ní.

english_verse: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
translation_verse: Se ke e ngɔ zugba a fa ko ngɔ ha e tsɔli ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko ɔ, lɛɛ é hi tsɔlɔ ɔ nine nɔ kɛ yaa si Heyemi jeha nɛ a kpaleɔ níhi kɛ haa nɔtsɛmɛ ɔ maa su. A kpale kɛ ha ganɔ ɔ ekohu, konɛ e pee e nɔ́; se e bimɛ ɔmɛ lɛɛ a weto ní nɛ a na a kɛkɛ nɛ e pee mɛ hu a nɔ́ kulaa.

english_verse: The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him. The Sacred Kitchens
translation_verse: Ganɔ ɔ nɛ ngɔ lɛ nitsɛ e blɔ fami nɔ́ kɛ ha e bimɛ; se ye ma mi bi ɔmɛ lɛɛ a ko kpɔ nɔ ko weto ní ngɛ e dɛ.” Yawɛ we ɔ he kuehi

english_verse: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
translation_verse: Jehanɛ nyumu ɔ ngɔ mi kɛ ya tsu ɔmɛ nɛ a hɛ mi kpee omleyi je ɔ a nya. Tsu nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ mi mi je kue ɔ we agbo ɔ nya ngɛ leneyi je. A ma tsu klɔuklɔu nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ha osɔfo ɔmɛ. Nyumu ɔ tsɔɔ mi he ko ngɛ tsu ɔmɛ a beleku je,

english_verse: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
translation_verse: A kɛ tɛ fia gbogbo kɛ bɔle eko tsuaa eko kɛ kpe, nɛ a ma la tɛ ngɛ gbogbo ɔmɛ a he tsuo kɛ kpe.

english_verse: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ de mi ke, “Bɔ ɔmɛ nɛ ma a ma ba sã a, kuehi nɛ Yawɛ we ɔ mi sɔmɔli ɔmɛ maa hoo lo ɔ ngɛ a mi ɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
translation_verse: Nyumu ɔ ngɔ mi kɛ ba Yawɛ we ɔ agbo ɔ nya ekohu. Nyu hia kɛ je kpoku ɔ sisi, nɛ e be kɛ yaa beleku je, he nɛ Yawɛ we ɔ plɛ e hɛ mi kɛ kpee ɔ. Nyu ɔ hia kɛ je we ɔ leneyi je kɛ ya be ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ leneyi je.

english_verse: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ nyumu ɔ kɛ mi gu omleyi je agbo ɔ mi kɛ je kpo kɛ lɔgɔ si kɛ ba agbo ɔ nɛ hɛ mi kpee beleku je ɔ nya. Nyu ɔ ngɛ kpo jee ngɛ agbo ɔ leneyi je kɛ ngɛ bee kaa pa wayoo ko.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ e de mi ke, “Nɔmlɔ adesa, to nɔ́ nɛ ɔ he hɛ saminya!” Jehanɛ, nyumu ɔ kɛ mi nyɛɛ pa a tue kɛ kpale kɛ ba.

english_verse: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
translation_verse: I na kaa jehanɛ tsohi babauu nitsɛ maa si ngɛ pa a nya hiɛ kɛ hiɛ tsuo.

english_verse: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
translation_verse: E de mi ke, “Nyu nɛ ɔ bee ngɛ zugba a mi kɛ yaa beleku je, kɛ yaa Yordan kɔ̃ ɔ mi, nɛ e ya sɛɛ Ngo wo ɔ mi. Nyu nɛ ɔ tsakeɔ wo nyu ɔ kɛ peeɔ nyu mua.

english_verse: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Kɛ je Engedi pa a nya kɛ yaa si Eneglaim pa a nya tsuo ma hyi kɛ wo hɛli nɛ a ngɛ a yahi kae ngɛ wo ɔ nya. A maa gbe lo slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi babauu ngɛ pa amɛ a mi kaa bɔ nɛ a naa ngɛ Mediterenia wo ɔ nitsɛ mi ɔ.

english_verse: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
translation_verse: Se taku ɔmɛ, kɛ mɔsɔ ɔmɛ lɛɛ a be tsakee; a maa nɔ ngo.

english_verse: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
translation_verse: Tso slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi maa bɔ ngɛ pa a nya hiɛ kɛ pa a se tsuo. Tso ba amɛ be nglae, nɛ a yiblii ɔmɛ hu be tae. Nyɔhiɔ tsuaa nyɔhiɔ ɔ, a maa wo yiblii he; ejakaa nyu nɛ a naa a, Yawɛ we ɔ mi a naa kɛ jeɔ. Tso ɔmɛ ma ha niye ní babauu, nɛ a ba amɛ ma ba pee tsopa nɛ a kɛ ma tsa ma a.” Zugba a huzu ɔmɛ

english_verse: The Lord God said to the people of Israel: When the land is divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, the Joseph tribe will receive two shares. Divide the land equally, because I promised your ancestors that this land would someday belong to their descendants. These are the borders of the land:
translation_verse: I wo nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ si ke ma ngɔ zugba nɛ ɔ kɛ ha mɛ, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ dla lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ha nyɛ he, nɛ e pee nyɛ weto ní.

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad,
translation_verse: “Zugba a we omleyi je huzu ɔ je Mediterenia wo ɔ nya kɛ ya gu Hetlon blɔ kɛ ya gu Hamat yo kpɛ blɔ ɔ, kɛ muɔ Zedad,

english_verse: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
translation_verse: kɛ ya na Berota kɛ Sibraim ma amɛ nɛ ngɛ Damasko kɛ Hamat huzu ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ, kɛ ya na Tikon nɛ ngɛ Hauran huzu ɔ nya a.

english_verse: So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
translation_verse: Huzu nɛ ngɛ omleyi je ɔ ji kɛ je Mediterenia wo ɔ nya kɛ ya na Enon ma a ngɛ Damasko huzu ɔ nya, nɛ e be lejɛ ɔ he kɛ ya gu omleyi je kɛ ya muɔ Hamat huzu ɔ.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
translation_verse: “Beleku je huzu ɔ je Hauran kɛ Damasko a kpɛti, kɛ Gilead kɛ Israel zugba a hu a kpɛti ngɛ Yordan pa a he kɛ ya su Tamar tɔɔ ngɛ Ngo wo ɔ nya.

english_verse: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: “Leneyi je huzu ɔ je Tamar, kɛ gu Kadesh Meriba nyu ɔmɛ a he kɛ ya muɔ Egipt huzu ɔ, kɛ ya pi Mediterenia wo ɔ.

english_verse: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
translation_verse: “Bonyoku je huzu ɔ je Mediterenia wo ɔ nya hluu kɛ ya su Hamat yo kpɛ blɔ ɔ he.

english_verse: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: “Nyɛɛ dla zugba nɛ ɔ ha nyɛ he ngɛ Israel wɛtso ɔmɛ a nya.

english_verse: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
translation_verse: Á po zugba ha nyɛ wɛtso ɔmɛ, Israel fɔfɔɛ ɔmɛ, nyɛ nibwɔhi nɛ ba to nyɛ ɔ, kɛ a bimɛ tsuo nɛ ba pee Israel bi ɔ. A hyɛ, konɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ na e blɔ nya pɛpɛɛpɛ kaa Israel fɔfɔɛ.

english_verse: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Wɛtso mi he nɛ nubwɔ ko ba to ɔ, a ha lɛ weto ní ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Imi, Nyɔmtsɛ Yawɛ lɛ i de.”

english_verse: Each tribe will receive a section of land that runs from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. The northern border of Israel will run along the towns of Hethlon and Lebo-Hamath, and will end at Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between the kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The tribes will receive their share of land in the following order, from north to south: Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben, and Judah. The Special Section of Land The Lord said:
translation_verse: Zugba a we omleyi je huzu ɔ je Mediterenia wo ɔ nya kɛ ya beleku je, hluu kɛ ya na Hetlon ma a, kɛ ya gu Hamat yo kpɛ blɔ ɔ, kɛ ya muɔ Enon, kɛ ya su Damasko kɛ Hamat a kpɛti. Nyɛ susu zugba a, nɛ nyɛɛ wo huzu kɛ je beleku je kɛ ya na Mediterenia wo ɔ ngɛ bonyoku je kɛ ha wɛtso ɔmɛ.
