english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Waa kɛ mɛ ye sɛ; kɛkɛ nɛ lɛ ɔ hia. Lɛ ɔ nyɛɛ tɛɛ kɛ ba Koo; nɛ e nɔ jena a, wa ba Rodo, nɛ wa tsa nɔ kɛ je lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Wa na lɛ ko ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ yaa Foinike, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, wa ya sɛ mi, nɛ wa pue nɔ.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Wa ba su he ko nɛ wa na Kipro jee ngɛ wa hɛ mi, se wa ya gu e leneyi je, nɛ wa ba Siria. Wa ba kple ngɛ Tiro, ejakaa lejɛ ɔ nɛ a ma je lɛ ɔ mi ní ngɛ.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Se nɛ be nɛ wa to nɛ wa maa ye ngɛ a ngɔ ɔ nya ta a, wa si mɛ, nɛ wa pue blɔ. Nyumu ɔmɛ tsuo, kɛ a yi ɔmɛ, kɛ a bimɛ ɔmɛ ba je wɔ blɔ kɛ je ma a mi kɛ ya su wo ɔ nya. Wa kpla si ngɛ zia a nɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ wa sɔle.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, waa kɛ mɛ ye sɛ; kɛkɛ nɛ wa ya sɛ lɛ ɔ mi, nɛ mɛ hu a kpale a se kɛ ho we mi ya.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Wa kpale wó lɛ kɛ tsa wa blɔ hiami ɔ nɔ kɛ je Tiro kɛ ba Pitolemai. Wa ya nga nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ waa kɛ mɛ hi si ligbi kake.

english_verse: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
translation_verse: E ngɛ biyiwi eywiɛ nɛ gba we lolo, nɛ a fiɛɔ Mawu munyu ɔ.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Wa hi lejɛ ɔ be saii; kɛkɛ nɛ gbalɔ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Agabo ɔ je Yudea kɛ ba.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: E ba wa ngɔ, nɛ e ba ngɔ Paulo mlɛ mi fimi nɔ́ ɔ, nɛ e kɛ fi lɛ nitsɛ e nanehi, kɛ e ninehi; nɛ e de ke, “Bɔ nɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ de ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: Nɔ nɛ nɔ́ ji mlɛ mi fimi nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, kikɛ nɛ ɔ Yuda bi ɔmɛ maa pee lɛ ngɛ Yerusalem, nɛ a maa ngɔ lɛ ngɔ wo ma je li ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Benɛ wa nu nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, waa kɛ nihi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ tsuo kpa Paulo pɛɛ ke e ko ya Yerusalem.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Se e he nɔ ke, “Mɛni nyɛ ngɛ pee nɛ ɔ; nyɛ ngɛ ya foe kɛ ma tsɔ ye tsui kpa? Imi lɛɛ, pi fimi nɛ a maa fi mi ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ kɛkɛ nɛ i ngɛ blɔ hyɛe, se mohu i pee klaalo nɛ ma gbo ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Wa nyɛ we nɛ wa tsake e yi mi tomi ɔ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ wa nyɛ de kɛkɛ ji, “A pee nɔ́ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ suɔ.”

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ je Kaisarea a, a ti ni komɛ kɛ wɔ ho; nɛ a ha wa ya to Minason. Nyumu nɛ ɔ, Kipro no ji lɛ, nɛ e ba pee kaselɔ pi mwɔnɛ. Paulo ya slaa Yakobo

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Benɛ wa su Yerusalem ɔ, nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ he wɔ hɛmuɔ.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, waa kɛ Paulo ya Yakobo ngɔ. Wa ya na asafo nikɔtɔma amɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Paulo nga mɛ; nɛ bɔ mɛ níhi nɛ Mawu gu e nɔ tsu ngɛ ma je li ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ tsuo.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Benɛ a bu lɛ tue kɛ ya si nyagbe ɔ, mɛ tsuo a je Mawu yi. Kɛkɛ nɛ a de lɛ ke, “Wa nyɛmi Paulo, hyɛ, Yuda bi akpe abɔ nɛ he ye nɛ ɔ, o le bɔ nɛ a fiɛ we Mose mlaa a he ha.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: A nu kaa Yuda bi tsuo nɛ ngɛ ma je li ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ mɛ dee ji kaa a ko ye Mose mlaa a nɔ, a ko po a bimɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ a ko tsu Yuda bi a kusumi hulɔ.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ, a maa nu kaa o ba. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, kɛ wa maa pee kɛɛ?

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Ga nɛ wa ngɛ mo woe ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: Nyumuhi eywiɛ ngɛ wa kpɛti nɛ wo Mawu si.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: O kɛ mɛ nɛ ya, nɛ kusumi nɛ a peeɔ kɛ tsukɔɔ nɔ he ɔ, nyɛ ya pee, nɛ o wo hiɔ ɔ ha mɛ, konɛ a sɛ a yi. Ke o pee ja a, nihi tsuo maa na kaa níhi nɛ a ba sɛɛ ngɛ o he ɔ be mi, se mohu mo nitsɛ po o yeɔ Mose mlaa a nɔ sisiisi.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Ma je li nɛ ba he ye ɔ, mɛɛ lɛɛ wa ngma mɛ womi ke wa ma nya si kaa a ko ye wɔ nya ní, a ko ye lo nɛ muɔ ngɛ mi kɛ mwɔɔ, nɛ a ko ye lohwe nɛ a kika e kuɛ hulɔ. Jehanɛ hu, a hyɛ a he nɔ saminya, nɛ a ko fiɛ nyumu kɛ yo yakayaka fiɛmi.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e nɔ jena a, Paulo kɛ nyumu ɔmɛ ho nɛ a ya pee kusumi kɛ tsukɔ a he. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ya sɔlemi we ɔ, nɛ a ya wo si kaa otsi se ɔ, a maa gbe kusumi ɔ nya, nɛ a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ ma ba sã bɔ. A nu Paulo ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Benɛ e piɛ bɔɔ nɛ otsi ɔ maa su ɔ, Yuda bi komɛ nɛ je Asia zugba a nɔ ɔ na Paulo ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ. Nimli nɛ ɔmɛ sú ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo ngɔ wo Paulo he, nɛ a nu lɛ.

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: A kpa ngmlaa ke, “Tsaatsɛmɛ Israel bi, nyɛ ba piɛ wa he! Kikɛmɛ a nyumu nɛ ɔ yaa he tsuaa he ya tuɔ munyu yaya kɛ gbee Israel ma a he guɛ; e tuɔ munyu kɛ siɔ Mose mlaa a, kɛ wa sɔlemi we ɔ. Jehanɛ lɛɛ e ngɔ ma je li tete kɛ ba sɔlemi we ɔ ba ble he klɔuklɔu nɛ ɔ hulɔ!”

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: A de jã, ejakaa a na Paulo kɛ Trofimo nɛ je Efeso ɔ ngɛ ma a mi momo, nɛ a susu kaa Paulo kɛ lɛ ba sɔlemi we ɔ.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Ma a mi tsuo pee gidigidi; ni ɔmɛ tu kɛ ba kɛ fo, nɛ a ba nu Paulo; kɛkɛ nɛ a gbla lɛ kɛ je sɔlemi we ɔ kɛ je kpo. Amlɔ nɔuu ɔ, a nga sinya amɛ.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Benɛ basabasa peeli ɔmɛ ngɛ hlae nɛ a gbe Paulo ɔ, nɔ ko ya sɛɛ ha Roma asafoatsɛngua a ke Yerusalem tsuo pee gidigidi.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Amlɔ nɔuu ɔ, e ngɔ ta buli, kɛ asafoatsɛmɛ kɛ piɛ e he kɛ fo kɛ je mɔ ɔ mi kɛ ba na basabasa peeli ɔmɛ. Benɛ ni ɔmɛ na asafoatsɛngua a, kɛ ta buli ɔmɛ ɔ, a jɔɔ Paulo kongomi.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ asafoatsɛngua a hɛ lɛ kɛ su Paulo he, nɛ e pɛtɛ e he, nɛ e fa ke a wo lɛ kɔsɔkɔsɔ enyɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ e bi ke, “Nyumu nɛ ɔ, mɛnɔ ji lɛ; nɛ mɛni e pee?”

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Lejɛ ɔ tsuo pee hoo kɛ ngmlaa. Benɛ ni komɛ ngɛ nɔ́ kake dee ɔ, ni komɛ hu ngɛ nɔ́ kpa dee. Basabasa a nya ba wa bɔ nɛ asafoatsɛngua a nyɛ we nɛ e le nɔ́ tutuutu nɛ ngɛ nɔ yae. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e fa e we bi ɔmɛ ke a ngɔ Paulo kɛ ya mɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Benɛ a su atlaakpe ɔ nya a, gidigidi ɔ nya ba wa tsɔ, nɛ e hia kaa ta buli ɔmɛ nɛ a hɛɛ Paulo ngɛ kɔɔhiɔ mi;

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: ejakaa ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo nyɛɛ e se gidigidi kɛ ngmlaa ke, “A gbe lɛ!” Paulo je e nya

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Benɛ ta buli ɔmɛ miɔ nɛ a kɛ Paulo maa sɛ mɔ ɔ mi ɔ, e de asafoatsɛngua a ke, “Ma bi mo nɔ́ ko bɔɔ!” Asafoatsɛngua a bi lɛ ke, “O tuɔ Hela gbi lo?

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Paulo he nɔ ke, “Imi lɛɛ Yuda no ji mi. A fɔ mi ngɛ Tarso, Kilikia ma nɛ ngɛ biɛ saminya a. I kpa mo pɛɛ, ha nɛ i kɛ ma a nɛ tu munyu bɔɔ.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛngua a ngmɛ lɛ blɔ; kɛkɛ nɛ Paulo da atlaakpe ɔ nɔ, nɛ e fɔ ma a nine ke a pee dii. Benɛ lejɛ ɔ jɔ klanaa a, e tu munyu ngɛ Hebri gbi mi ke:

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Benɛ ni ɔmɛ nu kaa Hebri gbi e kɛ mɛ ngɛ tue ɔ, a pee dii pe kekle ɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ e tsa nɔ ke,

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: “Yuda no ji mi; nɛ a fɔ mi ngɛ Tarso ngɛ Kilikia mohu, se Yerusalem hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ nɛ a lɛ mi ngɛ. Gamaliel lɛ tsɔɔ mi ní. A tsɔse mi bɔ nɛ sa ngɛ wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ a mlaa a nya. I kplɛɛ we nɔ́ ngɛ Mawu he kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ tsuo nyɛ ngɛ pee mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ hɛɛ kikɛmɛ a tsɔɔmi nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, i wa mɛ yi mi, nɛ ni komɛ po gbo ngɛ mi. I nuɔ nyumuhi kɛ yihi tete kɛ ya woɔ tsu.

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: Osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa a, kɛ kpe ngua a tsuo ma nyɛ maa ye mi odase. Mɛ nɔuu lɛ a ha mi womi nɛ ma kɛ ya ha wa nyɛmimɛ Yuda bi nɛ ngɛ Damasko ɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, jinɛ i yaa lejɛ ɔ, nɛ ma ya nuu nihi nɛ hɛɛ kikɛmɛ a tsɔɔmi nɛ ɔ mi kɛ ba Yerusalem, konɛ a gbla a tue.” Paulo sɛɛ nɔ́ nɛ ba loko e tsake e tsui (Ni Tsumi

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: “Benɛ i nyɛɛ blɔ kɛ yaa Damasko, nɛ e piɛ bɔɔ pɛ nɛ ma su maa pee piani pu dadɛ be mi ɔ, tlukaa a, la nɛ nya wa ko kpɛ nylam kɛ je hiɔwe ba bɔle mi.

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: I tsɔ fia si, nɛ i nu gbi ko nɛ bi mi ke, ‘Saulo, Saulo! Mɛni he je nɛ o ngɛ mi yi mi wae ɔ?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: I he nɔ ke, ‘Mo mɛnɔ, Nyɔmtsɛ?’ E de mi ke, ‘Imi ji Yesu, Nazaret no ɔ nɛ o ngɛ lɛ yi mi wae ɔ!’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ kɛ mi nyɛɛ ɔ na la a, se gbi ɔ nɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ɔ lɛɛ a nui.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: I bi ke, ‘Nyɔmtsɛ, kɛ ma pee kɛɛ?’ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ de mi ke, ‘Tee si nɛ o ya Damasko, nɛ lejɛ ɔ a maa tsɔɔ mo níhi tsuo nɛ Mawu to ha mo kaa o pee ɔ.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: La nɛ kpɛ ɔ ha nɛ i hyɛ we nɔ́ hu; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nihi nɛ kɛ mi nyɛɛ ɔ ta ye dɛ mi, nɛ a kɛ mi ya su Damasko.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: “Nyumu ko ngɛ jamɛ a ma a mi nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Anania. E jaa Mawu anɔkuale mi; nɛ e yeɔ Mose mlaa a nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yuda bi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Damasko ɔ tuɔ e he munyu kpakpa.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Lɛ nɛ e ba ye ngɔ, nɛ e ba da ye kasa nya, nɛ e de mi ke, ‘Ye nyɛminyumu Saulo, hyɛ nɔ́!’ Jamɛ a ngmlɛfia a nɔuu ɔ, i bɔni nɔ́ hyɛmi ekohu, nɛ i na lɛ.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: E de mi ke, ‘Wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ a Mawu ɔ hla mo ngɔ to, konɛ o le e suɔmi nya ní, nɛ o na e Tsɔlɔ nɛ peeɔ nɔ nɛ da a, konɛ o nu lɛ nitsɛ e nya mi gbi.

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: “I kpale ye se kɛ ba Yerusalem ekohu; nɛ benɛ i ya ngɛ sɔlee ngɛ sɔlemi we, nɔ́ nɔ ye nɔ.

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ i na Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nɛ ngɛ mi dee ke, ‘Pee esɔ nɛ o je Yeruslem mlamlaamla, ejakaa nihi nɛ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, ye he odase nɛ o ngɛ yee ɔ, a be tue bue.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: I he nɔ ke, ‘Nyɔmtsɛ, mɛ nitsɛmɛ a le kaa sa a, imi nɔuu lɛ i yaa kpe he ɔmɛ, nɛ nihi nɛ he mo ye ɔ, i ya nuɔ mɛ, nɛ i fiaa mɛ ní.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Benɛ a gbe Stefano, nɔ nɛ ye o he odase ɔ, imi hu i ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Ye bua jɔ e gbenɔ ɔ he, nɛ nihi nɛ gbe lɛ ɔ, imi lɛ i bu a tade ɔmɛ a he.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ de mi ke, ‘Yaa, ejakaa ma tsɔ mo ma je li ɔmɛ a ngɔ ngɛ tsitsaa lokoo!’ ”

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Ni ɔmɛ bu Paulo tue hluu kɛ ba si e wo munyu nɛ ɔ ta, kɛkɛ nɛ a bɔni ngmlaa kpami wawɛɛ ke, “A kɛ lɛ nɛ ho! A gbe lɛ! E sɛ kaa e hii je mi!”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Benɛ ngmlaa ngɛ pɛe ɔ, a ngɛ a tade ɔmɛ fɔ̃e kɛ ngɛ hiɔwe yae kɛ a nɔ bunyuku kpii.

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Roma asafoatsɛngua a fa e we bi ɔmɛ ke a kɛ Paulo nɛ ya mɔ ɔ mi. E de kɛ piɛ he hu ke a fia lɛ kpa kɛ hla e yi mi, konɛ a le nɔ́ he je nɛ a ngɛ ngmlaa kpae kɛ ngɛ lɛ woe kikɛ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Se benɛ a fi lɛ nɛ a maa fia lɛ kpa a, Paulo bi asafoatsɛ nɛ daa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ke, “Roma no nɛ a kojo we lɛ, nɛ a bui lɛ fɔ ɔ, nyɛ ngɛ he blɔ kaa nyɛ fiaa lɛ kpa?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Benɛ asafoatsɛ ɔ nu enɛ ɔ, e ya asafoatsɛngua a ngɔ, nɛ e ya de lɛ ke, “Mɛni o maa ho peemi ya nɛ ɔ? Nyumu ɔ, Roma no ji lɛ!”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, asafoatsɛngua a ba Paulo ngɔ, nɛ e ba bi lɛ ke, “Anɛ Roma no ji mo? De mi!” Paulo he nɔ ke, “Ee!”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛngua a de lɛ ke, “Sika babauu i ha loko i ba pee Roma no.” Se Paulo he nɔ ke, “Imi lɛɛ a fɔ mi Roma no.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Benɛ nihi nɛ kɛ lɛ yaa a nu enɛ ɔ, a laa ngɛ lejɛ ɔ amlɔ. Asafoatsɛngua a hu e tsui po; ejakaa e na kaa Paulo ɔ, mamoo Roma no ji lɛ, nɛ e wo lɛ kɔsɔkɔsɔ. A kɛ Paulo ba kpe ngua a hɛ mi

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛngua a suɔ kaa e le nɔ́ tutuutu he je nɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ po Paulo nya a. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e nɔ jena a, e je lɛ, nɛ e fa ke osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ, kɛ kpe ngua a mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ a ba bua a he nya. Kɛkɛ nɛ e ngɔ Paulo ba da a hɛ mi.

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Anania, osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa a fa nihi nɛ daa si ngɛ e kasa nya a ke a gba e nya ma.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Paulo de lɛ ke, “Mo hu Mawu ma gba mo ma kokooko; mo nɛ o ngɛ kaa gli nɛ a sa he kalo! Mo nɛ o blɔ nya ji kaa o hyɛ nɛ a kojo mi ngɛ mlaa a nya a, hyɛ kaa mo mohu o je mlaa a se fa ke a gba mi ma!”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ daa si ngɛ e kasa nya a de lɛ ke, “Hyɛ! Mawu we osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa a o ngɛ jɛe nɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Paulo he nɔ ke, “Ye nyɛmimɛ Israel bi, i li kaa lɛ ji osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa a. Ngmami ɔ deɔ ke, ‘O ma mi nɔkɔtɔma a, koo tu e he munyu yaya!’ ”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Paulo kpa si kaa kpe ngua mi bi ɔmɛ fa kake ji Saduki bi, nɛ fa hu pee ɔ Farisi bi ɔ, e wo e gbi nɔ wawɛɛ, nɛ e de ke, “Ye nyɛmimɛ Israel bi, Farisi no ji mi, nɛ ye fɔli hu Farisi bi ji mɛ. A ngɛ mi kojoe ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, ejakaa i heɔ yeɔ kaa hwɔɔ se ɔ, ni gbogboehi maa te si kɛ ba wami mi ekohu.”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: Benɛ e de kikɛ nɛ ɔ kɛkɛ nɛ pɛ sɛ Farisi bi ɔmɛ, kɛ Saduki bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti, nɛ kpe ɔ mi gba enyɔ.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Huhui ɔ nya ba wa, nɛ mlaa tsɔɔli ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Farisi bi ɔmɛ a se ɔ te si kɛ pɛ wawɛɛ, nɛ a de ke, “Wɔɔ lɛɛ wa nɛ nɔ́ yaya ko ngɛ nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ he! Alini mumi ko, loo hiɔwe bɔfo ko kɛ lɛ tu munyu niinɛ!”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Benɛ pɛ ɔ mi ba wa a, asafoatsɛngua a ye gbeye kaa eko ɔ, a ma tsɔtslɔɔ Paulo mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e fa e ta buli ɔmɛ ke a kple si nɛ a ya ngɔ Paulo ngɛ a dɛ pani nya, nɛ a kɛ lɛ nɛ ba mɔ ɔ mi.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ba da Paulo kasa nya, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Koo ye gbeye. Bɔ nɛ o ye ye he odase ngɛ Yerusalem nɛ ɔ, ja o ya ye odase jã nɔuu ngɛ Roma hulɔ.” A so Paulo yi nɔ

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: A ya osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ a ngɔ ya de ke, “Wa ka wa he kita kaa wa be wa nya mi nɔ́ ko woe kɛ yaa si wa maa gbe Paulo.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ kɛ kpe ngua a mi bi ɔmɛ tsuo nyɛ ha nyɛ gbi ya su Roma asafoatsɛngua a. Nyɛ de lɛ ke e ngɔ Paulo ngɔ mane nyɛ. Nyɛɛ buá de lɛ ke nyɛ ngɛ hlae nɛ nyɛɛ hyɛ e sane ɔ mi fitsofitso. Se wɔɔ lɛɛ wa maa pee klaalo, nɛ wa maa gbe lɛ loko e maa su nyɛ ngɔ.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Se Paulo nyɛmiyo bi ko nu ga nɛ a to ɔ he; nɛ e pue nɔ kɛ ya mɔ ɔ mi, nɛ e ya de Paulo.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Paulo tsɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a ti nɔ kake, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Ngɔɔ niheyo nɛ ɔ kɛ ya asafoatsɛngua a ngɔ; e hɛɛ sɛ gbi ko kɛ ha lɛ.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛ ɔ ngɔ niheyo ɔ kɛ ya asafoatsɛngua a ngɔ, nɛ e ya de lɛ ke, “Paulo, nɔ nɛ a bɔ lɛ pã a tsɛ mi, nɛ e de mi ke ma ngɔ niheyo nɛ ɔ kɛ ba o ngɔ, ejakaa e hɛɛ sɛ gbi ko kɛ ha mo.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛngua a nu niheyo ɔ nine si, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ya se, nɛ e bi lɛ ke, “Mɛni sane o ngɛ nɛ o ma de mi?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: E de lɛ ke, “Yuda nikɔtɔma amɛ to kaa a ma ba de mo nɛ hwɔɔ ɔ, o ngɔ Paulo kɛ ba kpe ngua a hɛ mi. A maa buá ma de enɛ ɔ kaa nɔ́ nɛ e sane ɔ mi nɛ kpe ngua a mi bi ɔmɛ ngɛ hlae nɛ a hyɛ fitsofitso.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛngua a de niheyo ɔ ke, “Ko de nɔ ko nɔ ko ke o wo sane nɛ ɔ nɔ ta ha mi.” Kɛkɛ nɛ e wo niheyo ɔ blɔ. A kɛ Paulo ya ha amlaalo Felike

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Nyɛ hla okpɔngɔ komɛ hu ha Paulo nɛ e hi nɔ; nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ lɛ ya ha amlaalo Felike slɔkee.”

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛngua a ngma womi, nɛ e de ngɛ mi ke,

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ nu kikɛmɛ a nyumu nɛ ɔ, nɛ jinɛ a maa gbe lɛ. Se benɛ i ná le kaa Roma no ji lɛ ɔ, i kɛ ye ta buli ɔmɛ ya kpɔ̃ lɛ.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: I hla kaa ma le nɔ́ he je nɛ a ngɛ e nya poe ɔ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kɛ lɛ ya a kpe ngua a hɛ mi.

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ i na ji, nyumu ɔ pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ sa kaa a gbe lɛ, loo a wo lɛ tsu tete; e nya nɛ a po ɔ kɔɔ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a mlaa he nɔ jemi sane komɛ a he.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Se benɛ i ná le kaa a so e yi nɔ nɛ a maa gbe lɛ ɔ, i pee ye yi mi kaa a ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba o ngɔ amlɔ nɔuu. I de e nya poli ɔmɛ hu ke sanehi nɛ a ngɛ kɛ si lɛ ɔ, a ba o ngɔ, konɛ a ba jaje.”

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ ta buli ɔmɛ pee kaa bɔ nɛ a fa mɛ ɔ. A ngɔ Paulo, nɛ jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi nɔuu a kɛ lɛ ba Antipatri.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, ta buli nane nyɛɛli ɔmɛ kpale a se kɛ ba mɔ ɔ mi ekohu, nɛ a si okpɔngɔ ta buli ɔmɛ, konɛ a kɛ lɛ nɛ ho.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Benɛ a su Kaisarea a, a kɛ womi ɔ ya ha amlaalo ɔ, nɛ a tu Paulo hu ngɔ wo e dɛ mi.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Amlaalo ɔ kane womi ɔ, nɛ e bi Paulo kpokpa nɔ he nɛ e je. Jehanɛ, benɛ e ná le kaa Paulo je Kilikia a,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: e de lɛ ke, “Nihi nɛ kɛ mo na a, ke a ba su hiɛ ɔ konɛ ma bu mo tue.” Kɛkɛ nɛ e fa ke a ngɔ Paulo kɛ ya mɔ ɔ mi, nɛ a ya bu e he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Ligbi enuɔ se ɔ, Anania, osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa a, kɛ ma nikɔtɔma komɛ, kɛ otsiamɛ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Tertulo ɔ ba Kaisarea. A ba Felike ngɔ, nɛ a ba po Paulo nya ha lɛ.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: A tsɛ Paulo kɛ ba; kɛkɛ nɛ Tertulo bɔni e nya pomi ke, “Wa nɔmo Felike, o ngɛ wa nɔ hyɛe saminya kɛ juɛmi nɛ mi kuɔ, nɛ enɛ ɔ ha wa tue mi jɔ wɔ be babauu. A to blɔ nya kɛ ngɛ ní komɛ tsakee kɛ ha ma a nɔ yami.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: I sume kaa ma tu munyu fuu kɛ puɛ o be. I kpa mo pɛɛ, naa wɔ mɔbɔ, nɛ o bu wɔ tue kpiti.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: Wa na nyumu nɛ ɔ kaa ma ywialɔ. E woɔ Yuda bi a yi mi ngɛ he tsuaa he ke a tsɔ atuã. Jehanɛ hu, kuu nɛ a tsɛɛ Nazaree ɔ a nyatsɛ kpanaku ji lɛ.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: E fa nihi nɛ ngɛ Paulo nya poe ɔ ke a ba mo nitsɛ o ngɔ. Ke o ta e nya mi ɔ, mo nitsɛ o maa nu níhi tsuo nɛ waa kɛ ngɛ e nya poe ɔ.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ hu fia Tertulo nɔ́ ɔ se pɛpɛɛpɛ kaa bɔ nɛ e de ɔ. Paulo je e nya ngɛ Felike hɛ mi

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ ɔ, amlaalo ɔ fɔ Paulo nine ke e tu munyu. Kɛkɛ nɛ Paulo wo e nya nɔ nɛ e de ke, “I le kaa pi mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ nɛ o bɔni kojomi ngɛ zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i ná bua jɔmi saminya kaa ma je ye nya ngɛ o hɛ mi.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Ke mo nitsɛ o bu ɔ, o maa na kaa ligbi nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ pɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ i ba be kɛ ho Yerusalem ya nɛ ma ya ja Mawu.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Yuda bi ɔmɛ nɛ́ kaa i kɛ nɔ ko ngɛ nya sãe ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ mi a nɛ́ hu kaa i ngɛ ma a yi mi woe ngɛ kpe he ɔ, aloo he kpa ko ngɛ ma a mi.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Jehanɛ hu, sanehi nɛ a kɛ fɔ ye nɔ nɛ ɔ, a be nya nyɛe maa tsɔɔ kaa a ngɛ mi.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Niinɛ ɔ, wa nɛmɛ a Mawu ɔ i jaa ngɛ tsɔɔmi ɔ nɛ mɛɛ a deɔ ke e pi blɔ kpakpa a mi. Imi hu níhi nɛ a ngma ngɛ Mose mlaa a, kɛ gbali ɔmɛ a womi ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, i heɔ lɛ tsuo yeɔ.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: I heɔ Mawu yeɔ kaa adesahi tsuo maa te si kɛ je gbeje hwɔɔ se, ni kpakpahi jio, yayami peeli jio; nimli nɛ ɔmɛ heɔ enɛ ɔ yeɔ ja nɔuu.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i bɔɔ mɔde kaa daa nɛ ɔ ma pee nɔ́ nɛ maa sa Mawu, kɛ adesahi tsuo a hɛ mi, nɛ ye he nile be mi fɔ bue.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: “I hia blɔ kɛ je Yerusalem ya ye jeha babauu ngɛ ma se. Pee se ɔ, i kpale kɛ ba kɛ ye dɛ mi nike ní nɛ ma ba ha ye ma a mi bi komɛ, konɛ imi nitsɛ hu ma sã bɔ.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Benɛ i ngɛ kusumi ɔmɛ pee ɔ, a na mi ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ. Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, i pee kusumi ɔ kɛ tsukɔ ye he gbe nya momo. Nɔ ko nɛ́ mi nɛ i kɛ nihi fuu daa si, jehanɛ hu, nɔ ko pee we basabasa ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Se Yuda bi komɛ nɛ je Asia a ngɛ lejɛ ɔ; mɛ mohu nɛ sa kaa a ba o hɛ mi, konɛ ke a ngɛ ye he sane ko ɔ, nɛ a ba jaje.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ daa si ngɛ hiɛ ɔ amlɔ nɛ ɔ, mɛ nitsɛmɛ po, ke a na nɔ́ ko nɛ dɛ ngɛ ye he benɛ i daa si ngɛ kpe ngua a hɛ mi ɔ, a de.

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: Nɔ́ pɛ nɛ a ko nyɛ de ji, benɛ i daa si ngɛ kpe ngua a hɛ mi ɔ, i wo ye gbi nɔ nɛ i de ke, ‘Mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, a ngɛ mi kojoe, ejakaa i heɔ yeɔ kaa ni gbogboehi maa te si kɛ ba wami mi ekohu.’ ”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Felike le Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ tsɔɔmi ɔ he sane saminya, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e tsɛ̃ munyu ɔ ngɔ to, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Ke asafoatsɛngua Lisia ba su kɛkɛ ma buá sane ɔ he.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e fa asafoatsɛ ɔ ke e ngɔ Paulo kɛ ho nɛ e ya bu e he, se e ha nɛ e na he jɔmi bɔɔ; nɛ ke e huɛmɛ ba nɛ a ba pee nɔ́ ko ha lɛ ɔ, e ko tsi mɛ blɔ. Paulo ngɛ Felike kɛ Drusila a hɛ mi

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Be saii se ɔ, Felike kɛ e yo Drusila ba. E yo ɔ, Yuda no ji lɛ. Felike ha a ya tsɛ Paulo kɛ ba. Benɛ Paulo ngɛ munyu tue ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi ngɛ Kristo Yesu mi he ɔ, e bu lɛ tue saminya.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Se benɛ Paulo ngɛ dami, he nɔ yemi, kɛ kojomi nɛ maa ba a he munyu tue ɔ, Felike ye gbeye wawɛɛ, nɛ e de lɛ ke, “Yaa lolo, ke i na deka a, ma tsɛ mo ekohu.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Blɔɔ e hɛ ngɛ nɔ kaa Paulo ma ha lɛ sika, enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, ke pee ɔ, e tsɔɔ ya tsɛɔ Paulo, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ba sɛɛɔ ní.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Jeha enyɔ se ɔ, Porkio Festo ba ye Felike nane mi kaa amlaalo. Felike hla kaa e pee nɔ́ nɛ sa Yuda bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e tsi Paulo nya ngɛ tsu ɔ mi.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Festo ba bɔni amlaalo yemi ligbi etɛ se pɛ kɛkɛ nɛ e je Kaisarea kɛ ho Yerusalem ya.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ, kɛ Yuda ma nimeli ɔmɛ ba po Paulo nya ha lɛ. A kpa Festo pɛɛ

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: ke e hyɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ e tsɔ nɛ a ya ngɔ Paulo kɛ ba Yerusalem; mɛɛ lɛɛ a so e yi nɔ nɛ a maa gbe lɛ ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Se Festo he nɔ ke, “A wo Paulo tsu ngɛ Kaisarea, nɛ imi nitsɛ hu e be kɛe nɛ ma ya lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Nyɛ ha nyɛ nya dali ɔmɛ nɛ a kɛ mi nɛ ya Kaisarea, nɛ ke sane yaya ko ngɛ nyumu ɔ he ɔ, a de ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Festo ye maa pee ligbi kpaanyɔ, loo nyɔngma ngɛ a ngɔ, kɛkɛ nɛ e pue nɔ kɛ ho Kaisarea ya. E nɔ jena a, e ya hi kojomi sɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ e fa ke a kɛ Paulo nɛ ba.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Benɛ Paulo ba lejɛ ɔ, Yuda bi nɛ je Yerusalem kɛ ba a ba bɔle lɛ kɛ kpe, nɛ a kɛ sanehi babauu nɛ nya wa ba po e nya. Se níhi nɛ a de kɛ si Paulo ɔ, a nyɛ we nɛ a tsɔɔ kaa ní ɔmɛ ngɛ mi niinɛ.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Paulo je e nya, nɛ e de ke, “I tɔ we Yuda bi ɔmɛ a mlaa ko; i pee we nɔ́ ko kɛ ble we sɔlemi we ɔ, nɛ Kaisare ɔ hu i tɔ we e nɔ.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Se akɛnɛ Festo hla kaa e maa sa Yuda bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi he je ɔ, e bi Paulo ke, “O suɔ kaa o maa ya Yerusalem nɛ ma ya kojo mo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a sane nɛ ɔmɛ a he lo?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Paulo de lɛ ke, “Kaisare ɔ nitsɛ kojomi sɛ ɔ hɛ mi, he nɛ sa kaa a kojo mi ngɛ ɔ, lejɛ ɔ i daa si ngɛ nɛ ɔ nɛ. I tɔ we Yuda bi a nɔ kaa bɔ nɛ mo nitsɛ o le ɔ.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Ke i ye sane yaya ko, nɛ i pee nɔ́ nɛ sa gbenɔ ɔ, i de we ke a ngmɛɛ ye he. Se ke sanehi nɛ ni nɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ kɛ ngɛ ye nya poe nɛ ɔ be mi ɔ, nɔ ko be nyɛe maa ngɔ mi ngɔ wo a dɛ mi. I suɔ kaa Kaisare ɔ nitsɛ nɛ ye ye sane ɔ.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Festo kɛ e ga woli ɔmɛ hla munyu ɔ mi; nɛ lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e de ke, “Nɛ o ngɔ o sane ɔ kɛ ha Kaisare ɔ nitsɛ ke e ye ha mo ɔ, ma ha nɛ o ya Kaisare ɔ ngɔ.” Paulo ngɛ Agripa kɛ Bernike a hɛ mi

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Be bɔɔ ko se ɔ, Matsɛ Agripa kɛ Bernike ba Kaisarea nɛ a ba nga Festo kɛ pee lɛ baba hee.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Benɛ e ye be saii ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, Festo bɔ matsɛ ɔ Paulo he sane ɔ. E de lɛ ke, “Felike je pã mi no ko he ngɛ tsu mi ngɛ hiɛ ɔ.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: Benɛ i ya Yerusalem ɔ, Yuda osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ, kɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ ba ye ngɔ ba po e nya, nɛ a kpa mi pɛɛ ke ma bu lɛ fɔ.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: Se i de mɛ ke, e be Roma bi a mlaa a mi kaa a buu nɔ ko fɔ ke a gbe lɛ, ja nɔ nɛ a po e nya a, kɛ e nya poli ɔmɛ kpe hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi nɛ nɔ ɔ ná he blɔ je e nya ngɛ sane nɛ a ngɔ fɔ e nɔ ɔ he lolo.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, benɛ a nya ba bua ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, i tui tsle, se e nɔ jena a, i ya hi kojomi sɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ i fa ke a ngɔ nyumu ɔ kɛ ba.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: E nya poli ɔmɛ ba da si; se sane yayahi nɛ i susu kaa a kɛ ma ba po e nya a, a kɛ kake ngmelu po bɛ.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: Nɔ́ nɛ a ngɔ kɛ ba ji mɛ nitsɛmɛ a Mawu jami he nɔ́ jemi sane komɛ, kɛ Yesu ko nɛ gbo, nɛ Paulo lɛɛ e ke e ngɛ je mi kɛ mwɔɔ he sanehi.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: I li bɔ nɛ ma pee kɛ hla kikɛmɛ a sane nɛ ɔmɛ a mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i bi Paulo ke e suɔ nɛ e ya Yerusalem nɛ a ya ye e sane ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ lo?

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Agripa de Festo ke, “I suɔ kaa imi nitsɛ ma bu nyumu nɛ ɔ tue.” Festo he nɔ ke, “Hwɔɔ ɔ, ma ha nɛ o ba bu lɛ tue.”

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, Agripa kɛ Bernike mia saminya kɛ ba, nɛ a kɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ ma nimeli ɔmɛ tsuo sɛ tsu mi he nɛ a kpee ngɛ ɔ. Festo fa nɛ a kɛ Paulo ba tsu ɔ mi.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ Festo de ke, “Matsɛ Agripa, kɛ nyɛ nihi tsuo nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ wɔ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, nyɛ ngɛ nyumu nɛ ɔ hyɛe. Yuda bi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem, kɛ hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ hulɔ ɔ ba po e nya wawɛɛ. A kpa ngmlaa wo mi ke e sɛ kaa e hii je mi hu.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Se imi lɛɛ i na kaa e pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ sa gbenɔ. Akɛnɛ lɛ nitsɛ e ngɔ e sane ɔ kɛ ha Roma matsɛ ɔ he je ɔ, i ma nya si kaa a ngɔ lɛ kɛ ya ha Roma matsɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Se i be sane tutuutu ko nɛ ma ngma ya ha Roma matsɛ ɔ. Enɛ ɔ he nɛ i kɛ lɛ ba nyɛ hɛ mi, titli ɔ, mo Matsɛ Agripa o hɛ mi, konɛ ke o hla sane ɔ mi ɔ, ma na nɔ́ ko nɛ ma ngma.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: E peeɔ mi kaa e dɛ kaa a ngɔɔ pã mi no ko kɛ maneɔ, nɛ a tsɔɔ we nɔ́ pɔtɛɛ nɛ e pee.”

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: “Matsɛ Agripa, e ngɔ ye nya kaa ma je ye nya mwɔnɛ ɔ ngɛ o hɛ mi, ngɛ níhi tsuo nɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ kɛ ngɛ ye nya poe ɔ a he.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: Moo lɛɛ o le Yuda bi ɔmɛ a kusumihi tsuo, kɛ slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ a kpɛti ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o to tsui si, nɛ o bu mi tue.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Ke a maa ye odase anɔkuale mi ɔ, a maa na kaa kɛ je sisije ɔ, i hi si kaa Farisi no. Wa Farisi kuu ɔ ji nihi nɛ peeɔ veveeve pe kulaa ngɛ Mawu jami mi.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Wa wɛtso nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ ɔmɛ a hɛ ngɛ siwo nɛ ɔ nɔ. Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ a jaa Mawu saminya nyɔ kɛ pia, konɛ a nine nɛ su Mawu siwo ɔ nɔ. Nɛnɛ, kikɛmɛ a hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi nɛ ɔ he je nɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ ngɛ ye nya poe nɛ ɔ nɛ!

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Jehanɛ, nyɛ Yuda bi nɛ nyɛ ngɛ hiɛ ɔ, mɛni he je nyɛ he we yi kaa Mawu ma nyɛ ma tle ni gbogboehi si ɔ?

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: I na pee jã hulɔ ngɛ Yerusalem. Osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ nitsɛmɛ ngmɛ mi blɔ nɛ i wa nihi nɛ ji Mawu bimɛ ɔ yi mi. I wo a ti nihi babauu tsu, nɛ ke a bu mɛ gbenɔ fɔ ɔ, imi hu ye nya ngɛ mi.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: I ha nɛ a wa mɛ yi mi si abɔ ngɛ kpe he ɔmɛ tsuo; nɛ i bɔ mɔde kaa a ngmɛɛ a hemi kɛ yemi ɔ he. Ye hɛ dɔ wo mɛ, nɛ i tiu mɛ kɛ ya ma se zugbahi a nɔ tɔɔ ya wa mɛ yi mi. Paulo sɛɛ e tsui tsakemi he ní (Ni Tsumi

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: “Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ i pue nɔ kɛ ho Damasko ya kɛ ye dɛ mi womi nɛ osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ ha mi kɛ tsɔɔ kaa mɛ lɛ a ha mi he wami.

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: Nɛnɛ, piani katakata, benɛ i nyɛɛ blɔ kɛ yaa a, i na la ko nɛ kpɛ nylamnylam pe pu po kɛ je hiɔwe ba bɔle mi, kɛ nihi nɛ kɛ mi nyɛɛ ɔ.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Wɔ tsuo wa ya nɔ si, nɛ i nu gbi ko nɛ kɛ mi tu munyu ngɛ Hebri mi ke, ‘Saulo, Saulo! Mɛni he je nɛ o ngɛ mi yi mi wae? Ke o ke o kɛ mi ná a, o he awi kɛkɛ o ngɛ yee, kaa na nɛ ngɛ e tsɔ̃lɔ tso koli hɛɛe.’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ i bi ke, ‘Nyɔmtsɛ, mo mɛnɔ?’ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ he nɔ ke, ‘Imi ji Yesu nɛ o ngɛ lɛ yi mi wae ɔ.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Se, tee si ngɛ zugba, nɛ o da si. I je ye he kpo kɛ tsɔɔ mo, konɛ ma tsɔ mo, nɛ o ya ye ye he odase. Bɔ nɛ i je ye he kpo kɛ tsɔɔ mo mwɔnɛ ɔ, kɛ bɔ nɛ ma tsɔɔ mo hwɔɔ se ɔ, o ma ya fiɛ kɛ ha nihi tsuo.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: Ma je mo kɛ je yayami nɛ Israel ma a maa pee mo ɔ mi, nɛ ma je li ɔmɛ nɛ ma tsɔ mo a ngɔ ɔ hu a be mo awi ko nyɛe maa ye.

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: O ma ya bli a hɛngmɛ, konɛ a je diblii mi kɛ ba la he; o ma ya je mɛ kɛ je Abosiami ɔ he wami sisi kɛ ba Mawu ngɔ. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a ma he imi Yesu nɛ a ye, nɛ Mawu maa ngɔ a he yayami kɛ pa mɛ, nɛ a maa ba a hi he ngɛ nihi nɛ Mawu hla kɛ pee e ma a a kpɛti.’ Paulo sɛɛ bɔ nɛ e fiɛ he ní

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: I fiɛ ha ni ɔmɛ tsuo ke a tsake a tsui, nɛ a kpale kɛ ba Mawu ngɔ, nɛ a pee níhi nɛ tsɔɔ kaa a tsake a tsui niinɛ. I je fiɛmi nɛ ɔ sisi kɛ je Damasko kɛ ya gu Yerusalem kɛ ya muɔ Yudea zugba a, kɛ ya su ma je li ɔmɛ a ngɔ.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he nɛ Yuda bi ɔmɛ ba nu mi ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ, nɛ a ka kaa a maa gbe mi ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Se Mawu piɛ ye he kɛ ba su mwɔnɛ ligbi nɛ ɔ, nɛ i daa si ngɛ nyɛ hɛ mi kɛ ngɛ odase yee kɛ ngɛ nimli tsuo tsɔɔe, nimli wawi kɛ nimli nguahi tsuo. Nɔ́ nɛ Mose kɛ gbali ɔmɛ de to kaa e maa ba mi ɔ, lɔ ɔ nɔuu nɛ i ngɛ dee.

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ ji kaa Kristo ɔ maa na amanehlu, nɛ e ba pee kekleekle nɔ nɛ maa te si kɛ je gbeje. E ma ba fiɛ ha Yuda bi, kɛ ma je li tsuo ke a ma nyɛ ma he a yi wami, nɛ enɛ ɔ maa pee kaa la kɛ ha mɛ.”

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Paulo je e nya kikɛ nɛ ɔ, Festo de kɛ ngmlaa kɛ wo lɛ ke, “Paulo, o yi mi ngɛ puɛe pɛ! Womi kasemi sɔuu lɛ wo mo godo nɛ ɔ nɛ!”

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Paulo he nɔ ke, “Nɛnɛ Festo, i nui godo; anɔkuale ɔ i ngɛ tue ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ Agripa, i ngɛ munyu tue kɛ kã kɛ ngɛ mo tsɔɔe, ejakaa o le sane nɛ ɔmɛ a mi. I he we yi kaa ní nɛ ɔmɛ eko ngɛ nɛ a kɛ laa mo; ejakaa a pee we ekoeko ngɛ kɔkɔɔmi.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Matsɛ Agripa, níhi nɛ gbali ɔmɛ ngma a, tse o heɔ yeɔ? I le kaa o heɔ yeɔ!”

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Agripa de Paulo ke, “Be kpiti nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, anɛ o susu kaa o ma nyɛ plɛ ye yi mi nɛ ma pee Kristo se nyɛɛlɔ lo?”

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Paulo he nɔ ke, “Be ɔ kɛ jio, e kɛ́ we jio; i na nɛ jinɛ Mawu ha e ba mi kaa pi mo nɔ kake kɛkɛ, se mohu nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ mi tue bue mwɔnɛ nɛ ɔ hu ko pee kaa bɔ nɛ i ngɛ nɛ ɔ; kɔsɔkɔsɔ nɛ ɔmɛ pɛ lɛ a ko wo mɛ!”

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ matsɛ ɔ wo e he nɔ, nɛ amlaalo ɔ, kɛ Bernike, kɛ ni kpa amɛ hu te si ja nɔuu.

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: Benɛ a gbla a he si bɔɔ ɔ, a de ke, “Nyumu nɛ ɔ pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ sa kaa a gbe lɛ, loo a wo lɛ tsu.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Agripa de Festo ke, “Nyumu nɛ ɔ ngɔɛ e sane ɔ kɛ ha we Kaisare ɔ ke e ye jinɛ a ko ngmɛɛ e he.”

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Benɛ a ma nya si kaa wa ma wo lɛ kɛ ya Italia a, a ngɔ Paulo kɛ pamitsɛmɛ kpa komɛ hu ngɔ wo Roma asafoatsɛ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Yulio ɔ dɛ. Asafoatsɛ nɛ ɔ, “Roma matsɛ tabo” ɔ mi no ji lɛ.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Wa wó Adramitio lɛ ko kɛ ho. Lɛ nɛ ɔ yaa gu Asia wo nya ma amɛ a lɛsimuɔ he ɔmɛ. Aristarko, Makedonia no ɔ nɛ je Tesalonika a piɛ wa he.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: E nɔ jena a, wa ya su Sidon. Yulio hɛɛ Paulo saminya; e ngmɛ lɛ blɔ nɛ e ya slaa e huɛmɛ, nɛ a ha lɛ níhi nɛ hia lɛ.

english_verse: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
translation_verse: Wa hia kɛ je lejɛ ɔ, se akɛnɛ wa ngɛ kɔɔhiɔ kpee he je ɔ, wa ya gu Kipro kasa nya he nɛ zugba a tsi kɔɔhiɔ nya ngɛ. Kipro ji zugba kpɔ ko nɛ wo bɔle lɛ kɛ kpe.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Wa po Kilikia kɛ Pamfilia wo ɔ, nɛ wa ba da Mira ngɛ Likia.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Asafoatsɛ ɔ na Aleksandria lɛ ko ngɛ hiɛ ɔ nɛ yaa Italia, nɛ e je wɔ ngɔ wo mi.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Wa nyɛɛ blɛuu be saii nɛ dengme loko wa su Kenido ma a hanɔ. Se akɛnɛ kɔɔhiɔ ɔ ngmɛ́ wɔ blɔ nɛ waa ya hɛ mi he je ɔ, wa gba kɛ ya gu Salmone hanɔ kɛ tsɔ Kreta zugba kpɔ ɔ he. Zugba kpɔ nɛ ɔ tsi kɔɔhiɔ nya ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: Wa nyɛɛ kpo ɔ he haa, se dengme loko wa po mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba he ko nɛ a tsɛɛ Lɛsimuɔ he Jɔjɔɛ. Hiɛ ɔ, kɛ Lasea ma a he kɛ we.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Wa puɛ be babauu ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ ya si wa na kaa ke wa ke wa ma tsa blɔ hiami ɔ nɔ ɔ, e maa pee haomi sɔuu. Jehanɛ ɔ Kpatami ligbi ɔ hu be momo. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Paulo wo mɛ ga ke,

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: “Tsaatsɛmɛ, i na kaa kɛ je hiɛ ɔ kɛ yaa a, wa blɔ hiami ɔ maa pee haomi sɔuu. Lɛ ɔ maa ywia, tlomi ɔ maa laa, nɛ nimli a bimɛ a hɛ mi ma kpata.”

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Se munyu nɛ kudɔɔtsɛ ɔ, kɛ lɛtsɛ ɔ tu ɔ mohu ya asafoatsɛ ɔ yi mi pe ga nɛ Paulo wo mɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Lɛsimuɔ he ɔ pi he nɛ a ma nyɛ maa ye fĩɛ be ɔ ngɛ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a ti nihi fuu wo ga kaa a hia kɛ je lejɛ ɔ, nɛ a ka kaa alini a maa su Foinike, konɛ a ya ye fiɛ be ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Kreta lɛsimuɔ he ji Foinike, nɛ e ngɛ leneyi kɛ bonyoku je, kɛ omleyi kɛ bonyoku je a kpɛti. Wo nɔ kɔɔhiɔ nguaa hia

english_verse: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
translation_verse: Kɔɔhiɔ ba bɔni fiami blɛuu kɛ je leneyi je, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e pee ni ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ lɛ ɔ mi kaa nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ hlae ɔ ba mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a gbla sɛkɛ ɔ, nɛ a hia kɛ be ngɛ Kreta wo ɔ nya tataata.

english_verse: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
translation_verse: Tlukaa a, wo nɔ kɔɔhiɔ ko hia ba kpee mɛ. A tsɛɛ kɔɔhiɔ nɛ ɔ ke, “Omleyi kɛ beleku kɔɔhiɔ.”

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: Kɔɔhiɔ ɔ ba na lɛ ɔ, se akɛnɛ wa nyɛ we nɛ wa kudɔ lɛ ɔ kɛ kpee kɔɔhiɔ ɔ, wa ngmɛɛ lɛ ɔ he ha kɔɔhiɔ ɔ.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Benɛ wa kplaa kɛ ya su wo kpɔ nyafii ko nɛ a tsɛɛ Kauda a we leneyi je ɔ, wa ná mumi womi he bɔɔ, nɛ wa nyɛ nu lɛ ɔ mi boto ɔ.

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: A wo boto ɔ nɔ kɛ je wo ɔ mi kɛ ba lɛ ɔ mi, nɛ a fi boto ɔ kɛ wo angmla a he kpɛkpɛtɛɛ. A ngɛ gbeye yee kaa alini a ma ya sa zia kɛ mɔsɔ nɔ ngɛ Libia wo ɔ nya; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a gbe abalaa, konɛ kɔɔhiɔ nɛ kplaa lɛ ɔ kɛ ya.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Wo nɔ kɔɔhiɔ nɛ nya wa a doo wa nya wawɛɛ. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e nɔ jena a, a bɔni tlomi ɔ jemi ngɛ lɛ ɔ mi kɛ ngɛ wo ɔ mi puee.

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: Ligbi etɛne ɔ, mɛ nitsɛmɛ a je lɛ ɔ he ní ɔmɛ ekomɛ ngɔ pue wo ɔ mi.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Wa nɛ́ pu kɛ dodoe hɛ mi ligbi babauu. Be nɛ ɔ mi tsuo ɔ, kɔɔhiɔ ɔ ngɛ fiae wawɛɛ nitsɛ. Nyagbe ɔ, wa je wa hɛ fɔ si, ejakaa wa be hɛ nɔ kami kaa wa yi ma na wami.

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Ni ɔmɛ yi ní be saii enɛ ɔ ha Paulo te da si nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Tsaatsɛmɛ, jinɛ e sa kaa nyɛ ko bu mi tue, nɛ a ko hiɛ lɛ ɔ kɛ ji Kreta. Jinɛ wa ko ba nɛ nɔ́, nɛ níhi a hɛ mi hu ko ba kpataa we kikɛ nɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
translation_verse: Se kɛ̃ ɔ, i kpa nyɛ pɛɛ, nyɛ na tsui! Nyɛ ti nɔ ko nɔ ko be gboe. Lɛ ɔ kɛkɛ nɛ ma bɔ wɔ.

english_verse: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
translation_verse: Ejakaa nyɔ nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, Mawu, nɔ nɛ nɔ́ ji mi, nɛ lɛ nɔuu nɛ i jaa bɔfo ba da ye kasa nya,

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: nɛ e de mi ke, ‘Paulo, koo ye gbeye! Ja a kɛ mo ya da Kaisare ɔ hɛ mi kokooko. Mawu na mo mɔbɔ saminya, nɛ e he o kɛ nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ lɛ ɔ mi ɔ nyɛ yi wami.’

english_verse: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
translation_verse: Wa ma ya sa si ngɛ zugba kpɔ ko nɛ wo bɔle lɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a poo osɛkɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ wo wo ɔ mi, nɛ a pɛne kpa nɛ fi kudɔɔ ɔ hulɔ. Jehanɛ a wo abalaa nɛ ngɛ lɛ ɔ yi ɔ, konɛ kɔɔhiɔ ɔ nɛ ha nɛ lɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ ya hɛ mi. Kɛkɛ nɛ wa ngɔ wa yi kɛ pi wo kpo ɔ.

english_verse: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
translation_verse: Jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, lɛ ɔ mi ní tsuli ɔmɛ ka kaa a maa tu fo kɛ je lɛ ɔ mi. A je boto ɔ ngɔ wo wo ɔ mi, nɛ a buá pee kaa a yaa fɔ̃ osɛkɛ ngɛ lɛ ɔ yi je.

english_verse: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ ha a ye gbeye kaa alini nɛ lɛ ɔ ma ya sa si ngɛ tɛ sa nɔ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a fɔ̃ osɛkɛ eywiɛ ngɛ lɛ ɔ supa je kɛ ngɛ mlɛe nɛ je nɛ na mla.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: Se Paulo de asafoatsɛ ɔ, kɛ ta buli ɔmɛ ke, “Ke lɛ mi ní tsuli ɔmɛ je lɛ ɔ mi lɛɛ nyɛ be je mi tlɔe.”

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ta buli ɔmɛ poo kpa nɛ a kɛ fi boto ɔ, konɛ boto ɔ nɛ ho.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kpa nyɛ pɛɛ nɛ nyɛɛ ye ní, ejakaa lɔ ɔ lɛ ma ha nyɛ nɔmlɔ tso he wami. Nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be nyɛ ti nɔ ko pee.”

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: Benɛ Paulo de enɛ ɔ, e kɛ̃ abolo, nɛ e na Mawu si, nɛ ngɛ mɛ tsuo a hɛ mi ɔ, e ku mi, nɛ e bɔni yemi.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Kɛkɛ nɛ a nɔ gbagba te, nɛ mɛ tsuo a ye ní.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Benɛ a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ ye ní bɔ nɛ e ma nyɛ ɔ, a je ngma a tsuo ngɔ wo wo ɔ mi, konɛ lɛ ɔ nɛ pee huyɛhuyɛ. Lɛ ɔ butu

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Benɛ je na a, lɛ ɔ mi ní tsuli ɔmɛ li wo kpo he nɛ a ba su ɔ, se a na wo nya kɔtɔmi he ko kɛ e nya zia, nɛ a pee a yi mi kaa ke a ma nyɛ ɔ, a maa ngɔ lɛ ɔ kɛ ya sa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Lɛ ɔ ya hɛ zia kpɔ, nɛ e pu zu; e yiti ɔ ya hɛ si kpɛii, se e supa a lɛɛ oslɔke ɔ ywia lɛ wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Ta buli ɔmɛ pee a yi mi kaa a maa gbe pamitsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, konɛ a ti nɔ ko nɛ ko sile kɛ ho nɛ e ba tu fo kɛ je.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Se asafoatsɛ ɔ to e yi mi kaa e ma he Paulo yi wami, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e tsi a nya, nɛ a gbi nɔ ko. Mohu ɔ, e fa ke nihi tsuo nɛ le silemi ɔ, mɛ kekle a tu ngɔ pue wo ɔ mi, nɛ a sile kɛ ya nu kpo;

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: ni nɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ, a ti ni komɛ nɛ a bu gbegbelihi a nɔ, nɛ ni komɛ hu a kpla lɛ ɔ he kɛ ya nu kpo. Bɔ nɛ pee nɛ mɛ tsuo a ya su kpo slɔkee ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_verse: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
translation_verse: Benɛ wa su kpo slɔkee ɔ, wa ná le kaa zugba kpɔ nɛ wo bɔle lɛ nɛ ɔ biɛ ji Melita.

english_verse: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
translation_verse: Paulo ya bua lɛ tsɔwi nya, nɛ e kɛ ngɛ la a mi woe, kɛkɛ nɛ sinɔ ko je la glegle ɔ mi ba mimlaa e nine.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Benɛ lejɛ ɔ bi ɔmɛ na lohwe ɔ nɛ kplaa si ngɛ Paulo nine he ɔ, a de a he ke, “Nyumu nɛ ɔ, nɔmlɔ gbelɔ ji lɛ. E ná je osla mi ngɛ wo ɔ mi lɛɛ, se loloolo ɔ, e sɛsɛɛ ngmɛ́ lɛ blɔ kaa e hi je mi.”

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Se Paulo huanya sinɔ ɔ ngɔ wo la a mi, nɛ lohwe ɔ yi lɛ awi ko.

english_verse: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
translation_verse: Ni ɔmɛ ngɛ blɔ hyɛe kaa Paulo maa fuu, loo e ma tsɔ fia si nɛ e gbo tlukaa. Se benɛ a hyɛ blɔ hluu nɛ a nɛ́ kaa nɔ́ ko pee lɛ ɔ, a tsake a juɛmi, nɛ a de ke, “Mawu ko ji lɛ!”

english_verse: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
translation_verse: Zugba kpɔ nɛ ɔ nɔ nɔkɔtɔma a, a tsɛɛ lɛ Publio. E ngɛ ngmɔ nɛ kɛ he nɛ sane nɛ ɔ ba ngɛ ɔ kɛ́ we kulaa. Nyumu nɛ ɔ he wɔ hɛmuɔ, nɛ e pee wɔ nibwɔ saminya ligbi etɛ sɔuu.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Publio tsɛ hwɔɔ si kpotoo kɛ asla yaya kɛ mi mi pa. Paulo ya sɛ tsu mi he nɛ e ngɛ ɔ, nɛ e sɔle. E ngɔ e nine ngɔ pue hiɔtsɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ e tsa lɛ.

english_verse: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
translation_verse: Benɛ a tsa hiɔtsɛ nɛ ɔ se ɔ, hiɔtsɛmɛ kpahi nɛ ngɛ zugba nɛ wo bɔle lɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ hu ba, nɛ Paulo tsa mɛ.

english_verse: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
translation_verse: Ni ɔmɛ ke wɔ ní babauu, nɛ pee se benɛ wa sɛ lɛ nɛ wa maa ho hiami ya a, a ngɔ níhi nɛ maa hia wɔ ba wo lɛ ɔ mi ha wɔ. Paulo je Melita kɛ ya Roma

english_verse: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
translation_verse: Hlami etɛ se ɔ, wa je Melita. Wa wó lɛ ko nɛ je Aleksandria. Lɛ ɔ he so ji “Hawi ɔmɛ”, nɛ e ba ye fĩɛ be ɔ ngɛ zugba kpɔ nɛ wo bɔle lɛ ɔ nɔ.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Wa ba su Sirakusa, nɛ wa ye ligbi etɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.

english_verse: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
translation_verse: Wa je lejɛ ɔ kɛ ba ma ko nɛ a tsɛɛ Regio ɔ. E nɔ jena a, kɔɔhiɔ bɔni fiami kɛ je leneyi je nɛ wa ye ligbi enyɔ kɛ ba su Puteoli ma a mi.

english_verse: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
translation_verse: Wa ba na nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ekomɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ a kpa wɔ pɛɛ ke waa ye otsi ngɛ a ngɔ. Kɛkɛ nɛ wa ba su Roma.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Benɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Roma a nu wa he ɔ, a ba kpee wɔ ngɛ he ko nɛ a tsɛɛ “Apio Jua nɔ” kɛ “Nibwɔhi a to he Etɛ” ɔ tɔɔ. Benɛ Paulo na mɛ ɔ, e na Mawu si, nɛ e tsui nɔ e mi fuaa. Paulo ngɛ Roma

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
translation_verse: Benɛ wa ba su Roma a, a ngmɛ Paulo blɔ nɛ lɛ nitsɛ e hi e dɛ he, kɛ ta bulɔ kake nɛ ngɛ e he bue.

english_verse: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
translation_verse: Ligbi etɛ se ɔ, Paulo tsɛ lejɛ ɔ Yuda bi ɔmɛ a nikɔtɔma amɛ kpe. Benɛ a nya ba bua a, e de mɛ ke, “Ye nyɛmimɛ Israel bi, i pee we wa ma a yayami ko, nɛ wa nɛmɛ ɔmɛ a kusumihi nɛ a si ha wɔ ɔ hu i tɔ we ekoeko nɔ; se kɛ̃ ɔ, a nu mi ngɛ Yerusalem, nɛ a ngɔ mi ngɔ wo Roma bi ɔmɛ a dɛ mi kaa pã mi no.

english_verse: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
translation_verse: Benɛ Roma nɔ yeli ɔmɛ ta ye nya mi kɛ hla sane ɔ mi gbe nya a, jinɛ mɛɛ a hla kaa a maa ngmɛɛ ye he kaa i pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ sa kaa a gbe mi.

english_verse: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
translation_verse: Ní nɛ ɔmɛ a he je nɛ i tsɛ nyɛ kɛ ba, konɛ i kɛ nyɛ nɛ sɛɛ ní. Anɔkuale mi ɔ, kɔsɔkɔsɔ nɛ ngɛ ye he nɛ ɔ, nɔ nɛ Israel bi ngɔ a hɛ kɛ fɔ e nɔ ɔ he a wo mi ngɛ.”

english_verse: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
translation_verse: A de lɛ ke, “Wɔɔ lɛɛ wa na we womi ko kɛ ji Yudea ngɛ o he; nɛ jehanɛ hu, nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko bɛ hiɛ ɔ ba sɛɛ we o he sane ko, aloo o he munyu yaya ko.

english_verse: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
translation_verse: Se wa suɔ kaa wa maa bu mo tue nɛ waa le o juɛmi; ejakaa kuu nɛ o ngɛ mi nɛ ɔ, wa le kaa ngɛ he tsuaa he ɔ, a tuɔ e he munyu yaya.”

english_verse: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a to Paulo be kpa; nɛ jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, nihi babauu ba e ngɔ ngɛ he nɛ e ba to ɔ. E gbá níhi a mi tsɔɔ mɛ kɛ je mɔtu kɛ ya si gbɔkuɛ. E tsɔɔ mɛ sɛ gbi nɛ kɔɔ Mawu matsɛ yemi ɔ he ɔ, nɛ e kɛ níhi nɛ a ngma ngɛ Mose mlaa, kɛ gbali ɔmɛ a womi ɔmɛ a mi ɔ fi e munyu ɔ se, konɛ a na anɔkuale ɔ nɛ kɔɔ Yesu he ɔ.

english_verse: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
translation_verse: A ti ni komɛ he ye, nɛ ni komɛ hu he we yi.

english_verse: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Se nɔ́ kake too nɛ Paulo de, nɛ lɔ ɔ kɛ nya sami wawɛɛ ba ni ɔmɛ a kpɛti, nɛ́ kpe ɔ kɛ gbɛ ji, “Nɔ́ nɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ de nyɛ nɛmɛ ɔmɛ kɛ gu gbalɔ Yesaya nɔ ɔ ngɛ mi jã niinɛ!

english_verse: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
translation_verse: Mumi ɔ de gbalɔ ɔ ke, ‘Yaa, nɛ o ya de ma nɛ ɔ ke Nyɛ maa nu, se nyɛ be sisi nue. Nyɛ maa na, se nyɛ be se kɔe.

english_verse: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
translation_verse: Ejakaa ma nɛ ɔ nui nɔ́ sisi kulaa; nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko sɛ we a tue mi. Ke pi jã a, a maa hyɛ nɔ́, nɛ a maa nu nɔ́, nɛ a juɛmi ma kɔ nɔ́ se. Kɛkɛ ɔ, a maa kpale kɛ ba imi Mawu, ye ngɔ, nɛ ma he a yi wami.’ ”

english_verse: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
translation_verse: Benɛ Paulo de kikɛ nɛ ɔ, Yuda bi ɔmɛ je lejɛ ɔ. Nɛ́ a yaa a tsuo, a ngɛ nya sãe wawɛɛ ngɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a kpɛti.]

english_verse: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
translation_verse: Paulo hi we ko mi jeha enyɔ, nɛ e wo he hiɔ. Nihi tsuo nɛ ba slaa lɛ ɔ, lejɛ ɔ nɛ e kɛ mɛ kpee ngɛ.

english_verse: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_verse: E fiɛɛ Mawu matsɛ yemi ɔ he sane, nɛ e tsɔɔ mɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo he sane. E tu munyu kɛ kã nɛ gbeye yemi ko be e mi; nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko hu tsi we lɛ blɔ.

english_verse: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
translation_verse: Imi Paulo, Yesu Kristo tsɔlɔ kɛ bɔfo nɛ Mawu hla nɛ e tsɔ ke ma ya fiɛ sane kpakpa a nɛ i ngɛ womi nɛ ɔ ngmae.

english_verse: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
translation_verse: Se a tle lɛ si kɛ je gbeje ngɛ Mawu mumi ɔ he wami nya kɛ tsɔɔ kaa Mawu Bi ji lɛ; nɛ e ngɛ klɔuklɔu.

english_verse: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
translation_verse: Kristo nɔ i gu nɛ i na dloomi, nɛ a wo mi bɔfo, konɛ e biɛ ɔ he ɔ, je ma amɛ kulaa nɛ a bu hemi kɛ yemi ɔ tue.

english_verse: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
translation_verse: I ngɛ womi nɛ ɔ ngmae ha nyɛ tsuo nɛ nyɛ ngɛ Roma nɛ Mawu suɔ nyɛ, nɛ e tsɛ nyɛ kɛ ba pee lɛ nitsɛ e ni klɔuklɔuhi ɔ. Dloomi kɛ he jɔmi nɛ je wa Tsɛ Mawu ɔ, kɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo dɛ mi ɔ ha nyɛ! Paulo sɔle kɛ na Mawu si

english_verse: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
translation_verse: Kekleekle ɔ, i gu Yesu Kristo nɔ kɛ ngɛ ye Mawu ɔ si nae ngɛ nyɛ tsuo nyɛ he, ejakaa a ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi nɛ nyɛ hɛɛ mi ɔ he odase yee ngɛ je ɔ mi he tsuaa he.

english_verse: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
translation_verse: Mawu ɔ nɛ i sɔmɔɔ lɛ kɛ ye tsui tsuo kɛ gu sane kpakpa a nɛ kɔɔ e Bi ɔ he ɔ fiɛmi mi ɔ ji ye we odase kaa i kaiɔ nyɛ daa nɛ i jɔɔ we ngɛ ye sɔlemi mi.

english_verse: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
translation_verse: I kpaa pɛɛ kaa alinɔ Mawu suɔmi nya a jehanɛ lɛɛ blɔ ma bli ha mi nɛ ma nyɛ ma ba nyɛ ngɔ.

english_verse: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
translation_verse: Ejakaa ye hɛ ngɛ jae wawɛɛ ngɛ nyɛ he, nɛ i suɔ kaa ma na nyɛ, konɛ ma ba ha nyɛ mumi mi nike ní kɛ wo nyɛ he wami.

english_verse: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
translation_verse: I ngɛ tsɔɔe kaa i kɛ nyɛ tsuo waa ngɔ hemi kɛ yemi nɛ wa ngɛ ɔ kɛ wo wa sibi he wami.

english_verse: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
translation_verse: Ye nyɛmimɛ, i suɔ nɛ nyɛɛ le kaa i pee ye yi mi si abɔ kaa ma ba slaa nyɛ, konɛ ma ná yiblii komɛ ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti kaa bɔ nɛ i ná ngɛ ma je li kpa amɛ a kpɛti ɔ. Se kɛ ba si amlɔ nɛ ɔ, i na we blɔ.

english_verse: It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome. The Power of the Good News
translation_verse: Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, e ngɛ ye tsui nɔ wawɛɛ kaa maa fiɛ sane kpakpa a ngɔ tsɔɔ nyɛ nihi nɛ nyɛ ngɛ Roma a hulɔ. Mawu he wami ngɛ sane kpakpa a mi

english_verse: I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Sane kpakpa a he pee we mi zo, ejakaa e ji Mawu he wami nɛ haa nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ heɔ yeɔ ɔ yi naa wami, Yuda bi kekle, lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ma je li hulɔ.

english_verse: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
translation_verse: Ejakaa sane kpakpa a lɛ tsɔɔ kaa kɛ je sisije kɛ yaa si nyagbe ɔ, hemi kɛ yemi nɔ Mawu daa nɛ e kɛ buu nimli adesahi nihi nɛ da. Kaa bɔ nɛ ngmami ɔ deɔ ɔ, “Nɔ nɛ a gu hemi kɛ yemi nɔ bu lɛ nɔ nɛ da a yi ma na wami.” Nimli adesahi tsuo yeɔ fɔ

english_verse: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
translation_verse: Nihi nɛ peeɔ yayami, nɛ a bɔɔ musu kɛ tsiɔ anɔkuale ɔ nɛ kɔɔ Mawu he ɔ nya a, Mawu kɛ mi mi fumi nɛ jeɔ hiɔwe gblaa a tue.

english_verse: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
translation_verse: Mawu gblaa a tue wawɛɛ, ejakaa nɔ́ nɛ sa nɛ a le ngɛ Mawu he ɔ fɔɔ si paa; Mawu nitsɛ je tsɔɔ mɛ momo.

english_verse: God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse.
translation_verse: Kɛ je be nɛ Mawu bɔ je ɔ, e he wami nɛ ngɛ daa, kɛ e su nɛ ji níhi nɛ a nɛ́ kɛ hɛngmɛ ɔ jeɔ kpo paa ngɛ e nibɔ ní ɔmɛ a mi, nɛ adesa naa. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a be nya jemi ko kulaa.

english_verse: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
translation_verse: A tsɛɔ a he ní leli, se a plɛ pee kuasiahi mohu.

english_verse: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
translation_verse: Mawu nɛ gbo we gblee ɔ, a wui e hɛ mi nyami bɔ nɛ sa kaa a peeɔ, se mohu a ya woɔ níhi nɛ a puɛ kaa nɔmlɔ adesa nɛ gboɔ ɔ, aloo lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ, loo lohwe nane eywiɛɛywiɛtsɛmɛ, loo lohwehi nɛ sãã si mohu a hɛ mi nyami.

english_verse: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
translation_verse: Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Mawu ngmɛɛ a he, nɛ a ya nyɛɛ akɔnɔ yaya nɛ ngɛ a tsui nɔ ɔ se; nɛ a kɛ a sibi tsu mu níhi kɛ pue a nɔmlɔ tso ɔ hɛ mi si.
